Classification: Information Technology Specialist II

                          Unlimited, Full-time 

                          8:00 AM to 4:30 PM (Monday – Friday)

*A flexible work schedule may be approved with up to two days remote work per week (if applicable)

Salary Range: Hourly from $28.69 to $46.62; Annually from $59,863 to $97,343

*Salary placement is dependent on education and experience

(Please note that a different range may be displayed elsewhere in this post due to a glitch, this is the correct range.)

 

The vacancy is posted online from Friday, October 16 to Thursday, November 5 at 11:59pm

 

THE POSITION AND THE DEPARTMENT

The CRM Administrator provides technical, functional, and strategic leadership for Normandale Community College’s enterprise customer relationship management (CRM) platforms. This position is responsible for the implementation, administration, configuration, integration, optimization, security, and ongoing support of CRM systems that advance student engagement, recruitment, retention, communication, and other institutional priorities.  This is a highly responsible position that provides daily delivery of customer-focused college-wide technical support.

 

Serving as the primary CRM subject matter expert, the position partners with college departments to understand business needs, improve processes, evaluate new use cases, and translate functional requirements into effective technology solutions. The CRM Administrator also serves as the primary liaison among Normandale IT staff, CRM vendors, Minnesota State partners, and the faculty and staff who use these systems.

 

The position manages system enhancements, releases, integrations, access, data-related requests, vendor coordination, documentation, training, and governance activities. The CRM Administrator works independently with limited supervision, exercises sound technical and operational judgment, and communicates regularly with college leadership, faculty, staff, vendors, and other partners to ensure CRM services remain reliable, secure, accessible, and aligned with the college’s strategic and operational needs.  This position is responsible for ensuring appropriate information and data security protocols are implemented and adhered to.

 

This position will actively advance the college’s strategic goals, including to achieve equity in educational outcomes and to support a culturally responsive and service-oriented culture, through individual and departmental efforts.

 

 

YOUR QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum:

  • Two (2) years' experience administering, configuring, supporting, or implementing CRM platforms, enterprise business applications, or similar technology solutions.
  • Strong understanding of college recruitment and retention processes, goals, and departmental functions supporting them.
  • Ability to communicate written and oral technical information to technical and non-technical staff/users.
  • Demonstrated ability to gather, analyze, and translate business requirements into technical solutions and system configurations.
  • Demonstrated problem-solving, analytical, and critical-thinking skills sufficient to identify issues, evaluate alternatives, and recommend effective solutions.
  • Experience developing and delivering end-user training, documentation, or knowledge resources.
  • Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with partners across multiple departments, including the ability to understand business needs, build trust, and facilitate collaborative technology solutions.

 

Preferred:

  • Experience administering and configuring higher education CRM platforms, including systems supporting recruitment, admissions, student engagement, retention, or advising.
  • Demonstrated project management experience leading technology implementations, upgrades, or cross-functional initiatives.
  • Experience serving as a vendor liaison and managing software vendor relationships, releases/patches, or product roadmaps.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead meetings, facilitate discussions, and deliver presentations to diverse partner groups while effectively communicating technical and business concepts.
  • Experience supporting and monitoring data integrations, APIs, middleware solutions, or data synchronization processes.
  • Experience with SQL, relational databases, reporting, data analysis, or data integration technologies.

 

 

WHY NORMANDALE

Normandale is the largest community college in the Minnesota State Colleges and Universities system, annually serving almost 15,000 students from a diverse set of backgrounds, 42% of whom are students of color and nearly 25% are first-generation. We offer opportunities for individuals to grow, learn, and advance their careers while working for an organization that is committed to providing an inclusive and equitable space for students and employees to learn.  We are passionately committed to achieving racial equity in student outcomes and in advancing cultural competency in the classroom and services provided.

 

GREAT BENEFITS PACKAGE

As an agency of the State of Minnesota, Normandale offers a comprehensive benefits package including low cost medical, dental, vision insurance, short- and long-term disability, generous vacation and sick leave, 11 paid holidays each year, employer paid life insurance, pre-tax flexible spending accounts, retirement plans, and tax-deferred compensation plans. Additional benefits include tuition waivers available for yourself and eligible dependents once certain criteria are met.

For information on benefits, visit SEGIP’s website SEGIP. This position is also part of the Minnesota Association of Professional Employees (MAPE). The MAPE (https://mn.gov/mmb/employee-relations/labor-relations/labor/mape.jsp) contract outlines many additional benefits provided.

For more information on retirement benefits, please view the retirement brochure through MMB.

 

HOW TO APPLY

Interested applicants should submit their application materials to this job posting. You can also search for this job and more on the Minnesota State careers website at https://minnstate.wd115.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/Minnesota_State_Careers.  If you are unable to apply online, please contact the job information line at (952) 358-8269.

 

If you are a current Minnesota State employee, please log into Workday, click on the Careers Hub section and search for the Job Code.

 

The College regrets that it is unable to offer H-1B sponsorship at this time. The successful candidate, under U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services regulations, must be able to accept work in the U.S. by the day employment begins.

An offer for this position may be contingent upon the completion of a background check.

 

Equal Employment Opportunity

Normandale Community College is committed to honoring human differences and cultivating inclusion of different values and ideas in employment and education opportunity. The college is committed to the principle that all individuals are to be treated with equality and dignity.

 

No person shall be discriminated against in the terms and conditions of employment, personnel practices, or access to and participation in, programs, services, and activities with regard to race, sex, color, creed, religion, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. In addition, discrimination in employment based on familial status or membership or activity in a local commission as defined by law is prohibited.

 

Reasonable accommodations will be made to applicants with disabilities. If you are an individual with a disability who needs assistance, please contact Human Resources at (952) 358-8269 or jobs@normandale.edu. Please indicate what assistance is needed.


Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable bargaining unit agreement or personnel plan.


Benefits Information:

At Minnesota State, we take your well-being and work-life balance seriously. We offer a comprehensive benefits package that features low-cost medical and dental insurance with affordable deductibles, employer-paid life insurance, short- and long-term disability, and pre-tax healthcare and dependent care accounts with a roll-over option. To further support your holistic health, employees also have access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental health, legal, and financial counseling. Detailed plan details, rates, and coverage choices can be reviewed directly via the State Employee Group Insurance Program (SEGIP) website.

 

To support your life outside of work, our package includes 12 paid holidays, generous vacation and sick time, and six weeks of Paid Parental Leave. We also help you secure your financial future with a robust Pension Plan, 457(b) and 403(b) retirement accounts, and various investment options. Furthermore, we invest in your growth by providing dedicated professional development and tuition waivers for both you and your dependents. Please note that specific benefit eligibility and coverage levels may vary depending on the type of position, employee classification, and collective bargaining agreements.

Position Title:

Instructional Designer (Associate or No Prefix)

Job Category:

Academic Staff

Employment Type:

Regular

Job Profile:

Teaching, Learning, and Technology Specialist II

Job Duties:

The Instructional Designer (Assoc. or No prefix) will work in close collaboration with senior instructional design staff to assist with or support the design, development, and enhancement of instructional activities, programs, and curricula. The Instructional Designer works in close collaboration with various stakeholders to obtain content, apply learning theories and instructional design models, employ sound project management practices, and appropriately engage internal and external resources to meet learner and organizational needs.  

The Instructional Designer is responsible for creating courses in the learning management system (LMS) and ensuring the content of those courses meets high quality standards. Title placement will be dependent on the selected candidate’s qualifications and experience. 

Key Job Responsibilities:

  • Under the supervision of senior instructional design staff, meet with faculty members and/or subject matter experts to create and manage a curriculum development plan for online courses  
  • Build strong, collaborative relationships with constituents through face-to-face and remote interactions (e.g., emails, webinars, conference calls) 
  • Assist with the development of training materials and provide professional development to faculty regarding current research related to best practices for the development and teaching of online courses 
  • Assist with the selection, review, and integration of educational technologies to support pedagogical aims  
  • Provide training to faculty on the use of the learning management system and other associated educational technologies  
  • Coordinate with media staff on the creation of a media plan and associated content 
  • Assist with the identification and communication of opportunities to improve the learning experience for all students, especially those related to accessibility, and collaboratively work with faculty to carry out this work 
  • Aid faculty in locating and evaluating educational resources, and provide guidance on issues related to copyright and fair use guidelines 
  • Maintain a commitment to practitioner scholarship by keeping abreast of emerging theories and practices 
  • Perform other duties as requested 

Department:

The Office of Online & Professional Learning Resources is committed to providing service and support to the Universities of Wisconsin Administration and all 13 UW universities in online and continuing education, teaching, learning, and workforce skills training and resources. 


OPLR works in partnership with all 13 UW universities to develop and deliver online semester- and competency-based degrees and a broad array of credit and non-credit certificates, courses, and other credentials to help adult and professional learners achieve their academic and professional development goals and to develop the workforce of Wisconsin. 


Compensation:

The Instructional Designer (Assoc. or no-prefix) is a full-time salaried (exempt) academic staff position.  


Well-qualified candidates can expect a starting annual salary within a range of $50,000 - $67,000 commensurate with the candidate’s education, related experience, and qualifications. 


Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree  
  • Demonstrated knowledge of learning theory and instructional design models 
  • Experience working with learning management systems and related educational technologies 
  • Experience establishing professional relationships with stakeholders/clients to help meet their objectives while providing excellent customer service 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills 
  • Experience applying project management strategies to meet project goals and deadlines 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in instructional design, curriculum and instruction, educational technology, adult learning, continuing education, or a related field 
  • Knowledge of current learning/instructional design theories pertaining to online education  
  • Proficiency in the Canvas learning management system  
  • Proficiency in the use of basic programming related to online learning (e.g., HTML, XML, ActionScript, JAVA or JavaScript) 
  • Experience working collaboratively with other instructional designers 
  • Experience working in higher education on instructional design projects for others

Work Location:

Telecommuting or hybrid work options may be available, with a minimum in-office expectation of two days per month. However, depending on business needs, there may be occasions when additional in-office presence is requested. Department:  Academic Affairs                                                                 


POSITION SUMMARY:

 

The Center for Excellence in Teaching and Learning (CETL) at UWRF is searching for an Instructional Designer to help our educators thrive in an era of digital accessibility, AI, and an ever-changing educational landscape. The successful candidate will work with the CETL Director and other members of the campus community (e.g., administrators, technologists, student affairs professionals) to help develop curricula and programming that reflect evidence-based approaches to instructional design and delivery. Further, the successful candidate will provide training and development for effective online teaching, effective digital delivery across all modes of instruction, and assistance in selecting and applying educational methods and technologies that further student success.


RESPONSIBILITIES:


Instructional Design


  • Designs, develops, and delivers educational development programs and activities, including Canvas-based courses, communities of practice, and workshops, that will support instructor certification for online teaching and provide more general teaching development across a variety of issues (e.g., teaching and learning strategies, instructional modalities, artificial intelligence, digital accessibility) 
  • Assists and supports the use of educational technologies including, but not limited to, our Learning Management System (i.e., Canvas), screen recording software, digital annotation tools, and student response systems
  • Consults with individuals, programs, and departments across UWRF to provide expertise in pedagogy, instructional design, and learning technology
  • Works as part of various campus teams to identify and implement interventions that promote the use of evidence-based pedagogies across instructional modalities
  • Stays up to date and current with respect to research and emerging trends related to teaching and learning, educational technology, AI, and digital accessibility so as to provide helpful resources to the campus community
  • Infuses principles of equity, inclusion, and universal design into educational development opportunities, programs, and activities

University Support


  • Works with the CETL Director to advance CETL initiatives and programming
  • Represents CETL on both UWRF and UW (Universities of Wisconsin) committees or ad hoc groups to accomplish specific goals as well as to improve teaching and learning more generally
  • Advises and supports groups or committees working on program-level curricular design and development by contributing expertise in pedagogy, instructional design, and learning technology 
  • Collects, organizes, interprets, and disseminates data related to instructional program needs and educational development programs
  • Other duties as assigned

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:


Required Qualifications:


  • Master’s degree
  • Experience with instructional software, learning management systems/digital learning environments, online course delivery methods, and other instructional and learning technologies
  • Experience designing and delivering effective educational development
  • Experience with and/or knowledge of artificial intelligence and its potential impact on and integration within higher education (e.g., on instructors, students, the curriculum)
  • Demonstrated ability in interpersonal, verbal, written, and presentation skills
  • Organizational skills to effectively manage multiple projects simultaneously while meeting corresponding deadlines
  • Ability to work effectively in a team environment and to maintain effective working relationships with individuals from diverse backgrounds and abilities

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Experience designing and delivering effective educational development in higher education
  • Teaching experience at the higher education level, especially online or hybrid teaching experience
  • Experience with Canvas
  • Training or certification in learning technologies, instructional design, or instructional technology
  • Knowledge of digital accessibility and its application to learning materials
  • Ability to discuss and apply equity-minded and inclusive pedagogies and design principles
  • Capacity to work effectively with educators from a variety of disciplines
  • Experience with a range of learning technologies

Key Job Responsibilities:

  • Analyzes, tests, troubleshoots, resolves issues, and provides feedback regarding learning technologies
  • Collects, organizes, interprets, and disseminates data to identify instructional program needs and enhance effectiveness
  • Designs and develops engaging, effective learning experiences which may be face-to-face, blended, and/or online
  • Designs, develops, or recommends multimedia learning materials. Facilitates communications with multimedia service providers to ensure instructional needs are met
  • Designs, develops, organizes, maintains, and consults on instructional materials, activities, curricula, and assessment resources in accordance with current pedagogical practices, cognitive/learning science, and design tools and methods
  • Provides training and technical support directly to learners in settings such as classrooms, labs, clinics, and distance learning mediums
  • Designs, develops, and delivers faculty development and engagement programs and activities
  • Researches, designs, and/or acquires learning resources, technologies, materials, and/or processes to support learning
  • Provides consultation, training, and/or support for learning technology tools and platforms

Position Title:

Instructional Designer - College of Business and Economics

Job Category:

Academic Staff

Employment Type:

Regular

Job Profile:

Teaching, Learning, and Technology Specialist III

Job Duties:

Attention:

The College of Business and Economics at the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater seeks an Instructional Designer (Teaching, Learning, and Technology Specialist III, TL009).

Job Details:

The Instructional Designer serves as a strategic partner and expert pedagogical consultant to faculty and academic units within the College of Business and Economics (CoBE). This position applies advanced instructional design principles, learning theories, and user-experience standards to support the design, development, delivery, and continuous improvement of high-quality learning experiences across face-to-face, hyflex, and online modalities. Operating within the CoBE Tech team, the individual in this role acts as a primary pedagogical and educational technology resource, collaborating with instructional staff to implement effective assessment strategies, select appropriate instructional technologies, and ensure compliance with digital accessibility standards. This position reports directly to the Assistant Dean of Online Education & Technology at the College of Business and Economics. This is a full-time, 12-month Academic Staff position.

Key Job Responsibilities:

1. Instructional Design & Pedagogical Consultation

●       Consult with faculty on the application of learning theories, instructional design models, and evidence-based teaching strategies to develop engaging, learner-centered business education courses

●       Guide instructors in aligning measurable learning outcomes with course activities, structural sequencing, and robust, authentic assessment methodologies

●       Consult with faculty on the ethical integration of Generative, Agentic, and other relevant AI tools (e.g., LLMs, specialized business simulators) into coursework, assisting them in developing clear classroom AI policies and innovative, "AI-active" or "AI-resistant" assessment models

●       Use AI-assisted workflows to accelerate course mapping, draft creative case-study scripts, and generate diverse practice question pools aligned with professional accreditation standards

●       Conduct systematic quality reviews of new and existing courses using recognized quality assurance rubrics (e.g., Quality Matters)

●       Ensure all instructional materials, course layouts, and digital media adhere strictly to federal, state, and institutional accessibility guidelines (ADA, Section 508, and Universal Design for Learning principles)


2. Multimedia Production & Technology Integration

●       Collaborate directly with the CoBE Tech media production team to coordinate the design and seamless integration of high-quality visual graphics, animations, podcast setups, and broadcast-quality video/audio components into course environments

●       Utilize course authoring tools and the institutional Learning Management System (LMS) to build interactive, visually engaging learning modules

●       Evaluate emerging instructional innovations, educational applications, and AI-driven workflow solutions, recommending strategic equipment or software implementation to the Assistant Dean

●       Provide advanced troubleshooting and technical consultation for instructional technology platforms utilized within the college


3. Faculty Training & Support

●       Develop, coordinate, and deliver comprehensive training programs, workshops, and documentation for faculty and staff regarding instructional design best practices and LMS functionality

●       Provide supportive, client-focused technical assistance to educators across a wide spectrum of technical comfort and experience levels

●       As operationally feasible and approved by leadership, this position may include opportunities to teach courses within the college


4. Strategic Alignment & Administrative Support

●       Represent CoBE Tech on campus-wide committees and cross-functional initiatives related to institutional teaching, learning, and digital learning strategies

●       Assist the Assistant Dean with regular technology needs assessments to inform future resource and equipment planning

Department:

College of Business and Economics

Compensation:

Well-qualified candidates can expect a starting annual salary within a range of $65,000 – $75,000.

UW System employees receive an excellent benefit package. To learn more about the UW System’s comprehensive benefit package, review the UW System Employee Benefits Brochure.

Required Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in Instructional Design, Educational Technology, Education, or a closely related field

  • Minimum of 2 years of professional experience designing and developing courses within an education environment across multiple modalities (online, hyflex, face-to-face)

  • Demonstrated proficiency with enterprise-level Learning Management Systems (such as Canvas)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior teaching or instructional facilitation experience in a Higher Education setting, with eligibility/desire to teach business-related courses

  • Quality Matters (QM) Peer Reviewer certification

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Autonomy & Initiative: Strong ability to self-motivate, take initiative, prioritize projects, and work highly independently in a fast-paced environment

  • Consultative Communication: Exceptional active listening, written, and oral communication skills, with a proven passion for assisting users of varying technical skill and comfort levels

  • AI Literacy & Tool Fluency: Practical understanding of Generative AI platforms and prompt-engineering frameworks (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot) and how to apply them responsibly to course creation, writing assistance, and workflow automation

  • Design Frameworks: Deep knowledge of adult learning principles, modern assessment strategies, and quality assurance frameworks

  • Accessibility & Compliance: Thorough understanding of digital accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1, ADA, Section 508) and student data privacy regulations (FERPA)

  • Collaborative Mindset: Strong ability to collaborate effectively with faculty, media production specialists, and campus IT partners to achieve unified project goals

  • Ability to interact respectfully with people with diverse socioeconomic, cultural and ethnic backgrounds

  • Willingness and ability to be an active participant in following applicable safety rules and regulations including necessary training and drills

  • Cover Letter

Heather Taplick

Dean Assistant

262-472-1343

taplickh@uww.edu

If you have questions regarding this recruitment or if you are unable to complete the application online due to a disability or system problem, please contact us at (262) 472-1024 or hr@uww.edu.

CONDITIONS OF APPOINTMENT:

University of Wisconsin-Whitewater does not offer H-1B or other work authorization visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and maintain work authorization throughout the employment term. If you have questions regarding this, please contact Human Resources. UW-Whitewater is not an e-verify employer, therefore STEM extensions are not options for work authorization.

CAMPUS INFORMATION:

UW-Whitewater is a thriving public university located in southeastern Wisconsin. It leads the way in providing world-class, affordable higher education programs to more students than neighboring regional comprehensives in the University of Wisconsin System. Position Title:

Job Duties:

Attention:

The Department of Biology in the College of Letters and Sciences at the University of Wisconsin-Whitewater seeks a postdoctoral fellow in the area of developmental biology, cell biology, physiology, or molecular genetics beginning August 2026. This is a National Science Foundation funded position with responsibilities for research (75%) and teaching and mentoring undergraduate students (25%). Experience in developmental biology, cell biology, physiology, or molecular genetics is preferred.

Job Details:

This is a National Science Foundation funded postdoctoral position studying circadian gene regulation of metabolism and gene expression during dorsal mesoderm specification in Xenopus laevis  (RUI # 2523434). The project extends preliminary findings that circadian genes (bmal1 and rev-erba) impact the metabolic shift that occurs during dorsal mesoderm specification.  We use a variety of embryological and molecular genetic approaches.  The candidate will be trained in relevant techniques which include genome editing using CRISPR-Cas9, luciferase-based assay systems, RNA-Seq, bioinformatics, microinjection, and microdissection of Xenopus embryos.  The candidate will also receive training in pedagogical techniques by participating in workshops and programs at UWW as well as one on one mentoring by the PI.  The candidate can also expect the PI to support their career goals in the form of publication of results, sharing of reagents and resources, transgenic lines, support for writing grant proposals and attendance at professional meetings.

Responsibilities:

Teaching responsibilities include introductory biology lecture and lab courses and developmental biology. Research expectations include supporting the PI’s grant research, publication of results, mentoring undergraduate research students, and writing grant proposals. All students, faculty, and staff are required to ensure their materials are digitally accessible and utilize standard technology platforms supported by UW-Whitewater. Examples include, but are not limited to, Navigate, Canvas, and Microsoft Office applications – including Outlook, which is essential for university email communications and scheduling.

Department Information:

The Biology department at the University of Wisconsin – Whitewater offers Bachelor’s degrees in Biology, with emphases in five areas: Cell/Physiology; Ecology, Evolution, and Behavior; Honors; Marine Biology and Freshwater Ecology; and Pre-Biomedical Professions. The Biology department has more than 300 majors and ~30 minors. We also serve the University by offering several general education courses and supporting the pre-health professions certificates in dental, medical, physician’s assistant, optometry, and veterinary medicine. Our department is particularly supportive of undergraduate research with dedicated research labs for each of our faculty members, and many of our students have presented their work at national and regional meetings. More information about the College of Letters and Science (https://www.uww.edu/cls) and the Biology department (https://www.uww.edu/cls/departments/biology) may be found at the included links.

Job Category:

Instructional and Media Designer

Job Duties:

The University of Wisconsin Oshkosh is seeking a collaborative and innovative Instructional Designer & Learning Technology Specialist to support the READY RURAL initiative. This position serves as the lead for instructional design, educational technology, digital learning, and multimedia development, partnering with faculty and subject matter experts to transform content into engaging, accessible, and workforce-focused learning experiences.

In this role, you will design and develop high-quality instructional materials for online, hybrid, face-to-face, simulation, mobile, and partner-based learning environments. You will create innovative learning resources that support rural healthcare education, including topics such as telehealth, virtual care, remote patient monitoring, behavioral health, home-based care, interprofessional practice, care coordination, and workforce readiness. The position also supports the development of stackable credentials, continuing education offerings, faculty development resources, and workforce training programs.

The successful candidate will provide consultation and support to faculty and staff on instructional technologies, digital learning tools, accessibility, and inclusive teaching practices. Responsibilities include developing multimedia resources such as instructional videos, simulations, interactive learning modules, digital toolkits, and tutorials, while ensuring all learning materials meet quality and accessibility standards.

This position also plays a key role in managing instructional design and media development projects by coordinating timelines, maintaining documentation and reusable resources, training faculty and project personnel on educational technologies, and supporting the collection and interpretation of data to continuously improve learning experiences and program effectiveness.

Universities of Wisconsin also offers an extremely competitive benefits package for 2026 that includes:

  • Health plans, currently starting at $45 per month.

  • 176 hours of vacation per year (prorated for start date).

  • 36 hours of personal holiday, and 9 legal holidays (prorated for start date).

  • 176 Hours of sick leave for first 18 months. After this period, employees can earn up to 96 hours per fiscal year. Accumulates without limit and does not expire.

  • Paid parental leave after six months of continuous employment.

  • Wisconsin Retirement System (pension) with 7.2% employer contribution for 2026.

All employment benefits are subject to change. A full list of current benefits and eligibility requirements can be found on our website.

This position is funded through the READY RURAL grant and is initially offered as a one-year fixed-term appointment. The appointment is renewable annually for up to four years, contingent upon continued grant funding, satisfactory performance, and program needs.

The Center for the Advancement of Teaching and Learning (CATL) is searching for an Instructional Designer to help our faculty thrive as educators in the era of AI and other advanced technologies.   • Advises and supports groups working on program-level curricular design and development by facilitating the work, and by contributing expertise in pedagogy/andragogy, instructional design, and learning technology. May also contribute subject matter expertise.

  • Designs, develops, and delivers faculty development and engagement programs and activities (e.g., Canvas-based courses, communities of practice, and grant programs related to faculty development, teaching and learning strategies, instructional modalities or contemporary issues, such as artificial intelligence)

POSITION SPECIFICS​

Housing and Food Services at Penn State is seeking a highly motivated Food Safety & Quality Assurance Specialist to lead and maintain comprehensive food safety, allergen management, food defense, and quality assurance programs supporting Penn State Bakery and Warehouse operations.


This position plays a critical role in ensuring products are safe, consistently produced, meet regulatory requirements, and exceed customer expectations. The successful candidate will collaborate closely with bakery production, warehouse operations, purchasing, and leadership teams to develop, implement, and continuously improve food safety and quality systems.


Key Responsibilities


Food Safety, Food Defense & Regulatory Compliance

  • Develop, implement, and maintain HACCP plans, Preventive Controls programs, and other food safety documentation.
  • Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local food safety regulations.
  • Establish and monitor Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs), sanitation standards, allergen controls, and food safety procedures.
  • Conduct routine food safety inspections and maintain required records and documentation.
  • Support regulatory inspections, third-party audits, and compliance reviews.
  • Monitor changes in food safety regulations and communicate impacts to operations.
  • Develop and maintain Food Defense and Food Security programs, including vulnerability assessments, access controls, visitor management, and mitigation strategies.
  • Coordinate food defense training and maintain food defense plans.

Quality Assurance & Product Compliance

  • Establish and maintain finished product specifications and quality standards.
  • Investigate quality concerns, perform root cause analyses, and oversee corrective actions.
  • Create, review, and maintain compliant product labels.
  • Verify ingredient statements, allergen declarations, nutritional information, and other required labeling elements.
  • Evaluate formulation, ingredient, supplier, and packaging changes for food safety, regulatory, and quality impacts.
  • Support new product launches and process improvements.

Allergen Management

  • Develop and oversee allergen control programs for Bakery and Warehouse operations.
  • Implement procedures to prevent allergen cross-contact.
  • Verify cleaning, sanitation, and product changeover procedures.
  • Collaborate with production teams to develop allergen-conscious scheduling practices.
  • Maintain ingredient specifications and allergen information within menu management systems.
  • Deliver allergen awareness training to employees.

Sanitation & Environmental Monitoring

  • Develop and monitor sanitation procedures, schedules, and verification programs.
  • Oversee environmental monitoring and testing activities.
  • Verify cleaning and sanitizing effectiveness for facilities, equipment, and food-contact surfaces.
  • Monitor temperature controls, cold chain management, and storage requirements.
  • Investigate temperature deviations and coordinate corrective actions.
  • Manage pest control programs and verify completion of preventive measures.

Auditing, Traceability & Recall Readiness

  • Develop audit schedules, inspection tools, and compliance tracking systems.
  • Conduct internal food safety and quality audits.
  • Maintain documentation required for regulatory compliance and audit readiness.
  • Develop and test traceability and recall programs.
  • Conduct mock recalls and evaluate system effectiveness.
  • Support product holds, recalls, investigations, and disposition decisions.

Supplier & Ingredient Quality

  • Support supplier evaluation and approval processes.
  • Review Certificates of Analysis (COAs), supplier documentation, specifications, and food safety records.
  • Monitor ingredient and packaging quality and resolve supplier quality concerns.
  • Coordinate corrective actions and supplier follow-up activities when necessary.

Training & Leadership Support

  • Develop and deliver food safety, quality, sanitation, allergen, and GMP training programs.
  • Maintain training records and support employee development.
  • Coach employees and supervisors on food safety and quality expectations.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert and resource for food safety and quality-related questions.
  • Provide operational and supervisory support for Bakery and Warehouse operations as needed.
  • Act as a liaison between quality assurance, production teams, warehouse operations, and leadership.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Food Science, Food Technology, Animal Science, Microbiology, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and four years of relevant experience.
  • ServSafe Certification.
  • Experience developing, implementing, and maintaining food safety and quality management systems.
  • Experience conducting audits and managing corrective and preventive action programs.
  • Knowledge of FSMA Preventive Controls for Human Food requirements.
  • Knowledge of food allergen regulations and labeling requirements.
  • Experience with food labeling, ingredient declarations, and nutritional compliance.
  • Strong analytical, documentation, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Ability to effectively train, coach, and influence employees at all levels.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate across production, warehouse, culinary, purchasing, and leadership teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • ServSafe Instructor Certification.
  • Preventive Controls Qualified Individual (PCQI) Certification.
  • Experience in bakery, food manufacturing, food production, or warehouse operations.
  • Experience with environmental monitoring, microbiological testing, and food defense programs.
  • Experience managing Certificates of Analysis (COAs) and supplier quality programs.

What You'll Bring

  • A passion for food safety and quality excellence.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Ability to balance regulatory compliance with operational effectiveness.
  • Commitment to continuous improvement and risk mitigation.
  • Leadership skills that foster accountability, collaboration, and employee engagement.

At Penn State Housing and Food Services, you'll have the opportunity to make a direct impact on food safety, quality, and customer satisfaction while supporting one of the nation's leading university dining programs. You'll work alongside dedicated professionals committed to innovation, operational excellence, and delivering exceptional products and services to the Penn State community

Bachelor's Degree
3+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience accepted

None

POSITION SPECIFICS​

The Penn State College of Medicine, Cancer Institute is seeking a Research Assistant in Hershey, PA.

 

Position Summary

The Research Assistant provides intermediate-level support for clinical and translational research projects within the Penn State Cancer Institute, with a primary focus on Genitourinary (GU) Oncology research. This position supports non-treatment interventional and observational studies through study coordination, protocol development, participant consent and enrollment, data management and analysis, regulatory compliance, scientific writing, and research administration. The role works closely with investigators, collaborators, and research staff to advance the GU research portfolio and ensure the successful execution of research initiatives.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

Research Study Support

  • Assist in the design, development, and implementation of GU research studies under the guidance of faculty investigators, including Dr. Joshi.
  • Develop study protocols and supporting research documentation.
  • Support the conduct of observational and non-treatment interventional studies, including participant recruitment, informed consent, enrollment, and follow-up.
  • Assist in the development and maintenance of an NGS data biobank to support GU research initiatives.

 

Data Management and Analysis

  • Collect, organize, manage, and analyze research data to support ongoing studies.
  • Ensure the accuracy, integrity, and reproducibility of research data and study records.
  • Prepare figures, tables, reports, and summaries of research findings.
  • Maintain electronic and paper research records and databases.
  • Support manuscript preparation, scientific reporting, and data presentation.

 

Regulatory and Project Coordination

  • Maintain study documentation and ensure compliance with institutional, IRB, and regulatory requirements.
  • Coordinate day-to-day research operations, project timelines, and study logistics.
  • Schedule meetings and serve as a liaison among investigators, collaborators, sponsors, and laboratory partners.
  • Track study milestones and support timely completion of research objectives.

 

Research Administration

  • Assist with grant proposal development and submission.
  • Support preparation of progress reports, abstracts, presentations, and scientific communications.
  • Process purchase requests, reimbursements, invoices, payroll documentation, and budget tracking.
  • Maintain certifications, protocols, regulatory files, and administrative records.

 

Collaboration and Process Improvement

  • Evaluate research workflows, troubleshoot issues, and recommend improvements to enhance efficiency and data quality.
  • Participate in GU research meetings, presenting project updates and contributing to scientific discussions.
  • Collaborate with faculty, research staff, students, and trainees by providing technical support, assisting with onboarding and training, and fostering a collaborative research environment.

POSITION SPECIFICS​

Working location will be fully on-site, located in State College, PA. This role requires periodic travel to remote locations.


We are searching for experienced and dedicated Electric Propulsion and Power Systems (EPPS) Engineers to join the Electrical Power and Control Systems (EPCS) Department within the Undersea Systems Office (USO) at the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) at Penn State. You will lead multidisciplinary engineering teams in project development of cutting edge electric and hybrid electric propulsion and power systems for undersea vehicles.  Specifically, you will oversee the detail design, documentation, integration, and testing of high-power electric propulsion motors and controllers for undersea propulsion applications along with overall vehicle power system design and control.  This will include laboratory and field testing for U.S. military and related applications.


ARL is an authorized DoD SkillBridge partner and welcomes all transitioning military members to apply.


You Will:


  • Participate in full project life cycle design and development to deliver advanced, efficient and reliable electric and hybrid electric propulsion systems and power sub-systems
  • Participate in system requirements identification, flow-down, and functional allocation followed by design reviews, design acceptance and documentation packages
  • Execute detailed design stages including early design concept development, market surveys, analysis of alternatives, draft interface control and functional design documents, and write test plans/reports.
  • Test EPPS subsystems including advanced hardware-in-the-loop test methods to support integration with larger systems of systems
  • Use an array of advanced laboratory equipment to demonstrate the design satisfies the identified requirements and expectations
  • Capture approved hardware designs using state of the art CAD tools
  • Participate in large scale system integration exercises and requirement verification stages
  • Support laboratory and field testing of prototype EPPS systems to demonstrate and validate the final design

Additional Responsibilities for Senior Professional and Higher-level Positions Include:


  • Conduct independent and collaborative research, development, testing, and evaluation activities to solve complex scientific and engineering challenges supporting Department of Defense sponsors and national security missions
  • Investigate, evaluate, and apply established and emerging engineering principles, scientific methodologies, and advanced technologies to develop innovative technical solutions
  • Plan, perform, and lead analytical studies, modeling and simulation, laboratory experimentation, field testing, and prototype demonstrations to validate engineering concepts and system performance
  • Design, develop, integrate, analyze, and evaluate complex hardware, software, embedded systems, sensors, communications systems, electromechanical systems, or other mission-critical technologies within assigned technical disciplines
  • Apply systems engineering principles throughout the project lifecycle, including requirements development, architecture definition, design trade studies, integration, verification, validation, risk management, and configuration management

Required Skills/Experience areas include:


  • Single-phase AC, three phase AC, and DC power systems
  • Power conversion systems such as motors and drives, alternators, rectifiers, and DC-DC converters.
  • Open and closed-loop control methods
  • Analog and digital circuit design
  • Demonstrated ability to work within an engineering team and lead a team of technicians
  • Be hands-on, exhibit a solid understanding of electronics and power concepts
  • Possess a proven ability to build, troubleshoot, and integrate hardware into larger, more complex systems

 

Additional Preferred Skills:

JOB DESCRIPTION AND POSITION REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Anthropology is seeking a part-time undergraduate research assistant. The student will be conducting lab-based experiments designed to measure a key parameter in an ongoing international research project on Australian bush tomato (Solanum diversiflorum, called wamula in Martu Wangka) foraging ecology.


At the core of the project is a Central Place Foraging model predicting when a hypothetical forager will process wamula near a harvesting patch before transporting it back to camp, rather than carrying unprocessed fruit in bulk. The model requires estimating the field processing threshold (z), the travel distance beyond which field processing increases the net rate of energy delivery to a central place. A critical variable is y₀, the edible fraction of an unprocessed load, here measured not by weight (which we have estimated from fieldwork) but by container volume: how much of a carrying container's capacity is usable edible fruit when packed with whole unprocessed wamula, and how much more capacity becomes available once the fruit are processed (seeds removed, halved, and stacked).


The student will be processing tomatillos (a close wamula analog), measuring the time it takes to process and the changes in load utility (amount of edible fruit) that processing provides.

POSITION SPECIFICS​

We are seeking an experienced Optical Systems Engineer to join our Electro-Optics and Electronics Division, located in Freeport, PA. This position will support our imaging and other electro-optical system development programs where you will work with a multi-disciplinary team of scientists and engineers performing a wide range of applied research and development projects involving sensors, lasers, and electro-optical (EO) technology. The mission of the Penn State Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) is to develop innovative solutions to challenging national problems in support of Navy, Department of Defense (DoD), and Intelligence Community research, engineering and technology needs. 

ARL is an authorized DoD SkillBridge partner and welcomes all transitioning military members to apply.

You will:

  • Be responsible for novel and complex optical designs from concept through deployment

  • Design and tolerance optical lens systems to meet performance requirements

  • Perform analysis to validate performance of optical systems – stray light, thermal, MTF, distortion, vignetting, etc.

  • Collaborate with other team members on: opto-mechanical designs, athermalization, imaging sensors, alignment, image processing, prototyping, test, analysis, and evaluation.

  • Support field-testing of imaging systems

  • Contribute to proposals, reports, and presentations

Additional responsibilities of the higher-level include:

  • Perform systems engineering, project planning, budgeting, and scheduling

  • Lead other engineers in day-to-day tasking to satisfy stakeholder’s requirements and expectations

  • Provide technical leadership within the department for imaging and EO programs and initiatives

  • Independently manage multiple and/or large electro-optic projects

  • Develop and propose solutions for new applications

  • Plan, organize, and lead field tests events

  • Perform the role of Trusted Agent to the government to assess and validate state-of-the art EO systems and solutions from the Defense Industrial Base

Required skills and experience include:

  • Proficient in design of optics for imaging applications including infrared

  • Substantial experience with optical design and analysis software (Zemax, CODE V, Trace Pro, FRED, etc.)

  • Knowledge of current coating and optics fabrication techniques and limitations

  • Strong knowledge of optical assembly and alignment methods

  • Good working knowledge of physics, electro-mechanical devices and imaging sensors

Preferred skills and experience include:

  • Design, analysis, and test of complete imaging systems

  • Knowledge of various focal plane arrays types, imaging sensors, camera specifications, and video interfaces

  • Real-time image processing

  • Radiometry (analysis and laboratory measurements), development of link budgets, prediction of sensor response, and image quality metrics

  • Microcontroller programming

  • Software tools for instrument control, data analysis, and image processing (LabVIEW, MATLAB, ImageJ, Python, Open CV, etc.)

  • Infrared systems design and performance test methods.

  • Developing and fielding optical systems for military applications

  • Laser systems

  • Specification and use of optical components such as dichroic filters, polarizers, beam splitters, lasers, fast steering mirrors, and shutters

POSITION SPECIFICS​

The Office of Physical Plant (OPP) is an organization driven by its mission to “Provide Excellent Facilities Services for Penn State.” 

 

OPP is seeking an experienced Facilities Automation Systems Administrator Supervisor to lead the administration, maintenance, security, integration, and lifecycle management of facility automation systems supporting critical University facilities. 

 

Reporting to the Manager, Operational Technology Infrastructure and Security, this position provides technical leadership for facilities automation systems and supervises a team of Facilities Automation Systems Administrators.

 

This position offers a flexible work arrangement that combines remote and on-campus work. Questions related to flexible work should be directed to the hiring manager during the interview process.

 

The successful candidate will establish priorities, coordinate daily work, develop staff capability, and ensure that automation systems are secure, reliable, resilient, and aligned with University requirements. 

 

Technical Responsibilities 

  • Administer and support BAS, Environmental Control Systems, LMS, SCADA platforms, servers, databases, controllers, field devices, and related OT infrastructure. 
  • Administer and troubleshoot virtualization, storage, backup, and network environments supporting OT systems, including Proxmox VE, VMware vSphere/ESXi, Veeam, NetApp, and Juniper technologies. 
  • Management of Windows and Linux Operating Systems. 
  • Support Automated Logic/ALC and Johnson Controls systems, including supervisory workstations 
  • Monitor system/infrastructure performance, communications, alarms, trends, and operational data; identify anomalies and improve reliability. 
  • Design, maintain, and troubleshoot integrations among BAS, SCADA, LMS, energy management, maintenance management, and enterprise systems. 
  • Support BACnet/IP, BACnet MS/TP, Modbus TCP/RTU, SNMP, REST/API integrations, serial communications, and related protocols. 
  • Maintain OT infrastructure; DNS, DHCP, NTP, secure remote access, gateways, and protocol-conversion technologies. 
  • Develop standards for configuration, capacity planning, performance tuning, backup and recovery, business continuity, asset inventories, and infrastructure lifecycle management. 
  • Evaluate, test, validate, and deploy software, firmware, operating-system, and application updates through formal change-control processes. 
  • Diagnose complex hardware, software, networking, communications, and control-system issues. 
  • Coordinate incident response, outage recovery, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and system-health assessments. 
  • Maintain system architectures, network diagrams, configuration baselines, procedures, maintenance schedules, recovery plans, and other technical documentation. 
  • Support alignment with NIST SP 800-82, ISA/IEC 62443, University policies, and applicable safety, environmental, laboratory, and security requirements. 
  • Participate in commissioning, acceptance testing, inspections, audits, upgrades, and project implementation activities. 

 

Leadership/Supervisory  

  • Supervise a team of Facilities Automation Systems Administrators, including assigning work, establishing priorities, reviewing performance, coaching staff, supporting professional development, and participating in hiring and onboarding. 
  • Promote cross-training, knowledge sharing, consistent work practices, accountability, and a customer-focused culture. 
  • Collaborate with Facilities Operations, Operational Technology, Information Technology, Information Security, vendors, consultants, project teams, and campus stakeholders. 
  • Communicate technical information clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences. 

 

Preferred Skills and Knowledge 

  • Proficiency in Windows and Linux environments. 
  • Comprehensive knowledge of BAS, SCADA, and OT infrastructure. 
  • Familiarity with Proxmox, VMware, Veeam, NetApp, Juniper, Automated Logic/ALC, Johnson Controls, BACnet, Modbus, OPC UA, MQTT, and SNMP. 
  • Understanding of OT environments and their differences from traditional IT environments, including availability, safety, deterministic communications, long equipment lifecycles, vendor dependencies, and change-management risks. 
  • Knowledge of virtualization, storage, backup and recovery, network administration, cybersecurity, system integration, and infrastructure monitoring. 
  • Strong troubleshooting, documentation, analytical, organizational, and project-coordination skills. 
  • Demonstrated ability to supervise, coach, mentor, and develop technical staff. 
  • Experience in higher education, healthcare, research, laboratory, or large-scale facilities operations preferred.

6+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience accepted

JOB DESCRIPTION AND POSITION REQUIREMENTS

The Department of Health Policy and Administration in the College of Health and Human Development is seeking applicants for part-time job of Research Assistant- Health Services Research (Long-Term Care)


Position Description

The Department of Health Policy and Administration in the College of Health and Human Development at Pennsylvania State University is seeking a part-time Research Assistant to work with Dr. Jess Williams on a program of research examining Total Worker Health® (TWH) adoption and implementation in nursing homes. This NIOSH-funded project (Implementation of Total Worker Health® in Nursing Homes) has two aims: (1) assessing organizational factors — such as chain membership and community resources — that influence TWH adoption in nursing homes in Federal Region VII, using survey data linked with Medicare data; and (2) using in-depth interviews with Directors of Nursing to examine the decisional processes, competing priorities, and cultural factors that shape TWH implementation.

This position offers an excellent opportunity for a postdoctoral scholar interested in long-term care, health services research, and occupational health policy to develop an independent research trajectory while contributing to an active, externally funded project. The appointment is part-time and may be well suited to a candidate balancing another academic appointment, clinical role, or research position.


Responsibilities

  • Conduct quantitative statistical analyses of survey and Medicare claims/administrative data, primarily in Stata (R also acceptable), including data management, cleaning, and merging of complex datasets.
  • Support qualitative data analysis of interview transcripts with Directors of Nursing, including coding, theme development, and interpretation (training provided as needed).
  • Conduct literature reviews and synthesize prior research to inform manuscript introductions, discussion sections, and grant proposals.
  • Co-author and lead the drafting of peer-reviewed manuscripts, conference abstracts, and presentations reporting project findings.
  • Contribute to the preparation of research reports, dissemination materials, and stakeholder communications for academic and nursing home industry audiences.
  • Assist with the preparation of grant proposals and progress reports as opportunities arise.
  • Participate in regular research meetings with the PI and project team.

 

Required Qualifications and Experience

The following are required for this position:

  • In progress or earned Ph.D. in Health Policy, Health Services Research, Public Health, Gerontology, Health Economics, or a closely related field.
  • Demonstrated experience with statistical programming and quantitative data analysis (Stata strongly preferred; R acceptable).
  • Strong written communication skills, with experience contributing to peer-reviewed manuscripts.
  • Experience conducting literature reviews.

 

Preferred Experience

Experience in one or more of the following areas is strongly preferred:

  • Research related to long-term care, nursing homes, aging services, or occupational health and safety.
  • Experience with Medicare claims data or other large administrative/secondary datasets.
  • Qualitative data coding and analysis of interview transcripts (e.g., using NVivo, Atlas.ti, or comparable software).
  • Experience preparing or contributing to federal grant applications (e.g., NIH, NIOSH, AHRQ).

 

Application Materials

To be considered for this position, applicants must submit:

  • A cover letter describing their research experience and interest in occupational and health policy research.
  • A current Curriculum Vitae (CV).
  • Contact information for two professional references.

 

This is a part-time (50% FTE), limited-term position located at Penn State University Park and is funded until 8/31/2027.


Compensation:

The hourly rate for this job is $35.00

POSITION SPECIFICS​

Penn State Information Technology (PSIT) is seeking a Business Intelligence Specialist to serve as a member of a Data Analytics/Reporting Team, supporting both the SIMBA organization and the LionPATH Development and Maintenance Organization (LDMO).

The successful candidate will serve as a Business Intelligence Specialist, providing data extraction, report development, analysis, and recommended design of analytics applications, data models, and reporting solutions to meet complex operational, financial, student, and other institutional reporting requirements.

This role requires experience with two major enterprise systems supporting the University: SAP (used by SIMBA) and PeopleSoft Campus Solutions (used by the LDMO as the University’s Student Information System).

The individual will work across a range of analytics and reporting platforms, data modeling environments, and enterprise data sources. Responsibilities include developing and supporting reports, queries, dashboards, datasets, and semantic data models; integrating enterprise-level data into appropriate reporting tools; and collaborating with functional business partners to design analytical solutions that support strategic and operational objectives.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Design, implement, and maintain complex data models and business intelligence solutions, ensuring efficient access methods, performance optimization, data organization, security, and documentation.
  • Develop and enhance reports, queries, dashboards, datasets, and data transformations using modern business intelligence and analytics tools and delivered system functionality.
  • Analyze business processes, data structures, and source systems to identify optimal data sources and reporting strategies.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders and end users to translate business needs into technical specifications and analytics solutions.
  • Provide business intelligence support by defining system scope and objectives, preparing detailed design specifications, and developing or modifying analytics applications accordingly.
  • Manage solution design, data extraction, data modeling, testing, debugging, and related end-user documentation.
  • Promote adherence to data governance, development standards, and documentation practices.
  • Troubleshoot and collaborate to resolve data issues to ensure accuracy, consistency, and reliability in reporting outputs.
  • Learn and apply new analytics technologies and techniques in support of evolving business needs.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • Demonstrated experience as a data analyst, business intelligence developer, solutions architect, or in a similar role.
  • Experience developing reports, queries, dashboards, and data models in business intelligence platforms.
  • Experience working with SAP (SIMBA) and PeopleSoft Campus Solutions (LionPATH), including strong proficiency with PeopleSoft’s PSQuery tool.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Ability to learn new technologies quickly and work effectively in a dynamic team environment.
  • Candidate must be a US Citizen to apply.

Preferred

  • Understanding of accounting principles, financial and student data concepts, and enterprise administrative processes, including how transactional data supports reporting and analytics.
  • Experience working with enterprise data warehousing, semantic modeling, or modern analytics architecture.
  • Experience integrating and modeling data from multiple administrative or operational systems.
  • Experience supporting reporting and analytics in higher education or similarly complex organizations.
  • Experience using AI-powered tools or techniques in analytics, reporting, automation, data modeling, or solution design.

This role supports Penn State’s research mission by designing, operating, automating, and optimizing the GPU and AI and computing infrastructure used by researchers across the university, along with the high-performance computing systems that support it.  

The position will be filled at the Reserach Computing Systems Engineer - Advanced Professional level.

Candidates must be U.S. citizens due to specific access requirements associated with this position. 

 

This position is ideal for an engineer who enjoys building reliable, scalable systems for machine learning, data-intensive research, and advanced computing workloads. The successful candidate will work across GPU systems, HPC platforms, storage, networking, automation, and user-facing research workflows to enable cutting-edge research in AI, simulation, and computational science. 

 

Work Arrangement: This is a full-time position, which will report to the Research HPC Manager and requires on-site work at University Park and is not supportive of remote work.   

 

Responsibilities: As part of a collaborative engineering team, you’ll contribute across a broad range of responsibilities that include the following: 

  • Collaborate with teammates, users, and vendor support to diagnose issues and implement solutions across compute, storage, networking, and software environments.

  • Monitor, maintain, automate, and improve AI and HPC systems and supporting infrastructure.

  • Design, deploy, operate, troubleshoot, and optimize systems using DevOps and infrastructure-as-code practices.

  • Support GPU-accelerated computing environments for AI, machine learning, and scientific workloads.

  • Partner with researchers and ICDS staff to understand workload requirements and develop practical engineering solutions for system configuration, performance, and research workflows.

  • Support security, logging, documentation, and compliance process for the systems we operate, including environments subject to federal research security.

  • Contribute to planning, requirements gathering, process improvement, and operational readiness for new services and infrastructure.

  • Provide timely updates to system documentation and respond to user questions with clear, actionable guidance.

  • Evaluate and improve tools, platforms, and workflows that support AI model development, training, inference, and data movement at scale. 

 

Required qualifications and skills include the following: 

  • Administration of multi-GPU nodes at scale, including driver and firmware lifecycle management, NVLink/NVSwitch topology validation, GPU health monitoring and tuning for multi-GPU or multi-node GPU workloads.

  • Ability to work effectively in a Linux environment, including command-line tools, file editing, POSIX permissions, and system configuration.

  • Strong scripting ability in Bash and Python.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to debug complex systems.Ability to work collaboratively as part of a technical team.Experience using AI tools or AI agents to improve programming, debugging, development, or prototyping workflows.

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills.

 

Preferred qualifications:

Experience with one or more of the following is helpful but not required:

 

AI and HPC Workloads  

  • Experience supporting AI/ML infrastructure, including environments used for model training, inference, experiment workflows, and large-scale data processing.

  • Experience with job schedulers such as Slurm, PBS, HTCondor, or LSF.

  • Software development experience and familiarity with HPC programming environments such as C/C++, Fortran, CUDA, MPI, or OpenMP.  

 

Infrastructure and Automation  

  • DevOps experience, including Git-based workflows, CI/CD, automation, and collaborative development practices.

  • Experience with system deployment tools such as xCAT, Warewulf, OpenCHAMI, OpenStack/Bifrost, or MAAS.

  • Experience administering or supporting Kubernetes.

  • Experience with virtualization and containerization technologies such as VMware, Docker, Apptainer, or Podman.  

 

Networking and Storage  

  • Networking experience, including EVPN, BGP, and IPv6.

  • Experience with high-speed interconnects such as InfiniBand, HPE Slingshot, or similar HPC fabrics.

  • Experience with HPC or distributed storage systems such as GPFS, Lustre, Ceph, or VAST.  

 

Observability and Security  

  • Monitoring and observability experience with tools such as Grafana, Graphite, Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics, or InfluxDB.

  • Experience with databases such as MySQL/MariaDB or PostgreSQL.

  • Security experience including identity and access management, single sign-on, and LDAP/Active Directory.  

 

Background and Process  

  • Familiarity with Agile project development.

  • Prior experience in academic research computing, research data infrastructure, or large-scale shared computing environments.

  • A cover letter expressing the candidate’s interest in the role 
  • A current Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume

At ICDS, you’ll build and support infrastructure that enables advanced research in artificial intelligence, machine learning, simulation, data science, and computationally intensive discovery. You’ll work on clusters, storage and GPU systems Penn State researchers rely on for AI, machine learning and computational research. You won’t own a narrow slice of that. Our engineers work across provisioning, scheduling, storage, networking, GPU infrastructure and user-facing tooling. You'll debug problems from a user’s job submission all the way down to drivers and system firmware, and you’ll learn a lot on the way.  

 

You'll also be close to the science. You’ll talk to the people running the workloads, understand what they’re trying to accomplish, and engineer systems around actual research needs rather than requirements handed down from somewhere else.  It’s a collaborative team, and the problems are rarely the same twice.

POSITION SPECIFICS​

The Materials Research Institute (MRI) at Penn State University seeks an Applications Developer to develop user-facing software for a new Programmable Cloud Laboratory initiative funded by the National Science Foundation.

This position will be filled at the Applications Developer - Advanced Professional OR Senior Professional level.

The initiative will build upon existing scientific instrumentation and research infrastructure in MRI core facilities to provide researchers with secure remote access to experimental capabilities, data, and AI-enabled tools.

The Applications Developer will develop the Cloud Lab Command Center and related web-based applications through which researchers interact with the facility. The Command Center will provide an integrated suite of tools for learning about instrument capabilities, configuring and submitting workflows, monitoring progress, viewing data as it is generated, analyzing results, and collaborating with other researchers. The position has a strong front-end focus, requiring close collaboration with scientists, facility staff, and backend developers to translate complex experimental processes into intuitive, reliable, and accessible digital experiences.

This is a hands-on development role with ownership of features and product outcomes. As an early member of the Cloud Lab development team, the developer will contribute to software development practices, design standards, and release processes. The successful candidate will be comfortable working in an evolving research environment, learning new technologies as needed, and balancing rapid iteration with the reliability, security, and maintainability expected of a national research resource.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, test, and maintain responsive web applications for the Cloud Lab Command Center.
  • Build interfaces for experiment design, workflow configuration, collaboration, and reporting.
  • Develop reusable, accessible, and well-documented UI components.
  • Gather requirements and optimize user experiences through collaboration with researchers, facility staff, and software developers.
  • Use user feedback and iterative development practices to refine features and improve usability.
  • Work closely with backend developers to integrate front-end applications with APIs and data services.
  • Consume REST APIs and real-time data streams to provide timely information and updates.
  • Support application troubleshooting, quality assurance, and release activities.

Technical Environment 

  • JavaScript and TypeScript 

  • React and modern component-based frameworks 

  • HTML5, CSS3, and responsive design 

  • State management and front-end testing frameworks 

  • REST APIs and WebSocket-based integrations 

  • Git and collaborative development workflows 

  • Python 

  • Data visualization libraries 

  • Docker and containerized environments 

  • Scientific applications or research software 

  • AI-enabled tools and scientific data platforms 

Successful candidates will have demonstrated strong problem-solving, communication and collaboration skills and have extensive experience developing rich, interactive web applications and dashboards using JavaScript/TypeScript and React or comparable frameworks, data visualization libraries, implementation of responsive design, web-based data services, and REST APIs for interactive web applications and dashboards.

Preferred Skills and Experience: It is strongly preferred that successful candidates have experience with one or more of the following:

  • Familiarity with front-end testing frameworks and automated testing practices. UX/UI principles and user-centered design.
  • Agile or iterative software-development environments.
  • Familiarity with scientific software, research environments, or laboratory systems is a plus but not required. 

 

Application Instructions: To apply, applicants should upload a cover letter detailing their qualifications for and interest in the position, their resume, and names and contact details (e-mail addresses and telephone numbers) for three professional references. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.

POSITION SPECIFICS​

We are seeking a Research Computing Software Engineer to join the Visualization and Decision Support Division (VDS) of the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) at Penn State.  You will work within classified research and development and cloud computing (HPC) environments to develop and maintain software solutions to support the computational and data analysis needs of the research community; design, code, test, and optimize software systems that enhance research capabilities and streamline computational workflows.  The mission of VDS is to research, develop, and apply technical innovations that provide Decision Advantage to our sponsors through the use of data science, artificial intelligence, simulation, knowledge communication and virtual collaboration technologies. In this role, you will direct a team of engineers and researchers to fulfill this mission. 

The position will be located in either State College, PA or Reston, VA and is not eligible for remote work.

ARL is an authorized DoD SkillBridge partner and welcomes all transitioning military members to apply.

You will:

  • Develop, deploy, enhance, and maintain software applications and tools to support research computing needs
  • Implement efficient algorithms and data structures to handle large datasets and complex computations
  • Write clean, well-documented, and maintainable code using modern programming languages
  • Integrate software solutions with existing research computing infrastructure, including cloud platforms
  • Collaborate with other engineers and researchers to ensure seamless integration and functionality of software tools within the research environment
  • Analyze and optimize the performance of software applications, ensuring they meet the high demands of computational research
  • Identify and address performance bottlenecks, memory usage issues, and other technical challenges
  • Provide technical support and troubleshooting for software issues, assisting researchers in overcoming obstacles
  • Create and maintain comprehensive documentation for software tools, including user guides, technical specifications, and troubleshooting procedures
  • Stay up to date with advancements in software engineering and computational research technologies

Additional responsibilities of higher level positions include:

  • Propose and implement new features, improvements, and updates to enhance the functionality and usability of software tools
  • Lead or participate in software development projects, including planning, development, testing, and deployment phases
  • Manage project timelines, deliverables, and milestones to ensure successful and timely completion of software initiatives
  • May supervise staff members, including hiring, development, and performance management

Required skills and/or experience include:

  • Code analysis
  • Cross-team collaboration
  • Data Analysis
  • Presentation Skills
  • Programming
  • Software architecture
  • Software development
  • Software testing
  • Technology acumen
  • Trend analysis

Preferred skills/experience areas include:

  • Active or recently active TS/SCI clearance
  • A Master's degree in Geography is preferred

Your work location will be fully on-site located in State College, PA or Reston, VA.
