description:
The Opportunity

Help connect sports, research, and student learning as Cornell’s Sports AI and Analytics Project Associate. In this role, you will coordinate projects, partnerships, and programming that bring together faculty, students, Cornell Athletics, alumni, and external partners to expand hands-on research opportunities and advance the use of data science and artificial intelligence to address real-world challenges in sports.

 

As the Sports AI and Analytics Project Associate, you will:

  • Support the development, administration, and coordination of Cornell’s Sports AI and Analytics initiative. Assist with program planning, implementation, assessment, and continuous improvement in collaboration with faculty, students, Cornell Athletics, alumni, and external partners.
  • Coordinate project activities by facilitating communication among faculty, students, Cornell Athletics, and external partners; connecting students with research opportunities and datasets; tracking project activities; and supporting the implementation of applied research projects in sports analytics, data science, machine learning, and artificial intelligence.
  • Plan and coordinate conferences, workshops, meetings, and other program activities, including registration, scheduling, facilities, catering, technology, travel, and related logistics. Monitor programs and events, resolve issues, ensure compliance with university policies, and manage event budgets.
  • Coordinate program communications, reports, presentations, promotional materials, websites, and other digital resources. Support the dissemination of research through conferences, publications, and other academic and industry forums.
  • Coordinate administrative and logistical support for grant submissions, sponsorship activities, alumni engagement initiatives, and other external funding efforts. Develop and maintain relationships with internal and external stakeholders to support research, programming, and program growth.
  • Manage program budgets, accounts, expenses, and financial reporting.
  • Develop, create, and maintain databases and tracking systems to meet program needs. Track, gather, and report program statistics, including participation, research activity, partnerships, events, and program outcomes.
  • Evaluate program effectiveness and identify opportunities for future development. Collect, compile, and analyze program metrics and stakeholder feedback to support assessment, reporting, and future planning.
  • Recruit, train, and supervise temporary and student employees as needed.
  • Support the initiative’s broader goals of expanding student research opportunities, strengthening partnerships with Cornell Athletics, and advancing Cornell’s leadership in Sports AI and Analytics.
  • Oversee website maintenance, ensuring that information about contacts, policies and regulations, resources, events, and other program matters remains accurate and current.

 

About Cornell Ann S. Bowers College of Computing and Information Science

Cornell Ann S. Bowers College of Computing and Information Science is a college founded in recognition that computing is an essential tool in almost every scientific and scholarly discipline. It is a community of people committed to tackling some of the world's biggest challenges by working together across multiple colleges and two Cornell campuses. Bowers CIS is home to the three academic departments that power the information economy: Computer Science, Information Science and Statistics and Data Science. It is known for bold new ideas expressed in high-impact research and scholarship, inspiring educational contributions, and entrepreneurial and commercial engagement. The synergies among faculty, researchers and students make Bowers CIS more than the sum of its parts.


About the Statistics and Data Science Department

Statistics and Data Science (SDS) is a joint department with three participating colleges including ILR, CALS and Bowers CIS as the lead dean. The department combines the traditional tools of statistics, a solid foundation in probability theory, and the skills of computer science into a single, radically collaborative department. The department offers undergraduate degrees in Biometry through CALS and Statistics and Statistical Science through the College of Arts and Sciences, and also has a Master of Applied Statistics and a PhD graduate degree program. It is also closely associated with and oversees the Cornell Statistical Consulting Unit.

 

Cornell University is home to exceptional research across many disciplines related to sports, data science, analytics, and artificial intelligence. However, much of this work is currently distributed across different colleges and departments. Our vision is to create a centralized platform that showcases and connects sports-related research activities across the entire university, highlighting Cornell’s leadership in Sports AI and Analytics.

 

We aim to build strong partnerships with Cornell coaches and athletic teams to identify real-world challenges and develop research projects that contribute directly to athletic success. Through these collaborations, students gain access to authentic datasets and meaningful problems to solve, while coaches benefit from innovative, data-driven insights and solutions tailored to their needs.

 

A key objective of this initiative is to create a sustainable pipeline of research opportunities for students. Sports naturally inspire engagement and enthusiasm, making them an ideal gateway for students to deepen their expertise in data science, applied statistics, machine learning, and sports analytics while working on impactful projects.

 

Success Factors

You’ll thrive in this role if you demonstrate:

  • Proactive project coordination: You establish clear timelines and responsibilities, track progress, address obstacles, and keep collaborators informed to move projects from opportunity to completion.
  • Relationship building and collaboration: You build trust across academic and athletic settings, understand stakeholders’ needs, and connect students with meaningful research opportunities, faculty guidance, and datasets.
  • Strong organization and attention to detail: You coordinate well-run events, maintain accurate communications and records, and manage budgets and grant logistics reliably.
  • A commitment to continuous improvement: You use tracking systems, program metrics, and stakeholder feedback to assess results, inform priorities, and support program growth.

 

Hours, Location, and Appointment

This part-time position is based on Cornell’s Ithaca campus, with office and lab space in the new Computing and Information Science Building. Onsite presence is important for building relationships and launching projects with students, faculty, and Cornell Athletics staff. Some work may be performed remotely, with greater flexibility as projects become established, in coordination with the supervisor.

 

The position is 20 hours per week, generally Monday through Friday. Scheduling flexibility is needed to accommodate student availability, including student-athletes, with occasional evening or weekend meetings.

 

This is a term appointment through May 26, 2028, with possible renewal depending on available funding and performance.

 

What We Need

  • A cover letter and resume outlining your interest and how your experience and goals align with the potential for mutual success in the role are required for consideration.
  • Bachelor’s Degree and 2 to 4 years relevant experience or equivalent combination
  • Highly organized and excellent time management
  • Strong attention to detail
  • Excellent written and verbal communication
  • High level of initiative
  • Ability to cultivate and develop inclusive working relationships with students, faculty, staff, and community members. 
  • Knowledge of a University sports ecosystem

If you have all those things, great! We have a few more things that we would prefer you to have, but it’s ok if you don’t.


  • Ability to explain complex statistical models to non-technical stakeholders like coaches and players.
  • Demonstrated background managing multi-faceted technical projects, preferably within a high-performance sports or academic setting

Rewards and Benefits

  • This position is 20 hours per week, generally Monday through Friday, with scheduling flexibility needed to accommodate student availability, including student-athletes, and occasional evening or weekend meetings.
  • This position is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement, and employees typically perform this role in a hybrid format. The university reserves the right to modify, suspend, revoke, or terminate the hybrid work arrangement at any time.
  • Cornell receives national recognition as an award-winning workplace for our health, wellbeing, and sustainability.
  • Our benefits programs include comprehensive health care options, generous retirement contributions, access to wellness programs, and employee discounts with local and national retail brands. We invite you to follow this link to get more information about our benefits: Understand Your Benefits | Working at Cornell.
  • Our leave provisions include health and personal leave, three weeks of vacation and 13 holidays: Martin Luther King, Jr. Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, and an end of the year winter break from December 25-January 1. To offer greater flexibility for observing faiths and traditions we also offer two additional floating holidays. Learn more about our generous leave provisions: Holiday and Accrued Time Off | Working at Cornell
  • Cornell's impressive educational benefits include tuition-free Extramural Study and Employee Degree Program, tuition aid for external education, and Cornell Children's Tuition Assistance Program. Learn more about our extensive educational benefits: Education Benefits | Working at Cornell

Its name CEMI is said as “See Me” because the focus is on you: the people who use Cornell’s systems and data to accomplish your goals.

 

CEMI Donor Engagement and Experience Project (DEEP) is a major, multi-year effort to modernize and unify development and engagement technology across Cornell’s Ithaca and Cornell Tech campuses, Weill Cornell Medicine (WCM), and the Lab of Ornithology.

 

What will you do:

 

The CEMI Salesforce Platform Developer plays a critical role within the Cornell Enterprise Modernization Initiative (CEMI), with primary responsibility supporting Enterprise Salesforce Operations across Cornell's growing portfolio of Salesforce solutions.  A multi‑year effort to modernize and unify Salesforce technology across Cornell University campuses, including Ithaca, Cornell Tech, Weill Cornell Medicine (WCM), and Weill Cornell Medicine.

In collaboration with these partners, the developer supports and creates Salesforce solutions by interpreting stakeholder needs into scalable and supportable solutions, all while ensuring alignment with enterprise architecture, security standards, and business requirements.

Working Title: ETL Developer (CEMI) [Remote] [2 Year Term]

 

No Visa Sponsorship is available for this position.

 

This position will require occasional off-hours support.

 

This is a 2 year term appointment which may be ended or extended based on organizational needs, funding availability, and performance.

 

This position is eligible for remote work within the United States, subject to Cornell University's approval process for out-of-state work arrangements and all applicable legal and operational requirements. Candidates must be able to travel to Cornell's Ithaca campus periodically for meetings, training, and other business needs. The university reserves the right to modify or discontinue remote work arrangements as business needs require.

 

About Information Technology

 

Information Technology (IT) is a strategic enabler for many functions at Cornell University, with staff located across colleges, administrative units, and campuses throughout the institution. While comprised of many organizations, IT operates as one partnering closely with faculty, staff, and students to support teaching, research, and business operations. By being embedded where the Cornell community is, IT is well positioned to provide support ranging from day‑to‑day needs to large, complex initiatives that advance major academic, research, and operational objectives across the university. Check out this link to find out more about IT@Cornell


What will you do:

 

As a member of Cornell Information Technologies’ Data Warehousing and Integrations team, the ETL Developer is a member of a team who develops and supports robust, reliable, and standardized data solutions in support of Cornell’s data analytic, data warehousing and data lake ecosystem. This is an area of rapid change where the ETL Developer is expected to learn and apply new technical skills on an ongoing basis. The ETL Developer will work daily with customers and colleagues to develop and support a vast data environment.  


Primary Responsibilities include:

 

  • Work collaboratively with customers and IT team members to develop new data lake/data warehouse content that is enterprise grade and supportable
  • Proactively support the many data feeds, transformations, and updates which make up Cornell’s Data Lake / Data Warehouse (DL/DW) ecosystem
  • Act as a DL/DW liaison, and subject matter expert, to project teams requesting DL/DW resources
  • Research and conduct impact analysis of changing schema and data model requirements
  • Develop and maintain documentation and standard operating procedures
  • Support the migration of ETL code and database objects
  • Learn new tools and environments quickly as the data analytics space evolves
  • Participate in the 24X7 DL/DW On Call support rotation

 

While position responsibilities vary, every member of our community is expected to foster a culture of belonging and a healthy work environment by communicating across differences; being cooperative, collaborative, open, and welcoming; showing respect, compassion, and empathy; engaging and supporting others regardless of background or perspective; speaking up when others are being excluded or treated inappropriately; and supporting work/life integration of oneself and others.

 

Required Qualifications:

 

  • Bachelor’s degree with 3–5 years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Demonstrated experience using SQL, including Data Definition Language (DDL) and Data Manipulation Language (DML).
  • Development experience working with relational database platforms such as PostgreSQL, Oracle, or Microsoft SQL Server.
  • Proven experience developing data transformation solutions using one or more programming languages.
  • One to two years of related experience in at least two of the following areas:
    • Data analysis
    • Data warehouse or data lake design and construction
    • ETL development
  • Strong interest in and aptitude for becoming highly proficient in a rapidly evolving technical and analytical environment.
  • Strong development skills, including the ability to quickly understand functional requirements and efficiently apply technical solutions to achieve desired outcomes.
  • Demonstrated success working in a fast‑paced IT or business environment that requires continual learning and adaptation.
  • Proven problem‑solving skills and ability to independently develop technical expertise.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to multitask and work collaboratively in a team‑oriented environment.
  • Ability to cultivate and develop inclusive working relationships with students, faculty, staff, and community members. 

Preferred Qualifications: 


  • Experience developing and supporting data transformations using an ETL product such as: Informatica, Data Stage, WhereScape, Talend, etc.
  • Experience with a database procedural language
  • Experience with Python
  • Understanding of dimensional data modeling concepts
  • Experience with cloud services, such as AWS (S3, Redshift, Glue, Athena, RDS, EMR)

  • No Relocation assistance will be provided for this position.

description:
The Cornell Center for Materials Research (CCMR) has an immediate opening for a Surface Analysis Research Specialist (job class Research Support Specialist III). This position serves as a vital member of CCMR’s team of experts supporting fundamental materials research in our core facility on the Ithaca campus. CCMR encourages applications from individuals who have the skills and desire to enable cutting-edge research and train the next generation of researchers.

The successful candidate will bring advanced training in a relevant discipline (e.g., materials science, physical science, or engineering) and experience with X-ray photoemission spectroscopy and related surface analysis techniques. A self-motivated work ethic along with excellent communications and interpersonal skills will be critical to success in this role. The position is ideal for someone who enjoys collaborating with others and who can adeptly operate scientific instrumentation, optimize sample analyses, and prioritize multiple, changing tasks.

The Role
As Surface Analysis Research Specialist, you will directly support surface analysis techniques, primarily XPS (Xray photoemission spectroscopy) and profilometry, but also other techniques such as electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, spectroscopy, or focused ion beam. You will develop analytical techniques, find creative solutions to research requests, and upgrade and troubleshoot instrumentation. Along with other team members, you will work closely with facility users to plan measurements and provide hands-on training.


Key responsibilities will include:

  • Training researchers on safe and proper use of moderately complex instrumentation, ensuring acquisition of high-quality data
  • Developing new protocols and procedures in XPS, electron microscopy, scanned probe microscopy, confocal microscopy, and more.
  • Performing analyses for off-campus users and compiling research summary reports
  • Developing instrument use (standard operating procedures) and lab safety protocols
  • Documenting and disseminating procedures via training sessions, online documentation, and video tutorials
  • Working with instrument vendors to improve or update instrument capabilities
  • Monitoring records of equipment usage and maintenance for accounting, safety, and billing purposes
  • Performing routine preventative maintenance tasks and procuring inventory, supplies, and maintenance items


As part of the Cornell community, you will help foster a culture of belonging and a healthy work environment by communicating across differences; being cooperative, collaborative, open, and welcoming; showing respect, compassion, and empathy; engaging and supporting others regardless of background or perspective; speaking up when others are being excluded or treated inappropriately; and supporting work/life integration of oneself and others.

 

About Us
The Cornell Center for Materials Research (CCMR) supports fundamental materials research and serves students, scientists, and researchers from Cornell and other academic, government, or industry researchers from around the world. This vibrant and active facility of shared instrumentation is overseen by expert facility staff who maintain instruments, train the next generation of materials researchers, and analyze samples as a service for offsite customers.


What We Need
Send us a cover letter and resume outlining your interest in this position and explaining how your experience and qualifications match the position requirements. Your letter is an important component of your application. Note: Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.


When evaluating your candidacy, we will look for evidence of the following:

  • Master’s degree in materials science, physical science, engineering, or similar discipline and 3–5 years’ experience with XPS (x-ray photoemission spectroscopy) and related surface analysis techniques, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience 
  • Demonstrated strong work ethic and self-motivation
  • Ability to work independently as well as collaborate effectively with others
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
  • Desire to enable cutting-edge research and train the next generation of researchers
  • Excellent computer skills and proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
  • Ability to cultivate and develop inclusive and equitable working relationships with students, faculty, staff, and community members 


Additionally, although not required, we would like to see clear evidence of:

  • Ph.D. in materials science, physical science, engineering, or similar discipline
  • Experience with atomic force microscopy and related techniques, such as force imaging, piezo-force microscopy, electric-force microscopy, or magnetic force microscopy
  • Strong organizational skills and supervisory experience

  • This position is located in Ithaca, New York on the campus of Cornell University. Cornell receives national recognition as an award-winning workplace for our health, wellbeing, and sustainability.

title: Local Government Project (LGP) Temporary Research Specialist - Cornell Law School and the Cornell Jeb E. Brooks School of Public Policy
description:
Law School is a globally recognized institution known for excellence in legal scholarship, teaching, and experiential learning. The school offers JD, LLM, and JSD programs and is home to leading scholars and practitioners engaged in innovative legal research across a wide range of disciplines.

The Cornell Law School First Amendment Clinic’s dual mission is to teach students important aspects of the First Amendment and to vigorously defend its clients’ First Amendment rights. Through coursework and cutting edge First Amendment litigation, advocacy and research, students gain theoretical and practical skills while achieving the best possible outcomes for their clients. Aside from its free speech litigation work, the Clinic houses the Local Journalism Project, an innovative initiative that provides focus to the Clinic’s work on behalf of local and community news outlets and journalists and the Local Government Project, which examines how democratic values – especially free expression – are functioning at the local government level.

About The Cornell Jeb E. Brooks School of Public Policy
The Cornell Jeb E. Brooks School of Public Policy is Cornell University's interdisciplinary public policy school, dedicated to advancing evidence-based solutions to society's most pressing challenges through research, teaching, and public engagement. The school brings together leading scholars, practitioners, and students to address issues including democracy and governance, technology policy, health policy, social inequality, sustainability, and global development. Through its commitment to impactful research and community engagement, the Brooks School prepares future leaders while supporting public institutions and policy innovation at the local, national, and global levels.

   

Cornell Law School, through its First Amendment Clinic, and the Cornell Brooks School of Public Policy seek a highly motivated, entrepreneurial, and data-driven professional to serve as the Local Government Project (LGP) Temporary Research Specialist. This position supports a collaborative initiative focused on strengthening First Amendment protections and open government practices within New York State school boards.

 

Working under the supervision of Mark Jackson, Director of the First Amendment Clinic at Cornell Law School, and in collaboration with Paul Eastburg Friesen, Research Associate at the Center for Global Democracy at the Brooks School of Public Policy, the Research Specialist will lead the completion of a statewide pilot project examining school board policies and practices through a First Amendment lens.

 

The project seeks to identify opportunities for improvement in public participation policies, promote transparency, enhance freedom of expression, and support effective democratic governance at the local level. The successful candidate will work collaboratively with university researchers, students, community stakeholders, advocacy organizations, and school board officials across New York State.

 

This position is generously funded by the Henry Luce Foundation.

 

Project Background

The Local Government Project has been underway for six months and has already collected public participation policies from approximately one-third of New York State school boards. An interim report summarizing initial findings has been completed.

 

The Research Specialist will assume primary responsibility for:

·        Completing statewide data collection efforts.

·        Managing and supporting undergraduate and graduate student research assistants.

·        Examining how school board policies are implemented in practice.

·        Identifying trends, challenges, and best practices related to public participation and First Amendment rights.

·        Delivering a comprehensive final report with findings and recommendations.

 

The successful candidate will be expected to deliver:

·        A completed statewide database of school board policies and practices.

·        A draft final report summarizing project findings and recommendations.

 

Responsibilities:

·        Follow and implement the project's established methodology and research protocols for collecting and analyzing school board policies and practices.

·        Expand and complete the statewide database of school board public participation policies.

·        Assess policy implementation through qualitative and quantitative research methods.

·        Network and build relationships with citizens, advocates, school board members, administrators, and other local government stakeholders throughout New York State.

·        Identify emerging issues related to First Amendment rights, public participation, transparency, and open government.

·        Coordinate and supervise undergraduate and graduate student research assistants.

·        Collaborate closely with faculty, clinic staff, fellows, and student researchers across Cornell Law School and the Brooks School.

·        Analyze findings and develop recommendations aimed at enhancing First Amendment protections within school board governance.

·        Prepare and submit a final written report describing project findings and future opportunities for research and policy development.

·        Participate in project meetings and provide regular updates on research progress.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

·        Bachelor's degree with 3 to 5 years of relevant experience in public policy, law, government, research, social science, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

·        Excellent written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills.

·        Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving abilities.

·        Experience collecting, managing, and analyzing research data.

·        Ability to work effectively with diverse stakeholders, including public officials, citizens, advocacy organizations, and academic partners.

·        Experience supervising, mentoring, or coordinating student researchers or project teams.

·        Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.

·        Commitment to public service, democratic engagement, and collaborative problem-solving.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

·        Undergraduate degree from the Brooks School of Public Policy with 3 to 5 years of relevant experience.

·        Experience working with First Amendment, open government, transparency, or civil rights issues.

·        Familiarity with New York State local government or education governance structures.

·        Experience conducting policy analysis and data-driven research projects.

·        Demonstrated interest in democracy, civic engagement, public administration, or constitutional law.

 

 

Ideal Candidate:

·        Entrepreneurial and self-directed.

·        Passionate about strengthening democratic institutions.

·        Skilled at managing research projects from start to finish.

·        Comfortable engaging with a broad network of stakeholders.

·        Detail-oriented and committed to producing high-quality, evidence-based work.

·        Experienced in balancing independent work with collaborative team environments.

 

To Apply:

Please submit a cover letter and resume outlining your interest in the role and how your background, experience, and career goals make you a strong fit for this opportunity.

description:

This position is eligible for remote work within the United States.  However, while the position is remote, periodic travel to Cornell University's Ithaca, New York campus will be required for meetings, team collaboration, training, and other departmental or university business needs. The university reserves the right to modify, suspend, or terminate the remote work arrangement at any time.

 

About Information Technology @ Cornell

 

Information Technology (IT) is a strategic enabler for many functions at Cornell University, with staff located across colleges, administrative units, and campuses throughout the institution. While comprised of many organizations, IT operates as one partnering closely with faculty, staff, and students to support teaching, research, and business operations. By being embedded where the Cornell community is, IT is well positioned to provide support ranging from day‑to‑day needs to large, complex initiatives that advance major academic, research, and operational objectives across the university. Check out this link to find out more about IT@Cornell. 

 

What will you do:

 

Reporting to the Assistant Director for Identity & Access Management, the Identity Management Developer (CEMI) provides cybersecurity‑focused technical leadership and engineering expertise in support of Cornell University’s Identity & Access Management services within the university IT Security Office (ITSO). This position plays a key role in ensuring the secure, reliable, and effective delivery of enterprise authentication, authorization, and directory services that underpin the university’s academic, research, and administrative operations.


The Identity Management environment at Cornell consists of a diverse ecosystem of homegrown, open‑source, and vendor‑provided applications and services. The Identity Manager Developer operates primarily in an engineering‑focused capacity, contributing deep technical expertise to the design, planning, implementation, and ongoing improvement of identity services. This role is instrumental in maintaining a strong security posture while enabling scalability, resiliency, and ease of use for a broad and varied campus community.


In addition to technical leadership, this position serves as a key liaison between ITSO, campus business units, and external partners. The Identity Management Developer supports strong service relationships by helping stakeholders understand identity service capabilities, status, and access processes, and by translating complex technical concepts into clear, non‑technical guidance when needed. The role also contributes to the evolution of next‑generation Identity Management solutions by collaborating with vendors, peer institutions, and internal partners to stay current with emerging technologies and best practices in higher education cybersecurity.


The Identity Management Developer is expected to work collaboratively within the Identity Management team and across ITSO to meet service levels, support operational objectives, and respond effectively to system outages or changes, including availability outside of standard university business hours when required.


This is a two (2) year term appointment which may be ended or extended based on organizational needs, funding availability, and performance.


This position is eligible for remote work within the United States.  However, while the position is remote, periodic travel to Cornell University's Ithaca, New York campus will be required for meetings, team collaboration, training, and other departmental or university business needs. The university reserves the right to modify, suspend, or terminate the remote work arrangement at any time.

 

While position responsibilities vary, every member of our community is expected to foster a culture of belonging and a healthy work environment by communicating across differences; being cooperative, collaborative, open, and welcoming; showing respect, compassion, and empathy; engaging and supporting others regardless of background or perspective; speaking up when others are being excluded or treated inappropriately; and supporting work/life integration of oneself and others.

 

Required Qualifications:

 

  • Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of three to five years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Demonstrated success providing technical support and application or middleware development in a distributed, team‑focused computing environment.
  • Demonstrated expertise with one or more scripting or programming languages, such as Java, Perl, Python, and/or VB (.NET), ReactJS, Ruby, and/or PHP
  • Approximately 1 year+ of professional experience developing ReactJS applications and/or Ruby on Rails.
  • System administration experience with Linux required; and Windows experience preferred.
  • Working to advanced knowledge of one or more identity and access management technologies, including directory services, virtual directories, SAML2, OAuth2, LDAP, and Active Directory authorization technologies.
  • Proven experience writing technical design documentation, conducting code reviews, and working with version control systems such as Git.
  • Ability to translate user and business needs into clear functional requirements and technical specifications, and to promote effective and efficient information sharing.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate complex Identity Management concepts—including system functions, capabilities, and processes—into business terms that are clear, accessible, and meaningful to non‑technical stakeholders.
  • Proven ability to work effectively in a dynamic, deadline‑driven, and complex environment with multiple competing priorities.
  • Strong facilitation, problem‑solving, analytical, reasoning, and judgment skills, with the ability to evaluate options and recommend sound technical solutions.
  • Experience supporting and managing mission‑critical systems in a production environment, including troubleshooting and incident response.
  • Proven ability to identify, scope, and implement opportunities for automation or architectural improvements that enhance system reliability, security, or efficiency.
  • Ability to cultivate and develop inclusive working relationships with students, faculty, staff, and community members. 

 

Preferred Qualifications:

 

  • Experience working in higher education, research, or similarly complex enterprise environments, particularly those with diverse identity populations and federated access needs.
  • Familiarity with cloud‑based identity platforms and services (e.g., Azure AD, AWS IAM, Google Identity, or similar).
  • Experience with identity lifecycle management, provisioning/de‑provisioning workflows, and access governance.
  • Knowledge of zero trust, least‑privilege, and modern identity security architectures.
  • Experience integrating identity services with enterprise applications, including SaaS platforms and custom applications.
  • Demonstrated experience participating in cross‑functional technical initiatives, including collaboration with security, infrastructure, and application teams.
  • Experience supporting incident response, audits, or compliance efforts related to identity and access management.
  • Familiarity with DevOps or CI/CD practices, automated deployments, and infrastructure‑as‑code concepts.
  • Strong customer‑service orientation with the ability to balance security requirements with usability and operational needs.

Job Title

Research Technician I–II

Agency

Texas A&M University - Corpus Christi

Department

Harte Research Institute

Proposed Minimum Salary

Commensurate

Job Location

Corpus Christi, Texas

Job Type

Staff

Job Description

TAMU-CC is a dynamic university designated as both a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) and Minority-Serving Institution (MSI) with approximately 11,000 students from 47 states and 54 foreign nations. We employ over 1,400 full-time and 2,000 part-time Islanders (including students/GAs). The University attracts highly talented faculty and staff and offers an array of undergraduate and graduate degrees, including doctoral programs.  As a member of the Texas A&M University System, TAMU-CC benefits from a range of resources, increased visibility and influence, and opportunities to collaborate in mutually beneficial ways with peers across member institutions and associated agencies.

 

TAMU-CC’s beautiful campus is located on a 240-acre island on Corpus Christi Bay and was ranked #1 College by the Sea by Best College Reviews. Our natural setting is enhanced by its modern, attractive, and state-of-the-art classroom buildings and support facilities.


PURPOSE

The Research Technician I or II will contribute to ongoing research with the Coastal Conservation and Restoration Ecology Group at the Harte Research Institute. This position supports a variety of field and laboratory efforts focused on oyster reefs and other coastal habitats. The Technician will assist with sample collection, processing, and data management in support of scientific studies aimed at understanding and restoring coastal ecosystems. The role involves a fast-paced, hands-on work environment, and applicants should be comfortable with physically active fieldwork including wading, boating, and working outdoors in variable conditions. This position may be filled at the Research Technician I or Research Technician II level. Final classification will be determined based on the selected candidate’s education, experience, and qualifications in accordance with applicable TAMU System job profile requirements.

 

DESCRIPTION

Functional Area 1: Research

Percent Effort: 60%


  • Process samples in the laboratory (e.g., sorting benthic fauna, analyzing oyster tissue for disease, filtering water for chlorophyll and TSS, and preparing sediments for stable isotope analysis).
  • Identify invertebrate organisms using dichotomous keys.
  • Participate in field research, typically 1-2 days per week, including water and biological sample collection from boats or the shoreline. Fieldwork involves physical effort and often requires time in the water.
  • Operate University vehicles to safely transport personnel and equipment in support of field sampling and research activities.
  • Perform other duties as assigned

 

Functional Area 2: Operations

Percent Effort: 20%


  • Maintain and troubleshoot laboratory and field equipment.
  • Keep laboratory spaces clean, organized, and well-stocked.
  • Track inventory and coordinate ordering of consumables, field gear, and outreach materials.
  • Maintain organized and accurate data records.
  • Coordinate and provide logistical support for field activities, including preparing equipment, loading vehicles, and ensuring safety protocols are followed.
  • Operate University vehicles and conduct field sampling/research via boats

 

Functional Area 3: Support

Percent Effort: 20%


  • Coordinate and participate in educational outreach events, including tabling, hands-on demonstrations, and community engagement activities.
  • Maintain updated outreach materials and ensure that supplies and equipment and ready for use.
  • Assist with laboratory tours by preparing spaces, guiding visitors, and helping communicate research activities.
  • Provide internal support for reporting by gathering information, locating records, or summarizing activities as needed.
  • Assist in identifying and troubleshooting logistical or operational issues and contribute to the development of effective solutions.

 

QUALIFICATIONS


Research Technician I

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Two (2) years of related experience working in dynamic field settings such as intertidal or estuarine environments, or comparable experience in a related field.
  • Valid driver’s license
  • Willingness and ability to travel as needed and work long/nonstandard hours during fieldwork and sample collection.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to lift and carry objects weighing up to 50 pounds.

Research Technician II

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • Three (3) years of relevant experience working in dynamic field settings such as intertidal or estuarine environments, or comparable experience in a related field.
  • Valid driver’s license
  • Willingness and ability to travel as needed and work long/nonstandard hours during fieldwork and sample collection.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to lift and carry objects weighing up to 50 pounds.

 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field.
  • Field and/or laboratory experience with Eastern oyster (Crassostrea virginica) and other benthic invertebrates.
  • Competence in identification and classification of invertebrates using dichotomous keys.
  • Current valid SCUBA diving certification.
  • Experience operating and trailering small vessels.
  • Hands-on experience maintaining laboratory and field equipment.
  • Familiarity with data entry and quality control procedures using Microsoft Excel.
  • Educational outreach experience, including the ability to communicate research concepts to a broad audience.

SALARY:  Commensurate based on experience and qualifications.


Research Technician I

  • Up to $16.25 Hourly (Up to $33,800 Annually, Approximately)


Research Technician II

  • Up to $20.67 Hourly (Up to $42,993.60 Annually, Approximately)

NOTE: Employment may be impacted by the Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025 and the moratorium issued by Texas Governor Abbott on January 27, 2026.

From our generous benefits package and professional development opportunities, to our retirement programs and our commitment to service excellence, the Island University is an engaging and rewarding place to work.

Job Title

Research Associate

Agency

Texas A&M University

Department

Proposed Minimum Salary

Commensurate

Job Location

College Station, Texas

Job Type

Job Description

What We Want

We’re looking for a detail-oriented and collaborative research professional who is excited to advance translational research focused on healthy aging, nutrition, exercise, and metabolism. In this role, you’ll support innovative studies conducted through the Center for Translational Research in Aging & Longevity by preparing research materials, coordinating sample management, and performing analytical chemistry procedures within a Biosafety Level 2 (BSL-2) laboratory environment. The ideal candidate thrives in a hands-on research setting and enjoys contributing to projects that explore how nutrients and other key metabolic building blocks influence health and disease as we age. You'll work alongside multidisciplinary researchers to help generate meaningful discoveries that can improve the well-being of aging populations. If you're passionate about scientific inquiry, laboratory research, and making a real-world impact through health and kinesiology research, we encourage you to apply.

 

What You Need to Know

Salary: Compensation will be commensurate to the selected hire’s experience. 

Cover Letter/Resume: A cover letter and resume are strongly recommended and will help in our review. You may upload them on the application under the CV/Resume section.   

Other Requirements and Factors:

  • This position is grant funded, which is renewed under the provisions of the grantor of the agreement. Therefore, your position is contingent upon continuation of funding of these grants and/or contracts.
  • May have to work on the weekend and/or after normal hours.
  • May travel as required.

Essential Duties/Tasks

Research

  • Conducts and coordinates experiments in support of various research projects.
  • Evaluates, selects, and applies standard techniques of routine research, keeping detailed records of data.
  • Installs, operates, and/or repairs research equipment.
  • Uses computers, laboratory equipment to conduct data and statistical analyses, and technical evaluation of research experiments and results.
  • Evaluates and summarizes experiment results.

Laboratory Maintenance

  • Sample (storage) management
  • Equipment calibration and maintenance
  • Waste management
  • Ordering supplies

 

Research Reports & Publications

  • Utilizes summarized results in scientific and/or clientele-oriented publications.
  • Prepares and writes proposals to funding agencies and maintains financial accounts related to research projects.

Training

  • Trains undergraduate and/or graduate students and other laboratory, technical or field staff involved in research.

 

Qualifications

Required Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Two years of related experience in specialized and relevant fields of research.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s in (bio)chemistry.
  • Experience in a biosafety level 2 laboratory.

 

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Familiarity with appropriate laboratory and/or technical equipment.
  • Ability to effectively utilize a computer and applicable software.
  • Attention to detail.
  • Excellent math skills.
  • High level of organizational skills.
  • Good background in standard chemical-analytical laboratory techniques including:
    • preparation of sample batches,
    • making standard solutions,
    • routine equipment maintenance,
    • run MS analyses,
    • reporting results and quality control.

●       Comfortable working in a multidisciplinary and international environment

 

Machines and Equipment:

  • 2 LC-MS/MS Systems: SCIEX 5500 and 7500+ MS, both paired with an M5 Microanalytical LC system.
  • GC-Triple-Quad MS/MS (7000E, Agilent)
  • Multiplexed immunoassay system milliplex analyser, Luminex xMAP technology), with microplate washer (BioTek, 405 TS)
  • Epoch 2 Microplate Spectrophotometer (Agilent BioTek, Winooski VT)
  • AFS-8D Milli-Q analytical water purifier (Millipore)

Job Description

What We Want

We are seeking a proactive and customer service oriented Instructional Designer II to develop high-quality learning experiences, web content and design, and digital resources that support marketing and communications and faculty and academic leader professional development within Faculty Affairs. The role combines instructional design, adult learning, accessibility and technology expertise, with approximately 50% of the position focused on instructional design and related project work and 50% dedicated to webmaster and website operations responsibilities. The position collaborates with faculty, administrators, subject matter experts and university partners to create accessible, faculty-centered solutions aligned with institutional standards and Texas A&M brand requirements. As the primary webmaster for Faculty Affairs, the position also maintains and continuously improves the accessibility, usability, accuracy and effectiveness of Faculty Affairs web properties.

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Master’s or doctoral degree in instructional design, instructional technology, curriculum and instruction, education, UX/UI design, communications, digital media, web design/development or a related field.
  • Five or more years of professional experience in instructional design, higher education, training and development, faculty development, web content management, digital communications or related work.

  • Working knowledge of HTML and CSS and familiarity with JavaScript and related web technologies.
  • Knowledge of search engine optimization and web content best practices.
  • Knowledge of project management practices and tools.
  • Strong writing and editing skills with demonstrated ability to translate complex information into clear, concise, accessible and user-centered instructional and digital content.
  • Experience working in a higher education environment.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:  

  • Knowledge of instructional design principles, adult learning practices and development of learning experiences for professional or higher education audiences.
  • Ability to design and develop clear, engaging and effective instructional and professional development materials.
  • Experience developing and maintaining digital learning resources and web-based content.
  • Experience working with content management systems and publishing website content.
  • Knowledge of digital accessibility requirements and practices, including ADA, Section 508 and WCAG standards.
  • Ability to organize and present complex information in clear, accessible and user-centered formats.
  • Strong written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills.

  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities, exercise sound judgment, solve problems independently and follow work through completion.
  • Ability to learn and effectively use new instructional, web and digital technologies

Essential Duties/Tasks

Webmaster, Website Operations & Digital Content Management

  • Serves as the primary webmaster for Faculty Affairs web properties and provides day-to-day front-end website administration, content publishing, maintenance and quality assurance.
  • Creates, edits, formats, updates and publishes web content using university-supported content management systems and related digital tools.
  • Maintains web pages, navigation, links, documents, forms, multimedia and other digital content to ensure information remains accurate, current, accessible and functional.
  • Works with Faculty Affairs leadership, program owners and content contributors to translate organizational priorities, programs and user needs into effective website content, structure and presentation.
  • Applies principles of information architecture, usability, digital accessibility, search engine optimization and web content strategy to improve navigation, readability, discoverability and user experience.
  • Reviews web content, page layouts and digital assets for consistency with Texas A&M brand standards, university web standards and accessibility requirements.
  • Conducts routine website quality assurance and identifies and addresses broken links, outdated information, formatting inconsistencies, accessibility issues and other front-end problems.
  • Supports ongoing digital accessibility compliance through website reviews, audits, remediation and follow-up in coordination with appropriate university accessibility, communications and technology partners.
  • Uses Siteimprove, web analytics and other available reporting tools to evaluate website quality, usage and performance and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Monitors website content and performance and recommends improvements to content, navigation, page structure, usability, accessibility and other aspects of the user experience.
  • Troubleshoots front-end website and publishing issues and coordinates platform, hosting, development or other technical issues with Central Web Services, university IT or other appropriate partners.
  • Supports website enhancements, redesigns, migrations and other digital initiatives through content preparation, implementation, testing, quality assurance and rollout.
  • Maintains website documentation, publishing procedures, content standards and review practices for Faculty Affairs web properties.
  • Provides guidance and support to Faculty Affairs employees who contribute or maintain web content, including assistance with accessibility, page structure, content presentation, digital assets and publishing practices.
  • Coordinates website content lifecycle activities, including scheduled content reviews, updates, archival and removal of outdated or obsolete materials.
  • Maintains awareness of university web standards, digital accessibility requirements, CMS capabilities and emerging web practices and recommends appropriate improvements to Faculty Affairs web properties.

Instructional Design & Faculty Development

  • Plans, develops and delivers learning resources and professional development experiences for faculty and academic leaders, including guides, online modules, microlearning, templates, workshops, presentations and other instructional materials.
  • Assesses learning and performance needs by identifying challenges, gathering and analyzing relevant information, determining potential solutions and making recommendations.
  • Designs faculty-centered solutions appropriate to identified needs, ranging from individual resources, tools or workshops to multi-part learning experiences, certificate programs and other structured professional development initiatives.
  • Authors original content and modifies existing materials in collaboration with subject matter experts to create clear, engaging and effective faculty-focused learning experiences.
  • Applies adult learning principles and instructional design methodologies in the development of in-person, online and hybrid professional development.
  • Develops instructional strategies, activities, scenarios, case studies and assessments that support defined learning objectives and desired outcomes.
  • Takes ownership of assigned instructional design initiatives and follows projects through development, implementation, evaluation and completion.

Technology Innovation, Quality Assurance, Accessibility & Continuous Improvement

  • Creates, reviews and revises instructional and professional development materials to meet applicable accessibility standards and best practices, including ADA, Section 508, WCAG and Universal Design for Learning principles.
  • Reviews learning resources and related materials for accessibility, usability, consistency, accuracy and alignment with quality standards and best practices in higher education.
  • Collects and evaluates assessment results, learner feedback and stakeholder input during and following implementation and incorporates findings into revisions and future development.
  • Evaluates instructional content, delivery methods, learning technologies and related resources and recommends enhancements to improve effectiveness and the learner experience.
  • Researches emerging instructional design practices, technologies and trends and assesses their relevance and potential application to Faculty Affairs programs and services.
  • Applies current practices and emerging innovations in the planning and development of multimedia learning assets, including audio, video, graphics, interactive content and other digital media.
  • Administers and maintains online professional development resources and learning environments.
  • Supports the effective integration of learning technologies with Faculty Affairs websites and other digital platforms.

Project Management & Collaboration

  • Manages assigned instructional design and professional development projects and effectively prioritizes workload to meet established deadlines and project objectives.
  • Coordinates projects from initial needs assessment and planning through development, stakeholder review, implementation and evaluation.
  • Owns end-to-end creation of key learning assets, including presentations, facilitator materials, scenarios and case studies, video scripts, assessment instruments, templates and other resources.
  • Collaborates with faculty, academic leaders, subject matter experts, communications professionals, instructional designers, technology professionals and other university partners.

Our faculty impact and influence our students, society as well as the world around us. Therefore, we take great pride in our responsibilities of elevating our faculty and providing them exemplary support services.

Agency

Texas A&M Agrilife Research

Proposed Minimum Salary

Commensurate

Job Location

College Station, Texas

Job Type

Staff

Job Description

About Texas A&M AgriLife

Texas A&M AgriLife is comprised of the following Texas A&M University System members:

  • Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service
  • Texas A&M AgriLife Research
  • College of Agriculture and Life Sciences at Texas A&M University
  • Texas A&M Forest Service
  • Texas A&M Veterinary Medical Diagnostic Laboratory

As the nation’s largest most comprehensive agriculture program, Texas A&M AgriLife brings together a college and four state agencies focused on agriculture and life sciences within The Texas A&M University System. With over 5,000 employees and a presence in every county across the state, Texas A&M AgriLife is uniquely positioned to improve lives, environments and the Texas economy through education, research, extension and service.


Click here to learn more about joining AgriLife!


Position Information


Job Summary:

The Web Applications Developer II – WordPress & Full-Stack Web Development, under direction, performs complex and specialized web development functions in support of organizational websites, web applications, and digital platforms. WordPress is a primary development platform for this position, with responsibilities also extending to custom web applications, APIs, integrations, and related web technologies.


The role supports front-end and back-end development, modern WordPress theme, plugin, and block development, application troubleshooting, testing, accessibility, and ongoing platform support. The position works collaboratively with developers, designers, content managers, project leaders, and stakeholders to develop, modernize, and maintain public-facing websites and web applications across the organization.


Responsibilities:


Problem Resolution, Technical Evaluation, and Project Management

  • Reviews and analyzes web application and WordPress documentation, source code, configurations, and production results to facilitate problem resolution and identify root causes of application issues.
  • Troubleshoots and resolves complex problems in WordPress and other web application environments, including theme and plugin conflicts, custom code defects, block editor issues, application errors, performance problems, integration issues, and accessibility defects.
  • Evaluates and follows through on web development issues and problems until resolved or appropriately escalated.
  • Participates in application and data design for web solutions, including content modeling, database structures, APIs, integrations, and application components.
  • Participates in the evaluation of WordPress plugins, themes, block themes, frameworks, libraries, APIs, and other web development tools to determine applicability, security, accessibility, performance, and maintainability.
  • Assists the project leader with developing work plans and schedules for website and web application projects, including outlining phases, identifying technical needs, estimating development effort, and tracking milestones for development, modernization, and migration work.

Project Planning and Consultation

  • Consults with clients and stakeholders to understand project requirements and provides technical recommendations regarding WordPress capabilities, web development approaches, integrations, accessibility, and implementation options within established technical standards.
  • Reviews project plans and schedules, communicates development and testing results, and discusses technical problems or concerns with project leaders and stakeholders.
  • Contributes to technical specifications and design documentation based on project and stakeholder requirements.
  • Collaborates with project leaders, developers, designers, and content managers throughout development, testing, deployment, and ongoing support.

Design, Development, and Testing

  • Develops and implements complex WordPress websites, themes, block themes, custom blocks, plugins, and web applications according to established requirements and specifications.
  • Develops front-end and back-end components for WordPress and other web applications using appropriate web technologies.
  • Writes complex PHP, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, and related web application code in accordance with WordPress coding standards and established development guidelines.
  • Applies modern WordPress development practices, including the block editor/Gutenberg, block-based development, block themes, theme.json, and Full Site Editing where appropriate.
  • Develops and maintains integrations between WordPress, external APIs, data sources, databases, and other web applications as needed to support application functionality.
  • Tests and remediates WordPress solutions and other web applications for functionality, cross-browser compatibility, responsive behavior, overall quality, and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility.
  • Uses version control and established development workflows to manage source code and application changes.

Other Duties

  • Authors and maintains technical documentation, developer guides, application documentation, and onboarding materials for websites and web applications.
  • Provides technical support and guidance to less experienced staff on WordPress development workflows, application codebases, troubleshooting, and established quality standards.
  • Participates in code reviews and collaborative development activities.
  • Maintains knowledge of evolving WordPress and web development technologies and applies appropriate practices to assigned work.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications


Required Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Information Systems, Computer Science, or closely related field, or, an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
  • Four years of related experience.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others.
  • Working knowledge of front-end and back-end web development using HTML5, CSS3, PHP, JavaScript, and related web technologies.
  • Working knowledge of modern WordPress development and administration, including themes, plugins, blocks, templates, block-based site development, content management workflows, and site configuration.
  • Familiarity with APIs, databases, structured data, and web application integrations.
  • Knowledge of responsive web development and cross-browser compatibility.
  • Knowledge of web accessibility standards and accessible development practices.
  • Knowledge of version control practices and collaborative development workflows.
  • Ability to analyze technical problems, evaluate potential solutions, and communicate technical information to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Web Development, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • More than four years of WordPress, full-stack, or web application development experience.
  • Experience developing custom WordPress themes, block themes, plugins, or blocks using modern WordPress development practices, including Gutenberg, Full Site Editing, or theme.json.
  • Experience developing or integrating REST APIs and third-party services.
  • Experience working with relational databases or application data.
  • Experience with JavaScript frameworks or modern front-end development tools.
  • Experience with authentication or single sign-on integrations.
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines or automated web development and deployment workflows.
  • Experience with cloud or managed web hosting platforms such as WP Engine or Pantheon.
  • Experience developing accessible websites or applications conforming to WCAG standards.
  • Experience in a research, government, or higher education web environment.

Other Requirements:

  • Work beyond normal business hours and/or work on weekends.

 

What You Need to Know


Salary: Pay Grade: 70. Compensation is commensurate with the candidate’s qualifications.


Position Funding: This position is funded through grants or contracts. Continued employment is dependent upon ongoing funding and satisfactory job performance.


This position requires an on-site presence and is not fully remote. Flexible work schedules and limited partially remote work options may be available, depending on the nature of the role and employee eligibility, in accordance with AgriLife Alternate Work Location Procedures. Remote work arrangements are limited to Texas-based locations only. 


Sponsorship: Non-immigrant foreign nationals are prohibited by export control laws from performing the employment responsibilities associated with this position; sponsorship is not available.

Job Summary:

This position is expected to serve as Principal Investigator (PI), Co-PI, or contribute as a significant lead in research and proposal development within the Roadside Safety and Physical Security Division of TTI. Has an understanding of principles of quality and unbiased research. Completes projects on-time with completed deliverables. Conducts research following safety practices and guidelines. Understands rules, policies, and regulation of TTI, TAMUS, and IRB. Participate in technology transfer and implementation. Employee will be responsible for project management, composing various reports and papers, presenting deliverables and study results, overseeing students, developing proposals, and interprogram coordination. Continued employment in this position is contingent upon availability of funding and satisfactory performance.


Essential Duties:

  • Perform applied research duties, including performing engineering and simulation analyses in support of the design and development of roadside safety devices, and conducting crash testing to analyze and evaluate roadside safety features. Plan, schedule, coordinate, and report detailed phases of research and development projects. Conduct necessary literature review, background information searches, and surveys to support techniques and methodologies used, as well as documenting past research for reporting purposes. (60%)
  • Manage, communicate, and coordinate with multi-disciplinary teams comprising research staff, graduate and undergraduate students, and support staff to ensure the completion of research objectives and timely delivery of high-quality project deliverables. (10%)
  • Compile, document, and present research results in formats required for inclusion in reports, technical memoranda, and presentations. Prepare technical documentation, including literature reviews, analyses methods and results, and summaries. Prepare project reports and other deliverables as required. Prepare materials for presentation of research results and other deliverables at technical meetings or other venues and to sponsors. (10%)
  • Actively seek and obtain externally-funded research projects associated with performing work on basic and applied research and engineering problems, including preparation of research proposals as Principal Investigator (PI), Co-PI, or key researcher. (8%)
  • Prepare and give presentations to existing and potential sponsors at meetings or in conference settings. Prepare, schedule, conduct, and document research meetings. (5%)
  • Interact with sponsors and potential clients. (5%)
  • Other duties as assigned. (2%)

Required Education and Experience:

  • Master’s Degree in relevant field of engineering
  • 3 years of related professional experience to include:
    • Non-linear finite element modeling and simulation
    • Design and testing of roadside safety devices

Preferred Qualifications:

  • LS-DYNA, HyperMesh, Solidworks, computer programming

Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills along with interpersonal and presentation skills.
  • Strong technical writing skills.
  • Ability to handle multiple projects and responsibilities simultaneously and meet deadlines.
  • Strong analytical skills.
  • Ability to work cooperatively with others in a team environment.

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to perform common office functions
  • Ability to frequently communicate with other individuals within the workplace.
  • Ability to operate a computer and other office productivity machinery

The physical demands are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Job Description

Here's a Glimpse of the Job

The Research Scientist will be responsible for conducting complex independent research in their field of expertise. The Research Scientist will utilize techniques and strategies taught to them by their education and experiences to work towards solving the question presented by their research project. Writes and contributes to research papers, articles, and publications. Will collaborate with other researchers and/or faculty.


Opportunities to Contribute

  • Oversee the preparation and cleaning of worksite.
  • Organize worksite and determine what supplies are necessary to continue research in an effective manner.
  • Analyze research data and summarize results.
  • Assist with grant acquisition.
  • Assist student researchers, Postdoctoral Research Associates, Assistant Research Scientists, and/or Associate Research Scientists who are working on research related to the project.
  • May supervise assigned staff and/or students.
  • Prepare presentation materials on research topics that may be presented to small and/or large groups.
  • Participate in the preparation of required technical progress reports to research sponsors.

Qualifications:

  • PhD in a related field.
  • Six years of related experience in a specialized and relevant field of research.
  • BSL-2 training and experience.
  • Mouse and rat handling, injections, euthanasia, and necropsy training and experience.

A well-qualified candidate may also possess:

  • Experience with analysis of proteomics data.
  • Knowledge of innate immune system.
  • Experience writing papers.
  • Experience with mammalian cell culture, immunostaining, western blots.
  • Experience with drug development programs and preclinical drug development work.
  • Excellent verbal and written skills, presentation and analytical skills, and attention to detail.
  • Must be able to work independently as part of a multidisciplinary collaborative team. 
  • Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others.

Salary: Compensation will be commensurate based on the selected candidate’s education and experience.

Special Note: Due to this position’s salary having all or a portion of it being funded by grants or contracts, the continuing salary and overall employment is contingent upon availability of these funds in the future.

Schedule: May have to work on the weekend and/or after normal hours. May travel as required.

Why Texas A&M University?

Texas A&M University is committed to enriching the learning and working environment by promoting a culture that respects all perspectives, talents & lived experiences.  Embracing varying opinions and perspectives strengthens our core values which are: Respect, Excellence, Leadership, Loyalty, Integrity, and Selfless Service. 


The Department of Biology at Texas A&M University is responsible for research and teaching within the vast disciplines of the biological sciences, from molecular cell biology to ecology and evolutionary biology. Our faculty perform cutting-edge research in a wide array of biological sciences in the laboratory and in the field. Our graduate research programs prepare scientists for careers in academia, industry and government and enhance our understanding of the central role of biological systems in the global environment. Our undergraduate students gain a firm foundation in modern biological sciences to prepare them for a multitude of careers that depend on a solid understanding of biology. To learn more, please visit us at https://www.bio.tamu.edu/.


We are a prestigious university with strong traditions, Core Values, and a community of caring and collaboration.  Amenities associated with a major university, such as sporting and cultural events, state-of-the-art recreation facilities, the Bush Library and Museum, and much more await you.  Experience all that a big city has to offer but with a reasonable cost-of-living and no long commutes.

Position Information

Job Summary:

The Texas A&M Center for Grazinglands and Ranch Management is seeking a Research Associate with a strong work ethic to assist in executing projects related to exclusion fencing and mitigation of wild pig damage. This position will be responsible for working directly with landowners, managers, biologists, ranchers, and a wide range of constituents. The position will also be responsible for all field related work such as identifying study sites, collecting baseline data, setting, filling and maintaining corn feeders, building small exclusion fences and plots, monitoring animal activity with remotely triggered cameras, reviewing and assimilating data from pictures and video, data entry, and report writing. This position may also work with other project collaborators to design and implement wild pig exclusion methods in livestock operations to prevent damage, use of feed and water, and access to sensitive areas, which also may include use of farm equipment, implements, ATVs, UTVs, and similar to remediate damage from wild pigs. This position will involve frequent communication with landowners and coordination with project partners, so effective communication skills are required. Travel will be required to multiple study locations across Texas.


Texas A&M University’s Center for Grazinglands and Ranch Management (CGRM) aims to safeguard the ecologic and economic resiliency of grazingland resources and ranching operations with a focus on producer-directed, applied grazingland and ranch management research, outreach, and industry engagement. CGRM develops and supports interdisciplinary collaborations to address critical needs in the ranching community and strives to achieve three overarching goals: enhance operational resiliency, strengthen enterprise sustainability, and foster the future of the industry.  search and wild pig management activities across Texas, including data collection, monitoring, stakeholder coordination, and project support. This position works closely with landowners and project partners to implement and evaluate research and damage mitigation efforts. The work is intellectual and varied, requiring consistent discretion and judgment in planning, conducting, evaluating, and supporting research and management activities.


Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for working directly with landowners, managers, biologists, ranchers, and a wide range of constituents.
  • Responsible for all field related work such as identifying study sites, collecting baseline data, setting, filling and maintaining corn feeders, building small exclusion fences and plots, monitoring animal activity with remotely triggered cameras, reviewing and assimilating data from pictures and video, data entry, and report writing.
  • May work with other project collaborators to design and implement wild pig exclusion methods in livestock operations to prevent damage, use of feed and water, and access to sensitive areas, which also may include use of farm equipment, implements, ATVs, UTVs, and similar to remediate damage from wild pigs.
  • Frequent communication with landowners and coordination with project partners, so effective communication skills are required.
  • Travel to multiple study locations across Texas.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in relevant field.
  • Two years of related professional experience.
  • Strong work ethic and self-motivated
  • Ability to work in a remote location, sometimes under adverse conditions (hot, humid, biting/stinging insects), on working ranches with livestock operations
  • Ability to work independently and as a team with minimum supervision and be capable of planning an effective work day
  • Ability to analyze data and write reports
  • Ability to communicate effectively and efficiently (verbal and written);
  • Detail oriented
  • Ability to multitask and work cooperatively with others
  • Ability to learn new skills and techniques

Preferred Qualifications:

  • M.S. degree in rangeland management, natural resource management or closely related field; GPA of ≥3.0; more than two years of experience
  • Experience or working knowledge of ranching, wildlife, and rangeland management practices
  • Experience working directly with producers
  • Experience building various fence designs
  • Experience using 4-wheel drive vehicles, ATVs/UTVs, farm machinery/tractors, and ability to tow trailers
  • Knowledge or experience planning, coordinating, and conducting field activities
  • Technical writing skills
