description:
Job Description

Field of research:

Protein engineering, synthetic biology, and biochemical tool development with emphasis on optogenetically controlled RNA/DNA polymerases, programmable nucleic-acid writing, and in vitro assay systems for polymerase activity, specificity, and error control.

Purpose of the research project(s):

To build and execute the experimental pipeline for engineering and characterizing light-responsive RNA polymerase systems. The position will support molecular cloning, protein production, and cell-free functional assays needed to generate sponsor-facing milestones and publications on optogenetic polymerase control, sequence-programmed RNA synthesis, and related protein-sensor technologies.

Job Duties and Responsibilities:

- Molecular cloning and construct generation – 25%

Design and build plasmids for engineered T7 polymerases, optogenetic domains, protein binders, reporters, and assay controls using PCR, Gibson/Golden Gate assembly, mutagenesis, and sequence verification.

•    Protein expression, purification, and QC – 20%
Express and purify polymerases, binders, and optogenetic protein components (primarily from bacteria) using affinity chromatography/FPLC and standard QC methods such as SDS-PAGE, concentration assessment, and storage optimization.

•    In vitro functional assay development and execution – 25%
Develop and run cell-free transcription and polymerase assays, including time-course transcription assays, one- or few-base incorporation assays, and assays using modified nucleotides such as fluorescently labeled or biotinylated bases.

•    Optogenetic characterization and readout integration – 15%
Perform light-control experiments, fluorescence/plate-reader assays, and other optical measurements needed to evaluate gating behavior, kinetics, and retained function of engineered constructs.

•    Sequencing sample preparation and data/QC handoff – 10%
Prepare samples for sequencing-based readouts, organize construct/sample metadata, and maintain clean experimental records that support downstream analysis and sponsor reporting.

•    Project support, documentation, and collaboration – 5%
Maintain SOPs, reagent inventories, and experimental documentation; prepare figures/tables for meetings and reports; and coordinate day-to-day bench workflows with the PI, trainees, and collaborating groups.

Visa Eligibility

This position is eligible for H-1B sponsorship.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree in Biochemistry, molecular biology, bioengineering, chem biol, or related field and one year of relevant experience laboratory research.

Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.

Additional Requirements:Molecular cloning: PCR, Gibson/Golden Gate assembly, mutagenesis, bacterial transformation, plasmid preparation, and sequence verification.
•    Protein production: bacterial expression, affinity purification, chromatography/FPLC workflows, and protein QC.
•    Biochemical assays: experience with enzyme assays, transcription assays, fluorescence-based readouts, or related in vitro functional measurements.

Desire:

. Experience with cell-free transcription or nucleic-acid enzyme assays.
•    Experience using modified nucleotides (e.g., fluorescent, biotinylated, or otherwise chemically functionalized substrates).
•    Experience with optogenetic proteins, light-controlled assays, or photochemistry/fluorescence instrumentation.
•    Sequencing library preparation or sample-prep familiarity for assay readouts.
•    Experience with protein binders, display/selections, or protein-sensor engineering.
•    Basic computational comfort for organizing data, plotting results, and working with standard lab analysis tools.

•    Data quality and documentation: careful experimental record-keeping, sample tracking, and SOP development.
•    Communication and teamwork: ability to summarize results clearly and work closely with the PI and collaborators.

-         research assistantships/internships acceptable, strong hands-on

title: Research Scientist/Engineer 1
description:
Job Description

Field of Research:

Computational biology/bioinformatics with emphasis on spatial transcriptomics, proteomics, and immunosequencing using Pixel‑seq and an immune receptor‑focused multimodal expansion (“ImmunoPixel‑seq”). Work includes NGS data processing, spatial barcode mapping, single‑cell & spatial analysis, and cell segmentation in brain, tumor, and other tissues.

Purpose of the Research project(s):

To build and operate robust, reproducible pipelines that transform raw sequencing + barcode map into high‑quality, spatially resolved single‑cell datasets; to deliver disease‑focused analyses that advance mechanistic discovery and translational hypotheses (e.g., tumor microenvironment, neuroanatomical circuits).

Duties and Responsibilities:

End‑to‑end data processing (BCL/FASTQ → QC → counts) – 20%
Demultiplexing, adapter/quality trimming, UMI handling, alignment/quantification; generation of MultiQC reports and run manifests.

Spatial barcode mapping & registration – 15%

Build/validate barcode→(x,y) maps for Pixel‑seq; error correction; join gene/protein counts to spatial coordinates; QA of mapping rates.

Segmentation & QC – 20%
Apply/benchmark nuclei or whole‑cell segmentation (e.g., Cellpose/StarDist/SAM); maintain curated masks and QC thumbnails.

Downstream single‑cell & spatial analysis – 20%
Create annotated data objects (e.g., AnnData/Seurat); normalization, clustering, label transfer; spatial neighborhood/domain analysis; multi‑omic modeling for RNA+protein where applicable.

Pipeline automation & reproducibility – 10%
Implement/maintain Snakemake/Nextflow workflows with containers (Apptainer/Docker), CI tests, and clear documentation.

Project support, collaboration & reporting – 7%
Prepare figures/tables; concise analysis memos; contribute to methods sections.

Light server/environment maintenance & upgrades (DevOps‑lite) — 5%
Build and update containerized analysis environments, maintain conda/uv environments.

DevOps‑lite & data stewardship – 3%
Maintain analysis environments/containers; basic SLURM job scripts; coordinate with IT on storage/backup hygiene.

Visa Eligibility

This position is eligible for H-1B sponsorship.

Minimum Requirements:

Bachelor's Degree in CS, Applied Math, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, ECE and one year of relevant experience with Computational biology/bioinformatics.

Equivalent education and/or experience may substitute for minimum qualifications except when there are legal requirements, such as a license, certification, and/or registration.

Additional Requirements:

1. Programming & data: Python (numpy/pandas), basic R (Seurat/tidyverse), bash; Git; Linux.
2. NGS data processing: BCL→FASTQ demultiplexing; adapter/quality trimming; UMI handling; QC with MultiQC; alignment/quantification to reference.
3. Spatial omics: Pixel‑seq barcode→(x,y) mapping concepts; creation of spatially annotated objects (AnnData/Seurat).
4. Segmentation: Practical use of Cellpose/FICTURE (or similar); basic image QC.
5. Single‑cell & spatial analysis: Normalization, clustering, label transfer; spatial neighborhood/domain analyses (e.g., with Squidpy/Giotto).
6. Reproducibility & automation: Snakemake or Nextflow; containerization (Apptainer/Docker); clean documentation; basic SLURM job submission.
7. Communication: Clear writing of READMEs, short analysis memos, and figure captions for collaboration with biologists/clinicians.
8. Linux/HPC usage; Slurm job submission, resource requests, and environment management.

Desired Requirements:

1. Probabilistic modeling: scVI/scANVI/totalVI for RNA and RNA+protein integration.
2. GPU experience: PyTorch/CUDA for segmentation/model inference.
3. Data stewardship: DVC or equivalent data versioning; basic dashboarding/monitoring (Prometheus/Grafana).
4. Domain breadth: Prior coursework/research in biochemistry or genetics; interest in medical/MD‑PhD pathways.
5. DevOps‑lite: GitHub Actions CI, environment pinning, reproducible reference bundles, and runbooks.
6. Experience assisting with server upgrades in collaboration with IT (CUDA/cuDNN & GPU driver stacks, Slurm client updates, module systems).
7. Basic familiarity with configuration/monitoring for research workflows (e.g., Ansible basics, Prometheus/Grafana dashboards) under IT guidance.
8. Storage and I/O awareness for high‑throughput data (scratch NVMe vs. bulk); performance troubleshooting for pipelines.

description:
Position Title:

Research Technician II

Job Group:

Professional & Scientific

Job Description:

The Department of Animal Science at Iowa State University is seeking a Research Technician II to support innovative research investigating how environmental exposures, including per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), affect ovarian function and reproductive health.


This is a unique opportunity to contribute to research with potential implications for human health, addressing important questions in reproductive health that affect roughly half of the population, while developing expertise across animal research, molecular and cellular laboratory techniques, and research data analysis. You'll join a team that invests in professional development, provides opportunities to work with researchers across Iowa State and other universities, and supports individual career goals. You'll be part of a collaborative environment where strong organization, communication, and teamwork are essential to keeping research moving forward.


What You'll Do

  • Coordinate laboratory activities, prepare reagents and experimental materials, and maintain accurate research records and inventories.
  • Perform animal research procedures, including dosing, breeding colony management, tissue collection, necropsy support, and biological sample processing in accordance with approved research protocols.
  • Conduct molecular and cellular laboratory techniques such as RNA isolation, protein extraction, Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, histological processing, microscopy, and follicle quantification.
  • Collect, organize, analyze, and maintain research data from animal studies and laboratory experiments, ensuring data quality, accuracy, and integrity.
  • Prepare datasets, summaries, figures, and reports to support research publications, presentations, grant reporting, and other project needs.
  • Operate, calibrate, maintain, and troubleshoot laboratory instrumentation and specialized research equipment, addressing technical issues that may affect experimental outcomes.
  • Assist with developing, optimizing, and validating laboratory protocols and research methods and recommend improvements to laboratory processes.
  • Train and provide technical guidance to undergraduate researchers, graduate students, and other laboratory personnel on research techniques, laboratory procedures, and safety practices.
  • Communicate research findings, technical concerns, and recommendations with the principal investigator and research team.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in biology, animal science, biochemistry, molecular biology, reproductive physiology, or a related field.
  • Experience with molecular or cellular laboratory techniques such as RNA isolation, protein extraction, Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, histology, or microscopy.
  • Experience with animal handling, dosing, tissue collection, or other animal-based research procedures.
  • Experience collecting, organizing, analyzing, or interpreting research data.
  • Experience troubleshooting laboratory procedures, assays, or research equipment.
  • Experience training or providing technical guidance to students or other laboratory personnel.

This is a term appointment that may have opportunity for renewal.


Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. on an ongoing basis without sponsorship. Immigration sponsorship is not available for this position.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor - Psychometrics and Quantitative Methods
description: The Department of Educational Psychology seeks applicants for a nine-month tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor in our Quantitative, Qualitative, and Psychometric Methods (QQPM) program beginning August 2027. We are seeking individuals with a doctorate in psychometrics, measurement, quantitative methods, or a related field to be completed no later than August 2027. Expertise or interest in modern psychometrics (e.g., modern issues in testing, large language models, fairness, equating, computerized adaptive testing, diagnostic classification models, automatic item generation, scale/test development), latent variable modeling approaches (e.g., IRT, SEM, person-centered analysis, factor analysis), multilevel modeling, and/or a related approach is required. Experience or interest in methodological applications relevant to the areas of applied statistics, causal inference, non-parametric and/or categorical data, Bayesian estimation and/or inference, and/or program evaluation is desirable. RESPONSIBILITIES Developing and maintaining an on-going program of methodological research leading to publications in major quantitative, psychometric, statistical, and/or methodological journals. Collaborating with faculty across the College of Education and Human Sciences, UNL, and the University of Nebraska system on methodological issues related to substantive research projects. Effective instruction, student research advisement, and student mentoring. Participating in faculty governance. Participating in and/or preparing applications for external funding. Providing leadership and service at local, state, and national levels. We are a graduate-oriented department that offers master’s and doctoral degree specializations in QQPM, Development and Learning Sciences, School Psychology, and Counseling Psychology. The Department houses the Buros Center for Testing, the Nebraska Evaluation and Research Center, and the Nebraska Internship Consortium in Professional Psychology. The Department is also closely affiliated with the Nebraska Center for Research on Children, Youth, Families, and Schools, an interdisciplinary center identified as an institutional Program of Excellence. The Department cooperates with four other academic departments in providing learning experiences for undergraduate and graduate students in the College of Education and Human Sciences. title: Assistant/Associate Professor - School of Computing
description: The School of Computing (SoC) at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (UNL) is undergoing strategic expansion and invites applications for a tenured/tenure-track faculty position at the assistant or associate professor rank to begin in Fall 2027. SoC offers a collegial, collaborative culture and broad opportunities for interdisciplinary research across campus. We seek exceptional candidates who can establish a substantial scholarly research and teaching program in Robotics, with particular emphasis on the validation and verification of software systems that control safety-critical and mission-critical functionalities in autonomous aerial and ground vehicles. Areas of interest include formal methods, model-based design, software assurance, testing, verification, validation, runtime monitoring, digital twins, simulation-based evaluation, and certification of autonomous and robotic systems. The successful candidate will advance the dependability, safety, security, and resilience of software that enables perception, planning, decision-making, navigation, and control in next-generation autonomous vehicles and robotic platforms operating in complex and dynamic environments. Position Description The successful applicant will work in a team environment whose mission is to develop robotic systems to interact closely with the natural and built environment while working with end users of these systems. The successful candidate will be expected to develop a high-impact, nationally recognized research program in a self-identified area of applied robotics research or another closely related area. They will be expected to effectively obtain and leverage external and internal support for research; work with interdisciplinary teams; mentor students; publish in high-quality, high-impact peer-reviewed conferences and journals; and participate in scientific meetings and other appropriate professional activities. The successful candidate will have strong electrical, computing, and/or mechanical engineering skills and be interested in developing a collaborative program of applied research in robotics. For example, this may include sensor development, applied robotic perception, algorithm development, or other areas of interest. To support early-career success, the position includes a competitive startup package designed to establish a strong research program. This package provides funding for equipment, graduate student support, and research expenses, along with a reduced teaching load during the initial years. The successful candidate will also have access to modern laboratory space in our state-of-the-art facilities and shared resources, including advanced computational infrastructure provided through Holland Computing Center (hcc.unl.edu). School of Computing Overview The SoC is undergoing an exciting period of significant growth and has hired 14 tenured/tenure-track faculty members since 2019. We are committed to promoting inclusive excellence of our faculty and seek to attract and retain a high-performing and diverse workforce in which employees’ differences are respected and valued to meet the varying needs of the diverse populations we serve. The NIMBUS lab in SoC excels at developing Uncrewed Aircraft Systems for agricultural and scientific applications and also contributes to the $25 million Heartland Robotics Cluster. SoC is enhancing research in Data Science, AI, and Machine Learning, launching a new Data Science undergraduate major, and aiming to develop leading programs in health, agriculture, biocomputing, and robotics. The school also leads a Cybersecurity Initiative to tackle security challenges with AI and ML techniques. Additionally, SoC is a leader in IoT and Agricultural IoT, spearheading the Nebraska IoT Initiative through a public-private partnership. This includes collaborations on major infrastructure projects and the formation of the interlocal agency iLNK. Furthermore, SoC is also recognized for its work in Empirical Software Engineering, Testing, and Formal Methods, and is expanding into areas like Mining Software Repositories, Software Security, and Human-centered Software Engineering. College Growth The College of Engineering has hired more than 70 new faculty members over the past five years and continues to grow its faculty base to support future expansion. The School of Computing is central to advancing the College’s ambitious research goals, supported by state-of-the-art facilities, including a new $75 million research building and a $115 million engineering education building that opened in 2024. The College is committed to providing a world-class engineering education through initiatives such as the nationally recognized Complete Engineer® Program. Notably, UNL’s College of Engineering was among the first three institutions in the country to earn the ASEE Diversity Recognition Program Silver Award. We are seeking an innovative leader with a clear vision for growth and a strong commitment to excellence in research, education, and engagement within the School of Computing. About UNL, Lincoln, and Omaha The University of Nebraska-Lincoln is Nebraska’s land-grant research university, is a member of the Big Ten, and ranks among Doctoral Universities with the Highest Research Activity [Carnegie CIHE]. As the state’s flagship institution, UNL plays a key role in the region's research and innovation landscape and leverages CoE presence in Lincoln and Omaha. The city of Omaha, the largest metropolitan area in Nebraska, is a rising tech hub in the Midwest. Lincoln, the state capital, is also part of a growing high-tech region known as the ‘Midwest Silicon Prairie’. Taking advantage of both communities, UNL offers a vibrant, welcoming, family-friendly community with a strong economy, excellent public school systems, a modest cost of living, and a high quality of life. Learn more about life in Lincoln and Omaha at placetobelnk.com , aboutlincoln.unl.edu , and visitomaha.com .

title: Extension Instructor or Open Rank Extension Educator - HLES Urban Entomology (Lancaster County)
description: This is a full-time, 12-month non-tenured position based in Lincoln, NE with a geographic accountability region including Lancaster, Cass, Otoe, Seward and York Counties . The subject matter focus for this Extension professional is horticulture, landscapes and environmental systems (HLES) with a primary focus on Urban Entomology with an emphasis on plant and food insect issues as well as those insects that affect humans like head lice and bed bugs. This education professional’s primary responsibility is to develop and deliver educational programs and resources as an active participant in Nebraska Extension’s statewide mission. They will work closely with individuals, homeowners, producers, institutions, and organizations in communities to deliver programs in their geographic area and statewide, based on the statewide program area team’s priorities. The HLES Extension professional will contribute to the integrated extension land-grant mission of the home unit and the Institute of Agriculture and Natural Resources (IANR) as an effective scholar and citizen, including support for student recruitment and IANR science literacy efforts in entomology-related initiatives. In HLES we educate and engage Nebraskans, including pest control companies, and property managers, to protect natural resources and habitats, sustainably manage community spaces, be better consumers, and make wise business decisions. Nebraska Extension is an organization that values excellence; as a member of the Nebraska Extension team, you are expected to create and deliver world-class learning experiences focused on critical issues that empower Nebraskans to improve their lives. Expected impacts from this position: Nebraskans will adopt environmentally and economically sustainable integrated best pest management practices to address and reduce pests in urban areas. Nebraskans will increase awareness and adoption of best pest management practices for high-priority invasive and emerging insect pests such as, but not limited to, emerald ash borer, Japanese beetles, bed bugs, ticks and head lice. Nebraskans will adopt practices that enhance beneficial insect ecosystems. Programmatic Responsibilities (approximately 80%): Exemplifies positive and professional behavior and attitude towards colleagues, clients, and partner organizations. Develops and delivers proactive, innovative, and engaging educational programs and products, using teaching methods and strategies that have significant reach, engagement, and impact in your county, accountability region, and, as appropriate, statewide and nationally. Establishes and sustains a strong local and regional clientele base and programming portfolio that is documented and shared with colleagues. Employs innovative strategies and technologies to design, develop, implement, and assess programs for a strong Extension education program/engagement at the county, accountability region, and statewide levels. Engages and teaches in a collaborative learning and problem-solving environment, working with assistants, educators, and specialists to encourage learners to adopt research-based decision-making information. Deliberately engages and works closely with one or more Extension specialists to fulfill your Extension responsibilities. Collaborates with specialists and research faculty to conduct applied and validation research (e.g., landscape or community) that can be amplified via multiple engagement platforms. Shows robust contributions to multidisciplinary team settings with Extension professionals and other internal and external partners to translate and convey the latest research-based information. Engages local, regional, and statewide partners to identify and address high-priority issues where Extension is particularly well positioned to contribute. Fosters a culture of collaboration with local, regional and statewide leaders that nurtures and strengthens positive relationships among the University, its partners, and the people we serve. Employs innovative, revenue-generating practices to secure funding and develop partnerships that expand Extension program’s reach and impact. Creates ongoing programming revenue that supports the viability of individuals, teams, units, and the System. Leads and contributes value to high-performing Extension programming teams. Engages in personal and professional development opportunities that enhance knowledge, skills, and competencies relevant to your role. Supports youth development programs by contributing to areas related to your specific assignment. Conducts need assessments, identifies priorities, develops various program and engagement platforms to connect with a variety of audiences, measure program impact, and report the results in your annual report as well as to Extension boards, County Commissioners and Supervisors, State Senators, key stakeholders, at professional meetings, and in professional and Extension publications when appropriate. Educators will collaborate with lead educators, Extension specialists, Extension advisory committees, and local stakeholders within their accountability region to assess needs and offer access to engagement opportunities through various platforms (e.g., focus groups, surveys, stakeholder meetings, etc.). Participates in teams comprised of assistants, educators, specialists, other staff or faculty, industry, and community leaders. These teams focus on current or future needs or strengths and strategize in program areas where you contribute. Fosters a culture of collaboration with local leaders and accountability in the region that nurtures and builds positive relationships among the University, its partners, and the communities we serve. Cultivates open and welcoming learning environments. Completes PEARS data entry and reporting requirements. Fulfills annual IANR reporting requirements, including an individual impact report. Organizational Citizenship (approximately 20%): Contributes to and supports the Lead Educator as described in the Roles and Responsibilities of the Lead Educator document as determined in partnership with the supervisor(s). Coordinates with engagement zone coordinator(s) and other Extension professionals locally and in accountability region to develop a robust Nebraska Extension presence by Cooperating with local faculty and staff in a team environment to promote Extension’s educational opportunities and impact in the host county. Cultivating a culture of collaboration with local leaders and community members that builds positive relationships between the University and the community. Supporting the engagement of advisory or policy groups such as the Extension Board, Ag Society, or County Commissioners/Board of Supervisors. Understands and adheres to Equal Employment Opportunity compliance efforts. Accepts committee assignments, reporting responsibilities, and other special ad hoc assignments as requested at the administrative unit, college, division, institute, and/or university level. This twelve-month, non-tenure position carries the title of open rank extension educator or extension instructor, depending on the candidate’s level of education. Those possessing a graduate level degree in the requested area of instruction will be considered for an open rank educator position, a full-time, promotable, non-tenure track appointment. Those in possession of an undergraduate degree in the requested area of instruction will be considered for an instructor position, a full-time, non-promotable, non-tenure track appointment that will be renewed annually for a maximum of five years in the appointment. If hired as an instructor, the incumbent will be expected to make satisfactory progress towards and complete a master’s degree within the initial five-year appointment period. As part of the Nebraska benefits package, UNL offers tuition remission for full-time employees, up to 15 credit hours per year. Once the master’s degree is earned within that period, the position will advance to an assistant extension educator appointment. Some travel is required. Must meet driver standards according to UNL policy and have a valid driver’s license. Recognizing that collaboration and participation in teams enhances creativity, innovation, impact and a sense of belonging, the IANR and Nebraska Extension are committed to creating learning, research, and Extension programming environments where the unique contributions of each individual are acknowledged and valued. At IANR, we see every person and every interaction as important to our collective wellbeing and our ability to deliver on our mission. This position is not eligible for employment-based permanent residency sponsorship. UNL may be able to sponsor a temporary work authorization (e.g., H-1B) for the successful candidate.

Working Title: Research Technician II - Temporary (Full-time) Department: Nutrition & Health Sci IANR-0847 Requisition Number: S_260826 Posting Open Date: 10/08/2026 Application Review Date: (To ensure consideration, please submit all application materials before review date): 10/15/2026 Open Until Filled: Yes Description of Work: The laboratory of Dr. Tomasz Bednarski in the Department of Nutrition and Health Sciences ( NHS ) at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln ( UNL ) conducts in vitro and in vivo experiments, as well as molecular, biochemical, computational, and multi-omics analyses, to investigate the molecular and biochemical mechanisms underlying the development of metabolic diseases. Additional information about the Bednarski Lab and its research program can be found at: https://cehs.unl.edu/nhs/bednarski-lab/ . The Bednarski Lab is seeking a highly motivated Temporary Research Technician II to join our team and support the day-to-day operations of the laboratory. This position offers an excellent opportunity for professional and personal growth while contributing to cutting-edge biomedical research within a diverse and collaborative team of internationally recognized scientists. Current research projects focus on understanding the metabolic alterations associated with the pathogenesis of cardiovascular and liver diseases. The successful candidate will support studies utilizing transcriptomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, proteomics, and fluxomics, as well as a variety of traditional molecular biology and biochemical techniques. This position is ideal for a self-motivated, intellectually curious, and detail-oriented individual who is capable of working independently, thinking critically, and embracing new challenges. The successful candidate will demonstrate willingness to learn new techniques, contribute to a collaborative research environment, and pursue excellence in scientific research. As a full time, Temporary Research Technician II , you will: Order laboratory supplies and maintain accurate inventory records. Operate, monitor, and perform routine maintenance on assigned laboratory equipment in accordance with established protocols. Maintain the cleanliness and organization of laboratory equipment, glassware, and workspaces. Properly store research data, samples, and laboratory protocols in designated locations and formats. Organize and maintain accurate written and electronic records of experimental procedures, results, and analyses. Support laboratory personnel in maintaining compliance with biosafety regulations and laboratory safety procedures. Assist with collecting and organizing data to support ongoing research projects. title: Assistant or Associate Professor - Engineering Education
description: The College of Engineering (CoE) at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (https://engineering.unl.edu) is seeking applications for a tenure-track or tenured faculty position at the rank of assistant or associate professor in the area of engineering education. The primary faculty appointment will be in one of the following academic units in the College of Engineering: Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, Electrical & Computer Engineering, Durham School of Architectural Engineering and Construction (specifically Construction Management or Construction Engineering), depending on an applicant’s qualifications. Candidates selected will be expected to contribute to the academic programs in their CoE unit through teaching undergraduate courses as well as teaching graduate-level engineering education courses and supervising graduate research within the PhD in Engineering - Specialization in Engineering Education Research program. Candidates will be expected to establish externally funded discipline-based education research (DBER) programs and collaborate with researchers within CoE to study and transform engineering education through fundamental and applied research. The DBER initiative at UNL’s College of Engineering (https://dber-engr.unl.edu/) boasts four tenured or tenure-track faculty members and 6 PhD alumni since our program’s launch in 2020. DBER faculty reside in their respective disciplines where, through their presence and participation on their faculties, they build relationships and collaborations with their disciplinary colleagues to conduct engineering discipline-specific education research that focuses on aspects unique to the education and preparation of professionals in their discipline. DBER faculty also operate as a community to conduct cross-disciplinary engineering education research focused on aspects common to the education and preparation of all engineering professionals.

title: Asst/Assoc Professor - Secondary Mathematics Education
description: The Department of Teaching, Learning and Teacher Education ( https://cehs.unl.edu/tlte ) seeks a tenure-line Assistant or Associate Professor of Secondary Mathematics Education who can help prepare effective educators; collaborate with department colleagues, mathematics and STEM content specialists, and classroom teachers, and attract increased national interest and funding to nationally visible programs in mathematics education at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln. Our new colleague will be joining a dynamic and committed community of scholars in the department and a collaborative faculty group in secondary education. The program graduates 10-12 teacher candidates yearly and graduate math education courses that enroll 10-27 in-service teachers each during academic year semesters and during summer terms. Our programs benefit from long-standing and unique partnerships with the Department of Mathematics in the College of Arts and Sciences and the Center for Science, Mathematics, and Computer Education. We anticipate expanding our faculty in elementary, secondary, and mathematics education not only to prepare students for initial teacher certification, but also to provide professional learning in graduate education and expand opportunities for funded research and scholarship. UNL is the University of Nebraska system’s flagship university and a member of the Big 10 Academic Alliance. TLTE is recognized across UNL for distinguished teaching, strong collaborations with exceptional partner schools and has a reputation for scholarship that embraces diverse research methodologies. The candidate who fills this position will teach and advise undergraduate and graduate students in mathematics education. TLTE seeks a colleague who possess the understanding, commitment, and ability to contribute collaboratively to robust elementary and secondary education programs and mathematics education in the context of continuing demographic change in the state and nation. The College of Education and Human Sciences strives to be a vibrant, welcoming, and caring community driven by our mission to enhance the lives of individuals, families, schools, and communities, and strengthening the relationships among them. At the University of Nebraska, we strive for excellence in all that we do. True excellence requires that every individual is able to work and learn in an atmosphere of respect, dignity, and acceptance. Our commitment requires each of us to continuously ensure our interactions be respectful, protect free speech, and inspire academic freedom. Position Responsibilities Teach undergraduate coursework in Secondary Mathematics Education, including mathematics methods courses. Work with and supervise professional practicum students and student teachers. Teach graduate courses in K-12 Mathematics Education and related areas of expertise. Advise and mentor master's and doctoral students. Conduct a scholarly program of research appropriate to rank. Engage actively in collaboration and program development within and across content areas, programs, departments and colleges. Provide outreach to schools, other educational institutions, and communities. For additional questions, please contact Dr. Amanda Henson, Search Committee Chair, at amanda.thomas@unl.edu .

title: Open Rank Professor - Plant Metabolism
description: The Department of Biochemistry and the Center for Plant Science Innovation at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (UNL) invite applications for a tenure-track nine-month (academic year) faculty position of open rank (assistant/associate/full professor). This appointment is apportioned as 80% research and 20% teaching. Applicants are sought who will develop a vigorous, internationally recognized research program that seeks to identify novel metabolic pathways, regulatory mechanisms and/or biological processes with the goal of translating findings into strategies for crop improvement and/or bio-based products that support sustainable agriculture and biotechnology to enhance human health. Researchers will be able to leverage UNL’s extensive research infrastructure that includes the Plant Transformation Core Research Facility (PTCRF), multi-location biotech fields, and advanced field and greenhouse phenotyping platforms, to validate and scale their discoveries. The Department of Biochemistry provides a robust environment for molecular research, offering access to state-of-the-art resources through shared equipment and the Nebraska Center for Biotechnology. Candidates will have the opportunity to utilize the UNL Cryo-EM facility for structural biology, mass spectrometry for metabolomics and proteomics, and bioinformatics and systems biology computational resources. The university offers a highly collaborative environment to develop plant-focused research programs with affiliated resources provided by the University Research Centers (Center for Plant Science Innovation, Center for Integrated Biomolecular Communication, Redox Biology Center, Center for Virology), Holland Computing Center, the Quantitative Life Sciences Initiative, Nebraska Innovation Campus and the Center for Biological Chemistry and Complex Biosystems graduate training programs. The University Research Centers and UNL provide cutting-edge research facilities that support multiple-omics, bioinformatics, supercomputing, flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, TEM, SEM, and metabolic engineering. A competitive start-up package and appropriate laboratory and office space will be offered. About Us To learn about UNL benefits and your total compensation, please see: https://go.unl.edu/aboutus . title: Dean of the College of Journalism and Mass Communications
description: The College of Journalism and Mass Communications The College of Journalism and Mass Communications is an inclusive community of faculty and staff committed to providing a top-quality, hands-on education to emerging professionals in advertising, broadcasting, journalism, public relations, and sports media and communication. The college is an important contributor to education, research, creative activity and outreach at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln. The faculty upholds the core principles of journalism and mass communication education and seeks to be leaders in the evolving communications environment. Through excellence in teaching, research and creative activity, the college educates ethical, socially responsible, well-rounded, flexible, fair and quick-minded graduates who carry those traits into the world. The strength of the college is exemplified by the success of its students and graduates and its numerous professional partnerships. The college is one of 11 chosen to be part of the Carnegie-Knight Initiative on the Future of Journalism and the only collegiate recipient of the Robert F. Kennedy Journalism Grand Prize. Its students have consistently finished in the top 10 in the Hearst Journalism Awards annual competition; this year, students won 1st and 3rd place in the National Writing Championship. The college was also the 2022 national champion in the Public Relations Student Society of America Bateman Case Study Competition. The college programs have been nationally accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications since 1972 and are the only accredited journalism offerings in the state of Nebraska. It offers bachelor’s and master’s degree programs that prepare students for careers in a wide range of media positions. Enrollment in the college is approximately 1,100 undergraduate and 75 graduate students. Students experience a variety of special hands-on learning opportunities including: The Experience Lab where students gain hands-on experience working with faculty liaisons and professional mentors, building on their academic skill set while exploring their professional interests in one of the college's media outlets; first-year learning communities; Jacht, a student-run advertising agency; 90.3 KRNU, a student-run FM radio station that just underwent an equipment upgrade; the Nebraska News Service, which provides state government coverage for smaller Nebraska newspapers and radio stations; an annual international photojournalism trip; investigative depth reporting such as a recent investigation into the Nebraska prison system; and an advertising and a public relations national competition team. The college has 35 full-time faculty members plus a large number of highly qualified part-time faculty from industry. The college faculty includes two Pulitzer Prize winners, recipients of Emmys in broadcasting and a National Gold ADDY award honoree. The journalism faculty includes veterans from Business Week, the Miami Herald, the Detroit News, ProPublica and the Tampa Bay Times. The broadcast faculty includes individuals who have held key positions with news stations in Omaha, Kansas City, and San Francisco. The advertising and public relations faculty includes former executives at Leo Burnett, J. Walter Thompson, IGN Entertainment, and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The Opportunity The University of Nebraska-Lincoln seeks an innovative, inspiring and forward-looking academic leader to serve as the next Dean of the College of Journalism and Mass Communications. The incoming Dean will have the opportunity to direct the vision of an energetic and engaged faculty, staff and student population. The new Dean will enjoy the advantages of a growing endowment with strong alumni and media support. The college’s educational experience is grounded in experiential learning, giving students meaningful opportunities to apply their skills in professional, real-world settings through strong connections with media, industry, and community partners. The Dean will have the unique opportunity to lead curricular innovation during a time of rapid change in journalism, media and communication and help define the future of the profession. The college looks to an exciting future under the direction of an outstanding leader to further broaden and deepen its impact. The Position The Dean reports directly to the Executive Vice Chancellor and is the chief academic and administrative officer of the College of Journalism and Mass Communications. The Dean has the responsibility for the strategic, programmatic, financial, fundraising, and management operations that support the mission and vision of the College of Journalism and Mass Communications and its role within the university and across the state. The Dean will join a group of fellow deans and campus leaders who are collaborative, supportive and committed. The Dean works alongside campus leaders to advance the values and mission of the university, ensuring the College’s efforts are in alignment with the overall priorities and goals. The incoming Dean will: Have the opportunity to define and implement the college’s next strategic vision with the input of talented faculty, staff, students, alumni and external advisory boards; Further the development of a relevant and distinctive identity for the college; Serve as a public voice to develop the reputation of the college externally on national and international stages, within the profession and private industry; Assure the continued prominence of the faculty by prioritizing the recruiting and retention of distinguished faculty at all levels; Support and engage staff, encourage their growth, and ensure they play an active role in the College's success and future. Cultivate academic programs that demonstrate professional relevance, impact, and sustainability, and champion the distinct, yet interconnected disciplines in the college; Work to fully realize and enact the college and university commitment to community and belonging, ensuring that all individuals and interactions matter; Seek out and continue valuable collaborations with other academic units and partners; Promote and support a strong research and creative activity agenda, including attracting external funding from federal agencies, corporations and foundations and continue to grow the College’s portfolio by expanding partnerships and pursuing new opportunities; Appreciate and foster the dual mission of research/creative activity and teaching to maintain an academic and professional focus; Assure that the college continues to serve its students with academic programs of the highest quality and effectiveness, promoting and sustaining practices for experiential learning, student success, persistence, retention, graduation and placement; Continue an upward trajectory of enrollment in the college; Engage alumni and other external supporters to advance the mission of the college; Take a leading role in attracting interested donors to support the college’s mission; and Be an engaged academic leader at the university, working collaboratively and advancing the overall mission and priorities of the campus.

title: Assistant Professor of Practice
description: Position Overview We seek a collaborative technical leader with comprehensive expertise in scenic construction and engineering, rigging and safety, fabrication, and related production disciplines, along with experience with contemporary entertainment technologies such as Vectorworks and/or AutoCAD, automation and show-control systems, CNC fabrication, and 3D printing. The successful candidate will be committed to practice-based learning and understand how foundational craft knowledge informs and enhances technological innovation. They will bring a passion for interdisciplinary collaboration and preparing students for current and future career paths across the entertainment industry. We seek a colleague who is curious about new technologies and methodologies, comfortable working in an evolving educational and production environment, and interested in contributing to the continued development of the School’s curriculum and pedagogical approaches. The successful candidate will have experience managing complex technical operations; demonstrated project-management and leadership skills; and the ability to work collaboratively with students, faculty, staff, guest artists, and industry partners. Key Responsibilities Technical Leadership and Production Oversee the physical construction and engineering aspects of School productions, including rigging, fabrication, and safety. Develop and implement technical systems supporting both conventional and emerging production methodologies. Integrate new production technologies into existing production processes and workflows. Provide technical leadership and problem-solving across the School’s production activities. Collaborate with faculty and staff across Entertainment Design & Production, Theatre, Film, and Emerging Media Arts to develop shared technical resources and workflows. Maintain and advance professional standards for safety, fabrication, rigging, and technical production. Teaching and Mentorship Teach and mentor students in technical theatre, entertainment technology, fabrication, and evolving production methodologies. Depending upon curricular needs and the candidate’s areas of expertise, courses may include: Computer-Aided Drafting Automation and Computer-Controlled Systems Rigging Special Effects Metalworking Entertainment Engineering Advanced Materials and Fabrication Advanced Carpentry CNC and Dimensional Printing Technologies The successful candidate will mentor students through hands-on, practice-based learning and help them connect foundational construction and fabrication skills with contemporary entertainment technologies. Curriculum and Interdisciplinary Collaboration Develop course work within the curricular structure that connects traditional craft, fabrication, engineering, and emerging production technologies. Foster interdisciplinary learning opportunities across theatre, film, and emerging media. Explore new technologies, methodologies, and teaching approaches as entertainment production continues to evolve. Contribute, as appropriate, to online and digitally supported curriculum development. Facilities and Technical Resources Contribute to the strategic development of technical facilities supporting the School’s expanding curricular and production needs. Help oversee scene shops, fabrication spaces, prop and storage areas, and associated making and production facilities. Ensure that facilities and technical practices meet current safety standards while supporting innovative production practices. Participate in planning for equipment, technologies, and infrastructure supporting Entertainment Design & Production and interdisciplinary production. Professional and Industry Engagement Maintain active engagement with current practices and emerging technologies within the entertainment industry. Help develop student connections to internships, apprenticeships, professional opportunities, and industry partners. Represent the School through appropriate professional organizations, conferences, and industry engagement. Contribute to conversations about the changing nature of technical production and entertainment education.

title: Assistant Professor - Elementary Mathematics Education
description: The Department of Teaching, Learning and Teacher Education ( https://cehs.unl.edu/tlte ) at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln invites applications for a tenure-line Assistant Professor of Elementary Mathematics Education who can help prepare effective educators, collaborate with department colleagues, mathematics and STEM content specialists, and classroom teachers, as well as attract increased national interest and funding to nationally visible programs in mathematics education at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln. title: Associate Director
description: The Associate Director leads undergraduate recruitment within Nebraska and key national markets, with a strong focus on transfer recruitment. The position executes and informs strategies to grow enrollment and strengthen pipelines from alternative high schools, community colleges, four-year institutions, military-affiliated populations, adult learners, and workforce partners. Under the guidance of the Executive Director of Admissions, this role uses data to identify new opportunities to expand the undergraduate student pipeline. As part of the Admissions Leadership Team in the Academic Services and Enrollment Management (ASEM) division, the Associate Director will collaborate with peers across the division, using data to guide recruitment and provide leadership to achieve enrollment goals. This position provides leadership and direct supervision for staff responsible for undergraduate student recruitment, working closely with the team to design and activate effective outreach, pipeline development, and recruitment strategies. The Associate Director trains staff in best practices and directs both in-person and virtual recruitment efforts to convert prospective student leads. The Associate Director reviews recruitment data and territory results and makes data-driven decisions to achieve enrollment targets. This position also provides backup support for the Associate Director of recruitment within Nebraska. The Associate Director exercises judgment in enforcing admissions policies, making recruitment decisions, and overseeing functional initiatives aligned with strategic priorities. The role works with units within ASEM and across campus to align recruitment objectives with university initiatives. As a liaison between Admissions and academic colleges, the Associate Director identifies undergraduate enrollment opportunities, streamlines pathways, and leverages resources such as articulation agreements to provide students with clear guidance. This role builds strong partnerships with advisors, counselors, workforce partners, and others to expand access and foster successful undergraduate enrollment pipelines. Additionally, the Associate Director coordinates with Visitor Experience to ensure effective resource allocation for on-campus recruitment events and activities. When needed, the position provides leadership support to the broader admissions team and may serve as a proxy for the Executive Director of Admissions. Regular travel, including evenings and weekends, is required. This position and its supervised staff are based in Lincoln, Nebraska. Travel to partner institutions, workforce organizations, recruitment events, and priority markets is expected. Please note: Sponsorship will not be offered for this position.

description: The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at UNL is seeking applicants for a tenure-line position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor with a focus in computer engineering systems, computer architecture, or networking, including connections to systems engineering. The person hired into this position is expected to develop a nationally recognized research program and contribute to academic programs in computer engineering, with opportunities to support interdisciplinary systems engineering research and education. Research and educational activities may include: Developing an externally funded research program in computer engineering systems, computer architecture, or networking. Developing and teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in these areas to prepare students for careers in industry, research, and academia. Mentoring undergraduate and graduate students and advancing collaborative research, capstone projects, and industry partnerships. The position will be based on the Scott Campus in Omaha, NE, and housed in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, with opportunities to support teaching and research on UNL’s City Campus in Lincoln. This location will facilitate collaboration with faculty across Nebraska Engineering, the University of Nebraska at Omaha, and relevant industry and government partners. Candidates are expected to have an outstanding publication record, a history of funded research, and a strong national/international reputation in the area of computer and system engineering and related topics. Preference will be given to candidates with experience building higher education degree programs. As part of this initiative, the Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering ( https://ece.unl.edu ) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant/Associate Professor level that will provide a nucleus for further hiring in this technical area. The Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering consists of approximately 35 tenured/tenure-track faculty, 400 undergraduate students, and 120 graduate students co-located in two cities, Lincoln and Omaha, Nebraska. An outstanding infrastructure exists for conducting research, including central facilities housing state-of-the-art instrumentation and computing, including the Holland Computing Center ( https://hcc.unl.edu ). Opportunities for collaborations across the University of Nebraska include the University of Nebraska Medical Center; the University of Nebraska-Omaha College of Information Science & Technology; the Nebraska Center for Energy Sciences Research; the Center for Brain, Biology, and Behavior; the Nebraska Athletic Performance Laboratory; the Midwest Roadside Safety Facility; Innovation Campus; and other state- and federally-funded research centers and programs.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The Psychology Department at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln is recruiting a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Addiction Science who studies antecedents, processes, and/or consequences of substance use and/or misuse. Potential areas of interest include but are not limited to developmental trajectories and/or aging processes; biological and neurobehavioral mechanisms, including human or animal models; social and interpersonal processes; addiction-related cognition and decision-making; risk and resilience factors such as trauma, stress, or comorbidity with mental health disorders; and addiction-related prevention, treatment, policy, and laws. Experience with advanced quantitative approaches is welcome but not required for the position. Responsibilities include maintaining an active research program, including the pursuit of external funding, and teaching graduate and undergraduate courses in addiction and substance use. Given that addiction and substance use are integral to a number of other disciplines, the successful candidate could be a valuable contributor to multidisciplinary research efforts involving multiple units on campus (e.g., Center for Brain, Biology & Behavior; Rural Drug Addiction Research Center; Minority Health Disparities Initiative; Nebraska Athletic Performance Lab; Center for Research on Children, Youth, Families, and Schools; Center on Children, Families, and the Law; the College of Education and Human Sciences; the Law School). The Department of Psychology values a collegial and supportive working environment in which a range of experiences and perspectives strengthens research and teaching, and we welcome applicants who will contribute to that environment.

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate in Plant Ecophysiology
description: A postdoctoral position examining plant physiological responses to environmental variability is available in the lab of Dr. Nick Smith in the School of Biological Sciences at the University of Nebraska – Lincoln (UNL). The Smith Ecophysiology Lab examines the responses of plants and ecosystems to change in abiotic conditions and the resulting feedbacks from these responses to global change. The successful applicant will join a vibrant group of researchers in the lab, which is housed within the Beadle Center at UNL. The postdoc will work closely with an international group of collaborators focused on improving understanding and predictability of plant physiological processes and their feedbacks to ecosystem processes under global change. The postdoctoral research associate will be given freedom to explore questions and develop projects pertinent to their interests and experiences. These should overlap with one or more of the following ongoing themes in the lab: Plant physiological acclimation to global change Development of quantitative plant ecophysiological theory The impact of belowground resource availability on plant physiological processes Scaling from leaves to the globe Interactions between plants and microbial symbionts and the impact on physiology Species and functional type specific responses to global change Land surface and Earth system modeling Plant resource uptake and use optimization Within the lab and at UNL, the postdoc will have access to state-of-the-art ecophysiological equipment, growth chamber and greenhouse facilities, as well as computational facilities both within the lab and through the University’s High Performance Computing Center. The Smith Ecophysiology Lab is also part of the Nutrient Network. The successful candidate will carry out empirical and modeling research examining plant physiological responses and feedbacks to environmental variability. The specific projects will be tailored to the individual’s interests and expertise. The position will also involve mentoring of graduate and undergraduate students in the lab.

title: Extension Instructor or Open Rank Extension Educator - Water & Cropping Systems (Dodge Co.)
description: Overview This position is based in Fremont, NE, with the geographic accountability region of Dodge, Cuming, and Washington Counties. This is a twelve-month, non-tenure track position. The extension professional serves as a trusted, research-based educational leader connecting the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, the agricultural industry, and Nebraska communities through practical, science-based extension programming and applied research. The extension professional is expected to maintain a visible and engaged presence within the communities they serve and become a recognized first source of trusted, unbiased agricultural information. Success in this role requires strong teaching and communication skills, community engagement, relationship building, leadership in agricultural education, and the ability to foster meaningful partnerships that support Nebraska agriculture and rural communities. Primary programmatic responsibilities are developing and delivering impactful water and cropping systems extension programming that: a) improves agricultural profitability and sustainability, b) reduces environmental risk, c) encourages natural resources stewardship, d) enhances agricultural resiliency, and e) expands public understanding of food, forage, grain, and fiber production systems. The extension professional translates complex research into practical, solution-based educational experiences for diverse audiences including farmers, ranchers, agribusiness professionals, community leaders, and the general public. Educational delivery methods may include workshops, field demonstrations, applied research trials, digital resources, consultations, media outreach, and collaborative partnerships. As a member of the statewide Water and Cropping Systems team, the educator actively contributes to the development of innovative, research-based resources and interdisciplinary solutions addressing current and emerging agricultural challenges for their assigned region and across Nebraska. The position requires collaboration with university faculty, extension colleagues, industry partners, agencies, and local stakeholders to identify needs and deliver responsive programming. This position carries the title of open rank extension educator or extension instructor, depending on the candidate’s level of education. Those possessing a graduate-level degree in the requested area of instruction will be considered for an open rank educator position, a full-time, promotable, non-tenure track appointment. Those in possession of an undergraduate degree in the requested area of instruction will be considered for an instructor position, a full-time, non-promotable, non-tenure track appointment that will be renewed annually for a maximum of five years in the appointment. If hired as an instructor, the incumbent will be expected to make satisfactory progress toward and complete a master’s degree within the initial five-year appointment period. As part of the Nebraska benefits package, UNL offers tuition remission for full-time employees, up to 15 credit hours per year. Once the master’s degree is earned within that period, the position will advance to an assistant extension educator appointment. PROGRAMMATIC RESPONSIBILITIES (approximately 80%) Exemplifies positive and professional behavior and attitude towards colleagues, clients, and partner organizations. title: Assistant Professor - Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
description: The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date in the 2027–2028 academic year. The department seeks an outstanding candidate who will establish a nationally visible, externally funded research program in catalysis and contribute to excellence in undergraduate and graduate education. Catalysis is a core discipline in chemical engineering and a central enabling technology for advances in energy, sustainability, advanced materials, agriculture, and value-added chemical manufacturing. Research areas of interest include, but are not limited to, heterogeneous and homogeneous catalysis; electrocatalysis and photocatalysis; biocatalysis; catalytic materials and interfaces; reaction engineering and kinetics; computational and data-enabled catalysis; integrated experimental–computational approaches; decarbonization; hydrogen technologies; carbon capture, utilization, and conversion; biofuels and biobased manufacturing; and catalysis for advanced manufacturing. Candidates whose work complements and expands existing departmental strengths are encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will be expected to develop a strong scholarly record and externally funded research program; teach undergraduate and graduate courses in chemical engineering, including courses related to reaction engineering, kinetics, and catalysis as appropriate; mentor undergraduate and graduate students; and contribute to departmental, college, and university service. The position offers opportunities for collaboration with faculty engaged in experimental and computational catalysis and with campus research entities including the Nebraska Center for Materials and Nanoscience and the Nebraska Energy Sciences Research Center. The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering provides an outstanding environment for research and education, with opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration across the University of Nebraska–Lincoln and the broader University of Nebraska system. The department's strategic growth in catalysis will support research and workforce development in areas important to Nebraska and the broader Midwest while enhancing competitiveness for federal and collaborative research initiatives.

title: Academic Success Coach
description: The Center for Academic Success and Transition (CAST) is seeking a passionate, student-centered professional to serve as an Academic Success Coach. This 20-hour, 10-month position is primarily responsible for providing one-to-one academic success coaching (in person and via Zoom) that helps undergraduate students develop the skills, strategies, and confidence needed to thrive at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln. Academic Success Coaches partner with students to strengthen time management, learning strategies, goal setting, motivation, organization, course preparation, and school-life balance while helping them navigate the challenges and opportunities of college. The position also includes proactive outreach and follow-up with students, management of assigned student caseloads, and delivery of presentations and workshops focused on academic success. The Academic Success Coach collaborates with colleagues across CAST and the university to connect students with campus resources, support student success initiatives, and contribute to a welcoming, student-centered environment. title: Assistant/Associate Professor - Audiology
description: The Department of Special Education and Communication Disorders at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (UNL) is seeking applications for a tenure-leading Assistant or Associate Professor in Audiology. This 9-month (academic year) appointment will contribute to the department’s teaching and research missions, with an emphasis on developing a nationally and internationally recognized research program in audiology. This position will be located in Lincoln, Nebraska, with a projected start date of August 16, 2027. The Department of Special Education and Communication Disorders at UNL is housed in a state-of-the-art facility in a newly expanded and renovated building. We have access to teaching and research equipment and resources that can help you launch a successful career. You will teach alongside our expert faculty in our spiral curriculum, where we integrate the expertise of our clinical and research faculty to create an environment where students are coached to make connections between research and practice. Our proximity to and collaborations with Boys Town National Research Hospital, Madonna Rehabilitation Hospital, UNL’s Center for Brain, Biology, and Behavior (CB3), and the University of Nebraska Medical Center may provide opportunities for you to build your program of research. We are excited to welcome a new colleague at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor with expertise in audiology to join our collaborative and supportive faculty. We are especially interested in candidates whose work focuses on hearing and balance sciences, amplification and hearing aids, vestibular assessment and management, cognition and aging, or pediatric audiology. At the same time, we encourage applicants from a wide range of research areas who share our commitment to advancing knowledge and improving the lives of individuals with hearing and balance needs. RESPONSIBILITIES Build a collaborative research program that contributes to the advancement of audiology and has the potential to attract external support; teach undergraduate and graduate courses in areas of expertise; mentor and guide student research; and engage in professional service within the department, college, university, and broader community. MORE ABOUT US The Department of Special Education and Communication Disorders ( https://cehs.unl.edu/secd ) houses graduate programs in Audiology, Speech Language Pathology, and Special Education. SECD’s Audiology program is ranked among the top 20 audiology programs in the U.S. Faculty conduct cutting-edge research in global hearing health, communication access, hearing aids, cochlear implants, and neuroimaging. Our research thrives through interprofessional and interdepartmental collaboration, bringing together expertise from speech-language pathology, special education, engineering, athletics, psychology, and beyond. description: Ranked as one of the Best Employers in Nebraska and certified as a Lincoln Family-Friendly workplace, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln is committed to providing a work environment and culture that fosters personal and professional success and satisfaction. As the Lead Water Analyst, you will: Plan, design, maintain, and/or improve campus-wide water chemistry testing and treatment programs to ensure safe, compliant, cost-effective, and high-performing operation of boilers, chillers, cooling towers, and conditioned water systems. Administer and execute water and steam chemistry programs to maintain regulatory compliance, maximize thermodynamic efficiency, support system reliability and capacity, and reduce corrosion, forced outages, and maintenance costs. Develop, implement, maintain, and oversee operational procedures, logs, documentation tools, and daily water chemistry practices to ensure consistent performance, regulatory compliance, and adherence to safety and environmental programs. Oversee daily water chemistry testing and treatment, including collection, analysis, documentation, and interpretation of water samples to verify compliance with established guidelines. Collect, monitor, analyze, and document water chemistry across plant conditioning systems, fuel samples, calculate and adjust chemical treatment requirements, and recommend or make equipment adjustments, including blow downs and chemical feed controls, to maintain proper system performance. Verify compliance with water treatment procedures and notify plant management of deviations from established guidelines. Monitor system performance, troubleshoot equipment issues, and perform preventive maintenance, repairs, outage-related testing, initiate testing to determine root cause analysis, and notify applicable personnel when applicable. Oversee and perform metallurgical testing and intervention activities for boilers and other plant systems and components. Evaluate, recommend, and install chemical treatment equipment and electronic programming for chemical feed control systems. Receive, prioritize, and complete work orders related to water and wastewater systems. Coordinate and manage chemical, water treatment, equipment, and regulatory projects, including cost estimates and ongoing cost control. Participate in planning activities related to treated water and wastewater systems to support future operational needs. Lead compliance activities related to wastewater, stormwater, hazardous waste management, chemical safety documentation (MSDS/Right to Know), spill prevention, and pollution incident prevention requirements. Coordinate with Environmental Health and Safety to support compliance for water chemistry operations and hazardous materials and participate in safety committees to promote adherence to applicable safety standards, regulations, and internal procedures. Maintain, prepare, and submit all necessary water treatment, equipment, and chemical safety documentation, and ensure records are current and accessible. Train and support plant personnel on safe water treatment operations, including systems, equipment, chemical controls, and disinfection products, through ongoing coordination, coaching, and EHS collaboration. Research vendors and coordinate purchasing of specialized supplies, equipment, and contracted services, and manage and evaluate contractor performance by providing feedback to support plant water chemistry and water treatment operations. Monitor and control chemical inventory, track chemical usage and expenditures, and provide budget input for chemistry operations, projects, and regulatory compliance needs. Oversee and perform safe storage, handling, transfer, delivery notification, and disposal of hazardous and corrosive chemicals. Participate in an on-call rotation to respond to and support emergency situations involving water chemistry issues. Provide leadership and oversight of staff performance, including setting goals, communicating expectations, delivering coaching and training, conducting evaluations, documenting performance, and recommending salary adjustments. Sponsorship will not be offered for this position. title: Survey Hydrogeologist
department: Survey Division - School of Nat Res
description: The Conservation and Survey Division (Nebraska Geological Survey), the natural resource survey component of the School of Natural Resources, is a unique, multi-disciplinary research, service and data-resource organization. The Division's mission is to investigate and record information about Nebraska's geologic history, its rock and mineral resources, the quantity and quality of its water resources, land cover and other aspects of its geography, as well as the nature, distribution and uses of its soils. As a Survey Hydrogeologist, you will: Conduct applied research on hydrogeology and geology . Assist in implementing and maintaining Conservation and Survey Division’s databases, web services, and ongoing research programs to be used in water resources management, research, and education. Provide technical support to state and local agencies, including the Natural Resources Districts across Nebraska Participate in the geologic mapping program. Prepare formal and informal technical reports and presentations on water resources projects and issues. Develop and deliver programs/activities related to hydrogeology, sustainable use of groundwater, and quantity and quality of groundwater. Provide water resources service to governmental and educational agencies, industry, and the general public. Assist public and governmental agencies in developing programs to monitor and manage water and other natural resources. Respond to questions by evaluating and interpreting data. Present findings at various venues including seminars, workshops, guest lectures, and national scientific meetings. Work collaboratively with School of Natural Resources Environmental Science faculty and Conservation and Survey Division personnel. description: The Nebraska Center for Research on Children, Youth, Families, and Schools (CYFS), in partnership with the College of Education and Human Sciences (CEHS) at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, seeks an accomplished research leader to serve as Director.
