CYFS is a nationally recognized, revenue-generating research center advancing high-impact scholarship in the social, behavioral, and educational sciences. For more than two decades, CYFS has played a central role in driving research excellence, external funding, and interdisciplinary collaboration across the University of Nebraska system. As the sole collegewide research center in CEHS, CYFS provides critical research infrastructure and expert pre- and post-award grantsmanship support—driving faculty productivity, securing competitive external funding, promoting research partnerships, and ensuring high-impact research implementation and outcomes. Learn more at https://cyfs.unl.edu/ . Why this role, why now. CYFS is entering a pivotal leadership transition following more than two decades of sustained growth and success under its founding director. The Center is financially stable, highly productive, and supported by an experienced research and administrative team. At a time when federal funding increasingly favors interdisciplinary, multi-institutional research, this role offers a rare opportunity for an established leader to build on a strong foundation, scale major research initiatives, and shape the next phase of CYFS’s national impact. The Director will provide strategic leadership for a mature, high-performing research organization operating in an increasingly competitive federal funding environment. Key Responsibilities Sustaining and expanding external funding. Guiding long-term strategic planning. Strengthening interdisciplinary research collaborations. Overseeing fiscal and administrative operations. Positioning CYFS for continued growth, visibility, and scholarly impact. Play a central role in shaping research priorities and mentoring research faculty and staff. Cultivating internal and external partnerships at the university, community, state, and national levels. The position is expected to be a fiscal year (FY) appointment with a split FTE of up to 0.75 FTE as Director apportioned as 100% administration and supported with an administrative stipend. The position is expected to have an apportionment that is aligned with teaching a minimum of one course a year. The Director will report to the CEHS Dean and will hold a faculty appointment within CEHS, commensurate with disciplinary background and scholarly accomplishments. The successful candidate should have academic and scholarly achievements that support the rank of Full Professor with tenure, according to CEHS and UNL standards. In addition to providing administrative and strategic leadership for the Center, the Director is expected to maintain an active program of externally funded research and to lead CYFS faculty, staff, and university-wide affiliates in advancing a vibrant, interdisciplinary research enterprise with sustained national prominence. title: Director, Buros Center for Testing; Full Professor
description: The Buros Center for Testing, housed in the Department of Educational Psychology (EDPS) in the College of Education and Human Sciences (CEHS) at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (UNL), seeks an accomplished academic leader to serve as Director. The Director serves as the chief executive and academic leader of the Buros Center for Testing, a globally respected, non-profit organization committed to improving the science and practice of testing and assessment through rigorous scholarship, psychometric research, and editorial leadership of industry-standard test reviews. The director works at the intersection of academia and practical, high-stakes testing, focusing on ensuring that assessments meet rigorous standards for testing validity and reliability. Why this role, why now. The Center is entering a pivotal leadership transition following more than two decades of sustained growth and success under its current director. The Director plays a critical role in sustaining the Center’s financial self-sufficiency, advancing its research mission, and maximizing its economic and scholarly impact. A new Director is essential to provide leadership for long-term planning, interdisciplinary collaboration, and external partnerships, while ensuring continuation of the mission to improve the science and practice of testing and assessment. The Center is financially stable, highly productive, and supported by an experienced team. The Center’s strong tradition of integrity coupled with its progressive vision has made it a premier research and resource center for testing that continues to influence the use and understanding of measurements. The work of the Center serves to enhance the quality of tests worldwide and to provide evaluation services and research leadership essential to improving the science and practice of testing and assessment. Key Responsibilities Academic and Editorial Leadership Co-editing key publications, including the Mental Measurements Yearbook, Tests in Print, and Pruebas Publicadas en Español . Editing the journal Applied Measurement in Education. Supervising personnel and managing the daily operations of the Center. Teaching, advising, and mentoring students within the Department of Educational Psychology. Psychometric and Evaluation Services Directing projects related to the independent evaluation of test quality and fairness. Providing technical consultation and oversight for proprietary testing programs in education, licensure, certification, and employment. Ensuring the integrity of test reviews and maintaining the Oscar K. Buros Library of Mental Measurements, the world's largest collection of commercially available tests. Advocacy and Administration Promoting assessment literacy through outreach, webinars, and workshops. Initiating, developing, and securing contract/grant activities to fund the Center's research and development work. Representing the Center on national and international committees related to testing standards, policy, and ethics. Managing financial resources, physical space, and personnel. The Director will report to the CEHS Dean and will hold a faculty appointment within EDPS. The position is expected to be a fiscal year (FY) appointment with a split FTE of up to 0.51 FTE as Director apportioned as 100% administration. The position is expected to have an apportionment that is aligned with teaching a minimum of one course a year. The successful candidate should have academic and scholarly achievements that support the rank of Full Professor with tenure, according to CEHS and UNL standards. title: Open Rank Research Professor - Water Sciences Lab Director
description: The Water Sciences Laboratory (WSL), is a core research facility at the University of Nebraska, administered by the Nebraska Water Center, part of the Daugherty Water for Food Global Institute (DWFI) and the Institute of Agriculture and Natural Resources (IANR). With a 100% administrative research apportionment, this 12-month (calendar year) non-tenure track, renewable appointment will have a 3-5 year initial appointment based on rank at time of hire. The position reports to the Nebraska Water Center director and leads all WSL activities, supervising a laboratory manager and technical staff, while supporting staff and users in day-to-day facility operations. This position is located in Lincoln, Nebraska, and will be affiliated with an academic unit in IANR to ensure the incumbent has a pathway to promotion conforming to UNL policies and guidelines. To learn more about Lincoln, please visit About Lincoln | Nebraska . Position Responsibilities Demonstrate strong communication skills, vision, and leadership to further the WSL mission to provide advanced, high quality, defensible results for water and environmental research Seek out and develop relationships with external stakeholders and faculty from the university system to support joint research and service projects, enhancing laboratory services to meet user requirements while implementing practical ways to maintain quality and improve operation efficiency. Actively collaborate on publications, contracts and grant opportunities, and work with the Nebraska Water Center staff to promote the facility widely to potential users on and off campus. Mentor laboratory users and staff to ensure timely processing of client samples, facilitate problem-solving, and assist the laboratory manager in implementing a robust quality assurance program using a new laboratory information management system. Prepare annual facility reports to the Office of Research and Innovation which integrate fiscal and technical input from an administrative advisory board, laboratory user group, and business office staff. In addition to the above-described duties, the individual will be expected to accept committee assignments, reporting responsibilities, and other special ad hoc assignments as requested at the administrative unit, college/division, institute, and/or university level. Recognizing that collaboration and participation in teams enhances creativity, innovation, impact, and a sense of belonging, the Institute of Agriculture and Natural Resources (IANR) and the Water Sciences Laboratory in the Nebraska Water Center are committed to creating learning, research, and Extension programming environments where the unique contributions of each individual are acknowledged and valued. description: Application review will begin September 15 and continue until positions are filled. Competitive candidates will demonstrate strong capacity for research that impacts public health, advances the field of epidemiology, and contributes to the department's teaching mission. As members of the Department of Epidemiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, faculty are expected to develop independently funded research portfolios, contribute impactful scholarly products, mentor master's and doctoral students, and teach core epidemiology methods and/or substantive area courses in epidemiology. The department's primary focus is the development and application of research methods to understand the patterns and causes of health and disease, and the application of that knowledge to improving the health of populations. The department provides strong training in research methods and opportunities to apply epidemiology to a wide range of health problems.

title: Student Services Specialist
description: The Student Success Specialist position is part of a team that focuses on the analysis, maintenance, and correction of student records and data. The position assists in communicating university policies and procedures as they pertain to student records and enrollment services. The position also works on special projects as assigned.

title: Community Director
description: Community Directors develop and coordinate residential communities of approximately 400-1000 predominantly undergraduate students that augment and extend the intellectual climate of the University. Community Directors serve as the lead educator for students in the community and are designated as managers of their communities; including facilities operations, budget management, student conduct, and crisis management. Community Directors assess, plan, implement, and evaluate intentional learning opportunities in the community to meet the developmental needs and learning objectives of students and staff. Community Directors have responsibility for the selection, training, evaluation, supervision and mentoring of 20-50 student staff. Community Directors are expected to have direct contact with residents, including advising a community government, providing guidance to Learning Communities where applicable, and through routine daily interactions. During their tenure, Community Directors may have the opportunity to instruct a section of the Peer Leadership in University Environments (PLUE) course. Summer Operations, as a major revenue-generating business, entails the assignment of the CD during summer months to either Summer School housing, Summer Orientation, Departmental Summer Projects, or conferences and camps. The successful candidate has a passion for working with a diverse student population, committed to student learning and development, and strong critical thinking and problem solving skills. A successful staff member demonstrates initiative, possesses the ability to work autonomously as well as part of a team, and maintains a positive attitude. Strong supervisory, administrative, communication, and counseling skills are essential. Community management functions include: administrative duties, budgeting, record-keeping, and timely response to requests for information; assessing and implementing changes that will connect the community to the academic functions of the University; serve as the primary resource and point-of-contact for residents in the community; manage crises, conflict, and conduct situations in the community and for areas when on-call; serve as a primary hearing officer for the community; maintain administrative and data entry functions related to the conduct process; serve as facility manager for the community, including responsibility for keys, furnishings, administrative functions, and liaison with Housekeeping and Housing Support. From May to August, provide oversight to conferences, camps, Summer School or Departmental summer projects: work in a small team with additional Community Directors to co-facilitate the supervision of student staff in joint communities. Be available to work non-traditional hours during opening and closing to accommodate check ins and check outs. Community leadership functions include: assess needs, develop outcomes, and create intentional learning opportunities that augment and support classroom learning; develop and facilitate activities, workshops, and seminars for residents and staff; establish working relationships with faculty concerning the developmental and pragmatic skills that foster learning opportunities; select, train, supervise, and evaluate an inclusive student staff; advise and provide oversight for community governments and residential learning programs; if applicable, provide leadership, direction, and support for faculty and professional staff within the assigned community. Demonstrate active involvement in the Department of Housing and Residential Education, the Division of Student Affairs, the University and the profession: serve as a representative of the department for issues involving student life, campus housing, and student learning opportunities; participate fully in committees and initiatives for the Residential Education Unit and the department; develop and implement a professional development plan in conjunction with a supervisor.

title: Scientific Program Manager
description: The Scientific Program Manager is responsible for overseeing all operational aspects of the Center for Generative Immunotherapy (CGI). They will ensure optimal efficiency, productivity and quality of all preclinical research and clinical trial components; coordinate site performance reports for presentation to CGI Directors; and develop remediation and improvement strategies, as needed. This person will work with CGI research staff and collaborators to facilitate the accomplishment of the program aims and communicate progress and challenges towards meeting these aims. This person will also develop, review and edit project plans, monitoring progress to milestones to assure consistency with project goals while providing organization and facilitation of project administration, finances, communications, and meetings related to program activities (preclinical research and clinical trial study organization, initiation, execution, and closure). This person will also be responsible for coordinating compliance with institutional regulatory requirements (e.g. staff training, EHS certifications, IRB communications etc.). Assistance with experimental work including sample processing, QA/QC, T cell culture, and preparation of libraries for next generation sequencing may be occasionally required but is not a major part of the job. Responsibilities may include but are not limited to: With the research team and collaborators (internal and external to UNC) develop and implement project plans and project management infrastructure (standard forms, operating procedures, dashboards). Coordinate the hiring and training of CGI staff. Facilitate communication between the collaborating partners including those responsible for laboratory experimentation and data management. Ensure that investigators, research staff, and external partners (e.g. collaborators, contract manufacturers, regulatory agencies) receive timely and accurate responses to program-related issues. Participate in the development and maintenance of written study documentation. Coordinate central training sessions. Collaborate internally in development and execution of data management systems for collection of clinical trial data in compliance with regulatory guidelines and preclinical experimental data in accordance with GLP guidelines. Develop specifications for data checks and monitor implementation. Develop specifications for analyses and tabulations for major study reports. Prepare written and/or verbal reports interpreting program data, including communications with the research sponsor. Work with Regulatory Team to maintain regulatory compliance including reports to the IRB, protocol amendments and modifications, and FDA communications. Provide oversight with the Directors of progress towards project milestones.

Position Summary: This position serves as the Research Assistant for the ADAPT clinical trial, an NIH -funded, randomized, triple-masked, placebo-controlled study investigating marine lipid precursors of specialized pro-resolving mediators in adults with chronic temporomandibular disorder ( TMD )-related pain. The Research Assistant supports the day-to-day conduct of study activities in accordance with the approved protocol, institutional policies, and applicable Federal regulations governing human subjects research. Primary responsibilities include assisting with participant recruitment, screening, scheduling, enrollment, and retention; distributing and posting IRB -approved recruitment materials; preparing study materials for participant visits; assisting with standardized clinical assessment procedures following training and calibration; and providing operational support to the Clinical Research Coordinator during participant visits and other study activities. Occasional work outside of standard business hours (including early mornings or evenings) may be required to accommodate participant scheduling and study visits. The position is responsible for collecting, processing, storing, and shipping biological specimens in accordance with study protocols and laboratory procedures and serves as a backup phlebotomist for the study. Additional responsibilities include supporting accurate study data collection, data entry, maintenance of study records and participant tracking systems, and preparation of study materials and administrative documentation necessary for efficient study operations. Working under the direction of the Clinical Operations Lead, the Research Assistant collaborates closely with the Clinical Research Coordinator, investigators, clinical staff, laboratory personnel, and study participants to ensure study activities are conducted in compliance with protocol requirements, Good Clinical Practice ( GCP ) guidelines, and human subjects protection requirements.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements: Bachelor’s degree; or equivalent combination of training and experience. All degrees must be received from appropriately accredited institutions.
Management Preferences: Experience working in clinical research, healthcare, or other human subjects research settings. Experience supporting participant recruitment, screening, scheduling, retention, and other study coordination activities. Experience collecting, processing, storing, and shipping biological specimens in accordance with established research protocols and safety requirements. Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice ( GCP ) guidelines, human subjects research requirements, and clinical research documentation and confidentiality practices. Demonstrated organizational, interpersonal, and communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with diverse study participants, faculty, staff, and clinical personnel; manage multiple concurrent responsibilities with accuracy and attention to detail; maintain confidential research and clinical information; and work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team.
Special Physical/Mental Requirements: Ability to stand, walk, and occasionally lift or transport study materials and laboratory supplies during participant visits and recruitment activities.
Campus Security Authority Responsibilities: Not Applicable.

title: Academic Genitourinary Pathologist
description: The Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, is seeking an Academic Genitourinary Pathologist for a tenure-track/tenured, fixed-term, or variable track position at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor. We are a subspecialized surgical pathology division seeking, and preference will be given to, candidates with fellowship training and/or expertise in Genitourinary Pathology. This position requires expertise in all aspects of Genitourinary Pathology; additionally, experience with adrenal resections and biopsies is preferred. Those who are willing to provide additional coverage in other services areas such as Gastrointestinal, Bone and Soft Tissue Pathology, and/or Cytopathology are also encouraged to apply. Participation in multidisciplinary tumor boards and effective communication with an active clinical care team that provides statewide integrated care is required. The successful candidate will be eligible for membership in the UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center, with opportunities to collaborate with a robust array of basic, translational, and clinical researchers. In addition to teaching clinical residents and fellows, opportunities are available for teaching in the School of Medicine, Graduate School, and Undergraduate School.

title: Histotechnologist
description: The Histotechnician will have the primary purpose of performing diagnostic laboratory procedures on tissue specimens obtained from patients with renal diseases. They will be responsible for processing, embedding, sectioning, staining and storage/retrieval of samples for immunofluorescence, light, and electron microscopy. Depending on the needs of the lab, the job duties will include cross-training in all three techniques which include immunofluorescence, light and/or electron microscopy. The technician will participate in training activities and serve as a technical resource for residents/fellows, graduate students, new staff and other scientists seeking knowledge of histological procedures. Work will additionally require monitoring equipment, quality control testing, general laboratory maintenance according to UNC-CH, SOM OSHA, and other regulatory bodies, maintaining logs and laboratory operating manuals, supply inventory and appropriately managing laboratory waste. This will include quality improvement activities and health and safety oversight for laboratory microscopy services.

title: Commercialization Manager - IEED
description: THIS POSTING IS FOR TWO IDENTICAL POSITIONS (POSITION NUMBERS 20078585 AND 20030805). BY APPLYING TO THIS POSTING, YOU WILL BE CONSIDERED FOR BOTH AVAILABLE POSITIONS. This position is located in the Office of Technology Commercialization (OTC) which is located in the Division of Innovation, Entrepreneurship and Economic Development. OTC manages the University's intellectual property including patenting marketing and negotiating licenses for the commercialization of University owned inventions. The Commercialization Manager (CM) helps researchers conceptualize and commercialize novel technologies in the computer, software, data analysis, digital health, engineering, chemical, or biological science industries. The CM educates faculty and manages the process of disclosing, protecting (patent, copyright, software, or tangible property), developing strategic marketing plans for, and licensing their inventions. Duties include evaluating technologies, evaluating copyright and software, managing patent prosecution, coordinating marketing plans, and drafting and negotiating a range of intellectual property-related contracts. The CM places special emphasis on building faculty relationships, making investment decisions, and developing commercialization strategies in coordination with a wide range of related offices and stakeholders.

title: Director of Foundation Administration
description: The Director of Foundation Administration functions as the chief of staff and lead administrative officer of the Arts and Sciences Foundation, with responsibilities for business and budget operations, human resources coordination and planning, board and executive engagement and support, strategic project management, and overall coordination and management of the executive and leadership functions of the Foundation. The Director of Foundation Administration reports to the Assistant Vice Chancellor and Executive Director, serving as a member of the AVC/ED's executive team. The Director provides leadership, strategic planning, and thought partnership for foundation operations. This position includes coordination and strategy responsibility for talent management and human resources; fiscal management, including budget, revenue forecasting, procurement, asset management, facility management, Foundation IT support, and strategy implementation. The Foundation Accountant and Business Services Coordinator report to this position, and additional direct reports are likely to be added over time.

title: Assistant Professor of Dramaturgy
description: The Department of Dramatic Art at UNC-Chapel Hill invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor of Dramaturgy. The position carries a 2/2 teaching load and with courses in dramaturgy, theatre history, dramatic literature, and related areas at the undergraduate level. The successful candidate will maintain an active program of scholarly and/or creative research, with an emphasis on Asian, African, and/or Latin American theatre and performance. The position will also contribute to the Department's production and artistic activities through dramaturgy, student mentorship, and/or collaboration with PlayMakers Repertory Company and/or the Kenan Theatre Company.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Geography and Environment at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for a full-time, nine-month tenure track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor specializing in Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) and Geospatial Data Science, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027. This position will establish and sustain an active, externally funded research program, teach effectively at the undergraduate and graduate levels, and provide service to the Department, the University, and the profession. Teaching responsibilities will include core introductory and advanced courses that support of the department's new B.S. Degree in Geospatial Data Science, as well as the development of new courses in GeoAI and machine/deep learning, high-performance geospatial computing, or others related to the candidate's area of expertise. The teaching load is three courses per year (2:1 schedule). Service responsibilities will include serving on MA and PhD committees, advising MA and PhD students, and actively participating in department colloquia and other programming/committees.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate - Cameron/Arnold Lab
description: The Cameron-Arnold laboratory in the Department of Microbiology and Immunology at the University of North Carolina School of Medicine in Chapel Hill, NC, is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral research associate to investigate the biochemical and biophysical mechanisms of RNA virus genome replication. Our laboratory has established, NIH-supported research programs focused on the enzymology of RNA-dependent RNA polymerases, viral ATPases and helicases, and the protein complexes responsible for genome replication in picornaviruses, alphaviruses, and coronaviruses. Research will focus on defining the molecular mechanisms of viral RNA synthesis, including initiation, elongation, nucleotide selection, fidelity, RNA recombination, and the regulation of viral replication machinery. Additional areas of investigation include the kinetic mechanisms of viral ATPases and helicases, the assembly and function of multiprotein replication complexes, coronavirus RNA proofreading and transcription, and the biochemical mechanisms of antiviral drug action and resistance. These studies employ a combination of quantitative enzymology, protein biochemistry, molecular biophysics, and complementary structural and cellular approaches. The successful candidate will develop and pursue mechanistic research projects within the laboratory's established areas of investigation. Our overarching goal is to establish a quantitative understanding of the molecular mechanisms governing RNA virus genome replication and to use this knowledge to identify opportunities for antiviral therapeutic development. The position offers extensive opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration, development of advanced biochemical and biophysical expertise, scientific publication, and preparation for an independent research career.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate - Cameron/Arnold Lab
description: The Cameron-Arnold laboratory in the Department of Microbiology and Immunology at the University of North Carolina School of Medicine in Chapel Hill, NC, is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral research associate to investigate the molecular and cellular mechanisms of RNA virus genome replication. Our laboratory has established research programs supported by the National Institutes of Health that focus on picornaviruses, alphaviruses, and coronaviruses. These programs seek to understand how viral and host proteins coordinate viral RNA synthesis, replication-complex assembly, genome maintenance, and virus multiplication. Research will integrate molecular biology, cell biology, genetics, and virology to investigate the mechanisms governing viral genome replication and the interactions between viral replication machinery and the host cell. Areas of investigation include the regulation of genomic and subgenomic RNA synthesis, formation and function of membrane-associated replication complexes, viral RNA recombination, and the contributions of viral and host factors to genome replication and virus assembly. These studies will complement ongoing biochemical and biophysical investigations of viral replication proteins and macromolecular complexes. The successful candidate will develop and pursue research projects within the laboratory's established areas of investigation, working collaboratively with faculty, postdoctoral researchers, graduate students, and scientific staff. Our overarching objective is to advance fundamental knowledge of RNA virus replication and identify mechanisms that may be exploited for antiviral therapeutic development. The position provides opportunities for scientific independence, interdisciplinary collaboration, publication, and professional development in preparation for an independent research career.

title: Purchasing Specialist
description: The Purchasing Specialist will assist Energy Services management with multi-departmental contract oversight and procurement of goods and services in support of the organization (Chilled Water Systems, Cogeneration Systems, Electric Distribution Systems and Water Systems). This position is responsible for assisting customers with contract interpretation, defined pricing, reporting, securing encumbrances and renewal reminders. In addition, this position will secure vendor quotes, assist with ensuring correctness and completeness of all procurement packages, process requisitions in Connect Carolina for purchases requiring a University Purchase Order, and coordinating with Central Purchasing to ensure timely completion of the procurement cycle.

title: Faculty Physician / Clinician Educator (Chatham Hospital)
description: The Department of Family Medicine at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, in partnership with UNC Health and Chatham Hospital, seeks a Family Medicine or Emergency Medicine Physician for the UNC Chatham Hospital Emergency Department. UNC Chatham Hospital is a 25-bed rural Critical Access Hospital located in Siler City, NC, approximately 30 miles from Chapel Hill. The newly renovated 15-bed ED sees approximately 18,000 visits annually and is staffed by Family Medicine and Emergency Medicine physicians and advanced practice providers. This is an excellent opportunity to join a diverse and energetic group of physicians providing emergency care to a rural community. The ED team is supported by advanced practice providers, telepsychiatry services, on-site interpreter services, a system transfer center, and UNC AirCare. We use Epic as our EHR with AI-powered documentation support. CT and ultrasound are available daily, with MRI available five days per week. Bedside ultrasound and GlideScope are also available. The Maternity Care Center is staffed 24/7 with cesarean section capability, and cardiology and general surgery consultants are readily available. Physicians in the ED practice group are employed through the UNC Department of Family Medicine, consistently ranked a top academic family medicine program in the United States. Our mission is to provide outstanding, compassionate health care to the surrounding rural community. The ED serves as a training site for medical students, residents, and fellows. Faculty interested in academic advancement have opportunities for professional development across the department's missions, including teaching, clinical excellence, research, and administration. The position offers flexible scheduling options with a mix of day, evening, and overnight shifts. Full-time equivalent is 1520 hours annually. The manageable patient volume allows for meaningful patient interactions while maintaining work-life balance in a collegial, team-based environment. Faculty rank and salary are commensurate with qualifications and experience. The position includes excellent UNC faculty physician benefits and clinical incentive pay. Benefits include: Competitive salary with clinical incentive compensation Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance Generous retirement contributions (UNC system) Paid time off and CME allowance Professional liability coverage Opportunities for academic advancement

title: Open Rank
description: Flexible work arrangements, including virtual and hybrid work locations, are an integral part of the School of Medicine’s Working Forward initiative. This position may be eligible for a virtual or hybrid work arrangement, in accordance with UNC policy and subject to approval based on the unit’s business needs. Please note that the approved work location may change over time to meet operational requirements. Position Description The Department of Radiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking an Abdominal Imaging Radiologist to join the Abdominal Imaging Division. This position supports the department's clinical, educational, and academic missions within a high volume academic medical center. The Abdominal Imaging Division provides diagnostic imaging services across the UNC Hospitals system, including a Level I Trauma Center, Women's Hospital, Children's Hospital, Neurosciences Hospital, and the NCI designated Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center. Faculty collaborate closely with multidisciplinary clinical teams to support comprehensive patient care. Position Responsibilities Interpret a full range of abdominal imaging studies, including CT, MRI, ultrasound, radiographs, and fluoroscopy Participate in teaching and mentoring diagnostic radiology residents, fellows, and medical students Collaborate with multidisciplinary clinical teams through conferences, consultations, and protocol development Participate in departmental, divisional, and institutional quality improvement initiatives Engage in scholarly or research activities consistent with departmental needs Appointment Details This is an open rank, fixed term faculty appointment at the rank of Instructor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

title: Clinical Cytogeneticist
description: The Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill School of Medicine, is seeking a PhD, MD, or MD/PhD academic Clinical Cytogeneticist for a tenure-track/tenured, fixed-term, or variable track position at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor. The UNC Hospitals Clinical Cytogenetics Laboratory is a full-service laboratory which performs both constitutional (prenatal and postnatal) and cancer cytogenetic testing on approximately 4,500 cases annually. Responsibilities of this position will include oversight and direction of the day-to-day operations of the clinical cytogenetics diagnostic service, laboratory case sign-out (conventional cytogenetics, FISH, and SNP microarray), technical and analytical troubleshooting, and new assay development. All Laboratory faculty are expected to teach a variety of learners, including medical students, pathology and medical genetics residents, and fellows from various programs including Laboratory Genetics and Genomics, Molecular Genetic Pathology, and Maternal Fetal Medicine. Opportunities also exist to engage in a variety of ongoing research projects including several that involve next generation sequencing.

title: Adjunct Assistant Professor
description: Treat infections and injuries at the UNC emergency room. Use your extensive residency training in the emergency room. Duties include requesting medical tests, performing follow-up visits, and creating treatment plans.

title: PET/Nuclear Medicine Technologist
description: Primary purpose of the position is to facilitate MRI, MR/PET and PET/CT imaging services for the BRIC utilizing technical and administrative expertise. Technical areas of responsibility include providing for the safety of research subjects during research studies, and conducting MRI, MR/PET, PET/CT, and CT studies with and without the use of radioactive nuclides. Administrative areas of responsibility include ensuring proper use of the scheduling system for imaging research services, adherence to safety standards and SOPs, logging accurate machine time usage for billing purposes and managing relationships with multiple investigators. This work involves caring for research subjects and clinical patients of all ages, and levels of health. This includes children as young as 2 weeks of age and spanning adulthood. Applicants will working with subjects/patients of all ages, and people ranging from the very healthy to those who are very ill and toward the end of life.

title: Comprehensive Ophthalmologist (Open Rank Faculty)
description: An open rank, fixed-term Comprehensive Ophthalmologist position is currently available in the Department of Ophthalmology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. Responsibilities include a strong commitment to clinical, resident teaching and supervision as well as medical student teaching. Rank and salary are commensurate with experience. title: Program Manager
description: The Program Manager coordinates day-to-day activities for the National MCH Workforce Development and Training Center, a HRSA-funded cooperative agreement. The Center provides robust training and resources to strengthen the MCH public health workforce. It aims to improve the health of women, children and families by supporting the workforce's ability to implement federally and state-funded programs, including the Title V program. The Program Manager provides project coordination and administrative leadership to ensure successful implementation of all grant-funded activities. This position works closely with the Center's leadership team (Principal Investigator, Deputy Director and Director of Learning) to manage operations and coordinate activities with internal and external stakeholders, including UNC faculty and staff, subcontractors, independent consultants and national organizations involved in public health workforce development. In addition to program management and coordination, the position is also responsible for: Center team support, stakeholder engagement and communication, program operations and continuous quality improvement, and administrative support.

Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit: Collaborative Studies Coordinating Center The Collaborative Studies Coordinating Center ( CSCC ) is a division within the Department of Biostatistics of the School of Public Health at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, NC ( UNC ). As the coordinating center for a number of multi-center clinical trials and epidemiology studies, the CSCC provides study design, data management, statistical analysis, quality assurance, and study management services to a broad array of projects funded primarily by the National Institutes of Health ( NIH ). The organization includes faculty from the departments of Biostatistics, Epidemiology, and Medicine and research staff with training and experience in biostatistics, epidemiology, computer science/data management, and project management. Total employees currently number between 100 and 105. The CSCC is responsible for approximately $32,000,000 in funding for 55-60 contracts and grants, and an additional 65 subcontracts. The CSCC was established in 1971 as the Lipid Research Clinics ( LRC ) Coordinating Center and has operated continually since that time. To reflect the addition of new studies and expansion into new research areas, the LRC Coordinating Center changed its name to the Collaborative Studies Coordinating Center ( CSCC ) in 1984. Major research programs currently include the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study ( ARIC ); Adolescent Medicine Trials Network for HIV / AIDS Interventions ( ATN ); SPIROMICS II: Biological underpinning of COPD heterogeneity and progression ( SPIROMICS II); SPIROMICS GIC Support; Data, Modeling, and Coordination Center for PrecISE Network (PrecISE); Hispanic Community Health Study ( HCHS ); and Preconceptional health of Latinas and its association with child adiposity ( HCHS - FLOR ). Information on these, as well as others can be found at http://www.cscc.unc.edu/cscc/index.php
Position Summary: The Social/Clinical Research Assistant ( SCRA ) plays an important role on a study team and is involved in operational and research support for studies where the Center is the primary organization with responsibility for study operations, data management, and statistical analysis, often managing multiple studies within a network. In addition, the SCRA may provide support in coordinating and organizing centralized meetings of the research investigators (e.g., hotel and meeting arrangements, technical support), maintaining the study website (e.g., updating directories and documents, as needed), and providing regular status reports of study progress.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements: Bachelor’s degree; or equivalent combination of training and experience. All degrees must be received from appropriately accredited institutions.
Management Preferences: Previous research assistant experience preferred.

title: Assistant Professor - Neuromuscular Control and Biomechanics
description: The Department of Exercise and Sport Science invites applications for a 9-month tenure track Assistant Professor faculty position to deepen and expand research in any area of neuromuscular control and biomechanics while teaching in areas related to exercise and sport science, biomechanics, and/or motor control. We aspire to recruit faculty engaged in innovative and highly impactful scholarship that will diversify and enhance our research, teaching, and public outreach missions, and who can translate this research to teach undergraduate and graduate level courses in biomechanics, neuromuscular control, motor control, and/or sports medicine. This position assumes a lead research role within the Department of Exercise and Sport Science within the College of Arts and Sciences. Successful candidates will demonstrate expertise in neuromuscular control and biomechanics which may involve, but not be limited to, musculoskeletal health outcomes, mechanisms related to biomechanical and/ or neuromuscular disease, neurotrauma, and/or promoting healthy movement and performance. The individual is expected to possess expertise in their chosen neuromuscular control and biomechanics field, which may include biomechanical assessments, measurement, and analysis. Potential applicants should have a strong interest in developing impactful collaborative opportunities within the Department, across the College of Arts and Sciences, and across the greater UNC community (including the nationally ranked School of Medicine and Gillings School of Global Public Health, Human Science Curriculum and Department of Biomedical Engineering). Applicants should have a record of scholarly productivity and interdisciplinary research. The interest areas of the applicant should align with and complement the faculty affiliated with the Department of Exercise and Sport Science that are collecting neuromuscular control and biomechanics data including MOTION Science Institute, UNC Sports Medicine Institute, STAR HEEL Laboratory and/or the Matthew Gfeller Center. Responsibilities: * Plan, establish, and develop a focused independent research agenda, with preference for applicants who demonstrate a significant publication record and demonstrate a record of extramural grant submission * Seek extramural funding to support research efforts * Collaborate with colleagues across campus and in Exercise and Sport Science to support and develop multidisciplinary research projects * Serve as a mentor to undergraduate and graduate students across a diverse student population * Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in Exercise and Sport Science related to biomechanics, neuromuscular control, motor control, sports medicine and/or other classes aligning with the candidate's expertise as requested by the department Chair * Serve as a research advisor and/or committee member for undergraduate and graduate students in the Department of Exercise and Sport Science * Participate as a core faculty member and contribute to mentoring doctoral trainees in the Human Movement Science doctoral program * Perform other responsibilities and duties as may be assigned by the Department Chair

title: Faculty Position in School Counseling (Open Rank — Fixed Term/Clinical or Teaching)
description: The School of Education at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for a faculty position in School Counseling at the rank of Clinical Assistant, Clinical Associate, or Clinical Professor, starting July 1, 2027. UNC's nationally recognized CACREP-accredited School Counseling program prepares culturally responsive school counselors through rigorous coursework, immersive school-based fieldwork, and individualized professional mentorship. We seek candidates with professional experience in school counseling and a passion for preparing future counselors. This full-time, 9-month position is for a three-year term, with the potential to renew for additional terms, and will include undergraduate and graduate teaching and supervision, student mentoring, and program leadership. Candidates will: a) teach undergraduate courses in Human Development and Family Sciences as well as graduate courses in the School Counseling program in face to face, online, and/or blended formats, including fieldwork supervision courses; b) serve as the program's Clinical and Admissions Coordinator, providing program-level leadership for recruitment, admissions, and practicum and internship coordination in collaboration with School of Education faculty and staff; and c) provide advising, mentoring, and other supports to students.

title: Division Chief - Division of Hospital Medicine
description: The Division of Hospital Medicine within the Department of Medicine at the University of North Carolina School of Medicine seeks an accomplished academic physician to serve as its next Division Chief. This is an Open Rank faculty position that includes an at-will secondary appointment as Division Chief. The appointment will be at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor commensurate with experience and accomplishments. UNC Hospital Medicine is a nationally recognized academic division within a top-ranked academic health system, providing care across multiple sites, including UNC Medical Center in Chapel Hill and UNC Hospitals Hillsborough. The Division Chief will lead a large and dynamic group of academic hospitalists and play a critical role in advancing the division's missions of clinical excellence, medical education, research, quality improvement, patient safety, and faculty development. The successful candidate will be a visionary, collaborative, and innovative leader with a demonstrated record of accomplishment in academic medicine. The Division Chief will provide strategic leadership for a robust academic practice and foster the continued growth of the division's programs in research, education, complex clinical care, and quality and safety initiatives. Responsibilities will include a combination of administrative, clinical, educational, and scholarly activities, while partnering closely with departmental and health system leadership to support the division's continued growth and success. The Division Chief will be expected to recruit, develop, mentor, and retain outstanding faculty and staff; promote an inclusive and collaborative culture; advance educational programs for learners at all levels; and support scholarly productivity across the division. The ideal candidate will possess exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, sound judgment, and the ability to effectively lead a multifaceted academic division through a period of continued growth and innovation. In addition to division leadership responsibilities, the selected candidate will maintain an active clinical practice within UNC Hospital Medicine, with opportunities to participate in both teaching and non-teaching services across UNC Health facilities. UNC Health offers a highly competitive compensation package, comprehensive benefits, and robust support for professional development. Located in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, the position provides the opportunity to live and work in one of the nation's most desirable academic communities.

title: Teaching Assistant Professor
description: The Teaching Assistant Professor will teach three classes per semester including first year classes, engineering foundational courses, and upper-level electives in materials and engineering. The TAP will also be expected to provide service to the department by working with the Director of Undergraduate Studies to support the implementation of the new undergraduate program. This could include the development of one or more of the following: an assessment plan, student advising processes, peer teaching oversight, faculty mentoring, and undergraduate laboratory activities. This position may also have opportunities to teach summer school classes.

title: Community Navigator

As the position grows the Community Navigator will serve as a resource for individuals and families navigating the health care system.

title: Regional Liaison
description: The School of Social Work (SSW) at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for three (3) Regional Liaisons for the Public Service Leadership Program (PSLP) funded by 'The Workforce is Here: How to Support Thriving Communities and Healthy North Carolina Children, Individuals, Families, and Elders via Social Work Interventions and Research' grant program. This initiative plans to develop and offer a statewide, three-tiered public service certificate for both pre-service students at the high school, community college, undergraduate, and master's levels as well as in-service practitioners currently employed in public sector social work settings. The purpose of these certifications is to spark interest in pursuing public sector career opportunities and, for those already engaged in the social work workforce, to add a credential to enable career progression and acquired competencies of advanced skills. Each certificate will encompass a core set of common elements: a degree and/or curriculum enhancement to leverage foundational instruction; a tuition-free credential, with curriculum development and instructional costs incurred and covered through the initiative; emphasis on direct service; content focused on North Carolina's critical service delivery areas; a virtual delivery model to enhance accessibility; and a co-instruction model of university faculty, agency professionals, and individuals with lived experiences. This is a TIME-LIMITED position for one year and any extension is contingent upon available funding. This recruitment seeks to hire three Regional Liaisons, two of which will be situated in eastern NC and one central NC (e.g., the Triad, Research Triangle, or Charlotte-Mecklenburg). The Regional Liaisons will report to the Assistant Dean for Workforce Development and serve as the primary point of contact for enrolled PSLP participants in their assigned region. Regional Liaisons will support, within their assigned region, the development and implementation of PSLP's: 1) admissions and recruitment processes; 2) curriculum and academic program evaluation; and 3) resilience and well-being support across all program levels for prospective pre-service and in-service participants. These positions will play a key role in the collection and tracking participant admissions data, program learning data, and engagement in various in-person, virtual, and asynchronous program learning activities. The Regional Liaisons will also contribute to the development of marketing materials, facilitate information sessions, and provide on-ground, on-site coordination, and support for in-person training events, conferences, and outreach events. This hybrid position will be required to provide on-site and in-person support to PSLP participants and coalition partner campuses within their assigned region. The candidates selected for this position must reside within a commutable distance of at least one of coalition partner campuses within their assigned region and be willing to support the other coalition partner schools and programs. The position will require up to 25% travel to in-state NC human services organizations and partnering NC Social Work Coalition universities. Additionally, there may be required travel to Chapel Hill, NC for in-person meetings, statewide conferences, and other convenings to support the implementation of the PSLP.

description: INTERNAL ONLY: Internal posting for permanent, time-limited and layoff priority employees of UNC-Chapel Hill only. UNC Chapel Hill employees are generally required to reside within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned duty station. The Senior Research Administration Specialist serves as an advanced-level research administration professional responsible for leading complex pre-award activities while incorporating project management principles to support faculty and research teams across assigned units. This role functions as a subject matter expert in proposal development, sponsor guidelines, and research administration processes, with a strong emphasis on strategic planning, coordination, and execution of sponsored research proposals. The position will independently manage a portfolio of highly complex proposals and collaborates closely with principal investigators (PIs), departmental leadership, and central offices to ensure timely, compliant, and competitive submissions. title: Pediatric Program Coordinator (Part-Time)

The Program Coordinator will coordinate multidisciplinary team meetings, manage program operations and timelines, facilitate communication among clinical teams and external partners, support outreach and educational activities, assist with implementation of new program initiatives, and oversee collection and reporting of program metrics. The position will also support development and maintenance of the BPD patient registry, assist with regulatory and reporting requirements, coordinate patient tracking and follow-up workflows, and support grant-funded program activities. Additional responsibilities include website and educational resource development, preparation of program reports, stakeholder engagement, and other activities that advance the mission and growth of the UNC Children's BPD Program.

title: Adjunct Instructor
description: The Gillings School of Global Public Health – the top public school of public health in the nation – offers a variety of professional Master of Public Health (MPH) concentrations under the schoolwide MPH program. The MPH is the cornerstone of education in public health, preparing graduates for expanded roles in the 21st century. MPH degrees will ground students in a rigorous, integrated, public health core and focus on specialized skill building in a defined area of expertise via concentrations. The MPH will also emphasize experiential learning that provides opportunities for applying and integrating concepts, skills, and interdisciplinary content. The Gillings MPH includes quality residential and online programs offered in a variety of concentration areas relevant to today’s public health needs. These offerings are designed to meet the needs of a diverse student body and to fuel the public health workforce. Central to Gillings MPH is the MPH Core, an foundational interdisciplinary first-year set of core courses driven by the latest recommendations from the Association of Schools and Programs of Public Health (ASPPH) and the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH). The Gillings School has expanded its online offerings to add MPH@UNC, delivered with support from digital educational partner 2U . MPH@UNC is a flexible degree option for those with professional or personal constraints limiting participation in a residential program in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. Students learn from UNC lead faculty and section instructors through a unique blend of highly interactive online learning in small-group virtual classroom setting. MPH@UNC students must meet the same selective admissions criteria as the residential programs and upon graduation, earn an identical diploma. Section instructors for MPH@UNC will be responsible for teaching core or concentration courses. Section instructors teach live, online, synchronous class sessions once each week for 13 weeks. The MPH@UNC term is 14 weeks long with 13 weeks of content. The program recognizes some holidays and well-being days that are equal to one week off during the term. Classes are solely scheduled on weekday evenings, Monday – Thursday only. Key responsibilities of the section instructor include: * Facilitating weekly live sessions in which the class discusses and applies learning from self-paced modules developed by lead faculty. * Grading assessments and providing verbal and written feedback to students as appropriate. * Responding to student questions and issues related to the course. * Maintaining regular communications with lead faculty and the coordinator for MPH@UNC about students’ experiences, potential barriers, ideas for enhancement, etc. Section instructors will follow a standardized course syllabus, class plan, and use pre-developed instructional materials created by lead faculty for each course. Instructors will effectively engage class members in discussions during live class sessions, bringing their unique background and expertise to the course experience by helping students apply their new knowledge to relevant, real-world problems. Section instructors will provide feedback on and grade student work, while also supporting student learning by establishing and communicating regular office hours and responding to student issues and questions within forty-eight business hours. Section instructor is responsible for maintaining reliable access to the learning management system (e.g., meeting technical specifications and reliable high-speed internet access). In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification document form upon hire.

description: This position will be part of an embedded emergency department-palliative care team comprised of dual-trained emergency medicine and palliative care physicians. They immediately treat any injuries, infections, or other conditions to stabilize patients. Emergency department doctors request medical tests for patients, create treatment plans, and recommend patients to appropriate specialists. When providing palliative care consultation in the department, physicians will work closely with the emergency department team and broader palliative care/hospice team to care for seriously ill patients. Physicians will support medical decision-making, symptom management, and psychosocial needs for patients and families in the emergency department. This is a full-time position at 1.0 FTE. Clinical Instructors, Clinical Assistants, Clinical Associates, and Clinical Professors will be considered.

title: Administrative Support Specialist
description: The Administrative Support Specialist provides administrative support to the faculty, students and designated staff members for the Advanced Education in General Dentistry program to ensure efficient office operations. This position will assist the Preceptors in General Dentistry and Predoctoral Program Director with all courses, labs and schedules, student assignments, eMedley and STAR grading (report/exam/grading software) and student certificates/awards. The Administrative Support Specialist will electronically track students competencies and requirements so updates can be instantly reflected. The person in this position works in close collaboration with other administrative staff in the Division to manage social media groups (Facebook, Instagram, ASOD Weekly Wisdom, etc.) and on other projects as required. This position will work closely with the Business Coordinator and will provide backup support to the clinical front desks and use EPIC software when needed. The position is the first contact for the Department of Restorative Sciences - Generalists and will provide overall administrative management and coordination of functions for the area discipline within the department.

title: MRI Technologist
description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $5,000 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN 2 INSTALLMENTS WITHIN 12 MONTHS OF HIRE $2,500 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE AND $2,500 12 MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE **See eligibility for Sign-on Bonus below in the Special Instructions section. Primary purpose of the position is to facilitate MRI services for the BRIC utilizing technical and administrative expertise. Technical areas of responsibility include providing for the safety of research subjects during research studies, and conducting MRI, MR/PET, PET/CT, and CT studies with and without the use of radioactive nuclides. Administrative areas of responsibility include ensuring proper use of the scheduling system for imaging research services, adherence to safety standards and SOPs, logging accurate machine time usage for billing purposes and managing relationships with multiple investigators. This work involves caring for research subjects and clinical patients of all ages, and levels of health. This includes children as young as 2 weeks of age and spanning adulthood. Applicants should have a high level of comfort in working with subjects/patients of all ages, and people ranging from the very healthy to those who are very ill and toward the end of life.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate
description: A Postdoctoral position is currently open in the Dayton Lab within the Lampe Joint Biomedical Engineering Dept. This research position will lead research in advanced ultrasound imaging and ultrasound therapeutics. Post-docs with background in therapeutic delivery or imaging physics/engineering will both be considered for different projects. Our research group has more than 3000 sq feet of research space equipped with state of the art equipment for biomedical acoustics, including 1024 channel Verasonics engines, multiple clinical ultrasound systems, HIFU systems, and high speed cameras, as well as facilities for contrast agent and drug delivery vehicle pharmacoengineering. Current research areas include super-resolution imaging, neuromodulation, molecular imaging, superharmonic imaging, sonothrombolysis, BBB opening, targeted drug delivery, acoustically mediated immunotherapy, and bioeffects studies. Candidates will both conduct independent work and work with a team to conduct bench and translational research, analyze data, prepare papers, reports, and contribute to proposals.

title: Director of Experiential Learning
description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $10,000 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE. Reporting to the Associate Dean for Professional Development of the Graduate School, the Director of Experiential Learning will serve as a bridge between The Graduate School, students, and external partners, identifying and facilitating successful experiential learning opportunities for graduate students. This position is aligned with UNC's forward-looking approach to graduate education in which we seek to complement students' formal academic training to ensure their readiness for the career path of their choosing, e.g., engineering, health care, and technology sectors aligned with North Carolina economic needs. The Director will identify Carolina's differentiation advantage in experiential learning and develop innovative formats beyond traditional internships, including micro-internships, project-based learning, and industry-sponsored research opportunities. The Director of Experiential Learning will 1) create scalable solutions using data-driven and AI approaches 2) direct student programming for workplace readiness and 3) advance existing internal and external partnerships and generate innovative solutions for graduate student and employer needs and will actively cultivate existing and new industry partnerships aligned with North Carolina workforce needs. The Director of Experiential Learning will also collaborate proactively with others in The Graduate School and across campus to develop strategic approaches with metrics for success related to graduate student experiential learning and workforce outcomes. In addition, the Director of Experiential Learning will collaborate on alumni engagement, industry partnerships, and external funding to garner financial support for experiential professional development programming.

title: Materials Coordinator - Dental Labs
description: This position will be the primary administrator for the vendor-contracted dental laboratory services dispensary and other dental lab case management support requirements provided by Clinical Operations to the School of Dentistry's student clinics and other departments requiring this service. The lab coordinator will receive dental lab cases and inspect for quality assurance, receive prescriptions for contracted lab casework and assign appropriate vendors, document cases in the case management system, ship laboratory models to selected vendors, track casework costs, purchase supplies, prepare purchase requisitions, process financial transactions, and prepare financial reports. Secondary duties include cross-coverage in other Clinical Operations areas.

title: Child & Adolescent Psychiatrist - Open Rank
description: The UNC Department of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry is seeking a psychiatrist to provide inpatient clinical services to children and young adults in the Child & Adolescent inpatient and outpatient programs. This is a full-time fixed term (clinical) position The rank will be based on the qualifications of the applicants. We anticipate hiring a child and adolescent psychiatrist to work in the adolescent inpatient setting and an adult or child adolescent psychiatrist on the young adult unit at the new Child & Adolescent Psychiatry facility in Butner, NC. The position will be at least 50% inpatient and opportunity for up to 100% inpatient. The position can include outpatient work including in-person and/or virtual care services. Duties also include teaching/supervising fellows, residents, medical students and other trainees from a variety of disciplines.

title: Open Rank - MFM/Critical Care Specialist
description: The University of North Carolina's Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology is recruiting a tenure track or variable track Maternal-Fetal Medicine Specialist with expertise in critical care obstetrics to provide inpatient and outpatient care to high-risk obstetric patients, including those requiring intensive care management. This is a unique opportunity to serve as the clinical and academic leader of Critical Care MFM at UNC, with responsibilities extending well beyond direct ICU service. The successful candidate will be expected to: (1) provide consultative and co-management critical care services for pregnant and postpartum patients; (2) lead the development and implementation of evidence-based critical care protocols for obstetric patients; (3) build and direct a joint MFM-Critical Care fellowship program in collaboration with relevant departments; and (4) develop and expand tele-critical care (e-ICU) capacity to extend critical care expertise to obstetric patients across UNC Health's regional network. Additional responsibilities include education of medical students, residents, and fellows, and active participation in the division's research mission. The division's clinical programs include high-risk obstetric care, perinatal consultation, prenatal diagnosis, ultrasound, genetic services, invasive fetal therapy, and perinatal outreach. Division faculty members are engaged participants in the activities of UNC's Collaborative for Maternal and Infant Health (www.mombaby.org), which provides multidisciplinary care coordination for families referred for fetal malformations. Division members actively participate in student and resident teaching and provide subspecialty training for six Maternal Fetal Medicine fellows through its 3-year American Board of Obstetrics & Genecology (ABOG) approved fellowship program.

title: Open Rank
description: Flexible work arrangements, including virtual and hybrid work locations, are an integral part of the School of Medicine’s Working Forward initiative. This position may be eligible for a virtual or hybrid work arrangement, in accordance with UNC policy and subject to approval based on the unit’s business needs. Please note that the approved work location may change over time to meet operational requirements. Position Description The Department of Radiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking an Emergency Radiologist to join the Division of Emergency Radiology. This position supports the department's clinical, educational, and academic missions within a high-volume academic medical center and Level I Trauma Center environment. The Division of Emergency Radiology provides high-quality imaging interpretation services for emergency department patients at UNC Medical Center and affiliated clinical partners. Emergency radiologists work closely with Emergency Medicine, Acute Care Surgery (Trauma Surgery), and multidisciplinary clinical teams to support the rapid diagnosis and management of complex trauma, surgical emergencies, and urgent medical conditions. Division faculty are highly skilled in the interpretation of radiography (x-ray), fluoroscopy, ultrasound, computed tomography (CT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) performed in the emergency setting. Faculty provide timely and accurate diagnostic interpretations that directly support acute patient care and emergent clinical decision-making. This position follows a 7 days on / 14 days off schedule structure. Evening and overnight shift opportunities may be available, with scheduling details evolving alongside continued division growth. Position Responsibilities Interpret emergency and trauma imaging studies, including radiography, fluoroscopy, ultrasound, CT, and MRI examinations performed in the acute care setting Provide timely, high-quality diagnostic interpretations to support emergency department and trauma patient care Collaborate closely with Emergency Medicine, Acute Care Surgery, and multidisciplinary clinical teams in the management of emergent conditions Participate in the education and supervision of diagnostic radiology residents, fellows, and medical students Participate in departmental, divisional, and institutional quality improvement initiatives Engage in scholarly, academic, or research activities consistent with departmental needs No expectation to interpret MRI or pediatric imaging studies, and no requirement to perform procedures as part of the Emergency Radiology Division clinical practice. Appointment Details This is an open rank, fixed term faculty appointment at the rank of Instructor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

title: Pediatric Otolaryngology Faculty (Open Rank)
description: The Department of Otolaryngology/Head & Neck Surgery at University of North Carolina - Chapel Hill seeks a new member to join its Division of Pediatric Otolaryngology/Head and Neck Surgery as a fixed-term track faculty member; this is a fixed-term open rank recruitment; academic rank will be awarded at the level commensurate with experience. This role offers the opportunity to provide comprehensive, family centered care for infants, children, and adolescents with a wide spectrum of routine and complex ear, nose, throat, and head and neck conditions for children and families across North Carolina and the Southeastern United States. The Department's faculty members are a part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment, working closely with pediatric subspecialists, anesthesiology, speech language pathology, audiology, and other allied health partners. The position includes active involvement in teaching and mentoring medical students, residents, and fellows, as well as opportunities to contribute to UNC's academic mission through research, clinical trials, and ongoing scholarly activity. UNC offers robust clinical resources, a strong referral base, and a supportive academic culture that values innovation, collaboration, and professional growth. The successful candidate should have expertise in all aspects of Pediatric Otolaryngology/Head and Neck Surgery and an interest in contributing to a very strong clinical and research program in Pediatric Otolaryngology/Head and Neck Surgery. Special expertise and an interest in sub-specialization including Pediatric Airway/Aerodigestive Surgery, Pediatric Otology including Pediatric Hearing Loss and Cochlear Implantation, Craniofacial Surgery, Pediatric Head and Neck Surgery, Rhinology and Endoscopic Skull Base Surgery, and Research in Pediatric Otolaryngology/Head and Neck Surgery and have demonstrated the potential for teaching, patient care and clinical research are encouraged to apply for this position.

title: Electrical Engineer
description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $7,500 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN 2 INSTALMENTS WITHIN TWELVE (12) MONTHS OF HIRE: $3,750 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE & $3,750 12-MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE. The Electric Distribution Systems Engineering Technician manages construction/obsolescence projects. This position must be familiar with the North Carolina State Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) project framework and processes, have experience working in the construction industry and communicating with peers, customers, contractors, engineers and state officials. This position's duties require familiarity with Geographic Information System (GIS), Electrical Distribution System switching procedures, Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition System (SCADA), Electrical Distribution System Single Line Diagrams, Meter System, LiDAR capture and Field experience with overhead and underground Medium Voltage Electrical Distribution System circuit configurations. In addition to the above duties, this position will be required to manage assigned projects and write work orders. This requires knowledge of the Bluebeam Revu and IBM Maximo system (work management system) to produce work orders, purchase requests, produce sketches and have the ability to work with contractor/designers on the EDS system.
