Position Description The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill School of Medicine is seeking a Neuroradiologist to join the Division of Neuroradiology within the Department of Radiology. This position supports clinical care, education, and academic activities in a tertiary and quaternary care environment. The Neuroradiology Division provides diagnostic imaging services for adult and pediatric patients and collaborates closely with Neurointerventional Radiology, Emergency Radiology, and Pediatric Radiology, as well as multidisciplinary teams in Neurology, Neurosurgery, Oncology, Radiation Oncology, and related specialties. UNC Medical Center is a Level I Trauma Center and Comprehensive Stroke Center. Position Responsibilities Interpret diagnostic neuroradiology studies, including advanced CT and MRI of the brain, head, neck, and spine Supervise and teach neuroradiology fellows, diagnostic radiology residents, and medical students Perform basic fluoroscopic spine procedures Participate in multidisciplinary conferences and clinical consultations Participate in scholarly activities, research, or mentoring of trainees on academic projects, as appropriate Appointment Details This is an open rank, fixed term faculty appointment at the rank of Instructor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

title: IPS Employment Specialist
description: This position will function as a member of the Individual Placement and Support Supported Employment (IPS-SE) program within the UNC Center for Excellence in Community Mental Health. IPS-SE is a community-based service which aims to assist individuals with serious mental illness to find and maintain competitive employment in the community, an essential component of individuals' recovery. The IPS-SE program works closely with behavioral health service providers and the department of Employment and Independence for Persons with Disabilities (EIPD, formerly Vocational Rehabilitation). This IPS-SE team member will carry out direct services for IPS-SE participants including: Engagement - Providing information about employment and employment supports to encourage individuals to consider pursuing their vocational goals Assessment - Gathering information about individuals' employment and educational histories, goals, and preferences to create a person-centered employment plan Job Development - Connecting and developing warm relationships with potential employers in the community to better understand their hiring needs and create opportunities for IPS-SE participants Job Search - Assisting individuals in exploring employment opportunities that match their preferences and goals Follow-Along Support - Providing ongoing support to individuals after securing employment to promote success on the job and continue to make progress toward their personal goals. This position will participate in IPS-SE team activities including weekly team meetings, treatment team meetings with behavioral health partners, and regular meetings with EIPD. This position will be responsible for timely completion of required service documentation and may assist in outcomes tracking and reporting for the program.

title: Electrical/Mechanical Engineer
description: A SIGN ON BONUS OF $7,500 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN TWO INSTALLMENTS WITHIN TWELVE (12) MONTHS OF HIRE: $3,750 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE AND $3,750 12 MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE. The Cogeneration Systems Electrical/Mechanical Engineer provides technical expertise and oversight for all electrical Cogeneration Systems projects, including electrical systems, equipment, and components within the facility(s) and steam distribution network. Responsibilities include addressing plant operational concerns; design and implementation of major and minor plant modifications; developing and maintaining preventive maintenance programs; reviewing designs; and ensuring the integrity and reliability of systems and equipment. This position works closely with the Cogeneration Systems Management Team and Engineering Staff to support safe and reliable plant operations. This position interacts with designers throughout construction projects, including new capital improvement projects. Following operational acceptance of capital improvement projects, the position will design engineering modifications, as needed, to improve the performance of the Cogeneration Facility. Using its extensive knowledge of plant systems and equipment, this position also assists with training operations and maintenance personnel on systems and equipment related to its area of expertise.

title: Health Research Coordinator
description: The Department of Social Medicine is seeking a motivated, organized, and community-focused Health Research Coordinator to support the implementation of multi-component Food Is Medicine research study as part of the Healthy Living Anson research initiative in Anson County, North Carolina. The coordinator will be instrumental in coordinating the delivery of the Med-South Lifestyle Program (MSLP), a healthy lifestyle intervention focused on improving diet, physical activity, and overall health. The Health Research Coordinator will supervise Community Health Workers (CHWs) and work closely as part of a research team to ensure that the MSLP is delivered consistently as designed and integrated with the other study components. The coordinator will be responsible for supervising and training the CHWs, coordinating and tracking the CHWs delivery of the program and adherence to study procedures, following the project manager’s direction to ensure that the MSLP is integrated seamlessly with the other components of study, and documenting and reporting outcomes.

title: WUNC Technology Support
description: This position will provide technical support and/or programming to staff which may include installing and configuring computer hardware, software, networks, printers, and scanners, diagnosing, and solving hardware/software issues and analyzing any underlying issues as necessary. This position will also carry out project management of IT systems upgrades, migrations and organization.

title: Auxiliary Operator
description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $5,139 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN 2 INSTALLMENTS WITHIN 12 MONTHS OF HIRE: $2,569.50 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE AND $2,569.50 12 MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE. The position will assist the Assistant Control Room Operator (ACRO), Control Room Operator (CRO) and the Shift Supervisor (SS) in the safe and reliable operation of all plant systems and equipment related to the production of steam and electric generating facilities (Cogeneration Systems and Manning-Drive Steam Plant).

title: Senior Capital Project Manager
description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $7,500 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN 2 INSTALLMENTS WITHIN 12 MONTHS OF HIRE: $3,750 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE & $3,750 12 MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE. This position serves as a Senior Capital Project Manager to provide project management services to campus partners, ensuring that design and construction projects are on schedule, within budget, responsive to program needs and comply with or exceed UNC and State Construction Office standards and expectations. The Facilities Planning & Design department is comprised of design professionals who are responsible for the planning, design and management of all capital improvement projects across the Chapel Hill campus, and master planning and the collection and organization of space data and mapping for the greater University. The Capital Project Management team is specifically responsible for the planning and evaluation of space needs for campus partners and auxiliary groups, providing design project management services for the University's Capital Improvement Projects, and land use planning to create a campus environment that supports the University's mission through master planning, development plans and agreements. The department also facilitates Community Coordination where community concerns are addressed through adherence to all zoning regulations, permit requirements and development agreements. Responsible for the planning and management of formal capital projects, which may range from $500,000 to in excess of $100,000,000, and may include the planning and design of new buildings, repairs and renovations of existing buildings, additions, major infrastructure and open space improvements. This involves, but is not limited to, budget and schedule preparation, designer selection, contract negotiation, document review, monitoring of project progress and resolving situations that arise during design and construction. Works with contracted designers, campus partners, committees, authorities, contractors, and others to assure that projects are accomplished in accordance with established guidelines, master plans, policies, and procedures. Work may also involve interpreting and assisting in the development of methods and policy relating to planning and design activities, ensuring that project modifications are carried out in a timely manner, and other related duties as required.

title: Clinical Research Coordinator
description: This position will serve as a Clinical Research Coordinator within the Department of Neurology, Neurosciences Clinical Trials Unit (NCTU). The Clinical Research Coordinator is responsible for the planning, organization, and conduct of multiple clinical research study protocols, including independently collecting and recording data, project administration, and communication with various stakeholders.

title: Director of Energy Management
description: The Director of Energy Management will have overall management responsibilities for the supervision, maintenance and operations and strategic planning for the Energy Management section, which has responsibility for energy conservation activities; commissioning of Building Automation Systems (BAS), lighting systems and building envelope systems for new capital construction; targeted retro-commissioning of building HVAC and controls; management of energy conservation projects, and design review of energy models and life cycles cost analysis. Works closely with the Facilities Engineering section to coordinate design guidelines to capture energy conservation targets and best practices, and provides daily engineering support for Facilities Services maintenance personnel for the UNC-CH main campus, outlying facilities associated with UNC, and Carolina North. Leads and directs the development and implementation of new rules, policies, and procedures in response to evolving changes related to energy management programs on campus. Manages and anticipates complex and problematic work situations and develops solutions; resolves unique and unusual problems that occur on a large research campus with diverse engineering systems. Responsible for multiple State mandated energy reports, including annual energy and water consumptions and cost reporting; performance reporting of completed energy projects; identification, prioritization and cost analysis of proposed energy and water conservation projects. Large outreach focus across campus to educate on energy policies, best practices and strategies to achieve mandated energy and water conservation goals. Active participation and mentoring of RESPC, the student green fee group, engaging with the EcoStudio independent study program to propose student intern projects and hosting of student interns; robust data analysis, including energy dashboard; on-going engagement with Sustainable Carolina to collaborate and implement strategies that advance the sustainability goals for the University. Position manages a staff of 6 including professional engineers, designers, commissioning technicians, and data analyst and has responsibility of supervising other project managers. Position is responsible for monitoring utility budgets and demonstrating savings related to completed energy projects, including savings projections for proposed projects.

title: RN Clinical Nurse
description: The primary purpose of this Registered Nurse position is to provide nursing services with a focus on the care of participants who volunteer for clinical research studies conducted primarily in an ambulatory setting. The RN will provide specialized, professional nursing care to research subjects for healthy volunteers and to those with unusual and distinctive medical problems according to federal regulations, Good Clinical Practice, and local and institutional polices. The RN will support study implementation within the context of care delivery settings such as in the NC TraCS's Clinical and Translational Research Center (CTRC) and UNC Medical Center as well as provide research on location services at UNC Heath clinics and hospitals, and the Schools of UNC. The RN will provide management of clinical and research support activities in order to assure patient safety, address clinical needs and assure protocol integrity and accurate data collection. The RN will ensure the integrity of research data while maintaining care that is safe, efficient, timely, effective, equitable, compassionate and patient-centered. Job Responsibilities: Care requirements will be determined by the scope of study participation, the clinical condition of the participant and the requirements and clinical effects of research procedures. Duties will include but are not limited to, providing direct, individualized care to adult and pediatric research patients, phlebotomy and IV insertion, administration of investigational medications, monitoring and observation, performing ECG's, collecting and processing biological specimens, other data collection, providing direction and health teaching where applicable in relation to study protocol activities, reporting and recording care rendered, reporting the patient's response to that care, and contributing to the CTRC's continuous quality improvement programs including training of non-licensed research personnel.

title: Study Coordinator
description: This position plays a pivotal role in advancing cancer research and improving patient outcomes by facilitating the conduct of oncology clinical trials in compliance with federal regulations, Good Clinical Practice, and institutional policies. This position independently manages multiple complex trials throughout their life cycle, including activation, implementation, and closure, under the direction of a Clinical Operations Manager. Key responsibilities include: * Recruitment, consent, and enrollment of study participants * Coordination of study visits across various clinic settings * Documentation of procedures and visits, facilitation of sample collection, and data entry * Collaboration with research teams to ensure regulatory compliance and patient safety This position is integral to the mission of the UNC/LCCC Clinical Trials Office, maintaining research quality and safeguarding institutional integrity, and driving discoveries that shape the future of cancer care.

title: Associate Clinical Research Coordinator
description: THIS IS A TIME-LIMITED POSITION WITH AN ESTIMATED DURATION OF 1 YEAR. Flexible work arrangements, including virtual/hybrid work locations, are an integral part of the School of Medicine's Working Forward initiative. As such, this position's work location is designated as hybrid. Please note that the designated work location is subject to change based on the unit's business needs. This position will serve as an Associate Clinical Research Coordinator within the Department of Social Medicine. The Associate Clinical Research Coordinator is responsible for the execution of clinical research protocols, including leading efforts in gathering, compiling, and reporting data for a variety of research studies. The primary purpose of the Associate Clinical Research Coordinator position in the School of Medicine is to assist with the coordination and implementation of a research study as part of the North Carolina Community Engagement Alliance (NC CEAL). This study has multiple functions from implementing an intervention to providing support to improve the built environment in the community, data collection, and analysis to dissemination. This role would be primarily responsible for the data collection, analysis, regulatory, and dissemination areas of the study. The Associate Clinical Research Coordinator is responsible for planning and scheduling data collection activities, participant enrollment and data collection, and preparing study-related materials. This position plays a key role in organizing and maintaining research records, supporting data entry and validation processes, and assisting investigators with basic data summaries and reporting needs. This role is responsible for adhering to approved study protocols, IRB requirements, and federal funding guidelines. In addition, the Associate Clinical Research Coordinator tracks study progress related to recruitment and data milestones, maintains detailed documentation, prepares presentations, manuscripts, meeting minutes, and reports. This position requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, familiarity with research data processes, and the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously. The position reports directly to the program manager and study investigators and must be able to work as a member of research team and collaboratively with community stakeholders to ensure project activities are implemented with fidelity, cultural responsiveness, and alignment with study protocols and funding requirements.

title: Podcast Editor
description: The BME Grad Podcast production team within the Joint Department of Biomedical Engineering is seeking a motivated and experienced work-study student interested in helping bring the BME Grad podcast to listeners across the globe. This position will work closely with the host and producers of the podcast, the Joint BME Communications Specialist, as well as UNC School of Medicine Instructional Media Services. Primary production responsibilities include reviewing and editing recorded audio and video content for the podcast, creating short format content for social media posts. Additional responsibilities may include assisting with planning and scheduling guests, coordinating sound booth time with the UNC Instructional Media Services team, and assisting with hosting services (including posting). Communication responsibilities for this position may include working with the department's social media manager to cross-post podcast-related content to relevant social media channels.

title: Human Services Practitioner - CIND
description: Flexible work arrangements, including virtual/hybrid work locations, are an integral part of the School of Medicine's Working Forward initiative. As such, this position's work location is designated as hybrid. Please note that the designated work location is subject to change based on the unit's business needs. Our goal is to help clinical care teams provide more efficient, effective, and family-centered care that optimizes quality of life and well-being for children and youth with I/DD and their families. This position will serve as a professional peer resource for families seen by primary care providers (PCPs) in partner practices and will provide education, training, and guidance to practice staff on how to effectively support children with IDD and their families, including connection to local community resources. This position will serve as a family system navigator (FN). This position works directly with patient families to provide emotional, informational, and instrumental support to acquire desired services, resources, supports, and therapies. The FN duties and roles include and are not limited to the following: Supporting families (with emphasis on Eastern NC/Trillium connected families) directly in their I/DD and Mental Health (MH) system navigation needs, work with relevant referring UNC pediatric medical providers, liaison and develop key partners in the relevant Managed Care Organizations and other key agencies such as NC START, area provider agencies (Easter Seals, ARC, ASNC, etc.), support the teaching of other UNC pediatricians and pediatric resident physicians, medical students, and LEND trainees about the I/DD system and common I/DD support needs, connect and/or network with similar efforts such as Duke Pediatrics program, and interface with other family system navigators from related projects at UNC, Duke, and elsewhere, assist in the ongoing development of FN training materials, assist in the tracking and monitoring and reporting of key outcomes. Additional responsibilities include: conduct needs assessment with patients and family to identify needed resources, communicate identified needs with clinical teams, build and provide tailored support for clinical teams, patients and families, initiate and respond to contact from families and community service providers, and help patients, families, and providers increase their knowledge of programs and systems as well as develop their advocacy skills. FNs may also receive and track referrals and document outcomes of support provided, demonstrate accurate, clear, professional, and timely communication, and engage in regularly scheduled team meetings, peer support, and supervision. FNs will document or communicate in Epic electronic health record, Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel and Outlook email. FNs will adhere to all HIPAA compliance and patient confidentiality rules. FN's will engage in at least weekly clinical team meetings in which they will report back progress, share new information gathered from the family, and advocate on behalf of the family's self-determined and expressed priorities. This hybrid position is part time, approximately 20 hours/week. There is some flexibility in work hours for this position, however, applicants will be expected to complete approximately 15 hours/week of their works tasks during business hours, at the identified pediatric/family care office. The remainder of the hours can be completed virtually, with at least two mandatory meetings/week that will occur during regular business hours.

Responsibilities will include processing and curating large clinical datasets; developing reproducible computational pipelines; conducting internal and external validation studies; evaluating model discrimination, calibration, and robustness; and working with collaborators to interpret study findings. The successful candidate will be expected to lead or make substantial contributions to peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, and research reports; assist with preparation of grant proposals and regulatory or data-governance materials; document and share research software; and participate actively in interdisciplinary research meetings. Depending on experience and interests, the individual may also mentor graduate and undergraduate researchers and contribute to collaborative projects involving computer science, biomedical engineering, radiology, cardiology, and population health. Position Summary: As a member of the Global Food Research Program ( GFRP ) team, the GFRP Research Associate contributes to studies examining the impact of food and beverage policies in the US and around the world. GFRP research projects include evaluating the effect of policies and proposals using large-scale population-level datasets on the food supply, food purchases, prices, dietary intake, and health. The GFRP Research Associate works closely with our interdisciplinary team and collaborates with research staff, students, programmers, project managers, and many colleagues at UNC and across the globe. The GFRP Research Associate is responsible for planning, interpreting, analyzing, and evaluating results using household food purchase panel data, retail food sales, and packaged food and beverage nutritional data, thus experience with large and complex datasets is required. Expertise in longitudinal and other advanced statistical methods is required, as is the ability to develop and adapt statistical models, conducting diagnostics and management of these data. Familiarity with packaged food and beverage product labelling regulations and implications for data quality, methods, and analyses is required as is familiarity with the application of ultraprocessed food definitions and other nutrient and food classification systems. This position is expected to independently conduct data analysis with input from the GFRP Co-Directors and the research team, and to interpret, and validate and/or redirect research methodology, plans, and publications based on outcome of analyses and results. This position may provide consultation to both the GFRP team and collaborators as an expert involving complex data and methods; the ability and willingness to work with a large mix of people and work styles is critical. Shu Wen Ng, Lindsey Smith Taillie, and collaborators. This role includes co-authoring manuscripts, publications, and reports. A critical piece of GFRP’s research and evaluation is the time-sensitive dissemination of research findings to stakeholders to inform development and refinement of food policies. As needed, this position may also be responsible for the development of presentations, policy briefs, fact sheets, presentations, and other materials required to disseminate these findings in a time-sensitive manner and may serve as primary presenter. This position may collaborate with GFRP Co-Directors in the conception and design of original research.

title: Open Rank
description: The Division of Hematology and the UNC Blood Research Center (BRC) at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seek an accomplished physician-scientist to serve as Director of the UNC Blood Research Center. Candidates should be nationally recognized leaders in benign/classical hematology and eligible for appointment as Associate Professor or Professor on the tenure track. The UNC Blood Research Center is a multidisciplinary research organization focused on basic, translational, clinical, and population-based investigation of benign hematologic disorders. The Center serves as the scientific home for benign hematology research across UNC and fosters collaboration from laboratory discovery through clinical implementation. The successful candidate will have a strong record of scientific leadership, high-impact publications, and sustained extramural funding. Areas of interest include thrombosis and hemostasis, sickle cell disease and hemoglobinopathies, hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, hematopoiesis, iron metabolism, vascular biology, gene and cell therapies, and related blood disorders. The Division of Hematology includes physician-scientists, clinical investigators, and basic scientists engaged in research spanning laboratory discovery through clinical investigation. The Division maintains nationally recognized programs in sickle cell disease, bleeding disorders, and hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, with close collaboration across adult and pediatric hematology programs. Clinical and research activities are housed within the Eastowne Medical Office Building, which includes dedicated clinical research infrastructure. The Blood Research Center includes more than 40 investigators from multiple disciplines and benefits from strong collaborations across UNC, including the Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center, Gillings School of Global Public Health, Eshelman School of Pharmacy, and Biomedical Engineering. The Francis Owen Blood Research Laboratory further strengthens the Center's translational research capabilities. The Director will provide scientific and strategic leadership for the Blood Research Center and advance its mission as a premier center for benign hematology research. Responsibilities include: * Developing and implementing a strategic vision for growth in basic, translational, and clinical research. * Fostering multidisciplinary collaborations across UNC and with external partners. * Promoting translation of scientific discoveries into diagnostics, therapeutics, and clinical trials. * Supporting faculty development, mentoring junior investigators, and strengthening training pathways. * Serving as Program Director of the NIH-supported T32 training program and overseeing research training initiatives. * Leading recruitment of physician-scientists, translational investigators, and basic scientists. * Overseeing research space, shared resources, and Center finances. * Partnering with institutional leadership to enhance the national visibility and impact of benign hematology research at UNC. The Director will report to the Chief of the Division of Hematology and serve as the principal advocate for benign hematology research. Academic rank, leadership responsibilities, and compensation will be commensurate with the candidate's experience, accomplishments, and national stature. Academic rank will be commensurate with the candidate's experience and accomplishments. The successful candidate will be expected to meet UNC criteria to be appointed on the tenure track.

As part of energy management unit, this position is responsible to identify and analyze new energy and water conservation projects (scoping and life cycle cost analysis), building audits and drawing reviews to develop the energy conservation projects with fundable cost estimations and savings calculations. Familiarity with building energy modeling software like Trane Trace and Bin data calculations is a plus. This position will partner with engineering services and other units within UNC facilities department during implementation of energy conversation measures, new strategies for optimizing HVAC systems to improve operational efficiencies while considering O&M concerns and ensuring projects are completed under budget and on schedule. Tracking issues encountered during each project in an Issues Log to ensure discrepancies are addressed properly and timely and project share lessons learnt with the team to improve internal processes. This position will also provide technical support for building control technicians and EMCS system operators and will provide support on technical, process and other aspects related to energy management unit 's responsibilities, as needed by the supervisor. This position is neither remote nor hybrid. Position is located in Chapel Hill, NC and will require the incumbent to be present at the office and work on the UNC campus buildings during the work week.

title: Carpenter
description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $4,081 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN 2 INSTALLMENTS WITHIN 12 MONTHS OF HIRE: $2,040.50 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE & $2,040.50 12 MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE. Perform duties and responsibilities associated with the carpentry/construction trades, including but not limited to proper and safe use and operation of associated powered or hand tools of the trade; general maintenance, repair, replacement, fabrication, installation, and alteration of structures; reading and interpreting construction blueprints and detailed job descriptions; creating materials take-off lists and completing purchase requisitions for materials; completing requisitions for other purchases (i.e., tools and tool accessories as necessary;) planning, problem-solving, and reporting any issues to immediate supervisor. * Must possess a valid North Carolina Driver's License or ability to obtain one prior to start date.

title: Add Health Assistant Project Manager
description: The National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health (Add Health), housed and administered at the Carolina Population Center (CPC) is a comprehensive nationally representative longitudinal study that started in 1994-95 when our participants were adolescents, and was the first study to follow more than 20,000 young people from their teenage years into adulthood; over six waves of data collection to date. Over the 32 year long and continuing project, Add Health has and continues to collect rich demographic, social, familial, behavioral, psychosocial, cognitive, and health survey data from participants and their parents; a vast array of contextual data from participants' schools, neighborhoods, and geographies of residence; and in-home physical and biological data from participants, including genetic markers, blood-based assays, anthropometric measures, and medications. The primary purpose of the Add Health Assistant Project Manager is to assist with overseeing data collection, ancillary studies, lab coordination, and information management activities for the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health (Add Health). The Add Health Assistant Project Manager will utilize comprehensive knowledge and expertise to drive a variety of project activities. They will apply advanced knowledge of research and lab processes and principles to maintain responsibility for co-leading fieldwork activities, report creation and interpretation, and overall data quality assurance. This role will be instrumental in the design and execution of strategies for improving respondent communications, leading literature reviews, managing IRB submissions, editing and formatting manuscripts, and organizing the development of questionnaires and fieldwork protocols. In terms of data handling, the Add Health Assistant Project Manager at this level will have the ability to design data/information collection procedures, identify and report variations in data, and create new research tools as necessary. They will analyze and reconcile data from different internal and external sources, necessitating full knowledge of statistics and related information technology. The Add Health Assistant Project Manager will provide advanced synthesis and organization of data from various sources, including the creation of complex reports, and making recommendations based on their findings. Communication, research skills, and leadership will be key in this role. The Add Health Assistant Project Manager will be expected to effectively share project updates, present at team and staff meetings, and serve as the primary presenter to various audiences. They will have the ability to interpret findings, make informed recommendations, train project research assistants, and lead consultations. In the role of organizational and analytical support, the Add Health Assistant Project Manager must possess the advanced skills to concurrently manage multiple complex tasks, coordinate schedules for a multitude of investigators and staff, communicate in a professional manner with research partners, lab personnel, and university resources, and oversee the procurement and management of study materials, biomarker specimen collection kits, website design, and large-scale mailings. These duties will require the Add Health Assistant Project Manager to be a hybrid position with several days a week in office at CPC with other Add Health staff members.

title: Open Rank - Fixed Term - (Assistant/Associate/Full) Teaching Professor
description: The Division of Data Science and Society (DSS) in the School of Data and Information Sciences (SDIS) at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for 9- or 12-month, fixed-term, open-rank (Assistant/Associate/Full) Teaching Professor in Data Science, with a focus on artificial intelligence, including the ethical, practical, and societal applications of AI tools. The position is to provide high-quality undergraduate instruction in data science and artificial intelligence while contributing to the continued development and expansion of the School's data science and AI curriculum. The successful candidate will teach courses such as DATA 117, DATA 317, and DATA 110 and will have opportunities to develop and teach new courses and learning experiences in AI and related areas. The position will contribute to the School's ongoing expansion of data science and AI education by identifying emerging topics and instructional needs, developing innovative and accessible courses, and supporting curricular initiatives, including the AI minor launched in Fall 2026. The successful candidate will collaborate across disciplines to ensure that course offerings reflect evolving AI methods, technologies, applications, ethical considerations, and societal implications. We especially seek candidates with expertise or experience in: * Understanding how AI systems operate, including supervised learning, unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, generative AI, and related approaches. * Ethical, legal, and societal considerations in data science and artificial intelligence, including data privacy, regulation, responsible AI, and responsible data use. * Making AI accessible to students with diverse technical backgrounds through engaging and inclusive undergraduate teaching. * Creating hands-on learning experiences that apply AI to research, writing, data analysis, creative work, coding, and other academic and professional activities. * Teaching introductory data science or AI courses, particularly courses serving undergraduate and first-year students. * Advising and mentoring a growing undergraduate student population. The standard instructional assignment is three courses per semester for 9-month appointments (six courses annually) and four courses per semester for 12-month appointments (eight courses annually). This is a permanent fixed-term faculty position with an initial three-year appointment, subject to reappointment, and a pathway for advancement in rank.

title: Practice Director
description: The Practice Director serves as a senior operational and strategic leader within the Gillings School's practice enterprise, reporting to the Associate Dean for Practice and working in close collaboration with the Director of the North Carolina Institute for Public Health (NCIPH), faculty, staff, students, and high-level external partners across North Carolina and the country to help develop, refine, and deliver on the School's practice strategy; lead key practice initiatives; track impact; communicate progress; and ensure that the Gillings School is measurably improving the public's health. The Practice Director holds primary responsibility for designing, implementing, and evaluating the Gillings NC Practice Hubs. This includes leading co-development with community partners, facilitating engagement between Gillings' academic and practice resources and local communities, and developing long-term student practica, internship, and fellowship opportunities with governments, health care organizations, non-profits, and businesses. The Practice Director leads key governance structures including the internal Practice Coordinating Committee, the external Practice Advisory Committee, and the North Carolina academic public health practice network, and co-leads the development and implementation of a practice funding strategic plan in partnership with the Associate Dean for Practice and Advancement. In addition to project leadership, the Practice Director oversees program administration including practice metrics development, health data monitoring, impact tracking and reporting, and benchmarking of practice strategies and portfolios across peer schools of public health.This role also directs all practice-related communications, including the Gillings practice web presence, school-wide and community-facing communications, and the development of advancement materials in support of practice fundraising goals. This position will report to the Associate Dean for Practice.

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate
description: The Center for Innovation and Sustainability in Local Media seeks a postdoctoral researcher to help lead applied research on the future of local journalism. The position will support projects examining the sustainability, innovation and civic role of local news, including the impact of artificial intelligence, changing audience behavior and new business models. The researcher will contribute to study design, IRB development, data collection and analysis, reports and scholarly publications, and will work with faculty, students and external media partners to translate findings into useful tools and insights for the field. This position may be eligible for hybrid work schedule. Employees are generally required to reside in North Carolina, within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned duty station.

title: Control Room Operator
description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $6,953 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN 2 INSTALLMENTS WITHIN 12 MONTHS OF HIRE: $3,476.50 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE & $3,476.50 12 MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE. The position is responsible for the safe and reliable operation of all equipment and systems to meet the steam and electrical demand of the campus. It works independently or with minimal direction from the Shift Supervisor. This requires high-level plant operating skills with detailed plant and systems knowledge. This position communicates with the appropriate personnel to ensure that all malfunctions are corrected to maintain continuous steam and electric service to the customers. Communications with the operators and maintenance personnel must be clear and concise. Position is the first responder to off business hours neighbor telephone queries that must be handled in courteous and professional manner. Position runs nightly reports and updates the appropriate spreadsheet reports accurately and timely. The data in the reports is used for reports submitted to EPA, NC Department of Air Quality (DAQ), Department of Energy (DOE), NC Department of Water Quality (DWQ) and engineering studies. Be aware of the requirements of the One Plan that details the Facility Response Plan (FRP), Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure Plan (SPCC), the Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWP3), and the UNC Emergency Plan/DEHS Emergency Response Plan (UNCEP). Position is required to remain current on all operating procedures, plant configuration changes and provide recommendations for improvements and revisions if needed. The position is to assist Shift Supervisor in the training of junior level operators. The position will be trained in Shift Supervisor responsibilities and may be required stand in for Shift Supervisor if needed and qualified to do so. Use and enforce all safety and operating procedures at all facilities. Position will be the primary to issues all lockout/tagout clearances for maintenance. As part of the clearance, perform pre-job briefings at the beginning of the shift and when the job assignment has significantly changed. Always use PPE as designated for task and the work site. Also, includes housekeeping and maintaining a neat clean working environment. This position assists in facility security during non-business hours and weekends 24/7. THIS POSITION IS REQUIRED TO WORK A 24/7-365 DAYS/YEAR ROTATIONAL 12-HOUR SHIFT SCHEDULE. THIS INCLUDES NIGHTS, WEEKENDS AND HOLIDAYS. IT IS EXPECTED TO COVER ABSENCES BOTH PLANNED AND UNPLANNED WHEN NECESSARY. EXAMPLES INCLUDE: VACATION, SICK LEAVE, ETO, STAFFING SHORTAGES/CHALLEGES, ETC.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate
description: The ACM Lab (www.acmlab.org) in the Department of Psychiatry and Department of Computer Science at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seeks a talented, highly motivated postdoctoral researcher with a background in machine learning and/or biomedical image processing. The ACM Lab is developing software to support AI-driven techniques to rapidly diagnose, track, and treat neurodisorders. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in Agentic AI and large language models (LLMs), with demonstrated experience in designing autonomous or semi-autonomous AI systems for complex scientific workflows. The candidate will contribute to the development of next-generation AI software within the ACM Lab that leverages LLMs, multi-agent reasoning, and advanced machine-learning techniques to enable rapid, scalable analysis of large-scale neuroimaging datasets. Responsibilities for this position includes: * Developing deep-learning approaches for insight and analysis about mouse behavior from video * Machine Learning: use your expertise in statistics and machine learning to analyze high dimensional medical imaging data * Make it easy to get high quality, automated, results without expert intervention. Build scalable products and reusable libraries in Python, Scala, and/or C++, taking advantage of Spark, Hadoop, and other tool stacks as appropriate. * Developing computational and algorithmic approaches to understanding the neurobiological mechanism of neurodisorders. * Interact cross-functionally: work with people across the team to find creative solutions and deliver them. * Skilled at data visualization and presentation: The candidate will be called upon to present work at national and international research conferences.

title: Open Rank
description: Flexible work arrangements, including virtual and hybrid work locations, are an integral part of the School of Medicine's Working Forward initiative. This position may be eligible for a virtual or hybrid work arrangement, in accordance with UNC policy and subject to approval based on the unit's business needs. Please note that the approved work location may change over time to meet operational requirements. Position Description The Department of Radiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking an Abdominal Imaging Radiologist to join the Abdominal Imaging Division. This position supports the department's clinical, educational, and academic missions within a high volume academic medical center. The Abdominal Imaging Division provides diagnostic imaging services across the UNC Hospitals system, including a Level I Trauma Center, Women's Hospital, Children's Hospital, Neurosciences Hospital, and the NCI designated Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center. Faculty collaborate closely with multidisciplinary clinical teams to support comprehensive patient care. Position Responsibilities Interpret a full range of abdominal imaging studies, including CT, MRI, ultrasound, radiographs, and fluoroscopy Participate in teaching and mentoring diagnostic radiology residents, fellows, and medical students Collaborate with multidisciplinary clinical teams through conferences, consultations, and protocol development Participate in departmental, divisional, and institutional quality improvement initiatives Engage in scholarly or research activities consistent with departmental needs Appointment Details This is an open rank, fixed term faculty appointment at the rank of Instructor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, commensurate with experience and qualifications.

title: Open Rank, Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine Physician
description: The Department of Pediatrics at The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC)/ North Carolina Children's Hospital is seeking an individual for a 1.0 FTE, non-tenure track open rank, physician faculty position in the Division of Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine to provide clinical care and contribute to our other missions. Rank and salary will be commensurate with training, experience, and academic accomplishments. The North Carolina Children's Hospital is part of a quaternary care medical center with a 64-bed multidisciplinary Neonatal Critical Care Center (NCCC) that admits over 900 patients per year and supports active pediatric general surgery, pediatric cardiothoracic surgery, newborn airway programs, as well as being the referral center for central and eastern North Carolina. The Division of Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine currently consists of 19 faculty members and 7 fellows who are part of a fully accredited Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine Fellowship Program. NIH-funded research projects include the ELGAN-ECHO Study and participation in the NICHD Global Health Network, the Neonatal Research Network, the Pediatric Trials Network, and investigation focused on neonatal intestinal inflammation. Greater Chapel Hill is a two-town, three-county region situated in the center of North Carolina, equidistant to the mountains and the beach, and offers small town charm and big city cultural and athletic events. Our region features one of the best public-school systems in the country, world class health care facilities, and access to one of the best workforces in America. Chapel Hill is a community filled with brilliant minds, award-winning restaurants, innovative businesses, outstanding public schools, and a vibrant music and performing arts scene. This community is considered one of the best college towns in America.

title: Surgical Oncologist
description: The Department of Surgery at the University of North Carolina is seeking applications for a full-time surgical oncologist to join our Division of Surgical Oncology. This position is being recruited as an open-rank, open-track appointment at an FTE between 0.5 FTE and 1.0 FTE. The faculty member will be expected to perform both clinical and research duties, along with the academic responsibilities of an educational institution. While this is an open rank position, we seek applicants with significant experience in open and minimally-invasive surgery for cancers of the liver, biliary tree and pancreas. The Division of Surgical Oncology is among the 9 clinical Divisions in the Department of Surgery. The Division currently includes 16 faculty members and 10 Advanced Practice Providers that provide a broad array of clinical services in order to provide the highest quality multidisciplinary care for our oncology patients. The Division is also actively involved in leading and contributing to our vast portfolio of clinical/translation research and educational missions, through our collaboration with the Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center. Faculty members within the Division of Surgical Oncology possess a desire to commit to all three missions of the Department and School of Medicine, including the clinical, education, and research missions. Clinical responsibilities will include participation in multidisciplinary care, tumor boards, and surgical support of oncology programs. Faculty members are committed to delivering high quality clinical care that is of value to the patients of the UNC Healthcare system. Faculty members are expected to regularly participate in the education of medical students, residents, and fellows. Regarding the research mission, a commitment to any one of a broad array of research interests is critical, including but not limited to oncology clinical trials, outcomes, health services, basic science, translational, ethics, education, or global surgery research. Overall, the selected candidate will be professional, team-oriented, and have the ability to interact well with colleagues inside and out of the Division.

title: Anesthesiologist (Open Rank)
description: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill's Department of Anesthesiology is searching for a General Anesthesiologist (open rank) committed to patient care and Resident education. UNC Hospitals are located on the main campus of UNC Chapel Hill and provide full-service tertiary and quaternary care in a rich academic environment. The department also provides anesthetic care at several community hospitals and ambulatory surgical centers. The physician will be a member of the faculty practice and there are opportunities for scholarly contribution and development.

title: Nursing Professional
description: UNC Chapel Hill School of Nursing is seeking candidates for a Nurse Specialist position. This 12-month EHRA non- faculty position is focused on clinical supervision of students in the on- and off- campus clinical environment. This position requires the incorporation of evidence-based practice into clinical activities and maintaining a commitment to serving the school of nursing, university, profession, and community.

title: Business Services Coordinator
description: THIS POSTING IS FOR 2 VACANCIES. ALL APPLICANTS WILL BE CONSIDERED FOR BOTH VACANCIES. The School of Nursing Administrative Services Office is seeking two full-time temporary employees to provide administrative support for a variety of human resources and financial operations. These positions will assist with processing personnel and financial transactions, supporting faculty and staff, and ensuring compliance with university policies and procedures. The selected candidates will play a key role in supporting the day-to-day administrative functions of the School of Nursing. Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to: Human Resources Administration Initiating and tracking background checks for clinical preceptors and other personnel. Processing temporary employee hiring actions for student and non-student employees. Preparing and submitting lump-sum payment requests. Supporting HR-related transactions and personnel actions in university systems. Maintaining personnel records and ensuring compliance with university policies and procedures. Financial Administration Processing independent contractor, payment requests and related documentation. Processing invoices related to preceptor payments Communicating with faculty and staff to obtain required documentation for travel reimbursements, professional development activities, and other trust or F&A awarded funds. Reviewing financial documents for completeness and compliance with university requirements. Assisting with monitoring expenditures and resolving transaction-related issues. Supporting departmental financial processes and workflow management. Basic reconciliation of financial accounts on a monthly basis. General Administrative Support Interpreting and applying university policies, procedures, and guidelines to administrative transactions. Providing customer service and guidance to faculty, staff, students, and external partners. Maintaining accurate records and documentation. Assisting with special projects and other duties as assigned.

title: Pre-Award OnCore Financial Analyst
description: The Clinical Protocol Office in the Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center has created a Pre-award finance team to work with over 100 PIs to submit budgets associated with a variety of clinical trial funding sources, including federal, foundation, and private industry. Currently, the CPO Pre-award team is separated into two teams; Systems and Budgets. Both teams support the activation of clinical trials, with a slightly different focus -the Systems team focuses on ensuring all systems supporting the financial components of trial activation within the CPO (EPIC, OnCore) are in place quickly and accurately. The Budget team uses OnCore as well as UNC systems (RAMSeS, ALICE, CRMS) to focus on communication of financial details of trials to the University as well as negotiate budgets with clinical trial sponsors. Pre-Award OnCore Financial Analyst will work in the Systems team to translate business requirements into OnCore implementations and optimizations. Responsible for understanding and interpreting complex clinical trial budgets and payment term arrangements for clinical research funding received by the University from federal sponsors, as well as, private, for profit and not-for-profit sponsors including business, industry, associations, and foundations in order to ensure contract and budget terms are meticulously incorporated into OnCore. Works with Pre-Award and Post-Award team members to ensure all financial terms within OnCore is accurate against the Billing Coverage Analysis, fully executed Clinical Trial Agreement, Amendments, Informed Consent Forms and any other pertinent documentation. Works with the Lineberger, UNC Healthcare and other internal groups to identify and remedy errors within EPIC and OnCore's financials and coverage analysis consoles. Keeps abreast of new developments in research administration policies and requirements within the Lineberger CPO and UNC research community in order to serve as an up-to-date source of information and guidance on budgeting nuances. Acutely aware of all software modifications for OnCore which could adversely affect financials, patient care and patient billing. Monitor cross-functional hand-offs to ensure study activation timelines remain on track while sharing key information with key stakeholders throughout the process. Responsible for developing, planning, and implementing OnCore end user support.

title: Open Rank - Assistant or Associate Professor
description: The Division of Information and Library Science (DILS) in UNC-Chapel Hill's School of Data and Information Sciences (SDIS) invites applications for an open rank 9 month tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor position focused on the application of automated methods in cultural heritage and memory institutions broadly understood: libraries, archives, or museums, but also centers for data curation, research data management, or digital humanities. We seek a scholar-practitioner who can combine the craft work of design with the reflexive work of critique. The successful candidate's research will advance the understanding and use of automated methods while being deeply grounded in an understanding of cultural heritage and memory institutions and their values. Key Responsibilities: * Develop and maintain an active research agenda focused on the critical technical application of automated methods in cultural heritage and memory institutions, including but not limited to topics such as: designing benchmarks that reflect the missions and values of these institutions, investigating the use of open and ethically trained generative models, modeling data for both human and automated use, or grounding agentic workflows in trusted metadata infrastructures. * Teach courses on topics related to the ethical design and implementation of automated systems, contributing to the core curricular requirements of both undergraduate and graduate degree programs at DILS. These would include technical courses as well as courses that critically examine the relations between automated methods and cultural heritage and memory institutions. * Mentor and advise graduate and undergraduate students, guiding them in applied research and interdisciplinary projects. * Publish scholarly publications in high-quality, peer-reviewed venues and/or produce tools that prove their worth through wide adoption. * Seek external funding to support innovative research. * Engage in service activities within the division, the school, the university, and the broader academic community.

title: Compliance Investigator
description: The Compliance Investigator investigates complaints of violations of University policies, including, but not limited to the Policy on Prohibited Discrimination, Harassment, and Related Misconduct; the Policy on Prohibited Sexual Harassment Under Title IX; the Workplace Violence Policy; the Nepotism and Improper Relationships Policy; the Alcohol Policy; Whistleblower Policy; and other policies as directed. The Compliance Investigator also investigates complaints of retaliation as defined in University policies and complaints of other types of misconduct as directed. The Compliance Investigator investigates potential policy violations made by and against students, faculty, and staff. The Compliance Investigator is responsible for conducting prompt, thorough and objective investigations of complaints. The Compliance Investigator is responsible for identifying and applying the appropriate policies and procedures for each matter. The Compliance Investigator is responsible for ensuring investigations are conducted in a manner consistent with applicable state and federal law, including Title VI, Title VII, Title IX, the Americans with Disabilities Act, and other applicable law. The primary responsibility for this position is managing the daily responsibilities associated with conducting investigations of complaints, in close collaboration with office leadership. The Investigator will conduct prompt and thorough investigations of complaints, which includes: identifying and interviewing witnesses, gathering and securing relevant documentation, and identifying other information that would be helpful in bringing the matter to resolution. The incumbent acts as an impartial party in the investigation and provides a detailed report summarizing the findings of the investigation and, where appropriate, make conclusions about whether the policy has been violated. Additional responsibilities will include developing an investigative plan for complaints and incident reports, contacting all involved parties, and providing them with information about the investigative process, ensuring a well-documented investigation, analyzing information and working with the appropriate University offices in the course of investigations, maintaining accurate and thorough investigatory files and reports, providing on-going updates to the office leadership, as necessary, presenting the investigative record and/or determination in hearings or grievance proceedings, and continuously identifying and integrating best practices in investigations.

title: Department Manager
description: The Department Manager serves as the senior administrative leader for the department, responsible for translating academic and strategic priorities into effective operational execution within a decentralized school environment. This role partners closely with the Department Chair and faculty while coordinating extensively with centralized/shared service units (Finance, HR, Sponsored Research, and Accounting). The Department Manager ensures that departmental needs are met through proactive planning, service coordination, and escalation, while maintaining accountability for outcomes despite distributed service delivery. The position supervises department-based staff, including student services and administrative personnel. This role has process oversight responsibility across administrative functions and operates with an implicit dotted-line relationship to College functional leadership, including the Associate Dean for Finance, Accounting, and Sponsored Programs Support and the Associate Dean for Human Resources, to ensure consistency, compliance, and alignment with College-wide standards.

title: Virtual Psychiatrist - Open Rank
description: The UNC Department of Psychiatry is seeking an Open Rank Psychiatrist to work virtually providing psychiatric care to inpatient individuals and individuals in emergency departments via our EPIC platform. You will work virtually, collaborating with a multidisciplinary team at Jonas Hills Hospital and other entities within the UNC Health system. The candidate will maintain accurate and up-to-date electronic medical records (EPIC) and clinical documentation, ensuring compliance with all regulatory requirements. This position offers the flexibility of virtual work while making a significant impact on the lives of those in need. The primary shift would be weekdays, daytime hours and yet require participation in the call pool for occasional weekend coverage. This is a fixed term faculty position. Appointment rank will be commensurate with experience and qualifications.

title: Grants and Contracts Administrator
description: We are seeking a Grants and Contracts Administrator. Key duties- * Support preparation and coordination of NIH pre-award submissions, ensuring alignment with ACTG priorities and sponsor requirements * Track and manage proposal timelines and deliverables to support timely submission of complex, multi-component applications * Develop and compile proposal components, including budgets, budget justifications, biosketches, letters of support and supporting documentation * Facilitate communication between ACTG investigators, study staff, and UNC institutional offices to resolve pre-award submission needs * Review proposal packages for completeness, accuracy, and compliance prior to routing through RAMSeS and OSP submission

title: Curriculum Specialist
description: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking a Curriculum Specialist to join the Office of the University Registrar. This full-time temporary role, with a hybrid work schedule, is responsible for overseeing the configuration and maintenance of the University's curriculum within ConnectCarolina (PeopleSoft Campus Solutions), CourseLeaf, the course catalog system, and Simple Syllabus, the university's public syllabus repository. Serving as the primary liaison for curriculum-related matters, the Curriculum Specialist works closely with campus partners to manage course proposals, academic program revisions, academic plan updates, and syllabus submission support. The position ensures accurate system configuration, thorough documentation, and consistent communication regarding curriculum changes, deadlines, and procedures. Key responsibilities include maintaining course and academic plan data, developing controls that ensure the integrity of curricular systems, and delivering outstanding customer service to faculty, staff, students, and external stakeholders. The Curriculum Specialist also supports various administrative processes, including managing Formstack submissions related to role updates and workflow adjustments, while promoting and communicating university policies and procedures.

title: Assistant Professor
description: This is a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Southeast Asian Studies. The faculty member will teach 4 courses per academic year, at the undergraduate and graduate levels, and keep an active research profile and actively collaborate in program development and activities and perform other departmental service.

title: Assistant Professor
description: This is a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in the department of Computer Science. The faculty member will teach 2 courses per academic year, at the undergraduate and graduate levels, keep an active research profile, and actively collaborate in program development and activities and perform other departmental service.

title: Admin Support Associate
description: The Department of Health Sciences is seeking a Temporary Administrative Support Associate to provide essential clerical and operational support. This part-time, campus-based role requires a 100% in-person presence to maintain seamless day-to-day office workflows. Key Responsibilities: * Manage digital and physical document archiving, including high-volume scanning and filing. * Assist with ad-hoc organizational projects to improve office systems. * Provide front-facing and behind-the-scenes office coverage during peak operational periods or staff absences. Additional duties may involve: * Assisting with inventory and office supply management * Supporting departmental events

title: Program Specialist
description: The Program Specialist must learn to interpret and apply OTC policies and procedures for the purpose of managing specific activities within the technology commercialization process. Duties include completing material transfer/confidentiality agreements, monitoring license compliance, processing transactions, and managing government reporting. Individuals must be able to manage their work within and maintain the technology transfer database, administer compliance scheduling, and coordinate reporting as needed. Managing invention report intake and close-out procedures, including reporting information and documentation for federal funding into iEdison and other funding agencies. Serve as the primary contact for grant verification with the Office of Sponsored Programs to confirm if investigators have inventions and if they have been reported to the sponsor. Developed and implementing the automation of certain reporting tasks between BLUE and iEdison to increase efficiency in reporting time and reduce redundancy in recorded information. Creating and maintaining compliance reports for disclosed inventions to assist Commercialization Managers in keeping records up to date and ensure compliance with Bayh Dole regulations, funding agreements, University policies, and OTC procedures. Managing daily operations of the primary office email inbox by resolving inquiries directly and raising issues to the appropriate manager or director in a timely manner for resolution

title: Professor or Associate Professor in 20th- and 21st-century German Studies
description: The Department of Germanic and Slavic Languages and Literatures at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for a full-time, tenured position at the Professor or Associate Professor rank specializing in 20th- and 21st-century German Studies. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027. The successful candidate will demonstrate an active commitment to research and scholarship, teach courses across the undergraduate and graduate curricula, including advanced language courses, and participate in service activities supporting the department and the Carolina-Duke Graduate Program in German Studies.

title: Sr. Director of Development
description: This position may be eligible for a hybrid work arrangement that may include a partially remote work location, consistent with System Office policy. UNC Chapel Hill employees are generally required to reside within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned duty station. As a member of this valued team, the senior director of development will be responsible for the identification, cultivation and solicitation of Arts and Sciences principal and major gift prospects and donors. The primary focus will be on principal gift prospects. This position will work collaboratively with the Foundation team and will report directly to a senior director and assistant vice president of development at the Arts and Sciences Foundation. The senior director's responsibilities may include, but are not limited to: (1) building, managing, and working a principal and major gift portfolio; (2)working closely with the Foundation team to plan and execute principal and major gift activity; (3) playing an integral role in the Foundation's campaign coordination; (4) leading fundraising efforts for key priorities; (5) managing special projects as assigned.

title: Professor of the Practice
description: The Department of Communication at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seeks to hire a Professor of the Practice (fixed-term) in Screenwriting. The successful candidate will teach six undergraduate courses in screenwriting per year, including at least four sections of Intro to Writing for Film and Television. Courses may include small seminars and medium-to-large lecture courses.

title: Senior Assistant Director
description: The Office of Scholarships and Student Aid (OSSA) seeks a creative, collaborative, and highly organized professional to serve as Senior Assistant Director. This full-time, permanent EHRA Non-Faculty position reports to the Senior Associate Director and provides advanced administration, oversight, and counseling for financial aid programs serving graduate and professional students. The Senior Assistant Director independently applies complex federal and state regulations, institutional policies, and professional judgment to determine student eligibility and make financial aid decisions, including decisions that commit University funds. The position provides comprehensive financial aid counseling to current and prospective graduate and professional students; reviews and analyzes FAFSA and other financial aid application data; oversees the accuracy of financial aid awards and disbursements; and resolves complex cases and exceptions requiring professional judgment. The position serves as a key institutional resource and liaison for the Graduate School, individual schools and departments, the Cashier's Office, Heels Hub, Registrar's Office, and other campus partners. The Senior Assistant Director provides guidance regarding scholarship and financial assistance processes, supports the administration and reconciliation of graduate awards reported through GradStar, and assists campus partners in understanding the impact of departmental funding on financial aid eligibility. In addition to direct student support, the Senior Assistant Director identifies operational challenges, develops and recommends process improvements, monitors emerging regulatory and programmatic requirements, and helps ensure consistent and compliant financial aid administration across campus. The position also represents OSSA in student and campus-facing settings, including presentations and outreach to prospective and current graduate and professional students. Through these responsibilities, the Senior Assistant Director serves as a subject-matter resource for graduate and professional financial aid and provides critical operational support to the senior leadership of OSSA.

title: Principal Gifts Manager
description: The Principal Gifts Manager will serve as a senior leader and strategic partner responsible for raising major and planned gifts. The Principal Gifts Manager will lead WUNC's major gifts, planned giving programs, capital campaigns, and supervise WUNC's Grants and Major Gifts Officer. They will assure that new major gift funds are raised annually by developing and implementing cultivation and stewardship plans to meet WUNC's fundraising goals.

title: Assistant Professor Employment Law
description: The UNC School of Government seeks an attorney with a commitment to public service, a desire to teach, and a strong interest in legal research and writing to serve as an Assistant Professor of Public Law and Government with a primary focus on public employment law. Every unit of government is an employer and must meet the legal obligations related to employment that employers generally must meet. In addition, governments as employers have constitutional and other constraints related to their employment obligations that employers in the private sector do not face. North Carolina public employers look to the School for guidance on the law of employment generally and for help with individualized situations particularly. The faculty member in this tenure track position will provide research, training, and advising to state and local government officials on topics of public employment law, including constitutional protections including free speech in the government workplace and statutory requirements, including the Fair Labor Standards Act, the Family and Medical Leave Act, the Americans with Disabilities Act and workers compensation, as well as the application of the State Human Resources Act to local government employees. The faculty member will teach alongside colleagues in a variety of School of Government courses, many developed specifically for human resources professionals and attorneys. Other teaching will be as part of larger courses directed at other local government officials with supervisory responsibilities. Successful faculty members in this type of position become statewide experts and trusted advisors for public officials across North Carolina. Every consultation with a public official, every class taught, and every element of their published scholarship contribute to the School's 90-year legacy of improving North Carolina through better governance.

title: Politics Internship - WUNC Youth Reporting Internship
description: This is a spring 2027 paid internship for one or two days a week during regular business hours, Monday-Friday between 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM. It is responsible for writing and producing audio and digital stories for our daily broadcast newscasts and online platforms. This intern will be on the front line of covering government and politics during a “long” legislative session, focusing on researching introduced bills, government accountability, and other topics as needed. The intern will produce radio and digital reports of various lengths while covering legislative debates, reporting on election management and voting issues, learning to research political funding databases, etc. The intern will benefit from working with the WUNC News Politics team, a group of reporters and editors with more than six decades of cumulative experience covering every aspect of politics and campaigns. The position is expected to start in January and run through early May. Currently enrolled college students and recent graduates are encouraged to apply.

title: Newsroom Intern - WUNC Youth Reporting Internship
description: This is a spring 2027 paid internship for one or two days a week during regular business hours, Monday - Friday, between 9:00 AM - 6:00 PM. It is responsible for writing and producing audio and digital stories for our daily broadcast newscasts and online platforms. This intern will work within WUNC’s News department, primarily with the daily news team, and will be responsible for writing and producing audio and digital stories for our daily broadcast newscasts as well as digital platforms. The intern will have opportunities to complete feature stories, as time allows. There may also be administrative tasks or duties as assigned. Students are asked to dedicate one or two full days a week during regular business hours. The position is expected to start in January and run through early May.
