title: Senior Research Scientist
description: The Senior Research Scientist will provide scientific leadership for a multi-year cancer immunotherapy program focused on advancing AI-designed cancer vaccines and immunotherapies from discovery through clinical translation. Reporting to the Director of Clinical and Translational Sciences, this position will lead the design, execution, and validation of research initiatives aimed at identifying tumor-specific peptide-MHC targets, evaluating novel vaccine platforms, and developing targeted RNA delivery technologies. The Senior Research Scientist will oversee the generation and integration of complex molecular, immunologic, and clinical datasets, ensuring alignment between computational discoveries, experimental validation, and translational objectives. The position will provide strategic direction for research design, data quality, and scientific priorities while supporting development of personalized cancer immunotherapies and other emerging treatment approaches. This role will coordinate multidisciplinary teams across laboratory, computational, and clinical research programs; and monitor progress toward critical milestones throughout the four-year funding period. The position will also contribute to scientific publications, grant reporting, protocol development, and future funding initiatives. Through scientific leadership and collaboration, the Senior Research Scientist will help establish foundational resources for the cancer immunotherapy community, including validated target datasets, shared research protocols, and innovative therapeutic delivery platforms. This individual will play a key role in advancing the institution's strategic priorities in precision oncology, translational science, and personalized cancer immunotherapy. This role is central to achieving the program's four-year objectives and advancing AI-enabled personalized cancer immunotherapies from discovery through clinical testing. The position is expected to act as a collaborator and co-investigator on grants and scientific publications while fostering collaborations across institutional, national, and international research partners.

title: Senior Assistant Director
description: The Office of Scholarships and Student Aid (OSSA) seeks a creative, enthusiastic, and organized individual for the position of Senior Assistant Director. This is a full-time, permanent EHRA Non-Faculty position that will report to the Senior Associate Director of the Office of Scholarships and Student Aid and will provide on-site services at the UNC School of Medicine for all 7 divisions of the Department of Health Sciences under the direction of the Associate Chair for Administration of the Department of Health Sciences. The person in this position will also collaborate with partners in OSSA and Enrollment to ensure financial aid or scholarship practices and policies enacted at the School of Medicine Department of Health Sciences are in line with the mission and goals of the Division of Enrollment. The position will also contribute to the overall financial aid and communications strategy for Graduate and Professional students through collaborations with the Senior Assistant Director for Communications and Outreach and other graduate and professional aid colleagues. This person will have familiarity with HIPAA, OSHA, FERPA regulations and university rules and policies.

Position Description The Department of Radiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking a Cardiothoracic Radiologist to join the Cardiothoracic Imaging Division. This position supports the clinical, educational, and collaborative missions of the department within a high volume academic medical center. The Cardiothoracic Imaging Division is staffed by radiologists with specialized expertise in cardiovascular and thoracic imaging. The division is responsible for interpretation of portable and conventional chest radiographs, thoracic computed tomography (CT) examinations, cardiac CT and MRI studies, and the performance of chest fluoroscopy. The service functions in close collaboration with pulmonology, oncology, internal medicine, cardiology, and cardiac and thoracic surgical services. The division also performs image-guided thoracic procedures, including CT-guided lung and mediastinal biopsies, with opportunities for interested faculty to participate in procedural practice. Division faculty participate as integral members of the Multidisciplinary Thoracic Oncology and Interstitial Lung Disease programs and contribute imaging expertise to coordinated diagnostic evaluation and treatment planning. Faculty are also involved in education and academic activities across the department. Position Responsibilities Interpret cardiothoracic imaging studies, including chest radiographs, thoracic CT, and cardiac CT and MRI studies Perform and/or supervise chest fluoroscopy as part of the clinical service Participate in multidisciplinary clinical care through collaboration with pulmonology, oncology, cardiology, internal medicine, and cardiac and thoracic surgical services Contribute imaging expertise to multidisciplinary conferences and programs, including the Multidisciplinary Thoracic Oncology Program Teach and mentor diagnostic radiology residents, chest imaging fellows, and medical students Participate in quality improvement, scholarly, or academic activities consistent with departmental needs Appointment Details This is an open rank, fixed term faculty appointment at the rank of Instructor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor, commensurate with experience and qualifications. The department welcomes applications from qualified international candidates. Applicants with equivalent international training and qualifications suitable for academic appointment will be considered. Visa sponsorship may be available for candidates who meet institutional and federal requirements.

title: Pediatric Anesthesiologist
description: Be a Tar Heel! The University of North Carolina is seeking a talented and dedicated board-certified pediatric anesthesiologist (open rank) to join our team! The Department of Anesthesiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seeks a skilled pediatric anesthesiologist to join a collaborative and dynamic Division of Pediatric Anesthesiology. The division consists of 16 fellowship-trained pediatric anesthesiologists dedicated to excellence in clinical care, education, and multidisciplinary partnership. Faculty play an active role in resident and fellow education through a fully accredited Pediatric Anesthesiology Fellowship program, with opportunities for mentorship, program development, and leadership. We welcome applicants with a broad range of pediatric anesthesia experience. Candidates with additional training or clinical interest in congenital cardiac anesthesia and/or pediatric chronic pain are highly encouraged to apply. UNC Hospitals and North Carolina Children's Hospital provide a diverse and high-acuity clinical environment, with over 12,000 pediatric anesthetics delivered annually. Clinical practice spans a wide range of surgical and procedural care, supported by a 20-bed multidisciplinary Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) and a 13-bed dedicated Pediatric Cardiac Intensive Care Unit (PCICU). The institution supports an active pediatric cardiothoracic surgery program, as well as ECMO (Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation), burn, trauma, solid organ transplantation, and bone marrow transplantation services. The division maintains an active role in a multidisciplinary pediatric sedation service and a robust regional anesthesia program, supporting both perioperative care and enhanced recovery pathways. UNC Children's also offers a well-established inpatient pediatric chronic pain program and is actively expanding outpatient, multidisciplinary pain services to better meet the needs of patients and families. This position offers the opportunity to build a rewarding clinical practice within a collegial academic environment. The start date for this position is flexible.

title: Pediatric Anesthesiologist & Pediatric Anesthesia Division Chief
description: Be a Tar Heel! The University of North Carolina is seeking a talented and dedicated board-certified pediatric anesthesiologist (open rank) to join our team! Leadership opportunities available for interested candidates! UNC Children's Hospital is routinely ranked amongst the nation's best children's hospitals by U.S. News & World Report with tremendous projected growth including recently passed state legislation to support the creation of a free-standing Children's Hospital. The Department of Anesthesiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking a pediatric anesthesiologist to join our team at UNC's flagship Children's Hospital. Our pediatric anesthesiology practice includes all sub-specialties and spans the spectrum from healthy outpatients to complex neonatal surgery. UNC Children's Hospital is a major regional referral center with pediatric ICU, neonatal ICU, pediatric ECMO, cardiac, burn, trauma, pain, sedation, solid organ and bone marrow transplantation programs. The Division of Pediatric Anesthesiology provides over 12,000 anesthetics per year to the children of North Carolina and surrounding states. The department has an active ACGME accredited pediatric anesthesiology fellowship and serves as the pediatric anesthesiology training site for the University of North Carolina School of Medicine. Our department has a robust Global Health program, a state-of-the-art simulation lab and a strong relationship with the UNC School of Medicine. Protected academic time is offered to pursue clinical, quality, educational and research interests with supporting infrastructure. For applicants looking to launch their academic career, we offer a faculty development program with formal mentorship and a robust professional development curriculum. The department is committed to fostering an environment of diversity, inclusiveness, and equal opportunity. Additionally, the University offers a generous package of benefits.

title: Brand Marketing Strategist
description: Reporting to the Director of Marketing Strategy, the Brand Marketing Strategist is a strategic and execution-focused member of the University Communications and Marketing team responsible for developing, managing and evaluating integrated marketing campaigns that advance Carolina's institutional priorities, strengthen the University's brand and engage priority audiences. The position plays a lead role in moving campaigns from insight and strategy through creative development, activation, execution and measurement. The role also provides experienced marketing counsel to campus partners as needed. The position develops campaign strategies, briefs, channel plans, timelines, budgets and measurement frameworks; coordinates cross-functional teams and external partners; and ensures campaigns are executed cohesively across paid, owned and earned channels. A key responsibility is the ideation and execution of brand activations that bring Carolina's brand campaigns to life through experiences, events, partnerships, content opportunities and other audience-facing moments. The strategist identifies opportunities to extend campaign platforms beyond traditional advertising, develops activation concepts, coordinates production and partners, and evaluates results to inform future work. The position requires strong judgment, initiative, project leadership, creative problem-solving and the ability to manage complex campaigns with multiple stakeholders, deadlines and dependencies.

They will participate in the CEED Summer Research Fellow program, mentoring promising junior investigators in the field. Clinical responsibilities may include assessment and treatment services to children and families in inpatient and outpatient settings. Our research goals are to develop a deeper understanding of the causes of eating disorders and to create more effective diagnostic, treatment, and prevention strategies.

Position Summary: The Bioinformatics Analyst plays an important role in supporting the Center for Generative Immunotherapy’s ( CGI ) efforts to accelerate the development and clinical testing of AI-designed cancer therapies. This position helps researchers collect, organize, analyze, and interpret large amounts of clinical and biological data that are used to evaluate new treatments, improve personalized cancer vaccines, and advance RNA -based therapeutics. The position analyzes data generated from clinical trials and research studies, including genomic, sequencing, immune profiling, and other molecular datasets. The Bioinformatics Analyst develops and maintains data analysis workflows and bioinformatics pipelines that support the processing and analysis of large research datasets. These tools help ensure that data are analyzed consistently, accurately, and efficiently, allowing researchers to generate meaningful results and make informed decisions more quickly. This role provides opportunities to work with advanced sequencing technologies, large-scale genomic datasets, and modern computational tools used in cancer research and precision medicine. The analyst performs customized analyses, creates data visualizations, prepares reports, and communicates findings to researchers and clinical teams. The position collaborates with investigators in planning research studies and developing data analysis strategies. The Bioinformatics Analyst aids in providing input in scientific publications, grant applications, presentations, and other research activities by providing data analysis and technical expertise. Ultimately, this position helps maximize the value of the clinical and molecular data generated through CGI research programs. By ensuring that high-quality data are available for analysis and decision-making, the Bioinformatics Analyst supports the development of more effective cancer treatments and helps accelerate the translation of research discoveries into improved patient care.

The Early Childhood Development Practitioner will contribute to the maintenance of the childcare center's physical environment by discarding any broken or dangerous toys and informing supervisor of any health/safety hazards of the center's physical environment or of items that need to be replaced. This position will establish and maintain effective communication with parents and offer support, advice and encouragement to the parents regarding their child's goals, accomplishments and overall well-being. This position will communicate questions and concerns regarding Horizons and/or Sunrise Corner with other team members with appropriate supervisors.

title: Research Project Specialist
description: THIS IS A TIME-LIMITED APPOINTMENT WITH AN ESTIMATED DURATION OF 3 YEARS. The Research Project Specialist will provide day-to-day coordination, oversight, and management for a federally funded clinical trial evaluating a nutrition intervention for adults with pancreatic cancer. Our research lab focuses on the development and implementation of nutrition interventions, such as dietary coaching, nutrition counseling, and peer support, for adults receiving cancer treatment. The Research Project Specialist will coordinate recruitment and retention of study participants, including screening potentially eligible participants, consenting participants, educating participants about study procedures, scheduling study assessments and activities, sending approved reminders, and following up with participants as needed. This position will also coordinate with clinic staff, oncology providers, the study dietitian, and research team members to support recruitment, intervention delivery, participant follow-up, and study implementation. The Research Project Specialist will support study documentation, data management, and ongoing monitoring of study progress, including documentation in OnCore, REDCap, and study files; tracking recruitment, enrollment, retention, intervention completion, and assessment completion; and preparing study progress updates for the PI and research team. The position will also assist with IRB-related documents, protocol amendments, continuing reviews, recruitment materials, and other regulatory or study documentation. The Research Project Specialist may also assist with participant interviews, qualitative and quantitative data management and analysis, preparation of reports and presentations, and manuscript writing. The position will attend lab meetings and study team meetings and may meet with patients in clinic when needed for recruitment, enrollment, or follow-up.

title: Student Services Specialist
description: The Student Services Specialist for the Curriculum in Global Studies is responsible for the day-to-day management of all student services and related administrative work for both undergraduate and graduate students in Global Studies. This includes managing, promoting, administering, and leading activities in the areas of admissions, financial aid, and course registration as well as the creation, maintenance, and student enrollment in all of Global Studies's GLBL classes on an undergraduate and graduate level. Additionally, the Student Services Specialist is responsible for student development programming along with related budgeting creation and projections for program continuation. This position is responsible for managing data using a variety of computer applications; making independent decisions within university policy, interpreting, communicating, and adhering to policies; and managing student personnel along with maintaining effective working relationships with and among students, parents, faculty, and staff, and other external entities. This includes acting as the primary staff contact for the undergraduate student organization, Global Studies Student Association. Acting as the Curriculum's coordinator for all undergraduate and graduate events, this work includes research, planning, development, and implementation of student programming in response to student and university needs The Student Services Specialist will report to the Business Manager of the Curriculum and work closely with the Chair and Directors of Undergraduate and Graduate Studies. Employees will be required to exercise confidentiality in accordance with policy and applicable state, federal, and local laws such as FERPA (Family and Educational Rights and Privacy Act). Position will also be expected to make administrative decisions regarding budget management, facilities and inventory management, program expenses within current funding levels, as well as projecting future expenses for program continuation, development, and implementation.

title: Assistant Professor of Artificial Intelligence - Writing, Editing, and Digital Publishing
description: The Department of English and Comparative Literature at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is recruiting an Assistant Professor of Artificial Intelligence - Writing, Editing, and Digital Publishing. The successful candidate's duties will include teaching, research, and service. This Assistant Professor will teach a 2-2 load made up of graduate and undergraduate courses; contribute to both undergraduate and graduate curricula; mentor students; participate in select administrative activities; and engage in ongoing scholarly research.

title: Assistant Professor
description: Primary duties: Faculty member will be responsible for teaching a 2:2 load while achieving scholarly excellence in their own research, participating in departmental service, and mentoring undergraduate and graduate students. The Department of History at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in the history of science and technology. Responsibilities include teaching undergraduate and graduate students at both the introductory level as well as upper-level courses in areas of scholarly focus. Scholars who work on any chronological period and geographical specialization are invited to apply. We welcome applications from candidates whose work aligns with our departmental mission as outlined on our website (https://history.unc.edu/about-us/). Applicants must have PhD in hand in the field of history or a closely related field by July 1, 2027. Required Qualifications: Ph.D. in History or related field and evidence of excellence in teaching and scholarship. Teaching load of two courses per semester; salary competitive and commensurate with qualifications. The appointment begins July 1, 2027. An offer of employment is contingent on a satisfactory pre-employment background check. Applicants should submit online at http://unc.peopleadmin.com/postings/ 1) a cover letter; 2) a CV; and 3) the names of four references with contact information. The review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026, and continue until the position is filled.

title: Division Chief of Pediatric Cardiology
description: The Department of Pediatrics at UNC Children's is recruiting an open-rank, open-track (fixed term, tenure/tenure-track, or variable track) faculty member, who will serve as Division Chief of Pediatric Cardiology to lead and expand the division's clinical, educational, and research missions. The division provides comprehensive pediatric and congenital cardiology services across the continuum of care, supports a strong culture of clinical excellence and quality improvement, and serves as a central educational resource for the Department of Pediatrics and UNC Children's Hospital. The Division Chief oversees all clinical operations, including inpatient and outpatient pediatric cardiology services, advanced cardiac imaging, cardiac catheterization and interventional programs, heart failure and transplant services, fetal cardiology, and care for patients with congenital heart disease across the lifespan. The division plays a critical role in multidisciplinary care of children with complex cardiac conditions and collaborates closely with cardiothoracic surgery, critical care, and other subspecialties. This leader will join at an exciting time for child health within the UNC Health system as well as in the state of North Carolina. This past year the Children's Service Line was launched at UNC Health, with the goal of creating systems of care that will improve child health outcomes across the entire UNC Health system, statewide. In addition, planning is underway for North Carolina Children's Hospital, the first freestanding children's hospital in the state of North Carolina. This joint effort with Duke Children's will include a large tertiary/quaternary Congenital Heart program. This Division Chief will play a major role, along with Cardiac and CT surgical leaders at UNC Children's and Duke Children's in the organization and launch of this combined program. The Raleigh-Durham-Chapel Hill area of North Carolina is an attractive place to live and work, with a great climate, schools, and both mountains and beaches within a day's drive. UNC Health has a statewide series of hospitals and clinics and is affiliated with one of the nation's leading medical schools.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate - Wolberg Lab
description: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death and disability in the Western world, and blood coagulation abnormalities contribute to the pathophysiology of nearly every disease, including cancer, infection, and autoimmune and inflammatory disorders. An NIH-funded postdoctoral position is available in the Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine in the laboratory of Dr. Alisa Wolberg at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. The Wolberg Lab is part of UNC's internationally recognized Blood Research Center. Research in the lab focuses on cellular, biochemical, and biophysical mechanisms that regulate blood function and contribute to health and disease. The successful applicant will advance ongoing R01-funded research focused on mechanisms of hemostasis and thrombosis. Potential areas of emphasis include factor (F)XIII biology (including regulation of FXIII-A and FXIII-B subunits, roles in venous thrombosis and thrombus resolution, and therapeutic targeting strategies); fibrin(ogen) degradation and the cellular and enzymatic drivers of thrombus resolution beyond plasminogen; and cellular and plasma mediators of FXI biology that influence bleeding risk. Additional opportunities exist in women's health and blood disorders and mechanisms contributing to pulmonary embolism. Projects will be tailored to the fellow's expertise, with the expectation that the postdoc will initially contribute to established research efforts and, over time, develop an independent line of investigation leading to future fellowship or career development funding. Candidates with experience in biochemistry or enzymology, cell biology (including tissue culture), histology, mouse models of thrombosis and hemostasis, and/or bioinformatics are encouraged to apply. The Wolberg Lab provides a highly supportive, team-oriented mentoring environment with strong emphasis on professional development, grant writing, and opportunities to mentor trainees, while fostering independence and ownership of scientific direction.

title: Distinguished Professor
description: The UNC-Chapel Hill Department of Mathematics invites applications for a tenured Distinguished Professor. The position will also carry a secondary appointment as department chair. The successful candidate will provide visionary academic and administrative leadership for the Department of Mathematics, helping to shape and advance its intellectual direction and strategic priorities. In the chair role, the candidate will work collaboratively with faculty, staff, and university leadership to strengthen the Department's excellence in teaching, research, and service. Responsibilities will include leading and overseeing the Department, teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels, supervising graduate students, participating in academic service, and maintaining a strong, independent research program. For further information on the Department, please visit our website at http://www.math.unc.edu

title: Motor Drive and Starter Technician
description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $4,919 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN 2 INSTALLMENTS WITHIN 12 MONTHS OF HIRE: $2,459.50 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE & $2,459.50 12 MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE. Operates and maintains building HVAC and associated systems with an emphasis on Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) and motor starters primarily for fans, pumps and related equipment. Must demonstrate the TOP SERVICE values of Teamwork, Openness, Professionalism, Stewardship, Excellence, Responsiveness, Versatility, Innovation, Competence, and Efficiency. Must also contribute to the UNC safety culture and always consider safety first. *Must possess a valid North Carolina Driver's License or have the ability to obtain one prior to hire date.

title: Teaching Assistant Professor
description: This is a full-time, teaching-track position at the rank of Teaching Assistant Professor. Successful candidates will be prepared to teach a range of foundational computer science and/or artificial intelligence courses. Opportunities to teach upper-division courses, Honors courses, and in study abroad programs will be available in accordance with each candidate's skills and interests. Ideal candidates will be able to employ evidence-based pedagogical methods and instructional technologies to effectively teach large classes; train, utilize, and mentor undergraduate and graduate teaching assistants; and participate in the development of undergraduate curricula. Engagement in formal academic research is welcome but optional for teaching-track faculty. This position is a state-appropriated, permanent faculty line with an initial term of three years, to be renewed thereafter for terms of up to five years. It offers a promotion path to Teaching Associate Professor and Teaching Professor.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate
description: This Postdoctoral Research Associate will lead engineering work in the Bai lab's translational research program on wearable optical sensing. A central effort is a multispectral pulse oximetry technology that measures blood oxygen saturation accurately across the full range of skin tones. The goal is to advance it from a laboratory prototype toward a clinically validated, manufacturable device. The postdoc will: Design, build, calibrate, and maintain wearable multi-wavelength optical sensors, including the optical front end, embedded electronics, and firmware. Develop and validate signal-processing and machine-learning algorithms that account for skin pigmentation, low perfusion, and motion. Work with UNC clinical collaborators on IRB-approved human-subjects validation studies, including device deployment, data quality control, and statistical analysis. Collaborate with industry partners on design for manufacture, design documentation, and regulatory strategy. Prepare technical reports, manuscripts, and invention disclosures, contribute to grant proposals, and mentor graduate and undergraduate researchers. The position offers direct experience with the full path from academic research to medical device translation.

title: Assistant Professor - Sport Administration
description: The Department of Exercise and Sport Science at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for a 9-month tenure track Assistant Professor faculty position to deepen and expand research and teaching in Sport Administration. We aspire to recruit a faculty colleague who will engage in innovative and impactful scholarship that will diversify and enhance our research, teaching, and public outreach missions, and who can translate this research to teaching undergraduate and graduate level courses in sport law and other sport administration courses. Responsibilities: * Establish a focused line of research, publish articles in top-tier, peer-reviewed journals at a rate commensurate with an R1 institution, and seek intramural/extramural funding to support research. * Teach graduate and/or undergraduate courses (2/1 load) in sport administration including sport law and at least one other core undergraduate curriculum course (sport administration, sport economics/finance, sport marketing, sport facility and event management, sport revenue generation) or at least one graduate-level course ( NCAA governance and compliance, legal issues in college athletics, intercollegiate athletics administration, marketing college sport, college facility and event management, economics and finance in college athletics, research methods, and statistics). * Serve as a research advisor / thesis committee member for undergraduate and master's students in sport administration. * Participate in departmental and university service and governance functions. * Perform other duties as assigned by the department chair.

title: Director of Communications
description: The Director of Communications serves as a senior communications leader for the Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research (OVCR), reporting to the Assistant Vice Chancellor for Research and working closely with University Communications and Marketing (UCM) and the Vice Chancellor for Research (VCR) to advance a comprehensive communications strategy that elevates the visibility, impact, and reputation of the UNC Research enterprise. The Director provides strategic oversight of the Office of Research Communications (ORC), leading a high performing team responsible for advancing the visibility, impact, reputation, and competitive standing of Carolina's research enterprise. The Director also oversees internal and external communications efforts, working at the intersection of research strategy, federal policy, compliance communications, and institutional leadership, requiring scientific literacy, regulatory fluency, and a sophisticated understanding of the federal research funding landscape. The Director serves as the primary communications partner to the VCR as a national voice on research policy across federal agencies, Congress, APLU and AAU leadership, and the broader higher education community. The Director leads integrated communications strategy across ORC's full portfolio: executive communications and thought leadership, research impact storytelling, compliance and policy communications to a 20,000-member research community, stakeholder and philanthropic materials for donors, legislators, and federal partners, and community engagement including OVCR Office Hours and University Research Week. They also oversee the OVCR's primary communications channels to ensure alignment, reach, and engagement. This work is aligned with the OVCR's Research Roadmap, directly supporting research expenditure growth, faculty recruitment and retention, federal funding relationships, and the national reputation metrics that determine institutional standing.

title: Undergraduate Medical Education (UME) Coordinator
description: The Undergraduate Medical Education (UME) Coordinator provides advanced administrative and operational support for undergraduate medical education programs within the Department of Medicine, with primary responsibility for coordinating activities associated with the Inpatient Medicine Core Clerkship and related student educational initiatives. The position serves as a central point of contact for medical students, faculty, residency programs, School of Medicine administration, and statewide campus partners to facilitate the efficient delivery of educational programs and ensure compliance with institutional and School of Medicine policies and procedures. The position coordinates scheduling, course logistics, educational activities, examinations, meetings, communications, and student support services; maintains educational records and databases; tracks evaluations, attendance, grades, and required documentation; prepares reports and data summaries; and manages educational platforms and shared resources. The coordinator provides advanced administrative support to course directors and educational leadership by organizing meetings, disseminating communications, supporting accreditation and reporting activities, and assisting with special projects and continuous improvement initiatives. Success in this role requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, customer service, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders

title: Lead Electrician
description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $4,668 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN 2 INSTALLMENTS WITHIN 12 MONTHS OF HIRE: $2,334 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE & $2,334 12 MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE. Serve as a Lead Electrician in Maintenance Shop 245203. Guide shop employees in daily work assignments. Perform maintenance to a variety of equipment and electrical systems, install and repair electrical systems and components from the load side of the service transformer to the last device. To assist Supervisor in inspections to renovation and construction projects. Respond to daily emergency calls as needed. Keep Supervisor well informed of daily progress. *Must possess a valid NC Driver's License or have the ability to obtain one prior to hire.

title: Housekeeping Trainer
description: The position functions as a trainer for Housekeeping Services including conducting new hire orientations, Operating System 1 (OS1) training and other training programs for cleaning, safety, ergonomics and other topics. *Must have a valid NC Driver's License or ability to obtain prior to start date.

title: Assistant Professor
description: Application review will begin September 15 and continue until positions are filled. Up to four full-time tenure-track faculty positions in the rank of Assistant Professor in the Department of Epidemiology. Competitive candidates will demonstrate strong capacity for research that impacts public health, advances the field of epidemiology, and contributes to the department's teaching mission. As members of the Department of Epidemiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, faculty are expected to develop independently funded research portfolios, contribute impactful scholarly products, mentor master's and doctoral students, and teach core epidemiology methods and/or substantive area courses in epidemiology. The department's primary focus is the development and application of research methods to understand the patterns and causes of health and disease, and the application of that knowledge to improving the health of populations. The department provides strong training in research methods and opportunities to apply epidemiology to a wide range of health problems.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate
description: The Department of Mathematics at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for a postdoctoral position in the Cardiovascular Modeling and Simulation Laboratory (https://griffith.web.unc.edu). This position would support projects on (1) cardiac digital twins for heart failure and/or (2) cardiac fluid dynamics simulation software development in the Cardinal and IBAMR frameworks. The initial appointment would be for one year, with a potential for renewal. The start date is flexible but could be as early as December 1, 2026.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor
description: The Department of Philosophy in the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is recruiting at the level of Tenure-Track Assistant Professor or Tenured Associate Professor in political philosophy (broadly conceived to include philosophy of law), social philosophy (broadly conceived to include philosophy of race/gender and social ontology), or metaphysics. Significant promise of research excellence is a necessary condition for consideration, as is evidence of strong skills in teaching. The successful applicant will normally teach two courses per semester (graduate and/or undergraduate); will be involved in thesis supervision; and will have other standard non-teaching duties such as departmental administration, graduate and undergraduate mentorship, and participation in our department's vigorous intellectual life.

title: GFRP Research Specialist
description:
Department: Carolina Population Center-631100
Career Area: Research Professionals
Posting Open Date: 10/02/2026
Application Deadline: 10/16/2026
Open Until Filled: No
Position Type: Permanent Staff (EHRA NF)

Appointment Type: EHRA Non-Faculty
Position Number: 20078859
Vacancy ID: NF0010092
Full Time/Part Time: Full-Time Permanent
FTE: 1
Hours per week: 40
Position Location: North Carolina, US
Hiring Range: $65,000 to $75,000 dependent on qualifications
Proposed Start Date: 11/02/2026
Be a Tar Heel!: A global higher education leader in innovative teaching, research and public service, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill consistently ranks as one of the nation’s top public universities . Known for its beautiful campus, world-class medical care, commitment to the arts and top athletic programs, Carolina is an ideal place to teach, work and learn. One of the best college towns and best places to live in the United States, Chapel Hill has diverse social, cultural, recreation and professional opportunities that span the campus and community. University employees can choose from a wide range of professional training opportunities for career growth, skill development and lifelong learning and enjoy exclusive perks for numerous retail, restaurant and performing arts discounts, savings on local child care centers and special rates on select campus events. UNC -Chapel Hill offers full-time employees a comprehensive benefits package , paid leave, and a variety of health, life and retirement plans and additional programs that support a healthy work/life balance.
Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit: Since 1966, researchers at the Carolina Population Center have pioneered data collection and research techniques that move population science forward by emphasizing life course approaches, longitudinal surveys, the integration of biological measurement into social surveys, and attention to context and environment. We are also at the forefront of creating interdisciplinary training programs that integrate approaches from the social and biological sciences, building research capacity and training the next generation of scholars. Our faculty fellows address pressing research questions about population dynamics, fertility, health, mortality, migration, and the environment. Faculty come from multiple disciplines, benefiting from the cross-pollination of ideas. Our dedicated research and programming staff support fellows at every stage of project development, from conception through data collection or acquisition, analysis and dissemination, and project administration. https://www.cpc.unc.edu/about/
Position Summary: As a member of the Global Food Research Program ( GFRP ) team, the GFRP Research Specialist will have primary responsibility for leading GFRP’s data procedure & protocol design for evaluations of regulations around the world. The GFRP Research Specialist must be able to comprehensively identify and interpret regulations and legislation (including taxation, labeling, and marketing regulations) and remain abreast of related changes, timelines, nutrient profiles, and thresholds. This position will define standards for collection of nutrition facts panel ( NFP ) data, and instruct others in implementing such standards for accuracy, validity, and integrity. This position will be responsible for evaluating and designing methods and procedures for reviewing, cleaning, and linking datasets (including data on commercial products, marketing, dietary intake, and NFP ), will translate regulations into coding instructions for programmers to apply to various datasets, and verify coding applied accurately. This position will continually trouble-shoot and resolve quality control issues and will work towards improving efficiency and accuracy in protocols and procedures for applying regulatory schemes to various datasets. In the role as Lead for Vietnam, this position will plan, assign, and review work of others, including GFRP staff, contractors, and global collaborators, and will routinely assess needs of the projects and make changes in processes, workflow, and/or assignments. In collaboration with our global colleagues, this position will define work plans to meet objectives and established deadlines. The GFRP Research Specialist will collaborate closely with colleagues at our global collaborators’ research institutions in Vietnam to develop and coordinate instruction and training of staff, students, faculty, and collaborators in the performance of specialized methods of data collection, entry, cleaning, and utilization (including interconnection of data sources). Instruction may use in-person, virtual, recorded, or documentary methods, and communication may be in language of collaborators (Vietnamese). To support GFRP’s aims of capacity building with each of our collaborators, the work performed by this position to develop and train these teams is essential to fulfilling our goals. This role will also include the preparation of documents required for preparation of publications, reports, and proposal development. A critical piece of GFRP’s research and evaluation is dissemination of research findings to stakeholders to inform development and refinement of food policies. As needed, this position will also be responsible for the development of policy briefs, fact sheets, presentations, and other materials required to disseminate these findings. This position requires knowledge and understanding of complex research concepts from multiple disciplines, including dietary intake, dietary quality, obesity, non-communicable diseases, health disparities, food systems, food environment, consumer psychology, food marketing and advertising. As regulation and legislation is proposed, considered, and passed in various jurisdictions, this position will evaluate regulatory schemes by designing methods of application to databases and understanding of typical industry and consumer responses.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in a discipline related to the field assigned and one year of related training or experience; or equivalent combination of training and experience. All degrees must be received from appropriately accredited institutions.
Required Qualifications, Competencies, and Experience: * Strong public health and nutrition research skills (e.g., reviewing scientific literature, creating data collection instruments, managing databases, IRB applications and protocols, training data collectors). * Strong project coordination, interpersonal, and written and verbal communication skills. * High level of organizational skills, attention to detail, and demonstrated capacity to independently coordinate multiple aspects associated with large research studies. * Resourceful approach to problem solving. * Experience collaborating well in teams and ability to function well with culturally diverse colleagues and contacts, as many of our collaborators are international.
Preferred Qualifications, Competencies, and Experience: * Master’s degree and at least 2 years of experience in research preferred. * Experience planning, implementing, and coordinating research projects. * Experience with managing research compliance, Institutional Review Board ( IRB ) processes and submissions. * Bilingual in Vietnamese and English.
Campus Security Authority Responsibilities: Not Applicable.
