title: CISLM Associate Director
description: This position may be eligible for hybrid work schedule. Employees are generally required to reside in North Carolina, within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned duty station. The Associate Director is the senior operational leader for the Center for Innovation and Sustainability in Local Media (CISLM) and serves as the Director's principal partner in translating the Center's strategy into coordinated programs, projects, partnerships, and measurable results. The position manages the Center's day-to-day operations and maintains a comprehensive view of priorities, deadlines, budgets, staffing, grant obligations, events, communications, and external commitments. Working with substantial independence and delegated authority, the Associate Director anticipates needs, resolves operational problems, and brings decisions or risks to the Director at the appropriate time. The Associate Director coordinates the work of staff, students, contractors, faculty collaborators, and external partners; establishes systems that promote accountability and continuity; and ensures that the Center's initiatives are completed on time, within budget, and in alignment with its mission. By providing strong internal leadership and operational follow-through, the position enables the Director to devote significant attention to fundraising, donor cultivation, strategic partnerships, thought leadership, and the Center's long-term growth. The position also supports grant development and fundraising by organizing proposal development, coordinating information and materials, tracking prospective opportunities and donor follow-up, developing budgets and work plans with the appropriate School offices, and ensuring that funded commitments are carried out and reported accurately. Key Responsibilities: - Serve as the Director's principal operational and programmatic partner, converting strategic priorities into clear work plans, timelines, assignments, budgets, and measures of success. - Direct the day-to-day administration and execution of the Center's portfolio of research, education, professional development, public programming, and industry partnership initiatives. - Coordinate and supervise the work of staff, student employees, interns, contractors, consultants, and project teams; establish expectations and monitor performance and workload. - Maintain an integrated view of Center commitments and proactively identify risks, capacity constraints, missed deadlines, resource needs, and decisions requiring the Director's attention. - Manage grant and financial operations in coordination with School and University offices, including budgets, expenditures, contracts, purchasing, reporting deadlines, and compliance documentation. - Support fundraising and grant development through prospect tracking, proposal coordination, research, budget and work-plan development, stewardship materials, and donor or funder follow-up. - Represent the Center in internal and external meetings as delegated by the Director and maintain effective working relationships across UNC and with news organizations, funders, speakers, vendors, and community partners. - Oversee the systems, records, communications, and reporting needed to preserve institutional knowledge and demonstrate the Center's activity, reach, and impact. Occasional evening or weekend work and limited travel may be required to support Center programs, meetings, and events.

title: Academic Neuropathologist
description: The Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, is seeking an Academic Neuropathologist for a tenure-track/tenured, variable, or fixed-term position at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor, with an FTE of 0.5 FTE to 1.0 FTE. This position will involve diagnostic surgical neuropathology, autopsy neuropathology and ophthalmologic pathology; preferably with a second area of interest in a sub-specialized surgical pathology service, autopsy, or research. The successful candidate will be eligible for membership in the UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center and will contribute to the teaching of residents, fellows, medical students, and graduate students.

title: Open Rank
description: The Department of Dermatology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking applications from clinician educators at all career stages to join our team of talented academic dermatologists. We are a group of dedicated clinicians committed to a shared mission of improving the health of people in North Carolina. We are also teachers dedicated to training future leaders in dermatology through our nationally renowned residency program. We have a proud tradition of supporting innovation and research and have historically ranked among the top ten dermatology programs in the nation in terms of NIH funding. We offer flexibility to build a practice based on the applicant's clinical interests, and we offer support for faculty to develop subspecialty expertise. We have a robust clinical program with outpatient sites in Chapel Hill, Hillsborough, and Raleigh, NC, inpatient consultation services, dermatopathology, Mohs surgery, laser services, phototherapy, and a clinical trials unit. We offer diverse state-of-the-art patient care and support numerous subspecialty and multidisciplinary clinics. This position is being recruited as an Open Rank appointment at an FTE between 0.5 FTE and 1.0 FTE. The appointment will be offered as a fixed-term track, variable track, or tenure/tenure track appointment. Applicants must have strong clinical skills and a commitment to academic dermatology with interest and skill in teaching and participating in the training of medical students and residents. We offer a stellar collegial academic environment, a competitive guaranteed salary, an incentive plan, and a uniquely comprehensive benefits plan.

title: Endocrinologist - Open Rank
description: The Division of Endocrinology at the UNC School of Medicine seeks an open rank, fixed term faculty member to join our team. Academic rank will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. Clinical responsibilities will include coverage of our inpatient consult services, providing direct patient care in the outpatient clinic and precepting fellows. The ideal candidate will provide exceptional patient care, be skilled at communicating and working collaboratively across disciplines/departments, and participate in the education of colleagues and trainees, including but not limited to medical students, residents, and fellows. The outpatient practice is located at the UNC Eastowne Medical Office Building (MOB), a state-of-the-art center which opened in 2021 and is located just a few miles from the UNC Medical Center campus. The Eastowne MOB has on-site radiology, laboratory and infusion services, outpatient pharmacy, and ample complimentary parking. This building houses the academic clinical practices of most of the Department of Medicine's divisions, allowing for high-level collaboration, collegiality, and care delivery.

title: General Surgeon
description: The Department of Surgery at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking applications for a full-time academic General Surgeon to join the existing group of five UNC faculty based surgeons who have a focused practice of General Surgery within the community. The practice has some subspecialty focus as well given the fellowship training of the current group. This position will include clinical practice at both UNC Health Care Hillsborough Hospital and the UNC Chatham Hospital. The successful candidate will provide comprehensive general surgery services at both campuses while supporting the Department's mission to expand access to high-quality surgical care throughout central North Carolina and building an elective practice focused on community general surgery. UNC Health Care Hillsborough is a 163-bed community hospital that combines the culture and accessibility of a community hospital with the advanced technology and expertise of UNC Medical Center. It has 10 ORs including 2 with Robotic surgery capability. The campus includes an outpatient medical office building with clinic and procedure space, as well as a busy emergency department. The Chatham hospital is a 25 bed facility with 2 ORs, an outpatient medical office building, and an emergency room. The Department of Surgery is committed to growing both elective and emergency surgical services at Hillsborough and Chatham while extending specialty surgical care closer to the communities we serve. Clinical responsibilities will include elective and urgent general surgery, emergency general surgery call coverage at the Hillsborough campus, outpatient consultation and follow-up at both campuses, and collaboration with multidisciplinary teams across the UNC Health system. The successful candidate will work closely with colleagues across the Department of Surgery to ensure seamless coordination of care across campuses. This position is being recruited as an Open Rank, Open Track appointment at an FTE between 0.5 and 1.0, with academic rank commensurate with the candidate's qualifications and experience. The faculty member will be expected to perform clinical duties while fulfilling the academic responsibilities of an educational institution. Faculty members are expected to contribute to the Department's three core missions of clinical care, education, and research. Individuals who demonstrate exceptional skills and achievements may be considered for leadership opportunities within the Department of Surgery. Leadership roles are not guaranteed and will be dependent upon the needs of the Department of Surgery and UNC Health. Faculty members are expected to participate in the education of medical students, residents, and other learners through clinical teaching and mentorship in both the academic medical center and community hospital settings. Candidates with interests in clinical research, outcomes research, quality improvement, health services research, surgical education, global surgery, or other scholarly endeavors are encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will demonstrate a commitment to providing exceptional, patient-centered surgical care while advancing access to high-quality surgical services in a community practice environment. Candidates should possess expertise in a broad range of general surgical procedures, including minimally invasive surgery. The selected candidate must be collaborative, team-oriented, and able to work effectively with colleagues across multiple surgical specialties, hospital campuses, and interdisciplinary care teams. Individuals who exhibit exceptional skills and achievements may be considered for a leadership position within the department of surgery. Leadership roles are not guaranteed and are dependent upon the current needs of our surgical programs.

title: Open Rank Fixed-Term Faculty Interventional Pulmonary
description: The Division of Pulmonary Diseases and Critical Care Medicine at the UNC School of Medicine is recruiting for a full-time faculty member with expertise in Interventional Pulmonary Medicine. Duties include, but are not limited to, seeing referrals for diagnostic and therapeutic procedures related to known or suspected lung cancer, thoracic metastasis, infectious or interstitial diseases of the lung, and pleural diseases. They will be responsible for management of benign and malignant obstructive airway lesions, lung malignancies requiring endoluminal therapies, robotic assisted evaluation of suspicious parenchymal lung lesions, acute and chronic pleural processes, and performance of bedside tracheostomy placement. These duties will be conducted in the inpatient and ambulatory care settings. They will be responsible for teaching pulmonary procedures to fellow trainees in Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine and subspecialty fellows in Interventional Pulmonary. They will also have opportunities to attend in the Medical Intensive Care Unit with additional related teaching duties. Additionally, the position will include opportunities to conduct clinical research related to cancer diagnostics/therapeutics, pleural diseases, and innovative interventional procedures.

title: System Executive Director - Advanced Heart Failure & Transplant Network
description: The Division of Cardiology in the Department of Medicine seeks an accomplished physician leader in Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology to serve as System Executive Director of the Advanced Heart Failure & Transplant Network for UNC Health. This position will provide strategic leadership for the continued growth, integration, and advancement of a comprehensive statewide network for advanced heart failure, mechanical circulatory support, cardiogenic shock, and heart transplantation. Working collaboratively with physicians, administrators, surgeons, researchers, and clinical teams across UNC Health, the Executive Director will lead efforts to develop and implement a shared vision for network growth, clinical excellence, quality improvement, innovation, and patient access. The individual will be responsible for fostering alignment across academic and community-based programs, strengthening referral pathways, expanding access to advanced heart failure therapies, and advancing the system's mission in patient care, research, and education. This recruitment is for an Open Rank faculty position within the Division of Cardiology, with rank to be determined based on the selected candidate's qualifications, experience, and accomplishments. The successful candidate will hold a primary faculty appointment in the Department of Medicine and a secondary administrative leadership appointment as System Executive Director of the Advanced Heart Failure & Transplant Network, which includes an associated administrative supplement. Clinical responsibilities will include the care of patients with advanced heart failure, heart transplantation, mechanical circulatory support, and cardiogenic shock, while supporting the academic missions of research, education, and service.

title: Assistant Professor of Critical Game Studies
description: The Department of English and Comparative Literature at the University of North Carolina at Chapel is recruiting an Assistant Professor of Critical Game Studies. The successful candidate's duties will include teaching, research, and service. The position will teach a 2-2 load made up of graduate and undergraduate courses; contribute to both undergraduate and graduate curricula; mentor students; participate in select administrative activities; and engage in ongoing scholarly research.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate
description: This Postdoctoral Research Associate will develop novel optical, electrochemical, colorimetric, lateral flow and wearable sensors for various pathogens and analytes. The Research Associate should have an interest and research experience in biosensor development and performance using various receptors spanning proteins and antibodies, aptamers, nanoparticles, polymers, and small molecules from a variety of samples including sputum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples. Previous experience with cell biology and intracellular sensing, microfluidics, or 3D printing is a plus. In addition to bench research, the post-doctoral fellow will be actively involved with data analysis, writing scientific papers and grant proposals and presenting data at scientific meetings.

title: Open Rank Physiatrist
description: The Department of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PM&R) at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking a fixed-term open rank BC/BE physiatrist to join our expanding academic department. Rank will be based on qualifications and experience. This position will encompass a mix of skilled nursing facility rehabilitation care, hospital consultations and outpatient responsibilities that focus on general rehab in the Raleigh NC region. This position will work closely with Advanced Practice Providers (APPs), Rex SNF and Rehab staff and administration, and will serve as the Medical Director of the Raleigh Skilled Nursing and Rehab Facility. This position will be expected and given academic time to participate in educational, research, and administrative activities associated with their academic appointment and related area of expertise. Some on call responsibility and participation in quality improvement projects is required.

title: Postdoctoral Trainee
description: A National Research Service Award (NRSA) postdoctoral research fellowship is available in the Genetic Epidemiology of Heart, Lung, and Blood Traits Program at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. The position is funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, NIH. The goals are to support the training, career development, and professional growth of the post-doctoral fellow by fostering skills and knowledge in Genetic Epidemiology of Heart, Lung, and Blood Traits (GENHLB). The post-doctoral fellow will participate with mentors, other faculty, and peers in the Genetic Epidemiology Program in authoring publications, making presentations at scientific and/or professional meetings, and developing grant support. Responsibilities of the post-doctoral fellow are to work towards enhancing their substantive and methodological skills in genetic epidemiology and related disciplines.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Linguistics is recruiting for a tenure-track Assistant Professor specializing in Syntax/Semantics and Language Documentation. The responsibilities of this position include maintaining an active research program, teaching undergraduate and graduate courses, advising undergraduate honors theses and MA theses, and contributing service to the department and/or university. This position carries our regular teaching load for faculty with an active research agenda: two courses per semester.

title: Teaching Assistant Professor
description: The Teaching Assistant Professor, with a specialization in international relations, will be in the Curriculum in Peace, War, and Defense (PWAD). The position will teach 3 courses per semester (fall and spring) in support of the academic programs offered by the Curriculum in Peace, War, and Defense. Courses will include the introductory course in peace and security studies. The candidate will also teach other courses in the PWAD curriculum related to their area of expertise. There are no research expectations associated with this position.

title: Assistant Professor of Cello and Ensemble Studies
description: This position's teaching load will comprise a combination of studio lessons, courses, and/or ensembles that equates to a 2+2 load. The successful candidate will demonstrate a record of accomplishment in cello performance, classroom and/or ensemble instruction, and forward-thinking research areas that complement a department and campus of diverse interests.

title: Teaching Assistant Professor of Opera and Voice
description: This is a full-time, teaching-track (non-tenure-track) position with an initial three-year appointment, eligible for renewal and promotion. The teaching assignment will be the equivalent of a 3+3 load, with specific responsibilities distributed among opera direction, private voice instruction, and classroom teaching. The precise distribution of responsibilities will reflect departmental needs and the successful candidate's areas of expertise.

title: Teaching Assistant Professor
description: The Lampe UNC/NC State Joint Department of Biomedical Engineering is seeking applicants for a Teaching Assistant Professor in any area related to department specializations with priority given to bioinstrumentation, biomechanics and biologics-based design. This is a professional track faculty position with a focus on teaching and education. Responsibilities include but not limited to: -Delivery of lectures that cover the course objectives as stated on the course syllabus following the dates of the University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill and NC State University calendars for the given semester. -Assessment of student performance including exams, projects, laboratory assignments and/or homework assignments as outlined on the course syllabus. -If the course contains a lab section, overseeing the laboratory component to guarantee appropriate content of lab exercises and coordination of the lab with the lecture. -All other responsibilities associated with teaching the course including grading exams, papers and projects in a timely manner and providing help to students during scheduled office hours. -If a teaching assistant is provided, provide supervision to the teaching assistant and coordinate assignments not exceeding the workload of the teaching assistant. -The instructional load for this position will be 2 to 3 courses per semester for a total of 4 to 6 courses taught each academic year. Employment will be through UNC-Chapel Hill, but some courses may be taught on the NC State campus. -The individual must work productively and in a collaborative manner across all constituent BME entities, i.e. University of North Carolina College of Arts and Sciences, University of North Carolina School of Medicine and the NC State University College of Engineering. The Assistant Teaching Professor will conduct service in areas of need. This may include mentoring students or student organizations, developing study abroad programs, participating in assessment activities, curriculum development and/or academic advising.

title: Teaching Asst/Assoc. Professor
description: The Lampe UNC/NC State Joint Department of Biomedical Engineering is seeking applicants for a Teaching Assistant / Associate Professor in any area related to department specializations with priority given to bioinstrumentation, biomechanics and biologics-based design. This is a professional track faculty position with a focus on teaching and education. Responsibilities include but not limited to: -Delivery of lectures that cover the course objectives as stated on the course syllabus following the dates of the University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill and NC State University calendars for the given semester. -Assessment of student performance including exams, projects, laboratory assignments and/or homework assignments as outlined on the course syllabus. -If the course contains a lab section, overseeing the laboratory component to guarantee appropriate content of lab exercises and coordination of the lab with the lecture. -All other responsibilities associated with teaching the course including grading exams, papers and projects in a timely manner and providing help to students during scheduled office hours. -If a teaching assistant is provided, provide supervision to the teaching assistant and coordinate assignments not exceeding the workload of the teaching assistant. -The instructional load for this position will be 2 to 3 courses per semester for a total of 4 to 6 courses taught each academic year. Employment will be through UNC-Chapel Hill, but some courses may be taught on the NC State campus. Candidates with a proven history of publication and acquisition of funding for the scholarship of teaching and learning may lead new initiatives in the scholarship of teaching and learning and work with other faculty to support their pedagogical investigations and publications in lieu of one course per year. -The individual must work productively and in a collaborative manner across all constituent BME entities, i.e. University of North Carolina College of Arts and Sciences, University of North Carolina School of Medicine and the NC State University College of Engineering. This position will conduct service in areas of need. This may include mentoring junior faculty, mentoring students or student organizations, developing study abroad programs, participating in assessment activities, curriculum development and/or academic advising.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate
description: The purpose of the position is to help compute the matrix elements that govern the neutrinoless double-beta decay in an accurate way, with controlled uncertainty.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Chemistry at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor faculty position in inorganic chemistry, broadly defined. We seek candidates who will establish a vigorous independent research program, excel in teaching at both the graduate and undergraduate levels, and advance our department's mission to cultivate innovative leaders applying chemical tools to pressing challenges.

title: Assistant Professor of Analytical Chemistry, Focus on Pharmacoengineering
description: The Department of Chemistry at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seeks applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in analytical chemistry with a focus on bioanalytical and pharmaceutical measurement science. This position is part of a university-wide pharmacoengineering initiative designed to advance research, education, and innovation in pharmaceutical sciences, biotechnology, and therapeutic development. The successful candidate will develop an internationally recognized research program focused on analytical technologies relevant to pharmaceutical and biologic systems. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, biosensors, lab-on-a-chip and microfluidic systems, advanced separation science, analytical characterization of biologics, single-cell analysis, diagnostics, therapeutic monitoring, and other innovative measurement approaches that advance drug discovery, pharmaceutical manufacturing, precision medicine, and translational science. Faculty responsibilities include conducting innovative research, securing external funding, mentoring undergraduate and graduate students, teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in chemistry, contributing to interdisciplinary training initiatives in pharmacoengineering, and participating in departmental, university, and professional service.

title: Assistant Professor of Analytical Chemistry, Broad Focus
description: The Department of Chemistry at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seeks applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in analytical chemistry, broadly defined. We welcome candidates whose research advances the frontiers of measurement science and who are committed to building a nationally and internationally recognized research program. The successful candidate will pursue innovative scholarship, mentor students and trainees, and provide outstanding instruction at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Faculty responsibilities include contributing to curriculum innovation, participating in departmental and university service, and fostering a collaborative and inclusive academic community.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Anthropology at the University of North Carolina Chapel Hill seeks a sociocultural anthropologist at the tenure-track assistant professor level specializing in the study of Indigenous, Afro-descendant, and/or migrant communities. Topics of interest are those that, in line with the department's Race, Difference, and Power program, view social identities and positions as connected to complex matrices of power grounded in racial, class, gender, citizenship, and other differences and inequalities. Research and teaching that engage the ways that technology, data science, AI and algorithms shape the experience of inequality is especially valued. Of special interest are scholars working in the Americas, with a demonstrated commitment to decolonizing, feminist, or participatory research methodologies.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate
description: The Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for a postdoctoral research position in theoretical nuclear and high-energy physics, with emphasis on lattice QCD. The successful candidate will work with Prof. Kostas Orginos on first-principles calculations of hadron structure, including parton distribution functions, generalized parton distributions, and related quantities obtained from non-local matrix elements, as well as on the development of algorithms and software for large-scale lattice QCD simulations on DOE leadership-class computing facilities. Candidates with expertise in related areas, such as lattice field theory algorithms, machine-learning methods for lattice field theory, hadron spectroscopy, or hadron-structure phenomenology, are encouraged to apply. The postdoc will conduct independent and collaborative research, publish in peer-reviewed journals, present results at conferences and workshops, participate in the activities of the HadStruc collaboration and the broader USQCD community, and may help mentor graduate students. The initial appointment is for two years, with renewal for a third year contingent on satisfactory performance and availability of funds.

title: Politics Reporter
description: The Politics Reporter reports to WUNC's Supervising Editor. This position is responsible for reporting on State and local politics. The reporting includes quick turnaround spot news, interviews, reporter debriefings, anchor wraps, online reports and well-researched feature reports. It is based in the Legislative Building in Raleigh, NC. As news events do not conform to a regular 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. schedule, there are times when the Politics Reporter is called on for work during weekends and after hours.

title: Chiller Mechanic
description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $4.944 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN 2 INSTALLMENTS WITHIN 12 MONTHS OF HIRE: $2,472 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE AND $2,472 12 MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE. This position is assigned to Chilled Water Production and is responsible for air-cooled and water-cooled chiller systems. This includes preventive and predictive maintenance, troubleshooting technical problems (both control and mechanical) and making repairs and upgrades to chillers to maintain reliability. This position will address repairs including inspections and teardowns of chillers as needed. Employee must understand how large chillers operate (centrifugal, scroll, and screw). The employee shall be able to perform preventative and predictive maintenance procedures and repairs of cooling towers, pumps, motors, air compressors and auxiliary equipment that contribute to the production of chilled water. This position is also required to perform other job-related duties as required by the supervisor.

title: Hazardous Radioactive Materials Specialist
description: The Hazardous/Radioactive Materials Specialist is responsible for overseeing the receipt, storage, processing, and disposal of radioactive liquid and solid waste generated by the University and UNC Hospitals. This position collaborates with Hazardous Materials Technicians to transport radioactive waste to the storage facility for decay-in-storage management or temporary storage prior to shipment to an approved off-site disposal facility. This role also oversees medical waste disposal operations and coordinates the transport of hazardous waste to the storage facility. The Hazardous/Radioactive Materials Specialist provides technical expertise and operational support regarding hazardous waste accumulation, storage, and regulatory compliance requirements for non-laboratory areas across the University. In addition, the position is responsible for maintaining warehouse operations, including housekeeping, organization, routine inspections, and inventory management of supplies, materials, and equipment necessary to support waste management activities. The Specialist serves as a member of the University's Emergency Response Team, providing response support for chemical spills, hazardous materials releases, and other environmental emergencies. To ensure compliance with federal and state regulations governing hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facilities (TSDFs), this position must maintain required training and certifications. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) regulations require personnel working at a TSDF to complete a one-time 40-hour Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response (HAZWOPER) training course, as well as an 8-hour annual refresher course. Additionally, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill's RCRA Part B Permit requires personnel to complete initial and annual training in accordance with 40 CFR 270.14(b)(12) and 40 CFR 264.16. Required Licenses and Certifications: * Valid North Carolina Class C or higher Commercial Driver's License (CDL) with Hazardous Materials (HazMat) endorsement. * 40-Hour HAZWOPER Certification and annual refresher training. * RCRA Hazardous Waste Training Certification (initial and annual).

title: Assistant Professor
description: Primary responsibilities of the position will include conducting high-quality research, mentoring doctoral student research, publishing in peer reviewed journals and broader dissemination, seeking external funding for research, teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in cognitive psychology, and engaging in departmental, university, and professional service activities.

title: Human Services Practitioner-CIND
description: Flexible work arrangements, including virtual/hybrid work locations, are an integral part of the School of Medicine's Working Forward initiative. As such, this position's work location is designated as hybrid. Please note that the designated work location is subject to change based on the unit's business needs. If you would prefer workspace access outside of clinic hours, this position includes access to shared workstations at the CIDD. Our goal is to help clinical care teams provide more efficient, effective, and family-centered care that optimizes quality of life and well-being for children and youth with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) and their families. This position will focus on but not be limited to supporting Trillium connected families receiving care at UNC Pediatric outpatient services, CIDD clinics, and identified community practices (referred to as clinical teams going forward)., This position will also serve as a professional peer resource for families seen by primary care providers (PCPs) in outpatient services and clinics. In addition, this Trillium supported Family Navigator (FN) will be linked to the continually expanding network of UNC and NC based system family navigators via separate yet related projects. This position will serve as a family system navigator. This position works directly with patient families to provide emotional, informational, and instrumental support to acquire desired services, resources, supports, and therapies. The FN duties and roles include and are not limited to the following: Supporting families (with emphasis on Eastern NC/Trillium connected families) directly to identify family and patient needs, work with relevant referring UNC pediatric medical providers, liaison and develop key partners and organizations in North Carolina, support the teaching of other UNC pediatricians and pediatric resident physicians, medical students, and LEND trainees about ADHD and common ADHD support needs, connect and/or network with similar efforts such as Duke Pediatrics program, and interface with other family system navigators from related projects at UNC, Duke, and elsewhere, assist in the ongoing development of FN training materials, assist in the tracking and monitoring and reporting of key outcomes. Additional responsibilities include: conduct needs assessment with patients and family to identify needed resources, communicate identified needs with clinical teams, build and provide tailored support for clinical teams, patients and families, initiate and respond to contact from families and community service providers, and help patients, families, and providers increase their knowledge of programs and systems as well as develop their advocacy skills. FNs may also receive and track referrals and document outcomes of support provided, demonstrate accurate, clear, professional, and timely communication, and engage in regularly scheduled team meetings, peer support, and supervision. FNs will document or communicate in Epic electronic health record, Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel and Outlook email. FNs will adhere to all HIPAA compliance and patient confidentiality rules. FN's will engage in at least weekly clinical team meetings in which they will report back progress, share new information gathered from the family, and advocate on behalf of the family's self-determined and expressed priorities.

title: Orthopaedic Hand Surgeon
description: The Department Orthopaedics at the University of North Carolina is seeking applications for a full- time academic orthopaedic surgeon with specialization in hand and nerve surgery to join our Upper Extremity Service. The Department of Orthopaedics includes 34 faculty members who provide the full array of clinical orthopaedic services. This position will be a primary appointment in the Department of Orthopaedics. The clinical focus for this position will be hand, micro, and nerve surgery. Hand fellowship-trained applicants are encouraged to apply. The clinical position includes taking general orthopaedic call for the practice and will also include hand trauma, elective hand surgery, general reconstructive surgery, and microvascular reconstruction of the upper extremities. Faculty members must possess a desire to commit to the missions of the Department and School of Medicine, including the clinical, education, and research missions. Regarding the education mission, faculty members are expected to regularly participate in the education of medical students, residents, and fellows. Regarding the research mission, a commitment to any one of a broad array of research interests is desirable, including but not limited to clinical, outcomes, health services, basic science, translational, ethics, education, or global surgery research. Regarding the clinical mission, faculty members must be committed to delivering high quality clinical care that is of value to the patients of UNC. Selected candidate must be team-oriented and have the ability to interact well with colleagues inside and out of the Department. Outreach to our many rural referring hospitals is highly encouraged.

title: Chair, Department of Radiology
description: The School of Medicine at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seeks an accomplished, collaborative, and visionary leader to serve as Chair of the Department of Radiology. This recruitment is Open Track/Open Rank, and the appropriate track and rank will be determined once the top candidate is selected. Aligned with the mission of the UNC School of Medicine, the Department of Radiology is committed to improving the health and well-being of the people of North Carolina and beyond through excellence in patient care, education, and research. UNC Radiology brings together outstanding clinical and research faculty, trainees, advanced practice providers, and professional staff across the full spectrum of diagnostic imaging, image-guided interventions, and radiological sciences. The Department combines the strengths of a leading academic department with the reach and opportunities of a growing health system, providing specialized imaging and interventional services across academic, hospital, ambulatory, and community settings. The Chair will provide strategic leadership across the Department's clinical, educational, research, and administrative missions and will advance a shared vision for the future of UNC Radiology. The Chair will promote exceptional and compassionate patient care, educational excellence, scientific discovery and innovation, and the continued development of a nationally recognized academic Department. The Chair will recruit, develop, and retain outstanding faculty and leaders; foster a collaborative and high-performing culture; and ensure responsible stewardship of the Department's financial, human, technological, and institutional resources. Working in close partnership with the School of Medicine, UNC Faculty Physicians, UNC Health, and University leadership, the Chair will advance an integrated approach to imaging and image-guided care and position the Department to respond to evolving patient needs, workforce challenges, technological advances, and changes in healthcare delivery. The Chair will foster interdisciplinary collaboration, strengthen the Department's research and educational programs, and identify opportunities for strategic growth and innovation across the academic and clinical enterprise. As a senior institutional leader, the Chair will build strong relationships across organizational and disciplinary boundaries, contribute to broader School of Medicine and UNC Health priorities, and serve as a visible ambassador for UNC Radiology. The Chair will strengthen the Department's reputation and impact locally, regionally, nationally, and internationally while fostering a culture grounded in excellence, collaboration, compassion, professionalism, and respect.

title: Pediatric Cardiologist
description: The Department of Pediatrics at the University of North Carolina School of Medicine is recruiting for an open rank, fixed term clinical faculty position for the Division of Pediatric Cardiology. We are seeking a faculty member to join our growing Division to augment our team of non-invasive cardiologists in the expansion of subspecialty services. Primary responsibilities will include interpretation of non-invasive imaging, outreach and telemedicine, and inpatient care. Individuals with expertise in transesophageal imaging for surgical or catheterization interventions and/or advanced imaging experience are encouraged. Clinical research and quality improvement interests will be fostered. The faculty member will be involved in the educational mission of the School of Medicine. As a top-tier academic medical center, UNC Children's upholds a four-tiered mission to 'CARE,' aligning clinical care, advocacy, research, and education to deliver world-class family-centered care. The North Carolina Children's Hospital is the clinical home of UNC Children's. Our multidisciplinary experts work in satellite clinics across the state and deliver state of the art tertiary care at UNC Children's. The Triangle area of Raleigh/Durham/Chapel Hill is consistently ranked among the nation's best places to live. The region offers affordable living, a temperate climate, easy access to beach and mountains, vibrant dining and cultural offerings.

title: Open Rank
description: The Division of Hematology in the Department of Medicine at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is recruiting a faculty member interested in clinical research or clinician educator positions focused on the management of patients with acute leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes. This candidate will be expected to work with a group of faculty and APPs in the management of patients with acute leukemia, myelodysplastic syndromes and MDS/myeloproliferative neoplasms. This candidate will participate in a robust and active inpatient and outpatient clinical research program in Leukemia at the University of North Carolina. The responsibilities include attending on the inpatient hematologic malignancy service and managing patients with acute leukemia and MDS in the outpatient clinics at the University of North Carolina or our affiliated Cancer Centers. As this is an open rank posting, academic rank and track will be determined by the candidate's experience and achievements. This position can be fixed term, tenure track or variable track.

title: Data-Driven EnviroLab Temporary Research Specialist/Data Analyst
description:
Department: UNC Inst for the Environment - 635200
Career Area: Research Professionals
Posting Open Date: 09/30/2026

Position Type: Temporary Staff (SHRA)

Position Location: North Carolina, US
Hiring Range: $22.00 - $25.00 per hour
Proposed Start Date: 11/02/2026
Estimated Duration of Appointment: 6 months or longer
Be a Tar Heel!: A global higher education leader in innovative teaching, research and public service, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill consistently ranks as one of the nation’s top public universities . Known for its beautiful campus, world-class medical care, commitment to the arts and top athletic programs, Carolina is an ideal place to teach, work and learn. One of the best college towns and best places to live in the United States, Chapel Hill has diverse social, cultural, recreation and professional opportunities that span the campus and community. University employees can choose from a wide range of professional training opportunities for career growth, skill development and lifelong learning and enjoy exclusive perks that include numerous retail and restaurant discounts, savings on local child care centers and special rates for performing arts events.
Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit: The UNC Institute for the Environment (IE) has a multifaceted mission: (1) To strengthen environmental research capacity across UNC by supporting a multi-disciplinary community of scholars that enhances collaboration, increases sharing of knowledge, and identifies solutions to the world’s critical environmental problems. (2) To work in partnership across UNC and with external partners to coordinate and deliver 21st century educational programs that provide students with the experience and skills to thrive in a growing global economy. (3) To put new environmental knowledge into action by engaging and serving communities, here in North Carolina and around the world. (4) To fuel and harness the university’s sustainability activities through the Sustainable Carolina Initiative
Position Summary: This position may be eligible for a hybrid work arrangement that may include a partially remote work location, consistent with System Office policy. UNC Chapel Hill employees are generally required to reside within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned duty station. The Data-Driven EnviroLab ( DDL ) at UNC -Chapel Hill seeks a Research Specialist with a data science focus to support interdisciplinary research on environmental, climate, energy, and sustainability issues. The position will work across projects that use large and heterogeneous datasets to understand environmental and policy challenges, develop reproducible analytical workflows, and translate research findings into accessible tools and outputs for researchers, policymakers, and the public. This Data Scientist/Research Specialist position is ideal for recent BS/BA or Master’s graduates and early-career professionals interested in strengthening their applied research skills, including those considering doctoral study. The candidate will use R and/or Python to collect, clean, integrate, manage, and analyze data from multiple sources; apply quantitative, statistical, and, where relevant, geospatial methods; and contribute to data products, visualizations, and research outputs. Working with an interdisciplinary team spanning data science/statistics, computer science, climate policy, law, and social science, the candidate may contribute to projects that: - Develop and maintain research datasets by integrating administrative, web, geospatial, policy, and other public or proprietary data sources, with attention to data quality, documentation, and reproducibility. - Build and maintain data pipelines using APIs, web scraping, automated collection, cleaning, classification, and validation methods. - Conduct quantitative, statistical, and geospatial analyses to study environmental, economic, health, and policy questions; depending on the project, methods may include regression, panel-data analysis, machine learning, and spatial analysis. - Create dashboards, visualizations, and other data products that translate complex datasets and findings into accessible information for researchers, policymakers, and the public. - Contribute to research reports, academic publications, presentations, and other outputs produced by the interdisciplinary team. One current application of this work is DDL’s U.S. Data Center Dashboard, which tracks data center facilities and state and local policies related to data center development and may expand to incorporate community awareness and responses. In this project, the Research Specialist may help develop and validate facility and policy datasets, analyze environmental, health, economic, and policy implications, and support continued dashboard development. The position may also contribute to other DDL research projects as needs evolve.
Minimum Education and Experience Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in a discipline related to the area of assignment; or equivalent combination of training and experience. All degrees must be received from appropriately accredited institutions.
Management Preferences: Coursework in Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, Economics, Environmental Science, Geography, Public Policy, or another quantitative or computational field Strong programming skills in R or Python with experience working with large or complex datasets, including data cleaning, merging, quality assurance, documentation, or reproducible workflows Experience with quantitative or statistical analysis (e.g., regression, panel-data analysis, machine learning) or geospatial analysis (e.g., geographic coordinates, vector or raster data, spatial joins) Experience with research data tools or workflows such as Git/GitHub, APIs, web scraping, databases, or automated data collection. Ability to communicate technical findings clearly in an nterdisciplinary team
Campus Security Authority Responsibilities: Not Applicable.
