title: Data Manager
description: The School of Social Work at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking a Data Manager to serve as a data manager and programmer on the Creating Indicators and Improving Outcomes project. This position will be work under the leadership of Research Associate Professor - Dr. C. Joy Stewart. The Data Manager is responsible for managing and analyzing data from multiple human services information systems to support research, program evaluation, and reporting efforts. The individual extracts, maintains, and integrates data from various sources to create longitudinal datasets that track the experiences and outcomes of children and families participating in human services programs. Responsibilities also include maintaining and updating a public-facing website that provides key performance indicators and outcome measures, ensuring data accuracy, integrity, and quality through regular updates and quality control processes. In addition, the role supports the evaluation of human services programs by collecting and analyzing operational data, developing surveys and other data collection instruments, and assessing the effectiveness of training provided to child welfare professionals and social services staff. The individual contributes to broader program evaluation initiatives designed to measure the impact of social services programs and interventions. The Data Manager plays a key role in research activities, including the development and management of complex research projects, conducting quantitative and qualitative analyses, and preparing reports, publications, and presentations for state and local stakeholders. The individual collaborates with research teams to communicate findings, present results at meetings and conferences, and support grant and funding efforts through proposal development, research design, methodology implementation, and budget monitoring. Overall, the role combines data management, program evaluation, and research expertise to inform decision-making and improve human services outcomes.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The primary purpose of the Department of Psychology and Neuroscience is to provide excellent education, research and service in the field. This goal breaks down into four important components: 1) to teach psychology and neuroscience to undergraduates in a manner that will introduce them vigorously to its broad scope; 2) to offer scientific and professional training to graduate students in the areas of behavioral and integrative neuroscience, clinical, cognitive, developmental, quantitative, and social psychology; 3) to carry out cutting-edge research in these areas, and 4) to provide consulting and administrative support services to the science and profession of psychology and neuroscience as well as to the university, the community, the state, and the nation. The Department consists of six programs: behavioral and integrative neuroscience; clinical psychology; cognitive psychology; developmental psychology; quantitative psychology, and social psychology. Each program is designed to acquaint the student thoroughly with the theoretical and research content of the specialty and to provide training in the research skills needed to become a competent and creative investigator. In addition, the programs focus on the development of appropriate professional skills. The Department of Psychology and Neuroscience currently ranks 2nd in the College in grant funding with over $12 million annually in awarded grants and approximately $20 million annually in expenditures from all funds. The department has two large undergraduate majors (Psychology and Neuroscience) in the College of Arts and Sciences with approximately 2900 total majors, a minor in Neuroscience and one of the largest graduate Ph.D. programs with approximately 120 graduate students. The Department is also home to the UNC Psychology and Neuroscience Community Clinic, which provides therapeutic treatment and assessment services to a variety of constituencies on campus and in the community.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor
description: The Department of Philosophy in the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is recruiting at the level of Tenure-Track Assistant Professor or Tenured Associate Professor in Philosophy of Emerging Technologies, broadly construed, including, but not limited to, the ethical, societal, legal, and policy implications of innovations in biotechnology, AI, diagnostics, therapeutics, and other emerging technologies. The successful applicant will normally teach two courses per semester (graduate and/or undergraduate); will be involved in thesis supervision; and will have other standard non-teaching duties such as departmental administration, graduate and undergraduate mentorship, and participation in our department's vigorous intellectual life.

title: Professor of the Practice
description: The Division of Data Science and Society (DSS) at UNC-Chapel Hill's School of Data and Information Sciences (SDIS) is excited to announce a full-time Professor of the Practice position in data science. This position provides academic leadership for the culminating capstone experience in the school's graduate data science programs - the online Master of Applied Data Science (MADS) and the residential Master of Science in Data Science (MS) - and serves as the faculty lead for MADS. The successful candidate will orchestrate the delivery of the graduate capstone course, serve as instructor of record for the MADS capstone, and teach additional DATA courses in the MADS program as program needs require. Primary responsibilities include: * Orchestrate the delivery of the graduate capstone course by vetting projects in conjunction with the school's Office of Cross-Sector Partnership, overseeing and grading student work, and communicating with the external clients of capstone projects. * Teach a wide range of the DATA courses offered in the MADS program, including the culminating capstone experience, in coordination with other teaching faculty. * Serve on the Admissions Committee for MADS, reviewing candidates who meet program qualifications and making admission decisions. * Collaborate with school staff on curricular improvements to ensure the online program management vendor delivers services that meet university academic standards. * Oversee continuous quality improvement of the curriculum by reviewing instructor and student feedback and implementing changes. * Take an active role in planning and carrying out the optional on-campus immersion held during the summer. * Participate in virtual student recruitment sessions four times a year. Professors of the practice at SDIS bring deep professional and pedagogical expertise into the classroom and play a central role in connecting students with real-world practice. Working closely with teaching faculty, program staff, the Office of Cross-Sector Partnership, and the school's external partners, the Professor of the Practice will ensure that data science master's students complete a rigorous, client-facing capstone experience that translates classroom learning into professional practice. We invite you to join the DSS faculty and be part of this mission.

title: Carolina Latinx Center Program Assistant
description: The Carolina Latinx Center (CLC) Program Assistant provides daily administrative, programmatic, and communication support to CLC staff. The CLC Program Assistant will also provide direct support to both the Associate Director and the Director. This position will serve as CLC's initial contact with the public, from greeting visitors to managing the overall office operation. The Program Assistant at the Carolina Latinx Center, serves as the main point of contact for various programs and events, including Enlaces, community outreach to a bilingual elementary school, and other partnerships. They are responsible for coordinating volunteers and communicating expectations. Additionally, the Program Assistant will provide support for other programs like Exitos Awards Ceremony, Latinx Heritage Month Celebration, and more. The Program Assistant will be the primary to organizing the CLC's finances, documents, and more. This position will work in collaboration with the Development Officer to coordinate fundraising efforts, such as coordinating thank-you letters and sending invitations to special donor event, facilitating special events, and applying to grants.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate
description: The successful candidate will conduct research at the intersection of water and health as part of the UNC Water Institute at the Gillings School of Global Public Health. Depending on the specific appointment, research may focus on the development and evaluation of novel disinfection technologies, new methods in environmental health microbiology, and quantitative microbial risk assessment, applied to drinking water, wastewater, and other environmental matrices. Work will be conducted in the context of field- and laboratory-based studies and trials in the United States and internationally, in collaboration with faculty, students, and partner institutions and communities. The postdoctoral researcher will work closely with an interdisciplinary team that may include engineers, microbiologists, epidemiologists, and public health practitioners, and will interact with the broader UNC Water Institute community. Specific activities will include, but are not limited to, experimental design and execution, environmental sample collection and microbiological/analytical characterization, data analysis, and manuscript and proposal preparation. In addition to research activities, the successful candidate is expected to contribute to the mentoring of graduate and undergraduate students, and to other academic activities, as part of their postdoctoral training. The specific project, start date, and appointment length will depend on the funding source and supervising faculty member. Postdoctoral appointments are typically for one year, renewable annually based on satisfactory performance and funding availability, for up to three years.

title: Lead Preparator
description: The Lead Preparator performs all duties related to exhibition preparation and installation as well as contributing to the care of the collection. This position includes but is not limited to, matting and framing; wall and signage design and fabrication; packing, unpacking and movement of works of art; gallery renovations; installation and lighting of artwork on display; physical care and organization of the permanent collection; and maintenance of galleries, storage vaults, equipment and workspaces. The Lead preparator advises on all issues relating to the display of specific artworks including mount making, pedestal design and construction; and a variety of audiovisual issues. The Lead Preparator works closely with and contributes to the training and oversight of contract employees. The Lead Preparator reports to the Head of Exhibition Preparation and Installation. Must possess and maintain a valid North Carolina driver's license.

title: Clinical Instructor
description: The Division of Radiologic Science is recruiting for a faculty member to join our new Ultrasound Program. The faculty member will be responsible for participating and providing support for the development, implementation and evaluation of the philosophy, outcomes, policies, and curricular components of the Sonography program: o Responsible for supervision and evaluation in the clinical setting o Program content and student learning experiences within the curriculum. o Revisions in all course materials and experiences based on curricular changes and refinements and course evaluations. o Effectiveness assessment of curriculum design. o Compliance with accreditation standards and requirements affecting Sonography education. o Active role in accreditation activities. o Teaches and Designs Courses in area(s) where qualified.

title: Open-Rank Clinical Fixed-Term Faculty (3)
description: This posting is for three (3) open-rank Practicum Education fixed-term faculty positions. By applying, applicants will be considered for all available vacancies. The School of Social Work at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for three open-rank Practicum Education fixed-term faculty positions (1.0 FTE). The mission of the School of Social Work is to advance equity, transform systems, and improve lives. The curriculum supports this mission through a focus on evidence-based practice; commitment to disadvantaged, vulnerable, and oppressed individuals, families, and communities; and the design, implementation, and evaluation of social interventions. These positions will be reviewed annually for reappointment. We seek candidates to coordinate practicum education and teach graduate-level social work courses. Successful applicants will contribute to practicum education across a range of social work practice areas and teach up to four graduate courses per year. Candidates should possess broad social work practice experience and expertise, with the ability to teach in generalist practice and either direct practice or macro practice specialization courses. Preferred qualifications may vary across positions and may include expertise in assessment and intervention with individuals, families, groups, communities, and organizations; experience in practicum education; an LCSW credential; macro-level practice experience; and demonstrated success teaching graduate-level courses or professional training programs. These positions have a standard distribution of effort consisting of 90% teaching and instruction and 10% service and community engagement.

title: Teaching Assistant Professor in Bluegrass and Musicianship
description: This is a full-time, teaching-track (non-tenure-track) position with an initial 3-year appointment, eligible for renewal and promotion. Teaching load will be three courses (3 credit-hours each) per semester or the equivalent and may include a combination of individual lessons, ensemble direction, and classroom teaching of both music majors and non-majors. Responsibilities begin on July 1, 2027.

title: Open Rank
description: The Department of Radiology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is seeking a talented, team-oriented Abdominal Imaging Radiologist to join our expanding division. This is a compelling opportunity to practice advanced abdominal imaging, collaborate with nationally recognized colleagues, and help shape the next generation of radiologists at one of the most respected academic institutions in the country. Our division serves the mission to improve the health and well-being of North Carolinians at our UNC Hospitals complex, including a level 1 trauma center, a women’s hospital, a pediatric hospital, a neurosciences hospital, and the NCI designated Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center. Position Specifics This position will interpret high-quality CT, MRI, ultrasound, radiographs and fluoroscopy studies and help lead a high-functioning team focused on patient-centered care. You’ll also: Teach and mentor residents, fellows, and medical students Participate in research and scholarly activities in abdominal imaging Support institutional quality improvement efforts Engage in collaborative protocols, consults, and conferences Highlights This is a fixed-term position, with faculty rank (Instructor to Professor) commensurate with qualifications and experience. UNC School of Medicine offers a comprehensive benefits package, paid leave, and a variety of health, life and retirement plans and additional programs that support a healthy work/life balance. EPIC EHR About the Organization UNC School of Medicine is a leader in teaching, research, and public service, consistently ranked among top public universities. Known for its beautiful campus, world-class medical care, commitment to the arts and top athletic programs, UNC is an ideal place to teach, work and learn. One of the best college towns and best places to live in the United States, Chapel Hill offers a wide range of social, cultural, recreational, and professional opportunities throughout the campus and community.

title: Teaching Assistant Professor
description: This position is for a fixed-term faculty member at the rank of teaching assistant professor in any field in Economics. Teaching responsibilities are 6 courses per academic year. Duties will include undergraduate teaching, mentoring, and service. Teaching responsibilities will include enrollments ranging from 25-400 students.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Physics and Astronomy seeks to fill a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in astrophysics, with a focus on artificial intelligence and machine learning applied to large-scale astronomical data. The faculty member will establish and lead an independent, externally funded research program in this area, publish in peer-reviewed venues, and supervise graduate students and postdoctoral researchers.Research programs that will use the Argus Array are especially encouraged. The faculty member will teach undergraduate and graduate courses across the physics and astronomy curriculum, contribute to the Department's developing curriculum in artificial intelligence and machine learning methods, and advise and mentor undergraduate, graduate, and postdoctoral researchers. The faculty member will also contribute service to the Department, the College, the University, and the profession.

title: Assistant Professor (Molecular, Cell, Developmental Biology)
description: The Department of Biology at UNC Chapel Hill (https://bio.unc.edu/) is searching to hire a tenure track Assistant Professor to study critical questions in Molecular, Cellular, Developmental, or Microbial Biology. We seek candidates who focus on molecular mechanisms that illuminate fundamental aspects of the biology of cells and organisms, including their interactions with the environment. We seek candidates who work across scales, using transdisciplinary approaches including genetic, molecular biology, cellular biology, biochemistry and/or genomic approaches. Research programs that leverage model experimental systems and/or have direct relevance to human disease are particularly desirable. All candidates must have earned a Ph.D. or equivalent degree, have post-doctoral research experience, and be committed to teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Successful candidates are expected to build an active research group, contribute to Department of Biology activities, secure competitive external funding, and participate actively in the broad scientific community at UNC-CH. Successful candidates will have opportunities for synergy with other units at UNC such as the curriculum in Genetics and Molecular Biology, the Curriculum in Bioinformatics and Computational Biology, the Cell Biology and Physiology Curriculum, the Environment, Ecology, and Energy Program, the Department of Earth Marine and Environmental Sciences, the Department of Applied Physical Sciences, the NC Botanical Garden and Herbarium, the School of Data and Information Sciences, the Institute of Convergent Sciences, the Galapagos Center, the Institute for the Environment, and the Carolina Biodiversity Collaborative.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The Department is seeking candidates with a strong record of research in theoretical statistics, learning theory or adjacent areas, and the potential to develop an outstanding, independent research program. The Department is particularly interested in candidates whose work is motivated by challenges in artificial intelligence, machine learning, high-dimensional data, and other modern applications. The successful candidate will be comfortable with teaching courses in statistics at the undergraduate and graduate levels, as well as introductory courses in the Department. Research that creates opportunities for interaction and collaboration with other groups across the Department and the University will be a positive factor in the consideration of candidates. Primary responsibilities of the position will include high-quality research, publishing in peer-reviewed journals and broader dissemination, seeking external funding for research, teaching undergraduate and graduate courses, contributing to research mentoring of doctoral students, and engaging in departmental, university, and professional service activities.

title: Assistant Professor
description: This early career hire will focus on foundational statistical and optimization methods for safe and reliable AI, with applications in biomedicine and public health. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, robust and stochastic optimization, generative and foundation models, reliable and robust machine learning, uncertainty quantification, sequential decision-making, and AI systems operating under uncertainty in high stakes environments. The secondary appointment in Biostatistics will facilitate close collaboration with applied researchers and provide pathways for translating methods into practice. Primary responsibilities of the position will include high-quality research, publishing in peer-reviewed journals and broader dissemination, seeking external funding for research, teaching undergraduate and graduate courses, contributing to research mentoring of doctoral students, and engaging in departmental, university, and professional service activities.

title: Pediatric Urologic Surgeon (Open Rank)
description: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill's Department of Urology is seeking a dedicated Pediatric Urological Surgeon to provide advanced surgical and medical care for children with complex urological conditions. In this role, you will deliver expert care, perform cutting-edge surgical procedures, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams in a dynamic academic environment. You will also have the opportunity to contribute to research initiatives and mentor the next generation of physicians, shaping the future of pediatric urology through clinical innovation and academic leadership. This is an open-rank recruitment and academic rank will be awarded at a level commensurate with experience.

title: Assistant Director of Operations
description: The Assistant Director of Operations provides daily leadership and oversight for all indoor and outdoor Campus Recreation facilities including the Student Recreation Center, Rams Head Recreation Center, Woollen Gym, Hooker Fields, and the South Campus Recreation Complex. The position is responsible for supervising a full-time Facility Operations Coordinator and coordinating the development and implementation of policies, standard operating procedures, emergency action procedures, risk management plans, and safety practices. A primary operations responsibility is working with Housekeeping Services, Grounds Services, and Facilities Services to maintain and upkeep indoor and outdoor recreation facilities. The position works closely and communicates with the Assistant Director of Member Services and Events to ensure event and reservation schedules and logistics occur without issue or conflicts. In addition to supervising one full-time Coordinator, this position hires, trains, and supervises approximately 40 student site managers for Campus Recreation indoor facilities. The Assistant Director develops annual budgets for areas of responsibility and coordinates the purchase and inventory of shared equipment and staff supplies. The position collaborates with key stakeholders to purchase facility and fitness equipment, conduct preventative maintenance, repairs, replacement, and coordinate layout and installation of equipment. The Assistant Director also develops strategies to maximize use of different software systems to facilitate facility access, equipment checkout, locker rentals, and staff scheduling. Finally, this position has significant risk management responsibilities, including the development and implementation of emergency action plans for all Campus Recreation facilities. The position reports to the Associate Director of Facilities and Operations and assumes responsibility for Campus Recreation facilities and operations in the absence of the Associate Director. * CPR, First Aid, and AED certification is required upon hire or must be obtained within the first three months of employment.

title: Open Rank
description: The Division of Gastroenterology and Hepatology at the UNC School of Medicine is seeking a Gastroenterologist with expertise in gastroenterology and endoscopy. This position is being recruited as open rank on the fixed-term track, with rank and salary commensurate with qualifications and experience. Our division offers a wide range of subspecialty focuses, including inflammatory bowel disease, esophageal disease, motility disorders, and advanced endoscopy. The successful candidate will perform endoscopic procedures, provide care in outpatient clinics (in Chapel Hill and outreach clinics), provide inpatient consults and actively participate in the training of GI fellows, residents, and medical students.

title: Center for Women's Mood Disorders Psychologist - Open Rank
description: The Department of Psychiatry at the University of North Carolina (UNC) School of Medicine at Chapel Hill is seeking a fixed term faculty to join the Center for Women's Mood Disorders (CWMD). This position is primarily clinical in nature and will focus on providing evidence-based assessment and psychotherapy services to individuals experiencing mental health concerns during the perinatal period, including pregnancy, the postpartum year, and following pregnancy or infant loss. Clinical services will be delivered primarily through outpatient care settings using both in-person and telehealth modalities. Faculty rank will be commensurate with experience. Primary responsibilities include providing psychotherapy within the Perinatal Behavioral Health Psychotherapy Program and collaborating closely with psychiatrists, psychologists, social workers, advanced practice providers, trainees, and other members of a multidisciplinary team. The faculty member will provide assessment and treatment for a broad range of perinatal mental health concerns, including mood and anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive and related disorders, trauma-related conditions, adjustment concerns, and other reproductive mental health conditions. Experience working with individuals undergoing fertility treatment and those experiencing reproductive mental health challenges such as premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) and perimenopausal mental health concerns is highly desirable. This position may include teaching and supervision responsibilities within the department's training programs. The faculty member may provide clinical supervision to psychology interns, psychology fellows, practicum students, psychiatry residents, social work trainees, and other interprofessional learners. Additional teaching activities may include participation in seminars, case conferences, and didactic programming related to perinatal and reproductive mental health. Faculty are expected to contribute to the academic mission of the department through excellence in clinical care, education, service, and scholarly activity. Participation in program development, quality improvement initiatives, clinical research collaborations, and other scholarly endeavors is encouraged. The ideal candidate will demonstrate expertise in evidence-based psychotherapies for individuals in the perinatal period, including behavioral interventions such as Behavioral Activation and Exposure and Response Prevention, as well as third-wave behavioral approaches such as Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) and Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT). Candidates should possess strong interpersonal skills, a commitment to patient-centered and culturally responsive care, and the ability to work effectively within interdisciplinary teams.

title: Neurosurgical Oncology (Open Rank)
description: The UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center and the UNC School of Medicine's Department of Neurosurgery seek a full-time physician scientist, open-rank, faculty member specializing in the treatment and research of brain tumors to lead the Neurosurgical arm of the UNC Neuro-Oncology program. Ideal candidates will be fellowship-trained in Neurosurgical Oncology. The National Cancer Institute (NCI) first designated the UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center in 1990. UNC is one of only 40 Comprehensive Cancer Centers nationwide, and UNC Lineberger is the only public Comprehensive Cancer Center in North Carolina to have this designation. UNC Lineberger has been rated 'exceptional' by the NCI in its most recent reviews. The opportunities for both clinical practice and research are extensive and also leverage the excellence and proximity of the UNC Eshelman School of Pharmacy and Gillings School of Global Public Health. UNC Lineberger is the academic home to the cancer programs, and the clinical home is the North Carolina Cancer Hospital, a 320,000 square-foot dedicated cancer hospital opened in 2009, and across the street from UNC Lineberger. UNC Lineberger physicians have been offering multidisciplinary, patient-centered care for more than a quarter century, giving patients access to medical and patient support specialists in one place, often in one visit. UNC's system has been used as a model by other cancer centers and oncology programs nationwide. The Neuro-Oncology program boasts an established clinical practice comprising Neuro-Oncologists and Neurosurgeons with special expertise and interest in brain tumors, and dedicated Radiation Oncologists with research and clinical expertise in fractionated and stereotactic radiosurgery, working closely within this multidisciplinary structure. There is a robust clinical trials portfolio, a centralized clinical trials office providing broad research support and access to the Brain Tumor Trials Collaborative and the Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology.

title: Stereotactic and Functional Neurosurgeon - Open Rank
description: The Department of Neurosurgery at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC) invites applications for a fellowship-trained Stereotactic and Functional Neurosurgeon to join our growing multidisciplinary program. The successful candidate will join a dynamic academic environment comprising 12 neurosurgeons with expertise across subspecialties, supported by robust clinical, research, and educational infrastructure within the UNC School of Medicine and UNC Health. Neurosurgery Services: Our neurosurgery services include treatment for aneurysms and cerebrovascular disease, brain tumor treatment, epilepsy and functional neurosurgery, spine and head trauma, hydrocephalus, pituitary and skull base surgery, spinal neurosurgery, pediatric and fetal neurosurgery. The department has expanded in recent years with new neurosurgical faculty, including surgeon-scientists, master clinicians, and an extraordinarily talented multimedia medical illustration team. There is a new neurosurgical outpatient center at the ACC. UNC Health has acquired the latest technology, including the LITT, Robot, and high/low-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU/LIFU), and the department has established a new peripheral nerve and spinal oncology program. The department generated $2.52M in grant funding and received $2.95M in philanthropic support. In the last few years, the department has improved its standing in Blue Ridge and US News & World Report rankings. Primary Responsibilities: Provide surgical care for patients with epilepsy and movement disorders, in close collaboration with neurologists specializing in these areas. Participate actively in the education and mentorship of residents, fellows, and medical students. Contribute to the department's research mission, focusing on understanding the mechanisms of neurological disorders, the biologic and physiologic basis of neurosurgical interventions, and advancing surgical techniques for epilepsy and functional disorders. Engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across UNC's neuroscience, imaging, and engineering communities. A research support package including start-up resources and protected time will be provided in proportion to the candidate's experience, academic achievements, and funding history.

title: Research Program Manager
description: Flexible work arrangements, including virtual/hybrid work locations, are an integral part of the School of Medicine's Working Forward initiative. As such, this position's work location is designated as hybrid. Please note that the designated work location is subject to change based on the unit's business needs. ShepsGME (Sheps Graduate Medical Education) is a portfolio of federal, state, and organization funded projects which develop, implement, and evaluate technical assistance infrastructure for supporting the development, expansion, and sustainability of graduate medical education (GME) training opportunities. This mission of ShepsGME is to reduce the maldistribution of physicians and dentists in rural and underserved areas by supporting the development of rural and health center residency programs. The ShepsGME team is seeking a Research Program Manager to serve as a key member of our technical assistance center program team. The Research Program Manager will oversee and coordinate technical assistance services and educational offerings, and program evaluation efforts across state and federally funded projects that support the development of new graduate medical education (GME) and graduate dental training programs in rural and underserved communities. This role focuses on the development and execution of education and stakeholder engagement strategies in compliance with university and funder regulations. The Research Program Manager will be responsible for managing the center's stakeholder engagement products and educational offerings (e.g., national conferences, webinars, virtual workshops, and stakeholder meetings). This role also supports program evaluation and outcomes tracking, including collecting and analyzing quantitative and qualitative data on program performance and contributing to reports and dashboards for funders and university leadership. This role will be involved in translating relevant data and subject matter expertise to a variety of products for different audiences, supported by a team of experienced GME development technical assistance (TA) providers and researchers. This role must ensure that the ShepsGME Technical Assistance Centers' services are produced and disseminated within budget and in compliance with university and funder regulations.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate- CICBDD (Wang Lab)
description: The postdoctoral researcher will conduct independent and collaborative research in medicinal chemistry, with primary responsibility for designing and executing experiments aimed at the synthesis of biologically relevant molecules. This includes performing literature searches; maintaining accurate and detailed laboratory records, including electronic notebooks when required; preparing weekly research reports and other reports as assigned; adhering to and staying current with all laboratory safety protocols; and contributing to the cleaning, organization, and maintenance of laboratory spaces and equipment. The postdoc will also actively participate in scientific group meetings, departmental seminars, and problem solving sessions, and will assist in the preparation, writing, and submission of research reports and publications.

title: Open Rank (Cardiology)
description: The Division of Cardiology, at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is recruiting for an Open Rank, Fixed-Term, Tenure or Tenure Track or Variable Track Faculty appointment as a General Cardiologist. The position will be full time clinical, and responsibilities will include outpatient cardiology care (including developing a referral practice), attending on the inpatient units or consult service, and teaching of cardiovascular fellows, residents, and medical students. The position may also involve seeing patients at an outreach clinic and/or interpreting advanced cardiac imaging studies. Position rank and track (fixed term vs. tenure track vs. variable track) is dependent upon applicant qualifications and experience.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate
description: In 2024, the National Science Foundation inaugurated a Focused Research Hub in Theoretical Physics, 'Advancing the Theory of Nuclear Double Beta-decay (@NDB)'. The @NDB Hub involves theoretical physicists and statisticians at the University of North Carolina, Colorado State University, Los Alamos National Laboratory, the University of Maryland, Miami University, Michigan State University, the University of Notre Dame, Ohio University, the University of Tennessee, the University of Washington, and Washington University in St. Louis. The @NDB Hub anticipates hiring a post-doctoral research fellow who will join the project in September 2027 and be located at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. Research will be supervised by Prof. Amy Nicholson, and will involve the use of lattice QCD for computing observables relevant to nuclear double beta-decay. Applicants should have a strong research record, preferably in lattice QCD and Nuclear Theory. @NDB fellows will have many opportunities to interact with theorists at the other institutions, including with statisticians to improve uncertainty quantification in theoretical research on double-beta decay.

title: Open Rank
description: This posting is for two tenure-track positions. One position will be designated as tenure-track assistant professor. One position may be designated as a tenure-track assistant professor or a tenure-track/tenured associate professor, depending upon the applicant's qualifications. Both positions are open to candidates in any field of Economics. Teaching requirements are 3 undergraduate and/or graduate courses per academic year. These positions are also responsible for academic research in Economics.

title: Open Rank
description: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill is currently recruiting a full-time faculty member in the Division of Breast Imaging. We welcome applicants who seek to join a vibrant division of breast imaging radiologists who are dedicated to excellence in patient care, enthusiastic education of our imaging fellows, diagnostic radiology residents and medical students, scholarly endeavors, and a collaborative environment with our interdisciplinary colleagues. The responsibilities of this position consist of daily patient care, training graduate and postgraduate students, and possible research.Clinical services will be performed primarily in a teaching setting with fellow, resident, or medical student observation and participation. Our facilities are designated ACR 'Breast Imaging Centers of Excellence' and are MQSA certified. The Breast Imaging Radiologists perform all imaging and minimally invasive biopsies. We are active participants in a multidisciplinary team approach to breast disease.

title: Teaching Assistant Professor, Property Tax Appraisal
description: The School of Government seeks to recruit a fixed-term faculty member at the rank of teaching assistant professor who will specialize in property tax appraisal education. The selected candidate will advise and educate local property tax officials on the legal guidelines and best practices for the appraisal of property in North Carolina and support county tax offices as they plan and implement reappraisals. The primary responsibility of this position will be to develop and teach appraisal education courses appropriate for the needs of North Carolina tax officials. In addition, the selected candidate will respond to advising inquiries relating to tax appraisals from local and state government officials, North Carolina property owners, and the media. While research and scholarly publication will not be core responsibilities of this position, the selected candidate will have the opportunity to publish on appraisal topics as needed. Candidates will be expected to have experience with and the capacity to educate and advise on geographic information systems, the use of artificial intelligence in mass appraisals, and other technology relevant to North Carolina's property tax system.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Religious Studies is recruiting for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Chinese Religions. Candidates should demonstrate clear evidence of their commitment to research and teaching, as well as their interest in mentoring students and participating in departmental life and service. They are expected to teach various undergraduate and graduate courses (including introductory and upper-level courses in Chinese religions and the religions of East Asia) and contribute to the Asian Religions concentration. Candidates should complement the existing expertise of our current faculty, and their work should align with our departmental mission as outlined on our website (https://religion.unc.edu/about/mission-and-values/).

title: Temporary Fixed-Term Faculty
description: Teaching undergraduate and/or graduate students in the clinical setting, laboratory and/or classroom.

title: Clinical Preceptor
description: The Nurse Practitioner Preceptor serves as a clinical mentor and educator for graduate nursing students, providing hands-on learning experiences in a real-world healthcare setting. Preceptors play a vital role in supporting the clinical education, professional development, and competency of future nurse practitioners while collaborating with faculty to ensure student success. Key Responsibilities * Provide supervised, real-world clinical learning experiences for nurse practitioner students. * Offer guidance, mentorship, and clinical expertise to support students' development of diagnostic reasoning, assessment, and patient management skills. * Facilitate progressive student independence by assigning appropriate patient care responsibilities based on competency. * Review and approve student findings, diagnoses, and treatment plans prior to patient discharge. * Communicate regularly with assigned faculty regarding student progress, concerns, or questions. * Complete required student evaluations at mid-term and end of the clinical rotation. * Maintain a supportive and professional learning environment that promotes compassionate, high-quality patient care Clinical supervision ranging from approximately 60–240 hours per semester, depending on course requirement

title: Open Rank
description: The Department of Sociology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for an open rank (tenure-track) faculty position to begin July 1, 2027. We are seeking candidates with research and teaching interests in population health and aging. This is the first of an anticipated five related searches over the next four years in a new UNC-Chapel Hill initiative on biosocial health and aging. We seek applications from scholars who exhibit a record of strong and innovative research and excellence in teaching. Candidates are expected to hold a Ph.D. in Sociology or a related field by July 1, 2027.

title: Open Rank
description: The Department of Biostatistics in the Gillings School of Global Public Health at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC) is seeking two tenure-track or tenured faculty members, starting in Fall 2027. These 12-month full-time positions may be filled at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor, depending on qualifications and experience. The department seeks exceptional candidates who can contribute to its academic and research missions. Successful applicants will be expected to develop and maintain externally funded research programs and to engage in the teaching, mentoring, and service activities of the department. One position is expected to be filled at the Full Professor rank and will include appointment as Director of the UNC Gillings Center for Artificial Intelligence and Public Health, with a secondary appointment in the Department of Computer Science. This position is part of a UNC cluster hire on Safeguarding Artificial Intelligence in Health: Foundations, Uncertainty, and High Stakes Decision Making that includes three jointly appointed positions within the Department of Biostatistics, the Department of Computer Science, and the Department of Statistics and Operations Research. This cluster hire is structured to strengthen collaboration across these departments. The ideal candidate will provide intellectual leadership in AI safety for biomedical and public health applications, building on existing strengths in statistical machine learning, causal inference, and high dimensional data analysis. This individual will play a central leadership role in research, mentoring, and interdisciplinary collaboration, and will contribute to the continued growth and national visibility of AI in public health at UNC.

title: Associate Director for Sheps Integrated Research Solutions (SIRS)
department: Sheps Ctr for Hlth Serv Res - 633100

Sheps Center for Health Services Research. While Sheps(DATA)+ is not a Contract Research Organization (CRO), it functions similarly by providing the full suite of technical, data, and operational infrastructure needed to support health services research, while scientific leadership remains with the Principal Investigator. SIRS is a core component of this integrated service model, contributing to critical application development, data collection platforms, and workflow systems that enable coordinated, multiservice research efforts across the Sheps Center. In this role, the Associate Director is responsible for overseeing the delivery, quality and long-term sustainability of SIRS solutions, ensuring alignment with research goals, institutional policies, security and privacy requirements, and best practices in software engineering and product management. The Associate Director also plays a key role in identifying and advancing strategic initiatives for SIRS that are aligned with Sheps(DATA)+ strategic priorities and the broader mission of the Sheps Center. title: Post-Doc Research Associate
description: The Brunk Lab at UNC-Chapel Hill seeks a computational postdoctoral researcher to develop and apply methods for integrating single-cell sequencing and imaging data within controlled cell-line model systems. The project focuses on vertical integration of multimodal single-cell datasets, including single-cell DNA copy number, RNA expression, chromatin accessibility, protein abundance, protein localization, and cytogenetic imaging. The postdoctoral researcher will help build computational frameworks that connect sequencing-based measurements with imaging-derived single-cell features, including multiplexed protein imaging and AI-assisted cytogenetic image analysis. This position is central to a funded research program developing single-cell integration frameworks and AI imaging tools to understand how genome structure and molecular state coordinate across individual cells. The grant includes single-cell multi-omics sequencing, 4i protein imaging, CITE-seq validation, and AI-based cytogenetic analysis.

title: Research Associate Professor or Research Professor (Kenan Institute of Private Enterprise)
description: The Kenan Institute of Private Enterprise seeks a Research Associate Professor or Research Professor with expertise in applied economics, economic forecasting, regional economics, labor economics, public policy, or related fields to contribute to the North Carolina Advanced Economic Forecasting Initiative (the Initiative). The faculty member will provide intellectual leadership in economic forecasting methodologies, applied economic research, and public-facing analysis for North Carolina. Responsibilities include conducting and disseminating research, developing forecasts and analytical products, communicating findings to academic, business, government, and community audiences, and contributing to the Institute's mission of translating research into actionable insights. The successful candidate will collaborate with faculty colleagues, research staff, students, and external partners to advance understanding of North Carolina's economy and support evidence-based decision making. This position will serve as the Senior Research Economist for the Initiative, and in this role they will lead the development, refinement, validation, and interpretation of economic forecasts, nowcasts, scenario analyses, and related applied research products. Additionally, the Research Associate Professor or Research Professor will work closely with the Executive Director, Director of Research Data Strategy and Analytics, data analysts, faculty affiliates, communications staff, state and local partners, and other Kenan Institute teams to ensure that the Initiative's economic methodologies and research outputs are rigorous, transparent, actionable, and accessible to both technical and nontechnical audiences. The role will translate complex economic data and forecasting results into practical insight for policymakers, county leaders, economic developers, business organizations, community colleges, workforce partners, researchers and other stakeholders. The Research Associate Professor or Research Professor will help determine appropriate modeling approaches, evaluate forecast accuracy, communicate uncertainty and limitations, prepare written research products, brief stakeholders, and identify emerging economic issues that warrant additional county-level analysis. The Research Associate Professor or Research Professor reports to the Executive Director of the Kenan Institute of Private Enterprise (KIPE) and will work in close coordination with the Executive Director, who will lead the Initiative's strategy, operations, partnerships, stakeholder engagement and public-facing growth. This position may supervise or provide functional guidance to economists, analysts, research staff, students or contractors working on forecasting models, economic analysis, research briefs, county profiles, dashboards or stakeholder deliverables. The position requires strong technical expertise in applied economics, econometrics, forecasting, regional economics, labor economics, public policy or a related field. The successful candidate will help make the Initiative a trusted, objective, and methodologically sound source of economic intelligence for North Carolina. This position is contingent upon the continued availability of funding.

title: Plastic Surgeon
description: The Department of Surgery at the University of North Carolina is seeking applications for a full-time academic plastic surgeon to join our Division of Plastic Surgery. The Division of Plastic Surgery is among 9 clinical Divisions in the Department of Surgery. The Division currently includes 7 faculty members that provide a broad array of clinical services in order to provide the highest quality care for plastic surgery patients including oncologic reconstruction, gender affirming care, trauma (including facial and hand trauma), microvascular reconstruction, aesthetic and craniofacial procedures. The clinical focus for this position is general plastic surgery, with an emphasis on breast. Fellowship-trained applicants are encouraged to apply, but completion of a fellowship is not a requirement for this position. Other opportunites in general plastic surgery, including gender affirming care, microsurgical and post traumatic reconstruction are available. The clinical position includes call coverage for the general reconstructive surgery practice, as well as hand and/or facial trauma call. Faculty members within the Division of Plastic Surgery should be committed to all three missions of the department and School of Medicine, including the clinical, education, and research missions. Faculty members are expected to regularly participate in the education of medical students, residents, and fellows. An interest in any one of a broad array of research interests is desirable, including but not limited to clinical, outcomes, health services, basic science, translational, ethics, education, or global surgery research. Faculty members must be committed to delivering high quality clinical care that is of value to the patients of UNC. Selected candidate must be team-oriented and have the ability to interact well with colleagues inside and out of the Division. This position is being recruited as an open-rank, open-track appointment between 0.5 FTE and 1.0 FTE. Individuals who exhibit exceptional skills and achievements may be considered for a leadership position within the department of surgery. Leadership roles are not guaranteed and are dependent upon the current needs of our surgical programs.

title: Pediatric Urologic Surgeon (Open Rank)
description: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill's Department of Urology is seeking a dedicated Pediatric Urological Surgeon to provide advanced surgical and medical care for children with complex urological conditions. In this role, you will deliver expert care, perform cutting-edge surgical procedures, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams in a dynamic academic environment. You will also have the opportunity to contribute to research initiatives and mentor the next generation of physicians, shaping the future of pediatric urology through clinical innovation and academic leadership. This is an open-rank recruitment and academic rank will be awarded at a level commensurate with experience.

title: Developmental Behavioral Pediatrician
description: The Department of Pediatrics at the University of North Carolina and North Carolina Children's Hospital has an open rank, full time faculty position for a Developmental Behavioral Pediatrician (DBP) to work in our growing Development, Behavior and Learning Program. This program provides outpatient services through interprofessional care delivered by DBP, psychology, social work, and nursing. Services include assessment and ongoing care for children with or at risk for developmental disabilities such as autism spectrum disorder, intellectual disability, genetic conditions, and other related disorders. The DBP program provides an integral role in the training and education of pediatric residents and other learners. This faculty position will include participation in resident didactics, shadowing and supervision, and ultimately assistance in our future goal of developing a DBP fellowship. Given that UNC has a rich tradition of care for children with developmental disabilities, this role will also include close collaboration with UNC's Carolina Institute for Developmental Disabilities, the highest funded autism research center in the country and a Leadership Education in Neurodevelopmental Disabilities (LEND) site and UNC's TEACCH program. This position will be located in the Division of Developmental Behavioral Pediatrics, a newly formed Division within the Department of Pediatrics at UNC-Chapel Hill School of Medicine. The creation of this newly formed Division is one of many examples of the Department's commitment to the care of children with developmental disabilities. In addition to DBP, other key members of the Division include psychology, social work and nursing. Applicants should be board certified or eligible in Developmental and Behavioral Pediatrics. Applicants from groups under-represented in medicine are especially encouraged to apply. The Raleigh-Durham-Chapel Hill area of North Carolina is an attractive place to live and work with great climate, schools, and both mountains and beach within a day drive.

title: Pediatric Endocrinology Clinical Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Pediatrics at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, in partnership with the North Carolina Children's Hospital, is seeking a Pediatric Endocrinologist to support the Division's clinical and academic missions. This appointment is for a Clinical Assistant Professor, fixed term, 1.0 FTE, with compensation and responsibilities commensurate with the candidate's experience. North Carolina Children's Hospital is a leading academic medical center dedicated to delivering family-centered care through excellence in clinical care, advocacy, research, and education. The hospital is consistently ranked among the nation's best children's hospitals by U.S. News & World Report, and the Division of Pediatric Endocrinology is accredited by the American Diabetes Association. The faculty member will report directly to the Chief of the Division of Pediatric Endocrinology and join a well-established, multidisciplinary team, including board-certified pediatric endocrinologists, nurse practitioners, a clinical pharmacist, pediatric endocrinology fellows, pediatric residents, Certified Diabetes Educators, nutritionists, and nurses. Together, the team provides comprehensive care for children with endocrine and diabetes-related conditions. Clinical responsibilities will include both inpatient and outpatient care of children with diabetes and other endocrine disorders. Outpatient clinics are located at UNC Children's Specialty Clinics in Chapel Hill and Raleigh, NC, with regional care responsibilities as needed. In addition, faculty are expected to participate in scholarly activities, including quality improvement initiatives, clinical research, and medical education.

title: CPC BioSoc Post-Doc Trainee
description: The Carolina Population Center at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for a Postdoctoral Scholar position with the NICHD-funded T32 training program, 'From Biological to Social Processes: Interdisciplinary Training in Life Course Research'. This program aims to promote and support interdisciplinary training of PhD students and postdoctoral scholars from both the social sciences and biological/health sciences. The goal of this program is to train scientists to move across disciplinary boundaries and employ creative and integrative approaches to understanding the complex factors that influence health and health disparities across the life course. Trainees will have the opportunity to receive interdisciplinary mentorship and training in a wide array of methods and content areas, ranging from social inequalities to biological processes. Trainees will identify a co-preceptor team comprised of a mentor from their home discipline and another representing their new interdisciplinary interest area from among the current training faculty. The initial term of appointment is one year, with a preferred start date in January 2027 (negotiable). Reappointment for a second year is possible with continued funding. Additional supplementary materials are required. Please carefully review the special instructions section of this posting.

description: The Department of Ophthalmology, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, invites applications for an Open Rank Pediatric Surgical Ophthalmologist position. description: The Department of Sociology at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill invites applications for an Assistant or Associate (tenure-track or tenured) faculty position to begin July 1, 2027. In addition, we seek a colleague whose teaching will contribute to our interdisciplinary undergraduate Management and Society major, through existing or new courses on organizations, work and occupations, economic sociology, social psychology, non-profits, work and family, AI and work, or related topics. Applicants should specify their contribution to our Management and Society major in their cover letter. Candidates are expected to hold a Ph.D. in Sociology or a related field by July 1, 2027.

description: This tenure-track, open-rank, (Assistant/Associate Professor) position includes 40% teaching, 40% research and 20% service to the department/college. The service portion includes, but is not limited to search committees, review committees and administrative roles within the department and/or College. The current department teaching load of 2-1 courses per year. The position will also perform innovative research in the field of Asian Politics and show promise of research excellence and a desire to train and work with a diverse body of students.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate - Vaziri-Bowser labs
description: The Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine is seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Associate to join a collaborative, co-mentored research program between the laboratories of Dr. Cyrus Vaziri and Dr. Jessica Bowser. The successful candidate will investigate fundamental mechanisms of the DNA damage response (DDR), cell cycle regulation, and their implications for genome stability, cancer biology, and therapeutic response For recent related publications please see: Nat Commun. 2025 Aug 5;16(1):7214. doi: 10.1038/s41467-025-62368-8. PMID: 40764480; Cell Rep. 2025 Jan 28;44(1):115104. doi: 10.1016/j.celrep.2024.115104. Epub 2024 Dec 20. PMID: 39708320; Nat Commun. 2024 Mar 4;15(1):1957. doi: 10.1038/s41467-024-45979-5. PMID: 38438348. This position offers the unique benefit of dual academic mentorship, along with industry-relevant experience through collaborations with the Center for Integrative Chemical Biology and Drug Discovery (UNC) and the Metabolomics and Exposome Laboratory (UNC). These collaborations will provide the candidate with access to complementary expertise, resources, and scientific perspectives across multiple disciplines.

Frankfort, Department Chair of Ophthalmology.

description: A SIGN-ON BONUS OF $5,639 IS AVAILABLE FOR THE SUCCESSFUL APPLICANT OF THIS POSITION PAID IN TWO INSTALLMENTS WITHIN 12 MONTHS OF HIRE: $2,819.50 WITHIN 30 DAYS OF HIRE DATE AND $2,819.50 (12) MONTHS AFTER HIRE DATE. The HVAC Training & Safety Officer is responsible for developing and delivering safety and technical training for personnel working with heating, air conditioning, ventilation, refrigeration, controls, and related systems. Creates lesson plans, training materials, and schedules, and provides hands-on instruction emphasizing safe work practices, hazard recognition, compliance requirements, and proper use of safety equipment. In addition to training and safety responsibilities, the position performs preventive, predictive, and reactive maintenance on complex refrigeration equipment supporting an intensive biotechnology/life sciences research and health care campus. Systems supported include direct expansion (DX) units, environmental chambers, walk-in coolers and freezers, air dryers, ice machines, packaged units, computer room air conditioning (CRAC) units, dehumidification systems, refrigerated scientific equipment, ultra-low and cryogenic equipment, small chillers, and hot water and steam boiler systems. HVAC maintenance duties include troubleshooting complex control circuits; replacing compressors; repairing refrigerant leaks; replacing fan and blower motors; repairing and replacing refrigeration, mechanical, and electrical controls; and maintaining EPA refrigerant management logs. Additional responsibilities include maintaining and repairing complex boiler systems, calibrating boilers for efficient operation, and preparing boiler systems for state inspections. The position also performs selected equipment replacements and installations and may support construction and renovation projects by reviewing work and providing written comments regarding compliance with plans, specifications, codes, and established guidelines. *Must possess a valid North Carolina Driver's License or have the ability to obtain one prior to hire date. *Requires EPA 608 universal refrigerant certification.

title: Open Rank Pediatric Critical Care Physician
description: The Department of Pediatrics at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC) / North Carolina Children's Hospital is seeking an exceptional Pediatric Cardiac Intensivist for a faculty appointment in the Division of Pediatric Critical Care Medicine. This Pediatric Cardiac Intensivist will be committed to patient care, research, and education. This position is Open Rank, Open track, and salary will be commensurate with training, experience, and academic accomplishments. The North Carolina Children's Hospital is a quaternary care medical center with a 20-bed multidisciplinary PICU and a 13 bed PCICU that admits over 1200 patients per year. We have active pediatric cardiothoracic, ECMO, burn, trauma, and organ transplantation programs. The Critical Care Medicine division maintains a fully accredited pediatric critical care medicine fellowship program. Our team includes 17 physicians, 6 advanced practice providers, 8 fellows, 2 research and 2 administrative support staff. The Department of Pediatric Critical Care Medicine is rich in hospital leadership including the UNC Health Chief Medical Informatics Officer, UNC Hospitals Chief Medical Officer, and Director of the Pediatric Residency Program. UNC offers ready access to collaborators in other clinical and basic science departments, global and public health, public policy and other expertise across campus. UNC is a National Institutes of Health (NIH) Clinical and Translational Science Award (CTSA) funded institution that offers support for clinical and translational researchers at all levels. This support includes seed funding, regulatory assistance, data management, drug/device development and grant preparation among other things.

title: Open Rank
description: The Division of Nephrology at the UNC School of Medicine is recruiting for an Open Rank Faculty Position specializing in General Nephrology. Academic Open Rank Positions will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. Duties include, but are not limited to, dialysis, hospital service and consulting as well as outpatient clinic responsibilities. Responsibilities will include fellow/resident/student teaching.

title: Chair, Department of Emergency Medicine
description: The School of Medicine of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill seeks an accomplished and visionary leader to serve as Chair for the Department of Emergency Medicine. This recruitment is Open Track/Open Rank, and the appropriate track and rank will be determined once the top candidate is selected. The Department of Emergency Medicine is nationally recognized for excellence in clinical care, education, research, and service. The Department's mission is to improve the health of patients and communities through outstanding emergency care, innovative research, exceptional education, and meaningful service to the people of North Carolina and beyond. The Department is comprised of faculty physicians, advanced practice providers, residents, fellows, researchers, educators, and professional staff working across multiple clinical, educational, research, and administrative programs. Faculty members provide care throughout UNC Hospitals and affiliated UNC Health facilities while serving as leaders in emergency medicine, emergency medical services, critical care, disaster preparedness, quality improvement, patient safety, and healthcare innovation. Our clinical programs provide comprehensive emergency care to patients with acute illness and injury. As a major academic referral center and safety-net provider, the Department serves diverse populations and collaborates extensively with healthcare providers, community partners, and health systems to improve care, quality, and outcomes. Education is a central mission of the Department. UNC Emergency Medicine sponsors ACGME-accredited residency and fellowship training programs and provides educational experiences for medical students, residents, fellows, advanced practice providers, and interprofessional learners. Through innovative curricula, mentorship, and scholarly activity, the Department is committed to developing the next generation of leaders in emergency medicine. Research activities span clinical, translational, operational, implementation, health services, injury prevention, and population health sciences. Faculty investigators collaborate broadly across UNC Health, the School of Medicine, and the University to advance emergency care through scientific discovery, innovation, and dissemination of new knowledge. The Chair serves as the chief academic and administrative officer of the Department and is responsible for advancing all aspects of the Department's clinical, educational, research, and service missions. The Chair will provide strategic leadership, oversee faculty recruitment and development, ensure operational and financial stewardship, strengthen interdisciplinary collaborations, foster an inclusive and supportive culture, and advance the Department's local, regional, and national reputation. In addition to a primary faculty appointment in the Department of Emergency Medicine, the selected candidate will hold a secondary EHRA Non-Faculty administrative appointment as Department Chair. This structure is consistent with recent School of Medicine department chair recruitments.

title: Temporary Security Guard
description: The Security Division is seeking to hire individuals to perform security related duties at UNC facilities. Position requires a North Carolina Drivers License. We are currently accepting applications for individuals with availability any time, seven days a week. These positions should average between 20-30 hours per week. These are temporary contract positions with no benefits. These positions could last up to one year. Uniforms are furnished, but you must provide solid black shoes and belt. Since these are uniformed positions, you must adhere to departmental grooming standards. The officer will conduct routine patrols on foot or by assigned vehicle (golf cart) Security Officers will work individually and independently in generally unsupervised positions. The officer will lock and unlock doors as necessary. The officer will check and record any damage to University property and report this information to the appropriate designated department. Assist staff, individuals seeking services (directions, information) and visitors with concerns, escorts and disabled vehicles. Equipment malfunctions, power outages, heating and cooling problems, chemical spills, fire and any other health or safety related issues are to be duly noted in the officer’s activity report. Depending on the severity of the issue, all aforementioned items shall also be reported to UNC dispatch. Complete documentation in a log format while on duty arriving on time and in proper uniform attire. This position is considered to be an “ESSENTIAL" Employee position. This means that this position is one that is necessary to ensure that University operations continue uninterrupted during periods of adverse weather, and/or other emergency situations, including those that require the University to close. As such, employees will be required to report to work (or remain at work) according to your usual schedule, or upon notification, to report to work outside of your usual schedule. This is a continuous recruitment and will remain open until all positions are filled.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The tenure-track Assistant Professor will allocate effort approximately as follows: 40% teaching, 40% research, and 20% service. The position carries a two-course teaching load each semester during the fall and spring terms. Teaching assignments will be based on the candidate's expertise and departmental needs. The position will conduct rigorous research using appropriate methodologies, including a variety of quantitative and/or qualitative methods. The Assistant Professor will conduct service that includes, but is not limited to search committees, review committees and administrative roles within the department and/or College.

title: Teaching Assistant Professor
description: This full-time Teaching Assistant Professor will be expected to allocate effort approximately as follows: 80% teaching and 20% service. This service includes, but is not limited to, search committees, review committees, and administrative roles within the department and/or College. The position carries a three-course teaching load each semester during the fall and spring terms. Teaching assignments will be based on the candidate's expertise and departmental needs. The six courses taught by this Teaching Assistant Professor will be at the undergraduate level and include a mix of existing and new courses. This position will be hired with a 3-year initial contract with the possibility of renewal and promotion, in accordance with university and departmental personnel policies.

title: Transfusion Medicine Pathologist
description: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine is seeking a full-time physician for a tenure-track/tenured, fixed-term, or variable track position at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor for the Transfusion Medicine Service. Our Transfusion Medicine Service encompasses donor collections, therapeutic apheresis, hematopoietic progenitor cell collection and processing, blood component processing, and compatibility testing. Applicants with secondary interests in some other area of the pathology lab, such as surgical pathology, hematopathology, or clinical pathology, are welcome to apply.

title: Open Rank
description: The Department of Psychiatry at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill School of Medicine invites applications for an open-rank, tenure-track faculty position in the Child and Adolescent Anxiety and Mood Disorders Program (CHAAMP). This recruitment reflects CHAAMP's continued growth and is supported by its longstanding partnership with the Foundation of Hope, whose investment has played a vital role in advancing youth mental health research at UNC and beyond. Recruitment for this position is a priority under the leadership of Department Chair Dr. Warren Taylor. CHAAMP is a multidisciplinary clinical research program focused on the prevention, assessment, and treatment of anxiety and mood disorders across childhood, adolescence, and young adulthood. Faculty conduct a broad range of research, from neuroimaging studies to randomized clinical trials, with a strong emphasis on team science, external funding success, and partnerships across academic, clinical, and community settings. The successful candidate will lead an innovative, externally funded research program focused on the prevention and treatment of youth mental health problems, particularly among school-age children (K-8). Areas of interest include, but are not limited to: Risk factors underlying the co-occurrence of substance use and mental health disorders Community-based participatory research (CBPR) Mental health research in rural and historically underserved communities Development, evaluation, implementation, and dissemination of evidence-based prevention and intervention programs This position offers exceptional opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and scientific innovation within a highly collaborative research environment. CHAAMP investigators bring expertise spanning developmental cognitive neuroscience, clinical trials, prevention and implementation science, community-engaged research, digital technologies, and mobile health. A distinctive feature of this position is CHAAMP's partnership with the Foundation of Hope, which provides flexible philanthropic support to generate pilot data, launch new research directions, bridge funding gaps, and protect time for scholarship. This support has repeatedly helped investigators develop projects that later secured federal funding. In addition to research leadership, the faculty member will mentor postdoctoral fellows, graduate students, and research staff, contributing to CHAAMP's strong culture of training and professional development. CHAAMP is committed to fostering an inclusive, collegial, and supportive environment and has a strong record of helping early-career investigators secure career development and independent research awards. New faculty can expect individualized mentorship, internal grant review and development support, and immediate access to established research infrastructure, community partnerships, and participant recruitment resources. Appointment rank, start-up support, and internal research resources will be commensurate with the candidate's qualifications, accomplishments, and research needs.

title: Postdoctoral Research Associate - Marsico Lung Institute
description: A Postdoctoral Research Associate position is available for a Ph.D. or equivalent level candidate at University of North Carolina, Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine, and the Marsico Lung Institute. We are interested in quantitation and characterization of mucin macromolecules in health and diseases with mucus abnormalities such as COPD, asthma, CF. This study will employ a broad range of biochemical, biophysical, and proteomics characterization of mucins and their quantitation using light scattering and labeled mass spectrometry-based quantitation technologies. Our laboratory at the Marsico Lung Institute is one of the best-equipped and most focused mucin/mucus biochemistry and biophysics innate immunity laboratories in the USA. As such, it will provide the selected candidate with a unique opportunity to develop new skills and apply them to fundamental questions in innate lung defense.

title: Post-Doc Research Associate
description: The Postdoctoral Research Associate will study the interface between circadian rhythms and the genomics of nucleotide excision repair. Standard biochemistry and molecular biology equipment and procedures will be used.

title: Assistant Professor
description: This tenure-track Assistant Professor position focuses on Coastal Ecology. This position will teach graduate and undergraduate courses and conduct research in the field of Marine Biology.

title: Assistant Professor
description: This tenure-track Assistant Professor position focuses on Biological Oceanography. This position will teach graduate and undergraduate courses and conduct research in the field of Marine Biology.

title: Medical Physicist
description: The University of North Carolina is seeking a clinical radiation therapy physicist to provide services at two locations: the Departments of Radiation Oncology at the University of North Carolina Cancer Hospital (Chapel Hill) and the University of North Carolina Cancer Care Center at Rockingham (Eden, NC.) This full time position will share responsibilities for the two locations with another physicist on staff. Both The University of North Carolina Cancer Hospital (Chapel Hill) and The University of North Carolina Cancer Care Center at Rockingham (Eden, NC) are part of the broader University of North Carolina system. The Department of Radiation Oncology at Rockingham works under the guidance and oversight of the main Radiation Oncology Department located at the University of North Carolina Cancer Hospital in Chapel Hill, NC. North Carolina Cancer Hospital, Dept of Radiation Oncology: The department is currently staffed with 13 Radiation Oncologists, 7 Dosimetrists, 12 Medical Physicists, and 1 IT specialist.
