title: Software Development Engineers
description: The SCI Institute The SCI Institute is a world-class research institute located within the new Warnock Engineering Building on the University of Utah campus. We are a highly dynamic, driven group of over 170 faculty, staff, and students. The overarching goals of the SCI Institute’s scientific computing research are to create new techniques, tools, and systems, by which scientists may solve problems affecting various aspects of human life. We believe that to advance the state-of-the-art and create meaningful computational solutions for such complex systems, one needs to advance research in a number of areas within scientific computing, including: visualization, simulation, and modeling. The SCI Institute presents a highly challenging, collaborative work environment that can be deeply rewarding for the right individual. Further information is available at http://www.sci.utah.edu/ . We are seeking a Software Development Engineer with experience and interested in state-of-the-art AI technologies, data science, and research software engineering. This position offers the opportunity to work in a world-renowned research institute alongside faculty, software engineers, PhD students, and PostDocs on the development of cutting-edge AI-ready/agentic infrastructure for data and model discovery, model metadata extraction, and scholarly intelligence. The Software Development Engineer III/IV provides advanced technical leadership in the design, development, deployment, and operation of complex software systems, cloud platforms, data infrastructure, and AI-enabled research environments. This position serves as a senior technical contributor responsible for architecting and delivering scalable, secure, and innovative software solutions that support nationally significant research, artificial intelligence, advanced computing, and cyberinfrastructure initiatives. The position leads the technical design and implementation of large-scale projects supporting AI innovation, federated data ecosystems, privacy-enhancing technologies, cloud-native platforms, and scientific computing environments. Working with faculty, researchers, government agencies, industry partners, and multidisciplinary technical teams, the incumbent provides technical direction and oversight across multiple concurrent initiatives, including the NSF-funded SAFE-AI (Sandbox for Accelerated Feedback and Experimentation for AI Innovation), National Data Platform (NDP), and PARAPET (Prototype Architecture for Research Advances Using Privacy Enhancing Technologies) programs. The Software Development Engineer III operates with minimal supervision and substantial independence, serving as a highly skilled technical professional responsible for complex software engineering efforts and technical decision-making. The Software Development Engineer IV serves as a recognized subject matter expert and senior technical leader, providing strategic direction, architectural leadership, and mentorship while driving the development of advanced cyberinfrastructure and software platforms critical to organizational and national research priorities. description: Biostatisticians Job Summary The University of Utah Data Coordinating Center (DCC) is seeking a biostatistician to join our collaborative, data driven team. The Utah DCC partners with investigators nationwide to provide data management, project management, and statistical expertise for large-scale multicenter research studies spanning a wide range of clinical and public health topics. As a member of the team, you will contribute to study design, perform statistical analysis, and support reporting and dissemination of results across diverse research areas. Ideal candidates bring solid knowledge of standard statistical procedures, moderate programming skills in at least one statistical language (such as SAS or R), and familiarity with relational databases and large-scale data systems. Attention to detail, the ability to critically think through complex analyses, and a collaborative approach to problem-solving are essential in this dynamic research environment. This position offers the opportunity to work closely with investigators, data scientists, clinicians, public health experts, and other biostatisticians to advance high-impact research through data-driven insights. The Utah DCC is a full-service Academic Research Organization (ARO) that operates a comprehensive Clinical and Data Coordinating Center. We support investigators and sponsors in academics, government, and industry with end-to-end expertise in research design, management, execution, and analysis. Our mission is to harness the power of collaboration, advance science, move society, and benefit humanity. Our vision is a world where transformative scientific innovation persistently moves society and humanity forward. Responsibilities Ensure the statistical integrity and accuracy of biomedical or clinical research data. Perform statistical design, modeling, and analysis. Provide statistical summaries and reports of studies in support of product development. Consult with scientists and engineers to ensure proper use of statistical methodology and interpretation of results. Program statistical software packages (e.g., SAS/STAT, Stata, or R) to improve quality and efficiency of life science projects. May respond to questions from regulatory authorities on statistical issues. Develop and manage analysis datasets and associated documentation, including dataset specifications and data checks. Perform statistical analyses using standard methods and statistical software (e.g., SAS, R, Stata) and prepare analytic deliverables such as tables, figures, and reports for interim and final results. Interpret and clearly communicate results including statistical methods, findings, and limitations to both technical and non-technical audiences. Collaborate with multidisciplinary study teams including investigators, data managers, and other study staff by providing statistical perspective and input across all study stages (study design, enrollment, and post-enrollment). Maintain quality assurance and documentation standards for all analytic work to ensure reproducibility, transparency, and compliance with Utah DCC standard operating procedures. Coordinate with supervising and faculty biostatisticians to prioritize and manage competing project timelines, communicate progress, and proactively address challenges in data or design. Contribute to manuscripts, abstracts, and presentations including drafting analysis sections, generating summary outputs, and assisting with methodological explanations. Support database and data system development including collaboration on data structure design, data dictionary maintenance, and familiarity with relational databases (e.g., SQL, REDCap, or other clinical data management systems). Identify and troubleshoot statistical or data-related issues , proposing potential solutions and escalating as appropriate. Engage in continuous professional development , staying current on statistical methods, programming practices, and data management tools relevant to clinical and public health research. The Utah DCC offers a career ladder for biostatisticians and professional development opportunities such as conference attendance and other trainings. This position is not eligible for work visa sponsorship. (e.g. H1-B) To learn more about the Utah DCC, visit http://uofuhealth.org/UtahDCC Learn more about the great benefits of working at the University of Utah: https://benefits.utah.edu/ This is posted as open-rank and may be filled at any of the listed job levels.

title: Hourly Research Assistants
description: The Research Assistant supports the daily operation of clinical and community based research studies. This is a hands on role with a lot of direct participant contact. On a typical week the Research Assistant may screen a potential participant by phone, pull data from medical charts, drive to a partner site for an in person assessment, lead a study cycling class, and then enter and clean the data collected from all of it. The position works under the direction of the Principal Investigator and Research Coordinator and follows approved protocols, institutional policy, and federal regulations for human subjects research. Supervision This position works under the direct supervision of the Principal Investigator and Research Coordinator. The Research Assistant does not supervise other staff, but may orient and train student workers and volunteers on specific study procedures. Preferences/Skills/Experience the ideal candidate should have: We are looking for someone who is comfortable being the face of the study to participants and just as comfortable being the person who catches a data entry error before it becomes a problem. The best fit for this role tends to be a person who likes variety in the workday, keeps their own systems organized without being told to, and gets satisfaction out of a participant finishing a 12 week program because someone remembered to call them. Specifically, we hope you bring: • Genuine comfort working with people. You can build rapport quickly with participants who may be nervous, deconditioned, older, or unfamiliar with research, and you can explain a consent form without rushing anyone through it. • Reliability and follow through. Study visits and classes happen on a schedule, at sites across the valley, and the team needs to know you will be there and prepared. • A high tolerance for detail. Protocol adherence, source documentation, and clean data are the actual product of this job, and you should find that satisfying rather than tedious. • Independent judgment in the field. You will often be the only study staff member at a site, so you need to solve small problems on the spot and recognize the ones that need to go up the chain immediately. • Confidence leading a room. Whether you have taught cycling before or you are willing to get certified, you should be willing to get on a bike, cue a class, and keep an eye on how each participant is responding. • Comfort with data tools. Experience with REDCap, Excel, and a statistical package is a real plus, and a willingness to learn them quickly is required. • Discretion. You will see medical records and personal health information every day, and you should treat that access as the responsibility it is. • Flexibility about hours and location. Participants have jobs and lives, so some sessions land early, late, or on a weekend. Prior research experience is helpful but not the deciding factor. We have trained excellent research assistants who came from clinical, fitness, or education backgrounds and brought strong people skills and good habits with them.

Advanced roles provide technical expertise in irrigation design, mapping, and construction review; lead projects and staff; and collaborate with Facilities Management, landscape teams, and external partners to support capital improvements and campus development. title: Civil Engineers
description: Civil Engineer, II Job Code P45432 Research, design, develop, and evaluate plans, specifications, and layouts for residential, commercial, and industrial development projects, public works improvements, or other capital improvement projects using applied knowledge of civil engineering. Design naturally and physically built structures using knowledge of biology, statistics, dynamics, materials, kinematics, hydrology, hydraulics, and geotechnics. Prepare technical reports, create design specifications, and determine cost estimates. Oversee construction of projects to ensure adherence to design specifications. Ensure projects comply with local zoning and ordinances, as well as national regulatory requirements. Identify, evaluate, and document existing structures for signs for disrepair and provide design remedies as necessary. Create and interpret blueprints, technical drawings, and schematics. Use drafting tools or computer-aided design (CAD) equipment and software in design work. May manage project schedules and budgets. May be required to approve designs that can impact the health, safety, and welfare of the general public, as required by law. Typically requires a bachelor's degree in civil engineering and may require professional engineering certification. Requires moderate skill set and proficiency in discipline. Conduct work assignments of increasing complexity, under moderate supervision with some latitude for independent judgment. Requires a bachelor's (or equivalency) + 4 years or a master's (or equivalency) + 2 years of directly related work experience. Assumes work equivalency (1 year of higher education can be substituted for 1 year of directly related work experience). Civil Engineer, III Job Code P45433 Research, design, develop, and evaluate plans, specifications, and layouts for residential, commercial, and industrial development projects, public works improvements, or other capital improvement projects using applied knowledge of civil engineering. May be required to approve designs that can impact the health, safety, and welfare of the general public, as required by law. Typically requires a bachelor's degree in civil engineering and may require professional engineering certification. Considered highly skilled and proficient in discipline. Conduct complex, important work under minimal supervision and with wide latitude for independent judgment. Requires a bachelor's (or equivalency) + 6 years or a master's (or equivalency) + 4 years of directly related work experience. Assumes work equivalency (1 year of higher education can be substituted for 1 year of directly related work experience). The successful candidate will join our utilities department team helping to oversee and manage multiple utility systems for our campus of over 1,500 acres serving over 65,000 staff, students and faculty. For our Civil Engineers these include our Drinking Water, Secondary Water, Natural Gas Master Meter, Storm Water, and Sanitary Sewer systems. Whether we are reviewing new construction documents for 21st century buildings, or upgrading aging infrastructure from the 20th and sometimes the 19th centuries, there is always a variety of assignments to keep the work interesting. Come join us and be an integral part of our team as we work to meet the evolving utility infrastructure needs of the state's flagship institution of higher education. Go UTES!

title: Coordinator, Administrative Program
description: The Center for Campus Wellness ( CCW ) is a comprehensive wellness office that provides wellness education, trainings and workshops; victim-survivor advocacy services and support; safer sex services for students; alcohol and other drug support services; wellness coaching; basic needs support; resource navigation; and student involvement opportunities. This position will be committed to supporting the mission of the office by leading efforts to further develop, implement, and coordinate the Collegiate Recovery Program, Recovery at the U (RU). This position will assist in developing long and short-term goals, objectives, and strategic planning for the RU program. Approaching this position with a strong commitment to a student-centered, harm reductionist, strengths-based framework is integral for this role. This position will actively work towards growing the RU community for students in recovery from alcohol and other drug use as well as prioritize campus-wide programming and education for harm reduction initiatives. This may include sober-centered events, educational workshops, support groups for members, and leadership opportunities for those in the RU community. This position is a part of the CCW’s Prevention and Education program team which is committed to taking a comprehensive and holistic approach to wellness promotion at the University of Utah. This team actively addresses collegiate wellness topics including but not limited to relationship and sexual violence, sexual wellness, mental wellness, alcohol and drug harm reduction, and more, using a primary and secondary prevention focus. This position will report directly to the Manager of Health Education Programs. Applicants should be proficient in health education and promotion principles, best practices, and behavior change frameworks; have experience working with collegiate wellness initiatives; have experience with conducting needs assessments and other data collection strategies; and committed to a student-centered, harm-reduction, comprehensive approach to wellness education and promotion. Applicants should be committed to working with a diverse campus community whose experiences, backgrounds and perspectives may be different from their own. As a larger CCW team, we prioritize our team’s well-being and actively support each other in professional development efforts, engaging in self-care practices, and creating a positive and supportive team atmosphere that fosters growth. We operate with a hybrid work schedule which includes the possibility of 1-2 days for remote work pending job duties and approval from the direct supervisor. At various times of the year, remote working days may not be approved if on-campus priorities and programs require in-person attendance. Mission of the Center for Campus Wellness We support student well-being and success through holistic and comprehensive programs that center wellness, safety, and healing. About Student Affairs CCW is an office located within the Student Affairs division. Student Affairs is comprised of over 20 departments and is focused on supporting student well-being and success with the goal of assisting students in discovering their passion, people, and purpose. To that end, we aim to foster an environment that encourages employees to embrace innovative service delivery methods to best meet the needs of our students. As a result, students can participate in the creation of campus culture, collaboratively working alongside professional staff, student leaders, and academic partners. Student Affairs is committed to grounding our programs, procedures, and policies for all students’ success. Our expectation is that all employees are engaged in this work to create a welcoming environment that supports the success of both students and staff and ensures they have the opportunity to be fully incorporated into university life.

description: Performs research support and dietary production activities in support of clinical and metabolic research studies conducted through the Metabolic Research Kitchen. Performs food preparation, cooking, weighing, measuring, portioning, packaging, labeling, and storage of research meals and maintains accurate records of meal production. Responsible for procurement of food and kitchen supplies as directed, including identifying needed ingredients and supplies, maintaining inventory levels, placing or coordinating orders, receiving deliveries, and properly storing food and supplies. Responsible for maintaining the cleanliness, organization, and sanitation of the Metabolic Research Kitchen, including routine cleaning and sanitation of kitchen equipment, work surfaces, utensils, storage areas, and other areas of the kitchen. Ensures proper food handling, storage, temperature monitoring, and sanitation practices are consistently followed. Supports controlled feeding and metabolic research studies by preparing participant meals according to study-specific dietary requirements and production schedules. Accurately portions and packages meals, verifies labels and dietary specifications, maintains required study and production documentation, and coordinates meal distribution, storage, and collection as applicable. Communicates with research staff regarding meal production needs, study schedules, dietary requirements, and supply needs. May assist with data entry, creation and organization of study materials, and other research support activities. The candidate must have and maintain a Dietetic Technician, Registered (DTR) credential and a Current Food Handler Permit during employment.

title: Post Doc Res Assoc
description: The Postdoctoral Research Associate will conduct applied and fundamental research in energy systems engineering, with an emphasis on industrial energy systems, energy management, techno-economic analysis, modeling, simulation, optimization, and advanced control. The position will play a key role in a major collaborative research effort focused on improving the energy and economic performance of advanced manufacturing operations. Primary responsibilities will include developing and implementing a comprehensive industrial energy management program; characterizing and benchmarking facility energy and resource use; developing models, performance metrics, and strategies for continuous energy improvement; and conducting comprehensive techno-economic analyses of manufacturing processes, equipment, facilities, and scale-up pathways. The successful candidate will also contribute broadly to the research activities of the Energy Systems Research Group. Depending on the candidate's background and research interests, projects may include industrial decarbonization and smart manufacturing; hydrogen production and utilization; energy storage; renewable, nuclear, and hybrid energy systems; buildings and district energy systems; grid-interactive energy systems and demand response; process and energy system modeling; optimization and model predictive control; and applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning to energy systems. The position will involve developing computational models and simulation tools, analyzing experimental and operational data, formulating and solving optimization problems, evaluating technical and economic performance, and translating research results into practical engineering recommendations. The Postdoctoral Research Associate will be expected to lead and contribute to peer-reviewed publications and technical reports, present research findings, assist with research proposals and project deliverables, collaborate with university and industry partners, and help identify and develop new research directions. Additional responsibilities include mentoring and supervising graduate and undergraduate researchers, coordinating student research activities, supporting the development of research software and experimental or computational capabilities, and contributing to the overall intellectual and technical leadership of the research group. The position is intended for an individual who can work independently while collaborating effectively across multidisciplinary academic and industrial research teams.

title: Research Scientists (PhD)
description: The Research Scientist serves as a scientific and operational leader within the ORL, providing technical expertise, project leadership, and laboratory management in support of faculty-initiated and industry-sponsored research. This role oversees research projects from concept development through study completion while ensuring the laboratory operates safely, efficiently, and in compliance with institutional and regulatory requirements. The ideal candidate holds a PhD (or MS with equivalent experience) in engineering, biomechanics, biomedical sciences, or a related field and demonstrates strong technical, analytical, organizational, and project management skills. A track record of hands-on research, scientific productivity, and collaborative problem-solving is essential. This position offers a long-term career pathway with opportunities to expand leadership responsibilities over time in partnership with departmental leadership, supporting the department’s missions of discovery, innovation, and education. Department leadership envisions the ORL operating with a productivity model that emphasizes clearly defined objectives, measurable deliverables, efficient resource utilization, and timely project completion. As an ambassador for the ORL, the Research Scientist communicates laboratory capabilities to faculty, trainees, and industry partners and serves as a consultative resource for project planning, feasibility assessment, and collaboration development. The role helps establish project scope, timelines, deliverables, and resource requirements while promoting efficient project execution and minimizing scope creep. The Research Scientist provides end-to-end leadership for research studies, including project intake, experimental design, budgeting, protocol development, prototyping, data collection, statistical analysis, interpretation of results, and dissemination through abstracts, presentations, and peer-reviewed publications. The position also contributes to grant applications, industry-sponsored proposals, scientific peer review, and the development of external collaborations. Success in this role requires expertise in biomechanical testing, medical imaging, 3D modeling and fabrication, programming, and statistical analysis. The Research Scientist develops and maintains advanced analytical workflows using tools such as MATLAB, Python, LabVIEW, SPSS, and Stata. Experience working with human and animal cadaveric tissues is highly desirable. In addition to leading research activities, the Research Scientist oversees day-to-day laboratory operations, supervises research staff, and helps develop standard operating procedures that promote safety, quality, consistency, and operational excellence across all laboratory activities. description: Mitochondrial biology in metabolic health and disease: A postdoctoral position is available in the Chaudhuri lab within the Nora Eccles Harrison Cardiovascular Research and Training Institute (http://www.cvrti.utah.edu), at the University of Utah. Projects for interested candidates will focus on one of the following areas: (1) mitochondrial function in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, (2) development of therapeutics targeting mitochondrial function. About our laboratory: Our laboratory focuses on mitochondrial physiology in metabolic disease. We study the control of metabolism by ion channels and transporters, and are interested in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. Currently, we are studying mitochondrial calcium signaling and how it is altered in heart, liver, and kidney failure. Our research employs techniques in molecular and cellular biology, electrophysiology, imaging, genetic and whole-animal cardiovascular assays. This position represents an opportunity to work side-by-side with talented graduate students, postdocs, and specialists in a dynamic and stimulating research environment at the University of Utah. Interested candidates are encouraged to send an email describing research interests, a CV and the names of 3 references to d.chaudhuri@utah.edu

description: The Chen Wang Research Group is seeking a highly motivated, creative, and ambitious Postdoctoral Research Fellow to lead a project at the intersection of additive manufacturing, polymer chemistry, and materials science. Candidates preferably hold a Ph.D. in Materials Science, Polymer Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, or a related field, backed by a strong track record of first-author publications. This role requires hands-on expertise in vat photopolymerization 3D printing (SLA/DLP), custom resin formulation, and nanoscale characterization techniques like SEM. A deep understanding of polymer chemistry—specifically photopolymerization kinetics, polymerization-induced phase separation (PIPS), or dynamic covalent chemistry—is essential. Ideally, the preferred candidate will also bring experience in 3D printer customization, software/hardware integration, and CAD modeling skills.

description: The College of Science is seeking an experienced leader to direct a complex and rapidly expanding experiential learning enterprise at the University of Utah. The Science Research Initiative (SRI) is the College’s signature undergraduate research program that has grown into a large, sophisticated organization poised to provide meaningful hands-on research experiences to all incoming College of Science students in their first year on campus. A recent expansion includes the SRI Career Accelerator Program (SRI-CAP), which provides juniors and seniors with professional and technical skills development and industry connections. In addition to a small number of permanent staff, the program is supported by a team of more than a dozen SRI Fellows, postdocs who lead research streams and support an associated structured course. SRI has grown tremendously since its inception in 2020, with SRI and SRI-CAP currently serving approximately 650 undergraduate students per year. Substantial additional growth is projected. Beyond SRI, this position will be responsible for other related experiential learning programs in the college, including the ACCESS Scholars Program, a multi-year cohort program that supports students in becoming leaders in their scientific disciplines and beyond. We seek a visionary and experienced Director who will help shape the future of these programs during their next stage of development. The next phase of maturation for College of Science experiential learning programs requires strategic leadership to provide direction and vision, cultivate partnerships with internal and external stakeholders, and establish operational processes necessary to successfully scale up to serve the growing population of students. This position will work with college leadership to develop, refine, implement, and scale novel experiential learning opportunities for science and mathematics students at the University of Utah. The ideal candidate will have demonstrated experience leading complex educational programs, building organizational infrastructure, and developing high-performing teams. The College of Science at the University of Utah is a leading academic division dedicated to advancing scientific knowledge through innovative research, rigorous education, and community engagement. It encompasses eight academic units and several interdisciplinary programs that foster collaboration across scientific disciplines, including the Wilkes Center for Climate Science and Policy, the Center for Science and Mathematics Education, and the Henry Eyring Center for Cell and Genome Science. With state-of-the-art facilities and a strong emphasis on undergraduate research and graduate training, the College prepares students for impactful careers in academia, industry, medicine, and beyond. The University of Utah is located in Salt Lake City, one of the most livable cities in the western United States, which blends genuine urban amenities with unmatched access to the outdoors. World-class skiing at Alta, Snowbird, Park City, and Deer Valley is minutes from campus, alongside hiking, biking, and five national parks within a few hours’ drive. The city offers great neighborhoods, excellent schools, a vibrant dining and arts scene, and a full slate of professional sports — the Utah Jazz, Utah Mammoth, Real Salt Lake, Utah Royals and the Salt Lake Bees — plus the energy of University of Utah athletics right on campus. Start date for this position is negotiable. Program Management Direct/Manage/Supervise the design and implementation of programs that carry out the mission of the university. Develop strategies and goals to create programs offering the greatest impact to the community. Determine short- and long-term program plans to meet organization goals. Lab Technician
description: The Luo Lab at The University of Utah is seeking a full-time Lab Technician to join our team investigating the neural circuits underlying decision-making and attention. We combine sophisticated behavioral paradigms in rats with large-scale in vivo electrophysiological recordings and causal circuit manipulations using optogenetics. The successful candidate will be an integral member of our research group, providing technical support for ongoing projects and contributing to the lab's vibrant scientific environment.

title: Assistant Professor of Anthropology
description: The Department of Sociology and Anthropology at North Carolina State University (NC State) invites applications for an Assistant Professor of Anthropology beginning fall 2027. We are primarily seeking candidates working in cultural heritage (subfield open), with a focus on North America (preference for US Southeast). Candidates who could develop lab, field, or community-based learning opportunities for undergraduate and/or graduate students are particularly welcome.

title: Training Program Specialist
description: As the Training Program Specialist, you will build and expand Dairy Records Management Systems’ (DRMS, www.drms.org) customer education program, helping producers, Dairy Herd Improvement Association (DHIA) service affiliates, and consultants adopt and effectively use DRMS tools. You will develop standardized onboarding, scalable learning resources, and a Train-the-Trainer certification model to create consistent, repeatable training that can reach customers across the organization’s network. In this role, you will lead key training initiatives, deliver hands-on instruction, and equip internal teams and affiliates with the tools, content, and frameworks they need to provide high-quality education and support continued customer success. Primary responsibilities: Training Strategy & System Development Design and implement DRMS’s training strategy across producers, DHIA service affiliates, and consultants. Build a scalable training system, including onboarding frameworks, certification programs, and learning infrastructure (e.g., LMS). Develop a structured Train-the-Trainer certification model with defined learning paths and competency standards. Curriculum Development & Content Creation Lead development of structured training materials, including video, written guides, modules, and assessments. Translate complex software functionality into clear, role-based instruction aligned with how users learn and apply DRMS tools in real-world settings. Partner with Support, Marketing, and subject matter experts to incorporate field knowledge and product expertise into training content while aligning with DRMS messaging and communications. Program Delivery & Field Engagement Lead execution of training initiatives, including onboarding programs, product rollouts, and key education efforts tied to DRMS tools. Deliver training across formats (in-person, virtual meetings, and digital) to support user adoption and effective system use. Plan and participate in training events and sessions, including scheduling, logistics, materials, and participant experience. Program Evaluation, Metrics & Reporting Track training participation, engagement, and certification progress using key performance indicators (KPIs) for product adoption and user competency. Analyze training effectiveness using performance data, such as adoption rates, certification completion, and support patterns. Provide regular reporting and insights to leadership on program performance and opportunities for improvement. In this role, you will have the opportunity to shape how Dairy Records Management Systems educates and supports its customers by creating resources, delivering training, and equipping others to provide consistent, high-quality education across the DRMS network. If you enjoy developing engaging learning experiences, building scalable training programs, and helping people use technology effectively, we welcome you to apply. The work location for this position will be either Raleigh, NC, or Ames, IA.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Statistics at North Carolina State University in Raleigh, North Carolina, invites applications for two 9-month tenure-track Assistant Professor positions, each with a distinct research focus: Climate and environmental statistics, including sustainability. Statistics in human health and health sciences, including biostatistics and bioinformatics. For both positions, we are particularly interested in scholars whose research advances statistical approaches to complex challenges in their respective areas and may intersect with emerging fields such as machine learning and artificial intelligence. Key Responsibilities: Develop and sustain an independent, externally funded research program that advances statistical methodology and applications in the relevant research area. Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in statistics and related fields, and mentor doctoral students in research, dissertation development, and completion. Collaborate across disciplines to address complex scientific challenges through statistical and data science approaches, while contributing to the department’s academic mission and professional and university service.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor - Computer Systems & AI
description: The Department of Computer Science is looking to hire a tenure-track or tenured faculty member for August 2027 as part of NC State’s strategic engineering expansion. The Department of Computer Science expects to hire faculty predominantly at the Associate Professor level and exceptional Assistant Professors with strong research and funding records will also be considered. The department is seeking an excellent candidate in the following areas: AI Infrastructure and (Run-time) Systems Compilers and Programming Languages for AI Data-intensive High-performance Computing for AI Applications As a faculty member for the Department of Computer Science, responsibilities would include, but not be limited to: Participate in both high-quality and engaging undergraduate and graduate instruction, including courses in computer systems and compilers. Attract external funding and conduct research programs to advance the department’s strengths and priorities on a continuous and sustainable basis. Direct graduate student research at the intersection of systems, software/compilers/programming languages, and artificial intelligence and mentor students for their career development. Perform both institutional services and professional services to ensure the sustainability, quality, and external visibility of our education programs and research activities and advance the profession of computer science.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor
description: The Lampe Joint Department of Biomedical Engineering is a supportive, highly collaborative community driven by a shared mission: to improve human quality of life through rigorous study, analysis, research, and the design and translation of innovative technologies that benefit the people of North Carolina and the broader global community. In this role, candidates will join a vibrant department that values interdisciplinary thinking and real-world impact. We seek outstanding faculty candidates conducting research in areas that complement or expand our strengths in Biomedical Microdevices, Rehabilitation Engineering, Biomedical Imaging, Pharmacoengineering, and Regenerative Medicine. Lampe BME’s mission is to “Unite Engineering and Medicine to Improve Lives,” and our goal is to make an impact through ideation, translation, and commercialization of technologies to have an impact on human health and well-being. Candidates will have the opportunity to grow and sustain an independent research program while collaborating across engineering, basic sciences, and clinical disciplines. Patenting, licensing, and startup companies that license faculty’s University IP are highly encouraged. The position includes a primary appointment at NC State University with tenure home within the College of Engineering, access to shared resources at both NC State and UNC–Chapel Hill, and laboratory space located in Engineering Building 3 on NC State’s Centennial Campus—at the heart of the College of Engineering. Key Responsibilities: Establish, maintain, and grow an independent, externally funded research program in Biomedical Engineering. Engage in interdisciplinary research collaborations with engineering faculty, basic science researchers, and/or clinical investigators. Contribute to the department’s research mission through scholarship that advances biomedical technologies and improves human health. Teach and contribute to undergraduate and graduate education in biomedical engineering, in areas aligned with your expertise. Mentor undergraduate, graduate, and postdoctoral trainees and contribute to a supportive, open academic environment. Participate in service activities that support the department, college, and broader academic community. If you are a scholar looking to build an impactful biomedical engineering research program in a collaborative environment, who is motivated by translating research into technologies that improve human health, and is energized by teaching, mentoring and shaping the next generation, we encourage you to apply. This position is for a tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor in all areas related to Biomedical Engineering. Rank will be determined based on qualifications and experience. In addition to core responsibilities, there will be occasional opportunities to take on additional duties that support the department’s academic and research missions.

title: Clinical Veterinary Pharmacy Resident
description: The core philosophy of the NC State Veterinary Hospital Pharmacy is that pharmacist are expected to make meaningful contributions to non-human patient care through hospital service, education, community service, and research. Optimal pharmaceutical care can be defined as the identification, resolution, and prevention of drug-related problems that affect positive patient outcomes. We believe that this is best provided through a team approach that effectively integrates the knowledge and skills of the pharmacist with those of other health care professionals. Our vision is to ensure the safe and optimal use of pharmaceuticals for all patients of the NC State Veterinary Hospital by having pharmacists provide a central and visible role in all aspects of medication management. Duties and Responsibilities Resident will participate and lead clinical rounds in both small animal, large animal, and exotic animal clinics. The Resident will perform drug utilization review on hospital patients. Time will be spent in the clinical pharmacy or clinical pharmacology laboratory providing drug information, preparing sterile and non-sterile compounds and chemotherapeutics agents, designing, implementing and monitoring clinical drug studies. The resident will spend approximately 50% of time providing clinical pharmacy services, mentoring of APPE students, and responding to drug information queries; and approximately 50% of time in other activities including clinical service rotations, research activities, and outreach to North Carolina veterinarians and regulatory agencies. This is a two-year program.

title: Small Animal Internal Medicine Residency - Clinician Investigator
description: The Internal Medicine Clinician Investigator Program provides clinical training in small animal internal medicine and graduate research training toward the PhD degree. The residency portion of the program meets or exceeds the training requirements established by the ACVIM for candidates seeking board certification in Small Animal Internal Medicine. The primary objectives of the program are to develop clinical expertise in veterinary internal medicine, gain experience in didactic and clinical teaching, and become proficient in basic and applied research. The duration of the program varies according to each student’s ability to satisfy program requirements, but will be no less than five years, with the residency component of the program comprising the first three years. The Clinician Investigator Program is structured and rigorous, requires a team-oriented approach, and embodies a spirit of cooperation amongst clinical and basic science faculty. The program was designed to satisfy the needs of those individuals who are seeking a career in academic veterinary medicine, industry, or government. Successful completion of the program is dependent upon attracting candidates of the highest caliber who are capable of excelling in this demanding program. Because of the breadth and complexity of the program, the clinician investigator will participate in a diverse group of activities with increasing levels of responsibility. Clinical activity is most intensive in the first year of the program and clinical training is as for an Internal Medicine Residency Program. During the second and third years, both clinical and research responsibilities are scheduled. The remaining years of the program are devoted primarily to research activities. Duties and Responsibilities: Responsibilities include the supervision and education of veterinary students, interns, and other residents; patient care and client communication; and progressively increasing autonomy in diagnostic and therapeutic patient management. Attendance and participation in daily case rounds, intern/resident rounds, journal club, advanced medicine rounds, and the House Officer Seminar Program are required. Clinician investigators must maintain a case log and endoscopy log to allow the CI and residency committee to determine if seeing an appropriate balance of case material. Clinician investigators are expected to gain acceptance into graduate school by January 15th deadline (by year 1 of program), and complete 2-3 laboratory rotations (during years one and two) and identify a graduate mentor by the end of year two. For specific information on the clinician investigator program, please visit: https://cvm.ncsu.edu/education/residencies/small-animal-internal-medicine/ For specific information on the residency component of the program, please visit: https://www.acvim.org/ Starting in the second year, clinician investigators are paid bi-weekly instead of monthly. In the fall and spring semesters there is exemption from some taxes but student fees may be owed (approximately 1,300.00/semester, see https://studentservices.ncsu.edu/your-money/tuition-and-fees/graduate-students/ for additional information). There is no exemption from any taxes during the summer semesters.

title: Equine Emergency and Critical Care Fellowship
description: Duties and Responsibilities: The Equine Emergency and Critical Care (ECC) Fellowship is predominantly a clinical position, with 75% of time spent in clinics. Along with the other members of the Equine Emergency and Critical Care Service, the incumbent will serve as the primary clinician after hours. On-call hours are, 4:30 p.m. to 8:00 a.m. Monday through Thursday, and Friday 4:30 p.m. to Monday 8:00 a.m. The position provides for 3 months in the first year allotted from November to February for off-clinic board preparation. Along with the other members of the Service, the incumbent will be responsible for teaching 4th-year students on the ECC rotation, including leading rounds each Wednesday, Thursday and Friday morning. The incumbent will have direct mentorship throughout the fellowship period, provided by a diplomate of the American College of Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care – Large Animal.

title: Theriogenology Intern
description: The Theriogenology internship at North Carolina State University is a 1-year program that is clinically-based with an emphasis primarily on equine and canine species, with additional experience in bovine and small ruminant species. The Theriogenology internship at North Carolina State University is a 1-year program that is clinically-based with an emphasis primarily on equine and canine species, with additional experience in bovine and small ruminant species. There are 2 full-time faculty members, and a 3rd emeritus faculty member in the College with expertise in small animal and equine species. There are additional faculty members with board certification in the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine and American College of Veterinary Surgeons with interests in neonatology, urology and other related fields. The intern in Theriogenology will participate in reproductive cases as well as reproductive emergencies in the equine and small animal hospitals. Clinical duties will also involve participation in the breeding management, embryo transfer and assisted reproductive techniques (ARTs) of mares and stallions housed at the Theriogenology clinic at the Reedy Creek Farm in Raleigh, NC. The intern will be involved in clinical teaching of veterinary students. The intern will participate in current research projects of the Theriogenology section. Applicants must have a DVM or equivalent degree. There are additional faculty members with board certification in the American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine and American College of Veterinary Surgeons with interests in neonatology, urology and other related fields. The intern will be involved in clinical teaching of veterinary students. The intern will participate in current research projects of the Theriogenology section. Applicants must have a DVM or equivalent degree.

title: Administrative Coordinator
description: The Administrative Coordinator is a dynamic role serving at the intersection of academic research, creative immersive technology (VR/AR), and fast-paced artificial intelligence research center operations. This position manages multi-faceted administrative functions across grant management, hardware logistics, executive support, and cross-functional project coordination. The ideal candidate combines the compliance rigor of higher education administration, the technical resourcefulness of a VR studio manager, and the speed and adaptability of an AI operator.

title: Extension County Operations Support Specialist
description: N.C. Cooperative Extension in Alamance County is seeking a Support Specialist to provide administrative, customer service, and operational support to county Extension staff. This position supports the daily operations of the Extension office by assisting with file management, communications, program registrations, marketing activities, supply management, and financial processes. The Support Specialist works collaboratively with Extension staff, colleagues within North Carolina Cooperative Extension (NCCE), and county leaders to support the delivery of Extension programs and services. Responsibilities are performed in accordance with NCCE’s philosophy, objectives, policies, and procedures, with an emphasis on accuracy, professionalism, and confidentiality.

title: Extension County Operations Support Specialist
description: NC Cooperative Extension in Guilford County is seeking an Extension County Operations Support Specialist. The Outreach Specialist is a member of the staff of North Carolina Cooperative Extension (NCCE) and an important part of our team because they are often the first person the public and community partners interact with when calling our office or entering our facility. The primary responsibility is to provide administrative support to the County Extension office. The Outreach Specialist cooperates with colleagues in the NCCE and county leaders in performing assigned responsibilities.

title: Extension Agent, 4-H (Assistant, Associate or Full Agent)
description: The Extension Agent in this position will provide leadership for the 4-H Youth program in Montgomery County, and will plan, implement, and evaluate a wide variety of programs for youth ages 5-19. Duties include developing and maintaining community and school 4-H clubs, special interest youth programs, and in-school enrichment programs, training and management of volunteer staff, and evaluating and reporting impacts of program efforts. These programs will engage youth in positive, life-skill development activities to address issues of everyday life, enhance the community and environment where they live and give them access to high quality, experiential programming related to careers in the areas of Agriculture, Leadership, Science, Technology, Engineering, Math, etc.The agent will use a variety of educational methods such as organized 4-H clubs, school enrichment, 4-H summer programs, special interest and after-school programs. Volunteer development and utilization of an advisory system are essential to success. This position will recruit, train and coordinate adult and teen volunteers. Responsibilities will include coordinating program staff and management of programs funded through grants and fees. Agent will provide training and educational information for limited and non-limited resource audiences to acquire and gain skills to learn about community service and volunteerism, to participate in the community development process, and to provide an opportunity for youth to be trained in life skills to enhance the community and environment where they live and make smart choices related to healthy lifestyles. The agent will work closely with residents, community groups, professionals and volunteers that work with diverse groups. The position may be hired at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Agent level if the selected candidate meets the required qualifications.

title: COSS Support Specialist
description: N.C. Cooperative Extension in Onslow County is seeking a COSS Support Specialist to provide administrative, programmatic, and communications support to Extension staff. This position supports the delivery and promotion of Extension programs by assisting with public inquiries, maintaining records, coordinating events, preparing reports and correspondence, and developing and distributing educational and promotional materials. The COSS Support Specialist works collaboratively with Extension staff, colleagues within North Carolina Cooperative Extension (NCCE), and county leaders to support program operations and community engagement. Responsibilities are performed in accordance with NCCE’s philosophy, objectives, policies, and procedures. This is a full-time position (1.0 FTE), working 40 hours per week, funded entirely through a combination of state and county funds.

title: Study Director & Lead Weed Scientist
description: The Study Director & Lead Weed Scientist position will be an integral part of the IR-4 Biology and Registrations teams. This position reports directly to the IR-4 Associate Director for Regulatory Sciences and National Laboratory Director. Duties include, but are not limited to: Study Director – Protocol Development and Study Coordination 30% Provide technical direction for IR-4 residue studies conducted by cooperating scientists across North America in compliance with U.S. EPA Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations (40 CFR Part 160). Develop approximately 5 national residue study protocols annually in collaboration with registrant companies, study scientists, and IR-4 biologists. Ensure protocols are scientifically sound, operationally feasible, and completed in advance of study initiation timelines. Direct and manage approximately 30 concurrent IR-4 residue studies across multiple locations and phases (field and laboratory). Monitor study progress, including applications, sampling, shipment, analysis, and reporting. Review and approve protocol deviations and ensure timely resolution of study issues. Maintain communication with cooperators, laboratories, and QA personnel to ensure studies are conducted in accordance with protocols and GLP requirements. Review study reports and data for completeness, scientific integrity, and regulatory compliance, including application parameters, sampling procedures, storage conditions, and analytical results. Ensure all Quality Assurance findings are addressed and documented appropriately. Study Director – Data Package Development 20% Prepare approximately 3 regulatory data packages annually in accordance with U.S. EPA (OPPTS) and/or international (e.g., FAO/JMPR) guidelines. Develop clear, complete, and submission-ready reports for review by QA, IR-4 management, industry partners, and regulatory agencies. Identify and resolve data gaps through coordination with research collaborators and laboratories. Apply extrapolation, crop grouping, and other strategies to maximize the utility of generated data. Collaborate with other Study Directors on data interpretation and report preparation. Weed Science Leadership and Request for Assistance Management 20% Review and provide technical evaluation of all new IR-4 Requests for Assistance (PCRs) involving herbicides and plant growth regulators (PGRs) within the Food Program and, as needed, the Environmental Horticulture Program. Determine whether proposed uses are supported by existing federal and/or state registrations. When uses are not registered, assess data requirements based on product chemistry, use pattern, target weeds, crop sensitivity, and available data. Communicate with registrant companies to convey IR-4 assessments, determine interest in registration, and recommend next steps. Review and respond to company feedback as appropriate. Contribute to and lead discussions with industry partners regarding weed management technologies at IR-4 meetings. Identify potential research opportunities and maintain engagement with the IR-4 research network to encourage submission of new requests. Support priority-setting activities, including development of project lists, participation in regional calls, and facilitation of discussions at priority-setting workshops. Assist stakeholders with Priority Upgrade Proposals and Regional Upgrades and participate in selection processes. Provide technical recommendations to stakeholders based on current knowledge. Maintain current and accurate information in IR-4 databases related to herbicides and PGRs and assist with project closure following regulatory approvals. Maintain a working knowledge of weed science crop protection products, and modes of action and where there are gaps. Represent IR-4 at scientific and stakeholder meetings (e.g., Weed Science Society of America) and participate in relevant committees, as appropriate. Contribute to internal training, education, and knowledge-sharing activities within IR-4. Serve as a technical resource to stakeholders on weed management technologies and issues. Contribute to outreach and educational activities related to weed science and regulatory processes. Product performance research 20% Collaborate with IR-4’s national and weed science network to obtain information relevant to protocol development and study design. Develop and review efficacy and crop safety research protocols involving herbicides and PGRs. Provide technical guidance to cooperators conducting research and respond to protocol-related inquiries. Evaluate research results for protocol compliance and scientific quality. Prepare and distribute summary reports of research findings to stakeholders, including industry partners. Conduct site visits, as needed, to assess field trial performance and support research quality. Order test substance from suppliers and ensure collaborators receive samples. Collaborate with Study Directors to develop directions for use for GLP residue studies involving herbicides and PGRs. Provide subject-matter expertise during study conduct, including addressing issues related to product performance, crop injury, and crop biology. Other responsibilities as assigned 10% Participate in IR-4, grower, and professional meetings; contribute to presentations and committees as appropriate. Travel is an expectation of this position (6-10 times per year). Assist other Study Directors and the Senior Study Directors in completion of projects. Maintain effective working relationships across IR-4 Headquarters and the broader research network. Provide general support for IR-4 Headquarters operations and research programs. This position is based on-site at IR-4 Project Headquarters in the Venture IV Building on NC State University’s Centennial Campus in Raleigh, NC. Regular in-person attendance is required. Occasional evenings and weekends may be required during travel status or to meet project deadlines.

title: Research Assistant-Burclaff Lab
description:
Posting Number: PG194974EP
Internal Recruitment: No
Working Title: Research Assistant-Burclaff Lab
Anticipated Hiring Range: $50,000-$60,000
Work Schedule: Monday-Friday 8am-5pm working hours may differ based on lab work
Job Location: Raleigh, NC
Department: Department of Molecular Biomedical Sciences
About the Department: North Carolina State University’s College of Veterinary Medicine (NC State CVM ) is a dynamic community whose members are dedicated to preparing veterinarians, veterinarian scientists, and biomedical scientists while advancing animal and human health from the cellular level through entire ecosystems. The Department of Molecular Biomedical Sciences at the NC State CVM trains veterinarians, graduate students, and postdoctoral fellows in research-based careers focused on discovering new information about animal and human health and disease and using those findings to enhance animal and human health and wellbeing.
Wolfpack Perks and Benefits: As a Pack member, you belong here, and can enjoy exclusive perks designed to enhance your personal and professional well-being. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone. What we offer: Medical , Dental , and Vision Flexible Spending Account Retirement Programs Disability Plans Life Insurance Accident Plan Paid Time Off and Other Leave Programs 12 Holidays Each Year Tuition and Academic Assistance And so much more! Attain Work-life balance with our Childcare benefits, Wellness & Recreation Membership , and Wellness Programs that aim to build a thriving wolfpack community. Disclaimer: Perks and Benefit eligibility is based on Part-Time or Full-Time Employment status. Eligibility and Employer Sponsored Plans can be found within each of the links offered.
Essential Job Duties: We are seeking a proactive and curious Research Specialist to play an integral role in driving our science forward. Working in close collaboration with the Principal Investigator, you won’t just execute protocols- you will understand the why behind our research, actively contribute to novel experimental strategies, and help turn raw data into high-impact publications and grant proposals. This is an ideal role for an ambitious scientist looking to expand their technical toolkit, master cutting-edge biological models, and gain meaningful credentials for future graduate, medical, or biotechnology careers. What You’ll Do Advance High-Dimensional Stem Cell Models: Master and maintain cutting-edge primary cell cultures, human intestinal organoids, and established cell lines using advanced aseptic techniques. Drive In Vivo Research & Colony Operations: Manage mouse colony logistics- from breeding strategies and genotyping to tissue collection and key experimental procedures. Execute Molecular & Imaging Discovery: Perform vital translational assays, including DNA / RNA /protein extractions, RT-qPCR, tissue sectioning, immunofluorescence/ IHC staining, and live-cell imaging analysis. Contribute to Scientific Publishing: Actively assist in compiling research data, drafting documents, and co-authoring manuscripts, research reports, grant applications, and conference presentations. Power Daily Lab Operations: Keep the lab running seamlessly by maintaining critical instrumentation, managing inventory, and ensuring a safe, compliant environment. What Makes This Role Unique Direct Scientific Mentorship: Work directly with the PI in a collaborative, supportive environment where your career goals and intellectual curiosity are actively nurtured. In-Demand Technical Expertise: Gain rare, hands-on experience with human organoids, genetic modification, and advanced imaging platforms. Authorship & Career Growth: Active involvement in manuscript preparation offers real opportunities for publication credit and scientific visibility.
Minimum Education and Experience: Relevant Master’s Degree, or relevant bachelors and 3 or more years of relevant experience, or relevant independent experience and education.
Other Required Qualifications: Experience in mammalian primary cell culture (establishment and maintenance) Experience in molecular biology and biochemistry techniques ( PCR ; RT-qPCR; gel electrophoresis, DNA , RNA , and protein extraction; immunofluorescence; immunohistochemistry) Experience in mouse colony management (animal handling, breeding, weaning, genotyping, etc) and in vivo experimentation
Preferred Qualifications: Prior research experience Ability to work with animals Strong computer skills and ability to use highly specialized laboratory equipment with troubleshooting abilities
Required License(s) or Certification(s): N/A
Valid NC Driver's License required: No
Commercial Driver's License required: No
Job Open Date: 10/16/2026
Anticipated Close Date: 10/22/2026; if posting is still active we are accepting and reviewing applications.
Special Instructions to Applicants: Please attach a Cover Letter, resume/CV, and contact information for three (3) professional references.
Position Number: 00112294
Position Type: EPS/SAAO
Full Time Equivalent (FTE) (1.0 = 40 hours/week): 1.0
Appointment: 12 Month Recurring
Mandatory Designation - Adverse Weather: Non Mandatory - Adverse Weather

title: Program Director, Advising Technology
description: The Program Director, Advising Technology reports to the Associate Vice Chancellor and Associate Dean and works closely and collaboratively with academic colleges and campus partners. The position provides leadership for the implementation, management, and effective utilization of Navigate360 and other advising technologies to support student success, retention, and persistence to graduation through the strategic use of data, technology, and integrated student support practices. The Program Director, Advising Technology is responsible for, but not limited to: Oversee Implementation and Utilization of Shared Advising and Student Support Technologies Provide leadership and oversight for the implementation, ongoing utilization, and continuous improvement of shared advising and student support technologies across the university. Develop and deliver training, resources, and professional development opportunities to support effective use of advising and student support technologies by faculty, staff, advisors, and campus partners. Consult and collaborate with leadership across DASA, academic colleges, and other campus units to identify technology needs, enhance platform utilization, and support student success initiatives. Serve as a primary point of contact for advising technology inquiries, providing consultation, troubleshooting support, and guidance to campus partners regarding system functionality and effective use. Serve as the liaison to respective technology vendors and collaborate with university technology partners to coordinate system enhancements, integrations, upgrades, testing, and resolution of functional or technical issues. Office Management Provide day-to-day leadership and coordination for the advising technology program, establishing priorities and ensuring activities align with divisional and university goals. Develop, maintain, and communicate operational processes, procedures, documentation, and resources related to shared advising and student support technologies. Coordinate projects, initiatives, meetings, and implementation activities involving advising technology and related student success efforts. Monitor program needs, timelines, deliverables, and emerging priorities to support effective and efficient operations. Maintain strong working relationships with DASA units, academic colleges, technology partners, and other campus stakeholders to facilitate coordination and address operational needs. Assessment Coordinate and respond to data and reporting requests related to advising technologies, student support initiatives, and platform utilization. Oversee assessment activities and annual reporting processes, including the collection, analysis, interpretation, and communication of relevant program and utilization data. Serve as a liaison among campus partners, Enterprise Application Services (EAS), and Enrollment Management and Services (EMAS) to promote data accuracy, integrity, and consistency within shared platforms. Use assessment findings, institutional data, and platform information to identify trends, evaluate effectiveness, and inform recommendations for program and technology improvements. Collaborate with campus partners to establish assessment practices and measures that demonstrate the effectiveness and impact of advising technology and related student success initiatives. Campus Service Represent advising technology and related student support initiatives on university, divisional, and cross-functional committees, workgroups, and project teams, as appropriate. Build and maintain collaborative relationships with academic colleges, DASA units, faculty, advisors, technology teams, and other campus partners to advance shared priorities. Contribute expertise regarding advising technology, student support systems, data, and related practices to campus initiatives and decision-making. Participate in university initiatives and special projects that support academic advising, student success, retention, and effective use of shared technologies. Remain informed of emerging practices and developments in advising and student support technology and share relevant information and recommendations with campus partners.

title: Associate Dean for Academic Programs
department: 200101 - Dean's Office - Poole College Of Management
description: The Associate Dean for Academic Programs provides strategic leadership for Poole College of Management’s undergraduate, graduate, doctoral, and certificate programs. Reporting directly to the Dean and serving as a member of the Dean’s executive leadership team, the Associate Dean is responsible for the quality, relevance, coordination, performance, and continuous improvement of the College’s academic portfolio. Working in partnership with department heads, program directors, faculty, staff, students, and University partners, the Associate Dean ensures that academic programs remain rigorous, distinctive, financially sustainable, and responsive to evolving student and workforce needs. Departments and faculty retain primary responsibility for their degree programs and curricula through established faculty-governance processes. The Associate Dean provides College-wide leadership for academic portfolio strategy, enrollment and student success, curricular innovation, career readiness and experiential learning, graduate-program marketing, global programs, and academic program review. The position also contributes to College-wide strategy, resource allocation, accreditation, and organizational decision-making, while delegating routine academic operations to assistant deans, program directors, and professional staff. Primary Responsibilities include: Academic Portfolio Strategy and Innovation Lead strategic planning for undergraduate, graduate, doctoral, and certificate programs. Evaluate programs based on academic quality, demand, outcomes, capacity, and financial performance. Lead development of new programs, credentials, and delivery formats and recommend expansion, revision, consolidation, or discontinuation when appropriate. Promote curricular innovation, including integration of AI, analytics, experiential learning, and durable skills. Ensure program and curricular planning incorporates findings from Assurance of Learning and other assessment processes. Program Leadership and Performance Provide leadership and coordination across the College’s academic portfolio. Supervise undergraduate and graduate academic leadership and establish expectations for program planning and performance. Partner with department heads and faculty program directors to support departmentally owned and jointly administered programs. Lead enrollment planning and monitor recruitment, enrollment, retention, completion, and student outcomes. Oversee University-required academic program reviews and ensure findings inform program and resource decisions. Academic Resources and Student Success Provide strategic oversight of academic-program budgets, resource allocation, and financial performance. Align program growth with faculty, instructional, financial, and student-support capacity. Lead College-wide strategy for advising, retention, progression, completion, and the student academic experience. Oversee academic policies, exceptions, and appeals, addressing complex or precedent-setting matters. Represent the College with the Graduate School, Division of Academic and Student Affairs, and other relevant University offices. Career Readiness and Experiential Learning Partner with Career and Corporate Relations to integrate career readiness, employer perspectives, and professional competencies into academic programs. Support expansion of internships, practicums, applied projects, and other experiential-learning opportunities. Use employer, alumni, and career-outcome feedback to inform academic planning and curricular improvement. Marketing and Global Programs Supervise the Director of Marketing and align graduate-program marketing with enrollment and program priorities. Supervise the Director of Global Programs and align global opportunities and partnerships with College priorities. Evaluate marketing and global initiatives based on effectiveness, quality, strategic value, feasibility, and financial sustainability. College Leadership Serve on the Dean’s executive leadership team and contribute to College strategy, budgeting, accreditation, and organizational decision-making. Lead cross-functional academic initiatives and use evidence and outcomes to guide investment, expansion, modification, or discontinuation. Represent the College on relevant University committees and leadership groups. Undertake other responsibilities assigned by the Dean. Reporting Relationships include: The Associate Dean reports directly to the Dean. Direct reports: Assistant Dean for Undergraduate Programs Assistant Dean for Jenkins Graduate Programs Director of Marketing Director of Global Programs Dotted-line relationships: Faculty directors of undergraduate programs Faculty Director of the MBA Program Faculty Director of the Master of Management Faculty Director of the Master of Accounting Director of Graduate Programs in Economics (PhD and Master's programs) Other faculty program directors as assigned Faculty program directors also have a dotted-line relationship to the Associate Dean for Faculty, Research and Engagement solely for Assurance of Learning. The Director of Career and Corporate Relations reports directly to the Dean and has a dotted-line relationship to the Associate Dean for Academic Programs for career readiness, employer-informed curriculum, and experiential learning. Annual priorities and performance expectations are jointly established by the Dean and both associate deans. Indicators of Success include: A coherent and differentiated academic portfolio. Strong enrollment, retention, completion, and career outcomes. Timely development and revision of programs. Effective university program reviews and follow-through. Strong coordination across programs and departments. Effective graduate-program marketing and global programming. Expanded experiential-learning opportunities. Effective curricular responses to Assurance of Learning findings. The Associate Dean for Academic Programs plays a central role in shaping the academic direction and long-term success of Poole College of Management. Through strategic leadership of the College’s academic portfolio, the Associate Dean ensures that programs remain rigorous, relevant, innovative, and sustainable while supporting student success and responding to evolving educational and workforce needs. Working collaboratively with the Dean, department heads, faculty, academic leaders, and professional staff, the Associate Dean connects College-wide strategy with academic priorities and helps position Poole College to deliver distinctive, high-quality educational experiences across its undergraduate, graduate, doctoral, and certificate programs.

title: Facilities Maintenance Technician
description: ​Join NC State University’s Building Maintenance and Operations (BMO) team as a Facilities Maintenance Technician – Contributing and build your skills while helping keep our campus facilities safe, reliable, and operating at their best. This hands-on position works within a zone maintenance shop on NC State’s Original Campus, Centennial Campus, or Centennial Biomedical Campus (Veterinary School) and supports routine maintenance, operations, and repairs across building systems. In this role, you’ll gain hands-on experience with HVAC, plumbing, electrical, steam, and other building systems while working alongside experienced mechanics and technicians. You’ll perform preventive maintenance, assist with repairs, operate basic tools and equipment, monitor equipment, identify potential problems, and know when to elevate more complex issues to higher-level mechanics. If you’re dependable, hands-on, eager to learn, and interested in developing your skills in the skilled trades, we invite you to apply and become part of the NC State Facilities team! Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Perform basic maintenance, preventive maintenance, and repairs across HVAC, plumbing, electrical, steam, and other building systems . Assist higher-level mechanics with maintenance, troubleshooting, repairs, installations, and other assigned work. Perform routine tasks such as lubricating, cleaning, inspecting, re-lamping, repairing plumbing fixtures, and checking equipment . Take readings on boilers, chillers, and other equipment; check chemical levels and report unusual conditions or discrepancies. Recognize signs of equipment or system problems, including leaks, unusual noises, temperature changes, electrical outages, and equipment malfunctions. Troubleshoot basic maintenance issues and determine potential causes. Operate and maintain the basic tools and equipment used in assigned trades and follow appropriate procedures for each task. Follow preventive maintenance work orders and maintenance requests, completing assigned work accurately and within established timelines. Accurately document work performed, including time, materials, equipment readings, and identified issues . Develop working knowledge across multiple building systems and cross-train in building equipment operations and maintenance. Properly isolate and lock out equipment and systems as required before performing maintenance or repairs. Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment and follow all University safety, health, and established safe-work practices. Perform tasks requiring standing for extended periods, working in confined spaces, and utilizing various tools. Safely climb and work from different types of ladders to access elevated or below-grade areas (such as roofs, above-ceiling spaces, and utility pits). Be exposed to and work in areas where insects or small animals are occasionally present. All essential tasks must be performed with or without reasonable accommodations. Lift, carry, and maneuver materials weighing 60–90 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodations.
