Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follows verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs.

title: Engagement Specialist
description: The North Carolina Institute for Climate Studies Project Climate Engagement Specialist will lead engagement initiatives spanning a broad range of environmental research projects such as machine learning assisted wildfire prediction, extreme precipitation and flooding, air quality, and public health. This role entails crafting and executing dynamic engagement strategies that facilitate a two-way exchange of information, and serving as Institute liaison with external partners and entities. The incumbent must be able to effectively convey complex climate science research to a wide array of stakeholders while also collecting crucial insights to guide and enhance the research process. Key responsibilities for this position include: Data Analysis and Strategic Planning Develop and execute comprehensive engagement plans, strategies, and programs that align with Institute-wide goals and projects across a variety of areas. Translate complex scientific research into actionable ideas that resonate with a wide range of audiences. Maintain a working knowledge of climate information and its use, potential use, value, and applications for targeted audiences. Stay up to date on the latest developments in climate science, policy, and communication strategies, with the goal of refining and improving Institute engagement approaches. Develop and share science-based engagement content through a variety of formats (e.g., newsletters, web content, workshops, reports, social media, podcasts). Use and promote open data best practices and the principles of Open Science. Work with the NCICS Communications team to develop scientifically based messaging materials, newsletters, presentations, web content, etc. Collaborate with Institute project teams, utilizing relevant tools (e.g., Python, Jupyter Notebooks, GitLab, AWS) to develop interactive resources that support climate literacy and decision-making. Engagement Engage with a variety of agencies, organizations, partners, and stakeholders, providing timely and relevant information and materials. Design and deliver compelling presentations, workshops, training sessions, etc. to enhance the understanding of climate science, its impacts, and adaptation strategies. Plan and conduct community engagement activities to raise awareness of climate change challenges and promote resilience and adaptation efforts. Research, review, and participate in local, regional, and national climate-related events on behalf of the Institute. Investigate, identify, and connect with agencies and groups who could benefit from access to climate data. Effectively coordinate engagement event logistics, including venue selection, catering arrangements, scheduling, registration, speaker arrangements, platform management, event promotion, materials development, post-event follow-up, etc. Coordinate guest speaker opportunities to enhance engagement efforts. Update and develop new engagement strategies to improve environmental literacy. Utilize effective communication strategies to engage non-scientific stakeholders across different populations, in rural, and underserved communities. Serve as the main point of contact for Institute engagement activities, acting as a liaison between the Institute and external constituents. Partner Collaborations Support the Director of Corporate Engagement and Strategic Partnerships in building and nurturing partnerships with relevant organizations to broaden the impact of the Institute’s climate information initiatives. Develop and maintain positive relationships with local, regional, and national partners, policy makers, and the general public regarding the use, application, and awareness of environmental / Earth System science data. Engage with a variety of stakeholders, including those from academic, government, industry, and underserved sectors. Work cooperatively with Institute staff, partners, and external stakeholders in support of project objectives, including related engagement activities. Contribute to the planning, design, and development of events and programs, working with Institute staff to ensure alignment with communications and engagement goals. Investigate and pursue opportunities for external collaboration, including grant submissions and new sources of funding. Effectively communicate (verbally and in writing) with Institute staff, partners, stakeholders, and the general public. Demonstrate professionalism, tact, and diplomacy while representing the Institute in meetings, through written correspondence, and other official roles. Reporting Coordinate and participate in engagement activities’ reporting (summaries, annual reports, project reports, etc.). Monitor project and event timelines, ensuring deliverables are on time and within budget. Survey stakeholders, analyze engagement metrics, and identify trends to improve engagement and collaboration efforts. Develop an annual assessment of NCICS’ impact through engagement activities.

title: Technology Support Analyst
description: This position is expected to possess solid technical knowledge and proficiency, a strong commitment to improvement and teamwork, good follow-up and communication skills, and professional respect for all clients, team members and partners. The Technology Support Analyst is an integral team member within the Service Desk. Our clients are working primarily with people in this role so a service-minded approach is essential. Our Technical Support Analysts are the public face of our division and have the ability to shape the positive perception of our clients. This responsibility is an important part of our service. This candidate is expected to: Communicate effectively with clients of varying technical knowledge, addressing their needs and concerns. Utilize strong time management skills to prioritize competing support incidents, tasks and projects in compliance with Standard Operating Procedures. Exhibit a team-centric mindset by sharing ideas, information, feedback and support to others. Maintain demeanor and diplomacy in times of high volume or difficult situations. Provide Tier 1 onsite support to clients at assigned location. Assist other Tier 1 staff with remote support to clients at all locations. Methodically troubleshoot issues regarding network connectivity, hardware and software, and audio visual equipment while using all available resources to independently solve problems. Configure, maintain and organize device endpoints, security settings, and software via Active Directory, Group Policies, Microsoft Endpoint Configuration Manager and Jamf. Manage the health of computer lab inventory including desktop machines, large-format printers, and other peripherals. Act as Project Manager or Project Team Member for client-facing and technical improvement projects, leveraging assistance from team members, partners, and vendors for successful completion. Create and maintain detailed documentation in its proper location including ServiceNow ticketing system, Google Docs, Google Sheets, or Knowledge Base portals. Assist in the training and mentorship of Tier 1 staff, including Student Technicians. Other duties as assigned by the Service Desk Manager.

title: HVAC Technician
description: Join NC State University’s Building Maintenance and Operations (BMO) Department as an advanced HVAC Technician and play an important role in keeping the university’s buildings safe, comfortable, efficient, and operational. This position is responsible for the advanced operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, and installation of HVAC/R control systems and related mechanical systems across a large university environment. The role works with sophisticated building systems and equipment, including HVAC/R equipment, hydronic systems, electrical and electronic controls, plumbing and piping systems, and other building infrastructure. As an experienced trades professional, you will apply expertise across HVAC/R, electrical, and plumbing/pipefitting systems while using strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills to identify issues and develop effective solutions. You will also have opportunities to serve as a team leader or technical trainer, share knowledge with other trades professionals, and provide guidance on complex repairs and building operating systems. Ready to bring your technical expertise to NC State? Apply today and become part of the Building Maintenance and Operations team. Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Lead team projects and provide technical guidance to coworkers, serving as a team leader, technical trainer, or acting in a supervisory capacity when needed. Assign work orders and coordinate daily work activities to support maintenance and operational priorities. Maintain, troubleshoot, repair, install, and operate HVAC/R equipment, systems, controls, components, and related auxiliary equipment within a large university environment. Perform advanced-level maintenance and repairs across HVAC/R, electrical, and plumbing/pipefitting systems, with HVAC/R serving as the primary trade. Service air conditioning equipment, refrigerant and air compressors, chilled water, steam and hot water systems, pumps, valves, actuators, VAV boxes, variable frequency drives, pressure-reducing valves, and exhaust systems. Troubleshoot and maintain pneumatic, electrical, and electronic control systems and associated building automation technologies. Inspect, maintain, and repair electrical systems, equipment, components, and lighting systems operating at voltages up to 600 VAC. Maintain and repair potable and non-potable water systems, sanitary waste and vent systems, specialty plumbing and drainage systems, and piping systems of various sizes and materials. Research emerging building technologies, operating procedures, and system configurations to support effective maintenance and operation of advanced building systems. Analyze complex maintenance and operational issues, gather relevant information, evaluate alternatives, and develop timely, practical solutions. Train coworkers on advanced maintenance techniques, troubleshooting methods, building operating systems, and procedures across multiple trades. Cross-train team members on applicable HVAC/R, electrical, plumbing/pipefitting, controls, and building operating systems to strengthen team capabilities. Order materials and supplies needed to complete assigned work and support maintenance operations. Complete required administrative documentation and other operational tasks associated with assigned work. Perform tasks requiring standing for extended periods, working in confined spaces, and utilizing various tools. Safely climb and work from different types of ladders to access elevated or below-grade areas (such as roofs, above-ceiling spaces, and utility pits). Be exposed to and work in areas where insects or small animals are occasionally present. All essential tasks must be performed with or without reasonable accommodations. Lift materials and equipment weighing up to 30 pounds frequently and up to 60 pounds occasionally, with or without reasonable accommodation. Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follows verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs.

title: Environmental Services Technician I
description: Are you looking for a fulfilling career where you can make a tangible difference in creating a clean and welcoming environment? We are seeking a passionate, detail-oriented Environmental Services Technician to join our exceptional Environmental Services team in NC State’s Facilities Division . In this vital role, you will help maintain over 10 million square feet of campus space, ensuring a safe and inviting atmosphere for students, staff, and visitors. With support from a dynamic team of over 320 professionals, you’ll grow your skills, take pride in your work, and contribute to our vibrant campus community. Join us and be a part of a team that takes pride in delivering exceptional service to one of the most prestigious campuses in the region. Apply today and help us keep NC State shining bright! Working Hours: 4:00 am – 12:30 pm, Monday - Friday Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Clean and sanitize designated areas using standard cleaning assignments to maintain a safe and hygienic environment Report any discrepancies, damages, or maintenance needs within buildings and promptly respond to emergencies and inclement weather Operate housekeeping equipment such as vacuums, mops, and scrubbers to complete tasks like dusting, disinfecting, and replenishing supplies Periodically strip and refinish floors, shampoo and extract carpets, and perform pressure washing of entrances, exterior walls, and windows Remove and manage recycling from centralized indoor recycling sites Assist with window washing and other seasonal cleaning tasks as needed Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follow verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs. Perform lifting duties up to 30 pounds frequently and 60 pounds occasionally, with or without reasonable accommodations, and perform physical tasks such as grasping, pushing, and pulling cleaning equipment; reaching overhead; bending, squatting, climbing, and maintaining balance.

title: Administrative Assistant
description: NC State University’s Utilities and Engineering Services unit plays a vital role in keeping campus operations running by producing and distributing steam, chilled water, electricity, and potable water, while maintaining stormwater and sanitary sewer systems across three campuses. The unit also supports energy management, fuel procurement, and campus outreach initiatives. We are seeking an organized, proactive, and service-oriented Administrative Assistant to provide essential administrative and operational support to the Utilities team. In this role, you will work closely with the Unit Director, Engineering Managers, supervisors, and staff to coordinate daily operations, support recruitment and onboarding, manage employee programs, maintain records, and facilitate communication across the unit. You will also help coordinate special projects, events, and office improvements that support team effectiveness. If you enjoy keeping operations organized, supporting people, and contributing to the work that keeps a university running, we encourage you to apply and become part of the NC State Facilities team! Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Provide administrative support to the Utilities Unit Director, Engineering Managers, supervisors, and staff to support daily operations. Manage scheduling and communications by maintaining the Director’s calendar, coordinating training room reservations, answering calls, and distributing messages. Coordinate employee services by scheduling required medical exams, processing office supply requests, and maintaining administrative records. Dispatch urgent work requests by coordinating emergency AiM work orders with the appropriate Utilities personnel. Prepare and review documents by drafting correspondence, proofreading annual energy reports and building audit reports, and preparing other reports as needed. Administer leave and timekeeping processes by reviewing leave requests and processing monthly timesheets for the Utilities Engineering unit. Coordinate recruitment and onboarding by scheduling interviews, processing hiring documentation, and preparing new employee packets. Manage the new employee mentoring program to support onboarding, engagement, and employee development. Oversee the employee uniform program by coordinating requests, distribution, and related administrative activities. Coordinate special projects and events by supporting unit activities, office renovations, and other projects as needed.

title: Payroll Processing Manager
description: Reporting to the Payroll Director within the University Controller’s Office, you will oversee university payroll processing and lead a team of four payroll specialists to ensure accurate, timely, and compliant payroll operations. You will exercise independent judgment in managing payroll processes, interpreting complex regulations, administering payroll systems, and resolving issues that affect employees and departments across the university. You will guide daily operations, strengthen internal controls, oversee system updates and audits, and collaborate with campus partners and central offices to address complex payroll matters. Through staff leadership, sound decision-making, and continuous process improvement, you will support reliable payroll services and the university’s financial and administrative operations. Key Responsibilities: Program Supervision and Administration Lead, train, supervise, and develop a team of four payroll specialists by assigning work, establishing performance expectations, providing technical guidance, and managing performance and employee relations matters. Monitor service quality and workload, address operational challenges, and support staff in maintaining consistent and timely service delivery. Oversee daily payroll processing, resolve routine and complex issues, and review payroll transactions, financial documents, reports, and records for accuracy and compliance. Maintain current operational documentation, training resources, website content, procedures, and guidance materials. Communication and Campus Relations Interpret and communicate payroll policies, procedures, regulations, and deadlines to employees, departments, and campus partners, providing guidance for complex or unique situations. Respond to employee and campus inquiries through established service channels, including HRNow and email. Explain complex legal and regulatory requirements, including garnishments and levies, to non-payroll stakeholders. Build and maintain effective working relationships with campus units and central offices to support coordinated payroll operations. Payroll Compliance and Systems Administration Apply federal and state regulations, university policies, and applicable statutes to ensure payroll activities meet compliance requirements. Serve as the functional administrator for payroll processing systems, identify system and operational issues, test updates before implementation, and coordinate post-payroll audits. Evaluate internal controls, system reliability, and operational procedures to identify risks and improve payroll accuracy and efficiency. Contribute to strategic planning and the ongoing improvement of university payroll operations. Critical Thinking and Problem Resolution Analyze and resolve complex, unusual, and escalated payroll matters using sound judgment and interpretation of applicable regulations and policies. Identify potential payroll processing issues, assess operational risks, and implement corrective actions to maintain accurate and timely payroll services. Implement policy updates, internal controls, and procedural changes to strengthen compliance and reduce operational risk. Change Management and Process Improvement Coordinate and validate payroll system enhancements, software updates, and process changes in collaboration with central offices and cross-functional teams. Establish and implement unit goals and operational objectives that support university priorities. Identify opportunities to improve processes, encourage innovation, and guide staff through evolving operational and institutional requirements. If you are a payroll professional who enjoys leading a team, interpreting complex regulations, solving challenging operational issues, and improving systems and processes, we welcome you to apply for the Payroll Manager position and help support accurate, reliable payroll services at NC State University. Work schedule and location: Monday - Friday, 8:00 am - 5:00 pm (This position is eligible for a flexible work arrangement to include hybrid remote work).

title: Facilities Maintenance Technician- Journey
description: Join our dedicated Building Maintenance and Operations team as a Facilities Maintenance Technician and play a vital role in keeping our campus systems running safely, efficiently, and reliably. In this position, you’ll use your technical expertise to maintain, repair, and install a wide range of building systems, including HVACR, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical equipment. The ideal candidate is a skilled problem-solver with strong attention to detail and a commitment to safety and service excellence. You’ll have the opportunity to work in a dynamic environment where no two days are the same, ensuring our facilities remain comfortable, functional, and well-maintained for the entire campus community. If you take pride in hands-on work, enjoy troubleshooting complex systems, and thrive in a collaborative team environment, we invite you to apply and become part of our team that keeps the campus running smoothly every day. K ey responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Maintain, repair, and install HVACR systems , including air conditioning, refrigeration, and heating equipment Diagnose, troubleshoot, and repair steam/hot water boilers and auxiliary equipment, such as pumps, condensate receivers, steam lines, pressure-reducing stations, air compressors, and water softeners Perform preventive maintenance per manufacturer guidelines on refrigeration and air conditioning equipment Conduct electrical work up to 600 VAC, including installation, maintenance, and repair of electrical panels, breakers, switchgear, magnetic starters, disconnects, motors, and lighting systems Troubleshoot and repair control systems , including temperature controls, regulators, humidity controllers, sensors, pneumatic control valves, and regulators Install and maintain plumbing systems , including cutting, threading, assembling, and installing pipes, valves, and fixtures for gas, water, and sanitation systems Perform pipefitting and insulation work related to steam and water distribution systems Ensure compliance with safety standards and best practices while performing all duties Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follow verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs Perform lifting duties up to 60 pounds frequently and 90 pounds occasionally, with or without reasonable accommodations Perform tasks requiring standing for extended periods, working in confined spaces, and utilizing various tools. Safely climb and work from different types of ladders to access elevated or below-grade areas (such as roofs, above-ceiling spaces, and utility pits). Be exposed to and work in areas where insects or small animals are occasionally present. All essential tasks must be performed with or without reasonable accommodations

title: Facilities Invoice Coordinator
description: The Facilities Invoice Coordinator plays a critical role in keeping NC State Facilities’ financial operations accurate, efficient, and moving forward. This position manages the end-to-end invoice process, ensuring payments are accurately reviewed, properly documented, and processed in accordance with university policies, state procurement requirements, and accounting standards. Working across Budget and Accounting, Capital, Purchasing, Contracts, Finance, and Sponsored Programs, the Invoice Coordinator serves as a central point of coordination for invoice processing and payment inquiries. The position reviews invoices and purchase orders, monitors the invoice status dashboard, resolves payment issues, maintains accurate financial records, and helps ensure invoices are processed within established deadlines. This role offers an opportunity to make a meaningful operational impact by reducing payment delays, minimizing errors, strengthening financial accountability, and identifying opportunities to improve systems and processes. The successful candidate will bring strong attention to detail, sound judgment, organization, and the ability to independently manage a high-volume workload while collaborating effectively across departments. If you are an organized financial professional who enjoys solving problems, improving processes, and keeping complex operations running smoothly, we invite you to apply and join the NC State Facilities team. Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Independently receive, review, and process invoices from vendors and internal university customers, ensuring transactions are accurate, complete, and properly documented. Verify invoices against purchase orders, confirming amounts, applicable documentation, and available funds before payment processing. Identify insufficient purchase order balances and coordinate change orders to ensure adequate funding is available for invoice payment. Validate vendor documentation in PaymentWorks and resolve discrepancies that could delay payment. Upload and route invoices through NC State’s financial and work order systems in accordance with established procedures and deadlines. Monitor and maintain the Facilities Invoice Status Dashboard , identifying discrepancies and updating invoice statuses to support accurate tracking and accountability. Coordinate with internal departments, vendors, Purchasing, Contracts, Finance, Sponsored Programs, and other stakeholders to resolve invoice and payment issues. Review purchase order requests to confirm required documentation and contract information are complete and support appropriate financial processing. Monitor invoice processing timelines and support compliance with the University’s Net 30 payment requirement. Support month-end close activities by identifying outstanding invoices and forecasting their potential impact on Facilities budget performance. Maintain accurate and organized invoice, payment, and accounting records to support financial reporting and audit requirements. Ensure invoice and payment activities comply with applicable state procurement laws, university policies, accounting standards, and internal financial controls. Prepare reports and metrics related to invoice volume, routing, processing timelines, payment activity, and vendor activity for leadership review. Identify opportunities to improve invoice processing, tracking, communication, and financial systems, and support the implementation of process improvements. Provide guidance and training to staff on invoice submission procedures, documentation requirements, and applicable financial policies. Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follow verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs.

title: Associate Director, Donor Services
description: The Associate Director of Donor Services will oversee the endowment reporting and naming‑opportunity processes and, in partnership with Advancement Information and Technology, improve projects to enhance the donor experience and increase operational efficiency within Donor Services. The ideal candidate will possess exceptional writing, detail‑oriented editing and copyediting skills, along with a comprehensive understanding of endowments and endowment reporting. The position requires demonstrated experience in data analysis and quality control, including reviewing, interpreting and validating large, complex datasets. The successful candidate must be highly organized and capable of managing multiple, simultaneous, detail‑oriented responsibilities while collaborating effectively with frontline fundraising professionals and other campus partners. Key responsibilities include: Managing the preparation and distribution of annual endowment reports detailing corpus values, market values, investment performance and spending distributions. Analyzing financial and endowment data and ensuring the accuracy, quality and consistency of reporting. Overseeing the editing and quality‑control review of endowment reports. Collaborating with campus partners throughout the review and approval process for naming opportunities. Evaluating facilities and other spaces, programs and positions to recommend appropriate gift minimums for naming opportunities. Touring existing spaces and spaces under construction and recommending appropriate naming spaces to the respective colleges and units. Leading the preparation, review and coordination of naming materials for consideration by the Board of Trustees. Identifying and leading technology and process‑improvement initiatives that strengthen operations and enhance the donor experience. Building productive working relationships with frontline fundraising professionals, facilities personnel, financial partners and other university stakeholders. Providing strategic leadership, supervision, coaching and professional development for a small team of specialized staff responsible for the naming‑opportunities process, managing technology systems and data processes for Donor Services, and managing the endowment reporting process.

title: Open Rank - Assistant/Associate/Professor
description: The Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at North Carolina State University invites applications for multiple tenured or tenure track faculty positions at the rank of Assistant/Associate/Full Professor with particular interest in aerostructures, manufacturing, and engineering design disciplines. Aerostructures: Including but not limited to: 1) structures for space platforms; 2) fluid and/or thermal structure interactions, aerothermoelasticity, nonlinear structural dynamics and multiphysics phenomena as it relates to aerostructures; 3) physical reservoir computing and concepts relating to mechanically embodied intelligence for aerospace applications; and 4) advanced multifunctional structures for aerospace applications. Advanced Manufacturing for aerospace, mechanical, and marine applications: Including but not limited to: 1) modeling and simulations of manufacturing processes for innovation and scale up; 2) rapid and advanced manufacturing of hot structures and extreme-environment components, including space manufacturing; 3) multiphysics modeling, sensing, and process monitoring to inform manufacturing decisions; 4) AI/ML-enabled, intelligent, and autonomous manufacturing, including digital twins and advanced process control; and 5) quantum manufacturing paradigms, including quantum-enabled manufacturing and other transformative manufacturing technologies. Complex System Design for aerospace, mechanical, and marine applications, exploring how advanced computational tools can change the way systems are conceived, optimized, and manufactured . Including but not limited to: 1) Human-AI collaboration and co-teaming; 2) multidisciplinary optimization tools to synchronize design and digital manufacturing; 3) design decision-making under uncertainty; and 4) the strategic management of change to create resilient systems.

title: Semiconductor Research Engineer
description: NC State’s Nanofabrication Facility (NNF) is seeking a skilled and motivated Semiconductor Research Engineer to support the performance, reliability, and safe operation of its advanced fabrication equipment and processes. In this role, you will help maintain critical cleanroom infrastructure, troubleshoot complex equipment issues, optimize semiconductor fabrication processes, and support researchers in achieving their technical goals. Working closely with facility staff, equipment vendors, and research users, you will play an essential role in maintaining reliable operations, advancing process capabilities, and providing a safe, efficient environment for semiconductor research. Key Responsibilities: Equipment Maintenance, Troubleshooting, and Repair Perform preventive maintenance on semiconductor fabrication equipment to minimize downtime and maintain reliable cleanroom operations. Diagnose and resolve electrical, mechanical, and process-related equipment issues to restore functionality and support consistent performance. Coordinate with hardware engineers, technicians, and external service vendors to complete equipment repairs and routine maintenance. Schedule and oversee vendor service visits, major equipment repairs, and maintenance agreements. Process Development and Optimization Develop, test, characterize, and document standard fabrication processes for core semiconductor equipment, including photolithography, dry etching, and thin-film metal deposition. Evaluate process results against established quality standards and technical specifications to maintain consistent, repeatable outcomes. Partner with internal and remote research users to develop, refine, and implement custom fabrication processes that meet project requirements. User Training and Technical Support Deliver hands-on training to internal and remote users on semiconductor fabrication tools, preparing them to operate equipment independently and safely. Instruct users on equipment operating procedures, cleanroom protocols, and applicable safety requirements. Provide ongoing technical guidance and operational support to help users troubleshoot challenges and complete fabrication activities successfully. Cleanroom Operations and Administrative Support Work regularly in the cleanroom while following required gowning procedures, safety protocols, and facility operating standards. Maintain accurate process logs, baseline data, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and equipment performance records. Track inventory levels for cleanroom consumables, chemicals, and equipment spare parts to support uninterrupted facility operations. This role offers the opportunity to apply your engineering expertise, solve technical challenges, and work directly with researchers to support innovative projects. If you enjoy hands-on problem-solving, equipment optimization, and helping others succeed in a highly technical environment, we encourage you to apply.

title: Lifeguard
description: A Lifeguard is a trained and certified safety professional responsible for ensuring the safety and protection of people in and around an aquatic environment. In this role, you will ensure the safety of all users through continuous surveillance of the aquatic area. You will enforce aquatic guidelines to maintain a safe environment and be prepared to implement the Emergency Action Plan when necessary. Join our pack! Contribute Safety and Surveillance: Ensure the safety of users through continuous surveillance. Facility Inspection & Maintenance: Inspect the facility, perform preventative maintenance and report any unsafe conditions or equipment failures. Chemical Testing: Perform regular water chemistry tests and accurately log the readings to maintain water quality and compliance. Event Operations: Assist with the setup and teardown of equipment for various aquatic programs, special events and open recreation activities. Certification and Fitness: Maintain an up-to-date American Red Cross Lifeguard Certification and preserve the required fitness level (swimming skills, strength and endurance) necessary to effectively respond to all aquatic emergencies. Cleanliness: Maintain a clean and inviting aquatic environment.

title: Senior International Student & Scholar Advisor
description: As a Senior International Student and Scholar Advisor, you will provide immigration advice and support to international students and scholars while helping advance the Office of International Services (OIS) policies, processes, and programs. In addition to managing a substantial caseload, you will mentor colleagues, possibly supervise a graduate assistant or International Student and Scholar Advisor, lead process improvements, deliver campus training, and support the implementation of regulatory changes. Key Responsibilities: International Student and Scholar Advising Independently manage complex advising and immigration processes for F-1 and J-1 students and scholars, including sponsored students, exchange participants, Intensive English Program students, J-1 Student Interns, 3+2 programs, and other nontraditional populations. Process and issue visa documents; manage program extensions, changes in academic level or curriculum, transfers, amendments, employment benefits, dependent documentation, travel, changes of status, reinstatements, and related immigration matters. Monitor federal immigration regulations and procedural changes from USCIS, SEVP, ICE, the Department of State, and other relevant agencies. Serve as a subject-matter expert and lead trainer for faculty, advisors, and university partners on international student and scholar processes. Support staff onboarding and professional development. Serve as the OIS liaison for assigned colleges and their students, scholars, interns, faculty, and staff. Communicate immigration policies and procedures to students, advising colleagues, and campus partners. Participate in rotating weekly drop-in advising and scholar check-in services. Process Improvement and Training Leadership Own and maintain key OIS processes, including Optional Practical Training (OPT), Curricular Practical Training (CPT), initial scholar requests, and admissions liaison procedures. Coordinate process communications and outreach, update OIS website content and training resources, and maintain the internal OIS Advisor Manual. Lead recurring projects and programs that strengthen international student and scholar retention and success. Develop and deliver training for OIS colleagues and university faculty and staff, communicating policy updates and promoting effective support for international students and scholars. You will also Contribute to OIS staff meetings, policy discussions, case reviews, professional development activities, workshops, and university committees. Maintain accurate and current OIS policies, procedures, and related website content. Pursue ongoing professional and regulatory training through NAFSA, NCAIE, and other relevant professional organizations. Assist with front desk coverage, phone calls, and the OIS inbox as needed. Support additional projects and initiatives as assigned. Join the Office of International Services at NC State University and play a key role in supporting the success of international students and scholars. This position offers the opportunity to apply your immigration expertise, mentor colleagues, strengthen university partnerships, and lead process improvements that enhance service delivery and ensure compliance with evolving regulations.

title: Rental Coordinator Assistant - JC Raulston Arboretum
description: The JC Raulston Arboretum is seeking to fill our Rental Coordinator Assistant position. The ideal candidate to fill this position should be an active, confident, and detail-oriented team member to assist with our rental and events team. Strong attention to detail, adaptability, and a positive attitude are essentials. The desired candidate is tech-savvy but also teachable. If your notes are color-coded, you love helping people have a great time, and you seek new and efficient ways to accomplish tasks then this is the position for you! The position will be responsible for, but not limited to: Supporting the Rental Coordinator in all details necessary to facilitate and organize rental clients, their needs and requests Creating and/or facilitating room/garden layouts Collecting required information for rental requirements through scheduled communications Serving as visitor services mentor to support rental staff, students, and volunteers Creating a positive guest experience; implementing JCRA visitation policies and guidelines Guest/Client communications either phone/email/face-to-face Assisting team in guest experience improvements Supporting front desk and visitor center volunteers Managing incoming questions (emails and calls) Assist with annual fundraising events and programs such as Moonlight in the Garden, Raulston Blooms, Southeastern Plant Symposium, etc. (will include nights and weekends as needed for event facilitation) ○ Assist with coordinating event logistics ○ Assist with event planning ○ Assist with event facilitation Helping create event and rental promotional content Supporting ticket sales and promotion Supporting Rental Coordinator in all details necessary to book and execute a successful rental experience/event. ○ Communicating professionally with rental clients ○ Scheduling and assisting with site visits ○ Assessing client needs and requests to assure JCRA is a proper fit ○ Providing onsite support to ensure a positive experience Creating and/or facilitating room/garden layouts for rental clients using relevant data collected from database, clients & rental coordinator ○ Setting up gardens/rooms to approved layouts of rental clients Collecting required information for rental requirements through scheduled communications Customer/Guest Services Mentor to supporting rental staff, students and volunteers General administrative support of the Arboretum Opening and closing buildings and gardens Assist with keeping equipment, buildings and gardens presentable and functional ○ Submit facilities work order requests Helping safeguard Arboretum plant collection from damage during rentals and events Knowledge of rental policies/guidelines Implementing Arboretum visitation policies/guidelines

title: Facility Assistant
description: A Facility Assistant maintains a growth mindset, cares and takes initiative. In this role, you will manage the equipment room; maintain the cleanliness and aesthetics of all fitness, open recreation, and general facility spaces; set up activities and rooms; report maintenance and housekeeping issues; provide premier customer service; and promote a safe, clean facility. Join our pack! Contribute Safety: Ensure user safety through supervision, procedure, and guideline enforcement, and accident response. Customer Service: Develop knowledge about facilities and equipment to provide premier customer service. Cleaning and General Facility Operations: Clean, organize, and maintain equipment and spaces. Equipment Room: Oversee the equipment desk, handle check-out and check-in for recreational equipment, towels, and apparel; perform laundry duties; and manage lost and found items. Open Recreation and Setups: Supervise open recreation sports activities and spaces. Cleanliness: Maintain the cleanliness of equipment and facility.

title: Event Supervisor
description: A Sports Programs Events Supervisor is the primary point of contact for event execution, proactively directing activities, and ensuring a safe, supervised environment. In this role, you will provide support for external and student group events, oversee the successful management of facility reservations, and maintain effective operations during all evening and weekend shifts. Join our pack! Contribute Event & Facility Operations: Set up and break down equipment for events and vendors. Reporting: Stay up to date with event logistics and inform professional staff of shift details. Participant Education: Provide participants and visitors with correct information about events and the facility. Conflict Management: Manage participants and visitors behaviors and mediate conflict. Emergency Response: Proactively assess and respond to potential risks to prevent harm to participants or staff. Provide initial care and coordinate a professional response to injuries. Cleanliness: Maintain the cleanliness of equipment and facility.

title: Payables Manager
description: As the Payables Manager, you will lead accounts payable operations for NC State University, overseeing purchase order invoice processing, foreign currency payments, and payment disbursements. Reporting to the Assistant Controller, you will supervise and develop the payables team, ensure accurate and timely payment processing, resolve complex accounting issues, and support compliance with university and state requirements. You will also drive process improvements, coordinate financial system enhancements, and serve as a key resource for campus partners and suppliers. Key Responsibilities Accounts Payable Operations and Financial Reporting Oversee payment file verification, approval, and release through Wells Fargo and PaymentWorks, and assist with daily reconciliation of the Cash Requisition Report. Support fiscal year-end close, reporting, and quarterly duplicate payment reports. Research and resolve duplicate payment claims identified through the State Controller’s Office annual audit, coordinating with vendors and the State to recover funds through the NCFS system. Use financial data and technical information to support departmental and university goals, procedures, and compliance requirements. Team Leadership and Program Administration Manage the daily operations of five payables specialists and one payables accountant, including hiring, training, supervision, and ongoing guidance. Monitor service quality and productivity, address resource constraints, and support staff in delivering timely and accurate services. Oversee accounting processes, resolve complex operational issues, and maintain current resources, including websites, training materials, and desktop guides. Financial Systems and Process Improvement Identify opportunities to improve accounts payable processes, address operational bottlenecks, and develop training to support process changes. Coordinate with campus partners to recommend and implement modifications to existing financial systems and accounts payable procedures. Review system specifications, coordinate enhancements to the Financial System’s Accounts Payable module, and recommend improvements. Lead software testing in collaboration with the Systems team and campus partners to identify, track, and resolve defects and inconsistencies. Communication and Issue Resolution Troubleshoot financial system issues, determine corrective actions, and proactively address potential problems. Interpret and communicate policies, procedures, and guidelines to campus personnel, providing recommendations for unique college or departmental situations. Respond to campus and supplier inquiries and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to resolve payment and accounting issues. If you are a collaborative accounting professional who enjoys leading a team, solving complex problems, and improving financial processes, we welcome you to apply for the Payables Manager position at NC State University.

title: Registered Nurse
description: The Campus Health 12 month Professional Nurse rotates to the Medical Clinic, Treatment Clinic Services, Centennial Campus or Gynecology Services and is responsible for assessing patients, implementing treatment plans, and evaluating the patient’s response to treatment and care. This position is a member of the infection control team and oversees the autoclave and instrument processing in GYN services. Duties include but are not limited to: Administering IV fluid. Administering immunizations in compliance with state and university regulations. Working independently, utilizing standing orders. Assisting providers with procedures. Triaging patients. Instrument processing utilizing steam sterilization and other infection control duties as assigned. Documenting accurately in the electronic health record. Performing wound care. The position requires the ability to lift up to 35 pounds, stand for long periods of time, and bend to perform duties standard in providing health care. If you are a compassionate nursing professional who enjoys providing high-quality patient care, collaborating with a multidisciplinary team, and supporting a healthy campus community, we encourage you to apply and join the Campus Health team.

title: Executive Assistant
description: Are you an organized and detail-oriented individual who thrives in a fast-paced academic environment? We are seeking a dynamic and proactive Executive Assistant to join our team and support the Department Head in managing day-to-day administrative operations and initiatives. As the primary administrative contact for the Department Head, you will play a critical role in facilitating seamless communication and coordination within the department, college, and with external stakeholders. This is an on-campus role, hybrid or remote arrangements are not available. Key responsibilities of this position are as follows: Planning, Workflow Organization, and Alignment with Departmental Priorities Coordinate executive operations by managing complex calendars, scheduling meetings, reserving rooms, arranging travel, monitoring correspondence, coordinating signature and approval workflows, and ensuring departmental priorities remain on track. Support the Department Head with travel arrangements, email and calendar management, and scheduling. Responsible for planning and implementing both on-campus and off-campus meetings and events as required by the Department Head and the Associate Department Head. Coordinate logistics, preparation, recording attendance, and final meeting summary for monthly faculty and staff department meetings. Responsible for maintaining and updating a tracking system for administrative responsibilities of the Department Head; includes anticipating needs and alerting the Department Head to upcoming tasks and deadlines. Serve as the primary administrative support for the faculty search committee. Coordinate all faculty candidate interview scheduling, room reservations, reference letter requests, faculty feedback requests, status update presentations, travel arrangements, and reimbursements. Work with faculty members as needed on planned seminars and faculty interviews, including coordination of visit schedules with many participants in the department, college, or beyond. Track and monitor pending issues and action items for follow-up and completion. Develop productive and collaborative work relationships to coordinate initiatives of the Department head across organizational areas (as well as external entities) to raise the quality, visibility, and/or reputation of the department. Foster a collaborative departmental culture with departmental personnel (as well as external entities) by listening, understanding, and responding to apparent and underlying needs, resolving problems, and continually seeking to provide the highest quality service. Support Faculty Advancement Coordinate and manage the Reappointment, Promotion and Tenure (RPT) and the Post-Tenure Review (PTR) process for the department. Work with faculty members, departmental voting faculty, and Department Head on preparation of materials for promotion and tenure review, post-tenure review, and annual review of all faculty. Develop a thorough understanding of faculty promotion policies, as well as the NCSU systems used to manage and document promotion-related activities. Stay current with updates and changes to policies and system functionality. Continuously monitor faculty timelines to track eligibility, submission deadlines, and review various stages of the promotion and tenure review process. Correspondence and Communications Assist with developing executive communications by preparing correspondence, presentations, reports, briefing materials, agendas, meeting minutes, and recommendations that support informed decision-making and strategic leadership. Process non-routine requests and/or assignments as made by the Dean, faculty members, and external sources for the Department Head to participate. Coordinate and compile department reports for key alumni donors to aid in engagement and fundraising. Have awareness of policies/procedures and strategic plans of the department in drafting concise and specific memoranda to different audiences, and in supporting initiatives of the department. This position is open only for current NC State Employees, permanent or temporary.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor
description: The Department of Management, Innovation, and Entrepreneurship (MIE) in the Poole College of Management at North Carolina State University invites applications for a tenure-track, open-rank Assistant or Associate Professor in Organizational Behavior or Strategic Human Resource Management , with an anticipated start date of August 2027. Position Responsibilities The successful candidate will be expected to: Develop and maintain a high-quality, impactful research program resulting in publications in leading peer-reviewed journals. Deliver high-quality instruction in Organizational Behavior, Strategic Human Resource Management, and/or related areas at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Contribute to the academic mission of the department, college, and university through service and professional engagement. Collaborate effectively with faculty and contribute to a collegial, intellectually engaging, and interdisciplinary academic environment. Engage with students, faculty, and other stakeholders in ways that advance the teaching, research, and service missions of the department. Candidates should demonstrate a strong record of, or clear potential for, scholarly excellence in Organizational Behavior, Strategic Human Resource Management, or closely related areas. Candidates considered at the Associate Professor level should have an established record of high-quality scholarship, effective teaching, and academic or professional service commensurate with rank. This position offers an opportunity to join an engaged academic community within the MIE Department and Poole College of Management, advance impactful research, and contribute to the education and development of future business leaders. Faculty rank and compensation will be determined based on the successful candidate’s qualifications, experience, and scholarly record.

title: Career Counselor
description: The Career Counselor provides comprehensive career development services tailored to undergraduate and graduate students within the College of Humanities & Social Sciences (CHASS), while also providing career counseling to Exploratory Studies students and other student populations across the university as needed. As an integral member of the Career Development Center career education team, this position delivers individual and group career counseling, facilitates tailored workshops, coordinates major college career events, and collaborates with campus partners to prepare students for professional success. The position also supports daily center operations, campus-wide initiatives, and the supervision of student personnel. Duties include but are not limited to: Direct Career Education & Counseling Provide individual and group career counseling to undergraduate and graduate CHASS as well as Exploratory Studies students, covering topics such as career exploration, resume and cover letter development, interview preparation, and job/internship search strategies. Provide in-person and drop-in career counseling to other student populations across the university as needed or assigned to support center-wide coverage and service demands. Facilitate topical workshops (e.g., resume reviews, mock interviews, networking) for general student audiences and multi-disciplinary campus groups. Guide students across all disciplines in navigating and utilizing the university’s recruiting and job database system (ePACK). Assist students in leveraging university-wide resources to transition successfully into professional careers. College Partnerships & Event Coordination Plan, coordinate, and execute the annual College of Humanities & Social Sciences Career Fair, collaborating with the employer relations team to maximize employer participation. Develop and deliver preparatory workshops and marketing strategies to maximize student engagement and readiness for career events. Build and maintain collaborative partnerships with CHASS faculty, academic advisors, and department heads to integrate career development into academic programs. Serve as a primary resource for faculty and advisors on career decision-making strategies and industry trends relevant to humanities and social sciences disciplines. Technology & Campus Outreach Conduct training sessions for university students, faculty, and staff on effective utilization of the ePACK database system. Maintain active proficiency and technical expertise in ePACK and related career technologies. Represent the Career Development Center at university orientations, open houses, and campus-wide outreach events. Develop and deliver customized career presentations for campus student organizations, residence halls, and academic classes. Graduate Student Supervision & Operational Support Under the direction of the Associate Director for Career Education, recruit, train, and supervise graduate student workers supporting center operations. Meet regularly with graduate student workers to provide guidance,review work progress, address questions, and support their professional development. Support general daily operations and administrative functions of the Career Development Center.

title: Seafood Business & Market Development Specialist
description: As the Seafood Business & Market Development Specialist, you will serve as a trusted business and market development resource for North Carolina’s seafood industry, advising aquaculture growers, commercial fishers, processors, wholesalers, retailers, and other industry partners. You will translate business, market, and economic information into practical guidance that helps seafood businesses grow, diversify, strengthen supply chains, and respond to changing market conditions. Your work will connect people, products, markets, and resources to strengthen North Carolina’s seafood economy. Whether helping a grower identify a new market, a retailer connect consumers with local seafood, or an industry partner navigate distribution challenges, you will turn knowledge into action that supports resilient businesses and expands opportunities for North Carolina seafood. Key Responsibilities: Business & Market Development: Advise seafood businesses on planning, growth, market opportunities, financial resources, and operating challenges. Strengthen supply chains and distribution while connecting North Carolina seafood with retail, restaurant, and other markets. Support diversification through direct-to-consumer sales, value-added products, and “blue tourism.” Use market trends and economic data to help businesses anticipate risks and respond to market shifts. Consumer & Market Outreach: Strengthen branding, traceability, and value propositions that differentiate locally harvested seafood. Leverage resources such as Mariner’s Menu to build consumer confidence and demand for local seafood. Partnerships & Strategic Initiatives: Collaborate with Sea Grant, Cooperative Extension, researchers, industry, and state and federal agencies to advance seafood priorities. Support initiatives such as the NC Shellfish Mariculture Strategic Plan and engage with the National Sea Grant network. Applied Research & Program Development: Develop proposals, pursue funding, and support research and extension projects from development through reporting and evaluation. Contribute to Sea Grant planning, interdisciplinary projects, grant reviews, and program initiatives. Education & Industry Readiness: Deliver training and develop practical resources on business fundamentals, market readiness, marketing, supply chains, and seafood safety. Track program reach, outcomes, and performance for NC Sea Grant and the National Sea Grant Office. If you enjoy turning ideas, information, and relationships into practical solutions, you’ll find opportunities to make a meaningful difference. Join NC Sea Grant to strengthen seafood businesses, connect local products with new markets, and turn knowledge into opportunities for coastal communities.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The FPAC LAB at North Carolina State University is seeking an early-career scientist to lead impurity powder injection for wall conditioning experiments and to develop a model-based controller for the impurity powder dropper (IPD) on the KSTAR tokamak. The position is part of the multi-institutional DOE Office of Science FES project that is led by Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory. As fusion devices transition to tungsten walls, real-time injection of low-Z powders offers a route to continuous wall conditioning without extended downtimes. The NC State scope is to deploy the IPD to integrate wall conditioning into high-performance plasma scenarios at KSTAR while minimizing the amount of injected impurity material. The successful candidate will complete the IPD feedback control loop and develop an AI-/model-based predictive controller for injection rates that can be transferred to future devices, and design control schemes for long-pulse real-time wall conditioning. The role involves close, sustained collaboration with the KSTAR team and with U.S. collaborators, including travel to Korea for experimental campaigns. The position is under the supervision of Dr. Florian Laggner and will be based at the Department of Nuclear Engineering in Raleigh, NC. Duties and Responsibilities include: Develop and deploy a real-time, model-based controller for impurity powder injection on the KSTAR tokamak. Design and test control schemes for real-time wall conditioning in long-pulse scenarios that minimize the injected material while maintaining compatibility with high performance plasma operation. Develop a predictive, AI-/machine-learning-based model of IPD injection rates and powder delivery, suitable for real-time control. Complete the IPD feedback control loop and integrate it with the KSTAR plasma control system. Plan, execute and analyze experiments at KSTAR. Prepare and run experiments during international campaigns. Coordinate technical work with collaborators at PPPL and the KSTAR team. Communicate research results. Create scientific peer-reviewed publications. Attend conferences with oral and poster presentations. Provide research progress reports. Mentor undergraduate and graduate students at NC State. Provide scientific direction, guidance and mentorship to students as a key member of the FPAC LAB.

title: Student Engagement and Support Specialist - Agricultural Business Management Program
description: In this role you will serve as the primary point of contact for Agricultural Business Management Undergraduate Programs (ABMUP) within the Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ARE), supporting both Agricultural Institute and baccalaureate students. Reporting to the Director of Undergraduate Programs (DUP), this position strengthens undergraduate advising operations, student engagement, professional development, and program assessment. In collaboration with the Director of Undergraduate Programs, you will coordinate student programs, events, communications, and administrative processes that enhance the undergraduate experience. Key Responsibilities: Student Engagement and Program Coordination Build relationships with ABM students across all four years and serve as a resource for program questions and engagement opportunities. Coordinate cohort advising logistics, including scheduling, participation tracking, rosters, and support for faculty and student leaders. Organize departmental intramural teams and support student leadership initiatives, including the Undergraduate Teaching Assistant program, competition teams, and ambassador program. Staff and coordinate student events, including orientation, registration bootcamps, the Industry Workshop Series, and graduation. Manage event logistics, including registration, facilities, materials, communications, and day-of execution; coordinate recurring student activities and the departmental scholarship process. Communications and Outreach Develop and distribute student communications, including newsletters, deadline reminders, event announcements, and registration guidance. Create and maintain program materials, including flyers, presentations, handouts, web content, and student engagement platform and social media updates. Support recruitment and program visibility efforts in collaboration with prospective students and campus partners. Registration and Advising Support Assist with registration processes, including enrollment tracking, course overrides, waitlists, and routine student inquiries. Maintain advising records, degree audit resources, and student data used for cohort assignments and outreach. Coordinate internship credit and experiential learning documentation in accordance with established program standards. Refer complex or non-routine student matters to the Director of Undergraduate Programs. Program Assessment and Development Develop and administer student surveys, summarize findings, and track participation and outcomes across engagement programs. Support undergraduate program assessment by collecting and organizing data for university reporting requirements. Draft grant applications for student programming funds and recommend new programs or events based on student feedback, participation trends, and assessment results. As Student Engagement and Support Specialist you will play an important role in connecting students with the resources, experiences, and opportunities that support their academic progress and professional growth. This position is ideal for an organized, proactive professional who enjoys coordinating programs, building relationships, and helping undergraduate students make the most of their experience at NC State.

title: Assistant Director, Goodnight Scholars Program (Programming)
description: The Goodnight Scholars Program is a comprehensive, full-ride scholarship program designed to develop scholars into leaders within the STEM and Education fields. The program currently serves up to 300 undergraduates and is growing to 400 by 2028. As part of this growth, the Goodnight Scholars Program is seeking a student-focused professional who is passionate about creating meaningful experiences that support student development, academic success, and community engagement. In this role, you will help shape the scholar experience through engaging programs, educational travel, leadership opportunities, and signature events. You will also advise students, mentor student leaders, and contribute to outreach and recruitment efforts that strengthen the program and support incoming scholars. Key Responsibilities: Plan, coordinate, and implement student development programs, educational activities, and major program events that enrich the scholar experience. Lead and plan the annual retreat for approximately 100 incoming scholars, supervising the retreat leader and assistant team in collaboration with the Assistant Director for Outreach and Selection. Support summer onboarding and first-year selection activities, including interview day. Advise students in the Goodnight Scholars Program and co-select, train, and mentor more than 20 student Program Ambassadors who support program activities and student engagement initiatives. Develop and lead educational travel opportunities that expand scholars’ learning experiences and complement their academic and personal development. Assist with teaching a first- or second-year seminar and support student learning through related educational programming. Help manage the program’s registration system in Slate and coordinate the organization, maintenance, and upkeep of the student lounge. Support program outreach, recruitment, and student selection efforts to engage prospective scholars and strengthen the incoming student experience. Represent the Goodnight Scholars Program on university committees and initiatives, collaborate with campus partners, and assist student-led affinity groups in coordinating activities and engagement opportunities. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the college experience of Goodnight Scholars by connecting students with opportunities to learn, lead, and build lasting relationships. If you enjoy developing engaging programs, mentoring student leaders, and coordinating experiences that help students thrive, we invite you to bring your skills and enthusiasm to the Goodnight Scholars Program.

title: Crafts Center Director
description: The Director of the Crafts Center at NC State University leads one of the largest university crafts centers in the United States. The Director reports to the Associate Dean & Executive Director of Arts NC State. The Director of the Crafts Center will be responsible for but not limited to: Strategic Leadership, Academic Engagement & Arts-Integrated Initiatives Develop and implement a strategic plan to realize a new vision for the Crafts Center, including restructuring overall programming to support the evolving mission and priorities of Arts NC State. Increase academic support and develop collaborative relationships across disciplines, departments, and colleges to expand student engagement, experiential learning, and interdisciplinary opportunities. Advance arts-integrated research and student-focused programming aligned with Arts NC State’s Art + Wellness and Art + Science initiatives, including the new ArtsRx program. Identify and develop opportunities that strengthen the Crafts Center as a creativity hub for high-impact, hands-on experiential learning, research, critical thinking, and well-being. Build and maintain collaborative relationships with faculty, staff, students, and campus partners to integrate Crafts Center programs and resources into the broader academic experience. Staff & Instructor Leadership Manage and provide leadership to permanent staff and student employees, including supervision, coaching, performance management, and completion of required personnel processes. Coordinate the management, scheduling, and engagement of Crafts Center instructors to ensure high-quality instruction and meaningful impact across studios and programs. Lead and inspire staff, student employees, and instructors in support of the Crafts Center’s strategic direction, programs, and operations. Coordinate appropriate staffing and management-level coverage to support classes, workshops, evening and weekend operations, and special events. Ensure required performance evaluations and other personnel responsibilities are completed for applicable employees. Program Development, Exhibitions & Community Engagement Develop and coordinate Crafts Center programs, classes, workshops, and related learning opportunities in collaboration with Arts NC State staff and campus partners. Curate and coordinate exhibitions, demonstrations, special events, and other programming that showcase craft, visual arts, interdisciplinary work, and student engagement. Develop and maintain collaborative relationships with student organizations, campus partners, community organizations, guilds, artists, instructors, and other stakeholders. Assess programming and identify opportunities to enhance participation, impact, and alignment with the strategic direction of the Crafts Center and Arts NC State. Budget Management, Assessment & Administrative Oversight Manage the Crafts Center budget in collaboration with the Arts NC State Business Officer, supporting the effective allocation and stewardship of financial resources. Monitor revenues, expenditures, and overall budget status throughout the fiscal year to support established financial and operational goals. Lead the production of annual reports, assessment reports, and related reporting to evaluate program effectiveness and progress toward established goals. Provide oversight of administrative processes and technology supporting class registration, sales, receipts, and other Crafts Center business operations in accordance with university requirements. Studio Operations, Facilities, Safety & Compliance Serve as the Crafts Center facilities liaison and oversee the maintenance and effective operation of studios, equipment, supplies, and facilities. Ensure Crafts Center operations, equipment, and facilities comply with applicable university, state, and federal policies, procedures, and safety requirements. Coordinate the preparation and maintenance of studio spaces to provide safe and functional environments for classes, workshops, exhibitions, and other programs. Identify facility, equipment, and operational needs and coordinate with appropriate university and Arts NC State partners to address maintenance, safety, and operational concerns. University, Arts NC State & Community Representation Represent the Crafts Center and Arts NC State at university and community meetings, functions, programs, and special events. Develop and maintain relationships with university and community stakeholders that support the mission and visibility of the Crafts Center. Participate in Arts NC State events and activities that strengthen awareness of and engagement with the Crafts Center. Maintain flexibility to support evening and weekend operations, special events, and other activities requiring the Director’s participation.

title: Challenge Course Apprentice
description: A Challenge Course Apprentice is enthusiastic about gaining valuable leadership, collaboration, and facilitation skills. In this role, you will gain the technical and soft skills needed to become a certified facilitator and prepare for more advanced positions within our team. You must attend 40 hours of initial comprehensive training focused on developing high-course technical skills, debriefing strategies, and a deep understanding of safety protocols to learn how to facilitate team-building games and activities. Join our pack! Contribute Adherence to Standards: Strictly follow all procedures established by Wellness and Recreation and the Association for Challenge Course Technology (ACCT) for the safe operation of all elements. Rigging and Belay Management: Learn and execute proper rigging techniques. Practice and demonstrate proficiency in all required knots, belay systems, and technical rope work. Program Support: Co-facilitate team-building and leadership programs for various clients, including university students, campus staff, and external groups. Instruction: Clearly and enthusiastically deliver safety orientations, proper harnessing procedures, and technical instructions for ascending and descending high and low elements as part of our risk management procedures. Customer Service: Welcome and greet users, providing information on facilities, programs, services, and the local area. Facilitation Support: Assist in setting up and breaking down high-course, low-course, and team-building activities for groups. Educate students, faculty, and the community about outdoor recreation and our programs. Group Processing: Learn and practice facilitation techniques, including leading introductory activities, debriefing exercises, and managing group dynamics to achieve client learning outcomes. Equipment Maintenance: Ensure all gear is properly cleaned, dried, inventoried, and stored after use to maintain its serviceability and longevity.

title: Assistant Trip Leader
description: An Outdoor Adventures Assistant Trip Leader is a passionate and safety-minded student who helps inspire others to get involved in outdoor recreation. In this entry-level role, you'll assist in leading half-day, full-day, and weekend trips, workshops, and clinics to prepare for advancement as a trip leader. You will help with trip planning, equipment preparation, and group management while building valuable skills in leadership, risk management, and instruction. Join our team and help us guide new adventurers into the outdoors! Contribute Trip and Workshop Leadership: Assist trip leaders with all aspects of a trip, including group development, risk management, and instruction of technical skills. You will also help plan, create lessons, and facilitate educational workshops and clinics. P rogram Education and Marketing: Help market trips to the campus community and educate others about all Outdoor Adventures programs, including trips, clinics, and equipment rentals. Logistics and Equipment: Prepare equipment for trips and maintain gear by checking it in and out, cleaning, disinfecting, and performing minor repairs.

title: Temporary Research Specialist
description:
Posting Number: PG196258TM
Position Number: 11ASO3766
Position Type: Temporary
Essential Job Duties: The primary purpose of this position is to support research involving tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum ) cultivation, breeding, and plant transformation. Responsibilities include: Growing, maintaining, and propagating tomato plants under greenhouse and controlled environmental conditions Assisting with breeding crosses and plant transformation experiments Collecting and documenting plant growth, development, and experimental results. Developing and maintaining research databases to track plant lines, genetic backgrounds, breeding pedigrees, transformation events, and experimental data Additional responsibilities may include laboratory research, data analysis, and scientific documentation.
Is Time Limited: Yes
Wolfpack Perks and Benefits: As a Pack member, you belong here, and can enjoy exclusive perks designed to enhance your personal and professional well-being. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone. What we offer: Health Insurance for Temporary Employees Enhance your career with LEAD courses Attend non-revenue generating sporting events for free. Attain Work-life balance with our Childcare discounts , Wellness & Recreation Membership , and Wellness Programs that aim to build a thriving wolfpack community.
