title: Assistant Vice Chancellor for Research Strategy and Programs
description: As the Assistant Vice Chancellor for Research Strategy & Programs, you will provide strategic leadership for the Research Strategy & Programs unit within the Office of Research and Innovation (ORI). Reporting to the Associate Vice Chancellor for Research Initiatives, you will advance NC State’s research priorities by strengthening early-stage concept development, strategic research planning, and alignment with emerging federal priorities. You will lead research development activities that support cross-university individuals and teams, coordinate research strategy and federal engagement efforts within ORI, and assist with the coordination and oversight of Centers and Institutes administered by ORI. Working closely with the Associate Vice Chancellor, Proposal Development Unit, colleges, centers, and institutes, you will help advance institutional research priorities and strengthen the university’s competitiveness for research opportunities. Essential Job Duties: Research Strategy & Programs Leadership Lead strategic planning and concept development for the Research Strategy & Programs unit, with a focus on institutional research priorities, emerging federal priorities, and high-impact research opportunities. Direct the unit’s strategic research development and federal engagement activities, ensuring coordination with ORI priorities and university research strategy. Lead and support staff responsible for research development, federal engagement, and proposal readiness activities. Establish priorities and coordinate activities across ORI divisions, colleges, centers, and institutes to advance institutional research goals. Strategic Research Development & Federal Alignment Monitor and analyze emerging federal research priorities, multi-agency initiatives, and funding opportunities to identify areas of strategic opportunity for NC State. Guide development of competitive research concepts, teams, and strategies in high-impact and emerging research areas. Partner with colleges, centers, and institutes to strengthen research concepts and align institutional capabilities with federal priorities and sponsor expectations. Coordinate with the Proposal Development Unit to connect strategic research planning with proposal development and institutional positioning. Institutional Coordination & Centers and Institutes Advance cross-university coordination of strategic research initiatives involving ORI divisions, colleges, centers, and institutes. Support the Associate Vice Chancellor for Research Initiatives in coordinating and overseeing activities for Centers and Institutes administered by ORI. Contribute to enterprise-level planning and strategic alignment for ORI-affiliated Centers and Institutes. Represent the Research Strategy & Programs portfolio in institutional planning, working groups, and ORI-wide strategic initiatives. Stakeholder Engagement & Strategic Communication Build relationships with faculty, research leaders, and external partners to identify and advance strategic research opportunities. Communicate federal priorities, institutional research strengths, and emerging opportunities to internal and external stakeholders. Develop and contribute to briefings, presentations, and other materials supporting research strategy, federal engagement, and institutional priorities. Represent the unit in meetings and discussions with internal and external stakeholders as delegated by the Associate Vice Chancellor for Research Initiatives In this role, you will help shape NC State’s research strategy and strengthen the university’s position for future research opportunities. If you are a strategic research leader who can connect emerging federal priorities with institutional research strengths, build effective partnerships across a complex research environment, and advance high-impact opportunities, we welcome you to apply.

title: Temporary Field and Greenhouse Technician
description: Daily duties include: Supporting field and greenhouse activities within the Pea and yam projects Cutting plants, planting seed, planting transplants, applying fertilizer, field data collection and harvesting Other related activities as needed

title: Assistant Professor, Accounting
description: The Department of Accounting in the Poole College of Management at North Carolina State University invites applications for a 9-month tenure-track Assistant Professor of Accounting , with an anticipated start date of August 2027 . The department welcomes applications from both emerging scholars entering their first faculty appointment and experienced Assistant Professors. Key Responsibilities: Develop and maintain a high-quality, impactful research program in accounting resulting in publications in leading peer-reviewed journals and consistent with the expectations of an R1 research university. Deliver high-quality instruction in accounting at the undergraduate and graduate levels, including the Master of Accounting (MAC) and MBA programs. Contribute to teaching needs in areas such as managerial accounting, auditing, accounting information systems, analytics, artificial intelligence, and related areas. Contribute to the academic mission of the department, college, and university through service and professional engagement. Collaborate effectively with faculty and contribute to a collegial, intellectually engaging, and interdisciplinary academic environment. Engage with students, faculty, and other stakeholders in ways that advance the teaching, research, and service missions of the department. If you are looking for an opportunity to join an engaged academic community within the Department of Accounting and Poole College of Management, advance impactful accounting research, and contribute to the education and development of future accounting and business professionals, we encourage to you apply. Compensation will be commensurate with the successful candidate’s qualifications, experience, and scholarly record.

title: Assistant Professor, Finance
description: The Department of Finance in the Poole College of Management at North Carolina State University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Finance position, with a preferred specialization in Finance. Position Responsibilities Research : Develop and maintain a high-quality, impactful research program in finance consistent with the expectations of a Research 1 (R1) university. Teaching : Deliver high-quality instruction in finance at the undergraduate and graduate (MBA) levels, with the ability to teach in both in-person and online formats. Service : Contribute to the academic and professional community through service to the department, college, university, and relevant professional organizations. Engagement : Engage collaboratively with faculty colleagues and contribute to the continued growth and academic excellence of the Department of Finance and Poole College of Management. We welcome applications from scholars committed to high-quality research and teaching in Finance and interested in contributing to a collaborative academic environment. Appointment Details The anticipated start date is August 16, 2027.

title: Program Coordinator
description: The SE RISCC Program Coordinator brings together researchers, land managers, policymakers, and partner organizations to address invasive species and climate-related challenges across the Southeast and U.S. Caribbean. The role spans regional network coordination, scientific synthesis, knowledge exchange, and actionable research—helping move ideas and findings from research settings into practical tools, informed decisions, and on-the-ground management. At the center of this work, you’ll get the opportunity to strengthen connections across the region and help partners turn emerging science and knowledge into practical, science-informed solutions for invasive species management. Key Responsibilities: Manage the SE RISCC Network: Develop regional work plans with SE RISCC and SE CASC leadership and the Advisory Board. Coordinate Leadership and Advisory Committee meetings, agendas, and partner communications. Lead network communications, webinars, and website content. Identify emerging research needs and collaborate with scientists and partners to address them. Advance Scientific Synthesis and Actionable Research: Identify and coordinate high-priority research themes and collaborative projects addressing invasive species and climate-related management needs. Synthesize research findings into manager-focused briefs, management resources, decision-support materials, and other practical tools. Lead or coordinate actionable science efforts that connect research with the needs of managers and policymakers. Engage students, postdocs, and faculty in applied research and synthesis activities that contribute to regional management solutions. Coordinate Events, Webinars, and Communities of Practice: Plan and coordinate regional workshops, webinars, partner meetings, and manager-focused training. Facilitate communities of practice focused on priorities such as early detection, rapid response, climate-informed risk assessment, and management interventions. Create opportunities for knowledge exchange and collaboration across the region. Contribute to network reporting, evaluation, and communications. Engage with National, Interagency, and Inter-Regional Networks: Represent SE RISCC in national RISCC and inter-regional network coordination. Connect regional priorities with applicable federal strategies and broader invasive species initiatives. If you like to take initiative, work independently while contributing to a collaborative team, and connect people and ideas across different backgrounds, sectors, and disciplines, this role offers an opportunity to turn high-quality science into meaningful action. Bring your attention to detail, thoughtful communication, and commitment to professional, respectful relationships to help strengthen the network and create productive spaces for knowledge exchange and collaboration and join the SE RISCC.

title: Open Rank - Assistant / Associate / Full Professor
description: The Department of Nuclear Engineering at North Carolina State University invites applications for a 9-month, tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor rank, beginning August 2027. We welcome candidates whose expertise advances nuclear engineering in areas such as advanced reactor design, thermohydraulics, and materials, as well as emerging interdisciplinary fields. As a faculty member, you will help advance nuclear technologies to meet growing energy needs while strengthening the department’s experimental and computational research capabilities. Your work may span next-generation reactor systems, nuclear materials, intelligent energy systems, or the intersections of nuclear technology with digital engineering, infrastructure investment, climate change mitigation, and community engagement. Through research, teaching, and mentorship, you will contribute to the future of nuclear energy and the engineers who will shape it. Key Responsibilities: Advance research and scholarship in the department’s focus areas or emerging fields that complement its strengths. Build a sustainable research program by developing proposals and securing external funding. Disseminate research findings through peer-reviewed publications and technical presentations. Teach undergraduate and graduate courses, including Introduction to Nuclear Engineering and senior design projects. Develop graduate courses that reflect your research expertise and emerging developments in nuclear engineering. Mentor and supervise MS and PhD students conducting research in related fields. Foster experimental, computational, and interdisciplinary collaborations that expand the department’s research capabilities. Bring your expertise, collaborative approach, and commitment to teaching and mentorship to NC State.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: Organization/Department Overview The Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology (EPP) in the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS) at North Carolina State University is a Land-Grant University department with more than 40 faculty engaged in teaching, research, and extension programs addressing issues in entomology, plant pathology, and related biological sciences. The Department provides a rich environment for undergraduate and graduate education, research training, and interdisciplinary collaboration, with opportunities to apply current technologies and approaches in laboratory, greenhouse, and field settings. EPP houses several specialized facilities and resources that support research, education, and extension, including the Plant Disease and Insect Clinic, Larry Grand Mycological Herbarium, Micropropagation and Repository Unit, Structural Pest Management Training Facility, Insect Museum, and Center for Integrated Fungal Research. The Department's programs are supported by the broader resources of CALS, which includes 12 academic departments, extensive research facilities, and research stations located throughout North Carolina that facilitate collaboration with agricultural producers, stakeholders, and industry partners. Primary Purpose of Position The Postdoctoral Scholar will contribute to the interdisciplinary research project “Characterization of the Maize Pattern-Triggered Immunity Response.” The position will investigate the genetic, molecular, and microbiological mechanisms underlying pattern-triggered immunity in maize through research conducted in laboratory, greenhouse, and field settings. The scholar will work collaboratively with Dr. Anna Whitfield and Dr. Peter Balint-Kurti at North Carolina State University, as well as collaborators at the University of Illinois under the supervision of Dr. Tiffany Jamann. Specific research objectives and experimental approaches will be developed in consultation with the principal investigators and will evolve based on project needs and research findings. The scholar will be expected to exercise scientific independence in planning and conducting experiments, interpreting results, communicating findings, and contributing to scholarly publications. Duties and Responsibilities: Planning and Conducting Research – 60% Plan and conduct research in genetics, molecular biology, microbiology, and plant-microbe interactions in laboratory, greenhouse, and field environments. Develop and execute controlled experiments designed to address project objectives and research questions. Apply appropriate experimental designs, controls, protocols, and methodologies to ensure the quality and reproducibility of research findings. Maintain accurate, comprehensive, and organized records of experimental procedures, observations, and results. Analyze and troubleshoot experimental approaches and modify research methods as appropriate based on results and project needs. Collaborate with principal investigators, project team members, and external collaborators to coordinate research activities and advance project objectives. Interpreting, Presenting, and Publishing Research Results – 40% Analyze and interpret experimental results using appropriate scientific approaches and in consultation with project investigators and collaborators. Communicate research findings to principal investigators, collaborators, laboratory and departmental audiences, and other scientific stakeholders. Present research findings at professional meetings, conferences, seminars, and other scientific venues. Prepare research reports, abstracts, presentations, and manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed scientific journals. Lead and contribute to the development, revision, and submission of manuscripts and other scholarly products resulting from the research. Incorporate feedback from collaborators and peer review

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Department of Biological and Agricultural Engineering at North Carolina State University invites applications for a full-time Postdoctoral Research Associate to work with Dr. Daniela Jones, Associate Professor, in machine learning, AI surrogate modeling, and scientific model validation for large-scale agricultural and bioeconomy systems. The position supports REFRAME (Resource Engineering Framework for Responsible, Augmented Modeling and Engagement), a multi-year initiative funded by Schmidt Sciences through the Virtual Institute for Feedstocks of the Future (VIFF). REFRAME is developing a modular, AI-enabled, open-source platform that integrates legacy scientific models, artificial intelligence, optimization, and shared data infrastructure to evaluate future biomass systems across availability, accessibility, characterization, conversion, and impacts. The successful candidate will serve as REFRAME's scientific lead for AI surrogate methodology, providing project-wide leadership in the development, statistical validation, benchmarking, deployment, and long-term evolution of scalable AI surrogate models. Housed within REFRAME's Modeling Pillar, the researcher will work at the intersection of AI and agricultural domain science and collaborate with an interdisciplinary team of graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, faculty, software developers, the Platform Architect, and researchers within the Digital Backbone and Stakeholder Engagement Pillars. The position will also contribute to AI agents for model orchestration, scientific workflow automation, and stakeholder-facing decision support. The position is expected to begin in Spring 2027, with an initial one-year appointment and the potential for extension based on performance and funding availability. The Postdoctoral Research Associate will: Lead the development and implementation of project-wide methodologies for the development, evaluation, statistical validation, benchmarking, and deployment of scalable and scientifically rigorous AI surrogate models across REFRAME's modeling domains. Develop generalized surrogate modeling and statistical evaluation frameworks for computationally intensive scientific models, including approaches for calibration, uncertainty quantification, generalization and robustness assessment, and explainable AI. Apply knowledge of agricultural production systems, agronomic practices, crop and soil processes, and biomass systems to evaluate the scientific and practical plausibility of surrogate model behavior and outputs. Collaborate with and mentor interdisciplinary researchers developing AI surrogates while establishing standardized, reproducible scientific machine learning workflows across REFRAME. Collaborate with the Digital Backbone team to integrate validated surrogates into scalable, open-source infrastructure and contribute to AI agents for model orchestration, workflow automation, and scientific decision support. Lead and contribute to peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations, and contribute to research proposal development and the pursuit of external funding opportunities that advance REFRAME and related research

title: Open Rank - Assistant/Associate/Professor - Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
description: The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering at NC State University seeks highly qualified candidates to fill tenure-track or tenured faculty positions. We particularly encourage applications in the areas of energy or soft materials, with particular emphasis on integration of autonomous laboratories, AI, or machine learning in these fields. Your expertise and contributions will complement departmental strengths in energy and sustainability, materials, and data and computational engineering. Key responsibilities: Develop an externally funded research program of international reputation, including collaborative and interdisciplinary research. Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in chemical engineering, including topics in AI and machine learning. Perform departmental service, including committee work, as well as engage in broader initiatives that support the education and research missions of the institution. Contribute to the broader engineering community through professional service. If you are driven by original thinking and collaboration, we invite you to join the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering at NC State University.

title: Assistant Teaching Professor
description: The Biological Sciences department is seeking candidates for an Assistant Teaching Professor position. This is a 9-month professional-track faculty position focused on teaching undergraduate Introductory Cellular & Molecular Biology and Human Anatomy & Physiology courses. You will have an estimated teaching load of 6–9 credit hours per semester, depending on enrollment and other assigned responsibilities. Responsibilities: Teach Introduction to Cellular & Molecular Biology and Human Anatomy & Physiology, while providing instructional support for associated lab courses. Opportunity to develop and/or teach a 200-level or higher course in an area of your expertise. Serve as an advisor to undergraduate students and supervise graduate teaching assistants. Contribute to other departmental responsibilities shaped by the needs of the department and your strengths and interests. Join the Department of Biological Sciences at NC State and bring your teaching expertise to a community focused on providing a strong undergraduate education in the biological sciences. Your teaching, expertise, and interests will contribute to the learning experiences of students across the department’s undergraduate programs.

title: Transportation Assistant
description: Are you someone who enjoys staying active, working independently, and being an essential part of a team? Join the Rave! Catering team and play a vital role in delivering food, equipment, and supplies that help create exceptional dining and catering experiences across campus. The primary purpose of this position is to deliver finished product, equipment and supplies to all Dining locations and catering function locations, in good condition and following a set schedule in a timely fashion: Duties include, but are not limited to: Load and unload cargo at each location; assist with setup and breakdown. Assist in the catering stock room, including labeling, storing, pulling stock and equipment. Assist supervisor with routine preventative maintenance and inspection; keep proper records of maintenance and fueling of all vehicles. Comply with all Department of Transportation and State requirements for operators of motor vehicles. Must be able to lift 30 pounds above head and up to 60 pounds on rare occasions, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you're ready to be part of a team that keeps operations moving seamlessly, apply today! Bring your reliability, teamwork, and customer-focused attitude to a role where your contributions make a difference every day.

title: Crew Leader I - 44637
description: Join our team as a Crew Leader I , where you will lead impactful projects that help maintain the appearance, safety, and functionality of our campus. In this role, you will guide a dedicated team in completing essential work such as power washing entrances, window cleaning, floor care (including waxing), and other facility upkeep tasks that directly support the campus community. As a Crew Leader, you will coordinate daily operations, prioritize assignments, and ensure work is completed efficiently and to high standards. You will also play a key role in troubleshooting maintenance issues, supporting your team, and providing excellent customer service to campus partners. This is a great opportunity to step into a leadership role, make a visible impact, and grow your skills in a collaborative and service-focused environment. If you are ready to lead a team and take pride in maintaining a clean and welcoming campus, we encourage you to apply. Working Hours: 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday - Friday Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Lead projects , including power washing, window washing, floor waxing, and re-lamping fixtures and dispensers Inspect and verify maintenance discrepancies and ensure timely resolution Provide support to other zones as needed, filling in for vacant positions or absenteeism Collect and submit timesheets within established timelines Perform critical duties during adverse weather or emergencies as assigned Complete accident reports within 24 hours of an incident Assist with equipment inventory and maintain a monthly inventory of storage closet supplies Submit supply orders for manager approval to ensure adequate stock levels Train new employees, ensuring they understand tasks and safety protocols Transport employees to various locations for assignments Collaborate with maintenance staff inside and outside the unit to resolve issues efficiently Address and resolve customer requests via radio communications, work orders, and direct interactions Ability to lift a minimum of 60 pounds continuously and 90 pounds occasionally with or without reasonable accommodations, climb and balance on a ladder up to 8ft, and distinguish between colors. Perform physical tasks such as grasping, pushing, and pulling cleaning equipment; reaching overhead; bending, squatting, climbing, and maintaining balance; and communicate effectively with supervisors and the public.

title: General Manager
description: The primary purpose of this position is to serve as the General Manager and is responsible for the management of a residential dining unit within NC State Dining. Duties include but are not limited to: This position will be responsible for the strategic planning, analysis, and financial stewardship of the unit. This includes overall leadership, coordination, planning and innovation. The day to day management will be achieved by a team of culinary staff reporting directly to this position. This position is responsible for the design and execution of the marketing program and strategies for the unit. This initiative is targeted not only at NC State University students, faculty and staff but also directed at corporate partners on campus. The person in this position must be committed philosophically and operationally, to delivering high quality services in an efficient manner, while being sensitive to the service needs of NC State University. This position must act as an entrepreneurial manager and change agent who is dedicated to supporting the ongoing development of the NC State Dining department and its culinary services. Unit Management Provides administrative supervision of all dietary activities, including planning and establishment of menus. Collaborates with chefs, dietitian, and bakery to ensure food quality and presentation meets or exceeds NC State Dining’s standards and policies. Develops working relationships with business partners on and around campus and encourages strong communication within a group setting. Identify operational gaps, assess workflow needs, and develop, document, and implement new Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to improve efficiency, consistency, and compliance. Financial Administration Effectively monitors and manages the financial performance of the unit. Participate in the budget development process. Monitor and manage food service operations to meet agreed upon targets. Establishes goals for the unit and plan daily, weekly, semester work to meet those goals and those of the unit. Meet goals by planning work operations, setting priorities and meeting deadlines. Set weekly goals and meet budget goals by monitoring labor and cost of goods. Runs and analyzes Micros and CBord reports to effectively project operational needs. Responsible for keeping the food service equipment in good working order and submitting requests for necessary repairs. Evaluates equipment needs and submits requests for new equipment that is compliant with available budget and departmental and university guidelines. Provides feedback to and coaches employees on job duties and responsibilities, and provides corrective action as necessary. title: Open Rank T/TT Faculty (Assistant, Associate or Full Professor)
description: The Department of Communication at North Carolina State University invites applications for an open rank tenure/tenure-track Assistant, Associate or Full Professor in Communication specializing in science communication, beginning August 16, 2027. We seek a community-engaged scholar whose research demonstrates a passionate commitment to the study and practice of science communication, including topics such as (but not limited to) public trust in science, dis- and misinformation, public engagement in science, audience engagement, message design, research translation, and science literacy. The position is intended to complement and extend existing strengths in the Department, including interpersonal communication, organizational communication, public relations and strategic communication, rhetoric and civic engagement, and science, health, environmental, and risk communication. We welcome candidates whose research on science communication intersects with one or more of these areas or develops new connections among them. This position is part of the Leadership in Public Science Faculty Cluster, created in 2016. Cluster members—both individually and collaboratively—advance scholarship, teaching, and service to deepen our understanding and practice of the public’s engagement with science on campus and beyond. The cluster’s current focus spans citizen and community science, public engagement with science, civic and collective scientific literacy, and the democratization and decolonization of scientific knowledge. The new science communication faculty member will have the opportunity to collaborate with existing cluster faculty in the College of Natural Resources and College of Education as well as discipline-based educational research faculty in the College of Sciences. To expand and extend scholarship in public science, faculty will be expected to integrate science communication into interdisciplinary research endeavors, contribute to cross-disciplinary teaching and graduate mentoring, and engage in high-impact outreach. This new faculty member will contribute to Department of Communication undergraduate programs (B.A. in Communication and undergraduate minor in science communication) and graduate teaching and mentoring our graduate programs (M.S. in Communication and Ph.D. in Communication, Rhetoric, and Digital Media). Tenured and tenure-track faculty members have a teaching load of 2/2, develop courses in their areas of expertise and contribute, through service, to the intellectual life of the Department, the College, the University and the field. The faculty member will be expected to seek internal and external research funding and develop collaborative initiatives, in particular as part of the Leadership in Public Science Cluster. Rank will be awarded based on experience and qualifications.

title: General Manager
description: The General Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, strategic planning, financial stewardship, and operational oversight of a premier retail dining unit with NC State Dining. The incumbent is responsible for the strategic planning, analysis, and financial stewardship of the unit. This includes overall leadership, coordination, planning and innovation. The day to day management will be achieved by a team of culinary staff reporting directly to this position. Duties include but are not limited to: Design and execute the marketing program and strategies for the unit, targeted not only at NC State University students, faculty and staff but also directed at corporate partners on campus. The person in this position must be committed philosophically and operationally, to delivering high quality services in an efficient manner, while being sensitive to the service needs of NC State University. This position must act as an entrepreneurial manager and change agent who is dedicated to supporting the ongoing development of the NC State Dining department and its culinary services. We are looking for a professional who balances bold leadership with meticulous attention to detail. You should be someone who remains calm and respectful under pressure, views challenges as opportunities for innovation, and is dedicated to providing “The Wolfpack” with an outstanding retail dining experience. Unit Management Provides administrative supervision of all dietary activities, including planning and establishment of menus. Collaborates with chefs, dietitian, and bakery to ensure food quality and presentation meets or exceeds NC State Dining’s standards and policies. Develops working relationships with business partners on and around campus and encourages strong communication within a group setting. Financial Administration Effectively monitors and manages the financial performance of the unit. Participate in the budget development process. Monitor and manage food service operations to meet agreed upon targets. Establishes goals for the unit and plan daily, weekly, semester work to meet those goals and those of the unit. Meet goals by planning work operations, setting priorities and meeting deadlines. Set weekly goals and meet budget goals by monitoring labor and cost of goods. Runs and analyzes Micros and NetMenu reports to effectively project operational needs. title: Development Associate
description: Support the daily operations of the College of Engineering Advancement Office by providing high-level administrative, project, and operational support to the fundraising team. As the Development Associate , you will help coordinate team activities, facilitate communication with donors, prospects, volunteers, and campus colleagues, and ensure the efficient execution of advancement initiatives. This role is an integral part of the Advancement team and contributes to the effective delivery of fundraising and engagement efforts across the College. Key Responsibilities Administrative & Operational Support Coordinate team meetings and activities, manage calendars, schedule appointments, arrange travel for senior leadership, prepare correspondence, and provide day-to-day administrative support for the fundraising team. Project Coordination & Constituent Engagement Support projects and programmatic initiatives that advance fundraising efforts while facilitating communication and coordinating meetings with donors, prospects, volunteers, and campus colleagues. Organization & Process Improvement Maintain organized workflows, follow established processes with exceptional attention to detail, and identify opportunities to improve efficiency while supporting the ongoing operations of the Advancement Office. If you are a detail-oriented professional who enjoys coordinating projects, supporting collaborative teams, and providing exceptional administrative service in a dynamic environment, we encourage you to apply and become an integral member of the College of Engineering Advancement team.

title: Assistant Clinical Research Coordinator
description: As the Research Coordinator, you will coordinate research activities involving participants, clinicians, and members of the research team. You will manage scheduling, support participant recruitment and initial screening, coordinate research procedures and supporting tests, and maintain accurate research data and records. Working within established research protocols and under the guidance of senior team members, you will help ensure research activities are organized, accurately documented, and conducted in accordance with approved procedures. Key responsibilities: Coordinate schedules for research participants, clinicians, researchers, and facilities; arrange research activities through email and phone communication. Recruit potential participants through local clinics, hospitals, and on- and off-campus outreach activities. Conduct initial participant screening and explain established research procedures. Support research procedures and participant testing in accordance with established protocols, ethical requirements, and department policies. If you are organized, detail-oriented, and enjoy working directly with research participants and multidisciplinary teams, this position offers an opportunity to contribute to research that supports improved understanding and outcomes for patients and communities. We welcome you to apply and join our team.

title: Assistant Director, Pack Support Programs
description: In this role you will report to the Senior Director for TRIO Collegiate and Pack Support Programs and will play a key role in helping students successfully transition into and through NC State. TRIO Collegiate and Pack Support oversees programs including TRIO Collegiate, 1887 Scholars, and Pack Promise, which provide mentoring, academic guidance, educational programming, and other resources that support student success. The Assistant Director will support 1887 Scholars, Pack Promise, and First in the Pack, with additional responsibilities supporting rural students and other identified student populations as needed. The position develops and delivers student success programs, provides individual and group coaching, builds campus partnerships, and connects students with resources that support their academic and personal goals. As a successful candidate you will be able to manage multiple priorities, build strong relationships, and translate student needs into effective programs and services. Student Programming & Success Coaching Develop, implement, and assess programs that support student transition, engagement, academic progress, and success. Contribute to strategic planning, goal setting, program evaluation, and annual reporting. Lead signature programs and educational initiatives, including program delivery and instruction. Use structured coaching and development models such as Inside Track, StrengthsFinder, and other evidence-informed approaches. Provide individual and group coaching to a designated student caseload and connect students with appropriate campus resources. Collaborate with campus partners to coordinate services and opportunities that support student success. Program Evaluation & Assessment Develop and assess program learning outcomes using appropriate evaluation tools and methods. Research benchmarks and promising practices to strengthen programs and services. Analyze annual assessment data and prepare reports for DASA Assessment, funding agencies, and other stakeholders. Use assessment findings to identify opportunities for program improvement. Partnerships & Student Support Build relationships with university departments, faculty, staff, and community organizations to strengthen student support. Support program outreach and recruitment to ensure eligible students are aware of and connected to available services. Represent programs at campus and community events and serve as a knowledgeable resource for students and partners. Supervision & Operations Supervise, train, and evaluate two to three graduate fellows for the 2027–28 academic year. Provide regular coaching, feedback, and professional development to direct reports. Manage multiple projects, deadlines, events, and administrative priorities while ensuring timely follow-through. Participate in departmental training, program communications, and other activities that support effective program operations. Attend events and programs that may require evening and weekend availability. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact on student success at NC State by helping students navigate their transition to college, build confidence and connections, and achieve their academic goals. You will bring together coaching, programming, assessment, and campus partnerships to strengthen the student experience and help assigned programs deliver measurable results.

title: UTS - Interim Assistant Director of Student and Community Well-Being at NC State
description: The Interim Assistant Director of Student and Community Well-Being supports the department by coordinating, implementing, and assessing programs that promote student, staff, and faculty well-being, belonging, engagement, and community connection across the department. The position serves as a key resource for students and college constituents by providing referrals to campus support services, coordinating workshops and events, supporting student organizations, and helping create a supportive and health-promoting college environment. Primary responsibilities include: Planning and executing well-being and community-building programs. Coordinating logistics, communications, and outreach; tracking participation and program outcomes. Preparing reports and dashboards; maintaining web content and promotional materials; Supporting onboarding and transition programs. Collaborating with campus and community partners; and supervising student employees and graduate assistants. The position routinely utilizes Microsoft Office applications, survey and assessment tools, web-based communication platforms, and university systems to support programming, reporting, and outreach efforts. Work is performed in a collaborative university environment requiring significant interaction with students, faculty, staff, campus partners, and community stakeholders.

title: Assistant Grants & Finance Manager
description: Primary Duties and Responsibilities: Award Management & Grant Reporting: Manage sponsored projects by monitoring financial activity, expenditures, budgets, and projections; provide timely financial information and guidance to project teams to support informed decision-making and mitigate financial risk. Apply accounting principles, sponsor requirements, and university policies to budgeting, forecasting, personnel expenses, cost allocations, expenditures, and other sponsored project fiscal activities. Conduct regular financial reviews with project teams to assess spending, forecast future needs, identify potential issues, and recommend corrective actions to keep projects financially and operationally on track. Coordinate award modifications and required approvals by preparing project modification requests, including rebudgeting, no-cost extensions, changes in principal investigator, equipment purchases, travel, pre-award costs, and other university or sponsor actions. Manage subawards, contracts and project segments throughout their lifecycle, including setup, monitoring, financial and compliance oversight, reporting, and closeout, in coordination with project teams, university offices, and sponsoring agencies. Coordinate sponsored project closeout by resolving outstanding financial and administrative matters, completing reconciliations, obtaining required approvals, maintaining award records, and ensuring timely submission of final reports and documentation. Support the preparation and submission of sponsor-required financial and progress reports, ensuring accuracy, completeness, appropriate supporting documentation, and compliance with established deadlines. Monitor and manage cost-share commitments, ensuring expenditures are properly tracked, supported, reconciled, and reported in accordance with sponsor and university requirements. Proposal Development: Identify and pursue funding opportunities support the growth of the Industry Extension Services departmental sponsored project portfolio. Prepare, compile, and submit grant and contract proposals for the project teams through NC State University systems, including RED, and sponsor electronic submission portals such as Grants.gov, Research.gov, and ERA commons. Collaborate with project team to develop proposal budgets, budget justifications, and other required documents in accordance with university and sponsor requirements. Create and maintain accurate RED proposal records with campus offices to facilitate timely and accurate proposal submissions. Provide guidance to the project team regarding NC State business processes and requirements for proposal development and submission. Review proposal materials for completeness, accuracy, and compliance with applicable university and sponsor guidelines. Serve as a resource to the project team throughout the proposal process, identifying potential issues and coordinating resolutions with appropriate university offices. Financial Management: Support the financial management of state appropriated, state receipt and fee for services budgets by monitoring expenditures, processing budget adjustments, reconciling financial transactions, and ensuring compliance with university policies and accounting guidelines. Initiate and process a variety of financial transactions, including purchase requisitions, purchase orders, voucher payments, reimbursements, interdepartmental transactions, Marketplace orders, and related fiscal activities. Assist with monitoring fund balances and financial trends to identify potential deficits, surpluses and areas requiring attention and Support fiscal year end closeout activities Assist with Salesforce approvals and Purchase Request coding to support accurate and compliant purchasing activities Assist with Salary Redistributions

title: Social Media Adviser: Student-Generated Content
description: As the Social Media Advisor: Student-Generated Content, you will play a key role in shaping how current and prospective students experience NC State University through authentic, student-created social media content. This position leads the Student Creator Program, empowering a talented group of students to develop engaging content that brings the undergraduate and graduate student experience to life across NC State’s social media channels, with a focus on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube. In this role you will also recruit, coach and manage up to 10 student social media creators. The position provides creative direction, develops content strategies and helps student creators translate their experiences into compelling stories that strengthen awareness of and connection to NC State. Key Responsibilities: Lead and continuously enhance the Student Creator Program, establishing creative direction, content priorities and processes that support the university’s social media goals. Recruit, onboard, advise and manage two to three student editors and up to 10 student social media creators. Coach student creators in developing engaging, student-first content that authentically reflects academic, campus and student experiences. Brainstorm and develop content concepts tailored to TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and emerging social media trends. Review and optimize student-generated content to ensure it aligns with university brand standards, platform best practices and audience interests. Monitor social media performance and prepare analytics reports that identify trends, measure results and inform content decisions. Collaborate across a large, complex organization to coordinate content opportunities and strengthen the reach and effectiveness of student-generated storytelling. Serve as a member of the Social Media Strategy Hub leadership team and collaborate closely with campus partners, particularly Enrollment Management and Services and Admissions, to integrate student-generated content into broader university social media and enrollment strategies. In this role you will be able to combine creativity and excellent communication skills, with the ability to coach and develop student creators. This role is ideal for a collaborative social media professional who enjoys turning ideas into compelling content, using analytics to guide strategy and helping students tell stories that showcase the NC State experience. Join NC State’s social media team and help shape a dynamic, student-centered content program that connects audiences with the people, experiences and opportunities that make the university distinctive.

title: Director, Environmental Services
description: Join our Campus Operations and Maintenance team as the Director of Environmental Services and lead an essential operation that helps create a clean, safe, welcoming, and well-maintained environment for our university community. The Director of Environmental Services provides strategic leadership and overall management for a large, varied department delivering environmental services across academic, athletics, housing, hospital, research, dining, and other campus facilities. This position leads approximately 320 permanent employees and 20–40 temporary staff while overseeing a $17 million annual operating budget. In this highly visible leadership role, you will guide departmental strategy, strengthen operational performance, manage financial and workforce resources, advance sustainability initiatives, and ensure high-quality services that support the evolving needs of the university. If you are an experienced leader who enjoys developing people, improving complex operations, and making a meaningful impact on the campus community, we invite you to apply and help lead the future of Environmental Services. Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Provide strategic leadership and overall direction for Environmental Services , developing short- and long-term business plans that align departmental operations, services, and resources with university priorities. Lead and develop a varied workforce of approximately 320 permanent full-time employees and 20–40 temporary staff, including departmental leaders and managers, while fostering accountability, collaboration, professional growth, and a strong service-oriented culture. Oversee the department’s approximately $17 million annual operating budget, including financial planning, long-range fiscal allocations, resource management, and identification of appropriate funding sources for operational and workforce needs. Direct environmental services across a complex campus environment that includes academic, athletics, housing, hospital, research, dining, and other university facilities. Provide oversight for a broad range of services, including housekeeping, floor care, pest control, indoor recycling, relamping, Universal Waste Disposal, and other specialized environmental services. Develop, negotiate, and administer complex vendor contracts and service agreements, including contracted housekeeping, window washing, specialized floor care, and other outsourced services, while monitoring cost, quality, and performance expectations. Establish and maintain departmental policies, standard operating procedures, service-level agreements, quality standards, and reporting practices to support consistent and responsive service delivery across campus. Oversee recruitment, selection, performance management, employee relations, training, and workforce development while ensuring supervisors and managers operate in accordance with university human resources policies and practices. Provide leadership in resolving employee grievances and workplace conflicts, while identifying opportunities to strengthen employee engagement, career development, succession planning, and workforce readiness. Direct the department’s Green Cleaning Program and advance sustainability initiatives, environmentally responsible practices, and operational strategies that support university goals. Oversee departmental procurement, material and asset management, equipment evaluation, and the selection of chemicals, tools, equipment, and other resources necessary to support effective operations. Champion the implementation and effective use of technology, scheduling systems, and operational tools that improve communication, workforce deployment, efficiency, and service delivery. Provide leadership and departmental coordination for emergency preparedness, business continuity planning, severe weather protocols, and other operational response efforts. Partner with campus stakeholders to anticipate service needs, establish expectations, support university growth, and continuously identify opportunities to improve the quality, efficiency, and effectiveness of Environmental Services.

title: Personal Development Coordinator for Students with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities (IDD)
description: As Personal Development Coordinator, you will play an important role in the Elevate program, helping college students with an intellectual disability at NC State build confidence, develop independence and advocacy skills, and pursue meaningful personal goals. This position is ideal for a student-focused professional who enjoys building relationships, providing individualized guidance, and helping students recognize their strengths and turn their aspirations into achievable goals. As a key member of the Elevate team, you will provide teaching and individualized advising focused on physical and emotional wellness, personal development, and success throughout the university experience. Working closely with students, peer coaches, and program staff, this role facilitates a person-centered planning process that connects each student’s goals with their individual strengths, interests, and aspirations. You will help students identify meaningful goals, develop strategies for achieving them, and make informed decisions that support their continued growth and self-determination. Through consistent guidance and collaboration, the position helps students navigate the university experience while developing the skills and confidence needed to achieve their personal development goals. This is an opportunity to make a lasting impact by supporting students as they grow, pursue their goals, and build greater independence. As a successful candidate, you will bring a collaborative, student-centered approach and a genuine commitment to helping Elevate participants make meaningful progress toward their personal and wellness goals.

title: Small Animal Kennel Attendant
description: This position provides critical support for hospitalized patients through the rigorous sanitation of housing environments and direct assistance to veterinary clinical teams. Coverage includes the General Hospital (GH), Intermediate Care (IMC), Intensive Care Unit (ICU), and Emergency (ER) departments within the Randall B. Terry Jr. Companion Animal Medical Center. The successful candidate must possess foundational knowledge of veterinary clinical operations and a commitment to excel in a high-volume, academic teaching environment. This role requires seamless interaction with faculty, staff, and students to maintain a sterile and therapeutic environment for patients requiring specialized care for complex medical conditions. The Impact You’ll Make: Clinical Excellence: Directly support veterinary technicians and clinicians with patient treatments, including vitals (TPR), safe restraint, and diagnostic sample submissions. Advanced Biosafety: Serve as the frontline of defense against infectious diseases by managing rigorous sanitation protocols, antibiotic-resistant housing, and isolation ward stewardship. Patient Advocacy: Ensure our patients remain clean, dry, and comfortable during their recovery through proactive monitoring and specialized care. Collaborative Teaching: Integrate with a varied team of faculty, students, and staff to coordinate individualized patient housing and communicate critical diagnostic data through our hospital information systems. Operational Leadership: Manage essential logistics, from medical inventory and equipment maintenance to the orientation of senior veterinary students on clinical standards. What You Bring: Foundational Knowledge: A basic understanding of veterinary clinical operations and a passion for high-volume, specialty-level medicine. Adaptability: The ability to excel in a fast-paced, teaching environment where clinical needs evolve quickly. Communication Skills: A collaborative spirit and the ability to interact professionally with a world-class clinical team. Physical Readiness: The ability to maintain high energy and lift up to 50 lbs (with or without accommodations) to meet the needs of our varied patient population.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: Duties and Responsibilities: The Lu Lab ( https://changlulab.com ), based at NC State University, is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral scholar to develop single-cell and spatial epigenomic technologies and apply these tools to study brain neuroscience, investigate cancer therapeutic resistance, and decipher aging. Advanced single-cell and spatial omic technologies generate insights into development and diseases with unprecedented resolution. The Lu lab pioneered the development of microfluidics-based epigenomic technologies and applied these novel tools to profile tissue samples to gain biomedical insights. The postdoc will lead technology development projects and conduct mechanistic studies in the field of single-cell epigenomics. The position offers access to state-of-the-art facilities and close collaborations within interdisciplinary teams involving engineers, biologists, bioinformaticians, and clinicians. Technology Development : Design, implement, and optimize devices and methods to enhance or develop new epigenomic profiling capabilities. Focus on leveraging modern molecular biology technologies including sequencing and genome editing. Data Analysis : Gather and process large-scale omic data. Conduct multi-omic analysis to identify key features associated with development and diseases. Collaboration & Publication : Work closely with interdisciplinary teams of engineers, molecular biologists, and clinicians to apply advanced epigenomic and multi-omic tools to a variety of diseases. Publish results in high-impact journals and present findings at conferences. Mentorship : Mentor graduate students and junior researchers in experimental and bioinformatic studies.

title: Painter
description: Join our passionate Facilities team as a Painter in the Trade Shop, where your skills will help keep our campus vibrant, safe, and inviting. In this role, you’ll use your expertise in painting, finishing, and drywall repair to maintain the beauty and functionality of our buildings and spaces . If you enjoy hands-on work, attention to detail, and seeing the visible results of your craftsmanship, we invite you to apply and be part of the team that helps our campus shine. Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Prepare surfaces by cleaning, sanding, patching, priming, and ensuring optimal conditions for painting Paint a variety of surfaces, including walls, ceilings, casework, fixtures, handrails, bollards, and equipment Perform advanced surface preparation, including sanding, applying wood filler, Bondo, caulking, and completing drywall repairs. Match paint colors and finishes to maintain consistency throughout campus facilities. Mix and tint paints accurately using specialized equipment Inspect work areas, materials, and vehicles regularly to ensure safety and compliance with hazardous material regulations Review plans, product specifications, and PPE requirements to ensure proper application and disposal procedures Report safety concerns, infractions, accidents, and injuries promptly in accordance with University policy Assist with power washing and other maintenance projects across campus as needed Collaborate with other Trade Shops units to support broader maintenance and repair initiatives Lift up to 60 pounds frequently and up to 90 plus pounds occasionally, with or without reasonable accommodations. Communicate effectively with supervisors and the general public, understand and follow verbal and written instructions and other communications related to work assignments and other matters.

title: Program Coordinator
description: As the TRIO Talent Search Program Coordinator you will facilitate educational and social development enrichment activities for middle and high school program participants. In this role you will provide participants with an educational environment conducive to obtaining a high school diploma and assisting with preparation to gain entry into a post-secondary institution. Responsibilities: Student Advising & Support Services Provide program resources and services to ensure personal, vocational, and educational success Provide academic assistance to specified students in caseload Identify academic needs for each participant and address those needs Assist participants with the college application and financial aid process Academic Coordination & Monitoring Coordinate and support academic programming for both Talent Search programs Monitor academic performance (transcripts, report cards, etc.) Ensure accuracy of each student’s academic progress Program Planning & Participant Engagement Plan educational and personal growth activities for participants Coordinate activities to expose students to future career opportunities Recruitment & Outreach Visit all schools within assigned caseload Recruit program participants within target schools Data Management & Compliance Maintain student’s academic records and files securely Keep participant’s contact information up to date Staff Hiring, Training & Development Assist with summer personnel hiring process (interviews, hiring decisions)

The award-winning James B. Hunt Jr. Library on NC State’s Centennial Campus , offers access to advanced technologies that are enabling revolutionary ways to see and use information. Capturing NC State’s spirit of innovation in education and research, the Hunt Library is recognized as one of the world’s most creative and inspirational learning and collaborative spaces and a model for “the library of the future.” The D. H. Hill Jr. Library , serving the main campus , combines the best of tradition and innovation, housing special collections and a beautiful gallery alongside vibrant, experiential spaces for making, digital media creation, data analysis and visualization, and collaboration. Three branch libraries focus on design, natural resources, and veterinary medicine. The NC State University Libraries invites applications and nominations for the position of Research Data Facilitator . The Research Facilitation Service ( RFS ) is a university initiative led by the Libraries in collaboration with the Office of Information Technology ( OIT ) and the Office of Research and Innovation ( ORI ) to provide essential support for NC State’s research enterprise. It offers a single point of contact for researchers who need assistance identifying and accessing research computing and data services and support, serves as a communication conduit for service providers, and conducts continuous assessment of researcher needs and available research computing and data services.
Wolfpack Perks and Benefits: As a Pack member, you belong here, and can enjoy exclusive perks designed to enhance your personal and professional well-being. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone. What we offer: Medical , Dental , and Vision Flexible Spending Account Retirement Programs Disability Plans Life Insurance Accident Plan Paid Time Off and Other Leave Programs 12 Holidays Each Year Tuition and Academic Assistance And so much more! Attain Work-life balance with our Childcare benefits, Wellness & Recreation Membership , and Wellness Programs that aim to build a thriving wolfpack community. Disclaimer: Perks and Benefit eligibility is based on Part-Time or Full-Time Employment status. Eligibility and Employer Sponsored Plans can be found within each of the links offered.
Essential Job Duties: The Research Data Facilitator provides lifecycle research data management support across all disciplines, offering assistance and guidance from project planning through closeout. In collaboration with RFS , OIT , and Libraries colleagues, the incumbent consults with faculty and student researchers around best practices, tools, and strategies for data storage, movement, sharing, and preservation. They work with ORI colleagues and other collaborators to support researchers in drafting and operationalizing data management plans and ensuring compliance with funder requirements. They partner with colleagues to develop secure and compute-integrated data curation and handling pipelines, and to identify appropriate data repositories or other infrastructure for open data sharing and long-term archiving. The Research Data Facilitator works with the RFS team to develop and deliver training, workshops, documentation, and outreach materials to help NC State researchers leverage a broad range of computational and data resources and meet data sharing expectations from publishers and funders. Informed by this work, the position conducts ongoing tracking and assessment of researcher needs and the university landscape of available services and resources. The position deeply considers how their approach to their daily work reflects and advances the Libraries’ Strategic Plan , creating an environment and community that is welcoming for both patrons and colleagues alike. The position works closely with colleagues throughout the Libraries and with university partners, participates in library planning, and serves on library and campus-wide committees, task forces, and teams. Librarians are expected to be active professionally and to contribute to developments in the field. The position reports to the Director, Research Facilitation Service. This position is based in North Carolina. This position is eligible for flexible hours with a hybrid work environment and will require occasional onsite work. NC State promotes an integrated approach to problem solving that transforms lives and provides leadership for social, economic, and technological development across North Carolina and around the world. NC State’s land grant mission of teaching, research and service is dedicated to the service of North Carolina and its people. Applicants are encouraged to review the institution’s mission, vision and strategic plan, and consider how their background, interest and experience would enable them to support the university.

Applicants are encouraged to view the application process as an opportunity to demonstrate how they think, approach, and communicate their own work, including carefully considering their use of generative AI in their materials. Applicants are furthermore encouraged to think broadly about and communicate how their skills and experiences transfer to the qualifications below, including in ways that may not be obvious, such as how non-library-specific skills and experiences speak to the position responsibilities. We strongly encourage and welcome applicants with a variety of backgrounds, interests, and experiences to apply for this position. Demonstrated knowledge of best practices for research data management Experience providing research data support; awareness of compliance issues surrounding research data, including federal requirements and granting agency practices Demonstrated understanding of how researchers use high-performance computing, networking, collaborative research tools, cloud storage and computing, and other advanced cyberinfrastructure technologies, including tools for pipelines and data transfer Ability to manage relationships with stakeholders in a multidisciplinary environment Ability to serve and collaborate with a large user community reflecting a variety of backgrounds and disciplines Ability to work independently, creatively, and collaboratively in a team environment and contribute to operational efficiency Ability to foster an environment of belonging and well-being Evidence of ability for professional development and contribution

title: UTS - Temporary Purchasing & Operations Assistant at NC State
description: Position Summary The Temporary Purchasing & Operations Assistant provides vital operational, processing, and administrative support for Purchasing Services. Responsibilities include generating purchase orders, managing the team inbox, supporting invoice payment workflows, and handling general logistics to ensure seamless daily operations.

title: Extension EFNEP Educator (Program Assistant / Associate - Youth/Adult)
description: NC Cooperative Extension in Cabarrus County is seeking an Extension EFNEP Program Assistant. The Extension EFNEP Program Assistant (PA) serves as an employee of NC Cooperative Extension and NC State University and delivers nutrition education to limited-resource adults, families, and school-aged youth who meet federal eligibility requirements for participation in the Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program (EFNEP). Under the overall supervision of the County Extension Director (CED) and with programmatic guidance from the Regional Nutrition Extension Associate (RNEA), the EFNEP PA implements approved nutrition education curricula and teaching methods in individual and group settings. The position recruits and enrolls eligible participants, with an emphasis on reaching Spanish-speaking families, and provides practical instruction in nutrition, food preparation, and related healthy living practices in both English and Spanish. The EFNEP PA also works collaboratively with Cooperative Extension personnel, community agencies, and partner organizations to expand program outreach, recruit volunteers, connect participants with additional resources, and enhance the visibility and impact of EFNEP within the assigned service area.

title: Sous Chef
description: Bring your passion for food and teamwork to NC State Dining! We are hiring a Sous Chef at Fountain Dining Hall . As a Sous Chef, you’ll be part of a team that brings quality, care, and consistency to food served on campus. You will manage and monitor all activities in the kitchen, assign work to kitchen staff, enforce operational standards and serve as back-up to the unit chef in their absence. Key responsibilities include but not limited to: Follow and maintain the highest of culinary standards in all food areas, including the kitchen, serving line and display stations. Responsible for the quality of the food to be cooked, seasoned, and held correctly, according to the set recipes, and presented in an attractive manner. Execute the production of recipes required to fulfill the menu. Plan daily food production and assign staff accordingly to execute the plan. Review daily production sheets and check preparations amounts for accuracy and coordinate the flow of food in the unit. Maintain a clean, safe and efficient work environment in accordance with university and departmental guidelines. Responsible for face to face customer service and satisfaction. Communicate with personnel to ensure adequate amount of food for service while controlling overproduction. Respond to operational needs and challenges with professionalism and adaptability. May pick up or deliver food/supplies to other dining locations. This role requires physical stamina, including the ability to lift 30 pounds above head and up to 60 pounds on rare occasions, work in hot and cold conditions, and safely handle sharp tools and hot surfaces (all with or without reasonable accommodations). If you take pride in your work, enjoy being part of a collaborative team, and thrive in a dynamic environment where professionalism, adaptability, and customer service matter, this is your opportunity to make a meaningful impact in the heart of campus life.
