title: Teaching Assistant Professor
description: The Department of World Languages & Cultures at NC State University seeks applicants with demonstrable teaching excellence and ongoing commitment to undergraduate Greek and Latin language instruction as well as the ability to teach courses in classical literature and culture in translation. We especially seek applicants who are interested in developing innovative pedagogical strategies and reimagining the goals and methods of Classical Studies to embrace the needs and concerns of students across a broad range of majors in a large, land-grant state institution. The teaching load is 4/4, with a variety of in-person and asynchronous online courses. The ideal candidate will also be qualified to help with recently implemented courses and study abroad programs in Italy and Greece, assist with plans for secondary Latin education in North Carolina, and develop stronger ties with the Greek community in the Triangle.

title: Temporary-Technical/Paraprofessional
description: The North Carolina Institute for Climate Studies (NCICS) in Asheville, NC is currently seeking two temporary student interns to work remotely on a new project. This internship will involve working with NCICS scientists and NOAA collaborators in the application of machine learning techniques to analyze environmental observations and satellite data, with the goal of improving understanding of extreme event impacts in communities in the southeastern U.S. The student(s) will collaborate with other interns during the project to learn state-of-the-art machine learning models and tools, as well as other advanced data analytics skills.

title: Assistant Director
description: The Assistant Director is a full-time, 12-month, non-tenure track staff (EPS) position and a key member of the Academic Success Center (ASC) leadership team. In this role you will work closely with the Director and ASC colleagues, provide leadership for the Undergraduate and Graduate Writing Centers, and contribute to the Center’s teaching, training, programming, assessment, and strategic planning. This position offers an opportunity to shape high-impact writing and speaking support services and build partnerships that strengthen student learning across the University. Key responsibilities include: Administration and Program Leadership Provide independent oversight of the Undergraduate and Graduate Writing Centers, including hiring, scheduling, training, and supporting writing and speaking tutors. Establish and maintain effective data collection and reporting processes; analyze tutoring outcomes and communicate findings to relevant stakeholders to inform program improvement. Collaborate with the Director and ASC team to develop, implement, and evaluate policies, procedures, and initiatives that advance the Center’s goals. Programming and Partnerships Develop and deliver workshops, classroom presentations, and other resources that support writing and speaking across the curriculum. Build and maintain productive partnerships with key campus units, including the Libraries, Graduate School, First Year Writing Program, English as a Second Language Program, and Campus Writing and Speaking Program. Represent the Academic Success Center with campus and external constituents as requested by the Director. Teaching and Training Teach a one-credit writing and speaking tutor-training course each semester. Lead training and professional development that prepares writing and speaking consultants to provide effective, high-quality support to students. Supervision and Leadership Supervise a graduate assistant who supports the training and development of writing and speaking consultants. Provide strategic direction, coaching, and ongoing feedback to ensure the graduate assistant’s work supports ASC priorities and program objectives. You will bring strong organizational, communication, teaching, and program leadership skills, along with the ability to manage multiple priorities and build effective partnerships across campus. This is an opportunity to contribute to a collaborative academic support environment while helping advance programs that strengthen students’ writing and speaking skills and academic success.

title: Senior Analyst/Project Manager, Student Systems
description: As a Senior Analyst/Project Manager, you will play a key role in maintaining and enhancing NC State University’s complex PeopleSoft Student Information System. You will lead and contribute to enterprise application development projects, translating complex business and technical requirements into effective solutions that support critical student services across Admissions, Student Records, Advisement, Student Financials, and Financial Aid. Serving as a senior member of a team of analysts and/or programmers to maintain our Student Information System (SIS) within a technically complex environment. Working with the IT Director and Managers, Team Members, and Functional Offices in order to design, build, and implement moderate to advanced enterprise application development projects at NC State University with minimal supervision. Interpreting highly complex business processes and technological functions to develop specifications and provide input to management and customers on the appropriate resource and technology for automated solutions. Designing and executing regression testing, performance testing and quality assurance testing in an accurate and timely manner. Serving as a project manager/analyst on the Student Information System Applications Development Team across all modules including Student Admissions, Student Records, Advisement, Student Financials, and Financial Aid. Researching and keeping abreast of new technologies to evaluate feasibility for organizational needs. Possessing a strong understanding of the PeopleSoft Student Information System. Key Responsibilities: Serve as a senior member of the Student Information System (SIS) Applications Development Team, maintaining and enhancing enterprise applications within a technically complex environment. Collaborate with IT leadership, team members, and functional offices to design, build, and implement moderate to advanced enterprise application development projects with minimal supervision. Interpreting highly complex business processes and technological functions to develop specifications and recommend appropriate resources and technologies for automated solutions. Serve as a project manager/analyst across SIS modules, including Student Admissions, Student Records, Advisement, Student Financials, and Financial Aid. Design and execute regression, performance, and quality assurance testing to ensure application functionality, reliability, and performance. Research emerging technologies and evaluate their feasibility and potential application to organizational needs. In this role, you will have the opportunity to contribute to critical enterprise systems that support NC State’s student services and help shape technology solutions across the university. If you are an experienced application development professional with a strong understanding of PeopleSoft Student Information Systems and a passion for solving complex business and technology challenges, we welcome you to apply.

title: Temporary Plant Evolutionary Ecology Field Technician
description: The Sheth plant evolutionary ecology lab in the Department of Plant and Microbial Biology at North Carolina State University (Raleigh, NC) is currently seeking field technician to participate in an NSF-funded study ( https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2220928&HistoricalAwards=false ) under the direction of Dr. Seema Sheth and in collaboration with Drs. Susana Wadgymar (Davidson College), Jill Anderson (University of Georgia), Megan DeMarche (University of Georgia), and Emily Josephs (Michigan State University). The project combines approaches from evolutionary biology, field ecology, and population genomics in a broadly distributed native plant species ( Chamaecrista fasciculata , Fabaceae) to forecast population dynamics range-wide under climate change. The technician will be part of a dynamic, dedicated, and engaged research group as well as a member of a multidisciplinary and multi-institution collaborative group that includes Botanic Garden and conservation professionals. The successful candidate will contribute to a collaborative study of eco-evolutionary responses to climate in the partridge pea, Chamaecrista fasciculata , an annual legume that grows in disturbed habitats in central and eastern North America. The technician’s primary responsibilities involve collaborating with the PIs and other researchers to establish and maintain a large common garden experiment and to collect data from ~6,000 transplanted seeds at Mason Farm Biological Reserve in Chapel Hill, NC. This work includes preparing seeds for planting, planting seeds, setting up the garden infrastructure, building open-top chambers, collecting data on traits and fitness, entering data, maintenance tasks in the garden (e.g., weeding), processing samples in the lab, and communicating with Dr. Sheth and other team members. The technician will also have opportunities to train and mentor undergraduate students and work with graduate students. Start/End Dates: Exact start and end dates are flexible; this is a time-limited appointment for a maximum of 11 months. Work Schedule: Working hours are typically between 6-7 AM and 5-6 PM Monday through Friday, but there may be occasional need for hours before or after these times, and on weekends. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. Due to the large volume of applicants, we will not be able to respond to individual emails about this position or meet with applicants prior to submission of application materials.

title: Cook
description: Are you passionate about food, teamwork, and fueling the next generation of leaders, innovators, and thinkers? NC State Dining is looking for an energetic and reliable Cook to join our culinary team. In this role, you won’t just be prepping food—you’ll be a vital part of the campus experience, ensuring our community enjoys fresh, delicious, and safely prepared meals every day. As a Cook , you will handle everything from recipe execution to leading station workflows. Your daily duties will include: Master the Menu: Execute standard and routine recipes with precision to fulfill daily menus and keep our food stations stocked and looking great. Inventory & Logistics: Requisition the products you need, and help check in, store, and move food supplies to keep production running smoothly. Teamwork & Flow: Partner with front-of-house staff to coordinate a seamless flow of food from the kitchen to our guests, keeping track of food levels for timely service. Tech & Data: Step up in the absence of a supervising chef by entering necessary data into our Netmenu food production system . Kitchen Cleanliness: Maintain top-tier sanitation by cleaning utensils, workstations, tables, shelves, and equipment—and help delegate cleaning tasks to the back-of-house team. Lead by Example: Ensure daily prep lists are completed and products are properly rotated. You’ll also help assign tasks and direct the efforts of food service technicians, temporary staff, and student employees. Who You Are A team player who thrives in a fast-paced, high-energy environment. Detail-oriented about food safety, cleanliness, and recipe accuracy. A positive motivator who enjoys guiding and directing student and temporary staff. Reliable, punctual, and proud of the food you put out. At NC State, we cultivate a welcoming community of collaboration and growth. You’ll enjoy a vibrant campus environment, stable scheduling, and the opportunity to grow your culinary career with a trusted university employer. Ready to bring your passion to our kitchen? Apply today and help us keep NC State well-fed and moving forward!

title: Administrative Support Specialist
description: Support one of NC State's premier research facilities by helping ensure the efficient day-to-day operations of the NC State Phytotron. In this role, you will provide administrative, financial, and operational support that enables researchers to effectively utilize the facility while contributing to the smooth management of its business operations, records, and information systems. Key Responsibilities Administrative & Customer Support Serve as the primary point of contact for researchers, NC State employees, and visitors, providing administrative support and coordinating daily facility operations. Financial & Operational Administration Assist with financial administration by maintaining billing and financial records, supporting the use of facility funds, managing personnel files, and ensuring accurate administrative documentation. Information & Facility Support Support the maintenance and enhancement of the Phytotron website, internal network, and facility-related data to promote efficient operations and access to information. If you are an organized, detail-oriented professional who enjoys supporting research operations and providing outstanding administrative service, we encourage you to apply and become an important part of the NC State Phytotron team.

title: Open Rank Professional Faculty in Social Work
description: The School of Social Work invites applications for an open-rank professional-track position. The faculty member in this position will serve as BSW Practicum Coordinator, a role which includes building and maintaining relationships with practicum agencies, arranging practicum placements for undergraduate students, serving as liaison between the School of Social Work and practicum agencies, serving on the practicum leadership team, and supporting students by leading practicum seminars. Professional-track faculty members are expected to demonstrate excellence in teaching and advising. Faculty members may be expected to participate actively in community extension, engagement, and service to the school, college, university, and profession. We seek candidates with teaching experience in social work theory, practice, research, and policy. Primary teaching responsibilities will be in the School’s Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) program and/or Master of Social Work (MSW) program. The typical teaching load of 4 courses per semester will be reduced to account for practicum coordination responsibilities.

title: Assistant General Manager
description: NC State Dining is seeking a hands-on Assistant General manager to manage day-to-day operations in Fountain Dining Hall. The primary purpose of this position is to serve as the Assistant General Manager over daily operations of a dining hall located on the NC State University campus. The main focus or priority for this position will be to provide independent decision making in the day to day management for the dining hall and reports to the unit General Manager. Duties include, but are not limited to: Oversee the daily operations of Fountain Dining Hall, exercising independent judgment to ensure efficient service, operational excellence, and a positive guest experience. Supervise, schedule, and develop permanent, temporary, and student employees, including supporting recruitment, hiring, training, and performance management activities. Lead by example in delivering exceptional customer service and fostering a positive, team-oriented work environment. Maintain an active ServSafe certification and ensure compliance with all food safety, sanitation, and Wake County Health Department regulations. Partner with the General Manager to manage staffing, control operating costs, and achieve budgetary and operational goals. If you are a motivated leader with a passion for hospitality and team development, we encourage you to apply!

title: Dean - College of Engineering
description: Reporting to the Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost, the dean serves as the chief academic, administrative and budgetary officer and principal spokesperson for the College of Engineering. The dean provides strategic leadership for the college’s nine academic departments, research centers and institutes, academic programs, faculty, staff and students, while advancing the college's mission of excellence in education, research and engagement. As a member of the university's academic leadership team, you will work collaboratively with fellow deans, university leadership and external partners to advance NC State's strategic priorities and strengthen engineering's role in addressing society's most pressing challenges. You will foster an environment that supports excellence in teaching, research, innovation, entrepreneurship and public engagement while ensuring student success and preparing graduates to lead in an increasingly complex and technology-driven world. Key responsibilities:: Strategic Leadership & Growth: Providing visionary leadership that advances the College of Engineering's strategic priorities and strengthens its national and international reputation. Serving as a collaborative member of the university's leadership team and advocating effectively for the college within the university while contributing to institution-wide priorities. Providing strategic leadership for the college's continued growth, including expansion of academic programs, research infrastructure and state-supported capital investments. People & Academic Excellence: Recruiting, retaining, supporting, and developing an outstanding faculty, staff, and student community while cultivating an environment where all members can thrive and contribute fully. Recognizing and valuing the contributions of everyone in the college, encouraging the high performance and excellence of faculty, staff and units within the college and the delivery of high-quality academic programs. Adapting the college’s programs to shifting educational landscape and leading advancement of engineering education. Research & Partnerships: Strengthening the college's nationally recognized research enterprise by supporting interdisciplinary scholarship, expanding sponsored research and fostering collaboration across the university and with external partners; Building strategic partnerships with industry, government, national laboratories, alumni and philanthropic partners that enhance the college's educational, research and economic impact. Engagement & Institutional Impact: Engaging with internal and external constituencies regarding the development implementation, and evaluation of programs. Leading comprehensive fundraising efforts in partnership with University Advancement, the NC State Engineering Foundation and the Engineering Foundation Board of Directors to secure philanthropic support for the college's strategic priorities. Stewardship & Resources: Managing the college's financial and physical resources with transparency, accountability and sound stewardship while effectively advocating for new investments. If you are ready to bring your scholarship, leadership and vision to an opportunity with broad impact, we invite you to consider the role of Dean. You will have the opportunity to shape the college’s future, cultivate a strong academic community, and advance its contributions through research, teaching and service.

title: EFNEP Educator, Program Assistant
description: The Extension EFNEP Educator is an employee of NC Cooperative Extension, NC State University. Under the supervision of the County Extension Director with guided assistance from the District EFNEP Regional Nutrition Extension Associate (RNEA), the EFNEP Educator delivers nutrition and related subject matter to enrolled participants.

title: TAU Technician
description: Technician needed to assist with animal husbandry, including milking dairy cows and the daily feeding and care of livestock; hay distribution and assistance with general farm tasks as needed.

title: Director of Research Administration
description: The College of Engineering’s Director of Research Administration provides executive leadership, strategic direction, and operational governance across the full research lifecycle. Reporting to the Assistant Dean for Personnel and Administration & Interim Assistant Dean for College Operations, with a dotted-line reporting relationship to the Associate Dean for Research and Infrastructure, the Director leads the implementation and evolution of the College’s new Research Administration Hub Operating Model—a shared-services approach designed to strengthen and scale research administration across the College. The Director oversees a distributed network of approximately 50 research administration professionals, including Associate Directors, Hub Managers, and Sponsored Research Administrators, supporting academic departments, affiliated units, major research centers, and extension and outreach programs. In partnership with college leadership, the Director will anticipate and forecast research administration capacity and support needs as the college’s research portfolio, faculty and principal investigators, staff, and student population grow. In the role, you have the opportunity to shape how this new model operates and evolves at scale, partnering with senior College leadership to align research administration strategy, organizational capacity, workload, and risk with the College’s research priorities. Your proven leadership will help create a more consistent and scalable faculty and principal investigator experience, strengthen service delivery, improve proposal competitiveness, and position the College to effectively manage increasingly complex research portfolios with strong financial and regulatory stewardship. Key Responsibilities will fall within the following core functional areas: Executive Leadership, Research Administration Hub Governance & Strategic Initiatives: Lead the strategy, evolution, and operational governance of the College’s Research Administration Hub model, aligning research administration with College research priorities, faculty and principal investigator needs, and long-term growth. Advise the Dean, Associate Dean for Research and Infrastructure, and other senior leaders on research administration strategy, organizational capacity, emerging needs, and risk. Shape the administrative infrastructure for large-scale, multidisciplinary and multi-institutional research initiatives, including major center proposals, complex subrecipient relationships, institutional cost sharing, and industry partnerships. Establish enterprise-wide standards, service expectations, professional development, and leadership pathways that strengthen consistency, accountability, and long-term capacity across the research administration organization. Enterprise Capacity, Resource Allocation & Service Delivery: Lead enterprise-wide workload and capacity planning across research administration hubs, centers, and affiliated units, using research activity and organizational needs to inform resource allocation. Direct strategic deployment of resources during high-volume sponsor deadlines, staffing transitions, and other periods of heightened demand to sustain faculty and principal investigator support and operational continuity. Identify and scale effective practices across the College while balancing standardized service delivery with the distinct needs of a complex research enterprise. Research Intelligence, Analytics & Executive Reporting: Transform research administration and portfolio data into actionable intelligence by evaluating and adapting emerging tools, technologies, and approaches to integrate data, surface insights, and improve access to information that informs College strategy, resource decisions, research growth, and operational priorities. Lead executive-level reporting on research activity such as NSF HERD, USNWR, ASEE, proposal performance, sponsor trends, research strengths, interdisciplinary activity, and center performance. Establish meaningful performance measures that assess service effectiveness, identify opportunities for improvement, and demonstrate the impact of the Research Administration Hub model. Research Compliance, Risk Management & Institutional Stewardship: Provide strategic oversight of complex research administration requirements, financial stewardship, effort commitments, cost sharing, project modifications, and other regulatory obligations. Anticipate and mitigate operational and compliance risks while guiding College leaders through complex, high-impact research administration matters. Represent the College with central research administration offices and university-wide initiatives, strengthening institutional alignment and advocating for effective, scalable research administration practices. We are seeking a leader who can communicate with clarity, build trust, influence across organizational boundaries, and turn a compelling vision into an effective and sustainable research administration enterprise. If you are energized by the opportunity to shape a new model for research administration and lead meaningful change at the College level, we invite you to bring your perspective and leadership to this role.

title: Open Rank Assistant / Associate/ Professor of Practice, Finance
description: The Department of Finance in the Poole College of Management at North Carolina State University invites applications for a full-time, non-tenure-track open-rank Professor of the Practice in Finance . The position will support the department’s undergraduate and graduate programs, with particular opportunities to contribute in areas such as investments, capital markets, portfolio management, financial management, and related areas. The successful candidate will be expected to: Deliver high-quality instruction in finance at the undergraduate and graduate (MBA) levels. Teach courses in both in-person and online formats. Leverage professional and industry experience to connect classroom learning with current practices and developments in financial markets. Build and maintain relationships with industry partners to create meaningful experiential learning, professional networking, and career-development opportunities for students. Engage with and support student finance organizations and related extracurricular activities. Contribute to the academic mission of the Department of Finance and Poole College of Management through service, professional engagement, and collaboration with faculty and staff. Professors of the Practice typically teach three course sections (nine credit hours) per semester. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in teaching, student engagement, and connecting academic learning with professional practice. Faculty rank and compensation will be determined based on the successful candidate’s qualifications, professional experience, and credentials. Appointment Details The anticipated start date is August 16, 2027.

title: Academic Program Manager
description: In collaboration with the Institute Director and faculty, in this role you will oversee the day-to-day administration and delivery of academic programs for the Institute for Advanced Analytics (IAA). You will coordinate curriculum resources, instructional schedules, academic processes, student services, and program activities to support a high-quality graduate education experience. Serving as a key liaison among IAA leadership, faculty, students, university offices, alumni, industry partners, and other stakeholders, the Academic Program Manager ensures academic operations are organized, responsive, and aligned with university policies and IAA goals. The role requires sound judgment, discretion, strong organization, independence, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced graduate education environment. Duties include: Academic Program Administration Coordinate the day-to-day administration of IAA academic programs, including academic calendars, course schedules, program milestones, and curriculum-related activities. Partner with IAA leadership and faculty on academic planning, program changes, continuous improvement, and special initiatives. Interpret and apply university academic policies and procedures and serve as a resource to faculty, staff, and students. Monitor academic requirements, processes, and deadlines to ensure accurate and timely completion. Data, Assessment, and Reporting Maintain accurate academic records, databases, and program documentation. Compile and analyze enrollment, student progression, graduation, placement, engagement, and other program data to identify trends and opportunities for improvement. Prepare reports, presentations, and other materials to support program assessment, accreditation, institutional reporting, and strategic planning. Coordinate with Registration and Records, the Graduate School, Admissions, Career Development, Student Services, and other university partners to support academic operations and compliance. Student Success and Services Coordinate orientation, academic milestones, graduation activities, and other student programs. Advise students on academic policies, program requirements, deadlines, and university resources; monitor progress and coordinate appropriate interventions or referrals when needed. Support student engagement, professional development, networking, and career-related programming. Manage student communications and maintain accurate program records. Faculty and Instructional Support Support faculty in planning and delivering courses and academic activities, including teaching assignments, course materials, classroom needs, and instructional schedules. Coordinate academic logistics and serve as a liaison between IAA faculty and university administrative offices. Program Events and Communications Plan and coordinate orientation, Open House, recruitment, graduation, student presentation, alumni, and other academic program events. Develop and distribute timely communications for students, faculty, alumni, prospective students, and external partners. Maintain program websites, calendars, digital communications, and other informational resources, and coordinate marketing and promotional activities with IAA leadership and university partners. You will play an integral role in connecting people, processes, and resources to ensure the IAA’s academic programs operate effectively and students are positioned for success. This is an opportunity to contribute to a nationally recognized graduate program while working closely with faculty, university partners, students, alumni, and industry to strengthen the overall academic experience.

title: Fiscal Manager
description: As the Fiscal Manager, you will provide senior-level financial management, analysis, and regulatory oversight for sponsored research awards across NC State University. Reporting to the Office of Post-Award Financial Services, you will ensure the financial integrity, compliance, and accurate revenue cycle management of federal, state, and private contracts, grants, and cooperative agreements. In this role, you will independently interpret complex award guidelines, approve financial transactions, submit official sponsor financial reports and invoices under delegated authority, and serve as a primary post-award financial subject matter expert and collaborative partner to college and departmental research administrators and principal investigators across the University. Key Responsibilities: Professional Knowledge Apply extensive knowledge of federal and state research administration requirements, including Uniform Guidance (2 CFR 200), OMB Circulars, Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), GAAP, and COSO internal control frameworks, to interpret and execute post-award requirements across the University. Evaluate award documents, proposals, and RFPs to establish project setups and determine appropriate financial attributes, including purpose and budget codes, billing frequency, indirect cost rates, cost-share requirements, and closeout parameters. Monitor sponsored research financial activity for compliance with federal, state, sponsor, and University requirements and identify potential audit risks. Maintain current expertise in evolving research administration regulations and contribute to professional development and institutional process improvement initiatives. Design and deliver training for central post-award staff and college and departmental research administrators to strengthen financial and compliance knowledge. Financial Management, Monitoring & Analysis Manage financial analysis, revenue management, and accounting controls throughout thelifecycle of sponsored research awards. Manage system-generated and manual invoicing, accounts receivable, letter-of-credit draw-down analyses, and debt collection activities to support effective revenue management and institutional cash flow. Prepare, reconcile, and submit complex financial reports, cost-share reports, and billing statements under delegated authority, ensuring alignment with sponsor requirements, technical performance, and reporting deadlines. Conduct detailed account reconciliations, analyze expenditure trends, investigate discrepancies, and process budget reallocations, cost transfers, and accounting adjustments. Oversee award lifecycle transitions, including setup reviews, prior approval requests, carryover and budget modifications, time extensions, audit support, and final closeout procedures. Communication & Stakeholder Engagement Serve as a primary liaison and financial advisor to principal investigators, departmental research administrators, institutional leadership, and external sponsors. Provide proactive guidance on award status, financial performance, regulatory requirements, and upcoming deadlines while building collaborative partnerships across campus. Translate complex financial and compliance requirements into clear guidance for non-financial stakeholders and navigate sensitive award issues with sound professional judgment. Conduct financial reviews and consultation meetings with departmental research personnel to assess new, active, and expiring sponsored awards. Facilitate cross-training initiatives that strengthen operational continuity across central post-award contract and grant functions. Decision-Making & Problem Solving Apply advanced analytical skills and delegated authority to resolve complex, non-routine post-award financial and regulatory issues. Serve as a central resource for evaluating complex compliance matters and balancing sponsor requirements with University policy to develop appropriate, data-informed solutions. Evaluate financial risk, investigate transaction discrepancies, and implement corrective actions to maintain institutional compliance. Exercise independent judgment and delegated signature authority to approve or deny administrative requests, policy exceptions, and financial modifications based on applicable contract and grant terms.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Population Medicine and Career Success
description: The Assistant/Associate Professor of Population Medicine and Career Success specializes in Large Animal Population Medicine and Veterinary Education Scholarship. This dynamic role is designed for an innovative educator and researcher ready to shape the future of veterinary medicine by blending cutting-edge clinical instruction with ground-breaking educational research. This position plays a central role in delivering our core DVM curriculum while building a nationally recognized research program that drives innovation in farm animal health, AI integration, immersive learning, and student well-being. Teaching: Based on specific focus, this faculty member will contribute to population medicine and career readiness teaching in existing core, elective and selective courses. The faculty member will also have the option to participate in teaching and/or proposing new selective, elective or special topics courses. Interested individuals may contribute to ongoing development of house officer and graduate student competency-based training programs and trainee assessments. Research : This position is expected to establish an impactful, nationally recognized research program at the intersection of Large Animal Population Medicine and Veterinary Education Scholarship. This dual-focus program will address critical gaps in population health education by actively developing, implementing, and evaluating novel teaching methods. This position will focus on discovery that interrogates, innovates and transforms farm animal population health and career readiness training in veterinary education. The research will address gaps in knowledge and pivotal questions including, but not limited to, the following examples: Immersive Technologies and Virtual Reality (VR): Investigating the design, implementation, and educational efficacy of immersive virtual environments—such as "digital twin" models of production facilities, processing plants, or pasture ecosystems. This research will leverage VR to simulate complex, high-stakes population medicine scenarios (e.g., biosecurity breaches, foreign animal disease outbreaks, and large-scale herd epidemiology mapping). The focus will be on assessing how immersive environments support rapid systemic decision-making, epidemiological risk assessment, and spatial problem-solving without inducing real-world biosecurity or animal welfare risks. Competency-Based Veterinary Education (CBVE) & Advanced Assessments: Developing and validating robust, outcomes-based assessment methodologies. This includes creating standard-setting tools that reliably evaluate both technical execution (e.g., simulation-based herd analytics or theriogenology models) and non-technical professional competencies (e.g., communication, animal welfare advocacy, and One Health system collaboration). Experiential, Simulation, and Community-Engaged Learning: Evaluating the educational efficacy and scalable impact of ambulatory training and community-partnered outreach to bridge the gap between tertiary referral environments and general production practice. Comparing student learning outcomes relevant to population medicine in different clinical settings. Professional Identity Formation (PIF) and Career Sustainability: Investigating the longitudinal development of professional identity in DVM students and its explicit correlation to post-graduation career satisfaction, practitioner retention, and mental well-being. This research will evaluate how educational interventions, mentorship, and hidden curricula influence the psychological transition from student to clinician. Specifically, it will look at how to cultivate a resilient, "challenge-focused" professional identity within large animal and population medicine—equipping graduates to find career satisfaction while navigating the unique systemic, environmental, and socio-economic pressures intrinsic to production animal practice. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Digital Literacy: Investigating the integration of generative AI, intelligent tutoring systems, and clinical decision support models into the DVM curriculum. Research will evaluate how to foster AI literacy and "appropriate skepticism" while examining the cognitive risks of overreliance, algorithmic bias, and data privacy in production animal surveillance. This individual will join existing large and farm animal faculty and staff currently teaching population medicine and epidemiology in DVM years 1-4.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Large Animal Clinical Skills and Career Success
description: The Assistant/Associate Professor of Large Animal Clinical Skills and Career Success will join a dedicated group of faculty and staff currently teaching large animal clinical skills, medicine and surgery. A combination of models, simulations and farm animals at the Teaching Animal Unit and Reedy Creek Farm are used to facilitate assessments that can be used to develop skills portfolios and investigate best practices in feedback and remediation of clinical skills. Teaching: This faculty member will contribute to clinical skills, large animal and career readiness teaching in existing core, elective and selective courses. The faculty member will also have the option to participate in teaching and/or proposing new selective or elective courses. Interested individuals may contribute to ongoing development of house officer and graduate student competency-based training programs and trainee assessments. Research : This faculty member will establish an impactful and nationally recognized research program dedicated to advancing Large Animal Clinical Skills educational research. As veterinary curricula globally evolve to meet changing technological, societal, and agricultural needs, this position will drive evidence-based advancements in how veterinary students acquire, refine, and maintain large animal technical and clinical competencies. The faculty member will be expected to investigate current high-priority areas and address critical, unmapped gaps in knowledge within veterinary medical education. The prospective areas of educational research supported by this position include, but are not limited to: Simulation-Based Learning & Physical Model Innovation: Developing, validating, and optimizing large animal (equine, bovine, and production animal) procedural models, simulators and assessments (i.e. OSCEs, mini-CEX, etc.). A primary research gap in this domain is the critical lack of longitudinal data assessing the long-term transferability of skills from synthetic simulators to live animal clinical scenarios to practice, as well as addressing the historical "small animal bias" in existing commercial simulation tools. Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Digital Workflow Integration: Exploring the integration of generative AI, multimodal large language models, and AI-standardized stakeholders within clinical training and communication workflows. Research will target how to teach students to utilize AI safely, ethically, and responsibly for diagnostic reasoning and uncertainty management, while addressing student adoption challenges, cognitive overreliance, and technological biases. Competency-Based Veterinary Education (CBVE) & Assessment: Designing, implementing, and validating objective, standardized assessment instruments and grading frameworks for psychomotor skills. Research will focus on mapping competencies to pedagogical combinations that offer the highest cost-benefit ratios and efficacy for equine and production animal training. Remediation Strategies & Cognitive Load Management: Developing evidence-based intervention and remediation strategies for students experiencing difficulties with technical proficiency. This includes studying methods to lower student anxiety and ensure safety during the high-stakes transition from low-stress models to live, potentially unpredictable large animals. Spectrum of Care, Ethics, & Community-Engaged Learning: Investigating educational frameworks that prepare students to practice quality medicine across a spectrum of care, particularly in resource-limited, rural, or underserved environments. Research could address how experiential learning in these settings impacts clinical skill acquisition and influences veterinary workforce shortages in production animal medicine. Community-based Education Models & Educator Development: Assessing how the pedagogical characteristics, instructional proficiency, professional identity and career satisfaction of clinical educators affect student learning in off-campus clinical teaching environments. Research will target frameworks for standardizing educator professional development and mentoring ability among non-faculty clinical preceptors. Pipeline Development, Admissions Predictors, & Career Sustainability: Investigating the correlation between holistic DVM admissions criteria (e.g., non-cognitive attributes, rural or agricultural backgrounds, specific pre-veterinary experiences) and long-term career commitment to large animal and food supply veterinary medicine. Research in this domain will target the critical "pipeline leak"—the documented decline in large animal career interest that occurs over the course of the four-year professional curriculum. Prospective studies will explore how educational interventions, early tracking pathways, mentorship frameworks, and systemic support systems can mitigate burnout, bridge the pay-to-debt gap, and ensure the geographic and economic sustainability of the large animal veterinary workforce in rural and underserved areas. Wellbeing, Professional Identity, & Veterinary Humanities: Evaluating the intersections of clinical skills mastery with veterinary humanities, ethical reasoning, and professional identity formation. The program will examine how early, structured competence in large animal handling correlates with student self-care, resilience, and long-term career sustainability.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Department of Electrical Engineering (College of Engineering) and the College of Sciences (Department of Physics, Department of Mathematics) are searching for two (2) Postdoctoral Research Scholars in quantum computing at NC State University. The two positions will work synergistically on hybrid continuous-discrete-variable quantum computing, broadly defined. One position will focus on condensed matter physics, quantum simulation; the other position will focus on compilation, benchmark, and HPC simulation of quantum circuits. The postdocs will work with a cluster of vibrant quantum computing faculty at NC State, including Dr. Bojko Bakalov, Professor (Mathematics), Dr. Dror Baron (Electrical and Computer Engineering), Lex Kemper (Physics), Yuan Liu (Electrical and Computer Engineering, Computer Science, and Physics), Frank Mueller (Computer Science), and Huiyang Zhou (Electrical and Computer Engineering), with possible external collaborations with other universities and national lab. Other Duties and Responsibilities Explore relevant parameter regions for useful boson-fermi mixed quantum matter; Design, develop, and implement novel quantum algorithms to simulate them. Quantify resource requirements on simulation on hybrid CD-DV quantum processors under noise, and compare to qubit-based quantum computers; Explore compilation, benchmarking, HPC simulation, error mitigation, and error correction strategies on hybrid CV-DV quantum processors; Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to understand domain-specific requirements and integrate discoveries into the team's mission; Help to lead the project and mentor junior researchers; Publish research findings in reputable journals and conferences

title: Financial Operations Specialist
description: As the Financial Operations Specialist, you will serve as a professional accounting resource within the centralized Business Services unit, providing financial oversight and guidance across complex funding environments. You will apply accounting principles, regulatory requirements, and institutional policies to ensure the accurate classification, allowability, and appropriate treatment of financial activity across general ledger accounts and funding sources. A key focus of the role is providing accounting oversight for federally regulated CALS funding streams, including USDA NIFA, Hatch, Hatch Multistate, and Smith-Lever programs. You will interpret and apply federal, state, and institutional requirements to ensure expenditures meet allowability, allocability, and documentation standards while supporting compliance and mitigating institutional risk. Key Responsibilities Analyze CALS Ledger 4 project designations to identify underlying funding sources, including federal funds, state appropriations, and receipt-supported activities, and apply the appropriate accounting and regulatory requirements. Review and validate financial transactions across multiple funding sources and operational areas to ensure accurate classification, allowability, allocability, documentation, and compliance with institutional, state, and federal requirements. Provide accounting oversight and guidance for decentralized and centralized financial processes, including Procurement Card (PCard), Travel, Accounts Payable, and Accounts Receivable transactions. Review transactions submitted through departmental processes and centralized ServiceNow workflows and support accurate processing within PeopleSoft and coordination with the University Controller’s Office. Interpret accounting principles, university policies, and funding requirements to resolve complex financial issues, identify potential compliance concerns, and recommend appropriate corrective actions. Assess financial activity for potential errors, disallowed costs, reporting issues, and other compliance risks, and support timely resolution to maintain accurate financial records and reduce institutional risk. In this role, you will have the opportunity to provide meaningful accounting guidance, support responsible stewardship of university resources, and help ensure the integrity of financial activity across CALS. If you are an accounting professional who enjoys applying financial principles to complex funding environments and using sound judgment to support accurate, compliant financial operations, we welcome you to apply.

title: University Library Technician-Advanced
description: The University Library Technician applies technical, metadata, and data skills to support the increasingly complex responsibilities of monographic acquisitions and management for the Monographs Unit as well as the Acquisitions & Discovery department and the Libraries as a whole. This position assists with the acquisition, receipt, bibliographic control, and delivery of materials in all formats to facilitate use of, and access to, the Libraries’ collections. This position creates and maintains bibliographic, item, financial (purchase order, invoice, Pcard receipts), technical, and online data in the library’s integrated library system (ILS), university financial system, electronic resource management system (ERM), and related knowledge bases and vendor systems. This position handles complex ordering and receiving tasks and provides support for other Unit staff in these areas. They perform copy, complex copy and original cataloging for monographic resources in all formats and languages. They participate in complex electronic resource package work for the Libraries, including title list reconciliation processes, data quality control, cleaning and standardization, vendor and agent communication, knowledge base work, ERM data entry, and ILS work. The position participates in receiving and resolving cataloging concerns and questions across the Libraries, as well as electronic resource access troubleshooting and problem resolution utilizing a ticketing system and communicating with stakeholders. This position participates in creating, editing, updating and maintaining workflow documentation. This position provides daily monitoring and troubleshooting of all monographic ordering streams. They manage both manual and automated vendor invoice and order record loads, troubleshoots file load errors, and performs invoice and vendor account reconciliation. They participate in short and long term projects undertaken by the Monographs Unit and the Department, and they serve on cross-departmental teams. The position may also collaborate with the Monographs Unit head to develop acquisitions workflows and/or cataloging guidelines workflows for new formats, and may also assist with the training of new staff.

description:

About the Department: The Department of Crop and Soil Sciences encompasses diverse disciplines in research extension and teaching. The department’s mission is to develop future leaders in crop, soil, and environmental sciences, improve crop plants and products, devise effective and sustainable crop production systems, devise effective and sustainable soil management techniques in both agriculture and urban settings; and disseminate crop, soil, and environmental science knowledge for the benefit of users and producers of food, feed turf, biofuels and fiber in North Carolina, the nation and the world.

Essential Job Duties: As the Research Technician, you will provide technical and operational support for applied weed science research focused on soybean and small grains. You will conduct and support field, greenhouse, and laboratory research evaluating herbicides and weed management strategies, working closely with faculty, students, research station personnel, and collaborators to support research activities and generate reliable data. Key Responsibilities: Establish and maintain weed science field experiments, including field preparation, plot layout, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and other activities necessary to maintain experimental integrity. Prepare, calibrate, and apply herbicide treatments according to research protocols and pesticide label requirements using backpack, CO₂-pressurized, tractor-mounted, and other application equipment. Operate, clean, maintain, and perform routine repairs on tractors, planters, sprayers, mowers, utility vehicles, harvest equipment, and other agricultural research equipment. Collect, record, and maintain accurate research data, including weed control, crop injury, weed density, crop growth, plant populations, biomass, and yield. Assist with greenhouse and laboratory research activities, including planting, plant maintenance, herbicide applications, sample collection, and sample processing. Maintain accurate records of research treatments, pesticide applications, field activities, samples, and experimental data, and maintain herbicides, supplies, equipment, and research facilities in accordance with institutional and pesticide safety requirements. Travel to research stations, cooperating farms, and other locations to support research trials, Extension demonstrations, and field days. Work collaboratively with faculty, students, research station personnel, and other collaborators to support accurate, safe, and timely completion of research activities. If you are interested in applying your technical skills to applied weed science research and supporting field, greenhouse, and laboratory research activities, we welcome you to apply for the Research Technician position.
Other Responsibilities: Assist with supervision and training of temporary employees, undergraduate workers, and graduate students in field research procedures. Communicate field conditions, equipment issues, treatment concerns, and research observations to the supervising faculty member and research team to ensure experiments are completed accurately and on schedule. Support outreach activities associated with the Weed Science Program.
Minimum Experience/Education: Demonstrated possession of the competencies necessary to perform the work.
Preferred Qualifications: Previous experience working in small-plot agricultural or weed science research. Experience operating and maintaining agricultural equipment. Experience collecting, organizing, and managing research data and records using ARM , Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, or similar electronic data systems. Experience coordinating research activities and priorities while working collaboratively with graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, research station personnel, visiting scientists, and other research team members. Ability to work outdoors in varying environmental conditions while performing physically active tasks, including lifting up to 50 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.

title: Line Technician II
description: Join NC State’s Utilities and Engineering Department , where your expertise helps power a thriving campus community. We’re seeking a dedicated and skilled Utilities Line Technician II to help maintain and enhance the University’s electrical power system, supporting over 2,000 acres of facilities, classrooms, and research spaces. In this role, you’ll play a vital part in ensuring safe, reliable, and efficient power distribution across all NC State campuses . If you take pride in technical precision, problem-solving, and teamwork, this is your opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the daily life and operations of the Wolfpack community. Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Construct, operate, maintain, and repair the university’s electrical power systems, including both underground and overhead lines. Perform scheduled preventative and predictive maintenance on electrical systems and facilities across all campuses (North, South, Central, CVM, Arboretum, Stadium, and Centennial). Operate, maintain, and repair campus emergency generators. Maintain and repair campus street and area lighting systems. Construct and install power system components, equipment, and facilities to deliver electric service to new and existing buildings. Inspect systems to determine maintenance needs and establish repair priorities . Troubleshoot and resolve electrical issues using diagnostic instruments, including Fluke meters, voltmeters, and power meters, as well as computer tracking software. Identify and mitigate safety hazards related to electric shock, falls, burns, and chemical exposure. Plan and execute daily work activities efficiently to meet department objectives. Operate specialized equipment, including a line truck, as required. Collaborate with other power distribution electricians and escalate complex issues to a supervisor or team lead as needed. Lift and transport materials weighing up to 90 pounds with or without reasonable accommodations and perform a wide range of physically demanding tasks in varied outdoor environments, ensuring safe handling practices and maintaining productivity in varying weather and terrain conditions. If you’re ready to bring your technical skills to a university that values your contribution and supports your growth, apply today and help us continue to power NC State’s mission of teaching, research, and service.

title: Large Animal Clinical Technician Supervisor
description: The Large Animal Clinical Technician Supervisor is responsible for leading and overseeing the veterinary technician and assistant staff within the Equine and Farm Animal Veterinary Center (EFAVC). This role ensures an exceptional clinical learning environment for fourth-year veterinary students, provides high-level technical support across specialty services, and maintains superior patient care and customer service standards. Primary Responsibilities: Staff Management & Operational Leadership Direct, coordinate, and schedule EFAVC Clinical Technicians and assistants to ensure seamless daily clinical operations. Consult daily with specialty clinicians to align staffing support with patient care demands and service workflows. Support personnel across all EFAVC specialty areas, including: Equine Medicine Equine Soft Tissue Equine Orthopedics Equine Rehabilitation & Sports Medicine Farm Animal Internal Medicine & Surgery Farm Animal Field Services Quality Care & Safety Protocol Management Oversee patient care workflows to guarantee high-quality, timely medical delivery. Enforce rigorous infectious disease prevention, biosecurity, and sanitation policies. Maintain a clean, sanitary, safe, and fully operational hospital environment compliant with safety regulations. Teaching & Staff Development Mentor, train, and foster the professional growth of veterinary technicians and assistants. Assist in teaching and guiding fourth-year veterinary students during clinical rotations. Interdepartmental Communication & Client Relations Serve as the primary Liaison between EFAVC staff, hospital leadership, and ancillary hospital services to align operations and protocols. Maintain excellent working relationships across all hospital areas. Deliver exceptional customer service to both internal colleagues and external clients. Qualifications & Experience: Role Requirements: Extensive clinical experience as a Veterinary Technician or Assistant, with specialized knowledge in equine and/or farm animal medicine. Leadership Skills: Proven experience in supervisory duties, operational scheduling, and team management within a veterinary setting. Core Competencies: Strong communication, biosecurity adherence, clinical teaching ability, and client service skills. Key Skills and Abilities: Excellent communication skills with a commitment to maintaining a high level of professionalism at all times. Strong computer literacy paired with proven problem-solving abilities. Physically able to lift and handle up to 60 pounds regularly with or without reasonable accommodations.

title: Executive Director of Philanthropy, CALS
description: The Executive Director reports to the Assistant Dean of Philanthropy, CALS and serves on the leadership team for the division. This position is charged with developing and implementing strategies for securing financial support from a portfolio of donors and prospects including identifying, qualifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major gifts for the university from alumni and friends. The Executive Director prepares and implements strategic plans for the major gift team and is responsible for meeting annual goals based on new prospect discovery and qualifications, in-person meetings, proposals submitted and gifts closed. The Executive Director is charged with planning, coordinating, and representing university-wide fundraising initiatives and programs by closely partnering with colleges and units, university leadership, and development colleagues across campus. The Executive Director may serve as the direct supervisor, mentor and coach to major gift officers and program specialists, while maintaining their own fundraising portfolio. Essential duties and responsibilities of the Executive Director include, but are not limited to the following: Major Gifts Strategy, Pipeline Development, and Donor Portfolio Management Serve as a member of the College’s advancement leadership team and lead/execute projects related to the major gifts program. Grow the major gifts program and building a pipeline of individual major gift donors ($100,000+) through identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship cycles Actively manage a personal portfolio of current and potential major gift donors. In partnership with the Assistant Dean, leads the strategy to identify, qualify, prioritize, cultivate, solicit, all donors and prospects assigned to the College of Agriculture & Life Sciences. Prioritize and implement complex donor strategies involving multiple units and leadership. Fundraising Goals, Solicitations, and Donor Engagement Develop fundraising and program goals for staff in collaboration with Assistant Dean; monitoring progress against goals. Initiate and conduct personal meetings with prospects and donors throughout the year and leading / participating in solicitations with university leaders and development colleagues to meet and achieve individual and institutional goals. Foster and reinforce a non-territorial, sophisticated approach to donor-centric philanthropy that encourages flexibility and responsiveness throughout University Advancement. Staff Leadership, Coaching, and Advancement Team Coordination Lead and manage staff in a fiscally sound manner by ensuring that the appropriate systems, staffing and procedures are in place to support fundraising goals. Serve as a resource, role model, and coach to development staff on matters of prospect strategy and solicitation; regularly share new approaches and techniques. Ensure that all interested parties (team members) are well informed and engaged in efforts focused on specific prospects.

title: Open Rank Teaching Faculty
description: The Institute for Advanced Analytics invites applications for an open-rank Assistant, Associate, or full Teaching Professor. This 12-month non-tenure-track faculty position will play a central role in developing, delivering, and continuously improving the Institute’s portfolio of online professional certificate programs and graduate instruction. As a faculty member, you will shape how working professionals and graduate students learn and apply analytics in a rapidly evolving field. You will bring your expertise in analytics, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data science into the classroom while creating practical, technology-enabled learning experiences that connect academic knowledge to real-world challenges. Through teaching, mentoring, curriculum innovation, and collaboration with faculty and industry partners, you will help prepare learners to apply emerging tools and insights in their professional work. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas: Online Curriculum Development and Teaching: Lead the design, development, delivery, and continuous improvement of online certificate and graduate courses, creating engaging content and assessments that support meaningful learning outcomes. Create engaging asynchronous and synchronous learning experiences using modern educational technologies and evidence-based instructional practices. Continuously strengthen curriculum by incorporating advances in analytics and emerging technologies and using student feedback and assessment data to improve learning experiences. Partner with faculty, instructional designers, educational technology professionals, and media specialists to deliver high-quality online learning experiences. Deliver graduate and professional education courses in analytics and related disciplines. Student Engagement and Applied Learning: Mentor graduate students through industry-sponsored projects, connecting them with corporate partners and guiding teams from planning through final deliverables. Provide academic and professional advising through regular student engagement and office hours. Supervise graduate teaching assistants as assigned. Foster a collaborative learning environment that supports student growth and professional development. Program Development and Professional Engagement: Help shape professional education offerings in response to emerging workforce needs and opportunities. Partner with faculty, Institute leadership, and industry stakeholders to strengthen curriculum and experiential learning. Contribute to program assessment, accreditation, recruitment, outreach, and executive education activities. Build relationships with industry partners that expand learning and professional opportunities for students. Service and Scholarly Engagement: Contribute to Institute and university committees, admissions, curriculum planning, and faculty governance. Maintain current expertise through professional development in analytics education, instructional technology, and industry trends. Pursue scholarly and professional activities aligned with your expertise and rank, including applied research, presentations, publications, consulting, or industry collaboration. If you are energized by helping learners translate analytics and emerging technologies into meaningful solutions, we invite you to bring your expertise to a faculty community committed to innovation, applied learning, and the evolving needs of today’s workforce.

title: Sous Chef
description: Bring your passion for food and teamwork to NC State Dining! We are hiring a Sous Chef with NC State Dining . As a Sous Chef, you’ll be part of a team that brings quality, care, and consistency to food served on campus. You will manage and monitor all activities in the kitchen, assign work to kitchen staff, enforce operational standards and serve as back-up to the unit chef in their absence. Key responsibilities include but not limited to: Follow and maintain the highest of culinary standards in all food areas, including the kitchen, serving line and display stations. Responsible for the quality of the food to be cooked, seasoned, and held correctly, according to the set recipes, and presented in an attractive manner. Execute the production of recipes required to fulfill the menu. Plan daily food production and assign staff accordingly to execute the plan. Review daily production sheets and check preparations amounts for accuracy and coordinate the flow of food in the unit. Maintain a clean, safe and efficient work environment in accordance with university and departmental guidelines. Responsible for face to face customer service and satisfaction. Communicate with personnel to ensure adequate amount of food for service while controlling overproduction. Respond to operational needs and challenges with professionalism and adaptability. May pick up or deliver food/supplies to other dining locations. This role requires physical stamina, including the ability to lift 30 pounds above head and up to 60 pounds on rare occasions, work in hot and cold conditions, and safely handle sharp tools and hot surfaces (all with or without reasonable accommodations). If you take pride in your work, enjoy being part of a collaborative team, and thrive in a dynamic environment where professionalism, adaptability, and customer service matter, this is your opportunity to make a meaningful impact in the heart of campus life.

About the Department: Central Crops Research Station is one of eighteen agricultural research centers in the State of North Carolina. North Carolina State University owns the Central Crops Research Station with operational management through the Division of Research Stations. North Carolina State University and the Division of Research Stations establish the general operating procedures. The primary purpose of the Research Station is to provide land, personnel, expertise, facilities and equipment to research scientists conducting agricultural research projects which address specific questions of crop production in North Carolina.

Essential Job Duties: As the Agricultural Research Technician, you will support research activities across all three research units by assisting with the establishment, maintenance, treatment, and disposition of field crops, vegetables, fruit, tobacco, and animal research specimens. You will perform hand tasks on the ground and operate agricultural equipment, assist with research plot activities, and support operations in the seed laboratory and swine facility. Your work will contribute to the quality and reliability of agricultural research conducted at the Clayton, NC location. In this role, you will gain hands-on experience working across a variety of crops, research facilities, and field operations while collaborating with research personnel to carry out established research protocols. Key Responsibilities Agricultural Research & Field Operations Establish, maintain, treat, and harvest research plots involving field crops, vegetables, fruit, and tobacco according to established research protocols. Apply pesticides, fertilizers, irrigation, and other treatments to research subjects in accordance with protocols and safety requirements. Operate a variety of agricultural equipment for field preparation, treatment application, planting, cultivation, and harvesting. Perform hand planting and harvesting and assist with plot layout, treatment implementation, and research data collection and recording. Research Facility & Equipment Support Install, operate, and maintain irrigation systems, including solid-set pipe and drip irrigation. Assist with the maintenance of agricultural equipment, grounds, buildings, field plots, and other research facilities and infrastructure. Maintain work areas and research plots to support accurate and reliable research results. If you are interested in applying your agricultural skills in a hands-on research environment and contributing to research across multiple disciplines, we welcome you to apply for the Agricultural Research Technician position in Clayton, NC.
Other Responsibilities: Additional work hours may be required, especially during planting, irrigation and harvest seasons. Research projects or weather may alter work schedule. Other duties and task as needed.
Minimum Experience/Education: Demonstrated possession of the competencies necessary to perform the work.
Preferred Qualifications: Experience supporting agricultural, horticultural, livestock, or field-based research activities. Demonstrated ability to safely operate and maintain farm or research equipment, including tractors, loaders, or similar machinery. Experience maintaining data logs, research records, or field activity documentation with attention to accuracy and detail. Ability to work outdoors in varying environmental conditions while performing physically active tasks, including lifting up to 50 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation. Ability to follow written research protocols, safety procedures, and pesticide label instructions while working independently and as part of a research team
Required License or Certification: Valid NC Driver’s License or ability to obtain within 60 days of start. Public Pesticide Applicator License or ability to obtain within six months of hiring. Forklift certification will be required once training has been provided by the dept.
