title: Environmental Services Technician I
description: Are you looking for a fulfilling career where you can make a tangible difference in creating a clean and welcoming environment? We are seeking a passionate and detail-oriented Environmental Services Technician to join our exceptional Environmental Services team at NC State’s Facilities Division. In this vital role, you will help maintain over 10 million square feet of campus space, ensuring a safe and inviting atmosphere for students, staff, and visitors. With the support of a dynamic team of over 320 professionals, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your skills and take pride in your work while contributing to our vibrant campus community. Join us and be a part of a team that takes pride in delivering exceptional service to one of the most prestigious campuses in the region. Apply today and help us keep NC State shining bright! Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Clean and sanitize designated areas using standard cleaning assignments to maintain a safe and hygienic environment Report any discrepancies, damages, or maintenance needs within buildings and promptly respond to emergencies and inclement weather Operate housekeeping equipment such as vacuums, mops, and scrubbers to complete tasks like dusting, disinfecting, and replenishing supplies Periodically strip and refinish floors, shampoo and extract carpets, and perform pressure washing of entrances, exterior walls, and windows Remove and manage recycling from centralized indoor recycling sites Assist with window washing and other seasonal cleaning tasks as needed Operate standard cleaning tools and equipment safely and effectively. Perform physical tasks such as lifting (up to 30 lbs. frequently, 60 lbs. occasionally), bending, reaching, squatting, and climbing ladders with or without reasonable accommodations. Adhere to safety procedures and maintain work areas according to departmental standards. Communicate clearly and professionally with team members, supervisors, and the public.

title: Assistant Professor
description: North Carolina State University (NC State) is seeking a highly motivated and innovative individual for a tenure-track position at the level of Assistant Professor as part of the FRIB Experimental Bridge program. This unique position provides an exceptional opportunity for a dynamic researcher to thrive in a collaborative environment at the forefront of nuclear science. In this role, your professional efforts will be split between the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB) at Michigan State University (MSU) and the local facilities at NC State and the Triangle Universities Nuclear Laboratory (TUNL), located in Durham, North Carolina. This dual appointment offers a distinctive platform for cutting-edge research, leveraging the capabilities and resources of both renowned institutions. Key Responsibilities: Conduct cutting-edge research at FRIB, using its state-of-the-art facilities to advance the frontiers of rare isotope science. Lead an independent research program and engage in collaborative research at TUNL, where unique capabilities such as high-intensity particle beams, polarized photon beams, neutron beams, and advanced detection systems support a broad range of nuclear physics investigations. Develop a robust, externally funded research program that integrates work at both FRIB and NC State/TUNL. Teach undergraduate and graduate courses at NC State, demonstrating a commitment to excellence in education and mentorship. If you thrive in collaborative research environments and are excited by the opportunity to work alongside leading researchers while building your own research program, we invite you to apply.

title: Senior Research Accountant
description: As a Senior Research Accountant II in the Sciences Research Office, you will provide essential accounting and budgeting services to Principal Investigators (PIs), research associates, departmental staff, and graduate students. This role involves working independently to solve complex problems related to budgeting, purchasing, travel, and overall contract and grants management. Key Responsibilities include but are not limited to: Serve as a liaison between PIs, department administrators, COS Office of Research, and Contract and Grant Accounting by attending new project award meetings and project status meetings as needed. Audit and approve small purchase vouchers, interdepartmental transfers, travel reimbursements, HR actions, requisitions, purchase orders, and cost transfers. Perform regular review and audits for compliance and financial management on departmental expenditures, contract terms and agency requirements for assigned contracts and grants. Daily budget expenditures review, compiling summaries of activities and providing recommendations for budget allocations and adjustments Monthly analysis to determine post-award actions needed Quarterly reconciliation of grant accounts and provide summary to PI’s for re-budgeting purposes. Conduct quality control (QC) reviews of departmental accounting technicians’ work. Interpret and apply Cost Accounting Standards, University Policies, and Agency General and Specific Terms and Conditions. Stay current on Federal regulations, policies, guidelines, and agency-specific terms and conditions. Use internal software such as RADAR, WolfPack Reports, and PMR systems to review and adjust budgets. Join us to make a significant impact on our research projects and support the advancement of scientific knowledge!

title: Sr. Employee Relations Consultant
description: The Consultant provides advanced level strategic consultation to staff, faculty, post doctoral scholars, and administrators to support an engaged work environment and resolve workplace problems before they escalate to formal grievances, external complaints, or legal action. The Consultant mitigates institutional risk of non-compliance with employment law and provides training to campus units and partners as appropriate. The Consultant advises managers and hiring units on performance concerns and defensible corrective and disciplinary actions or sanctions to help ensure compliance with federal, state, university, Office of State Human Resources (OSHR), and campus employment laws, policies, and regulations. The Consultant will have programmatic responsibilities that may include performance management, engagement building, grievance, appeal and/or mediation programs, corrective action, training on employee relations (ER) issue identification and just-in-time remediation, and/or others as appropriate. Key Responsibilities: ER Consultation and Issue Resolution – 50% This position is required to deal with highly complex, intense, and sensitive personnel issues and situations. Therefore, the incumbent is expected to identify and analyze problem areas, uncover root causes, and recommend action plans which provide effective strategies to allow the client’s organization to achieve the desired goal/outcome. The position analyzes each situation and develops, facilitates, and recommends effective resolution strategies. The position must also evaluate each situation as to the urgency of circumstances and resources required and determine the appropriate parties to involve. The position addresses a variety of issues to include unlawful discrimination or harassment, alleged violations of policies and/or state and federal laws, reports of safety violations, provide guidance concerning employee performance issues, and assistance with recognition events. This position provides expertise in discipline and grievance matters by meeting and counseling employees and management on issues concerning the university’s grievance and disciplinary procedures. Program Management – 15% This position will assume responsibilities for one or more programs managed through Employee Relations. These may include but are not limited to: managing the University’s Employee Assistance Program; administering the Dispute Resolution and Staff Grievance Procedure; administering relevant human resources policy development; administering the performance management programs for SHRA and EPS employees; managing the mediation program; and managing the Exit Interview program, and assisting with the university and System Office Employee Engagement initiatives. Workplace Investigations – 15% This position will conduct detailed investigations of workplace related incidents and reported concerns, while appropriately engaging with business partners and advising client groups. Training – 10% This position will have responsibilities to recommend, assess, develop, implement and conduct training on a wide variety of employee relations topics at both the university and client level. These may include performance management, conflict resolution, wellness, management essentials, engagement and other employment related opportunities. Project Management -10 % May lead or participate in cross-functional project teams to modernize ER workflows, roll out proactive organizational culture and compliance programs, and translate workplace trend data into scalable solutions. If you are an experienced Human Resources/Employee Relations professional who enjoys navigating complex workplace concerns, providing thoughtful consultation, and developing solutions that support employees, managers, and the University, we welcome you to apply. In this role, you will have the opportunity to use your expertise in employee relations, investigations, performance management, training, and program development to help address workplace challenges and strengthen effective employment practices across NC State.

title: William R. Kenan, Jr. Distinguished Chair in Translational Science & Medicine
description: North Carolina State University invites applications for the position of the William R. Kenan, Jr. Distinguished Chair in Translational Science & Medicine in the College of Veterinary Medicine. This is an exciting opportunity for an individual to advance human and animal health and welfare through the application of the most current research techniques addressing complex medical problems at one of the nation’s leading colleges of veterinary medicine. We are seeking a dynamic and transformational scientist to join our research teams. The William R. Kenan, Jr. Distinguished Chair in Translational Science & Medicine will join and strengthen our research teams to provide transformational knowledge in comparative medicine and biomedical sciences. The discipline of interest for this position is expected to highlight and expand on already existing research strengths within the College of Veterinary Medicine, opening new frontiers in research and training for the future. The William R. Kenan, Jr. Distinguished Chair in Translational Science & Medicine will enhance the CVM’s abilities and expand our reach. The Professor will synergize with existing faculty to build an internationally-recognized program focused on developing integrated research methodology that improves medical care, particularly around the College and University’s current research strengths in infectious disease, genetics, gastroenterology, aging, regenerative medicine, cell, and neurobiology, amongst others. This individual will play an active role in training veterinary and graduate students by providing new perspectives on translational science and medicine. Apply cutting-edge scientific knowledge and techniques to develop impactful solutions for complex medical issues in humans and animals. Support and encourage leadership in comparative medicine; promote the ability to transfer excellence in research, service, and training from animals to human health. Leverage faculty access to our state-of-the-art veterinary teaching hospital to foster close collaborations between the CVM and other NC State groups, the medical schools at Duke and the University of North Carolina, and the North Carolina Research Triangle Park. Serve as an advocate for enhancing the abilities, visibility, and reach of the CVM’s research program and growing translational impact. Synergize with existing faculty to build an internationally recognized program focused on developing integrated research methodology that improves medical care, particularly around the College and University’s current strengths. Play an active role in training veterinary and graduate students by providing new perspectives on contemporary research approaches. Train graduate students and/or postdoctoral fellows. Participate in didactic teaching at the graduate level and augment veterinary student education. Secure significant extramural funding for their independent research program and trainees.

title: Assistant Athletic Trainer/Fellow
description: Serve as an Athletic Training Fellow within the Department of Athletics for Sports Medicine. The position is responsible for assisting with the care of student-athletes, to include prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation of the injured student-athletes under the supervision of the team physician for assigned sport(s). Sport assignment(s) may be modified at the discretion of the Sports Medicine administrative personnel. Duties and Responsibilities Include (but are not limited to): Work under the supervision and mentorship of a staff athletic trainer Assist in operating and maintaining the athletic training room(s) Ensure proper use of equipment and facilities by student-athletes Work with the Senior Associate Athletics Director for Sports Performance and the Team Physician(s) in providing comprehensive healthcare to student-athletes Referral to associated health care professionals when necessary Maintain medical records on the student-athletes to include physical examinations and screenings, insurance information, injury evaluation and treatment records Attend scheduled meetings, team practices, and events, including traveling with assigned team(s) and assist with secondary coverage as needed Provide emergency care when appropriate Assist with maintenance of athletic training room equipment Assist with annual physical examinations and drug testing programs for student- athletes Document services rendered consistent with best practices Follow all developed departmental policies and procedures

title: NC State University Libraries Fellow, 2027-2030
description: Why choose the NC State University Libraries as a first professional librarian position? The Libraries Fellows Program provides a launching pad for a career in academic librarianship. Fellows will experience the rewards of working in a leading research library and with a large user community reflecting a variety of backgrounds and disciplines, including outstanding faculty and students in nationally ranked academic programs. They will gain experience in a highly collaborative work environment with access to key decision makers throughout the organization. They will also develop expertise in and contribute meaningfully to a variety of essential functional areas in academic librarianship. In addition to a competitive salary, Fellows receive a generous professional development stipend. The success of the Program is illustrated by the success of the Fellows themselves. Since its inception in 1999, 95 Fellows have completed the Program. Ninety-five percent of Fellows have been offered academic positions or have entered doctoral programs upon completion of the program. Many former Fellows have been recognized more widely in the field, including seven named as Library Journal Movers and Shakers, adding to the reputation of the Program as a training ground for library leaders. What do Libraries Fellows work on? The NC State University Libraries is well known for its digital research and experiential learning initiatives, technological advances such as immersive visualization, support for open scholarship and student affordability, interdisciplinary teaching and learning, public engagement with research, and commitment to championing a culture of belonging and well-being in everything we do—all of which help to actively shape the future of librarianship. The Libraries is also defined by a staff who deeply consider how their approach to their daily work reflects and advances the Libraries’ Strategic Plan , creating an environment and community that is welcoming for both patrons and colleagues alike. We seek out candidates with interests and aptitudes in these areas, and Fellows assignments reflect these areas of focus. Fellows perform as entry-level librarians with their time during the first 18 months divided between two Libraries departments—allowing the Fellows to develop their interests and expertise in two functional areas of academic librarianship. The second 18 months will typically focus on areas that have emerged over the course of the Fellowship, taking into consideration both the Libraries’ operational needs and the professional interests and goals of the Fellow. The Libraries recognizes that self-determination is an important consideration in a Fellowship experience like this. During the interview process, candidates learn about the Libraries’ departments and initiatives. They are given the opportunity to indicate their preferences for their dual departmental assignments, and those preferences are considered in determining the placements of successful candidates.

title: Open Rank Professional Faculty in Social Work
description: The School of Social Work invites applications for an open-rank professional-track position. Hires for this position may be part-time or full-time. Professional-track faculty members are expected to demonstrate excellence in teaching and advising. Faculty members at .75 FTE or above may be expected to participate actively in community extension, engagement, and service to the school, college, university, and profession. We seek candidates with teaching experience in social work theory, practice, research, and policy. Primary teaching responsibilities will be in the School’s Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) program and/or Master of Social Work (MSW) program. The typical teaching load is 4 courses per semester for a full-time (1.0 FTE) faculty member.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Political Science, in the School of Public and International Affairs (SPIA) at North Carolina State University (NC State), invites applications for a tenure-track position at the assistant professor level, beginning August 2027. We seek highly qualified candidates with a research focus and teaching interests in the politics of Latin American states and the region. Teaching responsibilities will be at the graduate and undergraduate level in the department’s Master of International Studies (MIS) program as well as Bachelor of Arts and Bachelor of Science in Political Science. The applicant must be able to develop coursework in Latin American politics at the graduate level for our MIS program and be able to teach undergraduate course(s) on the politics and political issues relevant to Latin America as a region and/or specific countries in that region of the world. Scholars with interests in comparative political institutions, comparative political economy, security, energy, climate change, sustainability, social policy, environmental policy and/or democratization are particularly encouraged to apply.

title: UTS - Temporary Japanese Language Extension Instructor at NC State
description: The Japanese Language Extension Instructor shall teach varying levels of non-credit Japanese language courses, based on their skill and experience, to a mix of students from the community. Instructors shall teach a minimum of one course per semester, for a total minimum of three courses per year. Each course lasts fifteen weeks, with one class per week and each class lasts 2 hours. There may be exceptions for special courses designed by the instructor and the EECOM that may modify the number of weeks, classes per week, and class duration. Based on experience, skill, and interest, instructors will be assigned to courses ranging from beginner level up to preparation for the JLPT N1 exam. In order to stay consistent with for-credit courses and most universities in NC, classes are taught based on the Genki and Quartet series. Based on student demand and Instructor availability, Instructors may teach more than one class per week, but the total number of weekly hours shall be fewer than thirty hours. Courses are offered in both in-person and online formats; instructors may be assigned to teach either modality or a combination of both.

title: UTS - Temporary Part-time On-Call CDL Bus Drivers at NC State
description: University Bus Drivers operate activity buses ranging in size from 22 passengers to 44 passengers. A North Carolina State University Bus Driver is responsible for safely transporting students, faculty, staff, and school affiliates to and from designated locations. These locations may be within the same city or different cities. Trips may be field trips or labs to extend the academic experience, sporting events, or other extracurricular activities. Since the University Bus Driver accommodates student/faculty schedules, they generally work unusual hours. He/she may work early morning, late evening, or weekends. The Bus Driver maintains the cleanliness, organization, and safety of the bus itself. This role is expected to last 11 months with the potential to extend Essential Duties and Responsibilities: • Picks up and returns passengers at locations specified by reservation • Ensures that all passengers are safely and properly seated on the bus • Observes rules of the road and drives with caution • Ensures timely conveyance of passengers to their destination • Ensures that vehicles are kept neat and clean at all times • Carries out routine pre-trip and post-trip inspection of vehicles in the hour prior to the shuttle pick up; inspects tire pressure, oil levels, windshield wipers, mirrors and other details for any problems. Identify electrical or mechanical faults. May carry out simple maintenance on vehicles. Brings problems or maintenance needs to the attention of the Bus Dispatcher. • Fills bus fuel tank • Read maps and check weather and traffic reports to determine the best route to take • Keep all documents and receipts of the vehicle and maintenance services secure • Maintain a travel log to record travel locations travelled to, travel time, work hours and mileage for billing purposes. Knowledge, Skills and Abilities: A bus driver must be well-trained. He/she should be a skilled driver and must hold a CDL A/B operating license with passenger endorsement He/ she must have specific knowledge of traffic laws and rules of the road. Must adhere strictly to them The work of bus driving may involve loading and unloading of luggage, and frequent opening of doors requiring strength and stamina. The Bus Driver must be patient and calm in dealing with situations like irate passengers and traffic congestion. Must be capable of acting quickly and calmly in a crisis. Must be able to drive for a long period of time and possess a strong sense of direction, He/she must be a person who values lives and must think about the safety of his/her passengers and other road users. He/she must be focused, confident, and observant while driving. Must demonstrate a quick response time. Possess effective communication, leadership and team play skills, as well as the ability to adhere to instructions.

title: UTS - Temporary CMA/RMA at NC State
description: The primary duties of this position include the following: Comply with legal and regulatory health care requirements related to HIPAA/FERPA, OSHA, AAAHC, Infection Control, CMA/RMA codes of conduct and NC State University Regulations and Campus Health protocols. Perform patient intake and document chief complaint, vital signs, medication reconciliation and medication, material allergies or sensitivities in the electronic health record. Administer medications and injections as ordered by medical providers and documented in the electronic health record. Assist providers performing office based medical procedures for GYN and Primary Care visits Perform skills based tasks such as ekgs, ear lavage, applying DME, wound care Work with the GYN and Primary Care Nursing Supervisors on assignments such as chart reviews and other work group assignments. Complete unit based training with passing scores at hire, as needed, and annually if applicable Attend monthly nursing, nurse provider, and all staff meetings. Stock and prepare medical clinics for direct patient care per unit protocols.

title: Associate Director of Creative Video
description: The Associate Director of Creative Video actively produces and coordinates creative video initiatives while providing day-to-day creative leadership for NC State Athletics. Remaining a hands-on creative contributor, this position operates at a senior individual-contributor level within the SHRA structure, emphasizing advanced technical execution, daily leadership, and operational coordination rather than formal managerial authority over permanent staff. This role reports to and works closely with the Assistant AD for Video Services within Pack Productions to translate departmental direction into daily production outcomes. The Associate Director produces high-quality video content, coordinates recruiting deliverables across assigned sport programs, and oversees student interns through instruction, mentorship, scheduling, and performance feedback while maintaining compliance with NCAA, ACC, and institutional standards. This role also requires capability to carry heavy equipment up to 25-30lbs. Primary Responsibilities: Active Creative Leadership & Execution Serve as a senior creative contributor, setting day-to-day creative standards and production expectations. Translate departmental creative direction into actionable daily production plans and priorities. Provide hands-on creative guidance, instruction, and real-time feedback to student interns. Review projects to ensure alignment with brand standards and quality benchmarks. Student Intern Development & Oversight Oversee the Creative Video student intern program including recruiting, onboarding, training, scheduling, and supervision. Develop structured training plans and assign projects. Provide feedback and support professional growth. Recruiting Content Coordination Lead planning and execution of recruiting-focused video content across all NC State Athletics sports. Serve as a liaison with coaching staffs to identify recruiting needs and timelines. Ensure recruiting content aligns with NCAA, ACC, and institutional guidelines. Content Production & Execution Produce, shoot, edit, and deliver social, recruiting, and feature video content. Create content for video boards, live events, and broadcast platforms. Stay current with emerging trends to inform execution. Collaboration & Communication Work collaboratively with Athletics Communications, Marketing, Recruiting, and external broadcast partners. Communicate effectively with coaches, student-athletes, administrators, and external stakeholders. Serve as a trusted creative resource and mentor within Pack Productions. Supervisory & Leadership Responsibilities: Provide day-to-day functional oversight of student interns and student workers; does not supervise permanent employees. Direct daily work assignments, schedules, and project priorities for interns in support of departmental goals. Train interns on equipment, software, workflows, and professional expectations. Contribute to intern recruiting, selection, and evaluation in collaboration with department leadership.

title: Horticultural Specialist
description: Join NC State University’s Landscape Maintenance and Operations (LM&O) team as a Horticultural Specialist and help shape the beauty, sustainability, and long-term health of our award-winning campus landscapes. This position is ideal for someone who loves hands-on work, appreciates the natural environment, and takes pride in creating vibrant, well-maintained outdoor spaces. As a key plant-care expert for assigned campus zones, you will apply your horticultural knowledge, problem-solving skills, and creativity to support the university’s landscape standards, sustainability goals, and student engagement initiatives. You will also serve as a trusted resource to LM&O staff, helping mentor team members in best practices for plant care, seasonal maintenance, and thoughtful landscape design. If you’re passionate about working outdoors, making a visible impact, and being part of a collaborative and mission-driven team, this role offers meaningful, year-round work in a supportive environment. Key responsibilities and duties include but not limited to: Perform hands-on landscape tasks including pruning, weeding, mulching, planting, watering, blowing, and debris removal. Apply horticultural best practices and integrated pest management procedures across assigned campus zones. Monitor plant health and diagnose issues such as diseases, pests, nutrient deficiencies, or environmental stress; recommend and implement corrective actions. Ensure compliance with plant maintenance service agreements, including fertilization, soil testing, pruning schedules, and routine care standards. Evaluate plant conditions and provide clear reports and recommendations to the supervisor. Serve as a horticultural resource and mentor to LM&O staff by offering training, demonstrations, and guidance on effective plant care techniques. Troubleshoot landscape maintenance concerns and communicate findings promptly to the supervisor. Maintain and care for green roof landscapes, ensuring proper plant selection, watering needs, and adherence to rooftop safety procedures. Monitor indoor plant installations and ensure proper watering, lighting conditions, and timely plant replacement. Support student-led projects by consulting on plant selection, providing instructional guidance, and ensuring alignment with campus landscape standards. Support student workdays and internships by preparing tools, offering hands-on training, and ensuring safe field practices. Collaborate with Landscape Field Leads and Zone Managers on planting design, seasonal planning, and landscape project implementation. Advise LM&O staff on sustainable landscape practices, seasonal plant selection, biodiversity, and strategies that enhance long-term campus aesthetic and ecological health. Lift and transport materials weighing up to 60 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodations, and perform a wide range of physically demanding tasks in varied outdoor environments while maintaining safe handling procedures and consistent productivity. Understand verbal and written instructions regarding work assignments and other matter. If you’re energized by outdoor work, passionate about horticulture, and looking for a role where your contributions will be seen and valued every day, we invite you to apply and join our LM&O team at NC State University. Your expertise can help shape a campus environment that inspires students, staff, and visitors year-round.

title: UTS - Temporary Executive Assistant at NC State
description: The position serves as the liaison and/or coordinator between executive leadership and other university departments. The position exercises considerable independence, ensuring that administrative details are managed in accordance with executive objectives and work priorities. This position will maintain a high level of knowledge of division programs, activities, goals, priorities, and commitments, a high level of independence and accountability for speaking on behalf of executive leadership, and a high level of judgment and discretion concerning division operations. This individual is frequently called upon by directors and departmental administrators in the division to answer questions directed to leadership. The responsibilities of this position are to relieve executive leadership of as many matters as possible that do not demand personal attention.

title: Extension Agent, FCS (Assistant, Associate or Full Agent)
description: The agent in this position will provide leadership for the development and implementation of the Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS) program in Onslow County. The agent will proactively conduct needs assessments, interactive learning opportunities, and program evaluations to provide future direction of the program. Programmatic support of current research-based nutrition/healthy lifestyles curriculum for all ages, along with volunteer management will be expected of the agent to meet program goals.

title: Senior Vice Provost for Enrollment Management and Services
description: The Senior Vice Provost for Enrollment Management and Services reports directly to the Executive Vice Chancellor and Provost and serves as the university’s chief enrollment officer. As a member of the Provost’s senior leadership team, the Senior Vice Provost provides strategic and operational leadership for the university’s enrollment enterprise and advises university leadership regarding enrollment strategy, student access and success, enrollment trends, institutional capacity, and the policies, resources, technologies, and services necessary to achieve NC State’s long-term goals. In this role, you will shape how NC State responds to a changing enrollment landscape. You will bring together academic, financial, operational, and student perspectives to anticipate emerging challenges and opportunities, navigate complex decisions, and build alignment around strategies that advance sustainable enrollment and student success. Your leadership will translate changing student demand and educational needs into action, expanding access to an NC State education, supporting student success, and advancing the university’s land-grant mission. Key Responsibilities fall within the following core functions: Shape University Enrollment Strategy and Capacity: Develop and advance a comprehensive, long-term enrollment strategy aligned with NC State’s strategic plan, academic priorities, land-grant mission, institutional capacity, and the educational and workforce needs of North Carolina. Lead university-wide enrollment planning, establishing goals and projections while assessing academic, financial, operational, technological, and student-support capacity. Advise university leaders on enrollment opportunities, emerging trends, institutional capacity, student demand, demographic changes, and the potential enrollment and resource implications of university policies and strategic decisions. Lead university-wide enrollment planning by facilitating collaborative processes to develop enrollment goals, evaluate academic and operational capacity, assess institutional readiness, and align enrollment strategies with university resources and priorities. Lead undergraduate enrollment strategies spanning recruitment, admission, enrollment, retention, progression, and graduation. Advance Student Access, Success, and Experience: Advance strategies that expand educational opportunity, reduce barriers, and strengthen student access, successful transitions, academic progress, retention, and timely degree completion. Lead continuous improvement of programs, services, policies, communications, and practices that shape the student enrollment experience. Strengthen enrollment communications and partnerships that communicate the value of an NC State education and support institutional enrollment priorities. Cultivate educational partnerships, including with the North Carolina Community College System, to strengthen pathways and expand opportunity. Lead an Innovative, Data-Informed Enterprise: Provide executive leadership and fiscal stewardship for Enrollment Management and Services, aligning people, resources, technology, facilities, and operations with institutional priorities. Champion the strategic use of data, analytics, research, technology, and predictive modeling to inform enrollment strategy, resource planning, decision-making, and outcomes. Lead long-range organizational and operational planning that strengthens EMAS capacity, sustainability, innovation, and responsiveness. Ensure enrollment systems, policies, processes, and services are effective, coordinated, accessible, compliant, and responsive to evolving institutional and student needs. Build Institutional Leadership and Strategic Partnerships: Build a high-performing organization grounded in professional excellence, collaboration, accountability, innovation, ethical leadership, and a shared commitment to student success and public service. Establish priorities, accountability structures, and collaborative processes that translate institutional strategy into coordinated action across EMAS and the university. Build trusted relationships with academic and administrative leaders and represent EMAS in university planning, governance, policy development, and resource allocation. Represent NC State with the UNC System and external educational, governmental, professional, community, alumni, and other partners to advance enrollment and student-success priorities and contribute to the field of enrollment management. NC State welcomes leaders who bring sound judgment, curiosity, collaboration, and a commitment to listening and building trust across a complex university community. If you are energized by the opportunity to shape enrollment strategy, expand educational opportunity, and help advance the university’s mission through thoughtful and innovative leadership, we invite you to apply.

title: Systems Programmer/Specialist

Hosted Services provides support and services to NCSU departments and colleges for managing their servers, and related services, while hosting them in a stable and secure IT environment. These environments include on site and remote data centers, as well as various cloud providers such as Amazon and Microsoft. We work with many NCSU OIT infrastructure groups to determine hosting options based upon availability requirements (uptime, etc.), integration/middleware requirements, security requirements, disaster recovery, etc. Platform Compute Services provides the infrastructure and support for virtual computing, centralized storage, enterprise virtualization and backup services to campus units supporting NC State students, faculty, staff and partners. Services include the Virtual Computing Lab ( VCL ) environment that deliver private cloud computing services, and application delivery for faculty and students. We provide enterprise virtual hosting services, general storage services, block storage services, DR/backup solutions, and also provide consulting and departmental storage array management. Central Services and Integration ( CSI ) provides and supports enterprise-level integration of Linux/Unix services, as well as process ownership of NC State’s Configuration Management Database. Services include providing both shared and secure Linux build support environments, as well as Red Hat Satellite ( RHN ) patching and reporting for RHEL based systems. We provide monitoring, notification, and on call services, customized integrated paging solutions, and on call scheduling solutions. We provide NTP time services, mirror server services, MySQL/MariaDB/PostgreSQL hosted databases, proxy services, load balancing, ERP / EAS email relays, and ERP LDAP IPA services.

Puppet, Ansible, Chef ), Monitoring systems experience( i.e. Nagios, Grafana, Zabbix ), or similar systems Experience in some level of programming or scripting Experience in programming for systems automation and configuration
Preferred Qualifications: Experience in at least one Containerization( i.e. Kubernetes, Docker ) technology Experience programming in Python, JSON Experience working in Ansible

title: Temporary BJP Retreat and Events Associate - Reidsville, NC
department: 112401 - 4-H Youth Development & Family and Consumer Sciences
description: The Retreat and Events Associate provides leadership and oversight for retreat and rental programs, special events, marketing, community outreach, and year-round operations at the Betsy Jeff Penn 4-H Educational Center. The role coordinates with staff, user groups, and community partners to ensure successful program delivery, facility operations, and positive participant experiences while supporting the Center’s strategic goals, fundraising efforts, and ACA accreditation. Retreat Responsibilities Include: Oversee weekend rental and retreat groups throughout the calendar year Point of contact for the reservation and contract process with all rental and retreat groups Coordinate program planning prior to events, provide support during events, facilitate communications and program activities, and assist with post-program follow-up. On-site supervision will be rotated among camp leadership staff Oversee staff for facilitation of weekend programs when required Coordinate facility and equipment needs for group rental programs, including collaborating with Food Service and Maintenance supervisors to ensure facilities, equipment, and support services are prepared and maintained for user groups. Develop and implement marketing and recruitment plans and supporting materials for the group rental programs Collaborates closely with the Center’s leadership team Provide administrative and operational support, including assistance with hiring, budgeting, fundraising, and facilities maintenance, as assigned by the Center Director Special Events: Coordinate the planning and successful implementation of Betsy’s Bash, a biennial fundraising event held at Betsy Jeff Penn Serve as the primary point of contact and on-site coordinator for the event, collaborating with the Center Director, facilities and program staff as needed Work with the Center’s Advisory Council to plan, coordinate, and support event activities Program Marketing, User Support, and Community Outreach: Develop and implement marketing and communication strategies to promote the Center’s programs, events, rentals, and services and increase community engagement and participation. Maintain and support the growth of the Center’s email marketing database and communications. Develop outreach and engagement strategies to strengthen relationships with alumni and community partners. Create and coordinate content for the Center’s social media channels. Track and report program outcomes and assist with monitoring program activities within established budget parameters. Assist with the preparation, coordination, and attendance of Advisory Council meetings and related communications throughout the year. Center and Program Support and Resource Development: Participate in rotating on-call coverage to support group rental programs during fall and spring. Collaborate with the Betsy Jeff Penn camp team on year-round Center operations. Support the development of age-appropriate programs aligned with 4-H, Cooperative Extension, and ACA guidelines. Support ACA accreditation by maintaining program standards and best practices. Assist and train Health Coordinators/Camp Nurse on summer camp health policies and procedures.

title: Departmental Communications Manager
description: Working as part of a centralized communications team in the College of Engineering, this role manages a team of creative specialists who support the marketing and communications for multiple large engineering departments, including Electrical and Computer Engineering and Computer Science. This role ensures project management and resource utilization to provide authentic storytelling and both internal and external communications, highlighting student success, groundbreaking research and a direct impact on the state and country. This position ensures the success of the creative talents on their team, as well as working closely with Engineering Communications leadership to support needs college-wide and with campus partners in a collaborative and innovative environment. Departmental Communications & Staff Management The Communications Manager oversees marketing and communications staff that primarily supports four individual academic departments in the College of Engineering, in addition to specialist support needs (including videography, writing, digital media and social media management) across the college. Project Management & Resource Prioritization This position ensures consistent project management and resource sharing within the scope of the assigned departments, in addition to prioritization of requests and needs—ensuring consistent service to the academic departments, while ensuring progress on strategic goals set by Engineering Communications and Dean. This role is also expected to support high-touch content creation and event communication needs Strategic Communications & Brand Enhancement This area focuses on identifying and deploying specialist support (e.g., videography, writing, digital media, social media management) for projects that enhance the reputation and brand alignment of the academic programs and research activities. This includes promotion for flagship lecture series, support of philanthropic engagement, digital marketing, and recruitment communications. Planning, Assessment, & Reporting The manager will also assist in the development of annual communications plans and calendars in alignment with department and college strategic priorities. The manager will develop measures for tracking and reporting the results of communication outreach efforts for each department along with departmental communicators and have a good understanding of their assigned departments’ mission and priorities to ensure effective communication across varied audiences, and assess effectiveness to adjust strategies as needed.

title: Assistant Director and Financial Operations Supervisor
description: As the Assistant Director and Financial Operations Supervisor, you will provide formal leadership and accounting oversight for a centralized financial operations team supporting Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Travel, Procurement Card, and related financial systems. Reporting to the Director of Business Services, you will direct workflow, oversee high-risk financial activity, strengthen internal controls, and ensure financial transactions are processed accurately and in accordance with applicable federal, state, and university requirements. You will serve as a key resource and decision-maker for complex financial and compliance matters, applying accounting principles, regulatory requirements, and institutional policies across multiple funding sources. A significant component of this role is oversight of federally regulated programs, including USDA NIFA, Hatch, Hatch Multistate, and Smith-Lever funds, with responsibility for ensuring expenditures are appropriately evaluated for allowability, allocability, and classification. You will also provide oversight of CALS’ unique Ledger 4 structure, which combines federal, state, and receipt-supported funds within a single ledger and requires careful application of the appropriate regulatory and accounting framework. In collaboration with the Director, you will support the implementation of organizational initiatives and Business Services priorities while providing leadership to staff and promoting consistent, effective financial operations. Your oversight will help protect the integrity of financial reporting, mitigate financial and regulatory risk, and support compliance across a complex funding environment. Key Responsibilities: Supervision & Team Leadership Provide direct supervision, performance management, coaching, and professional development for financial operations staff. Assign, prioritize, and monitor workload across functional areas to support timely processing, balanced team capacity, and compliance. Oversee staff onboarding and training, ensuring understanding of accounting principles, financial systems, and funding-specific requirements. Promote consistency in financial processing, internal controls, and service delivery while addressing recurring operational issues and implementing corrective actions. Financial Oversight & Transaction Review Review, approve, and oversee high-risk and complex financial transactions to ensure accurate accounting treatment, appropriate documentation, and regulatory compliance. Oversee financial activity across federal, state, and receipt-supported funds, including Ledger 4 project structures and applicable funding requirements. Monitor reconciliations, financial data integrity, and internal controls while ensuring timely identification and resolution of discrepancies. Resolve complex financial and compliance issues requiring interpretation of accounting principles, regulatory guidance, and system functionality. Policy, Compliance & Internal Controls Interpret and apply University, State, Federal, and Sponsored Program regulations, including USDA NIFA, Hatch, Hatch Multistate, and Smith-Lever requirements. Ensure financial activity complies with applicable federal cost principles, internal controls, documentation standards, and audit requirements. Monitor audit findings, compliance risks, and corrective actions and recommend improvements to strengthen controls and reduce financial and operational risk. Serve as an escalation point for complex policy interpretation and compliance-related decisions. Operational Strategy & Continuous Improvement Partner with the Director to implement organizational initiatives and support the operational execution of Business Services priorities. Monitor operational performance, workload distribution, service levels, and productivity using dashboards, performance metrics, and data analytics. Lead process improvements and standardized operating procedures that enhance efficiency, consistency, compliance, and customer service. Coordinate workload balancing and operational resources in response to changing business needs and recommend improvements based on operational data and performance. Support employee development, cross-training, succession planning, and performance management within the assigned system. Communication & Stakeholder Engagement Communicate financial policies, compliance requirements, process changes, and decisions clearly to departments, faculty, staff, and campus partners. Serve as a liaison between CORE, central offices, and departments on financial operations, compliance matters, and system improvements. Translate complex accounting and regulatory requirements into clear, actionable guidance for non-financial stakeholders. In this role, you will partner with the Director and financial operations team to strengthen service delivery, promote sound financial practices, and help ensure Business Services operate effectively, consistently, and in support of the University’s priorities. If you are a thoughtful financial leader who enjoys developing people, solving complex operational challenges, and using data and sound judgment to improve processes, we welcome you to apply.

title: UTS- Temporary Tree Care Specialist at NC State University
description: Join the NC State Landscape Maintenance and Operations team to support the care, maintenance, and continued development of the university's campus forest. This position will assist the Tree Operations team with a wide variety of tree care activities, including young tree establishment, watering, tree planting, invasive plant management, light tree maintenance, and general arboricultural support. The position is intended to provide hands-on support across Tree Operations, with work varying seasonally and based on campus needs. Employees will work alongside tree care staff on projects throughout campus and gain practical experience in urban forestry, arboriculture, and campus tree management.

title: Crew Leader I - 62502
description: Crew Leader I , will lead essential projects, such as power washing entrances, window washing, waxing floors, and more. This role offers an exciting opportunity to guide a dedicated team, ensuring the cleanliness and functionality of campus spaces. You will be responsible for coordinating daily operations, resolving maintenance issues, and delivering excellent customer service. Working Hours: Monday - Friday 8:30am-5:30pm Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Lead projects, including power washing, window washing, floor waxing, and re-lamping fixtures and dispensers Inspect and verify maintenance discrepancies and ensure timely resolution Provide support to other zones as needed, filling in for vacant positions or absenteeism Collect and submit timesheets within established timelines Perform critical duties during adverse weather or emergencies as assigned Complete accident reports within 24 hours of an incident Assist with equipment inventory and maintain monthly inventory of storage closet supplies Submit supply orders for manager approval to ensure adequate stock levels Train new employees, ensuring they understand tasks and safety protocols Transport employees to various locations for assignments Collaborate with maintenance staff inside and outside the unit to resolve issues efficiently Address and resolve customer requests via radio communications, work orders, and direct interactions Ability to lift a minimum of 60 pounds continuously and 90 pounds occasionally with or without reasonable accommodations, climb and balance on a ladder up to 8ft. and distinguish between colors

title: Sponsored Research Administrator
description: The College of Engineering is looking to hire multiple Sponsored Research Administrators (SRA) within the newly established college-managed operating model, responsible for orchestrating both pre-award and post-award lifecycles for an assigned departmental faculty portfolio. While the incumbent is physically co-located within a department to provide high-touch, localized customer service, the position is an integral part of the centralized College ORA team. The primary purpose of this role is to apply advanced accounting principles, federal/state regulations, and university guidelines to ensure the fiscal and administrative integrity of all sponsored projects. Operating under this modernized model, the incumbent must balance localized portfolio execution with central compliance directives, actively participating in college-wide resource-sharing and standardized service-level agreements (SLAs). Detailed Description of Core Responsibilities Pre-Award Portfolio Management & Proposal Development Localized Faculty Consultation: Partner directly with PIs in the embedded unit to develop accurate, compliant proposal budgets and detailed justifications from initial concept through final submission. Standardized Regulatory Screening: Analyze complex agency Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and Funding Opportunity Announcements (FOAs) to ensure strict alignment with F&A rules, cost-sharing restrictions, budget caps, and direct cost allowability, reducing front-end submission errors. Institutional System Management: Fully execute and route records within institutional software suites, including RED Proposal Development, ensuring data integrity is validated at the departmental level before final central routing. Electronic Research Administration (eRA): Build, format, and package proposal submissions within varied sponsor portals (Research.gov, GRANTS.gov, eRA Commons, ASSIST), acting as the localized technical expert for the department's faculty. Post-Award Financial Management, Forecasting & Closeout Award Onboarding & Budget Translation: Review select incoming award notices alongside the PI to establish accurate internal ledger setups, ensuring F&A is calculated correctly based on MTDC or TDC parameters. Compliance Monitoring & Risk Mitigation: Perform continuous financial analysis of active grant ledgers. Monitor expenditures for accuracy, allowability, and strict compliance with Cost Accounting Standards (CAS), Uniform Guidance, state rules, and university policies. Projections & Planning Models: Build multi-year spending projections and variance analysis models for faculty to optimize fund utilization, prevent over-expenditures, and manage labor distributions/personnel charges. Reconciliations & Cost-Share Tracking: Audit human resource expenditures, travel vouchers, and procurement charges against grant terms. Track, document, and report mandatory or voluntary committed cost-sharing obligations. Lifecycle Closeouts: Execute comprehensive closeouts for expiring grant segments. Prepare and process Project Modification Requests (PMRs) for budget modifications, no-cost extensions, or residual balance distributions, ensuring audit-ready documentation is permanently archived. Model Alignment, Cross-Coverage & Leadership Matrixed Team Collaboration: Actively participate in the broader College ORA network to ensure alignment with university-wide research administration standards. Navigate the dual priorities of central College compliance policy and local departmental workflow. Cross-College Workload Balancing: Participate in the new model's agile resource framework, willingly stepping in to provide temporary pre- or post-award coverage for other COE departments during peak submission cycles or staff absences to maintain college-wide continuity. Faculty Onboarding & Training: Develop and deliver targeted resources, onboarding guides, or info-sessions for new faculty and departmental business officers regarding centralized ORA standard operating procedures and financial management tools.

title: COSS County Administrative Assistant

The County Administrative Assistant cooperates with colleagues in the NCCE and county leaders in performing assigned responsibilities. title: Extension Agent, Ag, Urban Ag /Horticulture (Assistant, Associate or Full Agent)
description: North Carolina Cooperative Extension (NCCE) in Mecklenburg County is seeking a Horticulture and Urban Agriculture Agent to provide dynamic leadership for the development, implementation, and evaluation of effective educational programs to meet the needs for commercial and consumer horticulture and urban agriculture, including small farms. This position is also responsible for pesticide education and certification programs. A general knowledge of sustainable and regenerative agriculture practices specific to an urban area is preferred. The position may be hired at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Agent level if the selected candidate meets the required qualifications. As a key member of the Extension office in Mecklenburg County, the agent will develop and market impactful educational programs. This role requires a high degree of self-direction, project management expertise, and the ability to build collaborative relationships with community members, organizations, and agency partners. Working with a team, the agent will lead the Extension Master Gardener Program in Mecklenburg County. The position will have a 75% focus on commercial horticulture and urban agriculture and a 25% focus on consumer horticulture/Master Gardener management .

title: Radiology Veterinary Assistant
description: The Radiology Department provides diagnostic imaging support to a variety of patients across our campus including small, large and exotic species, offering exposure to an array of cases and advanced medical procedures. In the role you will interact with internal specialty services requiring radiology support and their respective staff, clinicians and students to provide coordination, departmental structure, and assist with veterinary care for all patients associated with the anesthesia service. Direct duties include, but are not limited to: Provides direct patient care and clinical support , including patient assessment, restraint, transport, positioning, venipuncture, sample collection, medication administration, basic treatments, and continuous monitoring before, during, and after diagnostic imaging procedures. Supports diagnostic imaging procedures and specialized equipment , including digital radiography, fluoroscopy, ultrasound, and patient monitoring equipment; assists with equipment operation, routine inspection, cleaning, troubleshooting, and documentation to ensure safe and effective clinical use. Maintains departmental readiness, safety, and regulatory compliance by stocking supplies, preparing and maintaining imaging areas, and adhering to hospital, infection prevention, infectious disease, OSHA, EHS, and radiation safety policies and training requirements. Coordinates patient care and departmental workflow by supporting daily imaging schedules, maintaining accurate patient and procedure information within hospital information systems, documenting patient care and diagnostic procedures, and supporting patients across multiple veterinary specialty services. Provides education, communication, and infection-control support through orientation and coaching of staff, students, interns, and residents; adherence to protocols for infectious and antibiotic-resistant patients; and monitoring, communication, and documentation related to infectious disease and ongoing nosocomial testing. Physical Demand: Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds with or without reasonable accommodations. If you possess a good base knowledge of veterinary medicine, have good time management skills, a strong desire to work in a fast-changing, teaching environment and an ability to collaborate with a broad population of people, we invite you to join our team.

title: UTS - Development Events Coordinator at UNC–TV/PBS
description: This role supports the PBS North Carolina Development team by planning, coordinating, and executing donor, sponsor, community, and fundraising events that strengthen relationships and advance philanthropic engagement. Key Responsibilities include: Manage event logistics from concept to completion, including: Venue coordination Invitations and registration Vendor and catering arrangements Run-of-show development- Event materials and guest communications On-site support Collaborate closely with Development colleagues, the Marketing team, and partners across PBS North Carolina to ensure events are well organized, reflect the PBS North Carolina brand and mission. Provide a welcoming and meaningful experience for donors, prospects, sponsors, and community partners. This position is Hybrid (3 days on-site / 2 days remote)

title: Systems Librarian
description: The Systems Librarian provides primary administration and project management for the Libraries’ Ex Libris Alma platform and public-facing Primo discovery layer. The position facilitates collaborative decision-making for these discovery tools, including chairing the Libraries' Alma Product Team and working with all library services platform teams to align system policies with user and departmental needs. The position translates complex technical developments into clear, functional workflows for colleagues, helping to optimize processes across functional areas, including fulfillment, acquisitions, resource management, resource sharing, and user experience. They partner with other stakeholders to manage the Alma platform’s lifecycle, including monitoring software release schedules, assessing their impacts on library operations, utilizing analytics to generate reports for data-informed decision-making, implementing configuration updates, maintaining technical documentation, and providing functional support for library staff. The position acts as a primary technical liaison with Ex Libris and participates actively in professional communities such as ELUNA, the UNC System, and the Triangle Research Libraries Network (TRLN). They actively explore emerging services and technologies, including AI-driven improvements to library search, discovery, and internal workflows, working to enhance the library user experience. The position deeply considers how their approach to their daily work reflects and advances the Libraries’ Strategic Plan , creating an environment and community that is welcoming for both patrons and colleagues alike. The position works closely with colleagues throughout the Libraries and with university partners, participates in library planning, and serves on library and campus-wide committees, task forces, and teams. Librarians are expected to be active professionally and to contribute to developments in the field. The position reports to the Discovery Systems Manager in Digital Library Initiatives. This position is based in North Carolina. This position is eligible for flexible hours with a hybrid work environment and will require occasional onsite work. NC State promotes an integrated approach to problem solving that transforms lives and provides leadership for social, economic, and technological development across North Carolina and around the world. NC State’s land grant mission of teaching, research and service is dedicated to the service of North Carolina and its people. Applicants are encouraged to review the institution’s mission, vision and strategic plan, and consider how their background, interest and experience would enable them to support the university.

title: Food Service Supervisor
description: Are you a natural leader who thrives in a high-energy environment? NC State Dining is looking for a Food Service Supervisor to manage the daily operations at One Earth. This is a working supervisory position , meaning you aren’t just managing from an office—you are on the front lines leading your team during peak service periods to ensure every student and faculty member receives an exceptional dining experience. We are seeking a professional who is philosophically and operationally committed to efficiency, brand excellence, and the unique service needs of the NC State community. Key Responsibilities Operational Leadership: Supervise unit daily, ensuring all brand standards for food quality, drink preparation, and customer service are strictly maintained. Peak Performance: Lead by example by directing service flow and supporting the team during the busiest dining hours. Administrative Support: Handle essential business functions including planning, forecasting, ordering, and budgeting. Team Development: Hire, train, assign tasks, coach, and provide constructive feedback to employees. Foster a culture of team building and professional growth. Systems & Safety: Utilize menu management system and ensure operation complies with health codes, sanitation standards, and safety regulations. Problem Solving: Address and resolve routine operational challenges and customer concerns with professionalism and poise. The ideal candidate is a proactive mentor who stays calm under pressure. You take pride in “excellence in all tasks” and are dedicated to maintaining a clean, safe, and welcoming environment. Whether you are coaching a new employee or managing a complex lunch rush, your focus remains on delivering high-quality service to the Wolfpack. This role requires physical stamina, including the ability to lift up to 30 pounds, work in hot and cold conditions, and safely handle sharp tools and hot surfaces (all with our without reasonable accommodations). Why Join the Pack? At NC State, you’ll be part of a dynamic campus culture that values innovation and service. We offer a stable work environment where your leadership directly impacts the daily lives of thousands of students. Ready to lead? Apply today to join NC State Dining!

title: Locksmith III
description: The Locksmith III plays a critical role in supporting campus security and access control by providing expert technical knowledge, project management, and leadership for locksmith operations. This position ensures compliance with University standards, accurate project scoping, and efficient resource allocation while delivering exceptional service to campus partners. Locksmith III will guide and mentor technicians, manage complex projects, and advise hardware specifications and installation processes. Responsibilities include reviewing construction plans, preparing cost estimates, coordinating timelines, and ensuring timely completion of work orders. If you are ready to apply your technical expertise, lead impactful projects, and contribute to a safe and secure campus environment, we encourage you to apply today. Key Responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Serve as a technical expert, guiding, directing, and coaching journey and contributing level technicians on application and installation techniques. Research critical information, including key bittings array, construction documents, and guidelines. Understand and apply master key system management software enrollment process and procedures. Demonstrate the ability to review and verify construction plans and hardware specifications according to University specifications and construction guidelines. Proficiently work with hardware specification take-offs. Handle project management tasks with a working knowledge of processes and timelines. Provide cost estimates and proposals for work, which includes evaluating and researching necessary requirements from vendor sources. Monitor and track all orders to ensure timely completion. Assist the supervisor in developing timelines and milestones by identifying critical and less critical activities. Allocate appropriate resources and time for the completion of one’s own work and that of the team, avoiding scheduling conflicts. Communicate effectively with customers regarding the necessary scope of work. Lead by example journey-level technicians, ensuring that both Journey and Contributing level technicians have sufficient resources to complete jobs. Maintain clear verbal and written communication with supervisors, team members, and the public. Lift, carry, and maneuver materials weighing 30–60 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodations. Perform tasks requiring standing for extended periods, working in confined spaces, and utilizing various tools. Safely climb and work from different types of ladders to access elevated or below-grade areas (such as roofs, above-ceiling spaces, and utility pits). Be exposed to and work in areas where insects or small animals are occasionally present. All essential tasks must be performed with or without reasonable accommodations.

title: Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor
department: 140601 - Fitts Department of Industrial & Systems Engineering
description: The Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering (ISE) at NC State University invites applications for open-rank, tenure-track faculty positions at all career stages. The department welcomes candidates whose research and teaching interests align with the broad field of Industrial and Systems Engineering, with particular interest in artificial intelligence and/or quantum computing for optimization; logistics and supply chain management; data science and analytics; and emerging areas of national and international importance. Appointments may be considered at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor level based on qualifications and career stage. In this role, you will shape the future of Industrial and Systems Engineering through research, teaching, and collaboration. You will have the opportunity to establish a distinctive research agenda, pursue meaningful partnerships across disciplines, and translate your expertise into advances that address complex engineering challenges. Through your teaching and mentorship, you will help prepare the next generation of engineers, researchers, and leaders while contributing your perspective and expertise to the continued growth and excellence of ISE and NC State. Key Responsibilities include and are not limited to the following: Build and sustain an independent, externally funded research program that advances Industrial and Systems Engineering and contributes to emerging areas of national and international importance. Conduct and disseminate high-impact research through scholarly publications, presentations, and other contributions to the field. Develop interdisciplinary collaborations within NC State and with external academic, industry, government, and research partners to address complex engineering challenges. Teach and develop courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels, creating engaging learning experiences that prepare students for the evolving field of Industrial and Systems Engineering. Mentor and advise graduate students and support their academic, research, and professional development. Contribute to the department, college, and university community through service, leadership, and activities that advance the mission and vision of NC State. If you are an innovative researcher and educator ready to advance Industrial and Systems Engineering, collaborate across disciplines, and prepare the next generation of engineering leaders, we encourage you to apply.

title: Counselor and Coordinator of Masters Level Internships
description: The Counseling Center assists NC State students experiencing personal, academic or vocational problems. The goal of the Counseling Center is to provide students with professional counseling services and outreach to help them cope with issues that may impede successful academic performance. The Counseling Center also offers crisis intervention and psychological/psychiatric assessment as well as consultation with others who have concerns about the mental/emotional state of NC State students. Our services are primarily short-term in nature and we make referrals to other helping professionals and community agencies as appropriate. The Counselor and Coordinator of Masters Level Internships will provide professional individual and group counseling services and outreach to NC State students as well as consultation to University administrators, staff and others who have concerns about the mental/emotional status of NC State students. This position will have an emphasis on providing leadership and oversight of Masters Level Internship program. This cohort of trainees includes graduate students working on Masters Degrees in Social Work, Counseling and Advanced Practicum Students in Psychology programs. Generalist Counselor: 60% Individual direct service according to IACS standards (individual counseling, groups, crisis response): Individual and group counseling of NC State students/clients (personal, academic, and vocational assessment and counseling); psychological assessment; developmental and crisis counseling; couples counseling; evaluation of students for withdrawal from the University Development and participation in Outreach programming Some participation in after hours “on call” and possible evening office hours Providing evaluations and recommendations regarding students with academic and conduct problems 20% indirect time note writing, session preparation, consultation: Consultation with faculty staff, parents, and others General administrative responsibilities Coordination of the center’s Master’s Level Internship program 20% Training Responsibilities: Develop, organize and maintain a comprehensive clinical training program designed to meet the needs of Masters Interns as well as the overall clinical needs of NC State Counseling Center. Develop, implement and evaluate activities in a manner that is consistent with the academic needs of graduate students in training. Develop understanding of the training and licensure requirements for all three disciplines. Keep current with policies, practices, legal and ethical standards in regard to the provision of clinical training. Conduct evaluative reviews of the training curricula and implement appropriate changes and enhancements that enhance the service needs of NC State Counseling Center. Coordinate annual Intern selection process. Organize and monitor the administrative aspects of supervision to interns and communicate relevant issues to the Training Director, as needed. Communicate with Training Director regarding trainee progress and development. Collaborate with the Training Director and other staff to insure the provision of high quality clinical supervision and evaluation of trainees. Collaborate with Training Director in order to integrate the Master’s Level Internship into the overall Training program which includes trainees from different disciplines at both the Post-Master’s and Doctoral levels. Coordinate remediation and due process procedures for interns and provide reports, as requested by the Training Director. Coordinate staff participation in training activities (e.g., group consult, training seminars and case conferences). Participate in the coordination of needs assessment, strategic planning and outcome assessment for NC State Counseling Center’s Training Program. Provide clinical supervision to trainees and unlicensed staff members (assume oversight and responsibility for each of the trainees’ clients). Work with Training Director to coordinate the training schedule for all Master’s Level interns. Consult with administrative officials of various training programs with regard to any trainees exhibiting difficulties in fulfilling their clinical or professional duties. Coordinate assessment of all trainees to assess progress and outcomes of their learning contract. Maintain strong metrics and assessment procedures and processes to assess the satisfaction and efficacy of the training program and make adjustments as necessary.

title: Cook
description: Are you passionate about food, teamwork, and fueling the next generation of leaders, innovators, and thinkers? NC State Dining is looking for an energetic and reliable Cook to join our culinary team in the Case Dining Hall. In this role, you won’t just be prepping food—you’ll be a vital part of the campus experience, ensuring our community enjoys fresh, delicious, and safely prepared meals every day. As a Cook , you will handle everything from recipe execution to leading station workflows. Your daily duties will include: Master the Menu: Execute standard and routine recipes with precision to fulfill daily menus and keep our food stations stocked and looking great. Inventory & Logistics: Requisition the products you need, and help check in, store, and move food supplies to keep production running smoothly. Teamwork & Flow: Partner with front-of-house staff to coordinate a seamless flow of food from the kitchen to our guests, keeping track of food levels for timely service. Tech & Data: Step up in the absence of a supervising chef by entering necessary data into our Netmenu food production system . Kitchen Cleanliness: Maintain top-tier sanitation by cleaning utensils, workstations, tables, shelves, and equipment—and help delegate cleaning tasks to the back-of-house team. Lead by Example: Ensure daily prep lists are completed and products are properly rotated. You’ll also help assign tasks and direct the efforts of food service technicians, temporary staff, and student employees. Who You Are A team player who thrives in a fast-paced, high-energy environment. Detail-oriented about food safety, cleanliness, and recipe accuracy. A positive motivator who enjoys guiding and directing student and temporary staff. Reliable, punctual, and proud of the food you put out. At NC State, we culture a welcoming community of collaboration and growth. You’ll enjoy a vibrant campus environment, stable scheduling, and the opportunity to grow your culinary career with a trusted university employer. Ready to bring your passion to our kitchen? Apply today and help us keep NC State well-fed and moving forward!

title: Manager for Business and Financial Operations
