description: As the Manager for Business and Financial Operations, you will serve as the primary strategic fiscal advisor to the Department Head and departmental leadership team, co-piloting the unit’s financial strategy, resource allocation, and long-range sustainability. With HR and Research Administration transitioned to specialized College Hubs, you will focus on leading the department’s overall fiscal health, multi-year forecasting across all revenue streams, and high-level alignment among the Department Head, HR Strategy Partner (HRSP), and RA Hub Managers. In this role, you will maintain managerial oversight of the department’s transactional team, serve as the final departmental fiscal approver, and provide the financial insight needed to support strategic decision-making and long-term sustainability. Key Responsibilities Strategic Financial Planning & Analytics Comprehensive Multi-Year Forecasting: Build and maintain dynamic 3–5 year financial models encompassing all departmental revenue streams (State allocations, F&A returns, ETF, Service Centers/Recharge accounts, Foundation/Gifts, Tuition/Fees, and Discretionary streams). Scenario Modeling & Investment: Conduct “What-If” financial analysis for faculty hiring plans, startup package commitments, student funding mechanisms, and space expansion projects. Resource Optimization: Analyze spending trends and macro-level financial datasets to provide data-backed recommendations to the Department Head for strategic reinvestments, cost-savings, or revenue generation. Position & Budget Control: Oversee departmental position management and annual budget construction in close alignment with college financial leadership. Executive & College Reporting: Deliver executive-level financial reports, quarterly variance analytics, and closing metrics to the AD of Finance as requested. Strategic Research & Post-Award Oversight Portfolio Health & Burn Rates: Partner with the RA Post-Award Hub to monitor high-level research portfolio performance, identifying burn-rate anomalies, funding cliffs, and compliance risks (e.g., effort reporting). Proposal & Capability Alignment: Liaise with the RA Pre-Award Hub Manager to evaluate pending proposals against departmental cost-share capabilities, space availability, and long-term financial commitments. Faculty Transition Consulting: Consult with faculty on long-term funding sustainability, managing startup funds, and successfully transitioning early-career faculty to established, self-sustaining research portfolios. Budget Governance, Compliance & Exception Management Fiscal Authority: Serve as the final departmental authority on complex fiscal interpretations, operating on an “exception management” basis rather than approving routine transactions. Audit & Guidelines Compliance: Ensure all departmental funds across State, Trust, Endowment, and Grant accounts strictly adhere to University, State, and Federal regulations. Supervision & Delegation: Directly supervise, mentor, and evaluate in-department transactional finance team members, establishing clear operational workflows and internal controls so the Manager for Business and Financial Operations remains focused on high-level strategy and triage. Leadership & Strategic Partnering Executive Co-Pilot: Serve on the Department Head’s leadership team, providing monthly “Fiscal Health” briefings to both the Department Head and the AD of Finance. Cross-Functional Synergy: Act as the primary financial liaison to the HR Strategy Partner (HRSP) and RA Hub Managers to ensure personnel, research, and financial strategies are fully funded and operationally aligned. Faculty Consulting: Provide strategic financial advice directly to individual faculty members regarding lab financial management, graduate student support, and long-term funding sustainability. If you are a strategic financial leader who enjoys using data, sound judgment, and collaborative problem-solving to guide complex financial decisions, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the department’s long-term financial strategy and sustainability. We welcome you to apply and bring your financial expertise and collaborative approach to this important leadership role .

title: Capital Asset Accountant
description: As the Capital Asset Accountant, you will serve as the operational asset management specialist and subject matter expert for university staff, reporting to the Capital Asset Accounting (CA) Manager. Operating under general direction, you will serve as the primary frontline liaison between central finance and campus departments, ensuring accurate physical tracking, financial recording, and regulatory compliance for university-owned capital assets throughout their lifecycle. In this role, you will provide guidance and support to campus departments while helping ensure the University’s capital assets are accurately managed and accounted for. Key responsibilities: Capital Asset Recording & Inventory Control Identify, tag, and evaluate newly acquired, transferred, or donated equipment to capture physical attributes (make, model, serial number) for entry into the financial system. Monitor tracking reports to ensure timely tagging of assets in compliance with University and UNC System Office policies. Oversee the annual physical equipment inventory process, track departmental submissions, investigate missing assets, and resolve inventory discrepancies. Financial Analysis, Journal Entries & Reconciliation Analyze general ledger transactions, purchase orders, invoices, and journals to evaluate capitalization criteria, allocations, and asset valuations. Prepare general ledger journal entries to reclassify, adjust, and correct financial data across the asset life cycle (acquisition, depreciation, retirement). Reconcile State Surplus sales reports with the Asset Management System and investigate discrepancies. Compliance, Reporting & Audit Support Examine general ledger transactions to prevent and correct misclassifications, ensuring accurate reporting on University financial statements, Federal reports, and cost reports. Compile and format statistical data using Microsoft Excel to assist journey-level accountants and management with audit requests, KPI reporting, and ad-hoc financial analysis. Monitor internal controls and departmental certifications during inventory audits to ensure regulatory alignment. Assist in preparing year-end accrual schedules, depreciation analyses, and financial statements in compliance with Federal, State, and University regulations. Campus Support, Training & Customer Service Serve as the primary point of contact for Campus Asset Coordinators, guiding standard processes for asset acquisition, maintenance, transfer, and disposal. Conduct one-on-one and departmental training on utilization, asset management policies, and inventory procedures. Identify departments struggling with inventory management or compliance, providing remedial support and escalating complex or non-standard issues to higher-level staff. In this role, you will have the opportunity to apply your financial knowledge, problem-solving skills, and customer service approach to support the responsible stewardship of NC State’s capital assets. If you are a detail-oriented accounting professional who values accuracy, accountability, and collaboration, and you enjoy helping others navigate financial and asset management processes, we welcome you to apply.

title: Director of Public Relations
description: The Director of Public Relations, reporting to the Associate Vice Chancellor for Integrated Strategic Communications, leads public relations efforts that shape and protect NC State’s reputation across North Carolina and beyond. As a key member of University Communications and Marketing’s news team, this role develops and advances proactive media opportunities, supports strategic communications for high-visibility university priorities and events, and partners on issues management and crisis communication. The Director works closely with university leadership, communicators across campus, and external media to ensure NC State’s stories, priorities and perspectives are effectively represented. In this role, you will help shape how audiences understand and experience NC State by translating complex university priorities into clear, compelling communications and identifying opportunities to elevate the university’s impact. You will serve as a trusted communications partner on high-profile and emerging issues, helping leaders and campus partners navigate moments that require clarity, coordination and thoughtful response. Your work will contribute to strengthening NC State’s reputation, advancing its priorities and ensuring the university’s voice is represented consistently and strategically across audiences and platforms. Key Responsibilities: Promote and protect NC State’s reputation statewide, regionally and nationally in partnership with University Communications and Marketing, colleagues across campus and university leadership. Develop strategic communications plans and materials, including key messages, scripts, website content, stakeholder announcements, presentations and other communications, including messaging for the Chancellor and other executive-level communicators. Partner on the university’s issues management program by forecasting and triaging potential issues and executing appropriate internal and external communication strategies. Collaborate with University Communications and Marketing team members and senior communicators across NC State to support consistent, proactive outreach across media relations, research communications, social media and digital, marketing and creative teams. Contribute to the university’s media training program and serve as a communications consultant to campus partners, including leadership, faculty and staff. If you’re ready to help shape the conversation around NC State and bring the university’s stories, priorities and impact to audiences across North Carolina and beyond, we invite you to join our team.

title: Police Telecommunicator
description: In this role you will: Receive emergency and non-emergency calls. Dispatch police, fire and rescue to University locations. Operate and maintain Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD). Monitor and dispatch campus-wide fire and intrusion alarms. Operate Division of Criminal Information terminal. Issue and maintain records of departmental equipment. Maintain and update departmental records.

title: UTS - Temporary Executive Assistant at UNC Chapel Hill
description: This role provides high level executive, operational, and calendar management support to the three Vice Deans in the department at UNC Chapel Hill. The primary focus of this role involves managing complex executive schedules, triage and administration of email communications, and coordination of operational projects to ensure all commitments and deliverables are executed with precision and timeliness. Acting as a key administrative liaison, the Executive Assistant facilitates seamless communication and alignment between the Vice Deans, the Dean's Office, university leadership, and external stakeholders. This position requires independent problem solving, sound judgment, high level confidentiality, and the capability to represent executive leadership professionally across all university interactions.

title: Executive Director of Philanthropy
department: 200101 - Dean's Office - Poole College Of Management
description: The Poole College of Management at NC State University seeks an accomplished and collaborative advancement leader to serve as its Executive Director of Philanthropy. This senior leadership position provides strategic direction and oversight for the College’s comprehensive fundraising program while maintaining an active role in cultivating and securing significant philanthropic support. Reporting to the Dean of the Poole College of Management, with a dotted-line reporting relationship to the Assistant Vice Chancellor for University Development, the Executive Director will lead a team of five philanthropy professionals and collaborate closely with University Advancement, faculty and College leadership, alumni, corporate and foundation partners, volunteers, and other key stakeholders. The Executive Director will develop and execute strategies to expand philanthropic support for the College’s priorities, strengthen the donor pipeline, and increase major, leadership-level, and transformational giving. Primary Responsibilities Lead the College’s comprehensive fundraising strategy, including annual planning, goal setting, campaign initiatives, pipeline development, and donor engagement. Maintain an active portfolio of major and principal gift prospects and personally participate in the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of donors. Partner with the Dean, University Advancement, faculty, and College leadership to develop compelling philanthropic opportunities aligned with institutional priorities. Lead, mentor, and develop a team of five philanthropy professionals, establishing clear expectations and fostering a collaborative, accountable, and donor-centered culture. Build strategies to identify and advance prospects capable of making leadership-level, seven-figure, and transformational investments. Engage the Poole College Advisory Board, alumni, corporate partners, foundations, and other volunteer leaders in support of the College’s philanthropic priorities. Serve as a visible ambassador for Poole College and build strong relationships across the university and with external stakeholders. Provide leadership for the continued growth and evolution of the philanthropy program by encouraging innovation, evaluating opportunities, and aligning resources with strategic priorities. Monitor fundraising performance and ensure effective prospect management, reporting, budgeting, compliance, and operational practices. Collaborate across University Advancement to maximize philanthropic opportunities and strengthen long-term donor engagement. The successful candidate will be a strategic and results-oriented leader who combines strong people leadership with demonstrated fundraising expertise. They will be comfortable setting direction for a sophisticated development operation while remaining personally engaged with donors and prospects, and will bring the judgment, relationship-building skills, and collaborative approach necessary to advance the philanthropic potential of the Poole College of Management. Core Responsibilities Leading People: The Executive Director will lead and develop a high-performing philanthropy team by fostering a collaborative, accountable and donor-centered culture. This role will provide mentorship, establish clear expectations and support the professional growth and success of staff. Leading Change: The Executive Director will help guide the continued growth and evolution of the organization by fostering innovation, encouraging collaboration, and embracing new opportunities and ideas. This leader will be adaptable in a dynamic environment, thoughtfully aligning priorities, resources, and initiatives with the long-term goals of the organization. Working closely with internal and external partners, the Executive Director will help cultivate a shared vision that strengthens the organization’s impact, advances strategic objectives, and positions it for sustained success Results Driven: The Executive Director will be an inspiring and visible leader who will engage the collective talents and energies of the development team in collaboration with the AVC for University Development and University Advancement to develop areas of highest potential including donor pipeline building, campaign planning and implementation. They will make decisions that produce high-quality results by applying technical knowledge, and solving problems. They will hold self and others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, results. They will be committed to continuous improvement. Transformational Giving: In partnership with the Dean, University Advancement leadership, the Leadership gifts team and the Principal Gifts team, the Executive Director will help identify, cultivate, solicit and steward prospects capable of making seven-figure and transformational investments in the College. This role will build strategies to grow the pipeline for leadership and principal gifts, align donor interests with college priorities, and collaborate across the university to maximize philanthropic opportunities and long-term donor engagement.

title: CMA/RMA
description: Help support the health and well-being of the NC State community by delivering compassionate, high-quality patient care in a collaborative clinical environment. As a Certified Medical Assistant (CMA) or Registered Medical Assistant (RMA) , you will play an essential role in providing clinical support to medical providers while helping ensure students receive timely, efficient, and patient-centered care. You will work across Primary Care, Gynecology Services, and other Campus Health clinics, contributing to a positive healthcare experience for every patient. Key Responsibilities Clinical Patient Care Assist medical providers with patient intake, obtaining and documenting health information, preparing patients for examinations, and performing basic patient care under the supervision of a registered nurse or Advanced Practice Provider. Perform clinical procedures within scope of practice, including EKGs, venipuncture, medication and vaccine administration, nebulizer treatments, wound care, durable medical equipment (DME) application, ear irrigation, and other provider-directed treatments. Patient Support & Care Coordination Welcome and assist patients with clinic check-in, facilitate patient flow, chaperone examinations when needed, and provide patient education and follow-up instructions as directed by the healthcare team. Float between Primary Care, Gynecology Services, and other assigned clinics to provide flexible clinical support and help ensure continuity of patient care. Clinical Operations Maintain exam room readiness by stocking supplies, preparing equipment, and supporting efficient daily clinic operations. Accurately document patient information and clinical activities using the electronic health record while maintaining confidentiality and supporting quality patient care. If you are a compassionate, detail-oriented medical assistant who enjoys working in a collaborative healthcare environment and is committed to providing exceptional care to college students, we encourage you to apply. If you thrive in a fast-paced clinical setting, value teamwork, and take pride in helping patients feel welcomed and supported, we'd love to have you join the Campus Health team.

title: Sustainability Liaison
description: NC State Dining provides campus-wide food services to students, staff, and faculty on the North Carolina State University Campus. NC State Dining operates 10 cafes, 3 food courts, 6 dining halls, 4 markets, 1 restaurant, vending, a nutritional counseling service, and a catering department. The department employs approximately 1000 temporary and student employees and approximately 190 permanent EHRA and SHRA employees. NC State Dining and Waste Reduction & Recycling are seeking a dedicated Project Liaison to support the rollout of Oscar Sort—an AI-powered smart recycling assistant that retrofits to existing waste bins to visually guide real-time sorting and automate waste analytics. In this role, you will act as the primary operational link between Campus Dining, Waste Reduction & Recycling, campus stakeholders, and the system vendor (Intuitive AI). Your main focus will be overseeing system readiness, troubleshooting visual recognition and software bugs, registering campus packaging, and helping drive student engagement. Essential functions and responsibilities include but are not limited to: System Testing & Bug Resolution: Serve as the boots-on-the-ground lead for identifying visual recognition, hardware, or software errors with the Oscar Sort units. Work directly with the Intuitive AI vendor team to report, log, and resolve bugs promptly. Item & Packaging Registration: Audit campus dining items (containers, cups, lids, food packaging, and organics) to ensure all relevant items are properly scanned, cataloged, and registered within the Oscar AI visual recognition system. Deployment Readiness: Conduct pre-deployment checks to ensure Oscar units are correctly mounted, calibrated to campus recycling guidelines, connected to networks, and ready for daily operations. Peer Outreach & Tabling Coordination: Organize, train, and schedule student ambassadors for campus tabling events. Coordinate live demonstrations showing students how Oscar’s real-time AI nudges work (e.g., separating cup sleeves, emptying liquids, or sorting organics). Stakeholder Liaison: Act as the direct operational bridge between Dining staff, Waste Reduction & Recycling teams, and the student body, gathering feedback on how the units interact with students in high-traffic dining locations. Data & Analytics Tracking: Review initial waste analytics and sorting accuracy data provided by the Oscar platform to share user experience feedback and help optimize waste diversion strategies.

title: Clinical Pathology Residency
department: 196001 - Department of Population Health and Pathobiology
description: The College of Veterinary Medicine at North Carolina State University invites outstanding candidates to apply for a 3-year residency position in veterinary clinical pathology beginning July 2027. The training program focuses on in-depth learning of clinical pathology and ACVP board preparation under the supervision of 4 ACVP board-certified clinical pathologists. The resident will join a busy clinical pathology service and play a role in student education and hospital interactions. In addition, there are local veterinary diagnostic labs and the graduate programs at the CVM draw on abundant resources available in the Research Triangle region (universities, industry, and government) to provide unique research and career opportunities. Applicants must possess a DVM or equivalent degree(s), have an excellent academic record, strong communication skills, and be committed to a career in veterinary clinical pathology. Clinical or a post-DVM experience is desirable. NC State University is near two other major universities (Duke University and the University of North Carolina - Chapel Hill) and the Research Triangle Park, which includes multiple government agencies, non-profit institutes, biotechnology, and large pharmaceutical companies. To view full vacancy announcement, additional requirements, and to apply online, please visit https://jobs.ncsu.edu/ See https://cvm.ncsu.edu/education/residencies/residencies-clinical-pathology/ for program description and additional information. Applications should include (1) a curriculum vitae, (2) statement of career goals, (3) official college and professional school transcripts, and (4) three references (see link to form). We will begin reviewing applications on Oct. 15, 2026, and continue until a suitable candidate is found. The position is available July 15, 2027. The following link is for the reference form which will be in place of traditional letters. Please provide this link to your references https://forms.gle/Mm7Sgb2vBiwhNWZ79 Questions related to the application process can be directed to Caitlin Falls in CVM Human Resources. Reference forms and transcripts can be sent to her via email or regular mail.

title: Small Animal Internal Medicine (SAIM) Fellowship
description: The Small Animal Internal Medicine Service at the NC State Veterinary Hospital is seeking a highly motivated veterinarian for a one to two-year Small Animal Internal Medicine Fellowship . This program is specifically designed for individuals pursuing an academic career path , providing a bridge between residency training and a faculty role. Candidates will engage in advanced clinical service and specialized research training. Specialized Tracks: Applicants must select one of three core focus areas for their fellowship. Each track is designed to provide mastery in a research field while maintaining a strong foundation in general internal medicine: Aerodigestive Disease Vector-Borne Diseases Education and Artificial Intelligence Program Structure & Responsibilities: Clinical Commitment: 25 weeks per year on the Small Animal Internal Medicine service. Specialized Training: Hands-on clinical and research experience directly tailored to your chosen track. Professional Development: Earn professional certificates in your specialty where available (such as Teaching Certificate for the Education track). Research: Completion of a research project suitable for publication in a peer-reviewed journal, with a focus on your chosen sub-specialty.

title: Neurology Fellowship
description: The Neurology Service at the NC State Veterinary Hospital is seeking a board-certified or residency-trained veterinary neurologist for a 12-month Neurology Fellowship. The focus of the fellowship will be dictated by candidate’s interests. Possible areas of interest include (but are not limited to) neurosurgery, neuroimaging, electro diagnostics, epilepsy, neurodegenerative diseases and dementia, and spinal cord injury. Duties and Responsibilities: Provide additional clinical and teaching support to the Neurology Service to ensure there are 2 neurologists on clinical duty throughout the year. Time will be split between being on the clinic floor and advanced training. 34 weeks rotating on the clinic floor 16 weeks dedicated to training in the fellow’s area of interest and research 2 weeks of vacation During the clinical blocks, the fellow will serve as one of two primary clinicians on the Neurology Service, working alongside a second senior neurologist. The majority of the clinic time will be dedicated to supporting the general Neurology Service; however, the fellow will have the opportunity to initiate focus clinics in their area of interest, if appropriate. The off-clinic blocks will be dedicated to advanced training, research efforts, and teaching activities If desired, the fellow will identify a research project that they can reasonably get done in the time available and for which appropriate support is available. This project could overlap with any of their training opportunities.

title: Assistant Professor of Philosophy
description: The NC State Department of Philosophy and Religious Studies welcomes applications for an appointment as a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Philosophy with expertise in logic. Candidates must have completed a Ph.D. in Philosophy by May 2027. The responsibilities of the appointee will include teaching courses on logic up to and including the advanced level and contributing to the department’s teaching needs in other areas of philosophy. In addition to having a demonstrated ability to teach advanced logic, the ideal candidate will also have a record of philosophical research interests that extend beyond logic proper. The teaching load is two courses per semester. Other responsibilities include research and service.

title: Shift Lead
description: NC State Dining is seeking a dynamic, hands-on Shift Lead to assist in managing the daily operations of a high-volume dining location. This role provides leadership and guidance to temporary and student employees, helps ensure smooth and efficient operations, supports employee training, and maintains compliance with all dining, brand, safety, and customer service standards. Lead daily shift operations in a fast-paced food service environment, ensuring quality, efficiency, and adherence to recipes and food preparation standards. Support and guide team members while maintaining excellent customer service and fostering positive communication with staff and guests. Ensure compliance with all food safety, sanitation, and workplace safety procedures, including the safe operation of kitchen equipment. Follow and communicate written and verbal instructions, assist with training, and help the team achieve performance and operational goals. Perform physically demanding tasks, including lifting up to 30 pounds regularly, working in hot and cold environments, and handling kitchen equipment safely.

title: COSS County Administrative Assistant
description: NC State Extension is seeking an Extension Administrative Assistant in the Macon County Extension office. This position offers an opportunity to play an important role in supporting Extension staff and programs that serve local residents and communities. The Extension Administrative Assistant performs a variety of administrative, technical, and executive assistant functions in the Macon County Extension office. This work is characterized by its variety and complexity in serving the public and providing administrative support for Extension staff and programs relating to agriculture, family and consumer science, 4-H youth development, and expanded food and nutrition. The employee functions independently and reports to the County Extension Director. If you enjoy working with people, keeping things organized, and making a difference behind the scenes, we invite you to apply and become part of the NC State Extension team.

title: Temporary Aquatic Field Technician
description: Lead field fish sampling, use dichotomous key to identify fish, collect stream habitat data for project evaluating impacts of dam removal on freshwater fish and stream habitat.

title: Assistant Professor
description: North Carolina State University welcomes applications for an appointment as a tenure-track Assistant Professor with expertise in Hinduism. The faculty position will be housed in the Department of Integrative Humanities and Social Sciences (IHSS), with a joint appointment in the Department of Philosophy and Religious Studies (PRS). The appointment in IHSS will be based in one of the following programs: International Studies; Science, Technology and Society; Arts Studies; or Women’s, Gender and Sexuality Studies. A research focus on modern and/or contemporary periods preferred. Training in pre-modern languages and cultures welcome. The standard teaching load will be four courses per academic year, with two each in IHSS and PRS. Other responsibilities include research, publication, and service.

title: Assistant Professor
description: North Carolina State University welcomes applications for an appointment as a tenure-track Assistant Professor with expertise in film and/or media studies of the Korean peninsula and/or the diaspora. The faculty position will have a joint appointment in the Department of World Languages and Cultures (WLC), therefore the candidate must demonstrate a capacity to teach beginning, intermediate and advanced level of Korean language and culture courses. The appointment in Integrative Humanities and Social Sciences requires that the candidate have an interdisciplinary orientation, as it will be based in one of the following programs: Arts Studies; International Studies; Science, Technology and Society; or Women’s, Gender and Sexuality Studies. In addition to filmmaking and/or videography production, you would also have a strong fine arts background and/or formal training in photography, illustration, painting, drawing, or installation art. The standard teaching load will be four courses per academic year, with two each in the IHSS and WLC departments. Other responsibilities include research, publication, and service. Candidates must have successfully defended their Ph.D. by May 2027.

title: Media, PR, Web & Graphic Design Specialist
description: As a Media, Public Relations, Web & Graphic Design Specialist, you will play a key role in telling the story of the S elf-driving P latforms for E xpedited E xperimental co- D esign (SPEED), an NSF-funded national autonomous-science user facility at NC State. This position brings together science communication, media relations, digital content, web management, and visual design to showcase SPEED’s research, capabilities, people, and impact to audiences within and beyond the scientific community. Core Job Responsibilities: Develop clear, engaging science communications, including news releases, media materials, feature stories, and public-facing content. Manage and enhance SPEED’s website, keeping content, user resources, events, news, and facility information current and accessible. Create compelling visual materials, including graphics, scientific illustrations, infographics, presentations, and branded resources. Produce and edit photography, video, social media, and other digital storytelling content that brings SPEED’s research and capabilities to life. Design user-facing communications for workshops, calls, demonstrations, facility access, and other SPEED activities. Maintain a consistent and recognizable SPEED brand across communications and digital platforms while supporting accessibility, web analytics, media tracking, and content archiving. Support media visits, sponsor reviews, facility tours, major events, and other high-profile communications activities. Build and maintain reusable templates, image libraries, and digital asset archives to support efficient content development. Coordinate with NC State communications professionals and external media partners as appropriate to support SPEED’s communications goals. Translate complex technical and scientific research into clear, engaging content that resonates with broad audiences. This is an opportunity to shape how groundbreaking autonomous-science research is communicated and understood. You’ll bring creativity and strong communication skills to a dynamic research environment. Your work will help build awareness of SPEED’s capabilities and tell the story of the discoveries made possible through this national user facility.

title: Veterinary Surgical Assistant
description: Join a premier veterinary teaching hospital team! This position provides critical surgical support across both the Randall B. Terry Jr. Companion Animal Medical Center and the Equine and Farm Animal Veterinary Center. Our unique team of Veterinary Technicians and Assistants specializes in advanced sterile techniques for a varied array of small and large animal procedures. If you possess advanced knowledge of veterinary medicine and thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative teaching environment, we want you on our team. What You’ll Do: Surgical Prep & Aseptic Technique: Set up advanced surgical suites, validate sterility, manage equipment, and prepare patients using precise aseptic techniques. Intraoperative & Patient Care: Maintain sterile fields, assist during complex surgeries, calculate medications, and support anesthesia and isolation protocols. Equipment & Sterile Processing: Operate and maintain cutting-edge surgical technology (including C-arms, drills, lasers, and microscopes) and manage instrument sterilization. Turnover & Inventory: Ensure rapid room readiness by disinfecting suites, restocking vital supplies, and maintaining strict OSHA compliance logs. Coordination & Mentorship: Streamline surgical scheduling, document critical patient data, and help train the next generation of veterinary students, interns, and residents. What We Are Looking For: Team Players : Active problem-solvers who can work independently with sound judgment but know when to collaborate. Safety-Minded Professionals : Commitment to maintaining a clean, functional workspace in accordance with OSHA, EHS, and hospital infectious disease policies. Operational Agility : Ability to lift up to 50 pounds with or without reasonable accommodations, flexibility to extend hours based on patient needs, and comfort working around potential hazards (zoonotic diseases, chemicals, gases).

title: Outreach Coordinator
description: Help expand access to cutting-edge research while building meaningful connections across academia, industry, government, and education. S elf-driving P latforms for E xpedited E xperimental co- D esign ( SPEED) is an NSF-funded national user facility at NC State University that provides remote access to self-driving laboratories, combining robotics and artificial intelligence to accelerate discovery in chemistry and materials science. As the Outreach and User Engagement Coordinator, you will play a vital role in growing SPEED’s user community by recruiting new users, coordinating engagement activities, and developing programs that connect researchers, students, and external partners with advanced scientific resources. Your work will help strengthen research collaborations, support workforce development, and contribute to the facility’s long-term success and sponsor objectives. Key Responsibilities User Engagement & Community Building Recruit and engage prospective users through targeted outreach, conferences, meetings, partnerships, and networking activities to expand participation across academic, industry, government, and educational communities. Coordinate user onboarding, orientation, facility access, and project start-up activities to ensure a seamless experience for new and returning users. Build and maintain productive relationships with researchers, external partners, and stakeholders while serving as a key point of contact for user engagement initiatives. Programs, Events & Outreach Plan and coordinate workshops, bootcamps, webinars, demonstrations, facility tours, advisory board meetings, sponsor visits, and workforce development programs. Develop and distribute outreach materials, newsletters, announcements, and other user-facing communications that promote facility capabilities, opportunities, and accomplishments. Manage event logistics, registration, speaker coordination, and post-event communications to deliver high-quality engagement experiences. Program Operations & Assessment Maintain user and stakeholder databases, outreach calendars, and participation records to support ongoing engagement efforts. Collect user feedback, testimonials, and success stories while tracking participation, demographics, outcomes, and other program metrics to support reporting requirements and continuous improvement. Collaborate with SPEED leadership and communications staff to develop and implement outreach strategies that enhance user engagement and strengthen the facility's impact. If you are someone who enjoys connecting people with innovative research opportunities, building strong partnerships, and creating engaging programs that make a lasting impact, we encourage you to apply. If you thrive in a collaborative environment, excel at managing multiple priorities, and are passionate about supporting research, education, and scientific innovation, we'd love to have you join the SPEED team.

title: Research Scholar
description: Will work on Camcore research programs in various areas according to expertise. Possible areas include forest genetics, molecular genetics, wood properties, climate change, site species matching, silviculture, etc. Will develop research initiatives for Camcore members, design research experiments, analyze and interpret data, and communicate results to Camcore members. Will work with graduate students and publish scientific articles. Will provide short courses, webinars, and other training material on various aspects of forestry research to Camcore members. Will make technical visits to international member companies to coordinate Camcore breeding and research work, and to provide advice to members on their internal R&D programs.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The School of Social Work invites applications for two tenure-track Assistant Professor positions. Tenure-track and tenured faculty are expected to develop and sustain a strong record of research and scholarship, excel in teaching and advising, engage in community outreach and partnership, and provide service to school, college, university, and profession. We seek candidates with demonstrated expertise in social work theory, practice, research, policy, and a commitment to preparing the next generation of social work professionals. Primary teaching responsibilities will be in the School's Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) program and/or Masters of Social Work (MSW) program. The typical teaching load is two courses per semester.

title: UTS - Temporary Radiology Technician at NC State
description: The primary duties of this position include the following: Taking X-ray images of the human body per order by provider. Interact with internal staff, patients, and referring providers through email, phone, and in-person communications. Keeping equipment clean and in working order. Responsible for maintaining equipment and quality control. Attend scheduled meetings, drills, and training. Perform technical procedures, including patient positioning for radiographs and digital image capturing. Provide excellent patient care by applying full knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and disease processes. Provide quick and accurate information regarding each patient, acting as a liaison between clinicians and radiologists. Proficiently enter data into the electronic health record. Maintain a clean working environment to ensure standards are followed and infection is not spread. Handle medical, biological, and infectious waste appropriately. Follow all radiation safety, OSHA, and Environmental Health and Safety standards.

title: Asst./Assoc. Professor, ITAO
description: The Department of Information Technology, Analytics, and Operations in the Poole College of Management at North Carolina State University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor level. We seek collaborative and innovative scholars specializing in Operations and Supply Chain Management who demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in research, teaching, and service. Position Responsibilities Teaching : Deliver high-quality instruction in Operations and Supply Chain Management at both the undergraduate and graduate (including MBA) levels, in online and in-person formats. Courses may include topics such as operations management, purchasing and supply management, logistics management, operations modeling and analysis, or supply chain management. Research : Develop and maintain a productive research program that leads to publications in top-tier peer-reviewed journals. Service : Contribute to the academic mission of the department, college, and university through committee work, curriculum development, and professional engagement. Perform other duties as assigned by the department head. Candidates must be a contributing faculty member to department and college service activities. If you are a collaborative, innovative scholar with a passion for research and teaching in operations and supply chain management, and are eager to contribute to a dynamic academic community, we encourage you to apply. Appointment Details The anticipated start date is August 16, 2027.

title: Research Operations Coordinator
description: The Research Operations Coordinator serves as the central administrative, financial, and operational authority for a major research group, center, or specialized facility, supporting faculty, postdoctoral researchers, graduate researchers, and visiting scholars. This position bridges research administration and laboratory operations, providing coordination across pre- and post-award activities, budget management, sponsor reporting, service center billing, specialized procurement, equipment and facility operations, travel, vendor relations, and external partnerships. Operating with a high degree of autonomy, the Coordinator serves as a key liaison among Principal Investigators (PIs), College Research Administration, university administrative offices, external corporate partners, and government sponsors. As the Research Operations Coordinator, you will play a critical role in keeping research activities financially sound, operationally efficient, and aligned with university and sponsor requirements. You will coordinate complex administrative processes, anticipate operational needs, build productive relationships with internal and external partners, and help faculty and research teams navigate the administrative requirements that support successful research. Your attention to detail, sound judgment, communication skills, and ability to manage competing priorities will directly contribute to the effective operation and advancement of the research group Key Responsibilities: Embedded Research Administration & Financial Operations Monitor active project budgets and sub-segments across a multi-million-dollar grant portfolio and coordinate rebudgeting, account modifications, summer salary planning, project extension requests, and closeout preparations in alignment with College Research Administration guidelines. Initiate and reconcile high-volume financial transactions, including Vouchers, Journal Vouchers (JVs), Inter-Departmental Transfers (IDTs), P-Card reconciliations, and travel reimbursements in compliance with university and sponsor guidelines. Assist PIs with proposal development for federal, state, and corporate submissions by preparing RED records, drafting non-technical proposal sections, building preliminary budgets, gathering required documentation, and coordinating submission timelines with central proposal development units. Collect financial and technical data to assist PIs with quarterly, annual, and final progress reports for external sponsors and industry subcontractors. Draft and maintain Laboratory Use Agreements for specialized research facilities/centers, manage user activity logs and scheduling, and drive timely invoicing and billing for internal and external lab users. Serve as a local resource for university, state, and federal sponsor policies across academic, financial, procurement, and human resource functions. Independently resolve complex administrative issues and adapt workflows to meet evolving research needs. Laboratory Procurement, Facilities & Building Operations Act as the lead procurement strategist for the research group. Source specialized laboratory equipment, fabricated items, and research consumables via Marketplace, blanket purchase orders, and P-Card protocols. Coordinate with scientific vendors regarding pricing and specifications, oversee laboratory supply inventory, coordinate equipment repair and preventative maintenance contracts, and manage domestic and international shipping of research materials in accordance with compliance protocols. Serve as the primary facilities liaison for the research group’s designated building/lab space. Coordinate with University Facilities Management for maintenance requests, lab safety compliance, security access/key distribution, space scheduling, and emergency notifications. Program Management, Outreach & External Relations Act as the primary administrative point of contact for external corporate, university, and government collaborators. Foster relationships that support interdisciplinary initiatives and research commercialization. Plan and execute academic forums, workshops, sponsor site visits, solar/tech integration meetings, and visiting researcher seminars, coordinating venue logistics, catering, schedules, and visitor accommodations. Maintain and update research group websites, faculty/project profiles, and promotional materials to highlight research achievements and funding milestones. Travel Logistics & Administrative Coordination Design and execute complex travel itineraries for faculty, postdocs, students, and visiting scholars, including travel authorizations, funding approvals, international travel documentation, and post-trip reimbursements. Maintain electronic record archives, including SOPs, equipment manuals, and award files; manage daily group calendars, prioritize operational deadlines, and assist in onboarding new research staff, postdocs, and graduate students into the lab environment. This role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful operational impact by helping research teams move projects forward while ensuring the financial, administrative, and laboratory infrastructure behind that work operates effectively. If you are an organized, resourceful, and collaborative professional who enjoys bringing structure to complex research operations, navigating detailed administrative requirements, and building effective relationships across various groups, we invite you to apply.

title: Temporary Financial Operations Specialist
description: The Temporary Financial Operations Specialist provides accounting and financial operations support within the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS) Business Services unit. Business Services is transitioning to a cross-functional service model in which employees develop proficiency across multiple financial operations functions. Employees will support Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Travel, and Procurement Card (PCard) operations and may be assigned primary responsibilities based on operational needs. Work assignments may shift across functional areas to support workload balancing, team coverage, and continuity of business operations. Primary Responsibilities: Process and support Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Travel, and Procurement Card (PCard) transactions, as assigned. Process, review, reconcile, and analyze financial transactions for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with university policies and procedures. Apply accounting principles and established business processes to transactions across multiple funding sources. Review financial activity for appropriate documentation, classification, and compliance with applicable university, state, federal, and sponsor requirements. Research and resolve transaction discrepancies while maintaining accurate financial records and supporting documentation. Assist with financial monitoring, reconciliation, reporting activities, and audit support. Utilize university financial systems, including PeopleSoft, ServiceNow, and reporting tools, to process, review, and monitor financial activity. Provide customer service and guidance to departments regarding financial processes, documentation requirements, and transaction status. Collaborate with campus partners to resolve financial issues and support efficient business operations. Identify opportunities to improve processes, strengthen internal controls, and enhance operational effectiveness. Participate in cross-training and provide backup coverage across Business Services functions as operational needs require. Perform other duties as assigned

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Postdoctoral Research Scholar will lead the experimental research program on liquid electrolytes for wide-temperature lithium-ion batteries. The objective is a single liquid electrolyte that supports reliable Li-ion full-cell operation across a wide temperature range, where conventional carbonate electrolytes freeze in the cold and degrade at elevated temperatures. The Postdoctoral Research Scholar will design and formulate multi-component electrolytes (salt selection, binary and ternary solvent blending, fluorinated diluents, and additive engineering); build and test coin and pouch full cells under standardized protocols in environmental chambers spanning the full temperature window; characterize Li+ solvation structure and electrode/electrolyte interphases; carry out flammability and thermal-safety screening; and deconvolute electrolyte from electrode contributions to cell performance. The Postdoctoral Research Scholar will also be responsible for day-to-day execution of the NC State scope of work, for supervising the graduate and undergraduate students assigned to the project, and for preparing the deliverables, data packages, and technical reports owed to the prime contractor. Duties and Responsibilities include: Design, formulate, and optimize liquid electrolytes for wide-temperature lithium-ion cells, including salt selection, binary/ternary solvent blending, fluorinated diluents, and additive engineering. Assemble and test coin and pouch full cells (NMC||graphite and related chemistries) in an argon glovebox, including electrode slurry preparation, coating, calendering, and cell crimping. Execute standardized electrochemical evaluation across the full target temperature range using environmental and cryogenic chambers: galvanostatic cycling, rate capability, impedance spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry, and three-electrode/reference measurements. Characterize electrolyte physicochemical properties and Li+ solvation structure (ionic conductivity, viscosity, freezing and phase behavior, Raman, FTIR, NMR) and electrode-electrolyte interphases (XPS, SEM/EDS, and related tools). Perform flammability and thermal-safety screening of candidate formulations under approved safety protocols. Analyze, curate, and archive experimental data; maintain complete and auditable electronic laboratory records. Prepare monthly and quarterly technical progress reports, milestone data packages, and deliverables for the prime contractor and the Army technical point of contact; participate in sponsor teleconferences and program reviews. Write and submit peer-reviewed manuscripts and conference abstracts and present results at national meetings. Train, supervise, and mentor graduate and undergraduate students working on the project. Maintain and troubleshoot laboratory instrumentation (gloveboxes, battery cyclers, environmental chambers, potentiostats. and coordinate calibration and service. Comply with all EHS requirements for handling flammable organic solvents, lithium salts, lithium metal, compressed gases, dry ice and cryogens, and for battery testing.

title: Postdoc Research Scholar- Zhang Lab
description: The Zhang Laboratory’s goal is to continuously innovate and advance medical practice. Members are required to possess solid foundational scientific knowledge and skills while understanding the theories and methods of clinical research. Research areas include biomaterials, drug delivery, and bioprinting. Strategic Partnership Management Liaising with Industry: Acting as the primary point of contact for private sector partners to align research goals with commercial applications or milestones. Managing Material Transfer Agreements (MTAs): Oversight of the logistical and legal exchange of reagents, cell lines, or proprietary data between institutions. Identifying Synergy: Evaluating the capabilities of external labs to determine where collaborative efforts can fill technical gaps or provide access to specialized equipment. Scientific Communication & Representation Formal Advocacy: Representing the Principal Investigator (PI) or the institution in high-stakes meetings, ensuring the lab’s interests and intellectual contributions are protected. Interdisciplinary Translation: Bridging the gap between different scientific fields (e.g., explaining biological data to software engineers or investors) to ensure project cohesion. Stakeholder Reporting: Crafting and delivering progress reports to funding agencies, boards of directors, or steering committees. Conferences & Thought Leadership Dissemination of Findings: Selecting high-impact venues for the presentation of data, ranging from specialized workshops to major international symposia. Panel Participation: Serving as a moderator or expert panelist to influence the direction of the broader scientific discourse. Active Networking: Proactively identifying potential new collaborators and staying abreast of competitors’ progress to maintain the lab’s edge. Collaborative Project Oversight Coordinating Multi-Site Studies: Managing the timeline and data integration for projects involving multiple global locations to ensure consistency in methodology. Conflict Resolution: Navigating disagreements regarding data ownership, authorship order, or research direction between collaborative parties. Grant Support: Assisting in the writing and coordination of multi-investigator grant applications (such as NIH U-series or P-series grants). Other Duties and Responsibilities Ability to perform lab related skills in chemistry, biomaterials, or related fields. Scientific writing for lab research. Develop proposals that seek funding from federal agencies and industry in related areas of research. Conduct experiments using animal models.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The applicants should have proven skills in the following topics: Embedded systems Circuit design Wireless electronics preferably for wearables and/or implantable applications The postdoc will be responsible to conduct the following tasks: Develop and characterize novel, low-power wireless circuits for wearable, implantable, and ingestible devices. Integrate electrochemical and optical sensors with wireless circuits for bidirectional communication. Additional responsibilities include training undergraduate, graduate, and high school students and working with various collaborators.

title: Extension Program Assistant/Associate,4-H
description: Are you looking for a rewarding career that will let you give back to your community? NC State Extension extends research-based knowledge to all North Carolinians, helping them transform science into everyday solutions that improve their lives and grow our state. We are the model of excellence in non-formal, research-based education that advances agriculture, the environment, human health and well-being, youth and communities, while creating prosperity for all North Carolinians. Check out this video on what it’s like to work for NC State Extension. While our employees are located in NC County offices, they reap the benefits of employment at NC State University. Some of our benefits include: Paid time off Paid tuition Health Insurance Retirement Savings Supplemental Benefits Programs WolfPerks! You Belong Here! At NC State, our goal is for all employees to reach their fullest potential at work. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition ( https://news.hr.ncsu.edu/you-belong-here/ ) and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone. The primary role of the Program Assistant is to conduct 4-H curriculum/school enrichment programs at schools for grades K-12th (ages 5-18) and develop summer youth educational programs in accordance with the mission and priorities established by the National 4-H Council and in alignment with the mission and vision of N. C. Cooperative Extension. The Extension Program Assistant cooperates with colleagues on the Northampton Cooperative Extension Staff and county citizens in performing their assigned responsibilities. This position is responsible for expanding and developing programs to include under-represented populations. The 4-H Program Assistant is a member of the North Carolina Cooperative Extension Staff in Northampton County. The Primary role of the 4-H Program Assistant is to provide assistance mainly to youth-related programming but is not limited to the youth-only subject matter.

title: County Extension Director
description: Are you looking for a rewarding career that will let you give back to your community? NC State Extension extends research-based knowledge to all North Carolinians, helping them transform science into everyday solutions that improve their lives and grow our state. We are the model of excellence in non-formal, research-based education that advances agriculture, the environment, human health and well-being, youth and communities, while creating prosperity for all North Carolinians. Working for NC State Extension allows you to teach without being tied to a classroom and school bell. While our employees are located in NC County offices, they reap the benefits of employment at NC State University. Some of our benefits include: Paid time off Paid tuition Health Insurance Flexible Scheduling Retirement Savings Supplemental Benefits Programs WolfPerks! You Belong Here! At NC State, our goal is for all employees to reach their fullest potential at work. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition ( https://news.hr.ncsu.edu/you-belong-here/ ) and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone. The County Extension Director is a leadership position with Cooperative Extension at North Carolina State University. The major responsibility of the job is to provide leadership for and coordinate the efforts of the county Extension staff in developing an effective total county Extension educational program in cooperation with North Carolina A&T State University’s Cooperative Extension Program . The position requires a dynamic individual to provide visionary leadership for a comprehensive Extension program to meet the needs of all segments of the population. The County Extension Director serves as the County Extension administrative leader with responsibilities for administration, public policy issues, and community/leadership development. The County Extension Director is responsible for maintaining an effective advisory leadership system representative of all program areas. The County Extension Director provides leadership and expertise in coordinating/securing resource development for all program areas. Responsibilities include marketing Extension programs and impacts. The County Extension Director must maintain a strong, collaborative relationship in assisting the staff in delivering educational programs with county government input and support. Also, to meet the needs of county citizens, the position must network and collaborate with agencies and organizations, county departments, schools, town officials, area agencies, and University and Extension personnel. The position will be responsible for coordinating staff development, and training. The individual must demonstrate the ability to plan, organize, and work well with people.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor (Tenure Track) - Music Technology
description: The Department of Performing Arts and Technology at North Carolina State University seeks applications for a tenure-track, nine-month, full-time Assistant/Associate Professor in Music Technology. The successful candidate will play an integral role in the delivery and expansion of the Music Technology program that operates in collaboration with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. The successful candidate will be expected to develop an externally funded research program (45%) and teach courses (45%) in musical acoustics and psychoacoustics, sound isolation, recording, mixing, audio digital signal processing, audio effects development, sound design, video game audio, audio/musical electronics, and/or additional music technology areas associated with the candidate’s expertise. The successful candidate will also assist in student advising, serve on department committees, and assist in the management and maintenance of the classroom and lab technology for hands-on experimental learning projects.

title: Project Coordinator
description: The department of Psychology is seeking a project coordinator to assist with an NIH-funded research initiative through May 31,2027, with the possibility to continue in this role if new grant funding is awarded. In this role you will coordinate complex, multi-institutional research activities and ensuring project goals, deliverables, and collaborative commitments are achieved within established timelines and resource constraints. Working across research teams and institutional partners, you will coordinate project operations, manage workflows, and maintain the administrative and data infrastructure needed to support successful grant execution. You will serve as a key point of coordination among investigators and stakeholders, anticipating needs, resolving logistical challenges, and keeping priorities on track. Through thoughtful communication, organization, and follow-through, you will support critical administrative responsibilities, strengthen collaboration, and ensure research teams have the coordination and infrastructure needed to advance the initiative’s objectives and successfully meet project milestones. Key responsibilities will fall within the following functional areas: Project Management Collaborate with investigators, operational users, and subject matter experts to understand research and operational needs and support solutions that advance project objectives. Establish and track project deliverables, milestones, timelines, and reporting requirements across multiple collaborating teams and institutions. Coordinate project roles, requirements, review cycles, and dependencies to maintain alignment with NIH priorities, project goals, and resource constraints. Facilitate the preparation, organization, and ingestion of study metadata and related documentation into an online data portal while supporting compliance with data-sharing and documentation standards. Monitor project progress, identify emerging risks and operational challenges, and recommend practical mitigation strategies to project leadership and investigators. Lead and document project status meetings, communicate project updates, and prepare summaries and materials for investigators, advisory groups, and funding agencies as needed. Maintain visibility into project activities, deliverables, schedules, and operational needs while promptly communicating issues and coordinating solutions with project participants. Operations & Administrative Management Coordinate with institutional administrative and financial personnel to support subaward and independent contractor onboarding, agreement processing, invoicing, and related documentation. Assist with preparing and processing independent contractor agreements and other project-related administrative materials. Develop and maintain workflow documentation and repeatable practices that promote consistent communication, collaboration, and efficient project operations. Coordinate workshops, stakeholder meetings, training events, and collaborative research activities that support project goals and engagement across participating teams. Prepare post-event reports and summaries documenting participation, outcomes, recommendations, and follow-up actions. Partner with project leadership to identify, coordinate, and monitor resources needed to support project activities and strategic priorities. If you are an organized, collaborative professional who enjoys bringing structure to complex research initiatives, building strong partnerships, and keeping projects moving toward meaningful outcomes, this role offers an opportunity to make a direct impact on an NIH-funded initiative. Your coordination, communication, and problem-solving skills will help connect people, processes, and resources to support successful project execution and advance the initiative’s research goals.

title: Assistant Professor in Insect Ecology
description: The Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology invites applications for a nine-month, tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Insect Ecology with 60% effort in teaching and mentoring and 40% effort in research and discovery. We seek a dynamic scholar committed to excellence in undergraduate and graduate education, student engagement, and innovative teaching, alongside development of an active, externally funded research program. The Assistant Professor will play a central role in the department’s undergraduate curriculum, including instruction of ENT 201: Insects and People , a high-enrollment course serving approximately 140 students in an in-person spring section and virtual sections offered in spring and fall. Additionally this role will contribute to additional undergraduate and graduate courses aligned with the faculty member’s expertise and departmental needs. In addition to teaching, you will have the opportunity to establish a nationally recognized research program broadly focused on insect ecology, with research spanning areas such as insect behavior, plant–insect interactions, community ecology, conservation, global change biology, or related fields. Your research program will attract competitive extramural support from federal agencies, foundations, industry, and other sources while providing meaningful research and professional-development opportunities for undergraduate, graduate, and postdoctoral students. Key Responsibilities: Teaching and Mentoring: Lead instruction for ENT 201: Insects and People , including in-person and distance-education formats, and teach additional undergraduate and graduate courses aligned with expertise and departmental needs. Develop and use innovative, accessible, and technology-enhanced instructional approaches while contributing to curriculum development, assessment, and continuous improvement. Mentor undergraduate, M.S., and Ph.D. students through research, experiential learning, and career development. Support student recruitment, retention, and success while contributing to departmental teaching initiatives. Research and Discovery: Develop and sustain an externally funded research program in insect ecology that complements and strengthens departmental expertise. Conduct impactful research that may integrate field-based ecological studies with molecular, computational, spatial, or other data-driven approaches, and maintain a strong record of peer-reviewed publications and scholarly productivity. Engage undergraduate and graduate students in research, providing meaningful training and mentorship. Collaborate with departmental, university, and external partners to advance research, teaching, and outreach goals. Service and Engagement: Contribute to departmental, college, university, and professional service through committee participation, faculty governance, scientific societies, and manuscript and grant review. Foster interdisciplinary collaborations and contribute to a collegial and productive academic environment. Engage in outreach that enhances the visibility and impact of the department and university. If you are an engaged educator and collaborative scholar who sees opportunities to connect insect ecology with the questions that matter to students, communities, and the broader scientific community, we invite you to join the Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology.

title: Assistant Director, Electrical and Mechanical Engineering Systems BSE Program
description: The duties of the Assistant Director will include, but not be limited to, the following: Management and Coordination of Engineering Labs Supervise locally hired staff for engineering lab classes Oversee the maintenance of lab and work area equipment Plan for and acquire the equipment needed in the lab and work area Update lab manuals and maintain inventory of materials students need for the labs Coordinate instructional support for Raleigh and local classes Coordinate with Raleigh instructors special office hours and review sessions and maintain a relationship with MAE and ECE departments Maintain and troubleshoot DE equipment working closely with Engineering Online classroom support staff in Raleigh Assist students with design projects as needed Work closely with Havelock staff and Raleigh staff in the receipt and/or transmission of class lectures from Raleigh or other site locations, such as Asheville Review and improve program processes and procedures to support program vision Implement ABET and University continuous improvement assessment processes. Oversee integrated curriculum to ensure skills are effectively built as students move through the program Manage and participate in program recruiting and outreach Seek out opportunities in regional K-12 schools and community colleges to teach or expose students with the various engineering disciplines Develop special activities for students and their parents to visit the Havelock Engineering program.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The department of Philosophy and Religious Studies invites applications for a Postdoctoral Research Scholar in STS, empirical neuro ethics, or ethics of AI at the Neuro Computational Ethics Research Group, in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, beginning January 2027 . Duties and Responsibilities Include: developing and experimentally testing VR simulations for moral decision making broadly promoting AI ethics scholarship The position entails a specific research agenda that aligns with activities described in Dr. Veljko Dubljevic's NEH AI Center grant.

title: Temporary Genetics Research Technician
description:
Posting Number: PG196209TM
Position Number: 11ASO3757
Position Type: Temporary
Essential Job Duties: This is mainly a laboratory research position to conduct genetic assays of honey bees. The majority of the incumbent’s duties will be to participate in an active laboratory operation to support and participate in the apicultural research program. Duties and techniques may include dissections and bioassays of live queens, DNA extractions from animal (honey bee) tissue, PCR reactions, gel electrophoresis (agarose and polyacrylamide), molecular genotyping, RNA extractions, and qRT- PCR . Some field work is also likely in the position, such as sampling bees from colonies, but these activities constitute a minor component. Some logistical work and coordination for a summer internship program is also expected. Work Schedule: The normal work schedule will be up to five (5) days per week for four (4) to eight (8) hours per day. Flexibility in schedule, however, is necessary for the position. Many research projects necessitate, for example, longer hours for a given day or working on weekends.
