title: Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Psychology at NC State University is seeking a tenure-track Assistant Professor to advance research, teaching, and service in Lifespan Developmental Psychology beginning Fall 2027. We invite scholars who conduct applied developmental research at any stage of the lifespan, including infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and/or aging. While the research area is open, we are especially interested in candidates who bridge the gap between laboratory science and real-world impacts that improve lives in varied environments using multimodal data. Faculty members in Lifespan Developmental Psychology conduct both basic and applied research spanning the lifespan, with an emphasis on cognitive, socioemotional, and health-related development. The purpose of this position is to complement and extend these existing strengths while contributing to our collaborative, interdisciplinary approach to understanding development across the lifespan. In this role, you will develop a productive research program that advances understanding of development across the lifespan and contributes meaningful scholarship to the discipline. You will teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students, helping them develop as scholars and professionals, while contributing your expertise to the continued growth of the Lifespan Developmental Psychology program and the broader discipline. Key Responsibilities: Develop and sustain an independent research program in lifespan developmental psychology. Disseminate research through scholarly publications, presentations, and other professional outlets. Teach courses that support undergraduate and graduate education in psychology. Mentor undergraduate and graduate students in their academics, research, and professional development. Contribute service and professional leadership within the Lifespan Developmental Psychology program area, department, college, university, and broader field. If you are a scholar in lifespan developmental psychology who is excited to build a meaningful research program, connect laboratory science with real-world impact, engage students through teaching and mentorship, and contribute to a collaborative academic community, we encourage you to apply.

title: Temporary Food Service Supervisor
description: NC State Dining offers opportunities for employment across our retail and hospitality units. We offer competitive pay and opportunity for learning, growth, and promotion. Dedicated and experienced dining professionals are available to provide on-the-job training and support to help you meet your full potential. We are seeking individuals to Join our Pack as a Temporary Supervisor. Successful candidates will work in Clark Dining Hall dining facility located on the campus of NC State University. Essential Job Duties: Organize and manage the dining room to maintain operations for Clark Dining Hall. Supervise all employees on their shift. Ensure Unit SOP's are being followed and staff are on task. Provide professional redirection as appropriate. Assist with closing duties as necessary. Provide excellent customer service. Other duties as assigned to ensure NC State Dining business needs are met. Position may be asked to assist in other locations as necessary. NC State Dining provides campus wide food services to students, staff, and faculty on the North Carolina State University Campus. NC State Dining operates 10 cafes, 3 food courts and 6 dining halls, 4 markets, 1 restaurant, vending, a nutritional counseling service, and a catering department. The department employs approximately 1000 temporary and student employees and approximately 190 permanent EHRA and SHRA employees. This is an hourly position, that includes a State required 32-day break at the end of 11 months. Superior work performance may provide an opportunity to renew employment and/or advance into a benefits eligible permanent position.

title: Locksmith I
description: Join NC State University’s Facilities Division as a Locksmith I and help keep our campus buildings secure, safe, and fully operational. In this hands-on role, you’ll work alongside experienced locksmiths while gaining valuable skills in the installation, repair, and maintenance of a wide range of security hardware. You’ll assist with lock repairs and installations, master key systems, lock adjustments, and preventative maintenance across campus. This is an excellent opportunity to build your locksmith expertise, work with skilled professionals, and play an important role in supporting the daily operations of a large university campus. Ready to build your skills while making an impact at NC State? Apply today and join our Facilities team! Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Install, repair, and maintain mechanical security hardware, including door locks, desk and file cabinet locks, door closers, mortise locks, exit devices, and other door hardware. Cut keys by duplication and code while assisting with key blank identification and core keying. Change lock combinations and service small-format interchangeable cores. Perform preventative maintenance on locking systems to ensure long-term reliability and proper function. Assist senior locksmiths with lock installations, repairs, and master key system work across campus facilities. Learn and operate locksmithing equipment, including key machines, code machines, and keypunches. Troubleshoot mechanical locking hardware issues and assist in diagnosing system failures. Conduct initial situational assessments to identify the cause of malfunctioning locks or door hardware. Track work orders, document service requests, and provide status updates using the AiM work order system. Coordinate with faculty, staff, vendors, and shop personnel to complete assigned work orders and projects. Assist with ordering materials and coordinating supplies needed for installations and repairs. Complete assigned work within established timelines to support project schedules and budget expectations. Maintain the locksmith shop by assisting with organization, cleaning, and proper tool care. Support emergency response efforts and perform critical role duties when needed to maintain facility security. Verify work accuracy and ensure installations meet safety standards, building codes, and university requirements. Participate in ongoing training and demonstrate a willingness to learn emerging security technologies. Assist with project closeouts and coordinate follow-up communication with customers after work completion. Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follow verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs. Perform lifting duties up to 30 pounds frequently and 60 pounds occasionally, with or without reasonable accommodations.

title: Crew Leader I - 62239
description: The Crew Leader I plays a key role in maintaining a clean, safe, and welcoming campus environment. In this position, you will provide hands-on leadership and operational oversight for a variety of facilities projects, including specialized floor care, power washing, and window maintenance . You will coordinate daily work activities, guide and support team members, ensure quality and safety standards are met, and help resolve maintenance concerns in a timely manner. This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated leader who enjoys working collaboratively, delivering exceptional customer service, and making a visible impact on the campus community through high-quality facilities operations. If you are a dependable leader who takes pride in creating well-maintained spaces and supporting a successful team, we encourage you to apply and join us in making a difference every day. Working Hours: Monday-Friday, 4:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Lead projects, including power washing, window washing, floor waxing, and re-lamping fixtures and dispensers Inspect and verify maintenance discrepancies and ensure timely resolution Provide support to other zones as needed, filling in for vacant positions or absenteeism Collect and submit timesheets within established timelines Perform critical duties during adverse weather or emergencies as assigned Complete accident reports within 24 hours of an incident Assist with equipment inventory and maintain monthly inventory of storage closet supplies Submit supply orders for manager approval to ensure adequate stock levels Train new employees , ensuring they understand tasks and safety protocols Transport employees to various locations for assignments Collaborate with maintenance staff inside and outside the unit to resolve issues efficiently Address and resolve customer requests via radio communications, work orders, and direct interactions Ability to lift a minimum of 60 pounds continuously and 90 pounds occasionally with or without reasonable accommodations, climb and balance on a ladder up to 8ft. and distinguish between colors. Communicate effectively with supervisors, coworkers, and the general public, and follow verbal and written instructions related to work assignments and operational needs.

title: Assistant Professor in Elementary Teacher Education
description: The Department of Teacher Education and Learning Sciences (TELS) invites applications for an Assistant Professor in Elementary Teacher Education to be affiliated with undergraduate and graduate studies in elementary teaching and learning. This is a tenure-track appointment at the Assistant Professor level, with teaching, scholarship, service, and outreach expectations. We are seeking those who are scholars in elementary teacher education who will lead and contribute to research on approaches and programs that prepare pre-service teachers. You will engage in research primarily focused on elementary teacher preparation programs’ features and impact. This might include elements such as modality (e.g., face-to-face, hybrid, online), structure (e.g., traditional four-year programs, part-time programs for practicing teachers, competency-based education), or pathway (e.g., bachelor's degree, master's degree, residency, registered apprenticeship). Additionally, you will submit proposals for internal/external funding in support of the related research. The ideal candidate will teach undergraduate and graduate courses in elementary teacher preparation, including the Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) program, with a strong preference for those who teach elementary social studies education. As a faculty member, you will provide service and leadership to the Elementary Education program area, the department, college, and university. You will participate in outreach and engagement activities with elementary schools locally and across North Carolina, and collaborate with faculty within the department, college, and across the university. Position Responsibilities Maintain a high level of scholarly research, publication, and grant-writing activity that aligns with a tenure track position in a university with high research activity. Produce high quality research on pre-service teacher preparation programs, features, and impact. Seek external funding for research and development activities. Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in elementary education, with a strong preference for social studies pre-service teacher education graduate and undergraduate programs Recruit, advise, and mentor graduate students and serve on doctoral committees. Engage in collaborative research with other faculty and researchers within the College of Education, including the Friday Institute for Educational Innovation and the Belk Center for Community College leadership, as well as across the university. Provide service and leadership in the elementary education program, department, college, university, and professional organizations. Participate in outreach and engagement for department and college initiatives with underserved communities and high need areas and engaging with stakeholders across the state of North Carolina. If you are passionate about preparing future elementary educators and interested in teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in elementary teacher preparation, including the Master of Arts in Teaching (MAT) program, with expertise in elementary social studies education, we encourage you to apply and join our faculty.

title: UTS- Temporary Surplus/Warehouse Assistant at UNC Chapel Hill
description: The primary responsibility of this position is to support the operations of the department by efficiently handling incoming and outgoing property. This includes loading and unloading items, stocking shelves, and ensuring accurate inventory management. The role also involves assisting customers with property viewings and purchases, optimizing warehouse space utilization, maintaining communication across departments, and upholding cleanliness and organization standards. The individual must be capable of safely lifting up to 50 lbs. with or without reasonable accomodations and performing additional duties as assigned.

title: Assistant Professor
description: The Department of Economics in the Poole College of Management at North Carolina State University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor level. We seek a scholar specializing in macroeconomics who is committed to excellence in research, teaching, and service. Position Responsibilities Teaching: Deliver high-quality instruction in economics at the undergraduate and graduate levels, in both in-person and online formats as needed. Teaching responsibilities will primarily support courses in macroeconomics and related areas. Research: Develop and maintain a productive, independent research program in macroeconomics or closely related fields that results in publications in high-quality peer-reviewed journals and contributes to the department’s research mission. Service: Contribute to the academic mission of the Department of Economics, Poole College of Management, and NC State University through committee service, curriculum development, professional engagement, and other departmental activities. Appointment Details This is a full-time, tenure-track appointment at the Assistant Professor level. The anticipated start date is August 16, 2027. If you are a collaborative and engaged scholar who wants to strengthen the department’s expertise in macroeconomics and contribute to its research and teaching missions, we encourage you to apply.

title: Contract Negotiator
description: The Contract Negotiator will support NC State University’s sponsored research and other sponsored activities by developing and negotiating agreements with external sponsors. The position will work across a range of federal, state, local, nonprofit, and other organizations to help establish agreements that support the University’s research, instruction, and sponsored activities while aligning with institutional policies and applicable requirements. As the Contract Negotiator, you will apply subject-matter knowledge and sound judgment to navigate complex agreements, work with internal and external stakeholders, and help reach terms that support both the University and its research community. You will play an important role in identifying and addressing institutional risk while ensuring agreements are clear, accurate, and well organized. Key responsibilities will fall within the following functional areas: Contract Drafting & Negotiation: Draft sponsored project agreements using standard University templates for incoming and outgoing projects. Review and negotiate external sponsors’ agreements to ensure terms are acceptable and compliant. Identify non‑conforming contract language and negotiate modifications to align with University, UNC System, and regulatory requirements. Prepare and negotiate subawards with external entities, ensuring accuracy and compliance. Risk Assessment & Compliance Review: Analyze institutional risk tolerance and conduct subrecipient risk assessments. Interpret legal agreements and assess the impact of proposed terms. Consult with University compliance offices (Office of Regulatory and Institutional Compliance, Post Award Financial Services, Research Commercialization, General Counsel) to ensure negotiated terms support University and sponsor requirements. Stakeholder Engagement & Communication: Provide guidance to University clients on proposals, contract terms, and negotiation considerations. Communicate negotiation progress to stakeholders and ensure accurate, timely information sharing. Explain reporting obligations and provide complete information needed for financial and technical reporting. Training, Resources & Process Support: Develop training materials, update templates, and contribute guidance for the SPARCS website. Deliver classroom training or consultations to support research administrators across campus. In this role, you will have the opportunity to contribute to research and sponsored activities while helping the University manage risk, support its research community, and build effective partnerships with external sponsors. If you are an analytical and collaborative professional who enjoys navigating complex agreements, building productive relationships, and finding solutions that balance institutional and sponsor needs, we invite you to bring your negotiation and problem-solving skills to NC State University.

title: Health and Safety Specialist
description: Help create safer workplaces by delivering high-quality occupational safety and health training, consultation, and technical assistance to organizations across North Carolina and the surrounding region. As a member of Industry Extension Services (IES), you will empower employers, employees, and industry partners with the knowledge and resources needed to improve workplace safety while supporting the growth and success of the Southeastern OSHA Training Institute Education Center (SEOTI EC). Key Responsibilities Occupational Safety Training & Instruction Deliver OSHA Training Institute Education Center courses, including OSHA-authorized trainer courses, update courses, and topic-specific technical courses in both in-person and virtual learning environments. Ensure all OTIEC courses are delivered in accordance with OSHA Training Institute Education Center requirements, policies, procedures, and established course delivery standards. Client Consultation & Technical Assistance Provide customized occupational safety and health training, workplace safety assessments, and consultation services for manufacturing, construction, government and service industry employers . Communicate OSHA regulatory requirements, industry standards, and workplace safety best practices to varied audiences. Curriculum Development & Program Support Develop, revise, and maintain instructional materials, presentations, online learning content, and other training resources that support classroom and virtual learning. Participate in program planning, customer engagement, outreach activities, conferences, meetings, and special projects that contribute to the growth and revenue generation of Industry Extension Services and the SEOTI Education Center. Maintain current knowledge of OSHA regulations, industry trends, and emerging workplace safety issues while supporting organizational initiatives and other assigned responsibilities. If you are an engaging educator who enjoys helping organizations create safer workplaces, excels at communicating technical information to varied audiences, and values continuous learning and collaboration, we encourage you to apply. If you are organized, enjoy traveling to support clients, and are passionate about occupational safety and health, we'd love to have you join the Industry Expansion Solutions team.

title: Assistant/Associate Teaching Professor in Geospatial Analytics
description: The Center for Geospatial Analytics is seeking a highly qualified instructor to join our academic programs at the rank of Assistant or Associate Teaching Professor (non-tenure). The candidates we are seeking are forward-looking instructors with a strong background in both foundational geospatial concepts and skills alongside modern approaches, such as open-source and cloud-based/native platforms, WebGIS, GeoAI, Geospatial Data Science, and a strong interest in innovative geospatial pedagogy and dedication to student success. This is a full-time, 9-month professional track faculty position with an initial contract of three (3) years, with opportunities for multiple renewals and advancement based on annual performance reviews and progress. The Assistant or Associate Teaching Professor will play an instrumental role in developing and delivering high-quality courses for the Center’s highly-ranked academic programs. In this role, you will shape students’ learning experiences through 15–18 credit hours of teaching each academic year across the Fall and Spring terms. You will teach courses within the existing curriculum while also having the opportunity to develop new courses that reflect your expertise, interests, and emerging needs in the field of geospatial analytics. Teaching responsibilities will include: An undergraduate- or graduate-level introductory GIS course (3 credit hours) The undergraduate Minor Capstone Course, Geospatial Analytics in Practice (1 credit hour; Fall and Spring) Two additional undergraduate courses, or a combination of undergraduate and graduate courses, based on program needs and the candidate’s interests. Potential topics for new courses include, but are not limited to, Geospatial AI, Geospatial Ethics, AI and Data Literacy in GIS, Environmental/Public Health/Hydrological Applications, and Geospatial Communication and Cartography. Service and engagement responsibilities include: Participation in the Center’s academic community through student advising and mentoring, including serving as an academic advisor for a portion of MGIST students Participation in committees in support of program-level initiatives and outreach, as requested If you enjoy connecting technical geospatial concepts to practical applications, communicating clearly with students, and collaborating with colleagues to develop and strengthen courses, we encourage you to apply.

title: Assistant Dean of Philanthropy, Engineering
description: The Assistant Dean of Philanthropy is the chief fundraising and engagement officer for the College of Engineering and reports directly to the Dean with a dotted line to the Associate Vice Chancellor, University Development. This role provides strategic leadership for the college’s advancement program, manages the advancement team, and works closely with university leadership, faculty, alumni, donors, and community partners to advance philanthropic priorities and strengthen engagement. The Assistant Dean also serves as President of the NC State Engineering Foundation and sets the overarching strategy and vision for advancing philanthropy and provides strategic leadership to developing and advancing a comprehensive philanthropy program for the College. The position partners closely with University Advancement, the Leadership Gift team and the Principal Gifts team to cultivate and secure transformational support for the College and university. The successful candidate will lead and develop a team of advancement professionals while personally managing a portfolio of major, Leadership and principal gift prospects and donors. Key Responsibilities Leading People: The Assistant Dean will lead and develop a high-performing advancement team by fostering a collaborative, accountable and donor-centered culture. This role will provide mentorship, establish clear expectations and support the professional growth and success of staff across advancement functions. Leading Change: The Assistant Dean will help guide the continued growth and evolution of the organization by fostering innovation, encouraging collaboration, and embracing new opportunities and ideas. This leader will be adaptable in a dynamic environment, thoughtfully aligning priorities, resources, and initiatives with the long-term goals of the organization. Working closely with internal and external partners, the Assistant Dean will help cultivate a shared vision that strengthens the organization’s impact, advances strategic objectives, and positions it for sustained success Results Driven: The Assistant Dean will be an inspiring and visible leader who will engage the collective talents and energies of the development team in collaboration with the AVC for University Development and University Advancement to develop areas of highest potential including donor pipeline building, campaign planning and implementation. They will make decisions that produce high-quality results by applying technical knowledge, and solving problems. They will hold self and others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, results. They will be committed to continuous improvement. Transformational Giving: In partnership with the Dean, University Advancement leadership, the Leadership gifts team and the Principal Gifts team, the Assistant Dean will help identify, cultivate, solicit and steward prospects capable of making seven-figure and transformational investments in the College of Engineering. This role will build strategies to grow the pipeline for Leadership and principal gifts and collaborate across the university to maximize philanthropic opportunities and long-term donor engagement. Foundation Board Strategy: The Assistant Dean’s overarching responsibility is to promote philanthropic investment to fulfill and advance the mission of the College of Engineering. This encompasses working with the Dean of the College of Engineering, the AVC for University Development, Foundation board members and internal partners to foster a culture that advances philanthropy and engagement that goes beyond transactional and toward building lasting relationships with donors. Foundation Operations: As President of the NC State Engineering Foundation, the Assistant Dean will provide leadership for Foundation governance, board engagement, communication and fiscal oversight. This role will work closely with the Foundation Board of Directors to support effective operations, transparency in alignment with university policies and priorities.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Department of Materials Science and Engineering (MSE) at NC State University is a nationally recognized leader in materials discovery, design and deployment. Our faculty, students and staff work at the forefront of innovation: advancing materials that enable breakthroughs in energy, electronics, health, manufacturing and sustainability. Research in MSE spans theory, computation, synthesis, characterization and scale-up, supported by a collaborative culture and state-of-the-art facilities on NC State’s Centennial Campus. Faculty lead internationally visible efforts in areas such as artificial intelligence-driven materials design, wide bandgap semiconductors, energy storage, nanomaterials, soft and biomaterials and structural materials under extreme environments. Representative labs include: Atomic-Scale Materials Lab Wide Bandgap Semiconductor Lab AIMS Lab Corrosion and Advanced Materials Lab Augustyn Research Lab Learn how NC State MSE is leading the way to discover, create and enhance the world around us. Primary duties and responsibilities of this position include: Machine Learning Model Development : Design, implement, and optimize machine learning algorithms to enhance or develop new force fields for molecular simulations. Focus on leveraging modern techniques such as neural networks, Gaussian processes, and transfer learning to improve predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. Data Analysis & Preprocessing : Gather and preprocess large-scale simulation and experimental data. Identify key features, perform dimensionality reduction, and ensure the data is properly formatted for training machine learning models. Simulation & Benchmarking : Conduct molecular dynamics and quantum mechanical simulations to generate training and validation datasets. Benchmark newly developed models against existing force fields and experimental results to assess performance and reliability. Collaboration & Publication : Work closely with interdisciplinary teams of computational chemists, materials scientists, and biophysicists to apply machine learning models to a variety of systems. Publish results in high-impact journals and present findings at relevant conferences. Software Development & Documentation : Contribute to the development of open-source software tools and frameworks for machine learning-based force field modeling. Ensure thorough documentation and reproducibility of all work. Mentorship : Mentor graduate students and junior researchers in computational techniques, machine learning methodologies, and scientific writing.

title: Ergonomist or Senior Ergonomist
department: 140604 - Fitts Department of Industrial & Systems Engineering - Ergonomics Center
description: We are seeking an experienced ergonomics professional to join our team and contribute to the Center’s work supporting healthier, safer, and more productive workplaces across North Carolina and beyond. Based on your qualifications and experience, you will be hired either as an Ergonomist or Senior Ergonomist. The role offers the opportunity to provide industry consultation, deliver training, collaborate with professionals and researchers, and contribute to applied research through NC State University’s state-of-the-art Ergonomics Laboratories. As an Ergonomist , you will apply your technical knowledge to help employers and employees address ergonomics challenges across a variety of business and industry environments. You will lead consulting projects, deliver training, develop client relationships, support students, and contribute to applied research through NC State University’s state-of-the-art Ergonomics Laboratories. This is an opportunity to grow your expertise while working alongside experienced professionals and industry partners across North Carolina and the United States. In this role, you will: Provide ergonomics consultation to employers and employees across varied business and industry environments. Serve as project lead for ergonomics consulting engagements, coordinating internal and external resources with guidance from senior staff as needed. Deliver Center training classes aligned with your expertise and the Center’s needs. Build and expand the Center’s membership and client base through meetings, seminars, workshops, and other professional forums. Develop client proposals that define project scope, deliverables, and estimated timelines, with guidance from senior staff as needed. Create, update, and review training materials to ensure technical accuracy, consistency, and professional quality. Manage students assigned to the Ergonomics Services functional area and provide direction related to their work. Work effectively in a team-based environment to support Center priorities and initiatives. Collaborate with Center professionals, regulatory officials, researchers, and external partners to advance the Center’s mission. Contribute to the development of applied research projects conducted in NC State University’s state-of-the-art Ergonomics Laboratories. As a Senior Ergonomist , you will provide expert ergonomics consultation to employers and employees across a wide range of business and industry settings. You will lead consulting projects, develop client relationships, contribute to applied research, and help advance the Center’s ergonomics services and programs. This role offers the opportunity to apply your technical expertise while collaborating with professionals, researchers, regulatory officials, and industry partners across North Carolina and the United States. You’ll have the opportunity to work on a variety of projects, from routine maintenance and repairs to new construction, renovations, and welding projects , while helping ensure reliable utility services for research, academic, and animal hospital facilities. If you enjoy troubleshooting, hands-on work, and solving mechanical challenges that make a meaningful impact, we invite you to apply and become part of the NC State Facilities team! Test and certify backflow preventers, conduct fire hydrant flow tests, and perform inspections of wastewater collection systems, including grease traps and SSOs. Conduct annual inspections of wastewater distribution systems and report findings to the Environmental Engineer and shop supervisor. Align motors and pumps, set frames, and install related equipment such as fans, PRVs, and turbines for steam generation and control. Serve as backup ORC for wastewater collection system compliance, ensuring adherence to permit requirements. Anticipate, identify, and address customer service needs by balancing multiple priorities, ensuring repairs or solutions meet expectations, and fostering positive relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including vendors and subcontractors, while proactively developing options, implementing solutions, and verifying customer satisfaction.

You will work in a dynamic, collaborative research environment where your technical expertise and attention to detail directly contribute to ongoing scientific projects. Additionally, you will assist with laboratory management, including maintaining safety documentation and compliance, coordinating undergraduate research assistant schedules, and overseeing equipment purchasing, maintenance, and repair. Cultivate and maintain bacterial cultures and perform molecular and biochemical assays. Compile, analyze, and interpret experimental data to support research objectives. title: Director of Philanthropic Strategy & Prospect Management
description: The Director of Philanthropic Strategy & Prospect Management serves as the College of Engineering’s strategic advisor on fundraising performance, portfolio optimization, campaign readiness, and prospect strategy. This position partners closely with the Assistant Dean for Philanthropy and frontline fundraisers to maximize philanthropic results through data-informed decision making, fundraising analytics, CRM leadership, and strategic portfolio management. Rather than serving solely as a prospect manager, this role functions as a strategic partner to fundraising leadership by helping ensure gift officers are focused on the highest-impact opportunities and equipped with the information, systems, and strategy necessary to maximize fundraising success. Core Responsibilities 1. Philanthropic Strategy Provide strategic guidance that strengthens fundraising performance across the College. Key Responsibilities Serve as strategic advisor to the Assistant Dean and Executive Director on fundraising priorities and campaign readiness. Lead portfolio optimization and prospect assignment strategies. Facilitate prospect strategy meetings with frontline fundraisers. Identify opportunities, risks, and trends within all levels of the major gift fundraising pipeline – focusing on the continuum from major gift discovery to major gifts to principal giving. Develop recommendations to maximize fundraising productivity and philanthropic outcomes. Support campaign planning and principal gift pipeline development. 2. Prospect Management Lead the strategic management of prospect portfolios to maximize fundraiser effectiveness. Key Responsibilities Oversee portfolio management and assignment processes. Monitor prospect movement through the donor pipeline. Ensure portfolio health and accountability. Conduct regular portfolio reviews with gift officers. Coordinate closely with University Advancement Prospect Development on prospect management and research, working closely with analysts on research projects to fill fundraiser portfolios & gaps. Develop recommendations for prospect assignment and portfolio balancing. 3. CRM Strategy & Salesforce (Lobo) Leadership Serve as the College’s functional expert for Salesforce (Lobo), ensuring the CRM effectively supports fundraising strategy and frontline success. Key Responsibilities Serve as the College of Engineering’s primary functional lead for Salesforce (Lobo). Partner with University Advancement on CRM implementation, enhancements, testing, and user adoption. Develop best practices, workflows, and business processes within Salesforce. Train and support frontline fundraisers in the effective use of the CRM. Ensure data quality and consistency across fundraising operations. title: Financial Operations Supervisor
description: As the Financial Operations Supervisor, you will serve as a strategic financial anchor within the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS), providing direct leadership and accounting oversight for a centralized financial operations team. Reporting to the Director of Business Services, you will safeguard the integrity, accuracy, and compliance of high-risk transactions across a complex multi-funding environment—including federal (USDA NIFA, Hatch, Smith-Lever), state, and receipt-supported funds within CALS’ unique Ledger 4 structure. In this high-impact role, your expertise will directly mitigate regulatory risk, ensure audit readiness, and maintain the university's trusted financial standing. In this role, you will turn complex accounting requirements into seamless, efficient operations. By fostering a collaborative and accountable team culture, you will empower your staff to master intricate cost principles while serving as a supportive mentor who elevates their professional growth. Your direct influence will bridge the gap between central administration and non-financial department stakeholders, translating dense federal regulations into clear, actionable guidance. Ultimately, you will drive continuous improvement, building robust internal controls that allow the college’s critical research and extension programs to thrive with complete financial confidence. Key responsibilities will fall within the following functional areas: Leadership & Team Supervision Provide direct supervision, coaching, and performance management, cultivating a collaborative team culture focused on accountability, precision, and service excellence. Optimize Capacity: Assign, prioritize, and balance workloads across functional areas (AP, AR, Travel, P-Card) to maximize operational efficiency and maintain compliance standards. Design robust onboarding programs to ensure the team thoroughly understands core accounting principles, financial systems, and funding-specific requirements. Identify recurring operational bottlenecks and implement standardized workflows, proactively guiding corrective actions to improve team accuracy. Financial Oversight & Transaction Review Review and approve complex transactions, using critical evaluation to ensure accurate accounting treatment across federal, state, and receipt-supported funds. Direct staff analysis of CALS’ Ledger 4 project structures to guarantee correct funding source identification and regulatory framework application. Oversee reconciliation processes to ensure data accuracy, applying sound judgment to resolve financial discrepancies promptly. Serve as a key decision-maker and escalation point for ambiguous or high-risk financial and compliance issues, applying relevant accounting principles and policy precedents Policy, Compliance & Internal Controls Interpret and apply complex regulatory guidelines—including USDA NIFA, Hatch, Hatch Multistate, and Smith-Lever requirements—ensuring strict allowability and allocability. Oversee and strengthen internal controls, including segregation of duties and documentation standards, to ensure audit readiness and mitigate compliance risk Address identified control weaknesses, monitor audit findings, and implement long-term solutions to prevent recurrence. Stakeholder Engagement & Advisory Communicate intricate policy requirements, financial decisions, and process changes into clear, user-friendly guidance for faculty, staff, and non-financial partners. Serve as a diplomatic liaison between central university offices, CORE Support, and academic departments to streamline financial operations and resolve escalated concerns. Represent the financial operations unit in campus-wide meetings, championing collaborative solutions for system and workflow enhancements If you are a financial professional who enjoys leading a team, solving complex problems, and helping others navigate challenging financial and regulatory requirements, this role offers an opportunity to make a meaningful impact.. If you are a financial professional who takes pride in leading a team, solving complex problems, and providing thoughtful guidance, we invite you to apply.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Abolhasani Research Group in the Department of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering at North Carolina State University is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Scholar to develop artificial intelligence and machine learning methods for autonomous scientific experimentation as part of the NSF-funded SPEED Programmable Cloud Laboratory. The successful candidate will develop AI/ML methodologies that enable autonomous laboratories to learn from experimental data, select informative experiments, optimize complex chemical and materials systems, and generate transferable scientific knowledge. Research topics may include Bayesian optimization, active learning, uncertainty quantification, representation learning, multimodal scientific data, surrogate modeling, sequential decision-making, and AI-driven experimental design. A major emphasis will be translating AI/ML methodology into algorithms that operate directly with automated experimental platforms and real-world experimental data. Duties and Responsibilities include: Develop AI/ML algorithms for autonomous experimental design and optimization. Develop surrogate models and uncertainty-aware approaches for learning from sparse and heterogeneous experimental datasets. Develop chemical and materials representations suitable for closed-loop experimental optimization. Implement Bayesian optimization, active learning, and related sequential experimental-design methods. Develop methods for incorporating prior knowledge and historical experimental datasets into experimental decision-making. Integrate AI/ML algorithms with SPEED automated experimental platforms. Analyze multimodal experimental datasets and identify scientifically meaningful structure-property-processing relationships. Evaluate algorithm performance using both benchmark datasets and physical experimental campaigns. Develop reusable software modules and documented computational workflows. Collaborate closely with experimental scientists, automation engineers, and SPEED users. Prepare peer-reviewed publications, presentations, technical reports, and research proposals.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Abolhasani Research Group in the Department of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering at North Carolina State University is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Scholar to develop next-generation self-driving laboratories and autonomous experimentation technologies as part of the NSF-funded SPEED (Self-driving Platforms for Expedited Experimental co-Design) Programmable Cloud Laboratory. The successful candidate will develop and deploy closed-loop experimental platforms that integrate automated synthesis and experimentation, real-time characterization, data analysis, and AI/ML-based experiment selection. The research will focus on creating modular, reliable, and user-accessible autonomous laboratories for accelerated discovery and optimization in chemistry and materials science. Highly motivated candidates with experience in laboratory automation, autonomous experimentation, robotics, scientific instrumentation, process control, or related areas are encouraged to apply. Experience with Python-based automation and integration of laboratory hardware and analytical instruments is highly desirable. The successful candidate will work in a highly interdisciplinary environment involving chemical engineers, chemists, materials scientists, computer scientists, AI/ML researchers, and external academic and industrial partners. Duties and Responsibilities include: Design, develop, and deploy self-driving laboratory platforms for autonomous chemical and materials experimentation. Integrate synthesis, sample handling, analytical characterization, and data-processing tools into automated experimental workflows. Develop Python-based interfaces for laboratory hardware and scientific instruments. Implement closed-loop workflows connecting experimental platforms with AI/ML experiment-selection algorithms. Develop methods for automated calibration, fault detection, error recovery, and experimental quality control. Establish standardized workflows and interfaces that allow experimental platforms to be used by external SPEED users. Conduct autonomous and high-throughput experimental campaigns. Analyze experimental data and evaluate the performance and robustness of autonomous workflows. Collaborate with SPEED researchers in chemistry, materials science, AI/ML, data science, and automation. Prepare manuscripts, presentations, technical documentation, and regular project reports. Meet regularly with the PI and SPEED team to review progress, milestones, and future research plans.

title: Assistant Professor and Extension Specialist in Row Crop Entomology
description: The Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology seeks a tenure-track Assistant Professor (12-month) to provide statewide leadership in arthropod management for North Carolina row crop production, with a focus on sweetpotato, peanut, and soybean. The position is 70% Extension and 30% research , connecting applied research, grower needs, and emerging technologies to strengthen sustainable pest management across North Carolina agriculture. You’ll have the opportunity to build on your expertise in row crop entomology, integrated pest management, pest ecology, and insecticide resistance while shaping innovative approaches to pest prediction, decision support, and resistance management. Your work may draw on field experimentation, landscape-scale studies, pest monitoring, and data-driven tools, including artificial intelligence, precision agriculture, remote sensing, and drones. Through your research and Extension program, you’ll translate new knowledge into practical solutions that help growers and agricultural professionals make informed, sustainable pest management decisions. Key responsibilities fall within the following functional areas. Extension & Outreach: Shape a statewide Extension program that helps North Carolina growers address arthropod pest challenges in major row crops, including sweetpotato, peanut, and soybean. Translate research into practical recommendations that help growers, consultants, and industry stakeholders make informed pest management decisions. Connect with agricultural professionals and growers through field days, Extension programming, and innovative digital decision-support tools. Build strong partnerships with commodity groups, Extension agents, and state and federal partners to address emerging arthropod management challenges. Support the growth and development of graduate students and other trainees through mentorship, research guidance, and professional development opportunities. Strengthen agricultural workforce capacity by developing training and professional development opportunities for Extension agents, consultants, and agricultural professionals. Advance adoption of integrated pest management through innovative technologies and decision-support tools that translate research into practical solutions for North Carolina agriculture. Research & Discovery: Build an applied, externally funded research program that responds to grower needs and strengthens the impact of your Extension work. Advance understanding of pest ecology and management through field- and landscape-scale research addressing current and emerging crop protection challenges. Share new knowledge and practical solutions through peer-reviewed publications, Extension resources, and other scholarly contributions. Secure and steward extramural funding to advance applied research and strengthen the impact of Extension priorities. Mentorship, Teaching & Service: Mentor graduate students and other trainees through research guidance, professional development, and career preparation. Contribute to undergraduate and graduate instruction through teaching courses and supporting the department’s educational mission. Contribute expertise and perspective through departmental, college, university, and professional service activities. If you are a collaborative entomologist who enjoys connecting research with real-world agricultural challenges, building strong relationships with growers and partners, and developing innovative solutions for sustainable crop protection, we encourage you to apply.

title: Director of Philanthropy
description: The Director of Philanthropy is responsible for identifying, qualifying, soliciting, and stewarding major gift donors to NC State University. This position will serve as a member of the College of Agriculture and Life Sciences (CALS) Advancement team, reporting to a Senior Director of Philanthropy with an effort to maximize support to all areas of the College. As appropriate, the Director will also identify and coordinate the management of key volunteers. The Director will be expected to manage a portfolio of discovery and actively managed prospects while also collaborating with fundraising colleagues across campus. Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Major Gift Prospect Identification, Cultivation, and Solicitation Identification, qualification, cultivation and solicitation of prospects to create and grow a pipeline of major gifts ($100,000 and above) donors. Strategic development and management of a portfolio with approximately 150 prospects and donors capable of making gifts of $100,000 or more. Fundraising Strategy, Goals, and Portfolio Management Consistently meet or exceed annual goals for outreach contacts, qualifications, visits, proposals submitted, and funds raised. Creation and implementation of comprehensive strategies to leverage networks and maximize fundraising results. Volunteer, Donor, and Campus Collaboration Identification, coordination and management of key volunteers. Collaboration with colleagues to help align donors’ philanthropic interests with various priorities across campus. Coordination of stewardship efforts as needed with appropriate College Advancement and other campus colleagues.

title: Educational Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: This Educational Postdoctoral Research Scholar is designed to bridge the gap between clinical expertise and educational scholarship. By combining research training with hands-on teaching experience, the Postdoctoral Research Scholar will develop the skills necessary to become a leader in veterinary education and communication and professional pedagogy. Program Overview: Duration: 12-24 months Primary Objective: To equip DVM or PhD professionals with the methodological toolkit required to conduct high-impact research in health communication, communication and educational theory, and professionalism/professional identity. Eligibility & Qualifications : Must hold a DVM (or equivalent) or a PhD in a related field (Education, Communication, Psychology, etc.). Research & Methodological Training: The Postdoctoral Research Scholar will participate in a structured mentorship program to master mixed-methods research tailored to the veterinary healthcare and educational environment. Responsibilities include: Quantitative research methodologies, including survey design, statistical analysis of educational outcomes (such as competency-based assessments), and data-driven evaluation of communication interventions Qualitative research methods, including thematic analysis of reflective practice, conducting and coding focus groups and semi-structured interviews, and utilizing ethnographic or observational approaches Scholarly output through writing and submitting one first-author manuscript per year to a peer-reviewed journal (e.g., Journal of Veterinary Medical Education ) Teaching, Facilitation, and Curriculum: The Postdoctoral Research Scholar will be integrated into the DVM curriculum to ground ongoing research initiatives in active educational practice related to professionalism and communication training. Responsibilities Include: Communication Lab Facilitation - Leading small-group sessions using simulated clients (SCs) and providing real-time, constructive feedback to DVM students on clinical communication Guest Lecturing - Developing and delivering didactic content on topics such as conflict management, breaking bad news, or veterinary professional ethics Curriculum Development - Collaborating with faculty to refine and enhance learning modules and assessments across the professionalism curriculum

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar- Intestinal Microenvironment-Stem Cell Interactions
description: The McKinney-Aguirre Lab uses in translational large animal models to study epithelial recovery following clinically-relevant epithelial injury – with a special interest in the role of the microenvironment driving intestinal regeneration. The Lab is housed in the College of Veterinary Medicine and is part of Center for Gastrointestinal Biology and Disease. Duties and Responsibilities: The postdoctoral research fellow will participate in the management, processing, and analysis of studies employing a novel ex vivo intestinal perfusion models of intestinal injury. The fellow will also optimize new assays for evaluating intestinal response to injury and recovery including the application of ELISAs and advanced sequencing. This postdoctoral research fellow will interact regularly with scientists from various research backgrounds including experimental biologists. The successful candidate will be initiative-taking and enjoy working in a collaborative research environment. The postdoctoral research fellow will complete experiments, author primary research articles, and attend scientific meetings to present research progress.

title: Assistant Professor - Plant Pathology
description: The Department of Entomology and Plant Pathology seeks a tenure-track Assistant Professor to advance its undergraduate educational mission in plant pathology while developing a complementary research program. This is a 9-month faculty position that has split responsibilities of 60% teaching and 40% research. The role provides leadership in delivering and evolving the undergraduate plant pathology curriculum, integrating active learning, case-based instruction, emerging technologies, and innovative approaches to prepare students for careers and continued study in the discipline. The role includes approximately two to three courses annually, spanning foundational plant pathology instruction, team-taught and specialized courses, and the development of undergraduate and distance education offerings. In this role, you will help shape how plant pathology is taught, experienced, and applied across the curriculum while building a research program that complements the department’s strengths. Your scholarship may engage areas such as plant disease diagnostics and management, fungal biology, soilborne pathogens, plant disease ecology, plant–soil–microbe systems, or epidemiology. You will have opportunities to develop innovative teaching and research programs, create meaningful experiential learning experiences, and foster collaboration across disciplines while engaging students in discovery and inquiry. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas: Teaching and Mentoring: Deliver and modernize core undergraduate plant pathology curriculum, including PP 315 (Principles of Plant Pathology) and its laboratory component, through innovative approaches such as active learning, case studies, emerging technologies, and distance education. Contribute to graduate, team-taught, and specialized courses while helping shape curriculum innovation and assessment across the program. Create meaningful opportunities for students to connect classroom learning with research, discovery, and other experiential learning. Mentor undergraduate researchers, graduate students, and postdoctoral scholars in their academic and professional development. Research and Discovery: Build and sustain an active, externally visible research program that complements departmental strengths and advances knowledge in plant pathology. Develop collaborative research that engages students and connects teaching, discovery, and emerging areas such as soilborne pathogens, fungal biology, and plant–soil–microbe interactions. Pursue scholarly work, external support, and partnerships that expand the reach and impact of your research. Contribute to a culture of inquiry and discovery across the department and broader scientific community. Department Service and Professional Engagement: Contribute to department, college, and university priorities through service, faculty governance, and academic leadership. Foster interdisciplinary collaborations and professional partnerships that strengthen teaching, research, and engagement. Engage with the broader scientific community through professional leadership, manuscript and grant review, and scholarly activities. Support outreach and initiatives that enhance the visibility and impact of the department and university while fostering a collegial and productive academic environment. If you are an innovative educator, collaborative researcher, and engaged academic who is passionate about advancing plant pathology education and discovery, we encourage you to apply.

title: TRIO Chaperone
description: The Division of Academic & Student Affairs (DASA) is where students discover connections and community. It is where students live, where they gather, where they improve themselves, each other, and their university. DASA is where students seek guidance and support, both in and outside of the classroom. The Upward Bound Program is an early intervention pre-college program that helps students prepare for higher education. Upward Bound brings high school students to college campuses after school, on the weekends, and during the summer to receive instruction in mathematics, laboratory sciences, composition, literature, and foreign languages. Tutoring, counseling, mentoring, cultural enrichment, and work-study programs are additional components to the Upward Bound Program. The Upward Bound Program is looking for Chaperones that will be responsible for monitoring the transportation of students to and from program activities, provide head counts for TRIO staff, and help program staff with students during activities.

title: Painter
description: The Painter will be responsible for painting duties, which may include, but are not be limited to painting of buildings, fixtures, and equipment. The Painter will determine whether surfaces need to be sanded or patched before applying paint, and will then clean, sand, patch, prime and prepare areas to be painted. After the work of sanding, puttying or patching has been completed by self or others, the Painter will check surfaces before beginning the next phase of work. The Painter maintains a safe, clean and non-disruptive work area; sets up scaffolding or ladders; determines exact amount of paint that will be needed and how many coats of paint to apply, and works independently and/or assists other Painters as assigned. The Painter will also establish and maintain effective working relationships with a very wide range of contacts to include co-workers, contractors, other trades team members, vendors, customers/residents, and other University personnel. This position must also have the ability to set up and break down scaffolding, work from extreme heights and lift up to 30 pounds frequently and up to 60-90 pounds occasionally.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Abolhasani Research Group in the Department of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering at North Carolina State University is seeking a Postdoctoral Research Scholar in microreaction engineering and automated flow chemistry as part of the NSF-funded SPEED Programmable Cloud Laboratory. The successful candidate will develop automated continuous-flow and microfluidic experimental platforms for accelerated chemical and materials discovery. Research will combine microreaction engineering, multiphase transport, automated reaction screening, in-line/online analytical characterization, and closed-loop optimization. Applications may include homogeneous catalysis, photocatalysis, nanoparticle and semiconductor materials synthesis, and other solution-phase chemical and materials systems relevant to SPEED. Highly motivated candidates with experience in flow chemistry, microfluidics, reaction engineering, transport phenomena, catalysis, or automated chemical experimentation are encouraged to apply. Duties and Responsibilities include: Design and develop automated continuous-flow and microfluidic reactor platforms. Develop flow systems for homogeneous, gas-liquid, liquid-liquid, photochemical, and/or materials synthesis applications. Integrate pumps, valves, mass-flow controllers, temperature/pressure control, and other process equipment. Integrate flow reactors with in-line and online analytical characterization tools such as HPLC, GC, MS, UV-Vis, fluorescence, Raman, or IR spectroscopy. Develop automated reaction-screening and optimization workflows. Investigate mixing, mass transfer, heat transfer, residence-time distributions, kinetics, and other fundamental transport and reaction phenomena. Interface flow platforms with SPEED automation, data-management, and AI/ML infrastructure. Conduct high-throughput and closed-loop experimental campaigns. Analyze experimental results and develop mechanistic and data-driven understanding of chemical systems. Collaborate with chemists, materials scientists, automation engineers, and AI/ML researchers. Prepare scientific manuscripts, presentations, technical documentation, and project reports.

description: The Department of English at North Carolina State University invites applications for one full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Linguistics. title: CLAWS Lithography Engineer
description: We are seeking a highly-skilled lithography engineer to join our team and contribute to the ownership for NNF’s suite of lithography capabilities. The ideal candidate will have deep, hands-on experience in all lithographic processes; including contact lithography tools, stepper/projection lithography tools, automated wafer coat/develop stations, and e-beam/laser direct-write systems. Process Research & Development Advanced Development: Lead the design and optimization of cutting-edge photolithography processes tailored for next-generation applications, specifically targeting wide-bandgap devices for RF, power electronics, and photonics. Technical Consultation: Provide expert-level process integration support to internal and external users, translating complex device requirements into repeatable lithographic workflows. Service Excellence: Execute high-precision service work for external customers, ensuring all deliverables meet rigorous industry standards for semiconductor fabrication. Equipment Engineering & Maintenance Serve as the primary technical lead for lithography toolsets, ensuring maximum uptime and process stability through regular baseline monitoring. Maintenance & Repair: Independently perform scheduled preventative maintenance and diagnose/repair unscheduled hardware failures to minimize facility downtime. Vendor Management: Manage relationships with equipment manufacturers; coordinate complex service visits, manage service contracts, and oversee major tool overhauls. User Training & Technical Communication Develop and deliver comprehensive training programs for students and researchers, certifying users on tool operation, chemical safety, and lithographic theory. Act as the central communication hub for the lithography area, providing timely updates to management and users regarding tool status, process drifts, or facility interruptions. Facility Operations & Compliance Actively participate in facility safety audits and uphold strict cleanroom protocols to ensure a safe working environment for all personnel. Maintain meticulous records including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), maintenance logs, user databases, and training certifications. Oversee the lithography supply chain, managing the inventory of specialized chemicals, resists, and critical spare parts to ensure uninterrupted lab operations.

title: Journey Utilities Plant Operator - Nightshift
description: Behind every class, laboratory, residence hall, and campus event is a team making sure NC State has the reliable utilities it needs to operate. As a Utility Plant Operator , you’ll play a critical role in keeping the university running by operating and monitoring the central utility systems that provide electricity, steam, hot water, and chilled water across campus.
