title: Agriculture Marketing & Content Creator Internship
description: Capture,edit, prepare and upload agricultural educational content from small grains and Official Variety Trial programs to multi-media platforms. These may include NC State University web portals, social media accounts associated with the program including but not limited to facebook, X and Instagram. Content creation will be both short and long form. Short form to include images with written captions or short video clips with closed captioning. Long form will include 2 to 5 minute video content describing an agricultural concept with closed captioning. Development of written and visual program marketing materials will also be required, along with attendance at grower meetings and larger industry events to deliver those materials to stakeholders.

title: Landscape Maintenance Technician
description: Do you enjoy working outdoors and taking pride in creating beautiful, healthy landscapes? Join NC State University’s Landscape Maintenance and Operations team as a Landscape Maintenance Technician and help shape the campus environment that students, faculty, staff, and visitors experience every day. In this hands-on role, you’ll provide professional landscape care across NC State’s campus, using your knowledge of horticulture, turf management, and landscape maintenance to keep our grounds safe, attractive, and sustainable. You’ll work as part of a dedicated team that takes pride in maintaining one of the university’s most visible and important assets, its campus landscape. If you’re dependable, enjoy hands-on work, and want to see the results of your work make a difference every day, we invite you to apply and join the NC State Facilities team! Key responsibilities and duties include but are not limited to: Perform routine landscape maintenance, including mowing, edging, trimming, blowing, mulching, leaf collection, and general debris removal. Install and maintain plant materials including annuals, perennials, trees, shrubs, bulbs, and sod. Apply herbicides, pesticides, and insecticides safely and in accordance with all regulatory and product guidelines. Prune shrubs, trees, and ornamental plants to promote plant health, structure, and seasonal bloom. Monitor turf and plant health, identify pests, diseases, and soil deficiencies, and report concerns promptly. Operate and perform basic maintenance on landscape equipment such as trimmers, mowers, chainsaws, blowers, and utility vehicles. Assist with turf care through soil testing, seeding, fertilization, irrigation support, and sod installation. Collaborate with the irrigation team by monitoring system performance and assisting with repairs when needed. Maintain clean, organized, and safe worksites, vehicles, and storage areas. Respond to customer and field concerns professionally, escalating issues to Field Leads or Zone Managers when appropriate. Complete daily work logs, timesheets, and records with accuracy and attention to detail. Lift and transport materials weighing up to 60 pounds with or without reasonable accommodations and perform physically demanding outdoor tasks safely in various weather and terrain conditions. Ability to verbally communicate effectively with supervisors and the general public and understand verbal and written instructions and other communications regarding work assignments and other matters.

title: CaSA Temporary Administrative Support Associate
description: The Administrative Associate provides office support, under supervision, to the Climate and Sustainability Academy faculty and staff, focused on essential operational, logistical, and clerical support to the Academy team. The candidate will ensure compliance with university policies and procedures while providing exceptional customer service.

title: UTS - Temporary Landscape Maintenance Technician at NC State
description: Landscape & Turf Operations: Expertly operate mowers, blowers, weed eaters, hedge trimmers, chainsaws, edgers, and utility vehicles to deliver high-quality mowing, trimming, edging, and general grounds care. Plant Care & Grounds Prep: Prepare planting beds and install varied flora—including annuals, perennials, bulbs, sod, trees, and shrubs—bringing landscape designs to life under the guidance of the Field Lead. Turf Management: Assist in turf establishment and restoration through professional sod installation and seeding techniques. Equipment Care & Maintenance: Perform routine preventive maintenance on tools and machinery, ensuring all equipment remains safe, clean, and fully operational while promptly flagging repair needs. Site Sanitation & Cleanup: Maintain immaculate work sites, vehicles, and campus grounds through diligent leaf, debris, and waste removal. Safety & Incident Reporting: Champion a culture of safety by strictly following safety protocols and proactively reporting any hazards, accidents, or equipment damage. Teamwork & Campus Engagement: Collaborate effectively with crew members and represent the department with clear, courteous, and professional communication across the campus community.

title: Biotechnology Program Coordinator
description: In this role, you will play a central role in advancing the Biotechnology (BIT) Program and supporting the students, faculty, and partners who make it successful. You will serve as the program expert and a trusted advisor to students, helping them navigate their academic programs, connect with opportunities, and achieve their educational and professional goals. You will work closely with BIT leadership, faculty, university offices, students, and external sponsors to coordinate courses, monitor student progress, lead communications and events, and support program reporting. You will also lead data analysis and reporting for externally funded training programs, including NSF REU and NIH T32 grants, helping demonstrate program impact and support continuous improvement. This position offers an opportunity to take ownership of meaningful program activities, build relationships across the university and beyond, and directly shape the student experience and continued growth of a dynamic biotechnology education and training program. This role focuses specifically on BIT program operations and does not oversee ISI-wide education or partnership initiatives. Key Responsibilities: Academic Program Leadership Advise BIT undergraduate and graduate students on degree requirements, course planning, enrollment, and academic progression. Coordinate courses, instructors, classrooms, catalog updates, and graduate program activities. Maintain accurate student records and monitor enrollment, progression, and completion. Data, Reporting & Program Operations Manage program records, databases, calendars, and operational resources. Lead data analysis, longitudinal tracking, and sponsor reporting for BIT programs, including NSF REU and NIH T32 Monitor program and budget information and provide leadership with insights to support planning and decision-making. Communications, Outreach & Events Lead BIT communications, website content, marketing, and outreach to showcase program opportunities. Coordinate seminars, workshops, recruitment activities, visitors, and other program events. Manage announcements, calendars, and communication channels to keep students and stakeholders informed and engaged. Program Coordination & Support Serve as a primary resource for BIT students, faculty, staff, and partners, helping them navigate program processes and university systems. Coordinate meetings, schedules, presentations, reports, and other activities that support effective program operations. Take ownership of day-to-day program needs, solve problems, and help advance the BIT program's goals and student experience. This is a visible, multifaceted position that combines student advising, academic program management, data and reporting, communications, and event coordination . The role is well suited to a proactive, organized professional who enjoys managing varied responsibilities, solving problems independently, and serving as a trusted resource to students, faculty, leadership, and university partners. Success in this role requires strong communication and organizational skills, attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining a high level of service and accuracy.

title: Associate Vice Chancellor, Research Administration
description: The Associate Vice Chancellor, Research Administration (AVC-RA) serves as the university's senior executive leader for sponsored programs and institutional research administration, providing strategic oversight of enterprise-wide pre-award services, sponsored project administration, research contracts, research administration systems, and research administration data governance. Reporting directly to the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation, the AVC leads a high-performing leadership team that includes the Director of Institutional Research Systems & Reporting, the Director of Research Administration & Campus Liaison, and additional OSP directors. Working collaboratively with university leadership, colleges, research centers, faculty, federal sponsors, and administrative partners, the AVC ensures a coordinated, compliant, and service-oriented research administration enterprise that advances NC State's research mission while strengthening institutional stewardship and operational excellence. As the AVC RA, you will shape the future of research administration at one of the nation's leading public research universities. Your leadership will influence how investigators secure external funding, how research operations evolve to meet an increasingly complex regulatory environment, and how institutional systems, data, and policies support innovation at scale. Success in this position comes from balancing strategic vision with collaborative leadership—building trusted partnerships across the university, championing continuous improvement, and fostering an environment where faculty and research administrators have the resources, guidance, and infrastructure needed to expand NC State's research impact. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas. Strategic Leadership & Research Administration: Provide strategic leadership for the university's sponsored programs enterprise, aligning research administration priorities with institutional goals and the evolving external funding landscape. Advise the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation and university leadership on research administration strategy, sponsored programs, regulatory compliance, institutional risk, and operational effectiveness. Lead the development and implementation of university-wide policies, governance, and business practices that strengthen research administration and support faculty success. Foster a culture of collaboration, service excellence, continuous improvement, and accountability across the Office of Sponsored Programs and the broader research community. Enterprise Oversight & Risk Management: Provide executive oversight of institutional pre-award operations, research agreements, and sponsored programs administration to ensure consistent, compliant, and customer-focused service delivery. Safeguard the university's legal, financial, and operational interests through effective risk management, contract oversight, and compliance with federal, state, and sponsor requirements. Lead the university's response to significant regulatory changes, audits, investigations, and other matters impacting the research enterprise. Research Systems, Data & Operational Excellence: Provide executive sponsorship for research administration systems, institutional data governance, and modernization initiatives that enhance operational effectiveness and decision-making. Champion technology, process improvement, and analytics strategies that strengthen research administration services and support institutional growth. Ensure research administration infrastructure evolves to meet the changing needs of faculty, sponsors, and the university. University & External Engagement: Build trusted partnerships with university leadership, faculty, colleges, and research administrators to advance the institution's research mission. Represent NC State in relationships with federal agencies, industry, nonprofit organizations, and national research administration associations. Serve as the university's senior institutional representative for complex sponsor negotiations, strategic collaborations, and matters requiring executive-level consultation. If you are a collaborative and strategic leader who is passionate about advancing research, building strong institutional partnerships, and shaping the future of research administration, we encourage you to apply.

title: Associate Vice Chancellor, Research Commercialization
description: The Associate Vice Chancellor for Research Commercialization (AVC‑RC) provides executive leadership for NC State’s commercialization enterprise, spanning intellectual property management, licensing, startup formation, venture development, and investment programs. The AVC sets university‑wide commercialization strategy, ensures compliance with federal and institutional requirements, and leads programs that accelerate the translation of research into societal and economic impact. As the AVC-RC, you will have the opportunity to expand NC State’s innovation ecosystem by connecting researchers, entrepreneurs, investors, and industry partners to accelerate the journey from discovery to impact. You will lead initiatives such as the Wolfpack Investor Network (WIN), commercialization funding programs, and the NSF I-Corps Mid-Atlantic Hub, while representing NC State within regional and national innovation communities. Through your vision, partnership-building, and strategic leadership, you will help position NC State’s research enterprise for greater economic and societal impact while advancing a culture of innovation across the university. Key Responsibilities fall within the following functional areas. Strategic Leadership for Research Commercialization: Establishes and advances NC State’s research commercialization strategy, aligning innovation priorities with institutional research goals, economic development initiatives, and national R1 expectations. Sets enterprise-level priorities, performance measures, and service standards that strengthen commercialization outcomes across the university. Advises the Vice Chancellor for Research and Innovation on commercialization policy, innovation strategy, and external engagement. Intellectual Property, Licensing & Commercialization Governance: Provides executive oversight for intellectual property strategy, ensuring effective management, protection, and commercialization of university-developed innovations. Establishes policies, frameworks, and practices that support licensing, agreements, compliance, and responsible stewardship of intellectual assets. Provides university-wide leadership and guidance on intellectual property and commercialization matters. Venture Development & Innovation Funding: Leads NC State’s venture development ecosystem, expanding pathways for research discoveries to advance through startup formation, market validation, and investment opportunities. Provides strategic oversight for the Wolfpack Investor Network (WIN), commercialization funding programs, and NSF I-Corps Mid-Atlantic Hub activities. Cultivates relationships with investors, entrepreneurs, accelerators, and industry partners to strengthen commercialization opportunities. Innovation Ecosystem & Executive Leadership: Builds strategic partnerships with industry, investors, and innovation organizations to expand research impact and strengthen NC State’s role within regional and national innovation ecosystems. Provides leadership for a multidisciplinary commercialization team, fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Ensures effective governance, operational excellence, and high-quality services that advance the university’s commercialization mission. This is an opportunity for an accomplished commercialization leader to shape strategy, influence innovation at scale, and build connections that move groundbreaking research from discovery to impact. If you are ready to lead with vision and purpose, we invite you to apply.

Essential Job Duties: Support innovative research in reproductive physiology and molecular biology by providing technical expertise and laboratory support for multiple research programs. As a Research Technician, you will play an essential role in maintaining transgenic mouse colonies, conducting molecular biology experiments, and supporting faculty, students, and scientists in advancing high-quality research. This position contributes to the success of the laboratory by ensuring research activities are conducted safely, accurately, and in compliance with institutional and regulatory standards. Key Responsibilities Research & Laboratory Support Perform laboratory experiments and molecular biology procedures, including genotyping assays, to support ongoing research in reproductive physiology and molecular biology. Conduct animal-related procedures, including tail sampling and ear tagging, in accordance with established research protocols. Animal Colony Management Manage the transgenic mouse colony by coordinating breeding, weaning, tissue collection, colony maintenance, and accurate recordkeeping of pedigrees and colony health. Ensure compliance with institutional and regulatory requirements governing the care and use of research animals. Laboratory Operations & Collaboration Collaborate with faculty, graduate students, scientists, and research staff to support multiple research projects and laboratory initiatives. Maintain laboratory organization by managing research supply inventories, supporting laboratory cleanliness, and implementing laboratory safety procedures, including the proper handling and disposal of hazardous, non-hazardous, and radioactive waste in accordance with Environmental Health and Safety ( EHS ) protocols. If you are a detail-oriented research professional who enjoys working in a collaborative laboratory environment and is eager to contribute to innovative scientific research, we encourage you to apply. If you thrive in a hands-on setting, are committed to laboratory safety and quality, and enjoy learning new techniques while supporting a varied research team, we’d love to have you join us. This is a time-limited position with an expected duration of up to 3 years, depending on funding availability

Experience performing molecular biology and cell culture techniques in a research laboratory setting. Experience maintaining laboratory operations, including inventory management, laboratory safety practices, and the handling and disposal of hazardous, non-hazardous, and radioactive waste in accordance with Environmental Health and Safety ( EHS ) protocols.

title: UTS-Temporary Event Preparation Staff
description: NC State Continuing and Lifelong Education (NCSCaLE) is a division of the Provost within the Office of the Vice Provost for Continuing Education. The McKimmon Conference and Training Center (MCTC) reports to the Continuing & Professional Education Director. MCTC has 33,000 square feet of meeting space and assists with set-ups, exhibits, educational event gatherings, catering, and printing services which include shipping and receiving, and can provide 650 spaces of free parking. MCTC works with campus partners, private/corporate business industry, and local, state, and federal government. MCTC is dedicated to partnering with our global-class faculty and academic partners, as well as cultivating a culture of continuous lifelong learning by identifying and integrating best practices throughout your journey with us. MCTC can help create a meaningful experience that transforms into a lifelong experience. MCTC strives to enrich the lives of people and stay on the cutting edge of the industry. For example, the Bar Exam, Cyber Security, Engineering Career Fair, and Global Green Energy. Event Staff responsibilities span before and after an event. title: Budget Analyst
department: 200101 - Dean's Office - Poole College Of Management
description: The Budget Analyst provides professional budget and financial support to the Poole College Office of Business Services (OBS). Reporting to the Finance Officer, the position assists academic and administrative units with budget development, financial monitoring, and reporting to support effective fiscal management. As, the Budget Analyst you will analyze financial data, prepares budget reports, monitors expenditures, and advises departments on budgetary options and the financial implications of operational decisions. Additionally, you will work collaboratively with college leadership, department administrators, and central university offices to ensure compliance with university policies and funding requirements while supporting responsible stewardship of financial resources. Primary Responsibilities include but aren't limited to: Budget Development and Financial Monitoring Assist in the preparation and maintenance of annual operating, personnel, and departmental budgets. Monitor departmental budgets throughout the fiscal year and identify variances between budgeted and actual expenditures. Review expenditures to ensure compliance with university policies, funding restrictions, and budgetary provisions. Assist departments in evaluating available funding and understanding the budgetary impact of proposed expenditures. Support year-end budget reconciliation and fiscal close activities. Monitor salary funding, labor redistributions, and position funding to ensure accurate financial reporting. Financial Analysis and Reporting Compile financial data and prepare recurring and ad hoc budget and financial reports for college leadership and departmental administrators. Analyze budget activity and financial trends to support operational decision-making. Maintain financial records and reconcile budget information using university financial systems. Assist with financial reporting for operating, trust, grant, and other funding sources as assigned. Provide supporting documentation and analysis for budget requests and financial reviews. Budget Consultation and Customer Service Advise department administrators and staff regarding budget availability, funding options, and budgetary implications of financial transactions. Respond to budget and financial inquiries from faculty, staff, and administrators. Interpret university financial policies and procedures related to budget administration. Build collaborative relationships with academic and administrative units to support effective financial management. Provide guidance on budget processes and financial reporting requirements. Systems, Processes, and Continuous Improvement Assist in developing and maintaining budget tracking tools, spreadsheets, and standard financial reports. Identify opportunities to improve budget processes and reporting efficiency. Support implementation of process improvements and updates to financial systems. Maintain accurate financial documentation and records. If you are a detail-oriented financial professional who enjoys turning data into meaningful insights, solving problems, and partnering with others to support sound financial decisions, we invite you to apply.

Essential Job Duties: Join the Cotton Genetics and Breeding Lab and contribute to research that advances cotton genetics, genomics, and plant breeding. As a Research Technician, you will provide essential technical and operational support across field, greenhouse, growth chamber, laboratory, and seed-processing environments. Working alongside faculty, graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, and collaborators, you will help ensure research activities are conducted safely, accurately, and efficiently while supporting the development and evaluation of improved cotton breeding materials. Key Responsibilities Research Operations & Technical Support Support cotton genetics and breeding research by preparing field plots, greenhouse materials, and controlled-environment facilities for planting, phenotyping, harvesting, and research trials. Perform mechanical and manual planting, harvesting, ginning, acid-delinting, seed processing, and sample preparation while advancing and maintaining breeding populations through controlled crosses and self-pollination activities. Collect, measure, and record phenotypic and experimental data from field, greenhouse, growth chamber, and laboratory studies to support ongoing research projects. Data Management & Research Compliance Maintain accurate electronic records for phenotypic data, seed inventories, experimental documentation, and research activities using tools such as Excel and Google Sheets. Prepare and maintain documentation related to chemical storage, sample tracking, laboratory safety, and equipment use while ensuring compliance with institutional research and Environmental Health and Safety ( EHS ) requirements. Equipment, Facilities & Resource Management Operate, maintain, and perform basic troubleshooting of field equipment, laboratory instruments, ginning and acid-delinting machinery, irrigation tools, and state vehicles. Manage research resources by organizing seed stocks, supplies, greenhouse and field materials, and laboratory inventories to support efficient research operations. Collaboration & Field Operations Travel to research stations and off-campus facilities to assist with experimental setup, plot layout, planting, crop maintenance, data collection, and harvest activities. Coordinate daily research activities with cooperating scientists, graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, research station staff, collaborators, and visiting scientists to support timely project completion and effective program operations.
Other Responsibilities: Conduct ginning and acid-delinting of seed cotton; catalog, store, and prepare seed samples for field, greenhouse, and growth chamber planting. Travel to research stations and off-campus facilities to support field and nursery operations, including experimental design, plot layout, field marking, and planting. Perform mechanical and manual planting, harvesting, and seed processing of cotton in field plots, greenhouses, and controlled environments. Coordinate planting, breeding, harvesting, and seed processing activities with students, postdoctoral researchers, collaborators, and research station personnel. Prepare and maintain field plots and greenhouse materials, including envelopes, stakes, pots, growth media, reagents, and chemical solutions required for experiments. Conduct cotton breeding activities, including making crosses, selfing flowers, phenotyping plants and plots, and preparing samples for analysis. Collect, observe, measure, and record phenotypic and experimental data from field, greenhouse, growth chamber, and laboratory settings. Develop, maintain, catalog, and share digital records (e.g., Excel or Google Sheets) for phenotypic data, seed inventories, supplies, and equipment. Operate, maintain, and perform basic troubleshooting of field equipment, ginning and acid-delinting machinery, laboratory tools, and state vehicles. Prepare and maintain documentation related to chemical storage, sample tracking, laboratory safety, and equipment use. Ensure compliance with environmental health and safety regulations and institutional research compliance guidelines across all facilities. Manage program resources, including seed stocks, supplies, tools, equipment, greenhouse and field materials, and vehicles, following established protocols. Assist and work collaboratively with students, postdocs, visiting scientists, collaborators, and stakeholders to support research activities and compliance at work sites.
Minimum Experience/Education: Demonstrated possession of the competencies necessary to perform the work.
Preferred Qualifications: Previous experience performing cotton or other plant breeding or biology activities, including controlled crosses, selfing, phenotyping, planting, harvesting, and maintaining plant populations. Experience operating and performing routine maintenance or troubleshooting of agricultural, field, greenhouse, laboratory, ginning, or seed-processing equipment. Experience collecting, organizing, and managing research data and records using Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, or similar electronic data systems. Experience handling and documenting seed/plant samples, chemical materials, biological materials, laboratory supplies, and research equipment in accordance with established safety and compliance procedures. Experience coordinating research activities and priorities while working collaboratively with graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, research station personnel, visiting scientists, and other research team members.

description: The Department of Crop and Soil Sciences encompasses varied disciplines in research, extension, and teaching. The department’s mission is to develop future leaders in crop, soil and environmental sciences, improve crop plants and products, devise effective and sustainable crop production systems, devise effective and sustainable soil management techniques in both agriculture and urban settings; and disseminate crop, soil, and environmental science, knowledge for the benefit of producers of food, feed, turf, biofuels and fiber in North Carolina. Duties and Responsibilities: The primary responsibilities of this position are to conduct, perform, and execute cotton genetics and breeding research focused on genomic selection (GS), nested association mapping (NAM), and genome-wide association studies (GWAS) for important agronomic traits in tetraploid cotton. The candidate is expected to perform cotton genetics and breeding research in the field, greenhouse, and lab-based settings; develop and evaluate genetic, genomic resources, and analysis of genotypic data (GBS, resequencing, array-based and targeted genotyping panel SNPs) and phenotypic data, and use a varied array of statistical, genetics, and bioinformatics tools and methods. This position requires the candidate to summarize results, present them as technical reports and presentations at the meetings, and communicate through peer-reviewed publications. The candidate will have the opportunity to participate and cooperatively work with other lab members in the ongoing trait mapping and breeding projects towards dissecting the genetic architecture of agronomic traits and improving cotton productivity through advanced breeding tools. Further, the candidate is expected to mentor and supervise the students in the cotton program. This position is initially for one year but can be extended based on satisfactory research progress and availability of funds.

description: Help deliver high-quality diagnostic care to the NC State community by providing professional radiology services in a patient-centered clinical environment. As a Radiology Technician at Campus Health, you will produce high-quality diagnostic images using modern radiology equipment and cloud-based software while supporting providers with timely, accurate imaging that contributes to exceptional patient care. This role combines technical expertise, patient interaction, and a commitment to safety to ensure efficient clinical operations and positive patient experiences. title: Sterile Processing Assistant
description: The primary purpose of this position is to support the NC State Veterinary Hospitals by providing sterile processing services for surgical instrumentation and equipment to ensure safe, efficient, and uninterrupted patient care. This position is responsible for the decontamination, inspection, assembly, sterilization, inventory management, and distribution of surgical instruments and supplies while maintaining compliance with hospital policies and regulatory guidelines. The role also serves as a key support resource for clinical teams by delivering exceptional customer service and helping ensure the operational readiness of surgical services throughout the Veterinary Hospital. Sterile Processing & Instrument Reprocessing: Provide sterile processing support for the hospitals through the decontamination, inspection, assembly, sterilization, and distribution of surgical instrumentation and equipment in accordance with hospital and regulatory guidelines. Customer Service & Clinical Support: Deliver exceptional customer service to clinical teams by responding to questions regarding surgical packs, instrumentation availability, equipment operation, and procedural supply needs. Operating Room Coordination: Collaborate closely with Operating Room staff to support surgical scheduling, room turnover, and rapid instrument turnaround to ensure equipment and instrumentation needs are consistently met for procedures. Inventory & Systems Management: Maintain and manage surgical instrumentation, implant inventory, and component lists within ISIP Surgical to ensure accuracy, availability, and operational efficiency. Department Operations & Purchasing: Support departmental operations through coordination of equipment and instrumentation rentals, billing activities, and purchasing of implants and sterile processing supplies to maintain uninterrupted workflow and high-quality service. Professional Standards & Operations Safety & Compliance: Maintain a clean, safe, and functional workspace in accordance with OSHA, EHS, radiation safety, hospital infectious disease policies, and sterile processing standards. Team Collaboration & Communication: Participate actively in problem-solving and team advancement while working independently with sound judgment and seeking assistance when appropriate. Operational Agility & Physical Demands: Demonstrate the ability to lift up to 50 pounds with or without reasonable accommodations, work safely around potential hazards including zoonotic diseases, chemicals, and gases, and extend work hours as needed to support patient care and hospital operations.

title: Senior Lab Manager
description: The Senior Lab Manager provides strategic and operational leadership across Zeis Textile Extension’s pilot-scale textile manufacturing, testing and prototyping laboratories. This role oversees laboratory managers and supports the continued growth, modernization, and utilization of ZTE’s facilities to serve industry, research, workforce development and innovation needs. Working closely with the Zeis Director, Wilson faculty and staff as well as industry partners, the Senior Lab Manager helps position ZTE as a nationally recognized resource for applied textile innovation, technical problem solving, pilot-scale manufacturing, and workforce training. The role is responsible for advancing operational excellence, equipment strategy, laboratory safety, client engagement and business development across the organization’s technical service portfolio. Key responsibilities include: Leadership and Personnel Management Supervise all laboratory managers within ZTE (knitting lab, weaving lab, physical testing lab, dying and finishing lab, and testing and fabrication services, prototyping lab). Lead, coach, and develop the site leadership team, building a culture of accountability, responsiveness, collaboration and continuous improvement. Foster a collaborative and service-oriented culture that supports technical excellence, workforce development, and continuous learning. Manage, develop, and provide training for employees. Determine and manage staff assignments, and provide leadership and daily direction of other laboratory personnel. Represent the facility to employees, customers, partners and executives. Operations and Process Excellence Lead ZTE technical operations, including production, maintenance, safety, production quality, delivery and financial performance. Champion a Safety-First culture and ensure all labs maintain a clean and safe work environment. Update the laboratory safety plan with Environmental Health & Safety (EH&S). Serve on the Wilson College Safety Committee. Monitor and improve operational performance across laboratory utilization, project execution timelines, quality, customer responsiveness, and resource allocation. Drive operational excellence by optimizing staffing, scheduling, capacity and workflow to support production goals. Collaborate with teams to implement scalable processes and improve production flow, applying Lean, Kaizen, 5S and visual management to eliminate bottlenecks and raise operational efficiency. Business Development and Client Engagement Identify opportunities to expand technical services, pilot manufacturing capabilities and industry engagement activities. Collaborate with the Zeis Director to grow external funding, technical service revenue and strategic partnerships. Serve as the primary industry liaison for priority projects. Manage multiple laboratory resources and conduct multiple Fabrication Service Agreement (FSA) projects simultaneously, including establishing priorities in the use of laboratory resources. Prepare FSA estimates, write FSAs, coordinate and oversee work associated with the FSAs, and invoice for work performed through the business office in partnership with lab managers. Technical Expertise and Asset Management Oversee the proper and safe use of laboratory equipment and manage preventive equipment maintenance and repairs. Lead acquisitions of new equipment to modernize the laboratory and expand capabilities, soliciting quotes for new and used machinery. Keep up to date on the latest technology in the field through a strong network of machinery manufacturing contacts and by attending trade shows. Manage inventory control. Strategy and Partnership Partner with the Zeis Director and the Assistant Dean of Finance and Operations to develop and drive business planning, ensuring continuous evolution to meet customer needs. Translate the business plan into measurable KPIs and manage actions to achieve overall budget and margin targets with each associated entity ZTE. Ensure lab readiness for new equipment, technologies and capabilities through strong cross-functional alignment and disciplined change management. Collaborate with the Zeis Director, academic departments heads and college faculty to provide appropriate support for academic classes

title: House Director
description: The Division of Academic & Student Affairs (DASA) is where students discover connections and community. It is where students live, where they gather, where they improve themselves, each other, and their university. DASA is where students seek guidance and support, both in and outside of the classroom. The Division of Academic and Student Affairs is the place to work for values-driven faculty and staff who are passionate about promoting the success of the whole student. The Department of Fraternity and Sorority Life advises recognized fraternities and sororities, their governing councils, and manages Greek Village housing. The Department of Fraternity and Sorority Life prepares students for society through a values-based fraternal experience. Our work impacts the student experience in three ways: Chapter Services, Council and Community Development, and Living and Learning Environments. Fraternity and Sorority Life also provides several programs to enhance leadership development and to educate the Greek Community of over 2,800 students. The House Director will coordinate the student development and administrative functions of an Organization-Owned Fraternity or Sorority House and the community within. This position will be directly responsible for the following: Advising: Create a sense of community by promoting peer accountability among chapter residents. Provide training on university policies reinforcing community standards. Maintain a high level of visibility within the residential community for the purpose of serving as an on-site advisor to chapter residents, including but not limited to regular office hours, chapter programming, and chapter meals. Meet regularly with organization leadership, advisors, and House Corporation volunteers. Advise student residents on the development and implementation of programs, applicable policies and procedures, risk management, issues management, leadership development and organization management. Serve as a mediator to assist residents in addressing community conflicts when they arise. Maintain an environment conducive to student academic success and safety. Leadership: Provide leadership, administrative operations, programming, and facilities management in a residential house composed of about 40 residents with an additional 100 out of house student members. Make informed decisions based on a clear understanding of the impact and consequences involved. Create and maintaining an open community within the house. Serve as a communication link between Fraternity and Sorority Life, House Corporation, and residents. Exercise good judgment and remaining unbiased and impartial while addressing house issues. Participate in department decision-making regarding policies, procedures, programs, and facilities management. Oversee daily operations including facilities, overall resident management, occupancy management, financial budget management to ensure a positive, healthy and safe living-learning environment for our residents. Policy Enforcement: Respond appropriately to student concerns and addressing student issues. Follow all University Policies, Regulations, and Rules, as well as other University/Fraternity and Sorority Life Procedures, and Guidelines including but not limited to those pertaining to safety, civility, information security, and non-discrimination. Consulate with the Associate Director to refer cases to the Organizational Standards Board, Department of Fraternity and Sorority Life, CARES, Bias Incident Response or Behavior Assessment Teams, or the Office of Student Conduct. Crisis Management and On-Call Responsibilities: Make appropriate referrals to University support services ie, Student Health, Counseling Services, Behavior Assessment Team, and/or Student Ombuds. Respond to emergencies and providing leadership in crisis situations, collaborating with campus partners when appropriate. Must be onsite overnight except when prior arrangements have been made for time away. Demonstrate ability to work effectively under pressure. Practice effective communication with University administration, Organizational Leadership, and, if applicable, law enforcement or emergency personnel. Serve as a resource or referral agent for students experiencing personal concerns or crisis. Administration: Coordinate fall and spring student check-in and check-out system. Coordinate and direct the opening and closing of the house, as well as occupancy management of the facility through StarRez. Manage room assignment and room change process for the facility. Initiate change, developing, and implementing new ideas and concepts as appropriate. Participate in departmental and division programs, meetings, and committees as needed. Facilities: Coordinate inspections as required by the University, state, federal, or local agencies. Tour building and grounds on a regular basis to identify facility needs. Solicit building improvement ideas from staff and residents to share with appropriate organizational leadership and House Corporation. Working in conjunction with Fraternity and Sorority Life staff and Organizational Leadership to ensure the community is well maintained and a safe environment for residents. Work with vendors and maintenance workers to promote compliance with written agreements between the chapter and vendor; report issues of concern regarding outsourced services to the House Corporation. Assist the House Corporation representative in locating local vendors and contractors as needed and requested by the House Corporation. Work with organization leadership and meal plan vendor to establish menus for the chapter on a weekly and monthly basis. Consult with University Nutritionist as appropriate. Work with a meal vendor or catering service (when applicable) to promote compliance with written agreement between the organization and the service provider; report issues of concern regarding meal vendor or catering service to the House Corporation. Communicate periodic feedback regarding vendor provided services to the House Corporation Board and/or service vendor liaisons.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar - DEPP
description: We seek a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Scholar to conduct research in nematode genomics and molecular plant-nematode interactions. The position will focus on both basic and translational research aimed at understanding root-knot nematode (RKN) virulence, host adaptation, and mechanisms associated with resistance breaking in crops. The major focus of the project will be characterizing virulence-associated genes in M. enterolobii and investigating their interactions with crop hosts, including sweet potato. Additional projects will involve the integration of multi-omics datasets to better understand RKN-hosts interactions. The postdoc scholar will lead both laboratory experiments and computational analyses. The work will combine molecular biology, nematology, genomics, bioinformatics, and comparative transcriptomics. Depending on research interests and project needs, the successful candidate may also contribute to functional characterization of candidate nematode genes and host- resistant associated genes. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to work closely with collaborators at NC State University and other institutions Duties and Responsibilities: Conduct laboratory and greenhouse experiments related to plant-nematode interactions, nematode virulence, and host resistance Perform molecular biology experiments, including DNA and RNA extractions, PCR, qPCR, preparation of samples for genomics and transcriptomics analyses Conduct bioinformatics analyses using high-performance computing environments Maintain clear research records and contribute to reproducible bioinformatics workflows

title: ICU Veterinary Assistant
description: The Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Veterinary Assistant provides advanced nursing care within the 24/7 high-acuity unit of the Randall B. Terry Jr. Companion Animal Medical Center. Operating in a fast-paced teaching environment, this role manages a varied caseload of small animal and exotic patients. The position requires a high level of clinical expertise, professional communication, and the ability to coordinate care seamlessly between specialty services, clinicians, and students. Clinical Excellence & Patient Care Advanced Nursing Interventions: Perform complex medical treatments, including catheter placement (venous, arterial, and central), oxygen therapy (nasal/chest tubes), urinary management, and blood/plasma transfusions. Critical Monitoring & Diagnostics: Monitor vital signs (TPR, BP, ECG), manage ventilator support, and utilize specialized equipment such as pulse oximeters, wound vacuums, and ultrasound machines. Emergency Response: Perform CPR and provide immediate life-saving support for patients in crisis. Pharmacological Management: Calculate and administer high-risk medications, including constant rate infusions (CRI), intravenous fluids, and complex pain management protocols. Specialized Recovery: Manage post-anesthetic and post-surgical recovery for high-risk neurological, soft tissue, trauma, and extracorporeal patients. Infection Control: Maintain rigorous standards for isolation protocols, antibiotic-resistant cases, and infectious disease management. Coordination & Educational Support Clinical Communication: Coordinate patient admissions and care plans by synthesizing information from clinicians and students regarding diagnostics and treatment goals. Instruction & Mentorship: Actively teach, coach, and orient 4th-year veterinary students, interns, residents, and new staff on hospital policies and advanced patient care techniques. Data Management: Accurately record and communicate patient data, diagnostic results, and treatment histories using hospital information systems. Client Relations: Support and facilitate client visitations, maintaining professional empathy in emotionally charged or challenging situations. Professional Standards & Operations Safety & Compliance: Maintain a clean, functional workspace in accordance with OSHA, EHS, radiation safety, and hospital infectious disease policies. Team Collaboration: Participate actively in problem-solving and team advancement, working independently with sound judgment while requesting assistance when necessary. Operational Agility: Demonstrate the physical ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work around potential hazards (zoonotic diseases, chemicals, gases), and extend work hours as required by patient needs.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar- Bioelectricity Lab
description: The Department of Molecular Biomedical Sciences trains doctors of veterinary medicine, graduate students, and postdoctoral fellows interested in research-based careers focused on discovering new information about animal and human health and disease and using those findings to enhance animal and human health and well-being. The Bioelectricity Lab develops next generation technologies for the detection and treatment of diseases using electric field mediated phenomena. Duties and Responsibilities: The candidate for the Bioelectricity Postdoc Research Scholar position will lead large/small animal studies investigating the immunological effects a new pulsed electric field cancer therapy. The candidate will additionally lead with other experiments in the laboratory using in vitro models to investigate the effects of pulsed electric fields on biological tissues.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: We are a dynamic research team focused on elucidating the molecular mechanisms of plant-virus-vector interactions. Our mission is to develop new foundational knowledge of plant viruses and to translate this information into new control strategies and biotechnology tools for crop improvement. Grapevine red blotch disease has emerged as a major threat to winegrape production throughout North America in recent decades. We aim to develop tools and protocols for grapevine red blotch virus (GRBV) detection in insects and plants. We will integrate these new technologies with established methods to better understand GRBV localization in the insect vector throughout circulative transmission and make strides in understanding GRBV latency in grapevine and experimental plant hosts. The detection tools developed will also have applications for red blotch diagnostics. Duties and Responsibilities: The postdoctoral research scholar will express GRBV proteins in prokaryotic and eukaryotic (insect and plant) cells and purify proteins for antibody production. (50%) Characterize GRBV dissemination and tissue tropism in insect vectors with in situ methods. (50%) Molecular analysis of viral genomes, gene expression, and gene function. Primer design, DNA/RNA handling, protein expression, Western blotting. Develop and test standardized procedures for determining vector competence on candidate vectors.

They will run database queries and reports to support NC State's federally mandated Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) reporting to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and submit event based and periodic reporting to SEVIS as required. Under the direction of the Interim SEVIS Systems & Compliance Manager, synthesize data from multiple sources to manage the new student registration process, identify potential compliance issues for new students, and generate routine reports on expected arrivals for stakeholders. In coordination with the Interim SEVIS Systems and Compliance Manager, review and resolve student & scholar alerts in SEVIS and Sunapsis such as changes of curriculum and level, address changes, or assign to advisor for review Perform delegated SEVIS-related database maintenance and data clean-up services Run queries in SIS and Sunapsis to assist with data compliance and institutional reporting Remain current with SEVIS-related and regulatory updates pertaining to international students and scholars to ensure institutional compliance. Act as University back-up on all topics related to Sunapsis/Global Home. Other duties 10% Back up the Intake Specialist as needed during illness/vacation in assigning cases to advisors Attend and provide technical assistance to policies and procedures discussions with advisors Provide back-up support to the front desk as needed. Assist with communicating process updates and providing training to departments and other campus stakeholders. Attend conferences and give conference presentations when needed. Perform all other duties as assigned. This position is scheduled for 29 hours per week though work outside of standard hours may be required due to business needed.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor in Community Sport Development
description: The Department of Parks, Recreation and Tourism Management (PRTM) in the College of Natural Resources at North Carolina State University invites applications for an Assistant or Associate Professor with expertise in community sport development. We are seeking an innovative scholar and educator whose research explores the role of sport in strengthening communities through sustainable development, cultural engagement, health and well-being, youth development, economic impact, or related areas. In this role, you will shape the future of community sport development through impactful research, meaningful teaching, and collaboration with students, colleagues, and community partners. You'll have the opportunity to develop or expand a nationally recognized research program, mentor the next generation of sport leaders, and translate scholarship into practice through partnerships that improve communities across North Carolina and beyond. As part of NC State's land-grant mission, your work will extend beyond the classroom—creating lasting connections between the university, industry, and communities while contributing to innovative solutions with local, national, and global impact. Key responsibilities include: Develop Research by or expanding a high-impact scholarly research program that attracts external funding and contributes to the field of community sport development. Teach and Mentor undergraduate and graduate students through engaging instruction, student mentorship, and supervision of research and scholarly activities. Publish and Disseminate research through peer-reviewed publications, professional presentations, and other scholarly activities that advance knowledge and practice. Collaborate with faculty, community organizations, industry partners, and government agencies to foster interdisciplinary research and strengthen community engagement. Shape Academic Programs by contributing to curriculum development, continuous program improvement, and innovative learning opportunities across the department. Serve the University and Profession through departmental, college, and university committees, professional organizations, and public service activities that support NC State's land-grant mission. If you are an innovative scholar who thrives on collaboration, values student success, and is committed to advancing community sport development through impactful research and engagement, we encourage you to apply.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar- Theriot
department: 196001 - Department of Population Health and Pathobiology
description: The mission of the Department of Population Health and Pathobiology is to recruit, train, inspire, and graduate Doctors of Veterinary Medicine of exemplary knowledge, skill, and character. In order to maintain the intellectual and professional climate necessary to accomplish this mission, the department’s faculty will advance veterinary medical science through innovative basic and applied research, inspired mentoring of students (undergraduate, professional, residents, and graduate), excellence in clinical and diagnostic services, and innovative extension and engagement activities. North Carolina State University’s College of Veterinary Medicine (CVM) is a dynamic community whose members are dedicated to preparing veterinarians and veterinarian scientists while advancing animal and human health from the cellular level through entire ecosystems. The College has gained international recognition on the strength of its teaching, research, engagement, and patient care efforts and is ranked 3rd among the nation’s 28 colleges of veterinary medicine in the current U.S. News & World Report survey. Located on 180 acres near downtown Raleigh, the College encompasses 20 buildings on the main Centennial Biomedical Campus. Instruction is in three departments—Clinical Sciences, Molecular Biomedical Sciences, and Population Health & Pathobiology. In addition to the four-year Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree, there are programs leading to master and doctoral degrees in several areas with numerous opportunities for specialization. A postdoctoral scientist position (1+ years) is available in Prof. Casey Theriot’s group at North Carolina State University College of Veterinary Medicine (NCSU CVM). The successful applicant will characterize bacteria for their ability to alter bile acids, and compete against C. difficile for the same nutrients. The scholar will also bioengineer bacteria to manipulate bile acid and amino acid metabolism in the gastrointestinal tract. The Theriot laboratory (https://theriotlab.org) studies how the gut microbiota is able to provide colonization resistance against enteric pathogens, specifically C. difficile . They seek to define the mechanisms that provide protection by looking at the dynamics between the gut microbiota, metabolome, and host using in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo models. This will aid in the design of targeted therapeutics against C. difficile , but more importantly the design of precision probiotics to manipulate the gut microbiota. Requirements: Applicants are expected to have obtained a PhD in a field related to bioinformatics, microbiology, biochemistry, to have strong computational and communication skills, and to be interested in collaborative research. Applicants with a background in bacterial engineering, anaerobic bacterial physiology, and/or microbiology of infectious diseases are highly encouraged to apply. Experience in bioinformatics and characterizing bacteria for biotechnological applications and knowledge in gut microbiome analysis and other omics is desirable. Research efforts will contribute toward publications, presentations and other funding opportunities. The selected individual will be expected to have effective communication skills, both with the PI and students within the laboratory, and will be expected to work well independently and within a team.

NC State Extension extends research-based knowledge to all North Carolinians, helping them transform science into everyday solutions that improve their lives and grow our state. We are the model of excellence in non-formal, research-based education that advances agriculture, the environment, human health and well-being, youth and communities, while creating prosperity for all North Carolinians. Some of our benefits include: · Paid time off · Paid tuition · Health Insurance · Flexible Scheduling · Retirement Savings · Supplemental Benefits Programs · WolfPerks! You Belong Here! Primary Function of Organizational Unit North Carolina Cooperative Extension gives our residents easy access to the resources and expertise of NC State University and NC A&T State University. Through educational programs, publications, and events, Cooperative Extension field faculty deliver unbiased, research-based information to North Carolina citizens. Our mission is to partner with communities to deliver education and technology that enrich the lives, land and economy of North Carolinians. At 954 sq. miles, Columbus County is the third largest county in North Carolina and is home to over 55,000 residents. Columbus County is famous for its small towns and friendly atmosphere. To find out more about Columbus County, see https://columbusco.org/. To learn more about the NCCE Columbus County Center, go to https://columbus.ces.ncsu.edu/ Duties and Responsibilities N.C. Cooperative Extension in Columbus County is seeking to hire a Livestock Extension Agent. The agent in this position will provide leadership for the development, implementation, and evaluation of an effective educational program and informational assistance to meet the needs of the county youth and adult populations in the following area of responsibility – Livestock, to include but not limited to swine, cattle, goats, sheep, as well as forages and pasture management. The agent will be responsible for providing leadership in planning, implementing, evaluating and marketing educational programs and activities with measurable impacts in livestock production/management and forage/pasture management. Additionally, the person selected for this position will be expected to work closely with the 4-H Agent to provide leadership in planning, implementing, evaluating and marketing a youth livestock program. This position demands a responsible and self-motivated individual with outstanding relationship skills and a strong background in livestock production and 4-H livestock programming. title: EFNEP Educator, Program Assistant /Associate (Youth and Adult)
description: The Extension EFNEP Program Assistant is an employee of NC Cooperative Extension, NC State University. Under the supervision of the County Extension Director (CED) with guided assistance from the Regional Nutrition Extension Associate (RNEA), the EFNEP PA delivers nutrition and related subject matter to enrolled participants. The individual in this position will recruit and enroll adults and school-aged youth participants into the program, make regular teaching visits to enrollees either in the home or in group settings, teach basic principles of nutrition and food preparation skills, submit required program records as requested, market the program within the assigned area, recruit volunteers from within the community involving them in leadership roles, collaborate with local Cooperative Extension staff and agencies, and assist with securing program resources. The EFNEP PA receives programmatic guidance from the District EFNEP Regional Nutrition Extension Associate (RNEA) with overall supervision provided by the County Extension Director (CED). The EFNEP PA and the RNEA work with the Family and Consumer Science Agent, 4-H Agent and/or CED to meet the needs of the county. Renewal of the position is contingent on the availability of funds. Adult Expanded Food and Nutrition Education Program (EFNEP) involves the enrollment of limited resource individuals and their children who qualify for federal food assistance programs. Under the programmatic guidance of the Extension Associate, the EFNEP PA works with clients in small group settings and individually (as needed). This position is a full-time, 40 hours per week position. This position will serve 75% 4-H Youth and 25% Adult Programming. Youth Programing will take place at school settings and at informal educational settings with 4-H and community partner organizations. Although youth participants may range from 5 to 18 years old, they are typically 2nd to 6th grade students.

About the Department: The Sandhills Research Station is one of eighteen agricultural research centers in the State of North Carolina. North Carolina State University owns the Sandhills Research Station with operational management through the Division of Research Stations and the North Carolina Agricultural Research Service. North Carolina State University and the Division of Research Stations establish the general operating procedures. The regional distribution of research stations throughout North Carolina is designed to address agricultural questions as they pertain to specific geographic areas. The Sandhills Research Station is a vital link in the chain of research stations in addressing agricultural concerns of the Sandhills area of North Carolina. The primary purpose of the Research Station is to provide land, personnel, expertise, facilities and equipment to research scientists conducting agricultural research projects which address specific questions concerning crop production in North Carolina. The Sandhills Research Station encompasses 570 acres and is an important training facility for crop producers, graduate students, high school students and the general public. Current research projects involve the production or improvement of soybeans, cotton, turfgrass, peaches, blueberries, blackberries, landscape ornamentals, and sweet potatoes.

description: We are a dynamic research team focused on elucidating the molecular mechanisms of plant-virus-vector interactions. Our mission is to develop new foundational knowledge of plant viruses and to translate this information into new control strategies and biotechnology tools for crop improvement. The scientist will be part of a collaborative team using plant rhabdoviruses for crop improvement. title: Research Scholar
description: The School Planning and Transportation group supports Local Education Authorities (LEAs) in comprehensive planning for schools and communities (SchoolCAMP), enrollment, facilities and boundary planning (OREd) and school transportation (Bike/Ped, Transit, School Bus). This position combines demographics, transportation, land use, and community needs utilizing current best practices in K12 Operations and quality Applied Research. title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar - PHHI
description: The Postdoctoral Scholar will assist the Principal Investigator (Dr. Andrew Neilson) in the Plants for Human Health Institute by leading and conducting independent research (80%), along with some general laboratory management (10%), and some mentoring of graduate students as appropriate (10%). Duties and Responsibilities: The primary duties of this position will include conducting advanced independent and/or directed research with a focus on the interaction between plant-derived phytochemicals, the human gut microbiome and nutrition/health outcomes. Major research thrusts in the Neilson lab currently involve 1) utilizing phytochemicals to modulate production of gut microbiome-derived uremic toxins such as trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), phenylacetic acid, phenylacetylglutamine, and imidazole propionate, and 2) understanding individual genetic differences predict phytochemical bioavailability, metabolism, and efficacy for disease prevention, among others. The majority of the work will be performed using 4 key research tools: 1) anaerobic fecal fermentations, 2) rodent models of nutrition/disease (including models of genetic variety), 3) mammalian and/or bacterial cell culture, and 4) instrumental analysis (particularly LC-MS/MS). This will include study design, collection and analysis of data, ensuring quality of data, basic statistics analysis, generating tables and figures for presentation (in manuscripts and conference presentations) as it relates to impacts on human health, participation in preparation and submission manuscripts, reports and grant proposals. Other general duties will include general lab and instrument maintenance and management as well as other duties as assigned. In addition to performing assigned experiments, the successful candidate will contribute to the intellectual direction of the lab by identifying important research questions, formulating hypotheses and designing experiments (including adoption of new techniques) to test those hypotheses. The candidate must have a demonstrated ability to work independently and creatively. She/He will provide support to peers, collaborative partners, and students, have good communication skills, and be able to articulate clearly the scientific and technical needs in the field, set clear goals, and work within an interdisciplinary setting. The successful candidate will be expected to develop and submit (with guidance from the Principal Investigator) postdoctoral fellowship applications and other grant applications to sponsors such as USDA, NIH, etc. The successful candidate is expected to routinely publish their research in relevant peer-reviewed academic journals. This position is located in Kannapolis, NC.

Author, review, and present high-impact manuscripts and technical papers for publication in top-tier peer-reviewed journals and international academic conferences. Partner with internal and external multidisciplinary teams to transition novel photonic concepts into validated hardware prototypes and system demonstrations.

title: Postdoc Research Scholar- Nascone-Yoder Lab
description: The Postdoctoral Researcher will conduct independent research focusing on the development of anatomical left-right asymmetry. Specifically, the incumbent will investigate the cellular and molecular mechanisms of left-right asymmetric organ morphogenesis within the developing digestive tract. Research methodologies will utilize advanced gene misexpression strategies (CRISPR/morpholino oligonucleotides), transcriptomics (bulk and/or spatial), 3D imaging modalities (nano-CT), and/or computational modeling (CompuCell3D). Core Competencies & Responsibilities Project Leadership: Demonstrated ability to independently lead, manage, and execute complex research projects while working effectively within an interdisciplinary team environment. Communication & Collaboration: Excellent oral and written communication skills, with a proven track record of successful scientific collaboration. Technical Expertise & Preferred Qualifications Advanced Research Methodologies: Demonstrated expertise in microscopy, image processing/analysis, gene editing, immunostaining, and/or molecular biology. Scholarly Output: A strong record of publication in peer-reviewed scientific journals, reflecting the ability to synthesize and disseminate research findings. Research Design and Execution Independent Experimentation: Independently design and conduct research experiments to investigate developmental processes. Advanced Methodologies: Utilize advanced technical methodologies, including gene expression analysis, cell lineage tracing, and manipulation of genetic pathways. Model Organism Care: Manage, work with, and care for living model organisms (e.g., mouse, Xenopus ) as required by research protocols. Data Analysis and Interpretation Technical Analytics: Analyze complex experimental data using advanced techniques such as microscopy imaging and bioinformatics. Data Visualization: Generate high-quality figures, charts, and diagrams to clearly present research data. Results Interpretation: Interpret experimental results to draw meaningful, data-driven conclusions about the mechanisms of development. Publication and Dissemination Manuscript Production: Prepare and draft scientific manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals, managing data presentation, discussion text, and subsequent revisions. Research Presentation: Disseminate research findings at national and international conferences, as well as within internal collaborative networks. Collaboration Intra-Lab Support: Collaborate with laboratory colleagues and contribute to ongoing projects involving alternative organ systems. Cross-Disciplinary Partnership: Partner with researchers across scientific disciplines to exchange expertise and advance shared research aims.

description: Join NC State Facilities as an Electronics Specialist and play a critical role in supporting the systems that keep our campus running. This position provides advanced technical expertise in the maintenance, troubleshooting, calibration, and repair of sophisticated electronic and digital control systems within our thermal plant operations. As an Electronics Specialist, you will work with the technology and infrastructure that support high-pressure boilers, chillers, cogeneration systems, and other critical utility equipment . Your work will directly contribute to the safe, reliable, and efficient delivery of essential services across campus. This role offers the opportunity to solve complex technical challenges, work with cutting-edge control systems, and collaborate with a highly skilled team dedicated to operational excellence. We are seeking a motivated professional who enjoys hands-on technical work, thrives in a problem-solving environment, and takes pride in maintaining mission-critical systems. The ideal candidate will possess strong troubleshooting abilities, attention to detail, and a commitment to safety and reliability. This is an exciting opportunity to build your career while supporting one of the largest and most dynamic university campuses in the country. If you are ready to apply your technical expertise, contribute to essential campus operations, and join a team that values innovation and continuous improvement, we encourage you to apply today. Key responsibilities and duties include, but are not limited to: Independently troubleshoot mechanical, electromechanical, electronic, and digital control systems for thermal plant equipment, including chillers, boilers, fuel systems, and cooling towers. Identify and resolve unusual or complex plant control issues that require in-depth analysis and the application of journey-level trade knowledge. Diagnose and repair network communication issues and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems to ensure seamless data flow and equipment monitoring. Troubleshoot non-standard electronic devices (controllers, transmitters, sensors, actuators) even in instances where documentation is incomplete or unavailable. Independently perform recurring PM on control systems and field devices to prevent equipment downtime and ensure peak efficiency. Execute service and maintenance on thermal plant digital control systems, managing both physical hardware and the underlying software interfaces. Perform non-recurring tasks, including the installation of meters and specialized control devices, utilizing advanced electronic principles. Calibrate, test, and maintain a variety of field devices to ensure accurate sensing and mechanical response within the utility plant. Ensure all installations and repairs meet or exceed State and University codes, as well as Facilities Division standards. Conduct thorough inspections prior to, during, and upon completion of work to verify the proper maintenance of utility systems. Maintain strict safety standards while working on high-performance utility systems to protect personnel and university assets. Gather and interpret system information to understand the nature of complex malfunctions and determine the most efficient course of action. Evaluate multiple repair options, considering potential outcomes and operational impacts, before implementing solutions. Communicate clearly and effectively with supervisors, team members, and the general public to facilitate smooth daily operations. Comprehend and execute verbal and written instructions regarding work assignments, safety protocols, and general workplace matters. description: The Horticultural Science Summer Institute Counselors are the primary caregivers for the program campers. Be alert to campers and staff needs and assist them with personal and/or health problems, and discuss with program coordinator when appropriate.
