title: CARES Coordinator with Outreach Emphasis
description: The CARES Coordinator in NC State University’s Prevention Services (Division of Academic and Student Affairs) is responsible for conducting behaviorally and clinically informed assessments with students to identify and address barriers to personal and academic success, including safety threats. The role provides referrals, coordinates interventions, collaborates with campus partners, and delivers outreach, training, and prevention programming. Coordinators may also hold an area(s) of emphasis based on operational needs. Student Assessment and Case Management Conduct behaviorally and clinically informed one-on-one assessments with students to identify and mitigate barriers to personal and academic success, including threat assessment for self or others. Provide timely and appropriate referrals to university and off-campus resources; coordinate intervention plans to minimize or resolve student concerns. Monitor and track student progress to ensure compliance with recommendations, ongoing assessment, and identification of emerging concerns. Create and manage re-entry strategies for students returning after psychological hospitalization. Serve on key cross-campus support and assessment teams: NC State CARES Team – assess and support students of concern. Behavioral Assessment Team (BAT) – assist with threat assessments when appropriate. Sexual Assault Response Team (SART) – participate as needed. Participate in after-hours postvention and case review rotation; occasional evening or weekend outreach responsibilities. Maintain service schedule of approximately 50% direct student/faculty/staff support and 50% administrative responsibilities. Data Management, Documentation & Assessment Accurately document all correspondence, notes, and action items in the Maxient database. Assist in managing and maintaining ethically sound data collection and analysis related to students of concern. Use data to support continuous improvement and best-practice development in case management and prevention services. Outreach, Prevention Education & Training Provide comprehensive outreach and consultation to faculty, staff, students, and families through presentations, workshops, and creative multi-media efforts. Collaborate with campus partners to ensure consistent, integrated messaging around prevention, well-being, and student support. Complete required training (e.g., QPR Suicide Prevention) and deliver training programs to students, faculty, and staff. Support university-wide prevention initiatives addressing topics such as suicide prevention, case management, and well-being. Program Coordination, Areas of Emphasis & Campus Partnerships Coordinators may hold responsibility for one or more Areas of Emphasis based on unit needs. Coordinate resources, programming, and direct services within the assigned area(s) of emphasis (e.g., suicide prevention, alcohol and other drugs/recovery, peer education, training, assessment). Serve as the primary consultant for campus partners related to the assigned area(s). Maintain up-to-date content and resources for the designated emphasis area(s). Represent Prevention Services in relevant committees, meetings, or initiatives. Professional Collaboration, Supervision & Other Duties Engage with interns, graduate assistants, and temporary employees; may supervise or mentor these roles. Contribute to overall Prevention Services operations and team initiatives. Complete other duties as assigned within the scope of a prevention specialist and departmental needs.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: The Department of Forestry and Environmental Resources has a wide variety of strengths in forestry and natural resources management, policy and economics, environmental science and technology, wildlife and conservation biology, tree improvement, silviculture, forest biotechnology, and international forestry. The Department has over 90 full time faculty and staff, and more than 750 undergraduate and 150 graduate students. Faculty, staff, and students work together with business, industry, government, community groups, and non-government organizations to address a wide range of challenges facing our state and the world. Partnerships include Camcore, the Forest Productivity Cooperative (FPC), the Southern Forest Resource Assessment Consortium (SOFAC), and the Tree Improvement Program (TIP).These partnerships facilitate research and discovery, teaching and learning, and outreach and service. Additional information about the department can be found at http://cnr.ncsu.edu/fer . The College of Natural Resources (CNR) at North Carolina State University is a world leader in the sustainable use of natural resources. The college’s comprehensive approach to teaching, research, and service encompass the many and varied ways in which people’s physical, economic, and social needs are met through the wise use of natural resources. Primary purpose of the position: Designing and conducting experiments in the areas of Innovations in delivery of CRISPR components to tree cells, Innovations in regeneration technologies in tree tissue culture, Molecular analysis of edited samples, Phenotypic characterization of trees with improved traits, including productivity, adaptation, wood quality, and resilience. Conducting independent and collaborative studies, analyze and interpret data, and communicate results through reports, presentations, and publications in peer-reviewed scientific journals. Exploring fundamental questions in genome editing while contributing to practical outcomes—developing technologies that accelerate the improvement of traits of interest in forest trees. This role is ideally suited for curious and motivated scientists with experience in plant research, who thrive on problem-solving, experimentation, and contributing to both basic and applied advances in plant biotechnology.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: We are seeking a researcher to participate in an initiative in human-centered AI for public microtransit systems. The successful candidate will design and implement AI-driven strategies that enhance system performance by promoting prosocial rider behaviors—such as flexible departure timing to benefit vulnerable users—and by personalizing rider interactions to sustain long-term engagement. This role involves modeling individual travel preferences and adaptive time windows, analyzing the effectiveness of message themes (e.g., pro-sociality vs. system efficiency), and deploying tailored persuasive techniques optimized for varied user profiles. Responsibilities will include: Interdisciplinary collaboration: Work closely with faculty from computer science, transportation engineering, operations research, and psychology on integrative research related to microtransit systems. AI algorithms and engineering: Design and implement advanced methods to learn rider preferences and effective persuasive approaches to promote cooperation. Build robust pipelines for simulation and integration with a user interface and other app components. User studies: Develop an experimental platform and run user studies to test developed algorithms and analyze impacts. Conference presentations and journal publications : Lead or contribute to conference and journal papers for top venues.

As an Electronics Specialist, you will perform tasks such as: Conducting routine and preventive maintenance inspections on: Life Safety Systems Fire Detection and Suppression Systems Security Systems CCTV (Closed-Circuit Television) Systems Equipment Monitoring Systems Other miscellaneous electronic systems and subsystems Installing, maintaining, and modifying fire detection and suppression systems, Life Safety equipment, card access systems, CCTV, and equipment monitoring tools. title: CLAWS III-N Power Integration Engineer
description: We are seeking a highly skilled Wide-Bandgap Power Device Engineer to join our team and contribute to the development of next-generation power semiconductor devices. The ideal candidate will have expertise in semiconductor process integration, power device design (diodes, FETs, etc.), electrical characterization, and device simulation to drive innovation in high-efficiency, high-performance wide-bandgap power solutions. Key Responsibilities Power Device Design & Development (30%) Design and optimize GaN power devices (HEMTs, Diodes, lateral/vertical FETs) for high-voltage and high-frequency applications. Utilize TCAD simulation (e.g., Synopsys, Silvaco, etc.) for process and device modeling, electrical characteristics prediction, and performance enhancement. Develop and refine device layouts for wafer fabrication, ensuring manufacturability and reliability. Process Integration & Fabrication (30%) Work to define and optimize GaN-on GaN, GaN-on-Si, GaN-on-SiC, and other heteroepitaxial structures for power applications. Lead the wafer process flow development, including epi structures, etching, metallization, and passivation steps. Troubleshoot process integration challenges related to defectivity, yield, and reliability. Electrical Characterization & Reliability Testing (20%) Define and execute device characterization plans (IV, CV, breakdown, leakage, switching performance). Analyze reliability metrics such as TDDB, HTRB, HTOL, and step-stress testing to assess long-term device stability. Interface with packaging and application engineers to optimize thermal management and electrical performance in real-world applications. Cross-functional Collaboration (20%) Work with process engineers and R&D partners to drive technology improvements. Collaborate with circuit designers, applications engineers, and product development teams to translate device-level improvements into system-level advantages. Stay up to date with emerging GaN technology trends, competitive landscape, and industry benchmarks.

title: Assistant/Associate/Full Clinical or Tenure Track Professor of Radiation Oncology
description: The individual will be able to choose between either a TENURE TRACK or PROFESSIONAL/CLINICAL TRACK position, provided they meet the qualifications, with rank and tenure status determined based on experience level. Both positions come with similar responsibilities: the incumbent will oversee radiation oncology clinical case management, provide high quality clinical and pre-clinical teaching, demonstrate research productivity through the procurement of external grant funding and the publication of peer-reviewed scientific papers, and participate in college and departmental committees. The difference is that faculty in professional/clinical track positions spend a majority of their time in the clinic (34 weeks), with a small proportion of their time (5-10%) dedicated to research. By contrast, faculty in tenure track positions are expected to develop and/or run an independent research program, with a focus in clinical, translational, and/or basic research in the cancer and/or radiation-related sciences. Many collaborative research opportunities exist within the NC State University Comparative Medicine Institute, as well as with neighboring institutions including UNC Chapel Hill, Duke University, and Wake Forest University. Often, our faculty become eligible for associate membership in these NCI-designated Comprehensive Cancer Centers. Notably, the NC State Radiation Oncology team actively participates in a variety of clinical trials, and we are fortunate in that clinical research efforts are well-supported by our Clinical Studies Core, which provides assistance in study design, coordination and implementation. In addition to clinical service and research, the successful candidate will be responsible for participation in professional outreach, committee service, teaching, and curriculum development. Faculty radiation oncologists at NC State participate in resident training, and they assist in teaching general oncology in the professional DVM curriculum, host an elective course in feline oncology, and support elective clinical rotations in radiation oncology for 4th year veterinary students. There are additional opportunities for mentoring graduate students.

title: Postdoctoral Research Scholar
description: NC State Department of Civil, Construction, and Environmental Engineering (CCEE), seeks a postdoctoral researcher in the transportation area related to human-Autonomous Vehicle (AV) interactions. For questions regarding the position please contact Professor Danjue Chen (dchen33@ncsu.edu). The postdoc training and mentoring will be in: 1. Helping to advance research in human-automation interaction. 2. Helping to establish in the professional community. 3. Helping to get familiar with writing proposals. 4. Helping & supervising in graduate & undergraduate students advising. The research project will study how human users (as a driver or AV user) interact with AVs on the road to investigate a set of problems like (1) how human drivers decide whether to cooperate with AVs (e.g., to yield or not) and (2) how AV users decide whether to accept the cooperation from the algorithmic design? We are interested in learning the influential factors in such human-AV interactions, the decision-making process from the cognitive and/or behavioral economics perspective, and how to develop strategies to promote human-AV cooperation (e.g., via improved communication design, or nudging). We expect to utilize a simulator network consisting of multiple connected driving simulators (i.e., with embedded connectivity). Responsibilities include (1) designing and implementing research experiments, (2) conducting data analysis, and (3) paper writing.

Strong understanding of Linux command-line tools as well as programming and version control concepts; in particular shell script, python and git. Ability to support the use of conda, PIP , and Jupyter notebooks. Detailed understanding of remote access, clustering, backup, auditing, and virtualization technologies within a Linux environment. title: Area Specialized Extension Agent-(MIMB) More in My Basket Regional Outreach Facilitator-East
description: Are you looking for a rewarding career that will let you give back to your community? NC State Extension extends research-based knowledge to all North Carolinians, helping them transform science into everyday solutions that improve their lives and grow our state. We are the model of excellence in non-formal, research-based education that advances agriculture, the environment, human health and well-being, youth and communities, while creating prosperity for all North Carolinians. As you consider this opportunity, we encourage you to review our Employee Value Proposition ( https://news.hr.ncsu.edu/you-belong-here/ ) and learn more about what makes NC State the best place to learn and work for everyone. The Regional Outreach Facilitator (ROF) is an integral part of the NC Cooperative Extension and the More in My Basked program. The ROF is housed in Carteret County Extension Center and works under the guidance and direct supervision of Shawn Banks, Carteret County Extension Director and Dr. Carolyn Bird, Professor and Principle Investigator/Program Director. The applicant will serve as the Regional Outreach Facilitator with the following requirements: · Collaborate with and support Extension Agent outreach in eight primary eastern counties: Carteret, Columbus, Duplin, Jones, New Hanover, Onslow, Wayne, and Wilson. · Liaison with and provide the MIMB campus-based team with information on specialized needs for the region. · Organize and/or conduct regional agent update meetings with MIMB agents. · Collaborate with eastern Extension agents, including those neighboring the primary counties, to engage with the More In My Basket Program, for example, to; identify organizations serving low-resource audiences to expand partnerships build and extend community relationships with organizations participate in the delivery of workshop and booth outreach events facilitate SNAP eligibility screening and application completion assistance through connection with campus program team organize and/or conduct regional information meetings and outreach to neighboring counties not currently participating in MIMB · Serve as liaison between county program staff (Cooperative Extension Agents and CEDs) and NCSU program staff for any programmatic issues. · Provide day-to-day management of the ROF planned participation in outreach events. · Provide on-site support to county staff for outreach activities individually or in collaboration with other Program Staff. · Facilitate program evaluation by assisting with curricula evaluation during MIMB workshops and sending completed forms to the campus team. · Support primary Eastern and surrounding counties’ outreach through the development of community partnerships and participate in community coalition and related meetings to advance program outreach venues. · Collaborate with the MIMB campus team to include the Outreach Strategy and Planning Manager, Program Coordinator, Communications and Social Media staff, Bilingual Outreach Facilitator, and Resource Navigator. · Contribute to the campus partnership database through regular reports to support relationships and ongoing communication with collaborators to facilitate outreach events. · Refer local clients to the campus team for FNS/SNAP benefit screenings and application completion assistance. · Other duties as assigned. The program, More In My Basket (MIMB), promotes and facilitates the delivery of outreach education, information, and programming to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) eligible population. The position requires that you be self-initiating, as well as a collaborator, able to multi-task effectively in a complex educational/academic environment, and be skilled in managing its schedule of participation in events/meetings.

title: Assistant Professor in Dental Hygiene
description: The Dwyer School of Health Sciences, Division of Dental Education at Indiana University South Bend invites applications for a full-time, 10-month tenure-track Assistant Professor of Dental Hygiene. We seek an engaged educator and scholar who will contribute to the continued excellence and growth of our Dental Hygiene Program through teaching, scholarship, and service. We are particularly interested in candidates who bring research experience, interdisciplinary perspectives, and areas of expertise that complement existing strengths while introducing new directions that expand and strengthen scholarship in dental hygiene and preventive science. The full-time faculty workload (100% FTE) is 12 credit hours of contact time each fall and spring semester. The successful candidate will receive one 3 credit course of reassigned contact time for scholarly and creative activities, in accordance with university and campus policies, resulting in a teaching assignment of 9 credit hours of contact time per semester. The successful candidate is expected to maintain an active program of scholarship and contribute to service. Teaching responsibilities include on-campus didactic, laboratory, and clinical instruction in the Dental Hygiene Program; mentoring dental hygiene students; participating in interprofessional education activities; and supporting faculty calibration. Additional responsibilities include participation in closed-loop curriculum assessment, quality assurance of clinical services, and service to the program, school, university, profession, and community. We seek a candidate who demonstrates a commitment to excellence in the dental hygiene profession and proficiency in high-impact, learner-centered teaching practices. The successful candidate will contribute to strengthening the program’s scholarly capacity through research, collaboration, and engagement with students and colleagues. Candidates must demonstrate the ability to work effectively within an academic community that values a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Salary is commensurate with the candidate’s qualifications and experience. About Indiana University South Bend: Indiana University South Bend is a public, comprehensive and the largest regional campus of Indiana University, serving northern Indiana and southwest Michigan. Located along the St. Joseph River, the campus is known for its strong emphasis on teaching excellence, undergraduate research, faculty student interaction, commitment to access and community engagement within a supportive academic environment. title: Research Data Librarian
description: IU Indianapolis University Library seeks a Research Data Librarian to join the Center for Digital Scholarship. Reporting to the Director of the Center for Digital Scholarship, this position collaborates with library colleagues, faculty, and Indiana University partners to support research data management, sharing, discovery, and responsible use across the research lifecycle. The librarian advances institutional research priorities related to open scholarship, compliance, and research impact services. The position contributes to the research information management work of the Center and the strategic priorities of the University Library. Responsibilities Provide consultations on research data management, including data management plans, metadata, storage, sharing, preservation, and repository selection. Support researchers in meeting funder, publisher, and institutional requirements for data sharing and public access. Assist researchers with qualitative and quantitative data discovery and use. Contribute to the development and promotion of research data services, repositories, and data discovery systems. Assist with the ingestion, curation, and management of datasets within an institutional repository. Design and deliver workshops on research data management, data sharing, discovery, and research metrics. Develop and implement outreach strategies for data and research information services. Promote the responsible use of research data, including AI-related considerations. Support faculty and administrators in interpreting research impact data for reporting and planning. Collaborate with liaison librarians and campus partners to integrate research impact and data services into faculty support programs. Advance open scholarship and responsible research practices through participation in library and university initiatives. About Indiana University Indianapolis and University Library IU Indianapolis is an urban-serving institution with a mission and a vision focused on both diversity and community engagement. University Library is a Power of Libraries award winner and home to numerous award-winning professionals. University Library is looking for librarians who will support our commitment to engage with the wider educational community and whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts are inclusive of the rich diversity of our campus and our city. Compensation and Application Minimum salary is $58,000, with additional funding for professional development and travel. Benefits include 22 vacation days, 10 paid holidays, health/dental insurance options, and retirement contributions of 10% to a Fidelity Investments retirement plan. A start-up package includes $10,000 for moving and ongoing professional development expenses.

title: University Archivist
description: IU Indianapolis University Library seeks a University Archivist to join the Ruth Lilly Special Collections and Archives, part of Distinctive Collections. The University Archivist reports to the Director of Distinctive Collections and works collaboratively with library colleagues, faculty, and Indiana University partners to collect and provide access to university records. The position advances institutional priorities related to student and faculty research as well as community engagement and collaboration. This position will work with records of all types, including born-digital records such as websites, emails, and digital files, as well as audio-visual material. The University Archivist will support the full lifecycle of university records, which includes liaising with staff and faculty units about records management policies and the value of institutional records before transfer to the archives, as well as providing education and reference to researchers using these records of permanent value. Responsibilities Actively collect university records deemed of permanent value, including born digital materials and university websites Supervise and perform University Archives collection management activities: accessioning, processing, preservation, and creation of finding aids, including training and supervising student workers to assist in this work Provide reference services for University Archives, assisting virtual and in-person researchers (faculty, students, staff, and other researchers) in using university records Liaise with campus offices on the interpretation and implementation of records retention schedules Manage web archiving of university websites, including appraising URLs and setting appropriate capture schedules Promote interest in the history of IUI/IUPUI and the historic neighborhoods predating the campus, through reference, instruction, and outreach efforts Collaborate with Ruth Lilly Special Collections & Archives department members to improve service, provide access to collections, develop policies and procedures, and move department initiatives forward Secondary responsibilities Participate in development of records management policies in partnership with other campus archivists and the University Records Manager Serve as a member of the Digital Collections Advisory Group, which is charged with setting priorities, establishing best practices for digital collections creation, and evaluating potential digital collections projects Participate in University Library planning and decision-making activities Participate in University Library and campus faculty organizations Represent the library in local, state, and national library venues as appropriate. Participate in library and university initiatives that advance campus and community engagement with distinctive collections Support the mission, vision, values, and strategic priorities of University Library.

title: Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor of Music (Viola)
description: The Jacobs School of Music seeks candidates for a position in the Department of Strings in Viola. The successful candidate will have an extensive and successful background as a performer and teacher at the highest national and/or international level, will be able to work effectively with faculty colleagues, and will be able to inspire students in a professionally-oriented educational environment. Participation in departmental meetings, recruitment activities and auditions, doctoral committees, and recital hearing committees, along with other department activities, such as faculty recitals and outreach activities, master classes, service on Jacobs School of Music committees, and other similar activities is expected.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Global Production and Trade Governance
description: The Department of International Studies at Indiana University’s Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International Studies invites applications for an Assistant/Associate Professor, tenure-track faculty position in Global Production and Trade Governance beginning August 1, 2027. We seek a scholar whose research and teaching examine the governance, law, and political economy of global production systems. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, global value chains, international trade and investment politics, the regulation of transnational production networks, foreign direct investment, and the implications of global economic governance for development and inequality. The successful candidate will contribute to the department’s growing strengths in international political economy and global governance while supporting existing undergraduate and graduate programs, including the International Financial Governance, Trade, and Development degree and the finance and trade concentration within the Master of International Affairs (MIA) program. The position reflects rising student and institutional interest in issues surrounding globalization, economic interdependence, financial governance, and the evolving rules and institutions that shape international economic relations. We welcome applications from candidates employing diverse disciplinary and methodological approaches. Candidates should demonstrate a strong research agenda, evidence of or potential for excellence in teaching, and a commitment to interdisciplinary engagement within an international studies environment. Responsibilities include maintaining an active research program, teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in areas related to global production and trade governance, mentoring students, and contributing to departmental and university service. Applicants seeking appointment at associate rank with tenure will be required to undergo a review of appropriateness for hire with tenure at Indiana University as a part of the recruitment process. Applicants seeking appointment at assistant rank must have a doctoral degree in hand by August 1, 2027. Applicants should submit a letter of application, curriculum vitae, research statement, teaching statement, a sample course syllabus, writing sample, and contact information for three references. Review of applications will begin following a priority deadline of September 11, 2026, with all applications received by that date being guaranteed full consideration. Review of applications will continue until the position is filled. Interested candidates should review the application requirements and submit their materials via the PeopleAdmin applicant portal at: https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/33720

title: Assistant/Associate/Full Professor of Clinical Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation

title: Tenured/Tenure-Track Open Rank Faculty Position in Medical Oncology
description: Indiana University School of Medicine, Bloomington (IUSM-B) invites applications for two, dually employed tenured/tenure-track assistant, associate or full professor positions in the School of Medicine, Department of Internal Medicine, Division of Hematology/Oncology, and IU Health Medical Group – in the South Region. We seek candidates to join the Indiana University Simon Comprehensive Cancer Center Clinical Trials Program (IUSCCC CT) to lead clinical trials research in Bloomington, IN and to provide clinical care to patients in the South Region of IU Health. Candidates with research and clinical expertise in clinical trials with an emphasis on breast, lung, gastrointestinal and benign hematology preferred, however, other areas of medical oncology expertise will be considered. We encourage applications from scholars who apply interdisciplinary perspectives and share important research overlap with IU-Bloomington scholars in other health sciences, while also offering new dimensions that will expand and strengthen the statewide IUSM, IU Health, and IU Simon Comprehensive Cancer Center missions. These 12‐month appointments would ideally start August 1, 2027 , although an earlier or later start date is negotiable. Applications received by November 16th, will receive full consideration, and applications will be accepted until the positions are filled. Responsibilities: Tenured/tenure-track faculty at the Indiana University School of Medicine Bloomington are expected to substantially contribute to the overall academic excellence of the regional campus and academic department and division by developing and/or maintaining a robust research portfolio including pursuing and obtaining major extramural research funding to conduct cutting-edge investigator-initiated clinical and translational research both as a principal investigator and co-investigator, teaching and mentoring medical students and residents; and actively providing service within the academic department/division, regional campus of the IUSM, Indiana University Simon Comprehensive Cancer Center, and university alongside clinical service in the IU Health Medical Group. The senior faculty candidate will be responsible for building the clinical trials program as an extension of the IUSCCC CTO. These positions are located on the campus of Indiana University, Bloomington (IUB) in Bloomington, Indiana, at the Regional Academic Health Center, and successful candidates are expected to work on the IUB campus to allow full engagement with the campus, and the IU Health Medical Group in the South Region of Indiana. Indiana University bases its tenure and promotion recommendations upon performance in three areas including research, teaching, and service. All individuals hired through this initiative are expected to excel in research and provide strong performance in teaching and administrative/professional service. Additionally, individuals hired will have a clinical service expectation to provide patient care in the IU Health Medical Group South, at the IU Health Bloomington Hospital. IU School of Medicine is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana. Minimum Qualifications: Applicants must possess an MD/DO (or equivalent degree), with PhD (or equivalent degree) preferred in addition. They must be able to obtain and maintain a license to practice clinical medicine in the State of Indiana and be American Board Eligible or Board Certified in Oncology and Hematology. Candidates must be committed to excellence in scholarship and teaching at the medical student and medical resident level. Candidates for appointment with tenure must demonstrate a record of scholarly achievement appropriate for an appointment with tenure, including extramurally funded research as a corresponding principal investigator, current funding or strong potential to secure external funding, established record of publications and scholarly work, and experience leading sizeable research initiatives. Application Procedures: Review of applications will begin November 16th and continue until both positions are filled. Application materials should include: Cover letter (maximum of 3 pages in length, identifying your application for a position with tenure (associate/full professor) or a tenure-track position (assistant professor), summarizing your qualifications, and interest in the position. Current Curriculum Vitae Research Statement (maximum of 4 pages in length) describing experience and approach to investigator initiated trials and/or translational and preclinical work Teaching Statement (maximum of 2 pages in length) OPTIONAL Up to three representative scholarly publications Contact information for three professional references Professional references for applicants for tenure-track pre-tenure positions will only be solicited for those selected for screening interviews. Professional references for applicants for positions with tenure will only be solicited for those selected for a finalist interview and/or job offer. Applicants should apply at: https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/34713 All queries about the position or the application procedures should be addressed to Dr. Allistair Thompson, thompala@iu.edu , or Dr. Cindy Broderick, search coordinator, at faculty1@iu.edu . Before a conditional offer of employment with tenure is finalized, candidates will be asked to disclose any pending investigations or previous findings of sexual or professional misconduct. They will also be required to authorize an inquiry by Indiana University Bloomington with all current and former employers along these lines. The relevance of information disclosed or ascertained in the context of this process to a candidate’s eligibility for hire will be evaluated by Indiana University Bloomington on a case-by-case basis. Applicants should be aware, however, that Indiana University Bloomington takes the matters of sexual and professional misconduct very seriously. About Indiana University Bloomington : Founded in 1820, Indiana University-Bloomington (IUB) is the flagship campus of Indiana University. Located in Bloomington, IN, IUB constantly strives to embody its mission to create, disseminate, preserve, and apply knowledge. It does so through its commitments to cutting-edge research, scholarship, arts, and creative activity; inspired and challenging undergraduate, graduate, professional, and lifelong educational programs; meaningful experiences outside the classroom; expansive global educational opportunities while fostering a culturally diverse campus environment; first-rate library and museum collections; and far-reaching economic development and impact in the state and region. IUB is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities (AAU) since 1909, is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission and is a member of the North Central Association. Known for its Indiana limestone facades and green spaces throughout, IUB is widely considered one of the country’s most beautiful college campuses. With a robust portfolio of clinical trials, nationally recognized research programs, and strong partnerships with IU School of Medicine and IU Health, the Cancer Center provides exceptional opportunities for collaborative investigation and the translation of scientific discoveries into improved patient outcomes. The surrounding region, featuring nature preserves, National forests, and Indiana’s largest reservoir, offers exceptional outdoor recreation opportunities. Friendly, safe, affordable and welcoming, Bloomington is a gem set in the beautiful rolling hills of southern Indiana. Bloomington’s geographic position illustrates our state’s nickname “Crossroad of America.” It is within a 1 hour drive of Indianapolis, 2 hour drive of Louisville, KY, 3.5 hour of Columbus, OH, and ~4 hour drive to Chicago, IL, St. Louis, MO, and Nashville, TN. Bloomington has a low cost of living relative to entry-level faculty salaries. The community is home to many thriving affinity groups and offers an exceptional selection of cultural, educational, and recreational opportunities. Learn more here: https://bloomington.iu.edu/campus-life/bloomington.html .

title: Assistant Research Professor of Pediatrics
description: The Herman B Wells Center for Pediatric Research conducts basic science and translational research within the Department of Pediatrics at Indiana University School of Medicine. The Wells Center houses more than 300 faculty investigators, staff, and trainees seeking answers to the most pressing questions related to childhood illness. With the collaboration between scientists and physicians, the center aims to increase knowledge of causes and mechanisms of serious pediatric diseases. Our goal is to develop innovative approaches to the diagnosis and treatment of sick children in Indiana and beyond. The Felton Lab's current work builds on evidence that autoreactive B cell development and function are altered during T1D progression and that B cells exhibit distinct metabolic phenotypes in autoimmune disease. The lab also investigates immunomodulatory approaches and mechanisms, including type I interferon signaling, and integrates mechanistic research with efforts to understand T1D progression and risk. The Assistant Research Professor will serve as a senior scientific member of the Felton lab, supporting and advancing a translational research program focused on the immunologic and metabolic mechanisms underlying type 1 diabetes. The position will have particular responsibility for developing and executing studies examining B cell tolerance, immune cell metabolism, type I interferon signaling, and interactions between immune cells and the pancreatic islet microenvironment. Working closely with the PI, the Assistant Research Professor will provide intellectual and technical leadership for ongoing and emerging projects, including the design and execution of experiments, interpretation and integration of complex datasets, development of new experimental approaches, and preparation of manuscripts, abstracts, presentations, and grant applications. The individual will be expected to exercise substantial scientific independence while contributing to the laboratory's broader research strategy. The position will also provide day-to-day scientific leadership within the laboratory, including mentoring trainees and research staff, troubleshooting experimental approaches, establishing rigorous and reproducible laboratory practices, and coordinating projects and collaborations. The Assistant Research Professor may lead defined research projects and develop complementary areas of investigation that strengthen the laboratory's overall research portfolio. This position and scientific environment is particularly suited for an applicant with expertise in immunology, B cell biology, or autoimmunity. IUSM is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana.

title: Assistant Research Professor of Pediatrics
description: The Herman B Wells Center for Pediatric Research conducts basic science and translational research within the Department of Pediatrics at Indiana University School of Medicine. The Wells Center houses more than 300 faculty investigators, staff, and trainees seeking answers to the most pressing questions related to childhood illness. With the collaboration between scientists and physicians, the center aims to increase knowledge of causes and mechanisms of serious pediatric diseases. Our goal is to develop innovative approaches to the diagnosis and treatment of sick children in Indiana and beyond. Research in the DeRyckere and Graham labs focuses on the TAM-family tyrosine kinase receptors and their roles as potential therapeutic targets in the immune system and in cancer cells. Our goal is to develop new therapies for treatment of cancer in children and adults and we are actively engaged in development of novel drugs. In conjunction with this work, we also develop and apply next-generation model systems to advance our research and for precision medicine applications. Our lab is a fast-paced, collegial and supportive research environment. The DeRyckere and Graham labs are seeking a full-time Assistant Research Professor to lead a project focused on the TAM family kinases as therapeutic targets for treatment of breast cancer. Responsibilities will include experimental design and execution, data analysis and presentation, preparation of federal grant applications and reports, teaching and supervising students and trainees. This position is expected to comprise 65% lab research and data analysis, 25% reading and writing grants/manuscripts/presentations and 10% teaching/mentoring junior scientists. The ideal candidate will be a dynamic individual who is able to work independently to manage and complete multiple projects/tasks simultaneously. IUSM is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana.

title: Postdoctoral Fellow/Synthetic Chemist; Chemistry Zaleski Lab
description: Department Information: The Department of Chemistry in the College of Arts + Sciences at Indiana University, consists of a well-rounded research community with cutting-edge expertise in a wide variety of modern disciplines including analytical chemistry, organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry, physical chemistry, materials chemistry, and biochemistry. Job Summary: The Zaleski Lab in the Department of Chemistry at Indiana University is accepting applications for a postdoctoral research position. The position involves the design and synthesis of hybrid molecular and nanomaterial catalysts (see here for recent work: Accts. Chem. Res. 2019 , 52 , 1957; Chem. Sci. 2025 , 16 , 255. The desired start date is February 1, 2027, although this is flexible in-order-to accommodate the needs of outstanding candidates. The successful applicant will use a deep understanding of synthetic inorganic and organic ligand chemistry, as well as molecule preparation and purification to achieve research goals. Nanomaterial and catalysis experience is a plus but not required. Motivated applicants with a Ph.D. in any area of synthetic chemistry will be considered. A candidate with a strong background in solution-phase synthetic preparations and characterizations, as well as familiarity manipulating air- and moisture-sensitive chemicals, is ideally suited for the project. We seek to employ someone with demonstrable experience in chemical purification and characterization of starting materials and reaction products by standard techniques (NMR, EPR, IR, Mass spectrometry, X-ray diffraction,TEM, and DFT calculations also desirable). The Zaleski Lab is a dynamic multidisciplinary laboratory environment. The successful applicant will play an integral role within our growing team and will emerge with a skill set that is equally relevant to academia and industry. Trainees receive regular guidance and feedback to ensure progress is made toward their career goals, whatever those may be. Trainees are also afforded the scheduling flexibility needed to maintain an appropriate work life balance and a safe laboratory environment. Responsibilities: 1. Manage own academic research and administrative activities. This involves small scale project management and coordinating multiple aspects of work to meet deadlines. 2. Train graduate and undergraduate students in research methods 3. Adapt existing, and develop new, scientific techniques and experimental protocols to achieve research objectives. 4. Use specialist scientific equipment in a laboratory environment. 5. Assist in maintaining a research laboratory (e.g. setting up Schlenk lines, ordering equipment etc.) 6. Contribute ideas for new research projects. 7. Undertake comprehensive and systematic literature reviews and write up the results for publication in peer-reviewed journals. 8. Collaborate in the preparation of scientific reports and journal articles and occasionally present papers and posters. 9. Act as a source of information and advice to other members of the group on scientific protocols and experimental techniques. 10. Represent the research group at external meetings/seminars, either with other members of the group or alone. 11. Carry out collaborative projects with colleagues in partner institutions, and research groups.

title: Open Rank Professor of Political Science - International Relations
description: International Relations (Open Rank) The Department of Political Science at Indiana University Bloomington invites applications for a full-time tenure-track Open Rank Professor position in International Relations, beginning August 1, 2027. We seek a scholar focused on the relationship between emerging computational technologies and conflict processes/security studies. title: Postdoctoral Fellow in Quantum Materials and Quantum Optics
description: Working under the direction of Dr. Iqbal Utama, the postdoctoral fellow will lead experimental research focused on low-dimensional, molecular, and hybrid organic–inorganic materials for applications in quantum sensing, quantum photonics, and related quantum technologies. The successful candidate will design, fabricate, and characterize quantum materials and nanoscale devices, contribute to scientific publications and research proposals, and mentor graduate and undergraduate students in a collaborative research environment. This is an outstanding opportunity for early-career researchers to advance an independent research program, build a strong publication record, and contribute to cutting-edge developments in quantum science and technology within a highly interdisciplinary and well-supported academic setting. Specific Duties: Conduct experimental research on low-dimensional, molecular, and hybrid organic–inorganic materials for quantum sensing, quantum photonics, and related quantum technologies. Design, fabricate, and characterize quantum-material and nanoscale devices using techniques that may include materials synthesis and processing, nanofabrication, optical spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, magnetometry, and optically-detected magnetic resonance. Develop experimental protocols and assist with the setup, operation, maintenance, and documentation of laboratory instruments. Analyze and interpret experimental data and maintain complete, organized records of experiments, procedures, and results. Prepare manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals and present research findings at scientific meetings. Contribute to the preparation of research proposals, technical reports, and collaborative projects. Mentor graduate and undergraduate students and provide training in relevant laboratory methods. Contribute to a safe, collegial, collaborative, and intellectually engaged laboratory environment. Anticipated start date: December 1, 2026, or a mutually agreed date thereafter. Anticipated end date: November 30, 2027, based on a December 1, 2026 start date. Appointment term: The initial appointment will be for 12 months. The appointment may be renewed annually, subject to satisfactory performance and availability of funding.

title: Center for Possible Minds Postdoctoral Fellow
description: Center for Possible Minds Postdoctoral Fellow Vacancy The Center for Possible Minds at Indiana University, Bloomington, invites applications for Postdoctoral Fellows to join its Program for Advanced Research in Diverse Intelligences. The fellowship provides support to scholars studying intelligence/cognition/mind in diverse forms, from diverse disciplinary perspectives. Candidates must embrace interdisciplinary scholarship and be excited about substantial conversation and collaboration with other disciplines. This postdoctoral fellowship program aims to create a cohort of researchers optimally positioned to address questions about the nature of biological, artificial, and collective intelligence through collaboration across a wide range of fields. We seek enthusiastic scientists and scholars who will embrace the chance to help set the agenda for our new research center. Postdoctoral fellows will have the opportunity to organize meetings and workshops at the Center as well as to propose new Center initiatives. We expect to hire 2-4 postdocs through this search. Postdocs will have offices in the Center for Possible Minds, where they will be joined by visiting fellows and faculty. Fellows are expected to pursue research activities associated with their primary area(s) of scholarship, as well as to explore collaborative, interdisciplinary projects. These fellowships are designed to advance the careers of new scholars by providing opportunities to research, organize, and collaborate in a highly interdisciplinary environment. Strong applicants will demonstrate evidence of the sort of outstanding scholarly potential that would make them competitive for tenure-track faculty positions at Indiana University or other top research universities. Terms of Agreement Fellows are expected to pursue research, organize workshops and events, and participate in Center activities and seminars. Fellows may also teach classes in the appropriate department(s) or program(s), subject to curriculum needs and availability of funds. Fellowships are expected to be 2-year positions; fellows will be appointed as one-year contracts with the possibility for renewal. The start date is flexible; positions can begin as soon as August 1, 2026. Fellows will receive a salary of $60,000 plus health benefits and $3,000 each year in research support. title: Assistant Research Professor of Anatomy, Cell Biology & Physiology
description: The Sankar Laboratory and the Department of Anatomy, Cell Biology & Physiology at Indiana University School of Medicine are seeking a highly motivated Research Scientist to lead studies within a newly funded NIH project investigating cell-intrinsic pain mechanisms in osteoarthritis (OA). This interdisciplinary project will use global and conditional knockout mouse models to investigate sensory neuron and joint cell-intrinsic roles of Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase kinase 2 (CAMKK2) in OA pain using single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of the joint. The project will also employ cutting-edge 3D light-sheet microscopy to map sensory neuron dynamics and inflammation during OA progression and mechanistic signaling studies in the dorsal root ganglion. Applicants should hold a PhD, MD/PhD, or equivalent degree in musculoskeletal biology, neuroscience, immunology, molecular biology, or a related field. We seek a passionate, self-driven, and collaborative scientist with relevant postdoctoral or equivalent research experience and demonstrated expertise in OA, musculoskeletal and single cell transcriptomics, transgenic mouse models and colony management, animal surgery or behavioral phenotyping, molecular signaling, advanced microscopy, and bioinformatics. Experience in pain research is desirable but not required. Fluency in spoken and written English is required. The successful candidate is expected to drive research projects with a high degree of independence, analyze and integrate complex datasets, contribute to manuscripts and grant applications, and mentor junior laboratory members. Candidates will be considered based on their overall experience, scientific productivity, technical expertise, and potential to advance this interdisciplinary program. The Scientist will join the Indiana Center for Musculoskeletal Health, a vibrant and supportive multidisciplinary community offering outstanding collaborative opportunities and access to advanced genomics, imaging, computational, and animal research resources. Located in Indianapolis, Indiana University School of Medicine provides a highly collaborative biomedical research environment in an affordable and dynamic city with a growing life sciences sector and excellent quality of life. title: Assistant Research Professor of Pediatrics
description: The Herman B Wells Center for Pediatric Research conducts basic science and translational research within the Department of Pediatrics at Indiana University School of Medicine. The Wells Center houses more than 200 faculty investigators, staff, and trainees seeking answers to the most pressing questions related to childhood illness. With the collaboration between scientists and physicians, the center aims to increase knowledge of causes and mechanisms of serious pediatric diseases. Our goal is to develop innovative approaches to the diagnosis and treatment of sick children in Indiana and beyond. An Assistant Research Professor in this position is expected to provide leadership within the laboratory on scientific methods and practices for immunology and genetic measurements to determine risk or presence of Type 1 diabetes in human clinical research. This includes developing new techniques to measure relevant biomarkers, including methods using radioisotopes and quality control programs. This role will also provide leadership in obtaining and maintaining regulatory approval for performance, reporting and use of disease-related biomarkers. This role will provide support for writing reports, grants and academic manuscripts related to the work of the laboratory. We seek to study Type 1 diabetes and related autoimmune diseases, using measurements of antibodies, genes, metabolic signals, and related biomarkers. These are typically used in large clinical research studies to demonstrate efficient methods for identifying subjects at risk and/or for identifying triggering environmental exposures. The lab works on studies led by Dr. Hagopian, led by other IU investigators, or led by collaborating academic investigators at other institutions. The lab also maintains a biosample bank from Dr. Hagopian's historical studies which can be used to investigate biomarkers of disease. title: Clinical Laboratory Director
description: The Department of Medical and Molecular Genetics of the Indiana University School of Medicine is recruiting a Board-certified/Board Eligible M.D., or MD/PhD, or PhD for a Clinical Laboratory Director role in the Division of Diagnostic Genomics and Therapeutics. We seek an outstanding physicians with expertise in Clinical Molecular Genetics and/or Cytogenetics who is interested in combining leadership in genomic laboratory medicine with clinical practice and/or funded research. The successful candidate will devote a substantial portion of their effort to medical and operational leadership within the IU Genetic Testing Laboratories, with the remainder of their effort dedicated to patient care or, depending on the candidate’s interests and qualifications, externally funded research. In addition, the individual will participate in our ACGME-accredited Laboratory Genetics and Genomics fellowship training program and participate in training residents and graduate students as part of the departmental teaching mission. The academic appointment, salary and benefit package is commensurate with qualifications. Certification (or eligibility) by the ABMGG in both Clinical Molecular Genetics and Cytogenetics, or Laboratory Genetics and Genomics, is required. The Division of Diagnostic Genomics and Therapeutics includes five CLIA-certified and CAP-accredited clinical laboratories that together comprise the IU Genetic Testing Laboratories: Molecular Genetics, Cytogenetics, Pharmacogenomics, Biochemical Genetics and Diagnostic Genomics, which performs high-throughput Next-Generation Sequencing. The laboratories provide comprehensive diagnostic services, including prenatal, constitutional, and oncology testing, supporting patient care throughout Indiana and beyond. The Medical Director will participate in the leadership and continued development of a busy and expanding diagnostic laboratory service. Responsibilities will include shared oversight of clinical genomic testing, interpretation and reporting, assay development and implementation, quality and regulatory activities, and collaboration with laboratory faculty, staff, clinicians, and other members of the healthcare team. The specific scope of laboratory leadership responsibilities will be tailored to the expertise and interests of the successful candidate. description: Indiana University Bloomington (IUB) School of Public Health‐Bloomington (SPH‐B) invites applications for the position of Lecturer of Exercise Science in the Department of Kinesiology. The SPH-B seeks passionate, contemporary educators who will contribute to excellence in teaching and student learning in the study and application of human movement, physical activity, exercise, and human performance, preparing students for continued education and professional careers in kinesiology, allied health, or related fields. This 10-month instructional faculty appointment is planned to start August 1, 2027 . Appointment may be made at the rank of Lecturer, Senior Lecturer, or Teaching Professor, commensurate with qualifications and experience. Applications received by November 15, 2026, will receive full priority consideration, and applications will be accepted until the position is filled. This position is located on the Bloomington campus of Indiana University. Successful candidates are expected to work on campus to allow full engagement with the department, school, university, and community. Responsibilities and Opportunity: Non-tenure-track faculty or instructional faculty, Lecturers, are expected to substantially contribute to the overall academic excellence of the department primarily through teaching and student learning; developing, delivering, and enhancing courses and curricula within their areas of expertise; mentoring and supporting undergraduate and/or graduate students as appropriate to their assigned responsibilities; and engaging in ongoing professional development and other activities that support excellence in teaching, student learning, curriculum enhancement, and student success. The position may provide opportunities to contribute to the department through service in support of teaching and academic program delivery, such as internship coordination, experiential or service-learning initiatives, and community outreach. Notably, instructional faculty, including Lecturers, have an opportunity for promotion and advancement from Lecturer to Senior Lecturer and ultimately to the highest rank of Teaching Professor. The ideal candidate will contribute to the teaching mission of the department in exercise science, with the ability to support related areas of the curriculum including physical activity, health promotion, and pre-professional health preparation. About Kinesiology : As a legacy program on the IUB campus, the Department of Kinesiology, with 30 full-time faculty, has a strong and growing enrollment in the undergraduate Exercise Science degree program (~1,375 students), and healthy enrollments in graduate degree programs (~75 students) including an MS in Athletic Training, MS in Kinesiology, and a PhD in Human Performance. Faculty conduct research across numerous areas including exercise physiology (with historical excellence in environmental and clinical exercise physiology), biomechanics, sport neurotrauma, athletic training neuromuscular/motor control, physical activity and fitness interventions, with the latter including youth sport-based approaches to health and well-being. Finally, the department supports the Physical Activity Instruction Program, an extensive fitness and sport focused academic service program. title: Open Rank, Tenured/Tenure-Track Faculty Position in AI-Enabled Experiments for Scientific Discovery in Health
department: IU Bloomington Vice Provost For Faculty Affairs
description: Indiana University Bloomington invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor or tenured associate or full professor in the Department of Statistics, College of Arts and Sciences. We seek an outstanding researcher to develop a research program at the forefront of statistics, artificial intelligence, experimentation, and health. AI systems now participate not only in analyzing data but in designing experiments, selecting interventions, and guiding scientific discovery. This shift calls for new statistical foundations, and this opening offers a well-resourced professorship to build a research program that develops these foundations. We are especially interested in candidates developing statistical methodology for AI-enabled experimentation in health, aging, and related areas. Relevant settings include: autonomous and AI-guided experimentation adaptive and innovative clinical trials precision medicine self-driving laboratories digital twins and in-silico experimentation AI-enabled drug discovery. Regulatory frameworks are evolving alongside these developments, including recent FDA guidance on credible, validated applications of AI, model-informed approaches and new experimental methodologies in drug development. Exceptional candidates in other application areas will also be considered. We welcome candidates whose research develops methodology and theory in a variety of subfields of statistics relevant to AI-enabled experimentation, including: experimental design, clinical trial design, and sequential experimentation Bayesian optimization and active learning contextual bandits, reinforcement learning and online experimentation causal inference and treatment-effect heterogeneity statistical learning and machine learning evaluation and monitoring of AI systems micro-randomized trials uncertainty quantification prediction-powered inference. Indiana University Bloomington offers an unusually rich environment for this research. IU has established major academic-industry partnerships in health and biotechnology, including a five-year $40M partnership with Eli Lilly on AI-enabled clinical trials research, and a five-year master collaboration agreement with Cook Medical. These partnerships are coordinated through the IU Launch Accelerator for Biosciences and complement IU’s clinical and health-science ecosystem, including the IU Medical Center and IU School of Medicine, giving faculty the opportunity to work across the full span from statistical theory and methodology to applied industry collaborations and translation into practice. Located approximately one hour from Indianapolis, Bloomington provides access to one of the nation’s major health and life-sciences hubs. The successful candidate will join a collegial, research-active department with strengths in Bayesian methods, high-dimensional statistics, computational statistics, physics-informed inference, and biostatistics, and will help shape its direction in AI-enabled and health-oriented statistics. The department is closely tied to the Indiana Statistical Consulting Center, which serves researchers across the university, and has natural collaborators in the Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering, home to the Luddy Center for Artificial Intelligence and its focus on AI for digital health, as well as in the Department of Mathematics, Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences, the Cognitive Science program, and the School of Public Health-Bloomington. These 10‐month appointments would ideally start August 1, 2027 , although an earlier or later start date is negotiable. Applications received by December 1, 2026, will receive full consideration, and applications will be accepted until the positions are filled. The position is located on the campus of Indiana University, Bloomington (IUB) in Bloomington, Indiana, and successful candidates are expected to work on the IUB campus to allow full engagement with the department, school, campus, and community. Indiana University bases its tenure and promotion recommendations upon performance in three areas including research, teaching, and service. All individuals hired through this initiative are expected to excel in research and provide strong performance in teaching and service. Minimum Qualifications: Applicants should possess a PhD in statistics (or a related field) and be committed to excellence in scholarship and teaching at the undergraduate and graduate level. Candidates for w/tenure positions must demonstrate a record of scholarly achievement appropriate for an appointment w/tenure, including extramurally funded research as a corresponding principal investigator, current funding or strong potential to secure external funding, established record of publications and scholarly work, and experience leading sizeable research initiatives. Application Procedures: Review of applications will begin December 1, 2026 and continue until all positions are filled. Application materials should include: Cover letter (maximum of 3 pages in length, identifying your application for a position with tenure (associate/full professor) or a tenure-track position (assistant professor), and summarize your interest in the position. Current Curriculum Vitae Research Statement (maximum of 4 pages in length) Teaching Statement (maximum of 2 pages in length) Contact information for three professional references Professional references for applicants for tenure-track positions will only be solicited for those selected for a screening interview. Professional references for applicants for positions with tenure will only be solicited for those selected for a finalist interview and/or job offer. title: Postdoctoral Fellow - Capone Lab - ENVR
department: IU Bloomington Environmental and Occupational Health
description: A postdoctoral fellow position is available in the Capone Lab in the Department of Environmental and Occupational Health at the Indiana University School of Public Health-Bloomington. The fellow will join a multidisciplinary team conducting a five-year CDC-funded study focused on developing and applying integrated surveillance approaches for soil-transmitted helminth (STH) infection in the southeastern United States. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, but applications received by October 5, 2026 will be given full consideration, and the search will remain open until a suitable candidate is found. The earliest anticipated start date is October 19, 2026. Dr. Drew Capone’s research group ( https://caponelab.publichealth.indiana.edu ) has broad interests in environmental health microbiology. Current projects include public health surveillance using fecal waste streams, microbial fate and transport, the role of infrastructure in interrupting enteric pathogen transmission, and predicting public health outcomes using quantitative microbial risk assessment. Lab members conduct field research in Mozambique and Indiana, as well as wet lab work in Bloomington, Indiana. We use tools from engineering, epidemiology, and environmental health microbiology to investigate the problems affecting low-income individuals and aim to improve public health in the communities where these people live.

department: IU Bloomington Vice Provost For Faculty Affairs
description: Indiana University Maurer School of Law in Bloomington is seeking outstanding lateral tenured or tenure-track applicants in the regulation of artificial intelligence, robotics, and other emerging technologies. title: Postdoctoral Fellow (Bacterial Sulfur Metabolism) Giedroc Lab
description: Department Information: The Department of Chemistry in the College of Arts and Sciences at Indiana University Bloomington, consists of a well-rounded research community with cutting-edge expertise in a wide variety of modern disciplines including analytical chemistry, organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry, physical chemistry, materials chemistry, and chemical biology and biochemistry. title: Clinical Research-Focus Postdoctoral Psychology Fellow
description: Clinical Research-Focus Postdoctoral Psychology Fellow Teen POWER - Indiana University School of Medicine The Teen Program Of Weight and Eating Research (Teen POWER) at the Indiana University School of Medicine is seeking qualified candidates for one to two clinical-research-focused Postdoctoral Psychology Fellow position. Patient-oriented treatment research funded by NIH as well as pilot studies will provide advanced clinical-research opportunities for individuals interested in academic careers working with eating/weight disorders or adolescent behavioral health. This full-time position is 100% research effort (and therefore eligible for NIH loan repayment programs), but day-to-day activities will involve approximately 40% research activities and 60% clinical activities (therapy/assessment) delivered in the context of clinical trials. Clinical activities (60%) will involve serving as a research clinician performing assessments and providing evidence-based treatment on an NIH-funded randomized controlled trial treating adolescents with binge eating, as well as pilot studies. The postdoc will receive intensive training and ongoing supervision in the administration of diagnostic and semi-structured interviews (e.g., Eating Disorder Examination). as well as the delivery of evidence-based treatments (i.e., CBT-LOC, IHBLT) for eating/weight disorders. Additional pilot studies are planned and will involve similar activities. Research activities (40%) will involve data analysis, preparing data reports for grant progress reports and new grant applications, and submitting research papers for publication and presentation at conferences. Data from numerous completed treatment and longitudinal studies on eating/weight disorders will also be available for research projects and publications. The postdoc will also supervise/mentor research staff (e.g., postbac and graduate student research assistants) in data management activities. Candidates must have a doctoral degree in psychology, a completed APA-accredited internship, and experience working with eating/weight disorders and adolescents/families. Experience in data management systems (e.g., REDCap, Qualtrics) and strong statistical skills and experiences, and excellent writing skills (including publications in peer-reviewed journals) are required. This position is tailor-made for loan repayment program applications. It is ideal for individuals pursuing academic clinical-research careers, with a focus on research (e.g., tenure-track faculty) or clinical track (e.g., staff psychologist or clinical service director). The position offers intensive mentored opportunities for publishing and grant-writing. Working at Teen POWER Teen POWER is a new research clinic in the Department of Psychiatry. Our program received funding from the NIH to conduct treatment studies for adolescents with eating/weight concerns, building upon a six-year track record conducting similar behavioral clinical trials. Teen POWER is best suited for individuals who are curious and patient-centered. Teen POWER offers an ideal research environment to engage with colleagues about clinical observations, data results, and their significance. Beyond having a strong work ethic and being detail-oriented, Teen POWER prioritizes highly collaborative and collegial relationships with peers and faculty, who make it a point to be highly responsive and accessible. The Department of Psychiatry has a broad research, clinical, and teaching mission and maintains a clinical psychology internship, a psychiatry residency program, and fellowships in addition to training rotations for medical and graduate students. Indiana University School of Medicine is the largest medical school in the United States, with a large academic health center in downtown Indianapolis, the 17th largest city in the United States. In addition to having active sports, cultural, arts, and educational events and programs, Indianapolis is located centrally near several other major cities including Chicago, Louisville, Cincinnati, and Columbus. IU School of Medicine is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana. IU School of Medicine is closely aligned with our health system partner, IU Health, which has twice earned a place on the US News and World Report Honor Roll. The shared vision of both institutions is to lead the transformation of healthcare through quality innovation and education to make Indiana one of the nation’s healthiest states. IU Health is among the top ten largest single-state nonprofit health systems in the United States operating 16 hospitals statewide (a mix of urban, suburban and rural facilities). This partnership enables the seamless integration of research findings into patient care.

title: Post Doctoral Fellow
description: The Department of Geography at Indiana University Bloomington invites applications for a Postdoctoral Scholar to conduct independent research under the joint mentorship of Dr. Darren Ficklin (Indiana University Bloomington) and Dr. Margaret Zimmer (University of Wisconsin–Madison). The postdoctoral scholar will be based in the Department of Geography at Indiana University Bloomington and will have opportunities to interact and collaborate with research groups at both Indiana University and the University of Wisconsin–Madison. This position provides an opportunity for an early-career researcher to develop and lead an independent research project broadly related to the complementary research interests of Drs. Ficklin and Zimmer. Rather than being tied to a predetermined research project, the position is designed to support creative, independent scholarship. Applicants are asked to propose a research project that they would pursue during the postdoctoral appointment. Dr. Ficklin's research broadly focuses on hydrology and hydroclimatology, including climate change impacts on hydrologic systems, hydrologic modeling, streamflow and stream temperature, and large-scale computational approaches. Dr. Zimmer's research focuses on watershed hydrology, including water quantity and quality, surface water–groundwater interactions, non-perennial streams, and soil water, with a strong emphasis on field-based investigation. Together, these areas provide opportunities for research spanning field observations, process-based hydrology, hydroclimatology, and computational and modeling approaches. Broad areas of potential interest include, but are not limited to: · climate change impacts on hydrologic systems; · watershed and catchment hydrology; · hydroclimatology and climate–water interactions; · surface water–groundwater interactions; · non-perennial streams and hydrologic connectivity; · soil water and subsurface hydrologic processes; · water quantity and water quality; · streamflow and stream temperature; · hydrologic and environmental modeling; · field-based hydrologic and environmental research; · extreme hydroclimatic events; · large-scale or computational hydrology; · climate and hydrologic data analysis; and · related questions at the intersection of climate, water, and environmental change. Computational and modeling project ideas are all encouraged, particularly projects that creatively integrate observations with modeling, data science, remote sensing, or other quantitative approaches. Applicants are not expected to propose work identical to existing projects in either research group. Rather, proposed projects should take advantage of the complementary expertise of Drs. Ficklin and Zimmer while allowing the postdoctoral scholar to establish a distinct research direction. The successful candidate will have substantial independence in developing and carrying out their research agenda while being an active member of the Ficklin Lab at Indiana University. The postdoctoral scholar will work alongside Ph.D. and undergraduate students, participate in lab meetings and research activities, and contribute to a collaborative research environment. Regular interaction and collaboration with Dr. Zimmer and her research group at the University of Wisconsin–Madison will also be encouraged. Opportunities will additionally exist to develop collaborations within the Department of Geography and across Indiana University and the University of Wisconsin–Madison.
