title: Division Chief, Division of General Internal Medicine and Hospital Medicine
description: The Opportunity The Department of Medicine at Indiana University School of Medicine (IUSM) seeks an accomplished academic physician leader to serve as the founding Chief of a new Division of General Internal Medicine and Hospital Medicine. Two new divisions are being established through the strategic restructuring of the current Division of General Internal Medicine and Geriatrics, the second being the new ‘Division of Aging, Geriatric Medicine, and Palliative Care’. This restructuring is a deliberate investment in focused leadership intended to sustain and accelerate academic growth and excellence in the Department’s generalist and acute care missions. The founding Chief will lead approximately 280 faculty members organized into three sections, each with its own strategic plan and identity, and will report directly to the Chair of the Department of Medicine. This is a rare opportunity to define, from the outset, the structure, culture, and strategic direction of one of the largest general medicine and hospital medicine enterprises in American academic medicine. The Division: An Overview of Sections and Research Centers Division faculty have the opportunity to engage in the service, research, and education missions of the Department and IUSM. Faculty practice and teach across the full continuum of undergraduate and graduate medical education and hold impactful Departmental and School educational leadership roles, including the internal medicine residency program directorship, multiple Key Clinician Educator appointments, and clerkship and course leadership positions. Research faculty maintain deep partnerships with various Research Centers including the Center for Biomedical Informatics and Health Services Research at the Regenstrief Institute, the Center for Health Communication and Information at the Richard L. Roudebush VA Medical Center, the IU Center for Biomedical Ethics, the Center for Global Health, and the Regenstrief Center for Health Equity Research at Eskenazi Health. Researchers have consistently secured close to $3M dollars in federal and non-federal funding annually over the last three years. Examples of current research include diabetes prevention, improving the care of individuals with rare diseases, implementation of survivorship care plans, and the deployment of large-scale decision aids to guide colorectal cancer screening. • Section of Hospital Medicine (approximately 180 faculty members). The largest section in the Department, with faculty engaged in clinical care, scholarship and research, and teaching in hospital medicine care across IU Health, Eskenazi Health, and the Richard L. Roudebush VA Medical Center. • Section of General Internal Medicine (approximately 15 faculty members). The academic home for general internal medicine, including research faculty in health services research, biomedical informatics, global health, health equity, and medical ethics, and faculty who hold key educational leadership roles across the Department of Medicine and IUSM. • Section of Primary Care Internal Medicine (approximately 85 faculty members). Ambulatory internal medicine practice and general internal medicine care is an area of critical workforce need statewide and a stated development priority of the division's faculty. Faculty provide general internal medicine and medicine-pediatrics care across IU Health, Eskenazi Health, and the Richard L Roudebush VA Medical Center. A retrospective of the Division’s activities in the academic year 2025-26 can be viewed here . Position Summary Reporting to the Chair of the Department of Medicine, the Division Chief provides academic, clinical, financial, and operational leadership for the division across all sites and sections. The Chief recruits, develops, and retains faculty; sets and executes the Division's strategic plan in alignment with both the Department of Medicine 2026 to 2031 Strategic Plan and IUSM’s strategic priorities ; oversees the division's budget and clinical performance in partnership with our health system partners; advances the Division's research, scholarship, and educational missions; and represents the Division within the Department, the School, our affiliated health systems, and nationally. This leadership role is expected to reflect a mix of clinical practice and research or scholarly activity, configured with the Chair to fit the successful candidate's academic profile. Key Responsibilities Vision and strategy • Develop, in partnership with faculty, staff, and the Chair, the founding strategic plan for the Division and for each of its three sections. • Build a Division leadership team with clear accountability and create visible leadership development opportunities for faculty across all three sections. • Align the Division's missions across sites, employer groups, and stakeholders, and represent the Division's interests in health system planning. Education • Elevate the Division's undergraduate and graduate medical education mission, in close partnership with the internal medicine residency, the medical student clerkship, and IUSM educational leadership. • Support the academic advancement of clinician educators, including scholarship in teaching and education, and build the infrastructure that makes educational scholarship sustainable. Clinical care and primary care growth • Elevate academic internal medicine primary care, including recruitment, panel growth, practice model innovation, and the visibility of primary care within the Division and the health system. • Partner with IU Health, Eskenazi Health, and the VA on hospital medicine operations, quality and safety, throughput, care transitions, and value-based care. • Evaluate clinical workloads and targets and work with clinical partners to align them with academic success and clinician wellbeing. Research and scholarship • Sustain and grow research and scholarship infrastructure across education, general medicine, and hospital medicine, including strategic recruitment. • Foster scholarship collaborations across sections, Divisions, and Departments, supporting the Departmental goal of advancing IUSM's national NIH funding position. Faculty development and culture • Create dedicated pathways and supportive infrastructure for faculty advancement in teaching, clinical excellence, leadership, quality improvement, scholarship, and research at every site. • Advance clinician wellbeing as an explicit division priority. • Develop a centralized, equitable process for academic recruitment across sites. • Retain and grow collegiality, community, and connection among sections, divisions, and the school. title: Assistant/Associate/Full Professor of Clinical Pediatrics
description: The Division of Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine in the Department of Pediatrics at Indiana University School of Medicine is seeking to add a clinical track faculty physician to provide patient care and serve as a clinician educator. There is a new large pediatric clinical research center, a new pediatric outpatient center dedicated to general pediatrics and neurodevelopment related divisions in pediatrics, genetics, and psychiatry. title: Postdoctoral Fellow in Functional Genomics and Human Disease Mechanisms
description: The Department of Medical and Molecular Genetics at Indiana University School of Medicine is seeking a highly motivated and creative Postdoctoral Fellow in Functional Genomics and Human Disease Mechanisms to join the Azaiez-Booth Laboratory in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our laboratory uses human genetics and functional genomics to understand how disruption of genes, transcripts, and regulatory elements produces human disease. A central goal of the laboratory is to move beyond genetic association or variant annotation to experimentally determine the molecular and cellular consequences of disease-associated genomic variation. The successful candidate will lead mechanistic studies investigating genes and regulatory loci implicated through human genomic analyses. One major area of investigation involves long noncoding RNAs and regulatory genomic regions disrupted by structural variation, although the position is intentionally broader than lncRNA biology. The fellow will have opportunities to pursue diverse projects in which human genetic discoveries create compelling biological questions that require experimental investigation. This position is particularly well suited for a scientist interested in mechanistic biology, developmental or cellular genetics, and translating human genomic findings into experimentally testable models. Research Opportunities Projects may include: · Functional characterization of disease-associated genes, noncoding transcripts, and regulatory elements. · Investigation of structural variants that alter gene regulation or disrupt noncoding genomic loci. · Development of cellular models for studying candidate disease mechanisms. · CRISPR/Cas-mediated genetic perturbation and genome engineering. · Gene-expression and regulatory studies. · Transcriptomic and other genomic approaches for defining downstream consequences of genetic perturbation. · Mechanistic investigation of genes emerging from human gene-discovery studies. · Functional follow-up of candidate disease genes requiring additional experimental evidence. · Integration of molecular and cellular findings with human genetic and phenotypic data. A particular strength of this position will be the opportunity to work across both deep mechanistic projects and focused functional studies arising from ongoing gene-discovery efforts. This structure allows the fellow to develop a major hypothesis-driven research direction while also contributing to shorter, high-value projects that can rapidly generate biological insight. This work will include in vivo studies using mouse models along with cell- and molecular-based assays. Prior animal research experience is preferred but not required; however, candidates must be willing to work with mice and to learn the animal-handling and experimental procedures necessary for their projects. Training and Career Development Postdoctoral fellows will receive close mentorship while being encouraged to develop increasing scientific independence. Training will emphasize formulation of research questions, rigorous experimental design, manuscript preparation, scientific presentation, fellowship and grant writing, mentoring of junior researchers, and development of an independent research program. The fellow will have opportunities to collaborate broadly with investigators in human genetics, clinical genetics, genomics, molecular biology, and related disciplines across Indiana University School of Medicine and collaborating institutions. We especially encourage applicants who want to build a research career connecting human genomic discovery with experimental disease biology. Fellows will be supported in developing independent questions and preliminary data that can form the basis for future fellowship, career-development, and independent research applications. IU School of Medicine is committed to being a welcoming campus community, and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health and well-being throughout the state of Indiana. title: Postdoctoral Fellow in Auditory Genetics and In Vivo Functional Genomics
description: The Department of Medical and Molecular Genetics at Indiana University School of Medicine is seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Fellow in Auditory Genetics and In Vivo Functional Genomics to join the Azaiez-Booth Laboratory in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our laboratory investigates the genetic and molecular mechanisms underlying human disease, with a major research program focused on genetic hearing loss and the functional biology of the auditory system. We integrate human genetics with molecular biology, genome editing, functional genomics, and in vivo disease modeling to determine how genetic perturbations alter auditory function and to identify opportunities for therapeutic intervention. The successful candidate will play a central role in expanding the laboratory's in vivo auditory genetics program. This position is particularly well suited for a scientist interested in connecting human genetic discoveries to organismal phenotypes through mouse models, auditory physiology, molecular analysis, and experimental manipulation of the inner ear. Current and developing projects include functional characterization of genes associated with hearing loss, rapid generation of somatic CRISPR-based models, characterization of genetically engineered disease models, and development of in vivo approaches for manipulating gene activity within the auditory system. These studies provide opportunities to investigate fundamental mechanisms of auditory biology while also developing experimental platforms with translational and therapeutic applications. Research Opportunities The successful candidate will have opportunities to participate in and lead studies involving: · Generation and characterization of mouse models of genetic hearing loss. · Somatic CRISPR/Cas genome editing and in vivo functional genomics. · Auditory phenotyping, including auditory brainstem response and otoacoustic-emission measurements. · Inner-ear tissue collection, histology, immunofluorescence, and quantitative imaging. · Cochlear and inner-ear experimental approaches. · Molecular characterization of genetically perturbed auditory tissues. · Investigation of mechanisms connecting genetic perturbation with auditory and vestibular dysfunction. · Development and evaluation of therapeutic approaches, including gene-regulatory and gene-based strategies. · Integration of experimental findings with human genetic and clinical data. The laboratory is particularly interested in developing rapid and scalable strategies for testing gene function in vivo, allowing human genetic observations to be translated efficiently into experimentally testable hypotheses. Training and Career Development The Azaiez-Booth Laboratory provides a collaborative training environment designed to help postdoctoral fellows develop both technical expertise and scientific independence. Fellows will receive mentorship in experimental design, auditory and genetic approaches, manuscript preparation, scientific communication, fellowship and grant writing, mentoring, and career development. The successful candidate will be encouraged to develop an independent scientific niche within the laboratory's broader program in auditory genetics and functional genomics. Postdoctoral fellows will have opportunities to lead projects, establish collaborations, present research at national and international meetings, contribute to grant applications, and pursue individual fellowship or career-development funding. Indiana University School of Medicine provides a particularly strong environment for this work, with extensive expertise in human genetics, genomics, neuroscience, otolaryngology, auditory biology, genome editing, and translational medicine. title: Postdoctoral Fellow in Experimental Functional Genomics and Molecular Genetics
description: Postdoctoral Fellow in Experimental Functional Genomics and Molecular Genetics The Department of Medical and Molecular Genetics at Indiana University School of Medicine is seeking a highly motivated and creative Postdoctoral Fellow in Experimental Functional Genomics and Molecular Genetics to join the Azaiez-Booth Laboratory in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our laboratory studies how genetic variation causes human disease and develops experimental approaches to move from genetic discovery to biological mechanism. Research in the laboratory sits at the intersection of human genetics, molecular genetics, functional genomics, and precision genomic medicine, with particular interests in genetic hearing loss, RNA biology, variant interpretation, and the development of scalable functional assays. The successful candidate will take a leading role in our experimental functional genomics program, with opportunities to develop both high-throughput and gene-specific approaches for determining the functional consequences of human genetic variation. Current and developing projects include massively parallel splicing assays, functional characterization of coding and noncoding variants, development of new experimental strategies for genes that are poorly suited to existing assays, and mechanistic follow-up of candidate variants and genes emerging from human genomic studies. A major emphasis of this position is experimental problem solving and assay development. We are particularly interested in candidates with strong hands-on molecular biology skills who enjoy designing experiments, troubleshooting technically challenging systems, and developing new approaches. Expertise in one specific technology is less important than a strong experimental foundation and the ability to take a biological question from initial hypothesis through assay development, data generation, interpretation, and publication. Research Opportunities Depending on the project, projects may involve: · Development and implementation of high-throughput functional genomics assays. · Experimental characterization of variants affecting RNA splicing, gene expression, or protein function. · Massively parallel and sequencing-based functional assays. · Development of gene-specific assays for variants that cannot be adequately evaluated using existing platforms. · Molecular cloning, genome editing, cell-based functional studies, and quantitative molecular assays. · Integration of functional data with human genetic and clinical observations. · Mechanistic follow-up of genes and variants identified through human genomic studies. · Development of new experimental platforms that can be expanded into independent research directions. The fellow will be encouraged to develop scientific questions that complement the laboratory's broader research program while establishing an increasingly independent area of expertise. Training and Career Development The Azaiez-Booth Laboratory is committed to helping postdoctoral fellows develop the scientific independence necessary for their next career stage. Fellows will receive mentorship in experimental design, manuscript preparation, scientific communication, grant and fellowship writing, mentoring junior trainees, and development of an independent research program. Postdoctoral fellows will be expected to lead research projects, contribute substantially to manuscripts and collaborative studies, present their work at scientific meetings, and participate in the preparation of fellowship and research grant applications. Fellows will also have opportunities to collaborate with investigators in human genetics, genomics, clinical genetics, hearing research, and other disciplines across Indiana University School of Medicine and collaborating institutions. We especially encourage applications from scientists who are interested in building a research program at the interface of human genetics and experimental biology and who want to develop new approaches for translating genetic observations into biological insight. title: Post Doctoral Appointee
description: An NIH-funded postdoctoral position is available immediately in the laboratory of Dr. Laura Snell at the Indiana University School of Medicine in Indianapolis, Indiana. Nat Immunol. 2021) and use mouse models and cutting-edge technologies to examine the mechanisms by which CD4 T cells accelerate the clearance of chronic viral infections and tumors. description: The Department of Psychology at Indiana University South Bend is seeking to fill the position of Lecturer in Psychology. The candidate must be able and willing to teach Introductory Psychology and undergraduate courses related to methodology (e.g., research methods, statistics, non-experimental design, and APA style writing.) The area of specialization is open. The teaching load is the equivalent of 12 credit hours of undergraduate coursework each semester (fall and spring). Summer teaching is voluntary and compensated separately. Lecturers are expected to participate in service activities to the department, school, campus, or community, such as regularly attending and participating in faculty meetings and serving on relevant committees. This position does not carry expectations for a research program or publications. The Psychology Department at IU South Bend offers a BA degree. The departmental mission balances traditional and innovative approaches while merging technical skills with conceptual and critical understanding. We educate students about the power of psychology to inform and affect society. title: Open Rank Lecturer positions, Kelley School of Business (Communication Skills)
department: IU Bloomington Communication, Professional, and Computer Skills
description: The Kelley School of Business at Indiana University Bloomington (IUB) invites applications for full-time, open-rank Lecturer positions in Communication Skills beginning Fall 2027. These are 10-month, non-tenure-track appointments with an 18-credit-hour annual teaching assignment. Communication Skills faculty teach core undergraduate courses in business writing and business presentations. The curriculum emphasizes audience, purpose, rhetorical situation, and the effective use of written and oral genres in professional contexts. Faculty typically have a primary assignment in either Business Writing or Business Presentations, with the possibility of teaching both. Communication Skills Courses Business Presentations (3 credits) Business Presentations introduces students to oral communication in professional contexts through theory-based skill development. Students learn to analyze audiences, construct and deliver persuasive messages, develop oral arguments, and work effectively in teams. The course includes a team persuasive presentation addressing a real problem for a corporate client. Business Writing (3 credits) Business Writing develops students' ability to produce strategic, ethical, audience-centered professional documents individually and in teams. Students analyze communication situations, make rhetorical choices across business genres, and develop recommendations for authentic professional problems. The course includes a team-based report for a corporate client. The Faculty Role Lecturers have both teaching and service obligations including curriculum development, pedagogical development and service to the Communication, Professional, and Computer Skills (CPCS) academic area, the Kelley School, Indiana University, and the broader community. Annual professional development funding is available for activities including conference travel, purchasing books, and research. These positions are based at the IUB campus in Bloomington, Indiana. Faculty members are expected to work on campus to fully engage with the area, school, campus, and community. About Kelley CPCS Communication, Professional, and Computer Skills (CPCS) is an integral part of the Kelley undergraduate curriculum. With more than 60 faculty, CPCS brings together instructors from a range of academic and professional backgrounds who teach courses in communication, career and professional development, and computer skills. All Kelley undergraduates complete courses offered by CPCS. CPCS faculty develop their own course materials while coordinating with colleagues teaching the same courses, providing both individual responsibility for the classroom and opportunities for curricular collaboration. Indiana University Bloomington, IU’s flagship campus, serves more than 47,000 students in a vibrant college town, while Kelley undergraduates bring strong academic and professional engagement from across the U.S. and around the world. Application Information Interested applicants should review the position requirements and apply at https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/34552 . Questions may be directed to Rachel Landis, Search and Selection Committee Chair, landisr@iu.edu. To ensure consideration, applications should be submitted by January 1, 2027. The search committee will continue reviewing applications until the positions are filled. References will be requested later in the process. title: Associate or Full Professor in Convergent Biology and Biomedical Engineering
department: IU Indianapolis Department of Biomedical Engineering and Informatics – Luddy School
description: The Indiana University (IU) School of Science and the Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering at IU Indianapolis invite applications for a tenured Associate or Full Professor position whose research operates at the intersection of biology and biomedical engineering. This position is a strategic joint hire aligned with the Convergent Bioscience and Technology Institute (CBATI) and is intended to strengthen and expand interdisciplinary research capacity across biology, biomedical engineering, and translational biosciences. Strategic Research Areas of Interest Priority consideration will be given to candidates whose research programs align with one or more of the following areas: - Bacterial pathogenesis and antibiotic resistance, including microbiology, immune engineering, and host–pathogen interactions - Biohybrid and bioinspired materials and biological–synthetic interfaces - Bio-machining, bio-manufacturing, and biofabrication, including bioprinting and scalable living systems - Regenerative biology and regenerative medicine with translational relevance Role within the Convergent Bioscience and Technology Institute (CBATI) The Convergent Bioscience and Technology Institute (CBATI) drives interdisciplinary bioscience and technology research and collaboration with industry partners in pursuit of discoveries ranging from wearable and implantable medical devices and sensors to the advanced detection of biomarkers and AI-enabled drug discovery and delivery. With a goal of quickly delivering IU health and sciences innovations from the bench to bedside, the institute will aim to stimulate substantial growth in the disclosure and licensing of inventions, discoveries and innovations, as well as industry partnerships and IU-launched startup companies. This position is affiliated with the Convergent Bioscience and Technology Institute (CBATI), IU Indianapolis’ institute dedicated to advancing convergent bioscience and technology research. Faculty affiliated with CBATI are expected to participate actively in interdisciplinary research efforts and collaborative proposal development. IU has also recently broken ground on the Launch Accelerator for Biosciences (IU LAB) - a first-of-its kind academic-industry initiative to harness Indiana's extensive resources in bioscience discovery, leading to significant advancements in human health. Supported by a $138 million Lilly Endowment Inc. grant, IU LAB acts as the hub between industry and academia, positioning Indiana and the greater Indianapolis region as an international leader for biosciences research and innovation. IU LAB is expected to open in the 16 Tech Innovation District in 2027. The successful candidate will have opportunities to contribute to shaping collaborative research themes, support interdisciplinary training and mentoring, and engage with translational and industry-facing initiatives through CBATI and IU LAB, consistent with their interests and experience. Application Process Open until filled. Application materials include: Curriculum Vitae Cover Letter Statement of Research Statement of Teaching List of References About the Indiana University Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering – Indianapolis The Indiana University Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering is the first completely new school in the United States devoted exclusively to Informatics and a range of its subdisciplines. With its formative national role in creating the nation’s largest Informatics Program on the Bloomington and Indianapolis campuses, the school is the broadest and one of the largest information/computing schools in the U.S. At IU Indianapolis, the school also has strong ties with the health and life sciences in the areas of health data exchange, clinical decision support, consumer health informatics, integrated health information systems, and interactive health information technologies. The school provides state-of-the-art facilities including fully equipped classrooms, media and gaming labs, human–computer interaction research labs, usability and mobile development labs, ample research facilities, and studios for sound design and interactive media production. Access to advanced, high-resolution wall-sized displays and virtual environments are also available within the Informatics and Communications Technology Complex. The school has formed key research partnerships with the IU School of Medicine and the Regenstrief Institute, an internationally recognized medical informatics research center. The school also enjoys collaborations with the Roudebush VA Medical Center, IU Health (one of the largest health care organizations in the Midwest), the IU Schools of Nursing, Public Health, Health and Human Sciences, and School of Science. Luddy School faculty have access to state-of-the art computing resources. IU’s Quartz supercomputer, Big Red 200 is among the world’s fastest research supercomputers. Owned and operated solely by IU, these high-performance resources are designed to accelerate discovery in a wide variety of fields, including biomedicine, biotechnology, health care, and enable effective analysis of large, complex biomedical data sets (i.e., big data). About the Indiana University School of Science The School of Science is home to six departments and two interdisciplinary academic programs that serve over 2000 students. Each of the six departments hosts thriving PhD and research programs. The Department of Biology has 25 full-time faculty members, over 750 undergraduate majors, and approximately 60 graduate students enrolled in Ph.D. and M.S. programs. The Department of Biology has a strong record of externally funded research, well-equipped research laboratories and several core facilities. With an extensive hospital system and the IU School of Medicine, IU Indianapolis is home to a large and vibrant community of researchers and collaborators in all areas of biomedical science. Consistent with our health and life science focus, many faculty in the department have strong connections with the IU School of Medicine ( Indiana University School of Medicine (iu.edu) ) on the same campus, and pursue strong, externally funded, programmatic research. About Indiana University Indianapolis The IU Indianapolis campus, with over 21,000 students, is located adjacent to downtown Indianapolis. IU Indianapolis is the health and life science campus of Indiana University, the focal point of health profession education in the State of Indiana. IU Indianapolis offers a full range of academic programs, and is an academic leader in the development and use of information technology. IU Indianapolis shares a campus with the Indiana University School of Medicine, the largest medical school in the US. IU Indianapolis is an eight-time recipient of the Higher Education Excellence in Diversity Award by Insight into Diversity. IU Indianapolis is a campus renowned for service learning, civic engagement, and health sciences research. About Indianapolis Indianapolis is the nation’s 16th largest city, the capital of Indiana, home to the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, the NCAA, the Indianapolis Colts and Indiana Pacers, Indiana Repertory Theatre, Indianapolis Symphony, Indianapolis Ballet, Indianapolis Museum of Art, Indianapolis Zoo and one of the country’s most livable big cities. Indiana is entering a new era of dynamic growth led by the biosciences, manufacturing, artificial intelligence, healthcare and hospitality industries. Just last year, Indiana’s biosciences sector generated over $99 billion in economic activity, while its hospitality industry welcomed 30 million visitors who contributed $5.8 billion of economic impact. Indianapolis is a significant biotech hub, anchored by global giants like Eli Lilly and Roche, alongside numerous other major players like Elanco, AstraZeneca, Merck, and Sanofi, plus specialized firms such as Zimmer Biomet, INCOG BioPharma, Genezen Labs, and Beckman Coulter, making it a strong center for pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, and life sciences. To learn more about Indianapolis, see any of the following websites: IndyParks , with over 150 parks in and around the city Local Government & Neighborhoods Downtown Indianapolis Tourism Indianapolis Monthly’s “Best of Indy” Carmel, Indiana , rated the #1 Best Place to Live in the U.S.

title: Open Rank Clinical positions, Kelley School of Business (Operations and Decision Technologies, Information Systems)
department: IU Bloomington Operations and Decision Technologies
description: The Operations and Decision Technologies (ODT) Department of the Kelley School of Business at Indiana University – Bloomington invites applications for an open-rank, non-tenure-track clinical faculty position in Information Systems (IS) beginning in Fall 2027. The ODT Department consists of the Information Systems, Operations Management, and Decision Sciences groups and offers IS programs at the Undergraduate, Master's, and Doctoral levels. The Kelley undergraduate program in Information Systems is ranked #6 , and our graduate programs in IS are ranked #8 by US News & World Report. Clinical faculty play a critical role in the dept and School’s success. We offer opportunities to advance through the ranks, and clinical faculty are eligible for leadership roles within the School and the University.

title: Assistant Research Professor in Biostatistics and Health Data Science
description: Faculty position in biostatistics, health data science, and informatics areas available in the Department of Biostatistics and Health Data Science (BHDS), associated with the Indiana University School of Medicine and Fairbanks School of Public Health on the Indianapolis campus. Position level is Assistant Research Professor/Non-Tenure track. This is an exciting opportunity to join a fast growing BHDS Department with 36 faculty members and more than 50 professional staff. We are dedicated to excellence in biostatistical, health data science, and informatics research and education. We have an extensive portfolio of research program in related areas. Our NIH funding as principal investigators and co-investigators has been ranked among the top in the nation. The Department currently has an ongoing PhD program in Biostatistics, MS program in Biostatistics, and BS program in Health Data Science. We have established strong collaborations with both clinical and basic science research departments and divisions and health systems including IU Health and Eskenazi Hospitals as well as strong partnerships with major research institutes and centers including Regenstrief Institute, Center for Computational Biology and Bioinformatics, Indiana Clinical and Translational Science Institute (CTSI), Indiana University Simon Comprehensive Cancer Center, Indiana Institute of Biomedical Research, and Indiana Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center. Additional details about the Department and the PhD program are available on our web page: https://medicine.iu.edu/biostatistics. The position will focus on biomedical informatics, multimodal artificial intelligence, medical imaging, biomedical data modeling, and software/data engineering for large collaborative biomedical research programs. The successful candidate will participate in interdisciplinary research involving multimodal biomedical data integration, medical imaging, graph-based and AI modeling, biomedical informatics, and development of research software and data platforms. The position is expected to contribute to large collaborative federally funded research programs and to work closely with investigators across biomedical, clinical, and data science disciplines. The Indianapolis Campus is the focal point of health professions education at Indiana University, and the School of Medicine is the country’s second largest allopathic medical school. Indianapolis consistently ranks high nationally on many of the “best places to live” lists and has an economy that is growing in the life sciences arena. In addition, it has always been one of the cities with the lowest cost of living. Carmel, Indy’s northern neighbor, was recently named as the best mid-sized city in the country. IUSM is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana. Indianapolis is the capital and most populous city in the State of Indiana. It is growing economically thanks to a strong corporate base anchored by the life sciences. Indiana is home to one of the largest concentrations of health sciences companies in the nation. Indianapolis has a sophisticated blend of charm and culture with a wonderful balance of business and leisure. The growing residential base is supported by rich amenities and quality of life – the city possesses a variety of professional sports, arts venues and outdoor recreation areas. Residents of this dynamic city, and surrounding suburbs, enjoy leading educational systems and top-ranked universities, paired with a diverse population. Indianapolis International Airport is a top-ranked international airport, being named “Best Airport in North America” by Airports Council International for many years. For additional information on life in Indy: https://faculty.medicine.iu.edu/relocation The search will continue until the positions are filled.

title: Lecturer in Human Biology
description: The Human Biology Program in the College of Arts and Sciences https://humanbio.indiana.edu at Indiana University invites applications for a permanent full-time 10-month non-tenure-track position at the level of Lecturer. We seek applicants with expertise in microbiomes, evolutionary medicine and comparative approaches, human-wildlife interactions and One Health, and/or environmental health and health disparities and a record of excellence in teaching at the undergraduate level. Although non-tenure track, the position has a promotion track from Lecturer to Senior Lecturer to Teaching Professor. Teaching responsibilities will be in the Human Biology Program with three courses taught per semester. Some of these courses will assist with growing experiential learning opportunities, including internships, undergraduate research, and establishing a new lab classroom, while others will cover our B200, B300, and/or B400 core courses. Applicants should apply online at https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/34517 The IU Human Biology Program is a rapidly growing academic unit with almost 1000 students that offers BS, BA, and minor degrees. It is one of the largest and fastest growing majors on campus. Much of this success is due to IU Human Biology’s innovative educational practices, including interdisciplinary team teaching and active student research, that promote a holistic approach to scientific issues as they relate to the biology of humans. Current faculty within the program share appointments with numerous academic departments across the College of Arts and Sciences, including Anthropology, Biology, Geography, History and Philosophy of Science and Medicine, and Psychological and Brain Sciences. We encourage applicants from these disciplines and adjacent fields to apply. Please submit (1) a cover letter describing your educational background, research and teaching experience and current interests, and reasons for interest in the position; (2) curriculum vitae; (3) a statement of teaching philosophy including evidence of teaching ability, and (4) the names and contact information for three letters of recommendation. Questions about the position should be addressed to the Human Biology Program ( HUBIadm@iu.edu ) and the IU Human Biology Program Director, Dr. Michael Wasserman (mdwasser@iu.edu). Review of applications will begin Oct. 19. The search will remain open until the position is filled. title: Postdoctoral Fellow - – Health Equity, Health Disparities, and Community-Engaged Research
description: The Indiana University School of Nursing seeks a highly motivated Postdoctoral Fellow to join the Center for Enhancing Quality of Life in Chronic Illness (CEQL). The fellow will work under the mentorship of Dr. Amy Knopf, an established nurse scientist whose research focuses on health equity, health disparities, social determinants of health, bioethics, and clinical trial access. This fellowship is designed to support the development of an early-career nurse scientist pursuing an independent program of research focused on health equity, health disparities, ethics, and/or population health. The fellow will engage in ongoing research projects while receiving individualized mentorship in research design, data analysis, scientific writing, grantsmanship, community engagement, and academic career development. The Center for Enhancing Quality of Life in Chronic Illness (CEQL) is dedicated to advancing research that improves the quality of life of individuals living with chronic illness. CEQL fosters interdisciplinary collaboration, mentorship, and innovation to address complex health challenges through rigorous scientific inquiry, implementation science, and community engagement. The fellowship provides an opportunity to collaborate with interdisciplinary researchers, community organizations, health systems, and policy partners across Indiana University and beyond while contributing to innovative research that addresses health disparities and promotes equitable health outcomes. Research Focus Areas • Health equity and health disparities • Social determinants of health • Community-engaged and participatory research • Ethics • Clinical trial access, enrollment, and retention • Policy Primary Responsibilities of the Fellow • Develop an individualized career development plan leading toward research independence and external funding. • Conduct independent and collaborative research activities. • Work with faculty mentor on ongoing projects, including: study design, implementation, data collection, and analysis. • Prepare manuscripts for submission to peer-reviewed journals. • Present research at IU School of Nursing Research Forums and at regional and national professional conferences.

title: Assistant Professor of Pediatrics
description: The Herman B Wells Center for Pediatric Research conducts basic science and translational research within the Department of Pediatrics at Indiana University School of Medicine. The Wells Center houses more than 200 faculty investigators, staff, and trainees seeking answers to the most pressing questions related to childhood illness. With the collaboration between scientists and physicians, the center aims to increase knowledge of causes and mechanisms of serious pediatric diseases. Our goal is to develop innovative approaches to the diagnosis and treatment of sick children in Indiana and beyond. The Pediatric Cardiac Developmental Biology Research group in the Herman B Wells Center at Indiana University School of Medicine in Indianapolis is accepting applications for tenure-track faculty positions at the Assistant Professor rank. Scientific focus should be on Cardiac development, congenital heart disease and/or IPS related cardiac models of differentiation/ cell regeneration. Employment of zebrafish and mouse models is also considered a strength. The scientific environment at the School of Medicine and in Herman B Wells Center for Pediatric Research is highly interactive and collegial with and includes interactions with clinician in the Department of Pediatrics. Further interactions on campus include other Basic Science and Clinical Departments, as well as Research Centers and Institutes. IUSM is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Radiology, Pediatric Neuroradiology, Indianapolis
description: INDIANA UNIVERSITY SCHOOL OF MEDICINE DEPARTMENT OF RADIOLOGY AND IMAGING SCIENCES Indiana University Health PEDIATRIC NEURORADIOLOGIST FACULTY POSITION • PEDIATRIC NEURORADIOLOGY • INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA This position is eligible for a signing bonus of up to $100,000! The Indiana University School of Medicine Department of Radiology and Imaging Sciences invites applications for a fellowship-trained Pediatric Neuroradiologist to join the Pediatric Neuroradiology Division, at Riley Hospital for Children. This is an opportunity to practice the full spectrum of pediatric diagnostic neuroradiology at one of the nation’s premier academic medical centers, with provision to balance clinical and academic time. The position may be at the assistant, associate, or full professor level based on experience, with both tenured and non-tenure track appointments available. Practice Highlights • Pediatric neuroradiology coverage is based at Riley Hospital for Children in Indianapolis, ranked among the top children’s hospitals in the nation. • Daytime position with approximately one remote evening shift per week and no overnight call responsibilities. • Work-from-home opportunities shared among the Pediatric Neuroradiology team, in addition to on-site assignments. • Opportunities for cross-division appointment (i.e. Pediatric Radiology, Adult Neuroradiology, Nuclear Medicine, etc). • Work alongside nationally recognized experts in Neuroradiology, supported by a robust residency, a neuroradiology fellowship program, and a highly supportive, well-funded imaging sciences research program. Why IU? • Interpret all diagnostic pediatric neuroradiology imaging studies on a collegial and growing team. • Participate in multidisciplinary tumor boards and specialty conferences, collaborating closely with referring clinicians. • Be a part of the largest medical school in the nation. • New medical school campus and research buildings opened in downtown Indianapolis in 2025. • Practice at Riley Hospital for Children at IU Health, Indiana’s only nationally ranked children’s hospital and one of only 21 in the country ranked by US News & World Report in all 11 pediatric specialties. • Our department ranked 1st among Big Ten schools and 13th nationally in overall NIH funding by the Academy for Radiology & Biomedical Imaging Research in 2024. • Collaborate with the newly established departmental Medical Imaging Research Institute (MIRI), including the Cancer Imaging and Theranostics Research Center, Research Imaging Core, and state-of-the-art PET/CT, PET/MR, and preclinical imaging infrastructure. • Benefit from a strong dual-employment partnership between IU School of Medicine and IU Health, which provides access to the latest research, training, clinical care, and educational opportunities. Compensation & Benefits • Total compensation (salary + benefits) is estimated between $610,000-$650,000 depending on academic rank, with ample opportunities for supplemental income. • This position is eligible for a signing bonus of up to $100,000. • Balanced scheduling that supports personal well-being: daytime coverage with around one evening per week and no overnight call. • Flexible work model with both on-site and shared work-from-home reading opportunities. • Comprehensive benefits package through Indiana University, one of the state’s largest employers. • Dual-employment offers unique investment opportunities (401(k) plus 457(b) and 403(b), dual Roth contributions, HSA rollover). • Tuition benefit for dependent students attending Indiana University. • Relocation assistance and dual-career support. Vibrant City, Exceptional Suburbs Indianapolis offers a thriving downtown and family-friendly suburbs. Many faculty choose to live in Carmel, Zionsville, and Fishers, which are frequently ranked among the best places to live nationally. The region combines top-rated public and private schools, affordable housing, and cultural amenities with a strong life sciences economy. For additional information on life in Indy, please visit click here. RESPONSIBILITIES • Provide high-quality clinical interpretation of the full spectrum of pediatric diagnostic neuroradiology studies at Riley Hospital for Children and coverage of multiple in-state hospitals and imaging facilities. • Participate in multidisciplinary tumor boards and specialty conferences and contribute to educational initiatives across the department and Academic Health Center. • Teach and mentor medical students, residents, and fellows in a supportive academic environment. • Engage in scholarly activity, quality improvement, and faculty development opportunities aligned with the department’s four missions—clinical, research, education, and culture. HOW TO APPLY • Please see the online application: HERE • Interested candidates should submit a letter of interest, current CV, and references in PDF format. • For questions regarding the position and application process, please contact Dr. Brian Graner. • For more information regarding our institution, please see the department, division, and IU School of Medicine websites. title: Postdoctoral Fellow in Ophthalmology
description: The Eugene and Marilyn Glick Eye Institute at the Indiana University School of Medicine invites applications for a Postdoctoral Fellowship position in the Department of Ophthalmology. Our research focus is retinal cell biology with the goal of understanding the fundamental processes of vision and discovering small molecule therapy for photoreceptor degenerative disorders. To elucidate the disease mechanisms, we genetically dissect the molecular mechanisms underlying photoreceptor morphogenesis and maintenance in vertebrate animals. Our laboratory pioneered real-time imaging of proteins and small molecules within the retina and takes advantage of state of the art confocal/super resolution microscopy techniques. Our research also heavily depends on the tissue culture system to biochemically study the components required for photoreceptor morphogenesis/maintenance. The applicant is expected to be highly independent and be capable of designing experiments and conducting hypothesis-based research projects. The candidate is expected to be familiar with basic laboratory operations and proper documentation of experimental records. The candidate should have a strong background in cell biology, molecular biology, or biochemistry. Knowledge of fluorescence microscopy is favorable, although not necessary. The Glick Eye Institute is located on the IU School of Medicine campus in downtown Indianapolis. IU School of Medicine is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. Salary will be commensurate with experience and will adhere to current Indiana University School of Medicine guidelines. Applicants should submit a cover letter summarizing their relevant qualifications, and a copy of their curriculum vitae.

title: Open Rank, Tenured/Tenure-Track Faculty Position in Robotics
department: IU Bloomington Vice Provost For Faculty Affairs
description: Indiana University Bloomington (IUB) invites applications for a tenured/tenure-track assistant, associate, or full professor in the Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering, in the field of robotics. We seek exceptional researchers and educators whose work advances the science and engineering of intelligent, embodied systems and their societal applications. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to significantly contribute to the new Bachelor of Science in Robotics degree, shaping the next generation of roboticists through research-driven teaching and mentoring. We welcome applicants whose research advances human-centered robotics and human–robot interaction. We are particularly interested in scholarship in these areas addressing one or more of three interconnected themes: Interaction and collaboration: physical, haptic, and multimodal interaction; human–robot teaming; shared autonomy; and the design and study of interactive robotic systems. Embodied intelligence and mobility: robot design and control, humanoid robotics, whole-body control, and wearable robotic systems. Robotics in human environments: assistive, rehabilitation, healthcare, and field robotics, including the development, deployment, and study of robotic systems in real-world settings. We also welcome applicants whose work bridges these themes or brings complementary perspectives, methods, and application domains that broaden the scope of human-centered robotics at IUB. We encourage applications from scholars who apply interdisciplinary perspectives and share important research overlap with current IUB scholars while also offering new dimensions that will expand and strengthen IUB’s robotics research program . This 10‐month appointment would ideally start August 1, 2027 , although an earlier or later start date is negotiable. Applications received by November 15, 2026 , will receive full consideration, and applications will be accepted until the positions are filled. Responsibilities: Tenured/tenure-track faculty at Indiana University Bloomington are expected to substantially contribute to the overall academic excellence of their department by developing and/or maintaining a robust research portfolio including pursuing and obtaining major extramural research funding to conduct cutting-edge research both as a corresponding principal investigator and a collaborating investigator; teaching and mentoring undergraduate and/or graduate students as designated by the department chairperson; and actively providing service within the department, school and university alongside active engagement with the profession and/or the community. title: Postdoctoral Researcher - SOCIAL
description: Postdoctoral Researcher - Study of Affective Disorders’ Classification and Treatment (SADCAT) Lab Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences at Indiana University Bloomington The SADCAT Lab (PI: Lorenzo Lorenzo-Luaces) at Indiana University Bloomington (IUB) is an interdisciplinary research lab dedicated to advancing our understanding of internalizing disorders —particularly depression and anxiety—and improving their treatment through data-driven, empirically grounded approaches. We are interested in the intersection of technology, mental health, and data science in clinical psychology. The lab is currently supported by an R01 Research Project Grant from the National Institutes of Health (NIH; PIs Lorenzo-Luaces & Bollen), investigating the impact of social media on adolescent mental health. This project aims to clarify the bidirectional relationship between social media use and internalizing symptoms in a longitudinal sample of 1,000 adolescents. Essential Duties The postdoctoral researcher will contribute to ongoing projects examining internalizing disorders, technology, cognitive-behavioral therapies (CBTs), and the personalization of treatment. The main project focuses on adolescents (ages 13–20) and employs a longitudinal design, passive data collections, and ecological momentary assessments (EMA) to capture the dynamic nature of symptoms. The position involves engaging with multi-level datasets and contributing to statistical analyses. The researcher may also contribute to manuscript preparation and help develop new studies that extend the lab’s mission of using data science to advance clinical psychology and improve mental health outcomes. The anticipated start date is Fall 2027. Start date is negotiable. Salary for this position is based on the NIH postdoctoral salary guidelines, with a starting salary of $$63,480.00, commensurate with experience.

title: Postdoctoral Fellow, Biology Landeta Lab
description: The department of Biology is a large, unified department with strong undergraduate degrees, nationally-ranked graduate programs, and world-class research spanning the breadth of biological questions and experimental systems - from ecosystems to microbiology and developmental biology, from evolution to cell biology, from molecular biology to systems biology, bioinformatics, and genomics. It is always an exciting time for Biology - enormous advances in global genome analysis coupled with unprecedented developments in interdisciplinary research have made the 21st century the Century of Biology. For more information about the department, you can find it here: About: Department of Biology: Indiana University Bloomington. Indiana University is an equal opportunity employer and provider of ADA services and prohibits discrimination in hiring. The Landeta Lab in the Department of Biology at Indiana University, Bloomington is seeking a Postdoctoral Fellow. Our department is a large, unified department with world-class research spanning all levels of biological organization and diverse experimental systems. Our lab in Microbiology investigates the processes that take place in the bacterial cell envelope with emphasis into oxidative protein folding. The overarching goal for this position is to make timely progress on our NIH and CFF grants ( https://reporter.nih.gov/search/kpoQKsh8Pkqp4S1_RS1-PQ/project-details/11259946 ), which looks for fundamental insights into novel oxidative reactions, the exported proteins that depend on disulfide bonds, the substrate specificity among thiol-disulfide oxidoreductases and finding novel inhibitors against oxidative folding. We are excited about science and looking for another positive, curious person to join our team. Core topics to work on: (1) In vitro assays to determine inhibitor efficacy against redox membrane proteins (2) Cysteine enrichment of DsbA substrates in E. coli and Mycobacteria using proteomics. (3) determine differences between DsbA proteins of two model organisms, E. coli and M. smegmatis (4) Establishing termini restraining for inhibitor-protein crystallography in collaboration with Prof. Weikai Li. Other general responsibilities include: Supervising undergrads; managing general lab operations; writing up research (e.g. for our annual reports or for manuscripts); presenting findings at lab meetings, microphiles, retreats and conferences; and participating in lab meetings.

department: IU Bloomington Vice Provost For Faculty Affairs
description: Indiana University Bloomington (IUB) invites applications for an open-rank, tenured/tenure-track faculty position in the School of Public Health-Bloomington in the field of Aging and Technology. The position is part of Indiana University's Faculty 100 initiative, a strategic investment in exceptional scholars whose work advances the university's research excellence and national impact. Candidates with special interest in any of the following (or related) areas are encouraged to apply: Wearable & Ambient Sensors: Continuous physiological and behavioral monitoring; fall detection and prediction; dementia care and wandering prevention; activity tracking for chronic disease management. Conversational AI & Social Robotics: Companionship for socially isolated or lonely older adults; medication reminders for adherence; caregiver-facing information and guidance systems. Telehealth & Remote Monitoring: Chronic disease management; specialist access for rural populations; post-acute monitoring to prevent readmissions. Smart Home Technologies: Automated safety systems for dementia patients; environmental controls for mobility-limited adults; passive monitoring without wearables. About the University and the Town: Founded in 1820, Indiana University Bloomington (IUB) is the flagship campus of Indiana University . A member of the prestigious Association of American Universities (AAU) since 1909, IUB is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. The campus serves more than 47,000 undergraduate and graduate students across 16 degree-granting colleges and schools, offering more than 300 undergraduate majors, 300 master’s programs, and 150 doctoral and professional degree opportunities. IUB’s mission is to create, disseminate, preserve, and apply knowledge through cutting-edge research, scholarship, arts, and creative activity; challenging undergraduate, graduate, professional, and lifelong educational programs; meaningful experiences beyond the classroom; and expansive global educational opportunities. The University is also home to first-rate library and museum collections and contributes significantly to economic development and impact throughout Indiana and the region. Known for its Indiana limestone architecture and expansive green spaces, IUB is widely regarded as one of the country’s most beautiful college campuses. The College of Arts and Sciences is at the academic heart of Indiana University Bloomington. The College offers more than 225 academic programs spanning three broad areas: Arts and Humanities, Natural and Mathematical Sciences, and Social and Historical Studies. It is home to more than 70 departments and programs and three schools: the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design; the Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International Studies; and The Media School. More than 900 faculty members contribute to the College’s teaching, research, and creative mission. College faculty are regularly recognized with some of the nation’s and world’s highest academic and professional honors, including election to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, the National Academies, and the American Association for the Advancement of Science, as well as MacArthur and Guggenheim Fellowships, Fulbright Awards, Pulitzer Prizes, Oscars, and Emmys. The position is based in the Department of Biology , a large, unified department within the College of Arts and Sciences. Biology offers strong undergraduate programs, nationally ranked graduate programs, and a broad, collaborative research environment. Research in the department spans biological questions and experimental systems across scales, from ecosystems, evolution, and organismal biology to microbiology, developmental and cell biology, molecular and systems biology, bioinformatics, and genomics. This breadth provides opportunities for interdisciplinary research and collaboration across the department and the broader IUB research community. Located in the rolling hills of south-central Indiana, Bloomington is a vibrant community of approximately 85,000 residents that combines the character of a college town with many of the cultural and recreational amenities of a larger city. The community offers theater, music, and arts events—including the LOTUS World Music & Arts Festival—as well as quick access to approximately 250,000 acres of public recreation lands. With strong public schools and a reasonable cost of living, Bloomington offers an attractive environment in which to live and work.

We seek exceptional researchers and educators whose work advances the theory and practice of cybersecurity to join the Department of Informatics at the Luddy School. We welcome applicants in all areas of cybersecurity but are particularly interested in candidates whose research bridges technical cybersecurity (e.g., systems/network security; applied cryptography; security informatics) and human aspects of cybersecurity (e.g., policy or governance; trusted computing; the design of usable and inclusive security and privacy technologies; security and safety of AI systems; cyber risk management; international cybersecurity policy; law and privacy; and accessible security). Successful applicants will join a collaborative academic campus-wide cybersecurity community spanning Luddy, the O’Neill School of Public Policy, Hamilton-Lugar School of Global and International Studies, Maurer School of Law, Kelley School of Business, Cognitive Science Program, Psychology and Brain Sciences, the Center for Applied Cybersecurity Research (CACR), and the Ostrom Workshop, with opportunities for joint appointments, cross-listed teaching, and interdisciplinary doctoral advising. title: Multiple Tenured Associate or Full Professors in Microelectronics, Circuits, and Systems Design
department: IU Bloomington Vice Provost For Faculty Affairs
description: Indiana University Bloomington (IUB) invites applications for multiple tenured faculty positions at the associate or full professor rank in the Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering, Department of Intelligent Systems Design, in the field of microelectronics, circuits, and system design. We seek candidates who can teach and lead research in one or more of the following areas: analog and mixed-signal integrated circuits; digital VLSI and AI hardware systems; advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration; and power electronics and energy-integrated microsystems . We encourage applications from scholars who apply interdisciplinary perspectives across a variety of these domains and complement existing strengths within the department. We particularly welcome candidates whose work leverages innovative computational techniques and connects microelectronic circuits and systems with computing, AI, sensing, security, radiation effects, healthcare, or other emerging application domains. These 10‐month appointments would ideally start August 1, 2027 , although an earlier or later start date is negotiable. All applications received prior to October 16, 2026, will receive full consideration; applications will continue to be accepted and reviewed until all positions are filled. Candidates with special interest in the following areas are encouraged to apply: Analog and Mixed-Signal Integrated Circuits Key research areas: Low-power analog design; sensor interfaces; data converters (ADC/DAC); RF/mixed-signal integration; power management IC blocks. Digital VLSI and AI Hardware Systems Key research areas: ASIC/FPGA design flows; AI/edge accelerators; hardware–software co-design; modern SoC architectures; verification and architecture exploration. Teaching contributions: VLSI/Digital VLSI; hardware acceleration; capstone integration; design verification and prototyping experiences. Teaching contributions: Heterogeneous Integration & Advanced Packaging; packaging/reliability labs; cross-layer design projects linking devices to systems. Power Electronics and Energy-Integrated Microsystems Key research areas: Power ICs; wide-bandgap (GaN/SiC) integration; efficient power delivery; electrified transportation; energy-aware computing platforms. Teaching contributions: Power Electronics; power conversion labs; energy-constrained system design projects with hardware measurement. About Indiana University Bloomington : Founded in 1820, Indiana University-Bloomington (IUB) is the flagship campus of Indiana University. Known for its Indiana limestone facades and green spaces throughout, our campus is widely considered one of the country’s most beautiful. The College is home to over 70 departments and programs and three schools—the Eskenazi School of Art, Architecture + Design, the Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International Studies, and the Media School. Friendly, safe, affordable and welcoming, Bloomington is a gem set in the beautiful rolling hills of southern Indiana. Bloomington’s geographic position illustrates our state’s nickname “Crossroad of America.” It is within a 1 hour drive of Indianapolis, 2 hour drive of Louisville, KY, 3.5 hour of Columbus, OH, and ~4 hour drive to Chicago, IL, St. Louis, MO, and Nashville, TN. Bloomington has a low cost of living relative to entry-level faculty salaries. The community is home to many thriving affinity groups and offers an exceptional selection of cultural, educational, and recreational opportunities. Learn more here: https://bloomington.iu.edu/campus-life/bloomington.html .

title: Postdoctoral Fellow, Biology Smith Lab
description: The department of Biology is a large, unified department with strong undergraduate degrees, nationally-ranked graduate programs, and world-class research spanning the breadth of biological questions and experimental systems — from ecosystems to microbiology and developmental biology, from evolution to cell biology, from molecular biology to systems biology, bioinformatics, and genomics. It is always an exciting time for Biology — enormous advances in global genome analysis coupled with unprecedented developments in interdisciplinary research have made the 21st century the Century of Biology. For more information about the department, you can find it here: About: Department of Biology: Indiana University Bloomington . The Department of Biology at Indiana University Bloomington invites applications for a post-doctoral research position under the supervision of Dr. Chris Smith Home | Chris Smith . Our lab studies spatial population genetics, using simulation-based inference and machine learning to infer the evolutionary and ecological processes that shape genetic variation. The Postdoctoral Associate will conduct research exploring new inference techniques, applying cutting-edge tools to address biological questions, advancing deep learning models, or other topics discussed with the PI. We use publicly available and simulated genomic data. Core job duties include: (1) Building computational pipelines for simulation experiments and analyzing genomic sequencing data; (2), designing, implementing, and overseeing research projects focused on methods development for understanding genetic variation within and between populations; and (3) writing scientific publications and presenting findings at conferences. Other general responsibilities include: Actively participating in lab meetings and discussions. Education and experience required: Ph.D. in population genetics, computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, or a related field. Demonstrated experience leading computational research projects is required for the proposed research.
