title: Visiting Assistant Professor of Japanese Domestic Politics
department: IU Bloomington East Asian Langs & Cultures
description: Indiana University-Bloomington's Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International Studies seeks applications for a full-time visiting assistant professor (VAP) of Japanese domestic politics to begin January 1, 2027. The position is for up to three consecutive teaching semesters (Spring 2027, Fall 2027, and Spring 2028), subject to campus approval. This non-tenure-track VAP position is based in Indiana University’s renowned multidisciplinary Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures (EALC) and partially funded by the Japan Foundation. The teaching load is two courses per semester—including one course each semester focusing specifically on some aspect of contemporary Japanese politics (broadly defined). Eligible candidates will have a PhD in political science (or related field) in hand before January 1, 2027, and combine disciplinary rigor and area studies expertise to analyze Japan and East Asian politics. Candidates whose research agenda extensively utilizes Japanese-language sources and who demonstrate an interest in contributing to Hamilton Lugar’s 21st Century Japan Politics and Society Initiative (21JPSI) will be particularly competitive. 21JPSI expects to be able to provide the successful candidate with a funded manuscript workshop and a research trip to Japan in summer 2027. This is an exciting moment to join the Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International Studies as it leads Indiana University's international and area studies research and teaching missions. Hamilton Lugar’s EALC department boasts a robust and multidisciplinary Japan studies program, including faculty teaching on cinema, foreign affairs, history, language pedagogy, literature, music, religion, society, and visual culture. It also teaches Japanese language to over 300 students each semester. Established more than sixty years ago, the EALC department has a long history of interdisciplinarity and boasts faculty strengths in a wide array of the humanities and social sciences. The department’s mission related to research and teaching on East Asia is complemented by Hamilton Lugar’s East Asian Studies Center, the Institute of Korean Studies, and 21JPSI. Learn more at https://ealc.indiana.edu/ ; https://hls.indiana.edu/ ; and https://jpsi.indiana.edu/ . Interested applicants should send a cover letter, curriculum vitae, a brief description of four possible course offerings on Japanese and/or East Asian domestic politics (broadly defined), and a list of at least two references who may be contacted about the application. Sample syllabi—especially for a Japanese domestic politics course—are welcome but not required. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled, with all applications received by August 9, 2026 being assured full consideration.

title: Director of Research, Walther Center for Supportive Oncology, Endowed Position
description: Indiana University School of Medicine (IUSM) and the Indiana University Melvin and Bren Simon Comprehensive Cancer Center (IUSCCC) invite applications for a nationally recognized investigator to serve as Director of Research for the Walther Center for Supportive Oncology. This open-rank faculty position offers an exceptional opportunity to shape a growing, endowed, interdisciplinary research program at Indiana's only National Cancer Institute-designated comprehensive cancer center. The Director of Research will help define the next generation of supportive oncology science - research that improves the cancer experience for patients and families from diagnosis through treatment, survivorship, serious illness, and end-of-life care. The successful candidate will join a highly collaborative environment with substantial institutional commitment, endowed-chair support, access to a broad clinical enterprise, and opportunities to integrate research, clinical care, education, and community engagement. Why this opportunity is compelling · Endowed platform: The position is supported by one of five Walther-endowed chairs established to recruit academic leaders in supportive oncology. · Program-building scope: The Director will have a visible leadership role in expanding, integrating, and sustaining supportive oncology research across the cancer center, IUSM, IU Health, and community partners. · Integrated research and care environment: The Walther Center encompasses both research and clinical care, creating opportunities to embed discovery into real-world oncology practice. · Flexible academic home: The primary department and faculty rank will be aligned with the candidate's expertise, credentials, and scholarly discipline. · Clinical flexibility: Opportunities for limited clinical practice may be available for appropriately trained candidates and tailored to expertise and interests. · Statewide and national impact: IUSM, IUSCCC, IU Health, and community partners offer opportunities for team science, implementation, dissemination, and health equity-focused research across a wide variety of populations. Research focus areas We welcome investigators whose work advances supportive oncology across the cancer continuum and across the lifespan including children, adolescents/young adults, and adults. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to: · Psycho-oncology, psychosocial and behavioral oncology, cancer-related distress, resilience, and mental health · Palliative care, symptom science, patient-reported outcomes, communication, decision-making, and serious illness care · Survivorship, cancer and aging, caregiver and family outcomes, sexual health, and quality of life · Integrative oncology, rehabilitation, physical activity, exercise and lifestyle interventions, nutrition, music therapy, and mind-body interventions · Implementation science, dissemination, health services research, digital health, health equity, rural health, and community-engaged research Leadership responsibilities · Set and advance a strategic research vision for the Walther Center for Supportive Oncology in partnership with center and cancer center leadership. · Build collaborative, cross-disciplinary research programs that leverage the strengths of IUSM, IUSCCC, IU Health, and affiliated clinical and community partners. · Grow a high-impact portfolio of peer-reviewed extramural funding, publications, clinical and translational research, and dissemination initiatives. · Mentor faculty, trainees, and research staff; support career development for emerging investigators in supportive oncology. · Strengthen research infrastructure, including team-science models, data resources, patient-reported outcomes, pragmatic trials, and learning health system approaches. · Represent the Walther Center locally and nationally through scholarly leadership, partnerships, and visibility in supportive oncology research communities. About the Walther Center and IU Simon Comprehensive Cancer Center The Walther Center for Supportive Oncology is a major initiative of IUSM and IUSCCC, supported through transformational investment from the Walther Cancer Foundation and developed in partnership with IU Health. The center brings together complementary strengths in palliative care, psycho-oncology, integrative medicine, rehabilitation, symptom management, and survivorship to improve care and outcomes for people with cancer and their families. IUSCCC is Indiana's only NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center and a member of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network. Its investigators conduct basic, clinical, translational, population, and community-engaged research with a mission to reduce cancer mortality and suffering through discovery, education, and patient-centered care. About IU School of Medicine and Indianapolis IUSM is the largest medical school in the United States, with a statewide academic and clinical footprint and a strong record of research funding, education, and partnership. IU Indianapolis is located in the heart of a growing life sciences region with major health care, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and innovation partners. Indianapolis offers the advantages of a major metropolitan area - professional sports, arts and culture, restaurants, trails, parks, festivals, and an accessible international airport - with a cost of living and quality of life that support recruitment and retention. The region includes nationally recognized communities such as Carmel, Fishers, and Noblesville, along with a wide range of urban, suburban, and rural living options. IUSM is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana.

title: Postdoctoral Fellow in Medicine
description: A postdoctoral position is immediately available in the Division of Pulmonary, Critical Care, Sleep, and Occupational Medicine in the Department of Medicine. description: Position Summary The Division of Behavioral, Health, and Life Sciences at Indiana University Columbus invites applications for a full-time, open-rank non-tenure-track faculty position in Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems. The successful candidate will be rank of Lecturer, Senior Lecturer, or Teaching Professor, depending upon qualifications, experience, and the applicable Indiana University and academic-unit criteria. The successful candidate will also receive an initial administrative assignment as Founding Program Director for the proposed B.S. in Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems . The position reports to the Head of the Division of Behavioral, Health and Life Sciences. The proposed 120-credit Bachelor of Science program is designed to prepare students to secure computing systems that monitor or control physical processes. It combines foundations in programming, data structures, operating systems, networks, databases, distributed systems, cloud computing, cryptography, and cybersecurity with required study of embedded and real-time systems, industrial controls, hardware and firmware security, wireless and Internet-of-Things security, operational-technology incident response, security architecture, verification and validation, and system resilience. The program is intended to serve advanced manufacturing, connected products, automotive and engine systems, industrial automation, robotics, material handling, utilities, healthcare technology, logistics, and other critical-infrastructure environments. Hands-on learning will include laboratory-intensive courses, CPS Security Studios, an isolated instructional cyber range, embedded devices, PLC/HMI equipment, industrial protocols, robotics or equivalent CPS platforms, and a two-semester applied capstone. The anticipated Spring 2027 assignment will focus primarily on program finalization, student recruitment, curriculum and course development, laboratory planning, partner engagement, and implementation. The initial semester is not expected to include a regular classroom teaching assignment. Following program launch, teaching will be a central responsibility of the position, accompanied by an administrative course release for program leadership. This is a 10-month academic appointment with a preferred start date of January 1, 2027. Summer program-development and launch responsibilities may be assigned and compensated separately through a summer stipend, subject to approval and available funding. The position is based at IU Columbus and requires regular on-campus presence for program leadership, recruitment, student engagement, laboratory development, and face-to-face classroom and laboratory instruction. Primary Responsibilities Program Development and Implementation Under the direction of the Division Head, the Founding Program Director will: Coordinate final development and implementation of the B.S. in Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems. Lead preparation and coordination of new-course proposals, CARMIn submissions, remonstrance materials, catalog information, and curricular documentation. Coordinate development of course schedules, prerequisite sequences, degree maps, and the staged course rotation. Develop and maintain program assessment processes, curriculum maps, direct-assessment plans, and documentation required for university and state review. Coordinate laboratory and cyber-range planning, including equipment selection, instructional environments, safety and authorized-use expectations, and integration of laboratory resources into the curriculum. Support implementation of the program’s Market Launch Plan, including student recruitment, information sessions, school and career-center outreach, campus visits, and laboratory demonstrations. Coordinate development of advising, transfer, credential, career-pathway, and student-success materials. Assist with future faculty searches and coordinate the contributions of program faculty under the direction of the Division Head. Coordinate program review, annual reporting, and continuing curriculum improvement. Participate, as assigned, in planning and stewardship of externally supported equipment and laboratory resources. Teaching and Student Success The faculty member will: Teach introductory and advanced undergraduate courses supporting the program. Develop and teach laboratory-centered, project-based, and applied learning experiences. Teach introductory programming or information-infrastructure coursework and courses in multiple areas of cybersecurity and cyber-physical systems. Advise and mentor students entering through first-year, transfer, adult, veteran, and technical-career pathways. Support student retention, progression, credential preparation, career exploration, and timely degree completion. Supervise or coordinate studios, applied projects, capstones, internships, or employer-informed learning experiences. Use appropriate in-person, blended, and Canvas-supported instructional practices while maintaining the program’s required face-to-face laboratory experiences. External and Institutional Engagement Under the direction of the Division Head, the faculty member will: Coordinate an employer and education advisory group for the program. Develop productive relationships with employers, school corporations, career and technical education programs, community colleges, community organizations, and professional associations. Support transfer-pathway development and continuing coordination with Ivy Tech Community College and Vincennes University. Coordinate employer-informed projects, guest speakers, facility visits, internships, co-ops, capstone opportunities, mentors, and career activities, subject to partner capacity. Represent the program at recruitment events, professional meetings, community forums, and appropriate university activities. Participate in faculty governance and service appropriate to the appointment. Professional Activity This is a teaching-focused appointment and does not require a traditional disciplinary research agenda. The successful candidate will be expected to maintain professional currency and engage in scholarship or professional activity that supports teaching, curriculum development, applied student learning, industry collaboration, and the mission of IU Columbus. Appointment Contingency This position, the Founding Program Director assignment, and the anticipated January 2027 start date are contingent upon final program approval, continued institutional authorization, and the availability of funding. About Indiana University Columbus Indiana University Columbus offers accessible Indiana University degree programs in Columbus, Indiana, and serves students and communities throughout south-central Indiana. The campus emphasizes student success, career-connected education, community engagement, transfer access, and collaboration with regional employers and education partners. The region provides an especially strong setting for a Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems program because of its concentration of advanced manufacturing, engineering, connected-product development, automation, logistics, healthcare technology, utilities, and other critical-infrastructure activity.

title: Postdoctoral Fellow
description: The Jiang Lab invites applications for a Postdoctoral Researcher position. The postdoctoral researcher will lead independent research projects focused on developing next-generation neurotechnology and biomedical imaging methods, with particular emphasis on optical, ultrasound, and photoacoustic technologies. Working under the supervision of Dr. Ying Jiang, the candidate will contribute to the development of innovative approaches for neural circuit interrogation while collaborating with interdisciplinary research teams and mentoring graduate and undergraduate students. This is an excellent opportunity for early-career scientists looking to develop a strong publication record and build an independent research trajectory within a highly collaborative and well-resourced environment. Responsibilities include designing and conducting experiments, developing and integrating photoacoustic and ultrasound systems, validating technologies in animal models, and performing quantitative data analysis and computational modeling. The researcher will be expected to prepare manuscripts and conference presentations, contribute to grant proposals, help establish new technical capabilities and research directions within the laboratory, and work independently while contributing to a dynamic and collaborative research environment.

description:

The successful candidate will support the development and implementation of advanced ultrasound and photoacoustic systems for biomedical applications while working collaboratively within a dynamic and interdisciplinary research environment. This is an excellent opportunity for individuals seeking to expand their technical expertise in biomedical imaging and neurotechnology while contributing to innovative research with translational impact. Responsibilities may include experimental setup and testing, data acquisition and analysis, programming, instrumentation development, and support of research projects involving cells and other biological systems. title: Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor of Elementary Literacy Education
description: The Indiana University School of Education at Indianapolis is seeking an exemplary Clinical Assistant or Associate Professor faculty member to contribute to our Urban Teacher Education program with teaching and research strengths in literacy education; a commitment to urban education and communities; and a readiness to partner with local schools to provide transformative teacher education. The School of Education at IU Indianapolis is an urban serving institution located in the heart of Indianapolis. Our School of Education has approximately 30 full time faculty all of whom are actively engaged in teaching, scholarship of teaching, and research focused on urban education. Many of our faculty have scholarship interests that focus on partnerships with urban communities and schools and critical perspectives in education. Our Teacher Education program is specifically designed to engage in partnerships with urban schools. For more information, visit our website at: www.education.indianapolis.iu.edu Duties: Design and implement literacy teacher education curriculum that grounds pre-service teachers in deep understanding of science of reading, evidenced-based culturally and contextually responsive pedagogy, human development, and urban communities within strong field-based experiences. Collaborate with faculty in the urban teacher education programs to develop mutually beneficial partnerships with local schools. Lead or assist in ongoing program development, innovation, and evaluation. Engage in the scholarship of teaching. Provide service to School and university committees, professional organizations, and the community. About the Campus IU Indianapolis is a dynamic urban research campus, located in the heart of the state’s capital and largest city. Positioned at the center of a thriving metropolitan region, the campus connects faculty and students with schools, community organizations, healthcare systems, businesses, cultural institutions, and industry partners—creating exceptional opportunities for teaching, research, collaboration, and community impact. Building on more than five decades of achievement in Indianapolis, IU Indianapolis is entering an exciting new era of growth and innovation. For faculty, the campus offers the opportunity to help shape the future of a growing urban research university while preparing students to make a meaningful difference in the communities and professions they serve. With Indianapolis as an extension of the classroom, IU Indianapolis offers the energy and opportunities of a major city alongside the resources and reach of Indiana University. Here, location creates possibility—for experiential learning, interdisciplinary scholarship, community-engaged research, and lasting professional connections.

title: Assistant Librarian
description: Based in Indianapolis, IN, the Ruth Lilly Medical Library seeks a dynamic, collaborative, and talented Liaison Librarian. This position will plan, promote, and provide instruction and information services that support the needs of students, residents, faculty, researchers, and staff at the Indiana University School of Medicine (IU School of Medicine). In addition to serving as liaison to the Terre Haute IU School of Medicine campus, the successful candidate will have an opportunity to develop a specialty area that reflects their interests and expertise while advancing established priorities of the School of Medicine and the Library. This is a tenure-track faculty position reporting to the Associate Director for Public Services. IU School of Medicine is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana. We encourage early-career librarians to apply even if your experience does not cover all preferred qualifications. We appreciate that librarians bring a wide variety of valuable life and work experience. We are committed to working with our colleagues to develop the skills needed to support the mission of IU School of Medicine and the greater librarian community. IU School of Medicine is the nation's largest medical school with nine campuses throughout Indiana. This school is one of the nation’s premier medical schools and is an innovative leader in medical education, research, and clinical care. IU School of Medicine is located in Indianapolis on the Indiana University Indianapolis campus. Indianapolis (fondly known as Indy) is the 16th largest city in the nation, the state capital, and has a cost of living below the national average. Indy has a walkable downtown, an ever-expanding network of bike trails, lots of independent bookstores and coffee shops, and multiple professional sports leagues. RESPONSIBILITIES Liaison Services · Serves as a liaison to the Terre Haute campus. The librarian will be based in Indianapolis but will develop strong relationships with Terre Haute faculty, staff, students, and campus leadership through pre-scheduled campus visits. · Serves as a liaison to departments/groups across our nine-campus statewide system · Contributes to university- and campus-wide initiatives to develop policies, services, and infrastructure to support research services through collaboration with IU School of Medicine faculty and staff. · Provides and contributes to curriculum, course development, training, and workshops for IU School of Medicine students, faculty, and staff. · Provides reference and expert searching services to support research, clinical practice, and medical education. · Conducts literature searches and supports systematic reviews. This may include consultation and instruction related to systematic reviews, scoping reviews, and other forms of evidence synthesis. Collaboration · Participates in a team approach to providing prompt and effective consultation, instructional services, and reference expertise to students, faculty, and staff. · Cultivates partnerships and collaborates with faculty on projects including teaching, grants, manuscripts, papers, or poster presentations. · Contributes to the overall development and innovation of the library and the profession by participating in library, campus, university, state, regional or national meetings, committees, workgroups, and task forces or by representing the library. · Develops a full network of contacts within assigned liaison areas (departments/units, institutes, regional IU School of Medicine campuses, and centers) and anticipates and meets their information needs. · Identifies opportunities for library partnerships within IU School of Medicine and Indiana University at large. · Works with others to develop and revise programs and services to respond to changing information needs. Scholarly/Professional · Maintains current knowledge of the trends and issues in biomedical research, higher education, scholarly communication, artificial intelligence, research practice, and health care. · Pursues an active and ongoing career plan in the areas of job performance, professional development/research, and service. Standards are outlined in the Indiana University - Indianapolis Promotion & Tenure Guidelines: https://provost.indianapolis.iu.edu/Faculty-Affairs-Resources/PT-Process-Timelines · Designs and implements a plan for continuing education, continuing professional development and actively contributes to the development of health sciences librarianship through scholarly and service activities. · Contributes to departmental projects and initiatives as needed to support organizational goals. Participates in other projects and initiatives as assigned.

title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Clinical Radiology, Pediatric Radiology
description: Pediatric Radiologist The Department of Radiology & Imaging Sciences at Indiana University School of Medicine in partnership with Indiana University Health Medical Group is seeking a full-time fellowship trained Pediatric Radiologist to join its pediatric radiology division for a clinical track faculty position to provide care of pediatric patients at Riley Hospital for Children at IU Health in Indianapolis and across the IU Health system and region. Candidates must be certified (or eligible) in Diagnostic Radiology by the American Board of Radiology or its equivalent and must have passed or be eligible for the CAQ examination in Pediatric Radiology. Willingness to join one or more of our subspecialist groups (fetal, cardiac, musculoskeletal, or neuroradiologists) is desired but not required. Benefits include a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, CME, paid ACR membership, a business expense account, and paid malpractice insurance. Indiana University Health Medical Group is a multidisciplinary practice affiliated with Indiana University School of Medicine (IUSM). The Department of Radiology and Imaging Sciences includes approximately 180 clinical faculty, 52 residents, 10 physicists, and 30 research faculty. Riley Hospital for Children is a free-standing tertiary referral center and level one trauma center serving the entire state of Indiana. The Pediatric Division interprets approximately 180,000 examinations annually. Riley Hospital for Children is located in downtown Indianapolis but plays a central role in providing care for children across the state and is one of the top-rated children’s hospitals in the country. Numerous pediatric subspecialties at Riley Hospital for Children are consistently among the highest-rated nationally. The successful applicant would be joining a large Pediatric Radiology group which includes dedicated pediatric subspecialists such interventional radiologists, neuroradiologists, fetal imagers, cardiac imagers, musculoskeletal imagers, and emergency imagers (which staff all overnight hours). title: Assistant/Associate/Full Research Professor of Surgery – Surgical Oncology
description: The Indiana University School of Medicine’s Department of Surgery, Division of Surgical Oncology, is seeking an Assistant Research Professor to join the lab of Dr. C. Max Schmidt. title: Assistant/Associate/Full Professor of Clinical Pediatrics
description: The Division of Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine in the Department of Pediatrics at Indiana University School of Medicine is seeking to add a clinical track faculty physician to provide patient care and serve as a clinician educator. Expert neonatologists at Riley Children's Health deliver specialized, evidence-based care to neonates in need of lifesaving choices. In many cases, our care begins prenatally and continues through the transition to home with comprehensive, multidisciplinary follow-up. Clinically, this role is expected to perform twenty weeks of clinical service at Riley Hospital NICUs or a local level 3 community NICU location. On an annual basis, call responsibilities will consist of twenty-four in-house calls, eight weekend rounding shifts, and moonlighting options. As an educator, there are numerous activities to advance programs within the department at both the student and resident level across all campuses. Faculty are involved in supervision and instruction of residents and medical students on clinical services. We also encourage participation in various didactic programs, as well as activities in the skills lab and simulation center. There are numerous activities to advance our research programs within the department and we anticipate this individual to actively participate and facilitate research activities either through direct investigator lead research projects or via referral of patients to ongoing clinical research projects. The Department of Pediatrics at IUSM/Riley Hospital for Children is a 398-member faculty that is consistently within the top 10 pediatric departments in NIH funded research in the United States and has 19 Fellowship programs. There is a new large pediatric clinical research center, a new pediatric outpatient center dedicated to general pediatrics and neurodevelopment related divisions in pediatrics, genetics, and psychiatry. There are also State-of-the-art laboratories in a dedicated pediatric research building, a clinical research center, a well-functioning biobank, six T32 fellow training grants and one K12s that support research in the Department. Our nationally recognized Division of Children’s Health Research is available for collaboration and as a resource for combined fellowships with the pediatric hospitalist program. The Department also has research relationships with the Regenstrief Institute in Health Informatics. Pediatric Radiology and Pediatric Neuroradiology are strong research partners. IU School of Medicine is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana.

title: Assistant Professor in Media, Behavior, and Health
description: The Media School at Indiana University’s flagship Bloomington campus is pleased to announce a faculty search for an outstanding tenure-track colleague whose research and teaching examine the relationships among media, behavior, and health, to start August 1, 2027. We welcome applications from scholars working across a broad range of topics at the intersection of media, health, and well-being. Areas of interest may include, but are not limited to, media influences on mental and physical health; health communication and health behavior; social media and well-being; media representations of health, illness, and disability; stigma and stereotyping; cognitive, emotional, and behavioral responses to health-related media; health misinformation; and the development and evaluation of media-based interventions designed to improve health and well-being. We are particularly interested in scholars whose work helps explain how media environments, messages, and technologies shape health-related attitudes, psychological processes, decision-making, and behavioral outcomes. We welcome a range of theoretical perspectives and methodological approaches, including experimental, survey, longitudinal, computational, neuroscientific, qualitative, and mixed-method approaches. Candidates may study children, adolescents, adults, or populations across the lifespan. This position offers substantial opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration across Indiana University, including with faculty in the Media School, the School of Public Health, the Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences, the Irsay Institute, and other units engaged in health and behavioral research. The successful candidate will join a growing community of scholars examining media, behavior, health, and well-being across the campus. The chosen applicant will be expected to maintain a productive and theoretically significant research program, effectively teach and mentor undergraduate and graduate students on a standard 2-2 teaching load, and serve the university, profession, and wider community. Teaching opportunities may include courses in media psychology, strategic communications, health communication, social media, research methods, and other areas related to the candidate’s expertise. The primary criteria for this search are excellence in research and teaching related to media, behavior, and health. Evidence of potential to secure external funding is viewed favorably. External funding is conceived broadly to include government, industry, foundation, and other private sources. About the School The Media School combines a long-standing tradition of excellence in journalism, film, gaming, and communications with a commitment to digital and interactive media. It fosters a multidisciplinary approach to education and research, equipping students with the theoretical and practical tools necessary to lead and innovate in the media landscape of tomorrow. Faculty members are distinguished for their scholarly contributions and their dedication to teaching, offering a dynamic environment for engaging with media theory, production, and design. The Media School is home to the Center for Documentary Research and Practice, the Center for International Media Law and Policy Studies, the Institute for Communication Research, the Michael I. Arnolt Center for Investigative Journalism, the National Sports Journalism Center, the Observatory on Social Media, Indiana Public Media, Cream and Crimson Studios, the KIX Lab, and the Black Film Center & Archive. The school serves more than 2,300 undergraduate majors in eight degree programs (Journalism, Media, Game Design, Cinematic Arts, Global Media, Media Advertising, Public Relations, and Sports Media). It also offers graduate degrees (M.S. and Ph.D.) to approximately 75 graduate students, of whom two-thirds are in a doctoral program. Our state-of-the-art facilities include equipment for television, film and audio production, game design, and communication research. University and Community Setting Nestled in the lively community of Bloomington, our university campus is renowned for its stunning limestone architecture and scenic natural landscapes. This setting fosters a culture that values both the arts and sciences and provides substantial opportunities for interdisciplinary research and collaboration. Bloomington is a vibrant midsize city located within driving distance of Indianapolis, Chicago, Cincinnati, Columbus, and Louisville. Our community is small yet welcoming, a home to people from all over the world. Bloomington features an active arts community, with several independent music and performance venues and one of the best university cinemas in the country. Southern Indiana is also home to beautiful scenery, and residents enjoy year-round outdoor activities.

title: Post Doctoral Appointee
description: Position Title: Postdoctoral Fellow in Peptide Chemistry and Cancer Immunotherapy The Peptide Laboratory at the Indiana University School of Medicine is seeking an outstanding and highly motivated Postdoctoral Fellow to join a multidisciplinary research program focused on the discovery and translation of next-generation peptide-based cancer immunotherapies. The laboratory has pioneered B-cell epitope peptide vaccines targeting immune checkpoint molecules and oncogenic growth factor receptors and is advancing novel multivalent and multispecific vaccine platforms toward clinical translation. The successful candidate will lead innovative projects integrating peptide chemistry, structural immunology, cancer biology, and translational immunotherapy. This position offers the opportunity to work in a highly collaborative environment with access to state-of-the-art chemistry, proteomics, immunology, and animal research cores while contributing to projects with strong publication, patent, and clinical translation potential. Research Focus Current research programs include: Therapeutic peptide vaccines targeting PD-1, CTLA-4, TIGIT, IL1RAP, HER-2/HER-3, VEGF, and other immune and tumor-associated targets Development of multispecific and multivalent peptide vaccine platforms Peptide conjugation using click chemistry and advanced linker technologies Structural design and optimization of conformational B-cell epitopes Combination immunotherapy with chemotherapy, targeted therapies, and immune checkpoint modulation Translation of peptide vaccines from preclinical models to Phase I clinical trials Responsibilities The successful candidate will: Synthesize therapeutic peptide vaccine candidates using Fmoc solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS). Develop and optimize peptide conjugation strategies, including CuAAC, SPAAC, thiol-maleimide coupling, PEGylation, and multivalent scaffold assembly. Purify and characterize peptides using analytical and preparative HPLC, LC-MS, and MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry. Execute studies evaluating vaccine immunogenicity and antitumor efficacy in preclinical models. Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams in chemistry, immunology, oncology, and bioinformatics. Analyze and interpret experimental data and maintain detailed laboratory records. Prepare manuscripts for publication in high-impact journals. Contribute to NIH grant applications, progress reports, and intellectual property development. Mentor graduate students, technicians, and undergraduate trainees. Present research findings at national and international scientific meetings. title: Lecturer in Geosciences with additional title of STEM Center Director
description: Review date begins October 21, 2026: (Apply by this date to ensure full consideration by the committee). Final date: November 4, 2026: Applications will continue to be accepted until this date, but those received after the review date will only be considered if the position has not yet been filled. The Department of Biology and Geosciences within the College of Arts, Sciences, and Education at Indiana University Northwest seeks to fill a Lecturer in Geology and STEM Center Director position. The position is a full-time, 12-month appointment. The teaching load is to be half time during the Fall, Spring, and Summer (a 2/2/1 FTE equivalent) with the remainder devoted to directing STEM Center programs. Lecturer in Geology Teaching Responsibilities: We seek a broadly educated geologist with demonstrated commitment to teaching at the undergraduate level. This position will contribute to majors in geoscience, environmental science, and sustainability, as well as general education courses. The individual will have a focus on STEM student success, the ability to implement sound pedagogy for both in-person and online instruction, and a commitment to undergraduate engagement. Teaching responsibilities will include introductory and early-career courses in earth science, geology, or geography (including geographic information systems [GIS]) and upper-level geology and geography courses based on the successful candidate’s areas of expertise and departmental needs. Course assignments may include courses in GIS, field methods and laboratory techniques, and climate change science, and foundational courses at the 100- and 200-level including introductory courses in Earth science, historical geology, and a first-year seminar in geoscience. Expertise in GIS, surficial processes and systems (geomorphology, Quaternary, glacial/climate systems, soils), and other expertise that will complement departmental expertise in mineralogy, ocean science, petrology, sedimentology/stratigraphy, and structural geology is particularly valued. With the Fall 2026 reorganization, the Departments of Geosciences and Biology merged and offer B.S. and B.A. degrees in Biological and Physical Sciences that will include majors in biology, environmental science (B.S. only), and geoscience, and an online B.A. degree in sustainability, shared among five IU regional campuses. Additionally, the department contributes to programs in science education and a master’s program in liberal studies. Core teaching responsibilities include a 6-hour equivalent per semester teaching load in the fall and spring semesters, and a 3-hour equivalent teaching load in the summer in face-to-face or online modalities. The teaching load may be unequally distributed based on departmental needs. Additionally, the successful candidate will actively engage in service to the department, campus, discipline, and the community. STEM Center Responsibilities : The STEM Center Director will: Provide leadership in developing/maintaining an effective, integrated approach to support student success in STEM working closely with internal and community college stakeholders. Work closely with STEM faculty and key campus administrators to enhance outreach and recruitment efforts of students in STEM programs. Advocate for student retention and success initiatives across campus and assume a leadership role in developing a culture of belonging and success for all STEM students. Engage with high schools, community, and industry stakeholders to enhance student interest in STEM and increase student knowledge of, and access to, STEM employment opportunities during the school year, summer, and after graduation. Coordinate services and activities with STEM faculty and existing campus support services in counseling, advising, tutoring, mentoring, and career services to maximize resources and achieve project goals. Plan, develop, and integrate innovative support services and activities designed to facilitate the success of STEM students. Prepare regular reports on the center’s overall effectiveness for project and campus leadership in accordance with the approved evaluation plan. ABOUT INDIANA UNIVERSITY NORTHWEST One of ten campuses of Indiana University, IU Northwest is located in metropolitan Northwest Indiana, approximately 30 miles southeast of Chicago and 10 miles from the Indiana Dunes National Park. The campus has a student population of approximately 3,200 degree-seeking students and more than 30,000 alumni, most of whom remain in the Northwest Indiana region, and has been recognized by the Department of Education as a minority and Hispanic serving institution. The campus offers Associate, Baccalaureate, and Master’s degrees from the College of Arts, Sciences & Education, the College of Health and Human Services, and the College of Business & Public Affairs. The campus is also home to IU School of Medicine-Northwest-Gary, the region’s only four-year medical doctorate program. As a student-centered campus, IU Northwest is committed to academic excellence characterized by a love of ideas and achievement in learning, discovery, creativity, research and community engagement. title: Assistant Professor
department: IU Indianapolis Tourism, Conventions, and Event Management – School of Health & Human Sciences
description: Indiana University Indianapolis invites applications for a 10-month tenure-track Assistant Professor in Tourism, Hospitality, or Event Management to support its expanding programs in tourism, events, hospitality, and sport management. The anticipated start date is August 1, 2026. Located in the heart of downtown Indianapolis, IU Indianapolis offers a distinctive urban research environment in one of the nation’s premier destinations for conventions, mega-events, and sports tourism. Indianapolis is internationally recognized as the “Sports Capital of the World,” home to the NCAA headquarters, major professional sports franchises, global sporting events, and a thriving sport-tech ecosystem. The city also features one of the most highly regarded convention centers in the United States—the Indiana Convention Center—positioning Indianapolis as a leading convention and mega-event destination. This setting provides unparalleled opportunities for industry collaboration, applied research, and experiential learning partnerships across tourism, hospitality, event management, and sport industries. Position Overview The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate instruction in areas such as: Tourism and destination management Convention and event management Hotel operations and revenue management Hospitality leadership and strategy Sport and event tourism Tourism and hospitality analytics Sustainable and resilient destinations Experience design We welcome applicants committed to addressing complex challenges in tourism systems, destination competitiveness, event strategy, hospitality innovation, sustainability, technology integration, and data-informed decision-making. Research and Collaboration Opportunities We seek scholars who create or employ innovative qualitative, quantitative, or computational methods to examine issues including: Convention and mega-event impact Sport tourism and event-driven development Urban destination strategy and competitiveness Hospitality performance and revenue optimization Tourism analytics and predictive modeling Sustainable tourism and community engagement Technology, AI, and smart destinations Indianapolis provides a living laboratory for tourism and event research. Faculty have strong potential to collaborate with: The Indiana Convention Center and Visit Indy NCAA and national governing sport bodies Professional sport franchises and event organizers Major recurring events (e.g., large-scale sporting championships, conventions, and festivals) Hospitality leaders, venue operators, and destination management organizations Responsibilities Teach undergraduate courses in tourism, hospitality, event management, sport tourism, or related domains. Establish and sustain a productive research agenda with potential for external funding. Develop applied partnerships with tourism, hospitality, convention, and sport industry stakeholders. Contribute to interdisciplinary initiatives and community engagement. Mentor undergraduate students. Provide service at the departmental, school, and university levels. Support learners through effective, evidence-based teaching practices. Duties 50% Research 40% Teaching (2 courses/fall and spring semesters) 10% Service About IU Indianapolis IU Indianapolis is Indiana’s premier urban public research university and holds both Community Engagement and R1 Carnegie Classifications. The campus serves more than 22,000 students across 15 schools and is making major investments in research infrastructure, including: The Convergent Bioscience and Technology Institute The Institute for Human Health and Wellbeing IU LAB at 16 Tech, supported by a $138 million Lilly Endowment grant The School of Health & Human Sciences prepares graduates to lead in complex global industries and seeks scholars committed to impactful research, innovative teaching, and meaningful engagement with Indianapolis and beyond.

title: Visiting Clinical Assistant Professor
department: IU Indianapolis School of Liberal Arts
description: The Ray Bradbury Center in the School of Liberal Arts at IU Indianapolis invites applicants for a Visiting Assistant Clinical Professor position in the American Studies Program in the Department of Interdisciplinary Studies. The person in this position will bring expertise as an experienced Project Archivist to lead the arrangement, description, preservation, and public-access preparation of approximately 186 linear feet of unprocessed manuscript materials from the Ray Bradbury Collection. The Center holds over 150,000 manuscript pages, four decades of correspondence, Bradbury's working library of nearly 4,000 volumes, and the contents of his home office. This role requires prior archival processing experience, knowledge of archival metadata standards, and hands-on ArchivesSpace (or comparable) experience. Bradbury's filing practices were often associative and inconsistent, so the archivist must exercise sound professional judgment when original order is unclear. The Project Archivist reports to the Center's Director and collaborates with IU Libraries, University Collections, and the IU Indianapolis Arts and Humanities Institute. Established in 2007, the Ray Bradbury Center is the only public archive dedicated exclusively to Ray Bradbury (1920–2012), preserving manuscripts, correspondence, artwork, AV materials, and memorabilia documenting his creative and professional life. IU Indianapolis is opening a purpose-built reference library, reading room, and archival storage facility for the Center in October 2026. This position offers the opportunity to establish lasting intellectual and physical control over a major American literary archive and make it available for scholarly and public use. The initial appointment for this grant-funded visiting position is December 1, 2026, through August 31, 2028. This position requires regular on-campus presence. As the state’s premier urban research institution, IU Indianapolis is a dynamic campus of over 20,000 students and has been recognized for excellence in civic engagement and community partnerships. IU Indianapolis is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose scholarly efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty.

title: Assistant Professor or above of Clinical Otolaryngology-Head & Neck Surgery

title: Assistant/Associate/ Research Professor of Medicine
description: The Division of Cardiovascular Medicine in the Department of Medicine strives for excellence in research, education, and patient care. The division’s physicians, staff members, and learners work to reduce the burden of cardiovascular disease for Hoosiers, offering the highest quality care and fostering innovation that fuels better health for the people of Indiana and beyond. The division has multiple research laboratories, programs, and clinical trials conducting studies in various aspects of cardiovascular diseases. In addition, there are ACGME-approved cardiology training programs in cardiovascular diseases, cardiovascular electrophysiology, interventional cardiology, heart failure, and adult congenital heart disease. This position will utilize a broad range of cardiovascular experimental approaches, including advanced rodent CV physiology models and molecular biology techniques. This combination of physiologic, surgical, molecular, and translational expertise represents an important capability that will strengthen cardiovascular research within the Division of Cardiovascular Medicine. This will directly contribute to the IU School of Medicine Strategic Plan of accelerating discovery and clinical translation. This role will partner with faculty to help develop and execute rigorous cardiovascular phenotyping and preclinical studies. Depending on the needs of individual projects, this could include consultation on experimental design and model selection; development and implementation of cardiovascular disease models; advanced echocardiographic and hemodynamic phenotyping; cardiovascular surgical models; ex vivo physiology; tissue and molecular analyses; and integration of physiologic models with genomic and multi-omic approaches. IU School of Medicine is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana.

The department emphasizes high-quality teaching, active faculty scholarship, and strong connections to regional industry through internships, applied projects, and community engagement. Located along the St. Joseph River, the campus is known for its strong emphasis on teaching excellence, undergraduate research, faculty student interaction, commitment to access and community engagement within a supportive academic environment. title: Postdoctoral Researcher – Quantum and Classical Dynamics of Decision Making
description: Position Overview The Postdoctoral Researcher will join an NSF-funded project developing and testing computational models of how decisions evolve over time. The project integrates quantum and classical (Markov) approaches within an open-systems framework to investigate when decision dynamics exhibit interference, coherence, decoherence, and more classical stochastic accumulation. The position will be jointly mentored by Dr. Tim Pleskac and Dr. Jerome Busemeyer, with the postdoc taking a leading role in theory development, computational modeling, and experimental tests of the models. The position is based at Indiana University Bloomington, with opportunities to collaborate across IU’s strong communities in mathematical psychology, judgment and decision making, cognitive science, and quantitative modeling. This postdoctoral appointment is full-time and on-campus. Job Duties 80% – Research Develop computational models of dynamic judgment and decision making using quantum probability, open-system dynamics, and classical Markov processes. Derive and test behavioral predictions that distinguish quantum, classical, and intermediate open-system dynamics, including predictions about the time course of evidence and preference evolution. Design and analyze behavioral experiments that probe dynamic decision processes, including interference, oscillation, response-time, and evidence-accumulation phenomena. Implement simulation, parameter-estimation, and model-comparison methods in Python, MATLAB, R, or related computational environments. Lead and co-author manuscripts, conference presentations, and other dissemination of project findings. 10% – Project Management Work directly with the PIs to ensure efficient progress toward project objectives. Coordinate research tasks across graduate students, undergraduate research assistants, and collaborating researchers. Maintain reproducible modeling, simulation, data-analysis, and documentation workflows. 10% – Other Duties Participate in lab meetings, mentoring of junior researchers, grant-related activities, and other project duties as needed. Work Environment The postdoc will be embedded in the rich cognitive and mathematical psychology research communities at Indiana University. The researcher will work closely with Drs. Pleskac and Busemeyer and benefit from Indiana University’s long-standing strengths in mathematical psychology, decision science, and quantum cognition. Appointment Details Anticipated Start Date: January 1, 2027 (negotiable) Salary: $60,000 + benefits Work Schedule: Full-time, on-campus Supervisors: Dr. Tim Pleskac and Dr. Jerome Busemeyer Initial Appointment: 1 year, with expectation of renewal for a second year based on performance and funding

title: Visiting Assistant Research Professor of Pediatrics
description: Indiana University/Riley Hospital for Children is currently recruiting a Pediatric Team leader for their Academic Model Providing Access to Healthcare (AMPATH) program in Kenya. If you or a pediatrician you know is interested in working within a 30+ year international partnership, please see the details of the position below. The role of the AMPATH Kenya Pediatrics In-Country Lead is to be an ambassador, driver, and guide of the educational mission between the North American and Kenyan institutions of the AMPATH consortium. The team leader resides in Kenya full-time and their primary mission is to build capacity through workforce development. They accomplish this by working closely with Kenyan and North American faculty, residents, and medical students to support a positive learning environment that is respectful to all. Specific responsibilities for the Pediatrics Team Leader include: hosting North American visitors, (medical trainees and teaching faculty), in Kenya, coordinating electives for Kenyan learners in North America, and functioning as a visiting lecturer within the Department of Child Health and Pediatrics at Moi University School of Medicine and Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital. The team leader engages with other service and scholarly work to the degree that these advance the primary mission of capacity building and workforce development. Working Environment ● The Team Leader is required to live and work in Eldoret, Kenya, at the IU House whenever legal and institutional permissions allow. ● Office space and access to office equipment, (computer, printers, photocopying), will be provided in the IU Center for Global Health and at the IU House. ● The team leader is required to attend virtual meetings and perform some work remotely. Support This position is supported by the IU Department of Pediatrics and the IU Center for Global Health. The team leader will receive an appointment as a Visiting Assistant Research Professor in Pediatrics at Indiana University School of Medicine and a Visiting Lecturer in Pediatrics at Moi University School of Medicine. Salary is commensurate with experience. Supervision The Pediatrics team leader reports directly to both the IU Center for Global Health Director of Education and the Department of Pediatrics Vice Chair of Education. Day-to-day activities are supervised and managed by the AMPATH Executive Field Director. For clinical and teaching responsibilities related to the Moi University, the team leader will report to the Head of Department of Child Health and Pediatrics. Faculty Duties AMPATH Ambassador As the AMPATH ambassador for pediatrics, the pediatrics team leader is expected to: ● Attend weekly AMPATH consortium calls ● Participate in monthly meetings with IU Center for Global Health Education leadership ● Help maintain and update AMPATH Education SOPs ● Provide reports on activities related to the pediatric educational mission when requested Visiting Assistant Professor of Indiana University Department of Pediatrics As a member of the IU Department of Pediatrics, the pediatrics team leader is expected to: ● Assist with global health related educational activities for IU residents and students. This includes at least monthly meetings with Pediatrics Global Health Education leadership This may include book/journal clubs, development and implementation of new global health curriculum, mentorship of IU trainees in global health related projects, among other activities ● Maintain regular and prompt communication with the IU Department of Pediatrics. This includes timely submission of student and resident evaluations and prompt response to emails and requests for information. ● Facilitate pediatric research efforts in Kenya by helping to build relationships between researchers from the North American AMPATH institutions and researchers from Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital and Moi University School of Medicine. ● Host visitors to AMPATH with an interest in Pediatrics including donors, new faculty, researchers, and the many other interested parties that create future opportunities for AMPATH. Visiting lecturer of Moi University Department of Child Health and Pediatrics As a visiting lecturer of the Moi University Department of Child Health and Pediatrics, the pediatrics team leader is expected to: Participate in clinical care for pediatric patients at Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital. This primarily involves leading bedside teaching and rounds for teams of Kenyan registrars (residents) and medical students. Duties are 7 days at a time at an interval of every 3-4 weeks. The pediatrics team leader is tasked with developing and maintaining the schedule of service for the 4 attendings on the Upendo pediatrics inpatient team. Participate in Department of Child Health and Pediatrics staff meetings Participate in weekly registrar “mini-rounds” and journal club Participate in the administration of student and registrar exams Assist in writing questions for student and registrar exams Facilitate didactic teaching for medical students and registrars when requested Optional – supervise and mentor registrars with thesis research projects Educational Duties Co-precept IU learner pediatrics rotation Assist with predeparture orientation and provide re-orientations once IU visitors are in Kenya Complete all evaluations of trainees rotating in pediatrics in Kenya. These should be done in a timely fashion (no later than 15 days after the end of the rotation). Grade trainee reflection papers and other course requirements in conjunction with IU Center for Global Health Equity Education faculty Coordinate learners and visiting teaching faculty from all AMPATH North American schools Work closely with the IU Center for Global Health Equity Assistant Director for Logistics and Education Programs and other team leaders to track which trainees are coming for rotations, which specific rotations they will complete, and what dates they will be in Kenya. Assist in scheduling additional activities for interested visiting trainees Create schedules for each trainee (dates for each rotation, morning report date, date in various clinics, trainee requests, etc.) Send welcome email to visiting students/residents 2-4 weeks before arrival with their schedule, and the rules, protocols, logistics for the rotation. Inform Moi and MTRH leadership about planned trainee and clinical faculty visitors Orient visitors to clinical sites and info trainees of rotational requirements and schedule Introduce visitors to Kenya clinical colleagues and supervisors Didactics and Discussions The Team Leader will oversee and deliver educational activities and didactics for North American trainees, focusing on global health and healthcare delivery in Kenya. Key responsibilities include: Morning Reports : Facilitate and mentor students and residents through discussions on the complexities of healthcare in Kenya. Develop schedules and contribute key teaching points. Global Health Talks : Coordinate and deliver educational sessions on clinical topics relevant to healthcare in Eldoret. Collaborate with multidisciplinary faculty to create a comprehensive lecture schedule. Fireside Chats : Organize and lead informal discussions on critical global health issues, fostering thoughtful engagement among trainees. Debriefing and processing The pediatrics team leader is responsible for assisting trainees with processing their experiences in Kenya. This should be accomplished through, at a minimum, weekly debrief sessions. These can be in groups or individually and should be done with the goal of encouraging a posture of cultural humility among learners. Slemenda Scholars Rising second-year IU School of Medicine students travel to Kenya as part of the Slemenda Scholars program. The program was established in honor of Dr. Charlie Slemenda, an IU School of Medicine epidemiologist, who had a passion for global health. The program sends IU medical students to Eldoret to experience AMPATH by participating in rounds, collaborating on field projects, and working alongside Moi University medical students. In conjunction with the other team leaders, the pediatric team leader will work to create a schedule of clinical and learning opportunities for the Slemenda scholars including the opportunity to have an immersion experience in the COBES program if at all possible. In conjunction with the other team leaders, the pediatric team leader will work to orient and supervise the Scholars during their time in Kenya The pediatric team leader will mentor one Slemenda scholar and assist them with completing a project. Each team leader is responsible for being a primary mentor for at least one Scholar and/or to identify NA faculty on-ground willing to fold the student into their established projects and provide primary mentorship. SERVICE DUTIES Medical care for pediatric guests at IU House The pediatric team leader is responsible for the following medical care activities for IU House guests: Discuss medical issues in advance for children with chronic medical issues coming to IU Provide necessary urgent medical care for children staying at IU House and/or facilitate access to appropriate medical care at a local hospital/clinic. Keep pediatric medical supplies at IU house up to date and in stock. Manage pediatric HIV exposure with PEP protocol per IU House policies/procedures. Weekend Call Maintain and participate in schedule for weekend call, on average every 3-4 weekends. Communicate the call schedule to IU House staff. Weekend call duties include triage and management of minor medical issues for guests and long-term faculty, ensuring guest safety and compliance with policies, and providing orientation for weekend guest arrivals. Clinical duties In addition to clinical work on the pediatric ward at Moi Teaching and Referral Hospital the pediatrics team leader will have the opportunity to work in an outpatient clinic (AMPATH affiliated clinics, MTRH specialty clinics, etc.) Scholarly Work The pediatrics team leader will seek to engage in scholarly projects that will result in regular disseminated outputs (i.e. program development, quality improvement project, etc.). The pediatrics team leader will work with the IU Director and Associate Directors of Global Health to identify and mentor global health-related scholarly work for pediatrics trainees. Partner with Kenyan colleagues on scholarly projects Follow all AMPATH research protocols IUSM is committed to being a welcoming campus community and we seek candidates whose research, teaching, and community engagement efforts contribute to robust learning and working environments for all students, staff, and faculty. We invite individuals who will join us in our mission to improve health equity and well-being for all throughout the state of Indiana.

title: Dean, Herron School of Art + Design
department: IU Indianapolis Herron School Of Art & Design
description: Indiana University Indianapolis (IU Indianapolis) seeks an accomplished and visionary leader to serve as the next Dean of the Herron School of Art + Design. Herron seeks a leader that appreciates the many ways that art, music, and design contribute to campus life, student growth, and the advancement of the State of Indiana. The next Dean will build on more than a century of operation and engagement in downtown Indianapolis. Herron is home to more than 50 full-time faculty and 20 staff and has an annual operating budget of over $9 million. At the start of the Fall 2025 semester, 714 students were enrolled at Herron (10 doctoral students, 46 master students, and 658 undergraduates). The school offers fifteen undergraduate majors, nine minors, two certificates, and eleven graduate degrees and certificates. Herron also has distinctly unique offerings in Music Technology and Music Therapy programs. The Dean, reporting to the Provost and Executive Vice Chancellor at IU Indianapolis, serves as the chief strategic, academic, and administrative officer for the School. This individual is responsible for: · Defining the School’s direction and priorities at the highest level. · Collaborating and forming strategic partnerships with other IU Schools. · Overseeing its growth and development, including fundraising to support Herron’s strategic directions · Managing personnel, budget, and policy. · Shaping an environment for faculty, students, and staff to thrive. Direct reports to the Dean include two associate deans, an assistant dean, four department chairs, a gallery director, a director of development, a facilities manager, and a marketing lead. The Dean also works with the Dean’s Advisory Board, the Advancement Council, and the National Advisory Council to help guide the direction of the school, engage alumni and donors, and help support curricular innovation. IU Indianapolis is open to considering candidates from all parts of the world who may have been shaped by a variety of experiences, including leadership in the academic, private, professional, military, nonprofit, and government sectors.

title: Lecturer, Library and Information Science
department: IU Indianapolis Department of Library and Information Science – Luddy School
description: The Indiana University Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering in Indianapolis invites applications for one full-time lecturer-track faculty position in the Department of Library and Information Science. The appointment will begin on August 1, 2027 . This 10-month appointment (August through May) is annually renewable, based upon satisfactory performance. Additional compensation is available for candidates interested in teaching during the summer months. A committed educator is sought to join our department on the Indianapolis campus. We are interested in candidates with one or more of the following areas of expertise: Digital preservation & web archiving Electronic records management Archival intelligence Database and asset management Candidates must have experience effectively teaching in an online environment and five or more years of professional (industry) experience in one or more areas of expertise listed above. A deep understanding of career opportunities in the information professions and a passion for graduate student mentoring for academic and professional success is necessary. Ideal candidates will also shape their teaching in ways that leverage the unique strengths of Luddy Indianapolis, including its interdisciplinary and collaborative environment and commitment to service and community engagement. We especially welcome candidates who bring direct experience or novel approaches to incorporating generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) (and related tools) to enhance student learning. Public syllabi for courses offered in our program can be found at: https://syllabi.iu.edu/ Responsibilities Full-time lecturer-track faculty commit to a balanced workload of teaching and service, which includes: · Teach graduate courses in the LIS department; typically, four course section/equivalents per semester and 3-5 different courses per academic year · Supervise independent studies · Mentor graduate students · Contribute to course and curriculum development · Contribute to the department, school and campus level, and the professional community through service (e.g., committees, initiatives, task forces, etc.) How to apply Application instructions are available at https://luddy.indianapolis.iu.edu/about/openings.html . To ensure full consideration, please submit your application materials through our electronic system. Applications received by December 1, 2026, will receive priority. However, the position will remain open until filled. Questions about this position can be directed to search committee chair, Austin Stroud, austroud@iu.edu . About the Department of Library and Information Science │ https://luddy.indianapolis.iu.edu/departments/lis/index.html In 2000, the Indianapolis location of the Indiana University School of Library and Information Science was founded to provide high-quality library education to students who could not be residential students, needing distance learning options. The Department is ALA-accredited, offering students a wide array of academic and career specializations. The LIS department is particularly strong in the application of technology to the information professions and in public libraries, children/youth services, and increasingly archives, particularly digital curation. Tenure track and lecturer faculty work together to provide engaged and engaging education with a commitment to the development of the library and information professions. Securing external funding for student support and faculty research is important to the Department and to the School. About the Indiana University Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering – Indianapolis │ https://luddy.indianapolis.iu.edu/index.html The Indiana University School of Informatics and Computing was the first completely new school in the United States devoted exclusively to Informatics and a range of its sub-disciplines. In 2013 the Indiana University School of Library and Information Science merged with the School of Informatics. With its formative national role in creating the nation’s largest Informatics Program on the Bloomington and Indianapolis campus, the school is the broadest and one of the largest information/computing schools in the U.S. At IU Indianapolis, the school offers six Ph.D. programs (Bioinformatics, Data Science, Computer Science, Health and Biomedical Informatics, and Information Science), eight Master’s programs (Applied Data Science, Bioinformatics, Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, Health Informatics, Human–Computer Interaction, Library and Information Science, and Software Engineering), eight Baccalaureate programs (Artificial Intelligence, Biomedical Informatics, Computer Science, Data Science, Full Stack Developer, Health Information Management, Informatics and Media Arts and Science), and several undergraduate and graduate certificate programs. title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Clinical Radiology, Breast Imaging, Indianapolis
description: Breast Imaging Radiologist Dedicated Breast Imaging FACULTY POSITION • INDIANAPOLIS The Indiana University School of Medicine Department of Radiology and Imaging Sciences in partnership with Indiana University Health invites applications for a fellowship-trained Breast Imaging Radiologist to join our growing breast imaging team. title: Director of the Robert A. and Sandra S. Borns Jewish Studies Program / Lou and Sybil Mervis Chair in Jewish Cultural Studies
description: The Robert A. and Sandra S. Borns Jewish Studies Program at Indiana University, one of the world’s longest-established Jewish Studies programs, invites applications for its next Director. The appointment will be at the rank of full professor, beginning August 2027, and will be made in cooperation with the relevant disciplinary department. Candidates at the rank of associate professor would be considered in exceptional cases. Depending on their research expertise, the Director may also be eligible to hold the Lou and Sybil Mervis Chair in Jewish Cultural Studies for the duration of their tenure. The Director will serve an initial four-year term, with the expectation of renewal for at least one additional term. As Director, the successful candidate will provide visionary leadership to sustain and grow a program that spans literature, history, politics, religious studies, gender studies, sociology, musicology, languages, and the arts. We seek a leader with the capacity to strengthen enrollment, expand partnerships, foster exchange of diverse viewpoints, and articulate and execute a compelling vision for the program’s scholarly profile, public presence, and future growth. The program is home to two centers of excellence: Olamot: Center for Scholarly and Cultural Exchange with Israel, which fosters academic and cultural exchange with Israeli partners, and the Institute for the Study of Contemporary Antisemitism (ISCA), which advances the study of and teaching about contemporary antisemitism and houses a research lab on social media and hate. The program is also advancing several strategic initiatives. These include a major project funded by the National Endowment for the Humanities and led by ISCA and the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars, Addressing Antisemitism as a Global Challenge: Political, Cultural, and Intellectual Sources and Manifestations , and a new Israel Studies and Business program that connects students with the economic, entrepreneurial, and technological dimensions of contemporary Israel. The program also features an outstanding Hebrew curriculum supported by new technologies, and a strong Yiddish program, along with broad offerings in Jewish history, culture and society. The successful candidate will be a scholar or artist of exceptional distinction, with a PhD or equivalent terminal degree (field-dependent), and a record of original research or creative achievement. Indiana University offers strong support for research and teaching in Jewish Studies. Candidates may come from a wide range of disciplines in the humanities, arts, history and social sciences. The Lou and Sybil Mervis Chair in Jewish Cultural Studies was established to enhance understanding of modern Jewish culture and art, particularly in America, with special attention to Jewish contributions to theater and drama, humor, music, film, literature, radio and television, the visual arts, or related fields. The Mervis Chair provides resources to advance scholarship and creative work, including support for research and related needs. Interested candidates should review the application requirements and submit their application electronically at http://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/31666 . Application materials include a cover letter, curriculum vita, and the names of three references. Applications received before Monday, November 9, 2026 will be assured of consideration, but the search will continue until a suitable candidate is identified.
